His saying ﴿beneath which the rivers flow﴾: the scholars said: they flow beneath them without needing a structure to prevent the water from seeping away, nor digging a trench. They flow wherever you wish. Ibn al-Qayyim said in the Nuniyya:
Its rivers flow without a trench, glory be to the One who holds them back from overflowing.
So they are rivers that need no digging of channels nor establishing a ditch; they flow thus upon the earth. The scholars also said: they flow wherever the person wishes, instead of bringing building materials and direction; he wants them with his heart or commands them with his tongue. O Allah, make us among its people.
﴿Abiding therein forever; that is the great triumph﴾. ﴿Abiding﴾ (khālidīna) is a state (ḥāl). A state of whom?
* A student: Of the pronoun in ﴿He will admit him﴾.
* The Shaykh: Of the pronoun in ﴿He will admit him﴾. But there is a difficulty: a state is like an adjective, and an adjective follows what it describes in singular, dual and plural, whereas here the referent is singular and the state is plural. So what is the answer? The answer is that we say: the referent returns to (man), the conditional, and the conditional (man) may be treated according to its wording or according to its meaning. If you treat the wording, you return the pronoun to it in the singular; if you treat the meaning, you return the pronoun to it in the plural. Likewise, what resembles a pronoun, such as a state or adjective and the like, may be treated by meaning or by wording.
So here it says ﴿He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein﴾: it observed the wording in ﴿He will admit him﴾ and the meaning in ﴿abiding﴾.
It is also permissible to observe the wording and the meaning and then return a second time to observing the wording. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, said at the end of Surah At-Talaq: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness — He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah has certainly perfected for him provision﴾ [At-Talaq 11]. So He observed the wording first, then the meaning, then the wording again, and this is permissible in the Arabic language.
He says: ﴿abiding therein﴾, and His saying ﴿abiding therein﴾: the scholars said that khulūd is lasting, continuous staying, unless some evidence indicates that it is limited, in which case it means a long stay. Otherwise the basic meaning of khulūd is permanence, but if there is an indication that the intended meaning is a long stay, it is acted upon.
﴿Abiding therein; that is the great triumph﴾. ﴿That﴾ refers to what has been mentioned of this reward which Allah prepared for whoever obeys Him. ﴿The great triumph﴾: triumph (al-fawz) means profit; one says: so-and-so triumphed, meaning he profited. And great (al-ʿaẓīm) means possessing greatness, and greatness is the massiveness of a thing, its majesty, and also the abundance of a thing.
﴿That﴾ refers to what has been mentioned of this reward which Allah prepared for whoever obeys Him. ﴿The great triumph﴾: ﴿triumph﴾ (al-fawz) means: profit; one says: so-and-so triumphed, meaning he profited; and ﴿great﴾ (al-ʿaẓīm) means: possessing greatness, and greatness is: the massiveness of a thing and the majesty of a thing, and also the abundance of a thing.
It is known that the bliss of Paradise is characterized by massiveness, majesty and permanence, so it is the greatest triumph. A parallel to this is His saying, Exalted: ﴿Whoever is spared from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has triumphed﴾ [Aal Imran 185]. It is mentioned that az-Zamakhshari, who was one of the Mu'tazila, commented on this verse, ﴿Whoever is spared from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has triumphed﴾, saying: what triumph is greater than being spared from the Fire and admitted to Paradise? The interrogative here carries the sense of negation, meaning: there is no triumph greater than that.
Some annotators and critics of him said: he intended by this to negate the seeing of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because the seeing (...) and what is in it and greater triumph. Allah knows best whether he intended that. Whoever looks at the wording says there is in reality no indication in it, because among the necessary consequences of entering Paradise is — what? Looking at the face of Allah. And whoever knows the man's situation, that he was a Mu'tazili but intelligent, says: perhaps he intended that. Had such a phrase come from a person known to affirm the seeing of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, we would not explain it in this way and say that he intended to negate seeing. But one who knows his situation would not consider it unlikely that this was his intent.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the inheritance shares are among the limits of Allah.
* And among its benefits: whoever carries out these inheritance shares as Allah prescribed has this reward.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the division of inheritance is an act of worship, derived from the arrangement of the reward upon it and describing it as obedience.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the concern of the Shariʿa for delivering rights to their people, because the reality of inheritance is that rights reach their owners, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is a just judge who wants His servants to deliver rights to their owners.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: obedience to the Messenger, upon him be prayers and peace and upon his family, is obedience to Allah; for this reason He joined it with (wa, "and"), which indicates togetherness and association.
If someone asks: what is the reconciliation between this verse and the saying of the Messenger, upon him be prayers and peace, to a man who said to him: "What Allah wills and you will": "Have you made me a rival to Allah? Rather, what Allah alone wills"?[[Narrated by Ahmad (1839) and al-Tabarani (13005) from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas.]]
The answer: there is no harm in joining the Messenger, upon him be prayers and peace, with the Lord, Glorified be He, with "and" in legislative matters; but in matters of creation (kawniyya) it is not permissible, because they are among the attributes of lordship, and the action of the servant must follow the action of Allah. As for the ruling, the ruling of the Messenger is the ruling of Allah; for this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said in the Qur'an: ﴿And if only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them﴾, and He did not say "then His Messenger," and: ﴿and said, "Sufficient for us is Allah; Allah will give us of His bounty, and His Messenger"﴾ [At-Tawba 59]; because this giving is a legislated giving, the giving of zakat and legislated wealth. As for creational matters, no, because they are among the attributes of lordship, so the action of the servant must be after the action of Allah.
"What Allah wills and you will": this is not permissible, because you made the will of the Messenger like the will of Allah, and it is not so. But obedience to the Messenger is — what? Like obedience to Allah: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [An-Nisa 80]. Allah made obedience to the Messenger obedience to Him.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of reward on the Day of Resurrection, from His saying ﴿He will admit him to gardens﴾, and its basis is that admission to gardens is not in this world but in the Hereafter.
* And among its benefits: the description of the bliss of these gardens and that rivers flow beneath them, and the types of these rivers are known from another verse.
* And among its benefits: the permanence of the bliss of these gardens, from His saying ﴿abiding therein﴾. Is the abiding here everlasting or limited? Everlasting. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, mentioned this in several verses of the Qur'an, and the Muslims agreed that the bliss of Paradise is everlasting, and no disagreement has been reported on this.
* And among its benefits: that this bliss is the great profit that nothing equals, from His saying ﴿and that is the great triumph﴾.
I forgot to parse this sentence: ﴿That is the great triumph﴾. How do we parse it?
* A student: (dhā) is a demonstrative subject, indeclinable on sukun.
* The Shaykh: No, that is not the detail; (dhā) is a demonstrative subject.
﴿The triumph﴾?
* The student: Predicate.
* The Shaykh: The predicate of the subject.
* The student: ﴿The great﴾ is an adjective.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verses 13–14 (part 2 of 3):

* The Shaykh: It is an attribute (ṣifah) of ﴿al-fawz﴾ (the triumph). If someone says: ﴿That is the great triumph﴾, could ﴿al-fawz﴾ be a substitute (badal), an explanatory apposition (ʿaṭf bayān), or an adjective (naʿt) of ﴿dhālika﴾ (that)? The meaning would then be: "That triumph is the great one." This would be acceptable, but the first grammatical analysis (iʿrab) is better.

Then God Most High says: ﴿And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him to a Fire, abiding therein, and for him is a humiliating punishment﴾ [An-Nisa' 14]. Disobedience (maʿṣiyah) is opposing a command or committing a prohibited act. So whoever abandons an obligation has disobeyed, and whoever does a forbidden act has disobeyed. We say about ﴿whoever disobeys God and His Messenger﴾ what we said about ﴿whoever obeys God and His Messenger﴾, except that the grammatical analysis differs here. ﴿Yaʿṣi﴾ is the conditional verb (fiʿl al-sharṭ), in the jussive. By what is it jussive?

* The students: By the deletion of the weak letter.

* The Shaykh: By the deletion of the weak letter, which is the yāʾ.

And His saying: ﴿wa-yataʿadda ḥudūdahu﴾ (and transgresses His limits). Is ﴿yataʿadda﴾ with a fatḥah according to you?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: How is the fatḥah correct, given that it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the jussive ﴿yaʿṣi﴾?

* A student: It is jussive by the deletion of a letter, because it is not conjoined... (...) the conjoined element, and the fatḥah became a sign of the deleted alif.

* The Shaykh: That is, it is jussive by the deletion of the alif.

* The student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: And its root?

* The student: (yataʿadda).

* The Shaykh: (yataʿadda), yes.

And His saying: ﴿yatacadda ḥudūdahu﴾ means: he oversteps them. Does "the limits" here mean the commands or the prohibitions?

* Some students: The prohibitions.

* Other students: The commands.

* The Shaykh: There is no god but God! In ﴿yataʿadda ḥudūdahu﴾, what did we say before?

* Students: The commands.

* The Shaykh: The commands, yes. He did not say "whoever approaches His limits." He said: "whoever oversteps His limits," meaning he exceeds what has been set as a command. He did not say what has been set by commands.

﴿He will admit him to a Fire, abiding therein﴾: this is the answer of the conditional clause. The Fire is known; it is this burning, hot body. Or do we say: it is known, and that is sufficient?

* The students: It is known.

* The Shaykh: It is known and that is sufficient, just as we say: "The sky is above us and the earth is below us."

﴿Abiding therein﴾: here He said ﴿khālidan﴾ (abiding), and there, regarding the Garden, He said ﴿khālidīna﴾ (abiding, plural). Is there a subtle point here, meaning, my intention is: a benefit or a wisdom?

The answer: Yes. The people of Paradise enjoy gathering with one another, and for this reason He said ﴿khālidīna fīhā﴾. As for the people of the Fire, may God protect us, it has been reported that each one of them is in a coffin, not seeing anyone and not seen by anyone.[[Reported by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (36424), from the hadith of Suwayd ibn Ghaflah, as a mawquf report.]] Except as a form of rebuke. This is the secret, and God knows best, why He said of the people of Paradise ﴿khālidīna﴾ and of the people of the Fire ﴿khālidan fīhā﴾.

﴿And for him is a humiliating punishment﴾: meaning that together with his being admitted to the Fire and abiding in it, he never remains at ease at all. Rather, he is punished with a punishment of humiliation. So it is a bodily punishment and a punishment of the heart and soul, because bodily punishment is easier than the pain of the heart. For this reason the scholars said: a person should be circumcised while he is young, because the circumcision of a child involves only bodily pain. But if an adult is circumcised, there is bodily pain and pain of the heart and soul. He thinks: perhaps the wound will get worse, perhaps he will die, and so on. But a child, if he is cooled down, becomes quiet; and if the pain attacks him, he cries out. If we walk him, or walk with him if he cannot walk, he falls silent. The point is that the punishment of the people of the Fire, may God protect us, is a humiliating punishment, meaning one that involves humiliation, because they are reproached and censured.

* This noble verse contains benefits, among them: that disobedience to God, Mighty and Majestic, is a cause for entering the Fire, by His saying ﴿whoever disobeys God﴾ and ﴿He will admit him to a Fire, abiding therein﴾. We say "a cause" because it may be prevented by an obstacle, namely God's pardon, in cases other than shirk. As for shirk, its doer must certainly enter the Fire and abide in it: ﴿Indeed, whoever associates others with God, God has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 72]. Based on this, we say: if the disobedience is less than shirk, it is a cause for entering the Fire, but entering the Fire is not necessarily required by it, since one may be pardoned. If it is shirk, it is a certain cause, and its doer must enter the Fire and abide in it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the prohibition of a bequest to an heir. How is that? Because if you make a bequest to an heir, you have overstepped the limits. If a woman bequeaths a third to her husband, he would receive, according to the terms of the bequest, a third plus a half, and this is overstepping the limits. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "God has given every person with a right his right, so there is no bequest to an heir."[[Reported by Abu Dawud (2870) and al-Tirmidhi (2120), from Abu Umamah.]]

* A student: May God be good to you, O Shaykh. We have now said that major shirk is a cause for eternal abiding in the Fire. What about minor shirk?

* The Shaykh: It is not a cause for eternal abiding.

* The student: But he will enter it, O Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: This depends on His saying: ﴿Indeed, God does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾ [An-Nisa' 48]. Is this shirk general or unrestricted? If we say it is general, then shirk, even if minor, is not forgiven. This is the view of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may God have mercy on him.

* A student: How does a person know that something is minor shirk? Can it be delimited, O Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: It can be known from the texts. Whatever the Lawgiver has called shirk, and which does not take one out of the religion, is minor shirk.

* A student: O Shaykh, the conditions of Paradise are unseen, so what is the evidence that its rivers (...)?

* The Shaykh: Yes, there is a hadith about it, indeed there are several hadiths.

* A student: Shaykh al-Islam says: doing what is prohibited counts as abandoning an obligation. O Shaykh, does it not indicate (...) ﴿Those are the limits of God﴾ (...) in the commands (...) ﴿And whoever obeys God and His Messenger﴾?

* The Shaykh: No, the limits are in the commands and they are in the prohibitions.

* The student: No, here in the verse?

* The Shaykh: ﴿Those are the limits of God﴾ [An-Nisa' 13]: these are in the commands. And doing the commands is obedience. But perhaps His saying ﴿whoever disobeys God and His Messenger and transgresses His limits﴾ indicates this. This verse indicates it.

* The student: Because He said (...).

* The Shaykh: Correct: abandoning an obligation is falling into a prohibition, and doing a prohibition is abandoning an obligation, because it is obligatory upon you to refrain.

* A student: (...) in the saying of Ibn ʿAbbas about blood, whoever abandons an obligation in the Hajj (...)?

* The Shaykh: Ibn ʿAbbas says: "Whoever abandons something of his rites, or forgets it, let him sacrifice an animal."[[Reported by al-Bayhaqi in al-Kubra (5/30), from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas.]]

* The student: (...) What does this verse indicate?

* The Shaykh: Perhaps. I say: perhaps.

* A student: ﴿After a bequest he makes or a debt﴾: is the bequest (...) or has the Sunnah restricted it: "There is no bequest to an heir"?[[Reported by Abu Dawud (2870), from the hadith of Abu Umamah.]]

* The Shaykh: No, it is derived from the verse ﴿whoever transgresses the limits of God﴾, because whoever bequeaths to an heir has given him more than God has prescribed for him, so it is a transgression of God's limits.

* A student: Some exegetes say that whoever obeys God and avoids the prohibitions will certainly enter Paradise?

* The Shaykh: He will certainly enter what?

* The student: Paradise.

* The Shaykh: Without doing an obligation?

* The student: No, if he does the obligations and abandons...

* The Shaykh: The prohibited acts.

* The student: Then he will certainly enter it. Is this statement correct?

* The Shaykh: A man said to the Prophet ﷺ: "O Messenger of God, what do you think? If I make lawful what is lawful and make unlawful what is unlawful, will I enter Paradise?" He said: "Yes."[[Reported by Muslim (1/15-16), from the hadith of Jabir.]] So if a person makes unlawful what is unlawful, makes lawful what is lawful, and does the obligations, he enters Paradise. But there are things that may prevent this. Does everyone who does the obligations do them as they should be done? There is much shortfall. For this reason the hadith says: "You receive from your prayer only what you understood of it: half of it, or a quarter, or a tenth."[[Reported by Ahmad (18894), from the hadith of ʿAmmar ibn Yasir, with similar wording.]] This indicates that a person may pray, and his prayer may be valid and discharge the obligation, but he does not obtain the reward.

* A student: The hadith of the Prophet ﷺ: "No one will enter Paradise by his deeds." They said: "Not even you?"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5673) and Muslim (2816/75), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] (...)?

* The Shaykh: The scholars said: regarding His saying ﴿as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [As-Sajdah 17], and the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "No one will enter Paradise by his deeds," the way to reconcile them is to take the bāʾ in ﴿as a reward for what they used to do﴾ as causal (sababiyyah), and to take the bāʾ in "No one will enter Paradise by his deeds" as an exchange (muʿāwaḍah) and substitution. If your deed were measured against the reward, the reward would encompass the deed and would not be commensurate with it. Moreover, God's enabling a person to do righteous deeds is a blessing that requires gratitude.

* A student: His saying, Most High: ﴿He will admit him to a Fire, abiding therein﴾: is "Fire" (nāran) indefinite?

* The Shaykh: And here ﴿Gardens﴾ [jannāt] is also indefinite.

* A student: Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah says that minor shirk falls under God's saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, God does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾. Is this correct?

* The Shaykh: He says: because ﴿an yushraka bihi﴾ is a verb preceded by the verbal particle (ḥarf maṣdarī), so it is interpreted as a verbal noun. How do you interpret it?

* A student: That God does not forgive associating [others] with Him?

* The Shaykh: "Associating [others] with Him" (ishrākan bihi). And "ishrākan" is indefinite in a negative context, so it is general. But I have some reservation about this.

* A student: Is minor shirk considered among the major sins?

* The Shaykh: Minor shirk is greater than the major sins. Ibn Masʿud, may God be pleased with him, said: "That I swear by God falsely is dearer to me than that I swear by other than Him truthfully."[[Reported by ʿAbd al-Razzaq (15929), from the hadith of Ibn Masʿud or Ibn ʿUmar.]]

* A student: O Shaykh, you said in explaining ﴿khālidan﴾ that a hadith reports that each of the people of the Fire is in a coffin being punished. How do we reconcile this with the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise: "Pour water upon us"﴾ [Al-A'raf 50], which indicates that they are groups of people?

* The Shaykh: Yes, there is no contradiction. We also made an exception earlier, saying: "Except that God wills," or a similar phrase.

* A student: O Shaykh, may God be good to you. Regarding the hadith of ʿAdi ibn Hatim in Imam Muslim's Sahih: "A man stood and gave a sermon before the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'Whoever obeys them both has been guided, and whoever disobeys them both has gone astray.' The Prophet ﷺ said to him: 'What a wretched speaker you are! Rather, say: Whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has gone astray.'"[[Reported by Muslim (870/48), from the hadith of ʿAdi ibn Hatim.]] Is there a contradiction between this, O Shaykh, and the verse? And why did the Prophet ﷺ reject this speaker's words?

* The Shaykh: The best that has been said in answer to this is: the Messenger ﷺ criticized him, not because the statement is forbidden, but because the occasion did not call for it. The occasion called for detailing and elaboration, because you may address people with such a statement and they will think that misguidance only occurs when the command comes from God and His Messenger. Every occasion has its own speech. The Messenger ﷺ only criticized him for not using the sermon in its appropriate context, not because this is prohibited, since the Messenger ﷺ himself said the same.

* A student: O Shaykh, may God be good to you, what have some scholars said about this phrase?

* The Shaykh: Which one?

* The student: "Whoever obeys God and His Messenger has been guided," where he said: "Whoever obeys God," and then said: the Prophet ﷺ only rejected it because he said: "Whoever obeys God and His Messenger has been guided, and whoever disobeys both of them," and he remained silent, then said: "has gone astray." So it is as if "disobeys both of them" became conjoined to "obeys"?

* The Shaykh: By God, this is far-fetched. It requires proof that he paused. Furthermore, if a person was silent and did not speak, and said: "and whoever disobeys both of them," then said: "has gone astray," it is understood that the latter follows from what came before.

* A student: There are some framed notices in some places on which is written "God, Muhammad." Is this...?

* The Shaykh: Yes, this is a mistake and it must be removed, because whoever does not know Muhammad ﷺ may think that these two are on the same level.

* A student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: Yes. No: Paradise and Hell are not like love. Paradise and Hell are something separate.

* The student: And fear, O Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: And fear. Fear cannot be defined.

* A student: Regarding a woman continuing her studies (...) higher degrees?

* The Shaykh: A woman is like a man in the religious sciences. But in other fields, such as engineering, mathematical sciences, and the like, we do not think she should continue, because this would compel her to take a job and come tomorrow to the plots of land designated for construction to measure and map them and so on.

* A student: What about medicine, O Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: No, medicine is a necessity. There is no harm in her studying medicine, because women are half of men, indeed more than men, and they fall ill often and need women (doctors).

* A student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: That is, if people praise a person, he is pleased. No, this does not contradict good intention. A person loves to be praised by himself and loves for people to praise him. ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, when his son ʿAbdullah said, when the Prophet ﷺ presented them with the tree: "It is a tree whose likeness is that of the believer," and people disputed which tree it was, it came to his heart that it was the palm tree, but he did not speak because he was young. ʿUmar said: "If you had said it, it would have been such and such."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (131) and Muslim (2811/63), from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar.]] That is, something one is pleased with. This is not a problem. "Whoever is pleased by his good deed and saddened by his bad deed, that is a believer." This also, the praise of people for a person, is among the early glad tidings of the believer: ﴿For them are good tidings in the worldly life and in the Hereafter﴾ [Yunus 64]. The forms of glad tidings are many. Among them: good true dreams seen by a righteous man; among them: that he sees the effect of obedience on his heart as light and expansion; and among them: that people praise him and he is accepted. The forms of glad tidings are many.

* A student: May God be good to you. If a faculty member at the university says: "If the university had not forced me to research and write a thesis, I would not have researched it, knowing that its benefit is small," does this indicate soundness of intention?

* The Shaykh: Yes, because he wants to reach this degree which qualifies him for the position through which he wishes to benefit people. Much of university knowledge is not something a person would want for its own sake.

* A student: (...) in this nation, will he not think about it?

* The Shaykh: Think about what?

* The student: He thinks about a project.

* The Shaykh: A good project. This is a sincere intention.

* A student: (...) and does he intend nearness to God?

* The Shaykh: What do you say about this? A person worships God in order to attain knowledge, because God says: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance﴾ [Muhammad 17]. Is that right? We say: yes, this is a good intention. The evidence for this is that God loves righteous deeds: ﴿We will surely give him a good life﴾ [An-Nahl 97], and that He has set the legal limits (ḥudūd), the legal punishments, for the one who commits wrongdoing. Likewise, if an adulterer, for example, abandons adultery out of fear of God, but his fear of the legal punishment also influences his abstention, there is no harm.

* A student: He did not intend the face of God, especially knowledge, the attainment of knowledge?

* The Shaykh: Knowledge itself is an act of worship. Knowledge itself is an act of worship.

* * *

Shaykh Ibn 'Uthaymin's commentary on Surah an-Nisa', verses 13–14 (part 3 of 3):

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿And those of your women who commit immorality, bring against them four witnesses from among you. And if they testify, then confine them to their houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them a way.﴾ [15] ﴿And the two of you who commit it, harm them both. And if they repent and amend, then leave them alone. Indeed, Allah is ever Accepting of repentance and Merciful.﴾ [16] ﴿Indeed, the acceptance of repentance is only for those who do wrong out of ignorance and then repent soon. Those are the ones to whom Allah will return in forgiveness, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ [An-Nisa' 15–17].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And those of your women who commit immorality, bring against them four witnesses from among you.﴾ ﴿Wa-allati﴾ is the plural of (allati).

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits – He will admit him to a Fire, wherein he will abide eternally, and for him is a humiliating punishment.﴾

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the division of the one who opposes into one who disobeys (ʿasin) and one who transgresses the limits (mutaʿaddin lil-hudud). Disobedience here is the commission of what is forbidden, while transgressing the limits is the abandonment of an obligation or excess in it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that disobedience to the Messenger is like disobedience to Allah, since He linked it with disobedience to Allah by a particle that implies equality.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that whoever combines both matters, disobedience and transgression of the limits, will enter the Fire. But is his entry eternal or temporary? It is said: it depends on the disobedience. For Allah mentioned in the preceding verses that whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger enters the Gardens, and here He said: whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger enters the Fire. So it is said: the one whose obedience predominates enters the Garden without entering the Fire, and the one whose disobedience predominates enters it; the predominant one, if there is some obedience in him, enters the Fire (...). The one who combines obedience and disobedience enters both the Fire and the Garden, because in him are found the causes of entering both, and he is given the judgment of ﴿a recompense in accordance [with their deeds]﴾ [An-Naba' 26]. On this basis, the one who is absolutely disobedient and the one who absolutely transgresses the limits enter the Fire and do not enter the Garden, while the one who combines disobedience and obedience: if obedience prevails, he does not enter the Fire; if disobedience prevails, he enters the Fire according to the measure of his sin and comes out of it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of eternal abiding in the Fire, by His saying ﴿wherein he will abide eternally﴾. Allah the Exalted has stated that eternal abiding in the Fire is everlasting in three verses of the Qur'an: in Surah an-Nisa', in Surah al-Ahzab, and in Surah al-Jinn. In Surah an-Nisa' Allah says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and do wrong – Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path, except the path of Hell, abiding therein forever. And that is ever easy for Allah.﴾ [168–169]. In Surah al-Ahzab Allah the Blessed and Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blaze, abiding therein forever; they will not find any protector or helper.﴾ [64–65]. In Surah al-Jinn He says: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger – then indeed, for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever.﴾ [23]. Since Allah has mentioned everlastingness in three verses, any statement that contradicts this is invalid, because eternal abiding entails the permanence of the place. If it is said: "This one abides in the Fire forever," it necessarily follows that the place in which he abides is what? Everlasting; otherwise there would be no meaning to "forever." Therefore the saying of some scholars that they abide therein forever only as long as it remains is an invalid view with no basis in reasoning, because Allah has explicitly stated everlastingness – the everlastingness of abiding – and the everlastingness of abiding necessarily entails the everlastingness of the place, otherwise there would be no benefit.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that those in the Fire – and we seek refuge in Allah – are punished with a humiliating punishment, i.e., one that involves humiliation; they are not honored.

If someone says: How do you reconcile this verse with the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Then pour over his head the torment of boiling water. "Taste it; indeed, you were the mighty, the noble."﴾ [Ad-Dukhan 48–49]? The answer is one of two possibilities: either it is said to him in mockery, or it is said to recall his condition in the world, meaning: you were the mighty, the noble in the world, so that his regret increases, since he was mighty and noble in the world and is now humiliated and abased. Both of these – and we seek refuge in Allah – apply to the one to whom this address is directed: boiling water is poured over his head, and then it is said: ﴿Taste it; indeed, you were the mighty, the noble.﴾ Undoubtedly he will understand that it is said to him in mockery, and he will also recall his condition in the world, that he was honored and mighty in the world, and now he has reached this degree of humiliation.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verses 15–16 (part 1 of 2):**

Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And those of your women who commit lewdness, bring against them four witnesses from among you.﴾ ﴿Al-lati﴾ (those who, the relative pronoun) is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is the clause ﴿fastashhidu﴾ (then bring as witnesses). Here one asks: why is the particle (fa') attached to the predicate of the subject?

The answer: since the subject is a relative noun (ism mawsul), it resembles the conditional noun (ism al-shart) in generality, so it is given its ruling, and the fa' is attached to its predicate. Among the examples is the grammarians' well-known illustration: "Whoever comes to me, for him is a dirham." This is equivalent to your saying: "Whoever comes to me, for him is a dirham." Since the relative noun resembles the conditional noun in generality, the entry of fa' into its predicate is like the entry of fa' into the response of the condition.

As for His words ﴿allati ya'tina al-fahisha﴾ (those who commit lewdness): ﴿Al-lati﴾ is a plural. The plural of what? It is the plural of ﴿allati﴾ (the feminine singular), but it is irregular, because these words are not derived forms.

His words ﴿ya'tina al-fahisha﴾: al-fahisha (lewdness) is that which is considered shameful (yustafhash). That which is shameful is so in the Sharia and in custom. What is shameful in the Sharia is shameful in custom, in the customs of Muslims, not in the customs of non-Muslims. We specified this because adultery is shameful in the Sharia, and shameful by custom. By whose custom?
* Students: Of the Muslims.
* Shaykh: But by the custom of the disbelievers it is not shameful. From here we know that the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "Sin is that which troubles your soul and you dislike that people should see it"[[Recorded by Muslim (2553/15) from the hadith of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an.]] is specific to whom? To the Muslim who dislikes sin and fears that people will see him in a state of sinning. Otherwise, the disbeliever's soul is not troubled by sin.

His words ﴿al-fahisha﴾: what is meant by al-fahisha here? Its meaning is that which is shameful, that which is considered shameful by the Sharia and by custom. What is intended is adultery. The evidence is His saying: ﴿And do not approach adultery; indeed it is an indecency and an evil way﴾ [al-Isra' 32]. On this basis, the article (al-) is for the mental reference (al-'ahd al-dhihni), because it was not mentioned explicitly but is known in the Sharia. We have established this to refute the view of someone like Abu Muslim al-Khurasani, who said that what is meant is sahq (lesbianism between women). But this is far from correct, and, as far as we know, none of the Companions or the Successors held it. The correct view is that what is meant by al-fahisha is what? Adultery, and the evidence is ﴿And do not approach adultery; indeed it is an indecency﴾.

His words ﴿min nisa'ikum﴾ (from among your women): what is meant is the category, i.e., the category of women, whether they are our wives or not our wives. His words ﴿min nisa'ikum﴾: this ﴿min﴾ (from) is an explanation of the relative noun in His words ﴿allati ya'tina al-fahisha﴾.

﴿fastashhidu 'alayhinna arba'atan minkum﴾ (then bring against them four witnesses from among you): ﴿istashhidu﴾ means: seek the testimony of four. And ﴿arba'atan﴾ here is a number which indicates that the counted items are masculine. What is its reason?
* A student: The accusative of ﴿arba'atan﴾.
* Shaykh: The accusative of ﴿arba'atan﴾. That is, if it had come in the nominative, it would not have indicated that the counted items are masculine?
* Student: (...)
* Shaykh: Because a feminine number, below ten, takes a masculine counted noun. You say: "tis'atu rijal" (nine men) and "tis'u nisa'" (nine women). Is it clear?

﴿arba'atan﴾. His words ﴿arba'atan minkum﴾: the address is to the Muslims, because a condition of testimony, especially in this grave matter, is that the witness be a Muslim.

﴿fa-in shahidu﴾ means: if they testify to the commission of the lewdness. ﴿fa-amsikuhunna fi al-buyuti hatta yatawaffahunna al-mawtu aw yaj'ala Allahu lahunna sabilan﴾ (then confine them to their houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them a way). ﴿amsikuhunna fi al-buyut﴾: the address here, ﴿amsikuhunna﴾, is general, so who is it aimed at? It is aimed at the ruler (wali al-amr). The ruler is either a specific ruler or a general one.

His words ﴿amsikuhunna fi al-buyut﴾: ﴿buyut﴾ is the plural of ﴿bayt﴾ (house). That is: keep them in their house, confine them, do not let them go out, because that is a means of reducing adultery, since they remain confined in their house and do not go out, so they do not tempt people and are not tempted.

﴿hatta yatawaffahunna al-mawtu﴾ (until death takes them): ﴿yatawaffahunna﴾ (...). It is said: "tawaffaytu haqqi min fulan," meaning: I received my right from so-and-so. His words ﴿al-mawt﴾ (death) mean the Angel of Death, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: The Angel of Death who is charged with you will take you﴾ [as-Sajdah 11], but it is expressed by "death" in a broad sense. ﴿hatta yatawaffahunna al-mawtu﴾: death is the loss of life, and that is by the departure of the soul from the body, because the soul is a loan within the body; whenever it is called, it departs.

﴿aw yaj'ala Allahu lahunna sabilan﴾ (or Allah ordains for them a way): ﴿aw﴾ is a conjunction particle, and ﴿yaj'ala﴾ is conjoined to ﴿yatawaffa﴾ (...), so it is in the subjunctive. ﴿yaj'ala Allahu lahunna sabilan﴾ means: it becomes for them a way, i.e., a path to deliverance from this confinement. Allah has ordained for them a way by what? By His saying: ﴿The adulterous woman and the adulterous man—flog each one of them a hundred lashes﴾ [an-Nur 2]. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Take from me, take from me. Allah has ordained for them a way: the virgin with the virgin, a hundred lashes and exile for a year; and the married with the married, a hundred lashes and stoning."[[Recorded by Muslim (1690/12) from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit.]] Thus it becomes clear that what is meant by "the way" is what Allah has legislated as the punishment for the adulterer: flogging and exile, or stoning and exile.

Then He said: ﴿And the two of you who commit it from among you, harm them both﴾. ﴿Alladhani﴾ (the two who) corresponds to ﴿allati﴾. Is it for males or for females? It is for males. But the correspondence is not complete: here He said ﴿alladhani﴾, and there He said ﴿allati﴾. Why? Some scholars said: what is meant by ﴿alladhani﴾ here is the adulterer and the adulteress. But the ruling for the adulteress has already been stated, that she is confined to the house, while the adulterer is harmed, and [the ruling] ... (...) in the house. Other scholars said: what is meant by the two is the sodomite, i.e., the active and the passive partner. He attributed the act (ityan) to the passive partner, although he is the one acted upon, because the one who receives it, the consenting one, is like the doer. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever you find doing the deed of the people of Lot, kill the doer and the one it is done to."[[Recorded by Abu Dawud (4462) and al-Tirmidhi (1456) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] The correct view is this: the correct view is that ﴿alladhani﴾ refers to the two who commit sodomy, a man who sodomizes a man, and we seek refuge in Allah.

But there remains another consideration: why did He use the feminine plural for women and the dual for men? Because the spread of adultery among women is greater than the spread of sodomy among men. In the time of ignorance (jahiliyyah) they did not know of sodomy. Some even say: "If Allah had not related to us what He related of the story of the people of Lot, we would never have imagined that this would happen, because who could imagine that a man would consent to be treated as a woman is treated! This is impossible by nature and impossible by the Sharia." Therefore He expressed sodomy with the least number by which it can be realized. What is the least number by which it can be realized? Two. Unlike adultery among women, which is common.

﴿And the two of you who commit it from among you﴾: the pronoun in ﴿ya'tiyanaha﴾ refers to ﴿al-fahisha﴾ (lewdness), and the lewdness of men is sodomy, which is greater than the sin of adultery. The evidence of its greatness is that Lot said to his people: ﴿Do you commit the lewdness?﴾ [al-A'raf 80]. Regarding adultery, Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Indeed it is an indecency﴾ [al-Isra' 32], among the indecencies. As for this, He said ﴿al-fahisha﴾ (the lewdness), because it is—we seek refuge in Allah—considered repugnant in the mind of every person. Furthermore, the category of adultery may be permitted by a contract, but sodomy is never permitted under any circumstances, neither by contract nor otherwise, so it is more heinous.

﴿And the two of you who commit it from among you, harm them both﴾: harm them with what? With reviling, reproach, beating, and shunning, by way of discipline (ta'zir), boycott, and similar things. The point is, do whatever they will be harmed by.

﴿fa-in taba wa-aslaha fa-a'ridu 'anhuma﴾ (if they repent and amend, then leave them alone): ﴿in taba﴾ means repentance from what has occurred between them. ﴿wa-aslaha﴾ means amending their conduct in the future. ﴿fa-a'ridu 'anhuma﴾ (then leave them alone) is because the one who repents of a sin is like one who has no sin, so one turns away from him. Since the cause remains, the effect follows it; when the cause is removed, the effect is removed.

﴿inna Allaha kana tawwaban rahiman﴾ (indeed Allah is ever Oft-Returning, Most Merciful). ﴿inna Allaha kana tawwaban﴾: ﴿tawwaban﴾ is an intensive form, because of His great acceptance of repentance and the great number of those to whom He grants repentance. Those whom Allah grants repentance cannot be counted, and His repentance, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be enumerated; therefore He used the intensive form. And who is the one who repents? Allah's granting of repentance to the servant is of two kinds: a repentance before the servant's act of repenting, and a repentance after it. The repentance that comes before the servant's act of repenting means divine enablement (tawfiq), i.e., enabling him to repent, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then He turned to them that they might repent﴾ [at-Tawbah 118]. The repentance that comes after the servant's repentance is the acceptance of repentance, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾ [ash-Shura 25]. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is Tawwab in both senses: He is one who enables repentance for whomever He wills of His servants, and He is one who accepts repentance.

﴿Rahiman﴾ means: possessor of mercy, which He conveys to whomever He wills of His servants, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-'Ankabut 21].

In this verse there is some difficulty: His words ﴿kana tawwaban rahiman﴾. It is known that ﴿kana﴾ indicates the past, and it is understood from it that this attribute was and then ceased, as if you said: "Such-and-such was a student of knowledge," meaning in the past.

The scholars answered this difficulty by saying that ﴿kana﴾ may be stripped of its indication of time, and what is meant by it is the actual realization of the predicate's attribute. Everything attributed to Allah in this construction is meant in this sense: ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾ [an-Nisa' 23]; ﴿And Allah is ever Competent over all things﴾ [al-Ahzab 27]; ﴿And Allah is ever Encompassing of all things﴾ [al-Ahzab 126], and similar. What is meant is that He is characterized by it eternally, without beginning or end, but ﴿kana﴾ came to affirm the realization of His being characterized by this attribute.

* Student: May Allah reward you well. ﴿fa-a'ridu 'anhuma﴾: is this before having power over them or after having power over them?
* Shaykh: No, after having power over them.
* Student: After having power over them?
* Shaykh: Yes, but this ruling will be discussed, God willing.
* Student: The saying of the Exalted in Surah Hud: ﴿Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾ [Hud 107] (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, ﴿a gift uninterrupted﴾. And regarding the Fire He said: ﴿Indeed your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends﴾.
* Student: (...) ﴿abiding therein﴾.
* Shaykh: All of it, He said: ﴿as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾ [Hud 107].
* Student: What is the difference?
* Shaykh: The difference is that since this is a bounty, He clarified that it is an extended bounty. And since that is a punishment, He said: ﴿Indeed your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends﴾, so He carries out this punishment, because that is what His will requires.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon after. Those—Allah will turn to them in forgiveness; and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise. And repentance is not [accepted] from those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have now repented," nor from those who die while they are disbelievers. For those We have prepared a painful punishment. O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion, nor to make difficulties for them that you may take back part of what you gave them unless they commit a clear immorality. And live with them in kindness. And if you dislike them—perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good﴾ [an-Nisa' 17–19].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. We have previously stated that Allah the Exalted made the punishment of women who commit adultery what?
* Student: By bringing witnesses against them.
* Shaykh: No, the witnessing is for establishing...
* Student: ﴿fa-amsikuhunna fi al-buyuti hatta yatawaffahunna al-mawtu aw yaj'ala Allahu lahunna sabilan﴾.
* Shaykh: Correct. What is the way that Allah has ordained for them?
* Student: The saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah has ordained for them."
* Shaykh: In the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit.
* Student: (...)
* Shaykh: "Take from me, take from me, Allah has ordained for them."
* Student: "The virgin with the virgin: a year's flogging and a year's exile."
* Shaykh: A year's flogging?!
* Student: "A hundred lashes and a year's exile, and the married with the married: a hundred lashes and stoning."[[Recorded by Muslim (1690/12) from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit.]]
* Shaykh: Well done.

Does this count as abrogation (naskh)?
* Student: It is not abrogation.
* Shaykh: Why?
* Student: This is the way that He ordained.
* Shaykh: Yes, but why?
* Student: Because this (...).
* Shaykh: Yes. The first ruling was temporary, not general for all times, so His saying ﴿fa-amsikuhunna fi al-buyut﴾ is an explanation of that.

His words ﴿wa-allatani ya'tiyanaha minkum﴾: what is meant by it?
* Student: It was said: the one who commits adultery with her, the adulterer. And it was said: the sodomite.
* Shaykh: It was said: it is the man who sodomizes a man.
* Student: And it was said: the one who has intercourse with a woman.
* Shaykh: Yes. Based on the second view, how does ﴿allatani ya'tiyanaha minkum﴾ work out?
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: That is, there is an opinion that ﴿allatani ya'tiyanaha minkum﴾ means: the two who commit adultery.
* Student: Yes, Shaykh. Then the man is only harmed, while the woman is confined and harmed.
* Shaykh: She is confined until death takes her or Allah ordains for them a way.
* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Adultery among women is more common than among men, for prostitutes were numerous and widespread in the time of ignorance.

On the view that what is meant by ﴿allatani ya'tiyanaha minkum﴾ is a man who sodomizes a man, how is it valid for the one who is acted upon to be the one who acts?
* Student: Since the one acted upon consents, his ruling is like the ruling of the doer.
* Shaykh: Well done. The one who receives it is like the doer.

I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those of your women who commit lewdness...﴾ to the end.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the gravity of adultery, and that it is among the indecencies, since there is agreement that what is meant is adultery. The view that it refers to lesbianism is a weak opinion on which no reliance can be placed.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: that adultery requires the testimony of four upright men, because of His saying ﴿fastashhidu 'alayhinna arba'atan﴾. And His saying ﴿minkum﴾ (from among you) is addressed to the believers, and the Companions were all upright. Or we say that ﴿minkum﴾ is addressed to all the Companions, and this unqualified term is understood as meaning uprightness ('adalah), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And bring to witness two just men from among you﴾ [at-Talaq 2].
* From the benefits of this noble verse: an indication that a man is stronger and more reliable than a woman as a witness, because Allah the Exalted did not require, for adultery, any testimony except that of men.
* From it: that the prescribed punishment (hadd) is averted by doubt (shubhah), because requiring four men is for the sake of establishing the testimony, and the testimony of the four women involves doubt, since they have not been established as witnesses, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So that if one of them errs, the other will remind her﴾ [al-Baqarah 282]. And there is no doubt that the prescribed punishments are averted by doubts.

I need to translate this carefully. Here is the translation.

But there remains with us the criterion of the ruling: what is the doubt (shubha) by which the hadd punishment is averted? Among the scholars there are those who broadened it to the point of saying: if a man hires a woman for fornication and then commits zina with her, there is no hadd upon him, because his hiring her is a doubt, just as if he hired a house to live in. Among the scholars there are those who took a middle position, and those who were strict. Generally, when opinions differ into three, the middle one is the correct one; this is the general rule.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: there must be explicit testimony by the witnesses to the testimony in matters of zina, due to His saying: ﴿then if they testify﴾. For this reason the witnesses must say: "We saw his member entering her private part, just as the kohl stick enters the kohl pot." It does not suffice for the witnesses to say: "We saw a man on a woman while they were naked, and we saw his member between her thighs." This is not sufficient; there must be explicit mention of intercourse, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Ma'iz, when he said: "Did you penetrate her?" — not using euphemism, or he said: "Do not use euphemism."[[Reported by al-Bukhari (6824) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] For this reason Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him) said in his time: the hadd for zina has not been established by testimony until our day; it has not been established by testimony. Why? Because it is difficult, very difficult.

If someone says: Can we establish it by photographs? We say: We used to say so, but when we became aware of the forging (dablaja) of photographers, we said: we do not establish it. Do you know what dablaja is? That is, they combine and fabricate a picture and make a man on a woman as though he had intercourse with her, when that is not the case. The problem with this forgery—we ask Allah to spare us its evil—is that they have begun to forge speech now, as I have been told. They take, for example, a letter from my speech, a letter from one word, and a letter from another word, and they assemble some parts upon others and produce a sermon in my voice according to what they want. Do you understand? They gather letters, then shape them into words as they wish, while the voice is my voice and the intonations are my intonations. This is truly a problem: any person who wants to attribute false words to someone can now do so. We hope that Allah will send a virus against these machines, just as they now threaten with computer viruses, so that we and people may be saved from their evil.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: confining the woman to her house is among the causes of averting fitnah, due to His saying: ﴿keep them confined﴾, because this is a kind of punishment in one respect and a restraint against the causes of fitnah in another respect.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: an indication that the house is better for the woman, due to His saying: ﴿keep them confined in the houses﴾, and as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Their houses are better for them."[[Reported by Abu Dawud (5468) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]]

* Among its benefits: it is not permissible to confine a woman in her house in such a way that she is prevented from going out, except when there is fitnah and evil. Otherwise the default is that she is not prevented from leaving the house. This is supported by the fact that Allah the Exalted obligated the widow to remain in her house, which indicates that others are not obligated to remain in the house. That is so; so we should encourage women to remain in the house, but we do not compel them to do so.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the legitimacy of punishment by lifelong imprisonment. Do you agree with this, or is there a basis for punishment by lifelong imprisonment?

* Students: The second.

* The Shaykh: The second is closer to the truth: there is a basis for punishment by lifelong imprisonment in the Shari'ah. As for making it a legislated ruling when it has been abrogated, there is some reservation in the soul about it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of ja'l (making/appointing) for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, due to His saying: ﴿or Allah appoints for them a way﴾. Ja'l is of two kinds: legislative ja'l (ja'l shar'i) and cosmic, decreed ja'l (ja'l kawni qadari). Examples of legislative ja'l include His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a means of establishment for the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah 97], and His saying: ﴿Allah has not instituted any bahirah, sa'ibah, wasilah, or ham﴾ [al-Ma'idah 103]. ﴿Has not instituted﴾ means legislative ja'l; as for decreed ja'l, He has indeed made that: the bahirah, sa'ibah, wasilah and ham do exist. Examples of cosmic ja'l are numerous in the Qur'an, such as: ﴿We made your sleep a rest (9), and We made the night a covering (10), and We made the day a means of livelihood﴾ [al-Naba' 9-11], and the examples are many.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of voluntary actions (al-af'al al-ikhtiyariyyah) of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; that is, affirming the attribute of renewed action for Allah. Know that an action attributed to Allah is of three types: genus (jins), species (naw'), and individual instance (fard).

As for the genus, it is an eternal, everlasting attribute: Allah has always been and always will be an Doer; He is an Doer in eternity past just as He is an Doer in eternity future. For this reason the preponderant of the scholars' opinions is that events are a continuous succession in the past just as they are in the future. However, we do not know what has succeeded in the past except what He has informed us of. Apart from that, we believe that Allah has always been and always will be an Doer, glorified and exalted is He.

The second: the species type. The species type is like the istiwa' (establishment) upon the Throne, and this is originated; Allah did not establish upon the Throne before creating the Throne.

As for the individual type, it is numerous, such as descending to the lowest heaven every night, coming to judge between the servants, descending to the lowest heaven on the evening of 'Arafah, anger when its cause exists, pleasure when its cause exists, laughter when its cause exists, and wonder when its cause exists; many things. Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah affirmed this, while the Ash'aris, the Mu'tazilah and those who follow their path denied it and said: it is impossible for Allah to be described by any originated attribute at all. For this reason they regard the Qur'an in our hands as eternal. They justified this corrupt ruling by saying: the subsistence of originated events in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, necessitates that He be originated, because originated events subsist only in something originated. Undoubtedly this is a sickly, indeed dead, reason. Who told them this?! Rather, the fact that originated events subsist in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that He does what He wills, is evidence of His perfection and the perfection of His life. If a person conceived of a lord who does not act and a lord who acts, the dictate of human nature would be that the second is more perfect, without doubt. So the correct view, without doubt, is that the actions of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, are, as they are a genus, also a species and individual instances.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those two of you who commit it, harm them. And if they repent and amend, then leave them alone. Indeed, Allah is ever Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾.

* It is derived from this noble verse that sodomy (liwat) has two rulings: the first ruling is what the verse indicates, and the second ruling is what the Sunnah indicates. As for what the verse indicates, it is that the man who commits this abomination is to be harmed: harmed by speech, harmed by action, harmed by shunning, harmed with various kinds of harm. Many people may find the harm to them more severe than beating them or imprisoning them.

As for the second ruling, established in the Sunnah, it is the killing of both the doer and the one done to: due to the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Whoever you find doing the deed of the people of Lut, kill the doer and the one done to."[[Reported by Muslim (1690/12) from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit.]]

Here the absolute (mutlaq) is not to be read in light of the restricted (muqayyad), so as to say: "Kill the doer and the one done to if they are married (muhsan)," as is the case with zina. This is because one of the conditions for applying the absolute to the restricted is that the ruling and the cause be the same, and here the cause and the ruling differ. In zina the cause is intercourse in a private part that is permissible in general—correct?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: When is it permissible? By a valid marriage contract or by ownership of the right hand. But this is a sexual use of a private part that is never permissible at all. Likewise, this abomination—and we seek refuge in Allah—is difficult to guard against, unlike zina, because it occurs among males, and who can confine males from one another? It is impossible to confine them; guarding against it is difficult. If it has no strong deterrent punishment, it spreads in society, and when it spreads in society men and women are corrupted—we ask Allah for well-being—because among the consequences for the one who commits liwat is that he no longer desires women. If he no longer desires women, women are left idle and evil and corruption ensues.

The evidence that among the consequences for the one who commits liwat is that the desire for women is removed from him is the statement of Lut to his people: ﴿Do you approach the males of all the worlds, and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses?﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 165-166]. They only left women because the desire for women had been stripped from their souls; otherwise a person by his nature inclines toward women. When this punishment spreads in society, it is corrupted: its men and women are corrupted and its interests are paralyzed. Therefore wisdom requires eliminating this corrupt germ, by killing. This absolute should not be read in light of the restricted, for the reason you know: the cause and the ruling differ.

Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him) mentioned that the Companions unanimously agreed on killing the doer and the one done to, though they differed about the manner of killing: some said they should be thrown from the highest place in the city and then stoned with rocks; some said they should be stoned; and some said the sodomite, both the doer and the one done to, should be burned, because their crime is grave and abominable. Lut called it "al-fahishah" (the abomination), and in the Book of Allah zina is also called so: ﴿Indeed, it was an abomination﴾ [al-Isra' 32]. The first is more severe.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever repents and amends, it is obligatory to refrain from punishing him. Allah the Exalted has stated explicitly in the verse about the muharibun in Surah al-Ma'idah that this is conditional upon repenting before you have power over them. He said: ﴿except those who repent before you gain power over them. So know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ma'idah 34]. But if he repents after power is gained over him, the punishment is not lifted from him.

Yet what appears from the Sunnah is that whoever has been established by confession and then repents is left to repent. The evidence for this is the hadith of Ma'iz ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) when he came to the Prophet (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) and confessed zina in his presence, so he ordered his stoning. When the stones touched him—that is, the stones reached him—he fled. But the Companions, because the Messenger (ﷺ) had ordered his stoning, said: the Messenger's command must be carried out, so they carried out the stoning, then informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of that. He said: "Why did you not leave him to repent, so that Allah might accept his repentance?"[[Reported by Abu Dawud (4419), and Ibn Abi Shaybah (29257), the wording being his, from the hadith of Na'im ibn Hazzal.]] This indicates that one who confesses a sin and repents, even during the execution of the hadd, is left to repent, and Allah accepts his repentance.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: repentance from sin must be accompanied by amendment (islah), due to His saying: ﴿if they repent and amend﴾. But how is repentance in such a case? It was said: repentance in such a case is that he is solicited and refuses, do you understand? For example, it is said to the one done to: "We want to do this to you," and if he refuses, that indicates his repentance. And it is said to the doer: "This one wants you to do it to him," and if he declines, that is his repentance. The same is said of the male and female fornicator. But this view is a objectionable opinion, far from the truth, because solicitation occurs only in private, is that not so? It is not that one solicits a person in front of people; it would be in a private situation.

Furthermore, if the one soliciting is capable of the act, meaning it is expected of him that he would do it, he may well be accommodated, and then the abomination occurs. And if the one soliciting is not capable of doing it, the one solicited will realize that this one wants to test him, and he refuses. From this we know that this view has no basis in soundness. Rather, repentance from this is like repentance from other sins: when we know that the man has turned away from this matter and no longer goes to gatherings where this abomination takes place and the like, we know he has repented. For this reason repentance is here paired with amendment, so there must be something that shows he has repented, namely correcting his conduct and keeping far from this abomination.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation that a ruling revolves around its cause, existence and non-existence. Its basis is His saying: ﴿if they repent and amend, then leave them alone﴾. Therefore, when the cause ceases, the ruling ceases. That is so: the ruling revolves around its effective cause (illah), existence and non-existence. However, if the cause is stated explicitly, when it is absent the ruling must be absent; but if the cause is inferred (mustanbatah), the ruling should not be dropped merely because the inferred cause is absent, because it is possible that the legislated cause is not this inferred one, and we would thereby nullify a ruling of Allah established merely by possibility. But if the cause is explicitly stated, the ruling revolves with it, as in His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "If there are three of you, two should not confide in each other to the exclusion of the third, because that would grieve him."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6290) and Muslim (2184/37) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]] This indicates that if the private conversation would not grieve him, it would be permissible.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, At-Tawwab (the Accepting of repentance) and Ar-Rahim (the Merciful). We have already explained the meaning of At-Tawwab and why it came in the intensive form, and the meaning of Ar-Rahim.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verses 15–16 (part 1 of 2):**

Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And those of your women who commit lewdness, bring against them four witnesses from among you.﴾ ﴿Al-lati﴾ (those who, the relative pronoun) is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is the clause ﴿fastashhidu﴾ (then bring as witnesses). Here one asks: why is the particle (fa') attached to the predicate of the subject?

The answer: since the subject is a relative noun (ism mawsul), it resembles the conditional noun (ism al-shart) in generality, so it is given its ruling, and the fa' is attached to its predicate. Among the examples is the grammarians' well-known illustration: "Whoever comes to me, for him is a dirham." This is equivalent to your saying: "Whoever comes to me, for him is a dirham." Since the relative noun resembles the conditional noun in generality, the entry of fa' into its predicate is like the entry of fa' into the response of the condition.

As for His words ﴿allati ya'tina al-fahisha﴾ (those who commit lewdness): ﴿Al-lati﴾ is a plural. The plural of what? It is the plural of ﴿allati﴾ (the feminine singular), but it is irregular, because these words are not derived forms.

His words ﴿ya'tina al-fahisha﴾: al-fahisha (lewdness) is that which is considered shameful (yustafhash). That which is shameful is so in the Sharia and in custom. What is shameful in the Sharia is shameful in custom, in the customs of Muslims, not in the customs of non-Muslims. We specified this because adultery is shameful in the Sharia, and shameful by custom. By whose custom?
* Students: Of the Muslims.
* Shaykh: But by the custom of the disbelievers it is not shameful. From here we know that the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "Sin is that which troubles your soul and you dislike that people should see it"[[Recorded by Muslim (2553/15) from the hadith of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an.]] is specific to whom? To the Muslim who dislikes sin and fears that people will see him in a state of sinning. Otherwise, the disbeliever's soul is not troubled by sin.

His words ﴿al-fahisha﴾: what is meant by al-fahisha here? Its meaning is that which is shameful, that which is considered shameful by the Sharia and by custom. What is intended is adultery. The evidence is His saying: ﴿And do not approach adultery; indeed it is an indecency and an evil way﴾ [al-Isra' 32]. On this basis, the article (al-) is for the mental reference (al-'ahd al-dhihni), because it was not mentioned explicitly but is known in the Sharia. We have established this to refute the view of someone like Abu Muslim al-Khurasani, who said that what is meant is sahq (lesbianism between women). But this is far from correct, and, as far as we know, none of the Companions or the Successors held it. The correct view is that what is meant by al-fahisha is what? Adultery, and the evidence is ﴿And do not approach adultery; indeed it is an indecency﴾.

His words ﴿min nisa'ikum﴾ (from among your women): what is meant is the category, i.e., the category of women, whether they are our wives or not our wives. His words ﴿min nisa'ikum﴾: this ﴿min﴾ (from) is an explanation of the relative noun in His words ﴿allati ya'tina al-fahisha﴾.

﴿fastashhidu 'alayhinna arba'atan minkum﴾ (then bring against them four witnesses from among you): ﴿istashhidu﴾ means: seek the testimony of four. And ﴿arba'atan﴾ here is a number which indicates that the counted items are masculine. What is its reason?
* A student: The accusative of ﴿arba'atan﴾.
* Shaykh: The accusative of ﴿arba'atan﴾. That is, if it had come in the nominative, it would not have indicated that the counted items are masculine?
* Student: (...)
* Shaykh: Because a feminine number, below ten, takes a masculine counted noun. You say: "tis'atu rijal" (nine men) and "tis'u nisa'" (nine women). Is it clear?

﴿arba'atan﴾. His words ﴿arba'atan minkum﴾: the address is to the Muslims, because a condition of testimony, especially in this grave matter, is that the witness be a Muslim.

﴿fa-in shahidu﴾ means: if they testify to the commission of the lewdness. ﴿fa-amsikuhunna fi al-buyuti hatta yatawaffahunna al-mawtu aw yaj'ala Allahu lahunna sabilan﴾ (then confine them to their houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them a way). ﴿amsikuhunna fi al-buyut﴾: the address here, ﴿amsikuhunna﴾, is general, so who is it aimed at? It is aimed at the ruler (wali al-amr). The ruler is either a specific ruler or a general one.

His words ﴿amsikuhunna fi al-buyut﴾: ﴿buyut﴾ is the plural of ﴿bayt﴾ (house). That is: keep them in their house, confine them, do not let them go out, because that is a means of reducing adultery, since they remain confined in their house and do not go out, so they do not tempt people and are not tempted.

﴿hatta yatawaffahunna al-mawtu﴾ (until death takes them): ﴿yatawaffahunna﴾ (...). It is said: "tawaffaytu haqqi min fulan," meaning: I received my right from so-and-so. His words ﴿al-mawt﴾ (death) mean the Angel of Death, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: The Angel of Death who is charged with you will take you﴾ [as-Sajdah 11], but it is expressed by "death" in a broad sense. ﴿hatta yatawaffahunna al-mawtu﴾: death is the loss of life, and that is by the departure of the soul from the body, because the soul is a loan within the body; whenever it is called, it departs.

﴿aw yaj'ala Allahu lahunna sabilan﴾ (or Allah ordains for them a way): ﴿aw﴾ is a conjunction particle, and ﴿yaj'ala﴾ is conjoined to ﴿yatawaffa﴾ (...), so it is in the subjunctive. ﴿yaj'ala Allahu lahunna sabilan﴾ means: it becomes for them a way, i.e., a path to deliverance from this confinement. Allah has ordained for them a way by what? By His saying: ﴿The adulterous woman and the adulterous man—flog each one of them a hundred lashes﴾ [an-Nur 2]. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Take from me, take from me. Allah has ordained for them a way: the virgin with the virgin, a hundred lashes and exile for a year; and the married with the married, a hundred lashes and stoning."[[Recorded by Muslim (1690/12) from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit.]] Thus it becomes clear that what is meant by "the way" is what Allah has legislated as the punishment for the adulterer: flogging and exile, or stoning and exile.

Then He said: ﴿And the two of you who commit it from among you, harm them both﴾. ﴿Alladhani﴾ (the two who) corresponds to ﴿allati﴾. Is it for males or for females? It is for males. But the correspondence is not complete: here He said ﴿alladhani﴾, and there He said ﴿allati﴾. Why? Some scholars said: what is meant by ﴿alladhani﴾ here is the adulterer and the adulteress. But the ruling for the adulteress has already been stated, that she is confined to the house, while the adulterer is harmed, and [the ruling] ... (...) in the house. Other scholars said: what is meant by the two is the sodomite, i.e., the active and the passive partner. He attributed the act (ityan) to the passive partner, although he is the one acted upon, because the one who receives it, the consenting one, is like the doer. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever you find doing the deed of the people of Lot, kill the doer and the one it is done to."[[Recorded by Abu Dawud (4462) and al-Tirmidhi (1456) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] The correct view is this: the correct view is that ﴿alladhani﴾ refers to the two who commit sodomy, a man who sodomizes a man, and we seek refuge in Allah.

But there remains another consideration: why did He use the feminine plural for women and the dual for men? Because the spread of adultery among women is greater than the spread of sodomy among men. In the time of ignorance (jahiliyyah) they did not know of sodomy. Some even say: "If Allah had not related to us what He related of the story of the people of Lot, we would never have imagined that this would happen, because who could imagine that a man would consent to be treated as a woman is treated! This is impossible by nature and impossible by the Sharia." Therefore He expressed sodomy with the least number by which it can be realized. What is the least number by which it can be realized? Two. Unlike adultery among women, which is common.

﴿And the two of you who commit it from among you﴾: the pronoun in ﴿ya'tiyanaha﴾ refers to ﴿al-fahisha﴾ (lewdness), and the lewdness of men is sodomy, which is greater than the sin of adultery. The evidence of its greatness is that Lot said to his people: ﴿Do you commit the lewdness?﴾ [al-A'raf 80]. Regarding adultery, Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Indeed it is an indecency﴾ [al-Isra' 32], among the indecencies. As for this, He said ﴿al-fahisha﴾ (the lewdness), because it is—we seek refuge in Allah—considered repugnant in the mind of every person. Furthermore, the category of adultery may be permitted by a contract, but sodomy is never permitted under any circumstances, neither by contract nor otherwise, so it is more heinous.

﴿And the two of you who commit it from among you, harm them both﴾: harm them with what? With reviling, reproach, beating, and shunning, by way of discipline (ta'zir), boycott, and similar things. The point is, do whatever they will be harmed by.

﴿fa-in taba wa-aslaha fa-a'ridu 'anhuma﴾ (if they repent and amend, then leave them alone): ﴿in taba﴾ means repentance from what has occurred between them. ﴿wa-aslaha﴾ means amending their conduct in the future. ﴿fa-a'ridu 'anhuma﴾ (then leave them alone) is because the one who repents of a sin is like one who has no sin, so one turns away from him. Since the cause remains, the effect follows it; when the cause is removed, the effect is removed.

﴿inna Allaha kana tawwaban rahiman﴾ (indeed Allah is ever Oft-Returning, Most Merciful). ﴿inna Allaha kana tawwaban﴾: ﴿tawwaban﴾ is an intensive form, because of His great acceptance of repentance and the great number of those to whom He grants repentance. Those whom Allah grants repentance cannot be counted, and His repentance, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be enumerated; therefore He used the intensive form. And who is the one who repents? Allah's granting of repentance to the servant is of two kinds: a repentance before the servant's act of repenting, and a repentance after it. The repentance that comes before the servant's act of repenting means divine enablement (tawfiq), i.e., enabling him to repent, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then He turned to them that they might repent﴾ [at-Tawbah 118]. The repentance that comes after the servant's repentance is the acceptance of repentance, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾ [ash-Shura 25]. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is Tawwab in both senses: He is one who enables repentance for whomever He wills of His servants, and He is one who accepts repentance.

﴿Rahiman﴾ means: possessor of mercy, which He conveys to whomever He wills of His servants, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-'Ankabut 21].

In this verse there is some difficulty: His words ﴿kana tawwaban rahiman﴾. It is known that ﴿kana﴾ indicates the past, and it is understood from it that this attribute was and then ceased, as if you said: "Such-and-such was a student of knowledge," meaning in the past.

The scholars answered this difficulty by saying that ﴿kana﴾ may be stripped of its indication of time, and what is meant by it is the actual realization of the predicate's attribute. Everything attributed to Allah in this construction is meant in this sense: ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾ [an-Nisa' 23]; ﴿And Allah is ever Competent over all things﴾ [al-Ahzab 27]; ﴿And Allah is ever Encompassing of all things﴾ [al-Ahzab 126], and similar. What is meant is that He is characterized by it eternally, without beginning or end, but ﴿kana﴾ came to affirm the realization of His being characterized by this attribute.

* Student: May Allah reward you well. ﴿fa-a'ridu 'anhuma﴾: is this before having power over them or after having power over them?
* Shaykh: No, after having power over them.
* Student: After having power over them?
* Shaykh: Yes, but this ruling will be discussed, God willing.
* Student: The saying of the Exalted in Surah Hud: ﴿Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾ [Hud 107] (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, ﴿a gift uninterrupted﴾. And regarding the Fire He said: ﴿Indeed your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends﴾.
* Student: (...) ﴿abiding therein﴾.
* Shaykh: All of it, He said: ﴿as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾ [Hud 107].
* Student: What is the difference?
* Shaykh: The difference is that since this is a bounty, He clarified that it is an extended bounty. And since that is a punishment, He said: ﴿Indeed your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends﴾, so He carries out this punishment, because that is what His will requires.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon after. Those—Allah will turn to them in forgiveness; and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise. And repentance is not [accepted] from those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have now repented," nor from those who die while they are disbelievers. For those We have prepared a painful punishment. O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion, nor to make difficulties for them that you may take back part of what you gave them unless they commit a clear immorality. And live with them in kindness. And if you dislike them—perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good﴾ [an-Nisa' 17–19].

* Student: By bringing witnesses against them.
* Shaykh: No, the witnessing is for establishing...
* Student: ﴿fa-amsikuhunna fi al-buyuti hatta yatawaffahunna al-mawtu aw yaj'ala Allahu lahunna sabilan﴾.
* Shaykh: Correct. What is the way that Allah has ordained for them?
* Student: The saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah has ordained for them."
* Shaykh: In the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit.

* Shaykh: "Take from me, take from me, Allah has ordained for them."
* Student: "The virgin with the virgin: a year's flogging and a year's exile."
