* Student: "A hundred lashes and a year's exile, and the married with the married: a hundred lashes and stoning."[[Recorded by Muslim (1690/12) from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit.]]
* Shaykh: Well done.

Does this count as abrogation (naskh)?
* Student: It is not abrogation.
* Shaykh: Why?
* Student: This is the way that He ordained.
* Shaykh: Yes, but why?
* Student: Because this (...).
* Shaykh: Yes. The first ruling was temporary, not general for all times, so His saying ﴿fa-amsikuhunna fi al-buyut﴾ is an explanation of that.

His words ﴿wa-allatani ya'tiyanaha minkum﴾: what is meant by it?
* Student: It was said: the one who commits adultery with her, the adulterer. And it was said: the sodomite.
* Shaykh: It was said: it is the man who sodomizes a man.
* Student: And it was said: the one who has intercourse with a woman.
* Shaykh: Yes. Based on the second view, how does ﴿allatani ya'tiyanaha minkum﴾ work out?
* Student: (...)?

* Student: Yes, Shaykh. Then the man is only harmed, while the woman is confined and harmed.
* Shaykh: She is confined until death takes her or Allah ordains for them a way.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: If a man sodomizes a man, that is one view, and there is no difficulty in it. The difficulty lies with the one who says that what is meant by ﴿allatani ya'tiyanaha minkum﴾ is the two adulterers?

* Shaykh: Why did He express the women in the plural and the men in the dual?

On the view that what is meant by ﴿allatani ya'tiyanaha minkum﴾ is a man who sodomizes a man, how is it valid for the one who is acted upon to be the one who acts?
* Student: Since the one acted upon consents, his ruling is like the ruling of the doer.
* Shaykh: Well done. The one who receives it is like the doer.

I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those of your women who commit lewdness...﴾ to the end.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the gravity of adultery, and that it is among the indecencies, since there is agreement that what is meant is adultery. The view that it refers to lesbianism is a weak opinion on which no reliance can be placed.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: that adultery requires the testimony of four upright men, because of His saying ﴿fastashhidu 'alayhinna arba'atan﴾. And His saying ﴿minkum﴾ (from among you) is addressed to the believers, and the Companions were all upright. Or we say that ﴿minkum﴾ is addressed to all the Companions, and this unqualified term is understood as meaning uprightness ('adalah), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And bring to witness two just men from among you﴾ [at-Talaq 2].
* From the benefits of this noble verse: an indication that a man is stronger and more reliable than a woman as a witness, because Allah the Exalted did not require, for adultery, any testimony except that of men.
* From it: that the prescribed punishment (hadd) is averted by doubt (shubhah), because requiring four men is for the sake of establishing the testimony, and the testimony of the four women involves doubt, since they have not been established as witnesses, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So that if one of them errs, the other will remind her﴾ [al-Baqarah 282]. And there is no doubt that the prescribed punishments are averted by doubts.

But there remains with us the criterion of the ruling: what is the doubt (shubha) by which the hadd punishment is averted? Among the scholars there are those who broadened it to the point of saying: if a man hires a woman for fornication and then commits zina with her, there is no hadd upon him, because his hiring her is a doubt, just as if he hired a house to live in. Among the scholars there are those who took a middle position, and those who were strict. Generally, when opinions differ into three, the middle one is the correct one; this is the general rule.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: there must be explicit testimony by the witnesses to the testimony in matters of zina, due to His saying: ﴿then if they testify﴾. For this reason the witnesses must say: "We saw his member entering her private part, just as the kohl stick enters the kohl pot." It does not suffice for the witnesses to say: "We saw a man on a woman while they were naked, and we saw his member between her thighs." This is not sufficient; there must be explicit mention of intercourse, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Ma'iz, when he said: "Did you penetrate her?" — not using euphemism, or he said: "Do not use euphemism."[[Reported by al-Bukhari (6824) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] For this reason Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him) said in his time: the hadd for zina has not been established by testimony until our day; it has not been established by testimony. Why? Because it is difficult, very difficult.

If someone says: Can we establish it by photographs? We say: We used to say so, but when we became aware of the forging (dablaja) of photographers, we said: we do not establish it. Do you know what dablaja is? That is, they combine and fabricate a picture and make a man on a woman as though he had intercourse with her, when that is not the case. The problem with this forgery—we ask Allah to spare us its evil—is that they have begun to forge speech now, as I have been told. They take, for example, a letter from my speech, a letter from one word, and a letter from another word, and they assemble some parts upon others and produce a sermon in my voice according to what they want. Do you understand? They gather letters, then shape them into words as they wish, while the voice is my voice and the intonations are my intonations. This is truly a problem: any person who wants to attribute false words to someone can now do so. We hope that Allah will send a virus against these machines, just as they now threaten with computer viruses, so that we and people may be saved from their evil.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: confining the woman to her house is among the causes of averting fitnah, due to His saying: ﴿keep them confined﴾, because this is a kind of punishment in one respect and a restraint against the causes of fitnah in another respect.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: an indication that the house is better for the woman, due to His saying: ﴿keep them confined in the houses﴾, and as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Their houses are better for them."[[Reported by Abu Dawud (5468) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]]

* Among its benefits: it is not permissible to confine a woman in her house in such a way that she is prevented from going out, except when there is fitnah and evil. Otherwise the default is that she is not prevented from leaving the house. This is supported by the fact that Allah the Exalted obligated the widow to remain in her house, which indicates that others are not obligated to remain in the house. That is so; so we should encourage women to remain in the house, but we do not compel them to do so.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the legitimacy of punishment by lifelong imprisonment. Do you agree with this, or is there a basis for punishment by lifelong imprisonment?

* Students: The second.

* The Shaykh: The second is closer to the truth: there is a basis for punishment by lifelong imprisonment in the Shari'ah. As for making it a legislated ruling when it has been abrogated, there is some reservation in the soul about it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of ja'l (making/appointing) for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, due to His saying: ﴿or Allah appoints for them a way﴾. Ja'l is of two kinds: legislative ja'l (ja'l shar'i) and cosmic, decreed ja'l (ja'l kawni qadari). Examples of legislative ja'l include His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a means of establishment for the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah 97], and His saying: ﴿Allah has not instituted any bahirah, sa'ibah, wasilah, or ham﴾ [al-Ma'idah 103]. ﴿Has not instituted﴾ means legislative ja'l; as for decreed ja'l, He has indeed made that: the bahirah, sa'ibah, wasilah and ham do exist. Examples of cosmic ja'l are numerous in the Qur'an, such as: ﴿We made your sleep a rest (9), and We made the night a covering (10), and We made the day a means of livelihood﴾ [al-Naba' 9-11], and the examples are many.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of voluntary actions (al-af'al al-ikhtiyariyyah) of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; that is, affirming the attribute of renewed action for Allah. Know that an action attributed to Allah is of three types: genus (jins), species (naw'), and individual instance (fard).

As for the genus, it is an eternal, everlasting attribute: Allah has always been and always will be an Doer; He is an Doer in eternity past just as He is an Doer in eternity future. For this reason the preponderant of the scholars' opinions is that events are a continuous succession in the past just as they are in the future. However, we do not know what has succeeded in the past except what He has informed us of. Apart from that, we believe that Allah has always been and always will be an Doer, glorified and exalted is He.

The second: the species type. The species type is like the istiwa' (establishment) upon the Throne, and this is originated; Allah did not establish upon the Throne before creating the Throne.

As for the individual type, it is numerous, such as descending to the lowest heaven every night, coming to judge between the servants, descending to the lowest heaven on the evening of 'Arafah, anger when its cause exists, pleasure when its cause exists, laughter when its cause exists, and wonder when its cause exists; many things. Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah affirmed this, while the Ash'aris, the Mu'tazilah and those who follow their path denied it and said: it is impossible for Allah to be described by any originated attribute at all. For this reason they regard the Qur'an in our hands as eternal. They justified this corrupt ruling by saying: the subsistence of originated events in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, necessitates that He be originated, because originated events subsist only in something originated. Undoubtedly this is a sickly, indeed dead, reason. Who told them this?! Rather, the fact that originated events subsist in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that He does what He wills, is evidence of His perfection and the perfection of His life. If a person conceived of a lord who does not act and a lord who acts, the dictate of human nature would be that the second is more perfect, without doubt. So the correct view, without doubt, is that the actions of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, are, as they are a genus, also a species and individual instances.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those two of you who commit it, harm them. And if they repent and amend, then leave them alone. Indeed, Allah is ever Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾.

* It is derived from this noble verse that sodomy (liwat) has two rulings: the first ruling is what the verse indicates, and the second ruling is what the Sunnah indicates. As for what the verse indicates, it is that the man who commits this abomination is to be harmed: harmed by speech, harmed by action, harmed by shunning, harmed with various kinds of harm. Many people may find the harm to them more severe than beating them or imprisoning them.

As for the second ruling, established in the Sunnah, it is the killing of both the doer and the one done to: due to the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Whoever you find doing the deed of the people of Lut, kill the doer and the one done to."[[Reported by Muslim (1690/12) from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit.]]

Here the absolute (mutlaq) is not to be read in light of the restricted (muqayyad), so as to say: "Kill the doer and the one done to if they are married (muhsan)," as is the case with zina. This is because one of the conditions for applying the absolute to the restricted is that the ruling and the cause be the same, and here the cause and the ruling differ. In zina the cause is intercourse in a private part that is permissible in general—correct?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: When is it permissible? By a valid marriage contract or by ownership of the right hand. But this is a sexual use of a private part that is never permissible at all. Likewise, this abomination—and we seek refuge in Allah—is difficult to guard against, unlike zina, because it occurs among males, and who can confine males from one another? It is impossible to confine them; guarding against it is difficult. If it has no strong deterrent punishment, it spreads in society, and when it spreads in society men and women are corrupted—we ask Allah for well-being—because among the consequences for the one who commits liwat is that he no longer desires women. If he no longer desires women, women are left idle and evil and corruption ensues.

The evidence that among the consequences for the one who commits liwat is that the desire for women is removed from him is the statement of Lut to his people: ﴿Do you approach the males of all the worlds, and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses?﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 165-166]. They only left women because the desire for women had been stripped from their souls; otherwise a person by his nature inclines toward women. When this punishment spreads in society, it is corrupted: its men and women are corrupted and its interests are paralyzed. Therefore wisdom requires eliminating this corrupt germ, by killing. This absolute should not be read in light of the restricted, for the reason you know: the cause and the ruling differ.

Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him) mentioned that the Companions unanimously agreed on killing the doer and the one done to, though they differed about the manner of killing: some said they should be thrown from the highest place in the city and then stoned with rocks; some said they should be stoned; and some said the sodomite, both the doer and the one done to, should be burned, because their crime is grave and abominable. Lut called it "al-fahishah" (the abomination), and in the Book of Allah zina is also called so: ﴿Indeed, it was an abomination﴾ [al-Isra' 32]. The first is more severe.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever repents and amends, it is obligatory to refrain from punishing him. Allah the Exalted has stated explicitly in the verse about the muharibun in Surah al-Ma'idah that this is conditional upon repenting before you have power over them. He said: ﴿except those who repent before you gain power over them. So know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ma'idah 34]. But if he repents after power is gained over him, the punishment is not lifted from him.

Yet what appears from the Sunnah is that whoever has been established by confession and then repents is left to repent. The evidence for this is the hadith of Ma'iz ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) when he came to the Prophet (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) and confessed zina in his presence, so he ordered his stoning. When the stones touched him—that is, the stones reached him—he fled. But the Companions, because the Messenger (ﷺ) had ordered his stoning, said: the Messenger's command must be carried out, so they carried out the stoning, then informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of that. He said: "Why did you not leave him to repent, so that Allah might accept his repentance?"[[Reported by Abu Dawud (4419), and Ibn Abi Shaybah (29257), the wording being his, from the hadith of Na'im ibn Hazzal.]] This indicates that one who confesses a sin and repents, even during the execution of the hadd, is left to repent, and Allah accepts his repentance.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: repentance from sin must be accompanied by amendment (islah), due to His saying: ﴿if they repent and amend﴾. But how is repentance in such a case? It was said: repentance in such a case is that he is solicited and refuses, do you understand? For example, it is said to the one done to: "We want to do this to you," and if he refuses, that indicates his repentance. And it is said to the doer: "This one wants you to do it to him," and if he declines, that is his repentance. The same is said of the male and female fornicator. But this view is a objectionable opinion, far from the truth, because solicitation occurs only in private, is that not so? It is not that one solicits a person in front of people; it would be in a private situation.

Furthermore, if the one soliciting is capable of the act, meaning it is expected of him that he would do it, he may well be accommodated, and then the abomination occurs. And if the one soliciting is not capable of doing it, the one solicited will realize that this one wants to test him, and he refuses. From this we know that this view has no basis in soundness. Rather, repentance from this is like repentance from other sins: when we know that the man has turned away from this matter and no longer goes to gatherings where this abomination takes place and the like, we know he has repented. For this reason repentance is here paired with amendment, so there must be something that shows he has repented, namely correcting his conduct and keeping far from this abomination.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation that a ruling revolves around its cause, existence and non-existence. Its basis is His saying: ﴿if they repent and amend, then leave them alone﴾. Therefore, when the cause ceases, the ruling ceases. That is so: the ruling revolves around its effective cause (illah), existence and non-existence. However, if the cause is stated explicitly, when it is absent the ruling must be absent; but if the cause is inferred (mustanbatah), the ruling should not be dropped merely because the inferred cause is absent, because it is possible that the legislated cause is not this inferred one, and we would thereby nullify a ruling of Allah established merely by possibility. But if the cause is explicitly stated, the ruling revolves with it, as in His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "If there are three of you, two should not confide in each other to the exclusion of the third, because that would grieve him."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6290) and Muslim (2184/37) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]] This indicates that if the private conversation would not grieve him, it would be permissible.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, At-Tawwab (the Accepting of repentance) and Ar-Rahim (the Merciful). We have already explained the meaning of At-Tawwab and why it came in the intensive form, and the meaning of Ar-Rahim.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 17 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do wrong out of ignorance and then repent soon. Those are the ones to whom Allah will turn back, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾

﴿Innama at-tawbah (Repentance is only)﴾: this is the subject (mubtada', the grammatical subject) preceded by the restrictive particle ﴿innama﴾ (only). The predicate (khabar) of the subject is either his saying ﴿'ala Allah (incumbent upon Allah)﴾ or his saying ﴿lilladhina ya'maluna as-su' bi-jahalah (for those who do evil out of ignorance)﴾. Both are possible.

His saying ﴿innama at-tawbatu 'ala Allahi lilladhina ya'maluna as-su'(Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil)﴾: ﴿as-su'﴾ means evil conduct, such as the forbidden deeds, committing what is prohibited or abandoning what is obligatory. But He restricted it with His saying ﴿bi-jahalah (out of ignorance)﴾. The meaning of ﴿jahalah (ignorance)﴾ here is foolishness (safahah), not ignorance in the sense of lack of knowledge, because one who commits evil out of genuine ignorance is excused and bears no sin, following the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake﴾ (Al-Baqarah 286). Rather, the meaning of ﴿jahalah﴾ here is foolishness. From this is the saying of the poet:

"Let no one among us act with ignorance,
Lest we act with more ignorance than the ignorant."

﴿Thumma yatubuna min qarib (then repent soon)﴾: meaning, when they do evil out of foolishness, then they repent to Allah soon. The word ﴿qarib (soon)﴾ here refers to the time before death. So if they repent before death, Allah turns back to them in forgiveness. However, it will come to us in the lessons (fawa'id) that repentance must be made immediately (fawran).

﴿Yatubuna (they repent)﴾ means they return to Allah, by abandoning what they had done of evil or by doing what they had neglected of obligation.

﴿Fa-ula'ika yatubu Allahu 'alayhim (those are the ones to whom Allah will turn back)﴾: this sentence, in relation to what precedes it, is an emphasis, because this ruling is understood from His saying ﴿innama at-tawbatu 'ala Allah (repentance is only incumbent upon Allah)﴾. But He emphasized what He, Mighty and Majestic, has committed Himself to by His saying ﴿fa-ula'ika yatubu Allahu 'alayhim﴾. He referred to them with ﴿ula'ika (those)﴾, which is the demonstrative for the distant, although they are, in terms of the context of discussing them, in a position of nearness. The near is referred to with what? With ﴿ha'ula' (these)﴾. But here He said ﴿ula'ika﴾, using the distant demonstrative, to indicate the elevation of their rank through repentance.

﴿Yatubu Allahu 'alayhim wa-kana Allahu 'alimam hakima (Allah will turn back to them, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise)﴾: that is, possessing knowledge, judgment and wisdom. Knowledge is the perception of a thing as it actually is. This definition excludes both kinds of ignorance: simple ignorance (al-jahl al-basit) and compound ignorance (al-jahl al-murakkab). Simple ignorance involves no perception at all, while compound ignorance involves perceiving a thing as other than what it is. So knowledge is the perception of a thing as it actually is.

* Student: With firm certainty.
* Shaykh: Yes?
* Student: With firm certainty.
* Shaykh: Correct, because one who is not certain has not truly perceived.

As for the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, it is complete and all-encompassing. "Complete" means that it is not preceded by ignorance and is not followed by forgetfulness. Musa (peace be upon him) said to Pharaoh when he asked: ﴿What about the former generations?﴾ He said: ﴿Their knowledge is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ (Ta-Ha 51-52). ﴿Neither errs﴾ means He is not ignorant, and ﴿nor forgets﴾ means He does not lose what He has known.

It is also all-encompassing, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿That you may know that Allah is over all things competent, and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ (At-Talaq 12). Allah, Exalted is He, has explained His knowledge in His Book sometimes in summary and generality, and sometimes in detail. In His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but Him. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it, nor a grain within the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry but that it is in a clear Record﴾ (Al-An'am 59), this is detail. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die﴾ (Luqman 34). Allah also knows these things, and there is some detail in them. As for generality, it is abundant in the Qur'an.

Knowledge is more comprehensive and broader than power, because it relates to everything, even the impossible. Power, by contrast, is all-encompassing for everything possible, but what is impossible is not considered a "thing" with respect to power. As for knowledge, it includes even the impossible. Have you not considered the saying of Allah: ﴿Had there been within them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ (Al-Anbiya' 22), and His saying: ﴿Allah has not taken any son, and there is not with Him any other god; otherwise, each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have overcome others﴾ (Al-Mu'minun 91)? The plurality of gods is impossible and inconceivable, yet Allah informed us that if it were the case, its result would be such and such.

His saying ﴿Hakim (Wise)﴾ is derived from ﴿hukm (judgment)﴾ and ﴿hikmah (wisdom)﴾. So He is ﴿hakim (judge)﴾ if we take it as derived from ﴿hukm﴾, and ﴿muhkim (one who perfects)﴾ if we take it as derived from ﴿hikmah﴾.

* Student: The story of Ma'iz and his repentance (...). The Messenger asked the Companions to leave him. He says: the meaning of that is that they should not stone him until he came, then spoke to him; otherwise, the punishment would be carried out on him. That is, he says: leave him until he comes to me, and I hear from him what he wants, and I carry out the punishment on him. Otherwise, what is the benefit of (...)? Did he not say: "If only you had let him repent"?
* Shaykh: No, there is room for objection in this, because the Messenger did not say: "Why did you not leave him to come to me so he could repent." He said: "He repents, and Allah turns back to him." That is, you left him without the punishment, and he rectifies his condition in the future. So the first repentance is repentance to submit to the legal punishment, and that is why he said: "I want you to purify me." The second repentance is by correcting his condition.
* Student: And the verse, Shaykh: ﴿Before you have power over them﴾ (Al-Ma'idah 34)?
* Shaykh: That is about highway robbers whose crime has been established by evidence, because the conduct of highway robbers is aggressive.
* Student: Shaykh, we said regarding freeing a slave in the verse of retaliation for killing that it must be a believer. We also said that this applies to all things. Does the same apply here?
* Shaykh: No. As long as evidence indicates an exception, we follow it. Or is this the original rule?
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, what most scholars now hold is that for the married adulterer, the ruling of flogging was abrogated and the ruling of stoning remains.
* Shaykh: Correct.
* Student: And in Sahih al-Bukhari it is reported from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that "he flogged Shurahah al-Hamdaniyyah on Thursday and stoned her on Friday, and when asked, he said: I flogged her by the Book of Allah, and I stoned her by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah."[1] 'Ali has a Sunnah to be followed, Shaykh, so should we do as 'Ali did?
* Shaykh: 'Ali has a Sunnah to be followed, but it comes after the Sunnah of the Messenger (peace be upon him). Do you understand? So there is room for objection in his statement, may Allah be pleased with him; because we could say: we stoned her by the Book of Allah as well. 'Umar clearly stated while on the pulpit that "stoning is established by the Book of Allah, a verse of the verses of Allah that we recited, memorized, understood and practiced. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stoned, and we stoned after him."[2] So the correct view is that this was 'Ali's own reasoning (ijtihad), may Allah be pleased with him, but it is a reasoning that was contradicted by the text.
* Student: Shaykh, does "innama" (only) indicate restriction wherever it occurs?
* Shaykh: Yes, this is what the scholars said, indeed.
* Student: The saying of Ibn 'Abbas: "Interest is only in credit (nasi'ah)."[3]
* Shaykh: Correct.
* Student: But what about the interest of excess (riba al-fadl)?
* Shaykh: He did not see anything beyond this, and that is why he considered riba al-fadl permissible. He considered it permissible until Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to him, and he returned.
* Student: Shaykh, ﴿You are only a warner﴾ (Hud 12), this occurred...
* Shaykh: But this is a relative occurrence. There are two kinds of restriction: relative (idafi nisbi) and absolute (haqiqi). That is: with respect to the knowledge of the unseen, benefit and harm, you are only a warner.
* Student: May Allah be good to you. If we say: one who confesses to adultery and then repents, his repentance is accepted even after power has been exercised over him. But if we open the door to criminals, if they know that, and then they are caught, and then they repent before the punishment is carried out on them?
* Shaykh: No. This is less problematic than those who say he may retract his confession. Now, the well-known position of the school, which is what judges practice, is that once he retracts his confession, it is obligatory to stop (the punishment) against him, even in the middle of the punishment. Even if he confessed a clear and detailed confession, saying that he committed adultery with a woman named so-and-so in this room on such-and-such night, and that first he had tea and milk and they enjoyed themselves together. Even if everything was detailed and the judge ruled that he be stoned or flogged, and in the middle of it he said: "No, I retract my confession," they say: "Enough, let him go." But in reality this is what Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him) said. He said: If we accepted the retraction of one who confesses to what requires a legal punishment, no punishment would ever be established in this world, since every person could retract, especially in the present time, when people have no sense of trust.
* Student: Should he not be disciplined (ta'zir), Shaykh?
* Shaykh: No. The legal punishment is lifted from him by his retraction.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: That opinion is weak, very weak.
* Student: So we carry out the punishment on him, Shaykh, even if he repents and says: "I..."?
* Shaykh: No, no. If he repents, we leave him. The one who repents is recognized as a truthful man. But if he retracts his confession, this is playing games. A man comes and burdens the judge, and his confession is written down, and it becomes known or not known (...).
* Student: If there is evidence, Shaykh?
* Shaykh: How can there be evidence when he has confessed?
* Student: Strong evidence that requires...
* Shaykh: That would mean the man's mind is unsound.
* Student: Shaykh, we said that the saying of Allah, ﴿Or Allah ordains for them a way﴾ (An-Nisa' 15), is not a matter of abrogation (naskh). Then we said, Shaykh: Is it valid to say that life imprisonment has a basis in the Sharia? We said: this is better than saying that it is practiced in the Sharia. So how can we say this when it has been abrogated? (In the fawa'id, it has been abrogated.) What does that mean?
* Shaykh: Yes, the meaning of "lifted" (rufi'a) is "preserved" (huffiza).
* Student: It is not abrogation.
* Shaykh: No, no. It is not in the technical sense that is agreed upon.
* Student: Do the ones who say that the Qur'an is eternal and not created not use the saying of Allah: ﴿No reminder comes to them from their Lord but that it is newly revealed (muhdath)﴾ (Al-Anbiya' 2)?
* Shaykh: Yes, yes, but what do they say? They interpret it. They say: "newly sent down (muhdath al-inzal)."
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: It is problematic. This door of metaphor (majaz) has opened many doors for us.
(...) It was previously mentioned that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has committed Himself to turning back in repentance. So who is it that Allah has committed to turn back to?
* Student: ﴿For those who do evil out of ignorance and then repent soon﴾ (An-Nisa' 17).
* Shaykh: Well done. We mentioned that repentance is of two kinds?
* Student: Repentance before repentance and then it completes.
* Shaykh: Yes. What is the evidence?
* Student: Yes, ﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil out of ignorance and then repent soon.﴾
* Shaykh: That is the acceptance of repentance. Yes.
* Student: ﴿Then He turned to them so they might repent﴾ (At-Tawbah 118).
* Shaykh: ﴿Then He turned to them so they might repent﴾ (At-Tawbah 118). What is the meaning of His saying ﴿evil out of ignorance﴾?
* Student: Yes, Shaykh: that is, without knowledge.
* Shaykh: That is, without knowledge.
* Student: In foolishness.
* Shaykh: In foolishness. Why do we interpret it as foolishness rather than ignorance, which is the opposite of knowledge?
* Student: Because one who does evil while ignorant bears no sin.
* Shaykh: Well done. Because one who does evil out of genuine ignorance bears no sin at all. Do you have evidence, or a witness from Arabic speech, that ignorance can mean foolishness? A witness from Arab speech is not a proof, but it is supporting evidence.
* Student: The saying of the poet:
"Let no one among us act with ignorance,
Lest we act with more ignorance than the ignorant."
* Shaykh: Yes, well done. What is meant by His saying ﴿soon﴾?
* Student: "Soon" indicates a short time. The word "soon" is what one uses as evidence for (...).
* Shaykh: That is, before death? Allah concluded the verse with His saying ﴿Knowing and Wise﴾ although one would expect Him to say ﴿Oft-Returning and Merciful﴾. What is the wisdom?
* Student: Because He knows everything that occurs of repentance and of committing evil deeds.
* Shaykh: Yes, but do knowledge and wisdom suit repentance? We said repentance is in the verse: ﴿Then He turned to them so they might repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful﴾ (At-Tawbah 118).
* Student: "The Accepter of repentance, the Merciful" was mentioned before this.
* Shaykh: Where?
* Student: It is before this.
* Shaykh: Where? ﴿And if they both repent and reform﴾ (An-Nisa' 16)?
* Student: ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Accepting of repentance and Merciful﴾.
* Shaykh: Yes, this one is in a specific matter.
* Student: It shows that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows who deserves repentance and who does not, and places it in its proper place.
* Shaykh: And places it in its proper place. Correct, because there will come a state in which repentance is not accepted, so it is fitting to show that His turning back to these people is based on knowledge and wisdom.
* Student: That is what you mentioned, Shaykh.
* Shaykh: Now I have mentioned it. If I did not mention it before, now I have mentioned it. And if I had mentioned it and you forgot it, then we complain to Allah about your forgetfulness.

We always speak about the Wise (al-Hakim) and say that it is derived from ﴿hukm (judgment)﴾ and ﴿hikmah (wisdom)﴾. So how many kinds of the judgments of Allah are there?
* Student: Cosmic judgment and legislative judgment.
* Shaykh: Cosmic judgment and legislative judgment. Give me an example of cosmic judgment.
* Student: Cosmic judgment is like the creation of the heavens and the earth.
* Shaykh: No, I mean a verse in which the word "judgment" is used to mean cosmic judgment.
* Student: The saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So I will not leave this land until my father permits me or Allah decides for me, and He is the best of judges﴾ (Yusuf 80).
* Shaykh: Yes, ﴿So I will not leave this land until my father permits me or Allah decides for me﴾, this is cosmic judgment. Now we want an example of legislative judgment?
* Student: ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ (An-Nisa' 11).
* Shaykh: No, this is general. I mean an example specifically concerning legislative judgment?
* Student: The saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you﴾ (Al-Mumtahanah 10).

---

[1] Reported by al-Bukhari (6812) and Ahmad (1185), whose wording this is, from 'Ali.
[2] Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (6829) and Muslim (1691/15), from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.
[3] Reported by Muslim (1594/99) and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2313), whose wording this is.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 17 (part 2 of 2):

* The Shaykh: When you mentioned the rulings concerning women who come to you from the disbelievers as believers, in Surah al-Mumtahanah, you did well. We also mentioned that it is derived from ḥikmah (wisdom), or from iḥkām, which is the perfecting of a thing, and that ḥikmah is of two types, is that right?
* A student: Ghā'iyyah (teleological) and ṣūriyyah (formal).
* The Shaykh: What is the meaning of the first?
* The student: Teleological wisdom means that the purpose of this thing is this (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: And formal wisdom is that this thing was made in this form.
* The Shaykh: Correct. That is, placing a thing in the state it is in is wisdom, and that its end is such-and-such is also another wisdom. Good. We have discussed this verse, and I think we have covered its benefits. Very well.
* From the benefits of the noble verse, ﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah﴾: the demonstration of the grace of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, toward His servants by His making repentance binding upon Himself. ﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah﴾.
* And from its benefits: that Allah may make obligatory upon Himself whatever He wills, and the servants have no right to make anything obligatory upon Him, due to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He cannot be questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [al-Anbiya' 23]. However, He may make obligatory upon Himself whatever He wills, and He may prohibit upon Himself whatever He wills. Allah, exalted is He, said in the ḥadīth qudsī: "O My servants, I have forbidden injustice upon Myself"[[Narrated by Muslim (2577/55) from the ḥadīth of Abū Dharr al-Ghifārī.]]. This is that He prohibited injustice upon Himself. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed upon Himself mercy﴾ [al-An'am 54]. This is an binding obligation and a requirement, and among this is this verse, ﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah﴾.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: that every doer of evil does it only out of ignorance and foolishness, and foolishness is the opposite of rushd (sound judgment). Whoever commits an evil has lost his rushd.
* And from its benefits: that rushd differs according to its contexts. Rushd in wealth is the good management of it. Rushd in guardianship is knowing what is due to the guardianship; if it is the guardianship of a ruler and command, it has a specific rushd, and if it is the guardianship of marriage, the rushd of the guardian is that he knows the suitable match (kafā'ah) for the woman and the interests of the marriage. If rushd is in dealing with people, then likewise it has its own specific rushd. All of this is encompassed by ihsān al-taṣarruf, the good handling of whatever one handles. This is rushd, and its opposite is mishandling.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: the exhortation to hasten to repentance, due to His saying: ﴿then they repent soon﴾. Indeed, hastening to repentance is obligatory, and its basis is that the intended meaning of "soon" here is death, and death's time is not known. When this is the case, hastening to repentance is—what?—obligatory, because a person does not know what will befall him. And this is so: hastening to repentance is obligatory. Also, when a person persists in disobedience his heart hardens, and that minor sin, even if it is one of the lesser sins, becomes a major one. For this reason some scholars mentioned that treating disobedience lightly and persisting in a minor sin turns it into a major one. So when a person commits a minor sin out of carelessness toward Allah and His commands, it becomes a major sin because of the carelessness that settled in his heart—what?—toward it.
Moreover, he said: And when a person commits a major sin while having great reverence for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and fear of Him, and shame before Him, but his soul tempted him to do it, this makes it a minor sin. The man who was flogged for drinking wine, when one of the Companions cursed him, the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "He loves Allah and His Messenger"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (6780) from the ḥadīth of 'Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.]].
Thus the sinner may have in his heart such awe of Allah, veneration and exaltation of Him, that when committing the sin he is ashamed before Allah and bashful toward Him, so the major sin turns into a minor one because of the fear, reverence, and exaltation of Allah that accompanied it, since good deeds erase bad deeds, and the reverse is also true. A person may be careless about Allah's command and disobey Him in a minor sin, yet he is careless and unconcerned with the greatness of Allah, so this minor sin becomes a major one because of the carelessness toward the right of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that settled in his heart.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: Allah's acceptance of repentance when a person repents soon, due to His saying: ﴿then those—Allah will turn to them in forgiveness﴾.
* And from its benefits: (...) of Allah, and the wisdom as well, which is understood from His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing, Wise﴾.
We have explained in the tafsir that the knowledge of Allah, exalted is He, is vast and encompasses everything small and great, near and far: ﴿Indeed, nothing is hidden from Allah, on the earth or in the heaven﴾ [Ali 'Imran 5].
* And from its benefits: the affirmation of these two Names for Allah, which are what? Al-'Alīm (the All-Knowing) and al-Ḥakīm (the All-Wise).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 18 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And repentance is not for those who commit evil deeds﴾. Here He said ﴿repentance is not﴾ and did not say "with Allah," because this repentance is negated by the Law, so it is not genuine. ﴿Repentance is not for those who commit evil deeds﴾. "Evil deeds" may be understood as a generic noun, which is the more apparent reading, or as a plural, since that is the apparent wording.

﴿Until, when death approaches one of them, he says: "Indeed, I have repented now."﴾ These people have no repentance, because their repentance is a repentance of compulsion, like that of one forced to act. The one forced to act has no legal ruling applied to his action, as is well known, because whoever is forced to disbelieve while his heart remains firm in faith is not judged as a disbeliever. Likewise this person who repents after despairing of the world and becoming certain that he is departing. This repentance does not benefit him. ﴿Until, when death approaches one of them, he says: "Indeed, I have repented now."﴾ Now, when he sees death, he repents. What sincere repentance is this from someone who knows he has left the world?!

This is similar, in some respects, to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The best charity is that you give in charity while you are healthy and stingy, fearing poverty and hoping for long life." The healthy person considers death remote, and he fears poverty because he is stingy. "And do not delay," meaning, do not postpone, "until, when the soul reaches the throat, you say: 'To so-and-so such-and-such, and to so-and-so such-and-such,' and it had already been for so-and-so." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1419) and Muslim (1032/93) from Abu Hurayrah.] "It had already been for so-and-so": who is so-and-so? The heir. This happens often. When a person despairs of his life, he goes off to make a bequest: "I bequeath such-and-such for righteous deeds, for charity to the poor, for printing books, for building mosques." Fine, why did you not make a bequest ten days ago? Because now he has despaired of his life and knows he will certainly depart.

He said: ﴿And nor is it for those who die while they are disbelievers﴾. He said: ﴿And nor is it for those who die﴾. The "wa" is a conjunction, the "la" is an emphatic addition, and ﴿those who﴾ is coordinated with His saying ﴿for those who commit﴾. That is, repentance is also not for those who die while they are disbelievers. Those who die while disbelieving have no repentance.

The apparent meaning of the verse is problematic, because whoever dies has ended his deeds, so how can He say ﴿nor is it for those who die while they are disbelievers﴾? We say: what is meant is their remorse on the Day of Resurrection, when they will regret and say: ﴿"Oh, if only we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers"﴾ [al-An'am 27]. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿"Rather, there has become apparent to them what they had been concealing before. And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden. And indeed, they are liars"﴾ [al-An'am 28]. So the repentance of the disbeliever after death means his remorse that he displays on the Day of Resurrection, and this does not benefit him, because the time for action has ended. Only the time of recompense remains, so it does not benefit him.

﴿For those, We have prepared a painful punishment﴾. ﴿Those﴾ refers to the disbelievers who died upon disbelief; Allah has prepared for them a painful punishment. As for one who dies upon sins short of disbelief, his matter is with Allah: if He wills, He punishes him, and if He wills, He forgives him. The preparation of the Fire is only for the disbelievers. As for the disobedient, they may be pardoned and never enter the Fire.

* This verse contains several benefits. The first benefit: repentance ends when a person is dying, that is, when death arrives, because of His saying: ﴿Until, when death approaches one of them, he says: "Indeed, I have repented now."﴾

* Among its benefits: the words of one who is dying have no legal effect. Has no legal effect, like this? Or do we say: his words have no legal effect as a plea for forgiveness, because in this state it is not the time for seeking to be pleased? But if he says some other statement, is it considered? The answer: the first. The dying person's words carry no weight, because he is not fully conscious, so his words are not relied upon.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is a condition for the validity of repentance that it occur in the time when repentance is accepted, which is before death arrives. At this point it is good for us to address the conditions of repentance. We have examined them and found them to be five.

The first condition: sincerity to Allah, may He be exalted, meaning that nothing motivates him to repent except love of Allah, seeking nearness to Him, and fear of His punishment. Not to obtain some worldly thing or to ward off a worldly blame. Sincerity to Allah, may He be exalted, is what motivates him to repent.

The second: remorse for the sin he committed. If he repents without remorse, his repentance is either invalid, because its conditions are not complete, or very deficient. Some scholars raised an objection to this condition, namely that remorse is a state of being affected, and a person acts but is not acted upon, so how can he feel remorse?

The answer to that is very easy. Remorse means that he perceives in himself that he has done wrong, so he grieves and wishes he had not done it. This is the remorse that is meant, and this is something possible, this is something possible. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) pointed out that being affected can be mastered by a person, when he said: "The strong one is not the one who overpowers others, but the strong one is the one who controls himself when angry." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6114) and Muslim (2609/107) from Abu Hurayrah.] Although anger is an affect, when its cause exists and a person is stirred, he cannot help it; yet he can still control himself. Likewise, stirring up an emotion is possible, calming an emotion is possible, and stirring it up is also possible.

The third condition: giving up the sin. If he does not give it up, his repentance is false, and it is closer to mockery of Allah than to exalting Allah. How can he say he has repented from drinking wine while he is addicted to it? How can he say he has repented from usury while he persists in it? This is mockery of Allah, may He be exalted. If you came to a king and said, "I repent, I repent, I will not curse you and will not say anything against you," but whenever you find the king distracted, even by speaking to someone beside you, or even by a gesture, you say, "This king has no good in him," would this be repentance? Never, it is not repentance. So how about the King of kings, may He be exalted? How can you repent to Allah from a sin you persist in? This is impossible.

If someone says: We see some people say that if the sin involves the right of a human being, then it is necessary to deliver it to him? We say: this condition does not depart from what we have said, which is giving up the sin. If your sin involves the right of a human being and you insist on wasting this right, then you have not given up the sin. If it is money, return it to him; if it is blood, deliver it to him; if it is his honor, seek his pardon, seek his pardon. If it is money and the one you wronged has died, what should I do? Search for his heirs, search for his heirs. If you cannot find them and it becomes impossible for you, then give it in charity. And then, do you give it in charity on behalf of the heirs or on behalf of the deceased?

* Student: He gives it in charity on behalf of the deceased.

* Shaykh: The deceased has died.

* Student: But the right remains for him in (...).

* Shaykh: When the deceased dies, the right passes to whom is in his wealth? To the heirs. So you give it in charity on behalf of the heirs, along with asking Allah's forgiveness for the deceased's wronging, along with asking Allah's forgiveness for the deceased's wronging. Therefore, if you delivered this money to the heirs, you have not repented a complete repentance until you ask Allah's forgiveness for the deceased, because in reality you came between him and his wealth. Now, if the right is blood, such as when a man ran over a person and fled out of fear of the authorities, then repented, what should he do? He goes to the family of the victim and says, "This is what happened." Likewise, if he killed someone intentionally and then repented, he goes to the victim's family and says, "I killed your companion intentionally."

If it is backbiting, meaning honor, that is, he wronged someone in his honor, what should he do? Some scholars said: he must seek the person's pardon. He goes to him and says, "I backbit you, so forgive me." Some scholars objected to this matter and said: if he goes and says to him, "I backbit you, so forgive me," the man may be seized by arrogance in sin and say, "No." Rather, there must be a distinction: if the person has come to know that you backbit him, then you must seek his pardon. But if he does not know, and you do not fear that he will know, then it suffices for you to ask Allah's forgiveness for him, according to the hadith: "The expiation for one whom you have backbitten is that you ask forgiveness for him." [Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (6368) from Anas ibn Malik with the wording: "The expiation for backbiting is that you ask forgiveness for the one whom you backbit."] So you ask forgiveness for him and mention him with good in the gatherings where you had backbitten him.

The fourth condition: that he resolves not to return in the future to what he repented from. If he repented, felt remorse, and gave it up, but in his heart he would do it again if he were able, then his repentance is not valid, because he did not resolve never to return. Rather, he must resolve never to return. If he speaks to himself that, if this sin came to him, he would return to it, then he has not repented.

You must know the difference between our saying "resolve not to return" and "condition of not returning." It is not a condition that he not return. The condition is that he resolve not to return. The difference between them is clear, because if you say that resolving not to return is required, and he resolved not to return, but afterward his soul tempted him and he returned, then the first repentance is valid. But if you say that not returning is required, then if he returns afterward, his repentance is invalid. However, the scholars say: it is required that he resolve not to return.

The fifth condition: that the repentance occur at a time when it is accepted from the penitent. If it occurs at a time when it is not accepted from him, such as when the appointed time has arrived or the sun has risen from its west, then repentance is not accepted. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Repentance does not cease until migration ceases, and migration does not cease until the sun rises from its west." [Narrated by Abu Dawud (2479) from Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan.] So if a person repents when the sun rises from its west or when the appointed time arrives, it is not accepted from him.

When Pharaoh was overtaken by drowning, he became Muslim, indeed he believed. He said: ﴿"I believe that there is no deity except the one in whom the Children of Israel believed"﴾ [Yunus 90]. That is, Allah, may He be exalted, but he did not state the name of Allah explicitly. Rather, he said: ﴿in whom the Children of Israel believed﴾, out of exaggerated humility and following the Children of Israel, after he had been what? Haughty over them, arrogant toward them. Now he had become a follower of them. ﴿other than the one in whom the Children of Israel believed, and I am of those who submit﴾, submitting to Allah. Then it was said to him: ﴿"Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters?"﴾ We ask Allah to bestow upon us and you repentance before the appointed time arrives.

The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, differed: is it a condition for the acceptance of repentance that one give up all sins, or is it not a condition?

* Student: It is not a condition.

* Shaykh: I say: they differed. You are among those who say it is not a condition. Some said it is a condition, meaning one must give up all sins, and that whoever repents from fornication while he practices usury, his repentance from fornication is not accepted, because true repentance is that which fills the servant's heart with fear of Allah and exalting of Allah, and the one who repents from one sin while persisting in another does not realize this in his case.

Others made a distinction and said: if the sin he persists in is of the same kind as the sin he repents from, his repentance is not accepted; but if it is of a different kind, it is accepted. An example: if he repents from looking at women with forbidden looks, but he touches women in forbidden touching, here the kind is one, so his repentance from looking is not accepted, because he is indulging in this kind, so the soul is attached to this kind (...) and he has not given it up. But if it is of a different kind, there is no harm (...), and he commits fornication or drinks wine. His repentance from usury is valid and accepted. And if he repents from drinking wine while he persists in fornication, his repentance from it is accepted.

The correct view is that repentance from a sin is accepted along with persistence in another, but the penitent does not deserve, I mean, the absolute description of "those who repent," the unrestricted description. Rather, he is a penitent with a restricted repentance, restricted to what? To this specific sin. So the absolute description of the penitents does not apply to him, but describing him as repenting from this sin is a restricted description that is established for him, because this is justice, and Allah, may He be exalted, commands justice and equity, and He, glorified and exalted, is the possessor of justice and equity. This view is the correct one.

Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, in Madarij al-Salikin, when he discussed this matter, said: "Furthermore, this issue has deep depths." That is, it is not a trivial matter whose rulings are cast on the tongue, because it is connected to the hearts, and hearts are sensitive, like a ball on the surface of water that trembles and nothing holds it. The matter is in reality of great depth, and the root of repentance is exalting Allah, may He be exalted, revering Him, fearing Him, and being in awe of Him. When this is realized in a person, repentance becomes easy for him. But without it, repentance is difficult for him. We ask Allah to accept our repentance and yours.

* Student: That repentance is not accepted when the appointed time arrives for a person; in the story of Abu Talib (...) the Prophet (ﷺ), when the appointed time had arrived for him (...)?

* Shaykh: This one raised the question: if repentance does not benefit when the appointed time arrives, then what is the answer to the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to his uncle Abu Talib: "Say: There is no deity but Allah, a word by which I will plead on your behalf before Allah"? [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3884) and Muslim (24/39) from al-Musayyib ibn Hazn.]

The answer to this: this is a specific case. Just as Abu Talib benefited from the intercession of the Messenger (ﷺ) to the exclusion of other disbelievers, he may benefit from his Islam, to the exclusion of other penitents, in this state. This is one point. The second point: the Prophet (ﷺ) did not affirm definitively that it would benefit him. What did he say? "I will plead," and one who pleads may have his plea accepted or not accepted. If this hadith does not indicate definitively that it would be accepted, then it is among the ambiguous texts, which are interpreted in light of the clear texts, and that repentance in this state is not accepted.

* Student: O Shaykh, (...) in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿who do evil in ignorance﴾ (...) with foolishness (...), meaning ignorance, as is apparent in the verse?

* Shaykh: No, ignorance is not called "ignorance" (jahalah).

* Student: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, did not describe (...). He said: knows the evil, because he is not actually a doer, O Shaykh, but no (...) an evildoer.

* Shaykh: We answer this with two answers. The first answer has already passed: that the doer of evil through ignorance, which is the opposite of knowledge, is not held accountable for it at all, so repentance from it is not required of him. The second: ignorance (jahalah) is not applied to the ignorance that is the opposite of knowledge; rather, it means foolishness.

* Student: O Shaykh, the case of the Jew to whom the Prophet (ﷺ) said, when he said "There is no deity but Allah," before his death: "Praise be to Allah who rescued him through me from the Fire" [al-Bukhari (1356) from Anas ibn Malik]. Is this also a specific case, O Shaykh?

* Shaykh: This is a specific case, and we do not know whether this Jew had reached the appointed time or was close to it.

* Student: O Shaykh, the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And nor is it for those who die while they are disbelievers﴾. We said that the remorse of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection does not benefit. Then does (...)?

* Shaykh: No, it does not benefit.

* Student: The implication of the verse, O Shaykh?

* Shaykh: Until (...) the believers; because if repentance ends with the arrival of the appointed time, then what comes after it is all the more so.

* Student: O Shaykh, may Allah be good to you. Now, some of the wicked people who drink wine and practice usury (...) from it, not out of repentance to Allah and fear of Him and exalting Him, so are they described as wicked for their persistence in what they are doing, since they have not stopped the outward repentance?

* Shaykh: Yes, did you hear? He says: some of the people who practice usury or drink wine or commit fornication may leave this thing, not out of repentance to Allah, but out of boredom with it. Are they described as wicked? We say: inwardly they are wicked, but outwardly no, because we judge only by the outward, even if there is an indication.

The evidence for this is the hadith of Usamah ibn Zayd (may Allah be pleased with him) when he pursued a polytheist. When he caught up with him, the polytheist said, "There is no god but Allah," but he killed him, interpreting the situation (mutawwilan). When the news reached the Prophet (ﷺ), he said to him: "Did you kill him after he said, 'There is no god but Allah'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Did you kill him?" He said: "Yes." He said: "What will you do with 'There is no god but Allah' when it comes on the Day of Resurrection?" (Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6872) and Muslim (96/158) from the hadith of Usamah ibn Zayd.) He kept repeating to him, "You killed him after he said, 'There is no god but Allah,'" until Usamah said, "I wished I had not embraced Islam until that day." Now, do we agree with Usamah on what? On the point that the man said it as a means of seeking refuge (ta'awwudhan), as Usamah said; he said it to protect himself from being killed. But even so, we do not make (...) an obstacle to judging by the outward appearance (hukm bi'l-zahir, judging by what is apparent).

* Student: His saying, "There is no god but Allah," is that not repentance?
* The Shaykh: It is repentance if he was sincere.
* Student: That he (...).
* The Shaykh: It is not repentance.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿And if you desire to exchange one wife for another, and you have given one of them a great amount of wealth, do not take back from it anything. Would you take it by slander and manifest sin? And how could you take it while you have gone in to one another and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?﴾ [An-Nisa' 20-21].
* The Shaykh: Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And repentance is not accepted from those who continue to do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have now repented"﴾ [An-Nisa' 18].
* From the benefits of this verse: (...) if he repents on the Day of Resurrection, his repentance will not benefit him; because of His saying: ﴿nor from those who die while they are disbelievers﴾.
* And from its benefits: the obligation to hasten to repentance (tawbah), because Allah has tied its acceptance to a term that is not known. If that is the case, it is obligatory (...) with it.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: that Allah, glorified and exalted, has prepared for the disbelievers who die in disbelief (...).
* And from its benefits: the refutation of the saying of those who say that the people of the Fire become accustomed to it (...) so its heat does not harm them; because Allah said: ﴿a painful punishment﴾, and if the matter were as they mentioned (...).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 19 (part 1 of 2):

Then He said: ﴿O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion﴾, to the end of the verse. We have already mentioned that when an address begins with the call "O you who have believed," it indicates its importance and the attention given to it. We have also mentioned that when it is introduced with this description, ﴿O you who have believed﴾, it is evidence that obeying it is a requirement of faith, and that opposing it (...). We have also mentioned that it contains evidence for the use of a name that stirs one to something (in other words, one that urges toward something), as in His saying (...), as if He is inciting them to accept what will be directed at them. This is because when a description is mentioned in a way that stirs a person, it becomes an incitement to it, as you say: "O generous one, do not be stingy with the guest," or "O man, do not let women overcome you," for this causes a person to be seized by enthusiasm until he complies.

He says: ﴿O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion﴾. The negation of permissibility (ḥill) necessitates prohibition (taḥrīm), and the one who makes lawful and unlawful (...) is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason (...) by prohibition, and sometimes by negating permissibility. In this verse He said: ﴿it is not lawful﴾, and after it, within a few verses, the explicit prohibition will come in His saying: ﴿Prohibited to you are your mothers﴾ [an-Nisa 23].

He says: ﴿it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion﴾. ﴿By compulsion﴾ means: forcibly against them, such that they are not content with that while you compel them to this inheritance. (...) Does "inheritance" here mean that they inherit them as they inherit property, meaning that they enslave them? Or that they succeed their husbands in them without taking possession? The second: because they do not inherit women as they inherit property; rather they inherit women, that is, they succeed their husbands in them. Allah called it inheritance, since whoever succeeds another in something is his heir. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We inherit the earth and whoever is upon it﴾ [Maryam 40], although He, the Mighty and Majestic, already owns it, and owns whoever is upon it (...) that He annihilates whoever is upon it while He, glorified and exalted, remains. And Allah the Exalted said concerning Zechariah: ﴿Grant me from Yourself an heir (5) who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob﴾ [Maryam 5-6], meaning: who will succeed me among my people in knowledge and prophethood, and it is not an inheritance of wealth, because prophets do not bequeath. So: ﴿it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion﴾, meaning: to succeed their husbands in them by compulsion.

As for His saying ﴿by compulsion﴾, this restriction (...). If it is to describe the reality, then it does not indicate that if they were content, men could succeed their husbands in them, for that is not permitted except by a lawful marriage contract. This is because they used to (...): when a man died, his heirs came after him and prevented the woman from marrying (...), and if they were from his paternal cousins, one of them would choose her and marry her by force against her will and by aggression. For this, Allah forbade it, saying: ﴿it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion﴾. Based on this, the restriction is a description of the reality, and what is a description of the reality has no implicit contrary meaning. Accordingly, it is not lawful that (...) their choice.

He said: ﴿And do not restrain them in order to take away part of what you have given them﴾. This is another matter similar to what preceded. ﴿Do not restrain them﴾ means: do not withhold their rights, forcing them to (...). ﴿In order to take away part of what you have given them﴾. This occurs often among oppressive husbands: a husband restrains his wife and withholds from her, and when she is distressed beyond endurance, she is compelled to ransom herself from him, why? In order to take back what he had given her earlier, either all of it or part of it.

As for His saying ﴿And do not restrain them in order to take away part of what you have given them﴾: if someone said, "If he restrains her in order to take all that he gave her, does it fall under the prohibition?" (...) because it is of the category of ﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾. And in one reading: ﴿mubayyanah﴾, meaning: except that they commit a clear immorality, then it is permitted for you. And what is the clear immorality? Regarding the clear immorality there are opinions:
It has been said: it is (...). If she commits adultery, he may restrain her so that she ransoms herself from him, because (...) she is an adulteress, and his soul will not be content to divorce her in this way and lose his wealth. So in this case he may (...) and withhold her right so that she seeks khul' or ransoms herself from him.
(...) The intended meaning of the clear immorality is foul language: that she is sharp-tongued against him and his family (...). For this is considered abominable by custom, so if this comes from the woman, he may restrain her until she ransoms herself from him.
And it has been said: the intended meaning is bad conduct (sū' al-ʿishrah), such that she does not give him his right with contentment, cheerfulness and openness, when he calls her to his bed (...) and she becomes difficult, her face reddens and pales, and she does not respond when he asks her for a need (...). This need which it is obligatory on her to grant, this is of the clear immorality.

This last view includes the two before it, for there is no doubt that bad conduct includes a woman deceiving her husband by committing adultery, may Allah protect us, and there is also no doubt that bad conduct includes foul and excessive tongue. Therefore, the relied-upon view is that the intended meaning of the clear immorality is: what? Bad conduct, by whatever means it occurs, whether of what is abominable in the Sharia such as adultery, or by custom, although adultery is abominable both by custom and by Sharia.

﴿And live with them in kindness﴾. This is the third clause. ﴿Live with them﴾ means the women. ﴿In kindness﴾ means: with what people recognize and the Sharia does not reject. Mu'āshara (living together) is a form of mufā'alah which is typically from both sides, since generally a verbal form of this pattern is performed by both parties, as in jāhada mujāhadah, qātala qitālan, yāsara mayāsarah, ʿāsara muʿāsarah, ʿāshara muʿāsharah; though sometimes it is not from both sides, as in sāfara musāfarah, for this travel is only from one party.

﴿Live with them in kindness﴾ means: that each of you should live with the other in kindness, that is, with what people recognize and the Sharia does not reject. Note well: with what people recognize and the Sharia does not reject. If something is recognized by people but the Sharia rejects it, it is not permitted; it is not kindness but wrong. Does "living together" mean by speech, by action, and by giving? By speech: that he speaks gently to her and she speaks gently to him. By action: service and the like. By giving: spending on her, including clothing, food, drink, housing, and paying her debts. What do you say?
* Students: No.
* The Shaykh: No, he is not obliged to pay her debts, nor is she obliged to pay his debts, except that if she borrows for a maintenance that is obligatory on him, then if she borrows for an obligatory maintenance he must pay this debt, because it is binding upon him.

﴿And live with them in kindness; and if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good﴾. That is: a person may dislike a wife and so not live with her in kindness, for it is part of human nature that when he dislikes something he does not submit to it or rejoice in it. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿if you dislike them﴾, because of their bad character or for other reasons.

﴿Perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good﴾. This is an indication that we should be patient, that we should endure with them; that is: be patient, if you dislike them, be patient. ﴿Perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good﴾, which you do not expect. Among the good is that Allah ordains between them a righteous child, for this is among the greatest goods. Also among the good is that Allah transforms her circumstances and qualities that he disliked into conditions and qualities he is pleased with, and then he becomes at ease with her and lives with her a good life.

* From the benefits of this verse: first, the prohibition of inheriting women in a manner they dislike, as was practised in the Jahiliyyah, by His saying: ﴿it is not lawful for you﴾.
* Among its benefits also: that the negation of permissibility is intended to mean prohibition, it is intended to mean prohibition, because negating a thing is an affirmation of its opposite.
* Among its benefits: that if one inherits a woman in a manner she is content with, there is no harm, but it is restricted by what? By the content of the Sharia, restricted by the content of the Sharia. So if a man marries, after the death of his paternal cousin, the wife of his paternal cousin, there is no harm in it. And if he marries his brother's wife after his death, with her consent and by a lawful contract, his brother's wife, there is no harm. And if he marries his grandfather's wife? Then there is no harm!
* Students: She is forbidden (muḥarramah).
* The Shaykh: Forbidden? So the grandfather is not a brother.
* A student: The grandfather is a father, O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: Did we not go over this in the chapter on inheritance?
* A student: According to a view other than the preponderant one.
* The Shaykh: According to a view other than the preponderant one, correct.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the prohibition of restraining a woman without right so that she ransoms herself; by His saying: ﴿And do not restrain them in order to take away part of what you have given them﴾.
* Among its benefits, and this is a point of discussion: the indication that khul' should not be for more than what he gave her; by His saying: ﴿part﴾. But this benefit may be disputed, and it is said: Allah prohibited restraining in order to take away part of what He gave her, to show that restraining in order to take any amount, even a little, is forbidden, and it does not address whether he takes more or less. We have already mentioned in the tafsir of Surat al-Baqarah the disagreement of the scholars on this: whether it is permitted for a person in khul' to take more than what he gave her or not, and we explained that the matter has three opinions: permissibility, prohibition, and disapproval.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility, or rather the variation of address; by His saying at the beginning: ﴿it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion﴾, and in the second: ﴿And do not restrain them﴾. This is if we take (lā) as a prohibitive particle. But if we take it as a negation for emphasis, and the implied sense of the verse is: "nor that you restrain them in order to take away," then the speech is on a single pattern, correct? The verse can allow that (lā) is prohibitive, and ﴿tuʿḍulūhunna﴾ is jussive by the prohibitive (lā); or that the waw is a conjunction and (lā) is an emphatic extra particle, and ﴿tuʿḍulūhunna﴾ is conjoined to His saying ﴿an tarithū al-nisāʾ﴾, meaning: nor that you restrain them. In the first case there is variation in style; in the second the style is on one pattern. But there is no doubt that it is part of eloquence, clarity and rhetoric for style and address to vary when rhetoric requires it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the dowry belongs to the woman; by His saying ﴿you have given them﴾, meaning: you gave them, and this is so. What has passed for us at the beginning of the surah is very clear, that the dowry is the woman's right, in His saying: ﴿And give the women their dowries graciously﴾. Accordingly, if she is legally competent and mature, the matter is in her hands regarding whether she remits part or all of the dowry to her husband, and no one has any objection to her. Likewise, it is not lawful for anyone to take anything from the dowry, neither by choice nor by force, except after the contract is completed and the wife owns her dowry; then she may give away what she wishes to whomever she wishes, if she is competent to donate. Is that so? Good.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that bad conduct permits restraining a woman so that she ransoms herself. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾, meaning: then you may restrain them in order to take away part of what you have given them.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of living with a woman in kindness; by His saying: ﴿And live with them in kindness﴾.
* Among its benefits also: the consideration of custom, the consideration of custom in referring the ruling to it, in referring the ruling to it; by His saying: ﴿in kindness﴾. Allah the Exalted has referred to custom in several places, such as His saying: ﴿And upon the father of the child is their provision and their clothing according to what is customary﴾ [al-Baqarah 233]. But this custom does not count or serve as a reference if it contradicts what the Sharia recognizes, because the Sharia is the judge and governs over custom.
* Among the benefits of this verse: an indication that the husband should be patient when he sees in his wife what he dislikes, for the outcome may be praiseworthy; by His saying: ﴿if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that although the ruling was revealed concerning disliking a wife, the reason is general. A person often dislikes a thing, and Allah, glorified and exalted, makes its outcome praiseworthy and beneficial to him; this is an observed and sensed matter. The outcome may not be praiseworthy, but generally Allah's promise is fulfilled.
If someone says: is "ʿasā" here for certainty or for hope?
* A student: For hope.
* The Shaykh: The scholars said: "ʿasā" from Allah is binding; that is, when Allah says "ʿasā," the matter will certainly occur. They said: among this is His saying: ﴿It is expected that Allah will pardon them, and Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾ [an-Nisa 99]. This is because hope is not applicable with regard to Him, the Mighty and Majestic, since He is the one who disposes and manages; hope is only from one who does not possess a thing and hopes for it from another. Based on this, the verse is a promise from Allah that whoever is patient seeking the face of Allah with what he dislikes, and seeking the reward of Allah, that Allah will make therein much good for him, this promise will be fulfilled for him. If this promise fails to materialize, it is due to the presence of what? Due to the presence of an obstacle; otherwise, the promise of Allah is true.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's attribute of making (ja'l), from where is it taken? ﴿and Allah makes therein much good﴾. We have explained earlier that making is of two kinds: cosmic (kawnī) and what? And legislative (shar'ī). Which predominates in the Qur'an, the cosmic or the legislative making? The cosmic making predominates in the Qur'an. Of the legislative?
* Students: ﴿Allah made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, ...﴾
* The Shaykh: ﴿Allah has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a means of standing for the people, and the sacred month﴾ [al-Ma'idah 97], although this may be a cosmic making. Among that is His saying: ﴿Allah did not institute any bahīrah, sā'ibah, wasīlah, or ḥām﴾ [al-Ma'idah 103], meaning: He did not legislate them, though He did decree them. Likewise His saying: ﴿or Allah makes for them a way﴾, which passed for us recently.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of the occurrence of dislike between a Muslim man and his brother; by His saying: ﴿if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good﴾, where Allah affirmed dislike as a condition and as a fact.
There is no doubt that this occurs: a person may dislike his Muslim brother. But he is commanded, when he finds dislike for his Muslim brother in his heart, to consider why he dislikes him. If it is for a legislative reason, let him advise his brother about that matter until it is removed and the dislike goes away. If it is not for a legislative reason (...), but mere dislike, as happens, then he must treat himself of this disease, for among the firmest bonds of faith is love for the sake of Allah. If that is so, and he finds that he dislikes this man with an ordinary dislike, not due to a flaw in his religion or character, then he must treat this disease until he removes the dislike for his brothers from his heart. ﴿And if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good.﴾ Then he said: all right, now it is time for questions.
