﴿For whoever among you fears falling into sin﴾: the prepositional phrase is the predicate of the subject. The predicate of ﴿This﴾ is omitted, and the estimated meaning is: established or applicable ﴿for whoever among you fears falling into sin﴾.

﴿Fears﴾ means feared. Khashyah (fear with awe) and khawf (fear) are synonyms, so one can replace the other. But the scholars distinguished them: khashyah is only from knowledge, as in His saying: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah﴾ [Fatir 28]. And the cause of khashyah is the greatness of the one feared, even if the one who fears is great. As for khawf, its cause is the weakness of the one who fears, even if the one feared is weak. So khashyah is stronger and more intense.

So His saying ﴿fears falling into sin﴾ means he feared it with a strong fear, meaning he feared it with emphatic fear.

﴿Sin (al-'anat)﴾ means hardship. From it is His saying: ﴿It grieves him that you suffer hardship﴾ [At-Tawbah 128], meaning that which is hard upon you.

His saying ﴿among you﴾ explains the "for whoever" in ﴿for whoever fears﴾.

﴿And that you be patient is better for you﴾: this is a nominal sentence of subject and predicate, but the subject is an interpreted (mu'awwal) construction, since the meaning of ﴿and that you be patient is better for you﴾ is: and your patience. Similar is His saying: ﴿and that you fast is better for you﴾ [Al-Baqarah 184], meaning: and your fasting is better for you. So the subject here is the verbal noun formed from "that" and the verb.

His saying ﴿you be patient﴾ means you restrain yourselves, because patience (sabr) is restraint. You restrain yourselves from what? From marrying slave women, even when the two conditions exist: the inability to afford marriage to a free woman and the fear of falling into sin. Patience is better for you than marrying slave women. The goodness here is unrestricted, and when Allah, the Exalted, leaves something unrestricted it becomes general, meaning it is better for you in every case. But if a person cannot be patient, the matter is flexible.

﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Ending the verse with these two noble names, Forgiving and Merciful, indicates that a person must be extremely cautious in this matter, so that he does not fall into sin. And Allah, the Exalted, only permitted us this because He is described by these two attributes, which the two noble names indicate: forgiveness and mercy.

Forgiveness (maghfirah) is covering a sin and overlooking it. It derives from al-maghfar, which is the iron helmet placed on the head to protect it from arrows. By it there is covering and protection. So forgiveness includes both meanings: covering and protection from punishment. It is not merely covering, nor merely protection from punishment, but both covering and protection.

As for mercy (rahmah), it is one of the attributes of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, which requires kindness to creation and warding off harm from them. Allah, the Exalted, named Himself "the Most Gracious" (al-Rahman) and "the Most Merciful" (al-Rahim), and described Himself as possessing mercy: ﴿And your Lord is the Forgiving, Possessor of mercy﴾ [Al-Kahf 58]. It is an attribute independent of will and of beneficence. According to the early generation (al-salaf) and the imams of Ahl al-Sunnah, it is an attribute additional to, or independent of, will or action.

Whoever does not affirm that Allah has mercy has distorted its meaning. It is said that mercy means the will to bestow favor, or the favor itself. They distorted it to this meaning because they affirm will, so they said: the will to do good, or the good itself. Because the good itself is separate from the Essence, its occurrence from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is not impossible in their view. These are the Ash'aris. In reality, if they returned to themselves they would find that their interpretation of mercy as this implies the affirmation of mercy, because the will to do good is only mercy toward one who deserves it and love for goodness. And the good separate from Allah can only be one of the effects of mercy. In any case, our creed, praise be to Allah, is the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah: that everything Allah named Himself by or described Himself with is affirmed for Him in its true sense, without tamthil (likening) and without takyif (specifying how).

* This noble verse contains benefits. ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford free believing women...﴾ and so on. First: encouragement to marry free believing women. The reason is that Allah did not permit turning away from marrying them except for need and excuse, by His saying: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women﴾.

* Among its benefits: marriage requires wealth, by His saying: ﴿whoever among you cannot afford﴾.

* Among its benefits: whoever cannot afford marriage should not borrow money, but should turn to another way instead of the marriage he is unable to afford. This is supported by His saying: ﴿then from what your right hands possess﴾. This is also supported by the Sunnah, the story of the man who asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to marry him to a woman who had given herself to the Prophet (ﷺ), when he said: "Marry her to me." The Prophet (ﷺ) asked him for the dower, and he said: "I have nothing, not even an iron ring." (He did not say: "Let me borrow.") The Prophet (ﷺ) then asked him: "Do you have anything of the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes." He said: "I have married her to you for what you know of the Qur'an."[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (5029) and Muslim (1425/76) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd.]] This is also supported by His saying: ﴿And let those who cannot find marriage keep chaste until Allah enriches them from His bounty﴾ [An-Nur 33], and by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "O young people, whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry, for it lowers the gaze and guards the private parts. Whoever is not able, let him fast, for it is a shield for him."[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (5066) and Muslim (1400/1) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is permissible for a free man to marry a slave woman under the two stated conditions: that he cannot afford the means to marry a free believing woman, ﴿the chaste believing women﴾. So he may marry believing slave women, as will be mentioned, Allah willing.

* Among its benefits: if he is able to afford the dower of a free woman who is a people of the Book, but not that of a free believing woman, he may marry a believing slave woman. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿the chaste believing women﴾. So if a person has five thousand riyals, which are not enough to marry a free believing woman but are enough to marry a free woman of the People of the Book or a slave woman, may he turn to marrying a slave woman, or must he marry a free woman of the People of the Book? The first: that is, he may turn to marrying a believing slave woman rather than a free woman of the People of the Book. This is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an.

Some scholars said: rather, a free woman of the People of the Book is preferable to a believing slave woman, because the children of a free woman of the People of the Book grow up as free, while the children of a believing slave woman grow up as slaves belonging to her master. This second view is the well-known position of Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him: that if he is able to marry a slave woman or a woman of the People of the Book, he may not marry a slave woman but must marry the woman of the People of the Book.

But the apparent meaning of the Qur'an takes precedence, because Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist, even if she pleases you﴾ [Al-Baqarah 221]. Also, a woman of the People of the Book cannot be trusted not to lead her husband astray, especially if she has high education or is eloquent and strong in expression. She may influence the husband so that he apostatizes and becomes a Jew or Christian. This is especially so if she has wealth and he is poor, for she will influence him. And if she does not influence him, she may influence his children. Therefore the apparent meaning of the Qur'an is what must be followed: that if a person can afford the dower of a free woman of the People of the Book or the dower of a slave woman but not of a free believing woman, it is obligatory that he prefer the slave woman, because Allah said: ﴿the chaste believing women﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the lower rank of slavery compared to the rank of freedom. This is indeed so, for the slave is owned property who is bought and sold and does not own himself. He is managed, so that if he is killed, his blood-money is his value, not the blood-money of a free man. Blood-money varies according to the attributes of the slain. One slave may be killed and his blood-money might be a million riyals, while another slave's blood-money might be ten riyals. Is that not so? Indeed. Therefore there is no doubt that the rank of freedom is higher than the rank of slavery.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is not permissible for one who cannot afford a believing free woman to marry a slave woman of the People of the Book. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿of your believing slave women﴾. So it is not permissible to marry a slave woman of the People of the Book if he cannot afford a believing free woman. If he is not unable to afford a believing free woman, may he marry a slave woman of the People of the Book? That is more so, a fortiori. By this it becomes clear that it is not lawful for a believer to marry a slave woman of the People of the Book. This is supported by His saying: ﴿This day the good things are made lawful for you. The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them. And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you have given them their due compensation﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 5]. Here "chaste women" means free women. It may be that the intended meaning is women chaste from fornication, but this verse shows that the intended meaning is free women, and that slave women from the People of the Book are not lawful to marry in any case.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of the knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, of what is unseen and hidden. This is from His saying: ﴿And Allah knows best your faith﴾.

* Among its benefits: it is permissible to use the comparative form (ism al-tafdil, the elative or superlative form) for the attributes of Allah, so one says: Allah is more knowing (Allah is A'lam), Allah is greater (Akbar), Allah is more mighty (A'azz), Allah is greatest (A'zam), and similar expressions. This differs from the view of those who say it is not permissible and that the comparative must be explained as an active participle. Such a person would say that ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمَانِكُمْ﴾ means "Allah is knowing of your faith." But this person does not realise that his phrase "Allah is knowing of your faith" falls short of ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمَانِكُمْ﴾, because "knowing" ('alim) is an active participle, which does not exclude sharing the attribute or the rank, whereas "more knowing" (a'lam) is a comparative, which excludes sharing the rank. It is a mistaken understanding to take the comparative used of Allah's attributes to mean an active participle, because this undoubtedly involves a deficiency compared with what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intended.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of ownership (al-mulk), namely the ownership that is slavery (al-riqq), as shown by His words: ﴿فَمِنْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾ ("from what your right hands possess"). This ruling remains in force until the Day of Resurrection and cannot be abolished under any circumstances; wherever its lawful causes exist, it is established. Yes, if the causes are absent, as when a person seizes human beings, kidnaps people and brings them to the markets to sell them, then slavery cannot be established by this means. But if slavery is established by a lawful means, it is established and cannot be lifted, as shown by His words: ﴿فَمِنْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾.

Here we ask: is a person's ownership of what he owns, whether a human being, an animal, a property or anything else, complete ownership? The answer is no, it is not complete ownership. That is why a person does not dispose of what he owns as he wishes; rather, his disposal is restricted by the Sharia. However, the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, regarded as full owner the one who has the right of disposal in a complete manner, and regarded as one whose ownership is restricted, for example, a renter, a borrower or something similar.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of applying a part to the whole. From where is this derived?
* Student: "A'lam bi-imanikum."
* Students: (...).
* Shaykh: ﴿فَمِنْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾ "from what your right hands possess." The meaning is "from what you possess," because the hands alone do not possess.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the use of what serves as a cause for the acceptance of a ruling, which we may express as lightening the matter for the one to whom the ruling applies, as shown by His words: ﴿بَعْضُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ ("some of you are from others"). This is because the Arabs had a great aversion to slave women and regarded it as a very serious and grave matter for a man to marry a female slave. They would say: the female slave is property, like a camel is property; so if one marries a female slave, then he is...?
* Student: "Like a camel."
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. They regarded it as very grave. For this reason Allah guided to this matter by His words: ﴿بَعْضُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ﴾, in order to make the matter easier for people. From this it is derived that the speaker should address the listener in a way that makes the ruling easier for him to accept.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the condition that the permission of the family is required for the marriage of slave women, as shown by His words: ﴿فَانْكِحُوهُنَّ بِإِذْنِ أَهْلِهِنَّ﴾ ("marry them with the permission of their families").

* A further benefit follows from this benefit: a woman may not marry herself off.
If someone says: this is evident in the case of a slave woman, that she may not marry herself, because she is owned; but what about a free woman? We say: if she is free, there are other proofs showing that she may not marry herself and that a guardian (wali) is necessary.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a slave woman owns her dower (mahr), as shown by His words: ﴿وَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾ ("give them their wages"), meaning the dowers. Some scholars held this view and said: the dower of a slave woman belongs to her, because she needs to adorn herself for her husband and to prepare the place, the house, the kitchen and other things for the husband. So her dower should not go to her master, since this is something her needs depend on. However, the majority of scholars disagree, holding that the dower of a slave woman belongs to her master, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever sells a slave who has property, his property belongs to the one who sold him."[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (2379) and Muslim (1543/80) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar.]]
They said: the attribution of the wages to them is either by way of specification or by way of considering the cause, because they are the cause of this dower; had it not been for them, the dower would not have come to their master. This is closer to the general principles of the Sharia.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the reference to custom ('urf). From where is this derived?
* Student: From His words ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ ("in a fair manner").
* Shaykh: It is derived from His words ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾, and this is a principle: for anything the Sharia has not defined, we refer to custom.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the condition that the marriage be a marriage of chastity (nikah ihsan), as shown by His words: ﴿مُحْصَنَاتٍ غَيْرَ مُسَافِحَاتٍ وَلَا مُتَّخِذَاتِ أَخْدَانٍ﴾ ("chaste, not fornicating, nor taking secret lovers"). A marriage of chastity is one whose conditions are fulfilled and whose impediments are absent; that is the marriage of chastity. If its conditions are not fulfilled, it is fornication (sifah); and if its impediments exist, it is fornication. An example of the first: if he marries a woman under compulsion, this marriage is fornication because the condition is missing. An example of the second: if he marries a woman during her waiting period ('idda), here the marriage is fornication because of the existing impediment, which is the waiting period.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that ihsan (chastity) applies to purity (iffah). From where is this derived? From His words: ﴿مُحْصَنَاتٍ غَيْرَ مُسَافِحَاتٍ﴾, where fornication is set in contrast to chastity.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the prohibition of taking secret lovers from among men, as shown by His words: ﴿وَلَا مُتَّخِذَاتِ أَخْدَانٍ﴾, even if no adultery occurs. Taking secret lovers, meaning companions and friends, is a cause of adultery; for this reason seclusion with a woman is forbidden out of fear of it, and it is forbidden for a woman to soften her speech out of fear of it.

* A consequence of this benefit: an explanation of the immoral condition of Western society, in which many of them have a female companion and girlfriend whom he goes out with, spends the night with her and she spends the night with him, but he does not have intercourse with her, because they do not consider intercourse lawful except within a marriage contract; yet they may well have intercourse. It is well known that when a person is alone with a woman and prolongs his stay and conversation with her, Satan flows through the son of Adam like blood, leading both of them astray, and evil results.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: if a slave woman commits adultery, she is subject to the prescribed punishment (hadd), as shown by His words: ﴿فَإِذَا أُحْصِنَّ فَإِنْ أَتَيْنَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ فَعَلَيْهِنَّ نِصْفُ مَا عَلَى الْمُحْصَنَاتِ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ﴾ ("When they are chaste, if they commit an immorality, then for them is half the punishment of free chaste women").

* And from it: there is no hadd punishment on her unless she is chaste; as shown by His words: ﴿فَإِذَا أُحْصِنَّ فَإِنْ أَتَيْنَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ﴾. If she commits adultery before becoming chaste, there is no hadd punishment on her; rather she is flogged with a discretionary flogging (ta'zir). As for what is reported in some narrations of Muslim: "Let him flog her the hadd," scholars have mentioned that the word "the hadd" (al-hadd) is an error of the narrator, as if he thought that flogging is only by hadd, so he said: "let him flog her the hadd." What supports this is that in the other narration it says: "let him flog her,"[[Related by al-Bukhari (2152) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] without restricting it to the hadd. And this is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an: there is no hadd punishment on her unless she is chaste; before that, her penalty is ta'zir.

And among the benefits of this noble verse: a slave woman who commits adultery is not stoned, even if she has married, because stoning cannot be halved, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَعَلَيْهِنَّ نِصْفُ مَا عَلَى الْمُحْصَنَاتِ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ﴾ ("then for them is half the punishment of the chaste women"). For this reason the scholars made a condition for stoning that the adulteress be free.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: if a slave woman commits adultery after becoming chaste, she is banished for half a year, on the general wording of His words: ﴿فَعَلَيْهِنَّ نِصْفُ مَا عَلَى الْمُحْصَنَاتِ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ﴾. This is based on the banishment (taghrib) of a free woman being established, which is a matter of scholarly disagreement. Some scholars say that banishment applies only to men and not to women, and they gave the reason that banishing a woman encourages her to wrongdoing, because when she is banished she is separated from her family and from those who watch over her, and the evil done by her becomes greater than if she were with her family. So they said: a free woman is not banished. On this view, a slave woman is not banished a fortiori. Then, on the view that a free woman is banished, as is apparent from the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit: "For a virgin with a virgin, a hundred lashes and a year's banishment,"[[Related by Muslim (1690/13) and Abu Dawud (4415) from the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, in similar wording.]] the question remains: is a slave woman banished or not? If we take the general wording of His words: ﴿فَعَلَيْهِنَّ نِصْفُ مَا عَلَى الْمُحْصَنَاتِ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ﴾, what is the ruling?
* Student: Then she is banished for half a year.
* Shaykh: Then she is banished for half a year. But if we say that the slave woman has an impediment to banishment, which is the right of her master, because if she is banished she may flee and not return to her master. Furthermore, she has such lowliness of station, or humble standing, that it does not prevent her from indecency, unlike a free woman. For this reason some scholars held that there is no banishment for slave women or slave men, for the reason we mentioned: their banishment would encourage them to commit indecency, because they are below free people in nobility and do not care whether they commit indecency. This view is strong, very strong, that she is not banished.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the permissibility of marrying slave women is conditional upon a person suffering hardship by abstaining from it, as shown by His words: ﴿ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ الْعَنَتَ مِنْكُمْ﴾ ("That is for whoever among you fears hardship").

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the excellence of arrangement in the context of the Qur'an, because Allah, Glorified and Exalted, mentioned the matter of adultery between the mention of the conditions for marrying a slave woman, to point out that a slave woman has such lowliness of station that it does not prevent her from adultery. This is part of the prohibition of marrying slave women except under the conditions. So two conditions apply: the first condition is that he cannot afford the dower of a free believing woman; the second condition is that he fears hardship from abstaining from marriage. Some scholars made a further condition: that he cannot afford the price of a slave woman. They said: if he can afford the price of a slave woman, it is not lawful for him to marry a slave woman. They derived this condition from the meaning, although it is not in the verse, but they derived it from the meaning. They said: if he is able to pay the price of a slave woman, he buys a slave woman and has intercourse with her by right of ownership, not by marriage, and intercourse by right of ownership is an honour and a dignity even among the Arabs. Furthermore, if she bears him a child, the child is free, not a slave. Some scholars, including the jurists of Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on them, made the condition that he be unable to afford the price of a slave woman; if he can afford the price of a slave woman, he buys her. Let us give an example: the dower of a free believing woman is ten thousand, the dower of a Christian woman is eight thousand, the value of a slave woman is six thousand, and the dower of a slave woman is five thousand, for example. He is now able, he has six thousand. The first condition is fulfilled, which is that he cannot afford the dower of a free woman; but here he is able to buy a slave woman and take her as a concubine. Shall we say to him: you may turn away from this and marry a slave woman for five thousand? If we say it is a condition, we say: you do not own her; buy a slave woman and take her as a concubine. If we say it is not a condition, as the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates, we say: you have a choice; if you wish, buy one, and if you wish, do not buy one. For he may say: if I buy a slave woman, duties become incumbent upon me that would not be incumbent upon me if she were a wife. Because if she is a wife and Allah does not create affection between them, what does he do? He divorces her and her master takes charge of her. But if she is his slave and bears him a child, what does he do? According to the well-known school view, she may not be sold, meaning he is obliged to maintain her while he does not want her. He says: I do not want to take a concubine, because duties may fall on me that would not fall on me if she were a wife.

In any case, holding to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an is better: we say the condition is: that he cannot afford the dower of a free woman; and that if he can afford the price of a slave woman, he is permitted to marry a slave woman.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that abstaining from marrying slave women is better than marrying them, even though that is permissible, as shown by His, Exalted, words: ﴿وَأَنْ تَصْبِرُوا خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾ ("that you be patient is better for you").

* And from it: that the permissible may have equal sides, as is the basic position, and it may be less preferred, as here; because Allah, Exalted, made marrying slave women lawful for us under the two conditions, but He said: ﴿وَأَنْ تَصْبِرُوا خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾.

* And from it: that a command to do something may be inferred from praise of the one who does it, as shown by His words: ﴿وَأَنْ تَصْبِرُوا خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾. It is as if He said: be patient, but He phrased it as encouragement.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of these two names of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the attributes they include, namely: the Most Forgiving (al-Ghafur) and the Most Merciful (al-Rahim).

* Student: Shaykh, the fighting now taking place between the Muslims and the Jews in Palestine: is it lawful to take their women and make them slaves?
Shaykh: What do you say? If a war broke out, it would be lawful; if war broke out, it would be lawful. But now it is not lawful, except if a group with strength entered Jewish lands and took the women as lawful, then that would be valid.
* Student: The Serbs?
* Shaykh: No, the Serbs are a war. The Serbs are engaged in war between them and the Muslims. Even with the Jews, the apparent position is that if there is no treaty, the default is war.
* Student: A sham treaty.
* Shaykh: (...) He pardoned seven of them and appointed ten in their place.

* * *

* Shaykh: (...) In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. And because a Christian woman cannot be trusted not to lead her husband astray, especially if she holds a high qualification and he does not have such a qualification, or if she is eloquent and strong in expression, she may influence the husband so that he apostatises and becomes a Jew or a Christian. Especially also if she has wealth and he is poor, she will influence him; and if she does not influence him, perhaps she will influence his children. For this reason the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, which must be followed, is that we say: if he can afford the dower of a free Christian woman, or the dower of a slave woman rather than a free believing woman, then the obligation is to give precedence to the slave woman. The correct position is to say: he has a choice, because a free Christian woman is lawful for him to marry.
(He has a choice) replaces (the obligation is to give precedence to the slave woman).
* Student: The evidence?
* Shaykh: The evidence for permissibility.
Student: (...).
Shaykh: (He has a choice) because Allah said: ﴿الْمُحْصَنَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾ ("chaste believing women"), replacing (the obligation is to give precedence to the slave woman). We will write (he has a choice) and what follows it.
* Student: And the verse?
* Shaykh: The verse says: ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنْكُمْ طَوْلًا أَنْ يَنْكِحَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ فَمِنْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ مِنْ فِتَيَاتِكُمُ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾ ("And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women, then from what your right hands possess of your believing young women"), meaning: marry from what your right hands possess.
If he is able to afford a means, but it is the means for a free Christian woman, then he now has a choice: if he wishes, he marries the free Christian woman, since it is permissible for him to marry her in every case; and if he wishes, he marries the slave woman. The difference between a believing woman and a Christian woman here is that if he can afford the dower of a believing woman, the slave woman becomes unlawful to him; but if he can afford the dower of a free Christian woman, he has a choice.
* Student: If he can afford a free believing woman, it is permissible for him.
* Shaykh: No, it is not permissible for him to marry a slave woman.
* Student: The Christian woman.
* Shaykh: Leave the Christian woman; the verse does not address her. But the brothers may be confused by the condition of faith. We say: the benefit is this: if he can afford the dower of a free believing woman, the slave woman becomes unlawful to him; if he cannot afford the dower of a free believing woman, the slave woman becomes lawful to him.
As for the free Christian woman, she is lawful to him in origin; therefore he has a choice between marrying the free Christian woman, on the basis that she is lawful to him in origin, or marrying the slave woman. This differs from the case where he can afford the dower of a free believing woman, in which case it is not lawful for him to marry a slave woman. The difference between this and that is: if he can afford the dower of a free believing woman, marrying a Christian woman becomes unlawful to him; and if he can afford the dower of a free Christian woman, he may marry a slave woman, on the implication of the verse: ﴿أَنْ يَنْكِحَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has given the person a choice when he finds the dower of a free Christian woman or the dower of a slave woman, between the two, by way of the implication of the verse.
Then, should he give precedence to the Muslim slave woman or the free Christian woman? He considers the benefit; we follow the indication of the verse, setting aside the disagreement of the scholars. It may be in his interest to marry a free Christian woman, and it may be the opposite, except if he stipulates that his children from the slave woman will be free; in that case the slave woman becomes the only option.
* Student: But what troubles me about this is His words, Exalted: ﴿وَلَا تَنْكِحُوا الْمُشْرِكَاتِ﴾ ("Do not marry polytheistic women") [al-Baqarah 221], and His words: ﴿وَلَنْ يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ سَبِيلًا﴾ ("And Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers") [al-Nisa 141]?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 25 (part 4 of 4):

* The Shaykh: No, Allah said: ﴿And do not marry polytheistic women﴾. He said it in Surah al-Baqarah, and in Surah al-Ma'idah: ﴿And chaste women from among the believing women and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you have given them their due compensation﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5]. Al-Ma'idah is among the last surahs revealed, after al-Baqarah.
* Student: (...) he gave us the choice between a disbelieving and a believing woman?
* The Shaykh: There is no contradiction, even if we suppose that he has the bridal payment of a free believing woman and the bridal payment of a free woman from the People of the Book; he has the choice: if he wishes, he may take a free believing woman, and if he wishes, he may take a free woman from the People of the Book.
* Student: Shaykh, (...) her master?
* The Shaykh: If he stipulates their freedom, then apparently in this case the prohibition is removed, except when he finds the bridal payment of a free believing woman. The correct view is that it is not permissible to marry a slave woman even if he stipulates that her children will be free, contrary to Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him.
* Student: Concerning the words of the Exalted: ﴿And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5], who are "those who were given the Scripture before you"?
* The Shaykh: "Those who were given the Scripture before you" means the Jews and the Christians.
* The Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, because they came before them; it is a statement of the reality, lest anyone who possesses a scripture, even those who claim to have a scripture, such as the Magians for instance, think that they are included. They say that they have a scripture that was lifted, and that they have a semblance of a scripture. The correct view is that they have no semblance of a scripture, and that marrying their women is not lawful, and that the jizyah is taken from them, as established in al-Bukhari[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3157) from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf.]], because it is taken from every disbeliever.
* Student: O Shaykh, regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿And chaste women from among the believing women﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5], some scholars say: the believing women here are mentioned by way of the predominant case, and the intended meaning is chaste women in general, including the women of the Scripture and others. Is this correct?
* The Shaykh: No, that is not correct, because there is a distinction between the believer and the disbeliever, a distinction between the believer and the disbeliever.
* The Student: According to this view, it is lawful for him to marry a woman from the People of the Book, and he does not have a choice; and if he has the bridal payment of a free woman from the People of the Book, he may not take a believing slave woman, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, stipulated "chaste women."
* The Shaykh: No, "believing women."
* The Student: "Believing women"; he says: by way of predominance.
* The Shaykh: No, that is not correct; we do not agree with this.
* The Student: How do we refute this?
* The Shaykh: We refute it by saying that the original principle regarding a qualifier is that it restricts.
* The Student: Without it, O Shaykh, does not the other verse say that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made lawful the chaste women from the People of the Book?
* The Shaykh: The women of the People of the Book, yes, it is lawful, and that is why we did not forbid it. We told him: if you have the bridal payment of a free believing woman, the slave woman is forbidden to you; it is forbidden for you to marry a slave woman. If you have the bridal payment of a free woman from the People of the Book, the apparent meaning of the verse is that you may marry a slave woman.
* Student: Shaykh, did Allah, Mighty and Majestic, equate the chaste believing woman with the chaste woman of the Scripture?
* The Shaykh: Where is that found?
* The Student: In the verse: ﴿It is made lawful for you﴾ ﴿and chaste women﴾.
* The Shaykh: There is no contradiction; this concerns marriage in its basic form. But in marriage to a slave woman, meaning a person moving from marrying a free woman to marrying a slave woman, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, stipulated that he not find the bridal payment of a free believing woman. If he finds the bridal payment of a free woman from the People of the Book, the apparent meaning of the verse is that he may marry a slave woman.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, is the slave woman not of a higher rank than the free woman from the People of the Book?
* The Shaykh: Each one is higher than the other in some respect: this one is higher in terms of Islam, and that one is higher in terms of freedom. If a free woman from the People of the Book is married, her children are free; and if a Muslim slave woman is married, her children are slaves.
* The Student: So this is in the respect you mentioned?
* The Shaykh: Each one is higher than the other in some respect.
* Student: Is marrying a woman (...) not...?
* The Shaykh: That is a second issue; it is not included in the topic.
* Student: Your eminence, is wealth necessary in marriage? "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married a man to a woman for what he had of the Qur'an."
* The Shaykh: Yes, because he did not find wealth, so he married her to him for what he had of the Qur'an, to teach the woman; and teaching is a substitute for which wealth may be taken.
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed.
* Student: May Allah bless you, O Shaykh. A man (...) a slave woman; this price he can use to buy a slave woman, and this price he can use to marry a slave woman, but he cannot use it to marry a free woman?
* The Shaykh: Meaning that he can obtain a slave woman by ownership or by marriage, is that it?
* Student: It exists in detail.
* The Shaykh: Yes, it exists; but in any case he buys the slave woman, because he will have intercourse with her by right of ownership and her children will be free.
* Student: Obligatory, O Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: According to the school, it is obligatory; there is a second opinion: no.
* Student: (....) the correct view regarding them, O Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: We mentioned in the explanation, we said: each one has a defect. If I buy the slave woman, I am burdened with her maintenance and troubled by her; and a wife, I divorce her and free myself from her, as is clear in the discussion.
* Student: If he marries a slave woman, O Shaykh, then the child who comes from her will be a slave, a bondsman.
* The Shaykh: A slave belonging to her owner.
* The Student: Yes indeed, O Shaykh; when she became pregnant, she was freed. Would the fetus then be free or a slave?
* The Shaykh: It follows its mother unless a condition is stipulated.
* The Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, it follows its mother.
* Student: We say: regarding the problem (...) her son (...) people will come and mock him; it will become a problem?
* The Shaykh: Yes, they will say to him: "O son of the slave woman!" That is why Allah, Mighty and Majestic, stipulated these conditions.
* Student: The words of the Exalted: ﴿And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist﴾ — by way of a stronger argument, the free woman is more so.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, there is no doubt.
* The Student: And does absolute superiority include both the free and the slave woman?
* The Shaykh: I think we mentioned two opinions in the tafsir, do you remember? Is the intended "slave woman" the one in bondage or the free one, because the Messenger ﷺ said: "Do not prevent Allah's female servants from Allah's mosques"[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (900) and Muslim (442/136) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar.]]. Likewise, the "servant" ( 'abd): is it the bondsman or the believing servant? Because the believer is a servant of Allah's servants, and whichever it is, there is no doubt that he is a Muslim, and even a slave in bondage is better than a polytheist.
* The Student: The distinction we mentioned, according to the degree of goodness in the verse, is it absolute?
* The Shaykh: Yes, but, may Allah bless you, the verse in Surah al-Baqarah, "the polytheistic women," does not refer to the women of the People of the Book; the People of the Book are not counted among the polytheists: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell﴾ [al-Bayyinah 6]. The People of the Book have special rulings, which is why their slaughtered animals are lawful, while the slaughter of a polytheist is not lawful.
* Student: What about one who fears marrying a free polytheist woman from the People of the Book, lest his children be enslaved?
* The Shaykh: He cannot enslave them.
* The Student: Perhaps she would go to the lands of disbelief?
* The Shaykh: No, he prevents them; he has the right to prevent them. It is not permissible for her to travel to the lands of the People of the Book.

I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan.

﴿Allah desires to make clear to you, and to guide you to the ways of those before you, and to turn to you in forgiveness. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ (26) ﴿And Allah desires to turn to you in forgiveness, but those who follow their desires desire that you deviate into a great deviation.﴾ (27) ﴿Allah desires to lighten for you, and man was created weak.﴾ (28) ﴿O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, except through trade by mutual consent among you. And do not kill yourselves. Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you.﴾ (29) ﴿And whoever does that in aggression and injustice, We will drive him into a Fire, and that is ever easy for Allah.﴾ [An-Nisa 26-30].

I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan. The Blessed and Exalted Allah said: ﴿Allah desires to make clear to you, and to guide you to the ways of those before you﴾. ﴿Desires﴾: the will (irada) here is the legislative will (irada shar'iyyah). The will of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is divided into two types: the universal will (irada kawniyyah) and the legislative will (irada shar'iyyah). The difference between them is that the legislative will relates to what He loves and approves of only, and what is willed by it may or may not occur. As for the universal will, it relates to everything He wills, and it may be something He loves or something He dislikes, and what is willed by it must occur, because it has the meaning of His will (mashi'ah). What Allah wills occurs, and what He does not will does not occur. So if the word "irada" means "love" (mahabbah), meaning that it may be replaced by "uhibbu" or "yuhibbu" (he loves), then it is the legislative will. And if it may be replaced by "yashao" or "sha'a" (he wills), then it is the universal will.

The Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Allah desires to make clear to you﴾, meaning: He loves that. He has done it, glorified and exalted is He, and has made clear to us in the utmost clarity in a clear Arabic tongue. The lam in His words ﴿li-yubayyina﴾ is extra (za'idah). It is an extra lam, which may indicate causation (ta'lil) and may not indicate causation, but rather serve to transitive the verb (ta'diyah). However, if it were omitted, and it were said: "Allah desires to make clear to you," like His words ﴿And Allah desires to turn to you in forgiveness﴾, the sentence would still be correct. But it has come, and they say that the lam after "irada" is extra. Every lam of genitive (jarr) after "irada" is extra; "aradtu li-kadha" means "aradtu kadha" (I wanted such-and-such).

His words ﴿li-yubayyina lakum﴾: the clarification (bayan) here includes verbal clarification (al-bayan al-lafdhi) and meaningful clarification (al-bayan al-ma'nawi), and both occur. Allah said to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation. So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation. Then upon Us is its clarification﴾ [Al-Qiyamah 16-19]. "Its clarification" means its manifestation. When Jibril would recite the Qur'an to him, the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) would hasten, rush, and snatch it from him out of love for it and compassion for it, meaning out of love for the Qur'an and compassion for it. So it was said to him: "Do not hasten." ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation.﴾ The pronoun in ﴿upon Us (alayna)﴾ refers to Allah, and what is meant is Jibril, for he is the one who recites it to Jibril. ﴿So when We have recited it﴾ means: when Jibril has recited it. ﴿Then follow its recitation. Then upon Us is its clarification﴾: the verbal and meaningful clarification.

﴿And to guide you to the ways of those before you﴾: ﴿yahdiyakum﴾ refers to guidance of indication (hidayat al-dalalah) and guidance of success (hidayat al-tawfiq). As for guidance of indication, it is what He sent down of revelation and sharia (sharʿ, divine law). As for guidance of success, it is that He grants success to whomever He wills of His servants to adhere to this guidance. Among the examples of guidance in the sense of indication is His saying: ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ [Fussilat 17]. ﴿We guided them﴾ means: We showed them the path of truth, but they preferred blindness over guidance.

As for guidance in the sense of success, it is in His saying: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾ [Al-Qasas 56], meaning: you cannot grant him success in following the path of guidance, because that is up to Allah.

﴿The ways (sunan) of those before you﴾: "sunan" is the plural of "sunnah," which is the way (tariqah). What is meant by "their ways" is what they were upon of legislations (shara'i'). However, the legislations differ according to the differences of nations and the differences of times and places: ﴿For each of you We have made a law (shir'ah) and a method (minhaj)﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 48]. But the basis is that people are equal in it.

His words ﴿the ways of those before you﴾ mean: the Jews, the Christians, and others to whom revelation was sent.

﴿And to turn to you in forgiveness﴾: ﴿yatuba﴾ is in the accusative case, coordinated (ʿataf) upon ﴿yubayyina﴾, meaning: and He desires to turn to you in forgiveness, that is, He grants you success in repentance (tawbah). The turning of Allah toward the servant is of two types: the turning of granting success to repent, and the turning of accepting repentance. Of the first is His saying: ﴿Certainly Allah turned in forgiveness to the Prophet and the Muhajirin and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of hardship, after the hearts of a group of them had nearly inclined away. Then He turned to them in forgiveness. Indeed, He is to them Kind, Merciful﴾ [At-Tawbah 117]. ﴿He turned to them﴾ means: He granted them success to repent, so that they would repent. Of the second is the repentance that is the acceptance of the repentance of those who repent, in His saying: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds﴾ [Ash-Shura 25]. The verse in His words ﴿and to turn to you in forgiveness﴾ here includes both meanings.

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾: ﴿ʿalim﴾: knowledge (ilm) is the perception of a thing as it actually is. By our saying "perception" we exclude ignorance (jahl), because it is not perception. By our saying "as it actually is" we exclude compound ignorance (jahl murakkab), because the one with compound ignorance perceives a thing contrary to what it actually is. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is ʿAlim, meaning possessor of knowledge. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has explained in another verse that His knowledge is vast, comprehensive, and encompasses everything in totality and in detail: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. And not a leaf falls but that He knows it, nor a grain within the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry but that it is in a clear register﴾ [Al-An'am 59].

﴿Hakim﴾ means: possessor of judgment and wisdom (hikmah). We have already explained this, and we showed that the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is in legislative judgment and universal judgment, and that it appears in the form of a thing and in its purpose, that is, formal and final.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of the will of Allah, from His saying: ﴿Allah desires to make clear to you﴾. And this will, is it eternal (azaliyyah) or is it originated (hadithah)?

We say: the will is of two kinds: eternal will and originated will. The will that accompanies the act is originated will, and the will that precedes the act is eternal will. This becomes clear to you through an example: you now want to pray ʿIsha. This is a will that precedes the act. When the call to prayer is made, you rise to prayer and pray. This is a will that accompanies the act. So the will of Allah that accompanies His act is originated, and His eternal will that precedes His act, and He is the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, of everything that will be, this is eternal will.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the vastness of the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, toward His servants, in that He willed to make clear to them. This is from His kindness and generosity, that He does not leave people in their ignorance.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that there is nothing in the sharia that is unknown to everyone, from His saying: ﴿li-yubayyina lakum﴾. The sharia cannot be hidden from everyone, but it may be hidden from a person for reasons: either lack of knowledge, or deficiency of understanding, or negligence in seeking, or bad intention. There are four causes for the hiddenness of a legal ruling from a person. The first: lack of knowledge, such as when a person has not reviewed, has not studied, and has not comprehended the books of scholars. The legal rulings are hidden from him because of his lack of knowledge. Or deficiency of his understanding: he has wide knowledge but is a blockhead who does not understand; much of the legal rulings also escapes him. Or negligence in seeking: a person who is negligent, who has knowledge and understanding, but does not strive to verify questions, refine them, and clarify them, so much escapes him. The fourth: bad intention, such that he wants only to support his own opinion. This one, we seek refuge with Allah, is deprived of goodness and deprived of correctness. Well, what is the remedy for these ailments and afflictions?

The first: lack of knowledge, its remedy is abundance of knowledge: that a person reviews and studies the books of scholars, the books of hadith, the books of tafsir, and reviews. Deficiency of understanding: this is a problem because it is an innate disposition (gharizah). But be assured that through practice one attains strength of understanding. Through practice one attains strength of understanding. Let me give you an example: if a person reviews the books of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, the first time he reviews them he will say: "These contain the barrier of Gog and Magog, we cannot understand them." But with practice upon them, he understands them.

Because of causes: either lack of knowledge, or deficiency of understanding, or negligence in seeking, or bad intention. Four causes for the hiddenness of a legal ruling from a person:

The first: lack of knowledge, such as when a person has not reviewed, has not studied, and has not comprehended the books of scholars. The legal rulings are hidden from him because of his lack of knowledge.

Or: deficiency of his understanding. He has wide knowledge, but is a blockhead who does not understand. Much of the legal rulings also escapes him.

Or: his negligence in seeking. A negligent person who has knowledge and understanding, but does not strive to verify questions, refine them, and clarify them, so much escapes him.

The fourth: bad intention, such that he wants only to support his own opinion. This one, we seek refuge with Allah, is deprived of goodness and deprived of correctness.

What is the remedy for these ailments and afflictions? The first: lack of knowledge. Its remedy is abundance of knowledge: that a person reviews and studies the books of scholars, the books of hadith, the books of tafsir, and reviews. Deficiency of understanding?

* Students: (...).

* The Shaykh: This is a problem, because it is innate. But be assured that through practice one attains strength of understanding. Through practice one attains strength of understanding. Let me give you an example: if a person reviews the books of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, the first time he reviews them he will say: "These contain the barrier of Gog and Magog, we cannot understand them." But with practice upon them, he understands them, and they become to him like al-Fatihah. So understanding requires practice. Among the exercises of understanding is discussion with people. He discusses, because often something of knowledge escapes you, and through discussion much becomes clear to you. Understanding.

The third: negligence in seeking. Its remedy is diligence and striving. Strive, do not slacken. Then, negligence in seeking does not mean a small amount of seeking; even the lack of arrangement in seeking harms a person and diminishes knowledge. Some people, for example, when they want to review a question in the large books, begin to scan the index, find a section, then go and research it, and forget the first. The first need they forget. This is an error. This is what cuts your time into pieces. As long as you want to verify a question, close your eyes to everything else, or else you will be like one who gleans locusts from barren land and gains nothing. Suppose you want to study a question on purification. You review the index, and pass over a question other than the one you want. You write: "I will review this, this is a good section, I want to see what the author says." Your time is wasted. This is negligence in seeking. It is not quantitative negligence, but qualitative negligence.

The fourth: bad intention. This is after a cause. Bad intention requires sincerity and advising for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. When a person intends to preserve the sharia, benefit creation, and inherit the prophets, good intention becomes easy for him, because when he knows that if a person seeks knowledge for other than Allah, he is deprived of goodness and is subject to threat, and that Allah removes the blessing of knowledge from him, he will be keen to make his intention good. These four matters are what a person is deprived of, in failing to clarify the legal rulings. Otherwise, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has guaranteed: ﴿Allah desires to make clear to you﴾ [An-Nisa 26].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the perfection of this Ummah and its sharia, from His saying: ﴿and to guide you to the ways of those before you﴾ [An-Nisa 26]. There is no good that the nations possessed except that this Ummah has a share of it.

﴿And to guide you to the ways of those before you﴾. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) gave the example of himself among the prophets before him as a palace, built and admired by observers, except that when they walked around it, they said: "This palace is complete except for the place of this brick, for it is a flaw." He said: "So I am the brick." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3535), and Muslim (2286/22) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.] Allah completed with it the noble characteristics and beautiful deeds, so the palace was completed by him (peace and blessings be upon him). This is also indicated by His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you﴾ [Al-Baqarah 183]. Why did He say: ﴿as it was prescribed for those before you﴾? As an honor to this Ummah, and that it was completed with the virtues that others had, and also as consolation for it; that is, do not think that our obligation of fasting upon you is specific to you, but it is for you and for others.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, loves those who turn in repentance. From where do we take this?

* A student: Because Allah, glorified, has made clear that He desires to turn to people in forgiveness, and what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, desires is undoubtedly something required of us.

* The Shaykh: Yes, this is the will of love. So Allah, the Exalted, loves for us to repent. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves﴾ [Al-Baqarah 222].

* And it branches from this: the ultimate generosity of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Its aspect: is repentance beneficial to Him or to us?

* Students: To us.

* The Shaykh: Who benefits from it? We do, and He loves it for our benefit. It has been established from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): "Allah rejoices at the repentance of His servant more than a man who lost his camel in a barren desert, searched for it and did not find it, so he lay down under a tree, waiting for death, having despaired of life. Then suddenly the rope of his camel was there, so he took hold of it and said: 'O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your lord.' He erred from the intensity of joy." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6309), and Muslim (2747/7), and the wording is his, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.] They must be prepared for it, meaning as if they are prepared for Allah's warning to them, prepared for the warning. I do not see this, and praise be to Allah, the one standing in prayer, and the one sleeping is excused, and it is a communal obligation (fardh kifayah), not an individual obligation upon..

* A student: Shaykh, if a trustworthy person who is certain informs me, Shaykh...

* The Shaykh: What?

* The student: That the moon has eclipsed and the sun has been eclipsed, is prayer obligatory on me, Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: After its time has ended?

* The student: No, now the moon eclipsed suddenly, meaning there was no call to prayer. So is it obligatory on me?

* The Shaykh: Did you not see it yourself?

* The student: I did not see it.

* The Shaykh: But is this one who told you trustworthy?

* The student: And certain.

* The Shaykh: Yes, there is no contradiction. It means he prays just as if he had informed you of the entry of the time.

* A student: Shaykh, may we pray at home, is it valid?

* The Shaykh: It is valid, based on the generality of His saying: "Pray" [part of a hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1041), and Muslim (911/22), from the hadith of Abu Mas'ud al-Badri.] But the Sunnah is congregation.

* A student: There is a paper with you, Shaykh (...).

* The Shaykh: It is obligatory. The 'aqiqah is not obligatory, because the one responsible for it is the father. Changing the name: if the name is one of the names of non-Muslims, he changes it to the name of a Muslim person, to a Muslim name.

* A student: Immediately?

* The Shaykh: Immediately. Yes, what?

* The student: The circumcision?

* The Shaykh: Circumcision immediately.

* The student: He fears, Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: Who fears?

* The student: This one who has recently become Muslim.

* The Shaykh: A Muslim by choice is not one who fears, because the procedure now is easy, praise be to Allah. Yes, if we see that his Islam is fragile, we wait a while. Whose turn is it?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 26 (part 2 of 2):

﴿وَاللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [النساء ٢٧] Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah desires to accept your repentance﴾.

* Student: Explain the benefits, the benefits.
* Shaykh: Have you not finished?
* Student: We have taken five benefits.
* Shaykh: What are they?
* Student: First: affirmation of the attribute of will (irada) for Allah.
Second: the vastness of the mercy of Allah the Mighty and Majestic toward His servants.
Third: that there is nothing in the Sharia (sacred law) that is unknown to everyone.
Fourth: the perfection of this Ummah (community) and its Sharia.
Fifth: that Allah the Mighty and Majestic loves those who repent often (al-tawwabin).
* Shaykh: Excellent, well done.
* Among the benefits of this verse: affirmation of two of Allah's names, al-'Alim (the All-Knowing) and al-Hakim (the All-Wise), and what they contain of attributes. Al-'Alim contains knowledge, and al-Hakim contains judgment and wisdom, since it is derived from hukm (judgment) and hikmah (wisdom).
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a person's conviction in what Allah the Mighty and Majestic decrees of legislative rulings (ahkam shar'iyyah) and cosmic decrees (ahkam kawniyyah). The reason: what Allah the Mighty and Majestic decrees of rulings is accompanied by what?
* Students: By wisdom.
* Shaykh: And once you know that, you are convinced, whether these are cosmic or legislative rulings. Even the calamities that befall the servants certainly have a wisdom, and a person is convinced of their existence and does not object, does not object to Allah the Exalted through them.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse, in the matter of conduct (al-faedah al-maslakiyyah): watchfulness of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, watchfulness of Allah in private and in public. From where is this derived? From the affirmation of the attribute of knowledge, for whenever you know that Allah knows you, this necessarily produces in you watchfulness of Allah the Glorified and Exalted; that He not find you where He has forbidden you, nor miss you where He has commanded you.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: an allusion to repentance (tawbah). This was discussed recently, and we explained that the conditions of repentance are how many?
* Students: Five.
* Shaykh: Five.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 27–28:

Then He said: ﴿And Allah desires to accept your repentance, while those who follow their desires desire that you deviate into a great deviation﴾. Someone may say: this, together with what precedes it, is repetition, for He said: ﴿Allah desires to make clear to you and guide you﴾ and ﴿to turn to you in forgiveness﴾. So how does He say: ﴿And Allah desires to accept your repentance﴾? We say: the benefit of this is two things:

* The first thing: emphasis (tawkid). When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, emphasizes that He desires to accept our repentance, this is something that gladdens us and increases our eagerness to seek the repentance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* The second benefit: preparation (tawti'ah). His saying: ﴿and those who follow their desires desire﴾ means a paving and preparation for what is mentioned after it, namely that Allah has this desire, and those who follow their desires have this desire. For this reason He repeated it. ﴿And Allah desires to accept your repentance, while those who follow their desires desire that you deviate into a great deviation﴾. ﴿Those who follow their desires desire﴾: who are they?

It includes the disbelievers and the sinners, because the disbeliever desires desires; rather, he follows desires, and so does the sinner. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Then there succeeded them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed desires, so they will meet evil (ghayy)﴾ ﴿except those who repent﴾ [Maryam 59–60]. So those who follow their desires are the disbelievers and the grossly sinful, who desire that you deviate a great deviation. ﴿That you deviate﴾ means: that you swerve from what Allah, Glorified and Exalted, desires for you of the means of repentance, which are performing the commands and abandoning the prohibitions. Thus they desire one thing while Allah desires the opposite.

Then He said: ﴿Allah desires to lighten (the burden) for you, and man was created weak﴾ [An-Nisa 28]. ﴿Allah desires to lighten for you﴾: lightening is the opposite of burdening. His lightening, Glorified and Exalted, is a lightening in the commands and a lightening in the prohibitions. As for lightening in the commands: when Allah, Glorified and Exalted, mentioned what is obligatory upon us regarding purification—ablution, ritual bath, and tayammum—He said: ﴿Allah does not desire to place upon you any difficulty, but He desires to purify you﴾ [al-Ma'idah 6]. Likewise in the prohibitions, He lightened for us, saying: ﴿He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except what you are compelled to﴾ [al-An'am 119]. So it is not forbidden, and this is a lightening—praise be to Allah—upon the servants.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verses 29–30 (part 1 of 2):

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly﴾. The address (al-nida'), as has already been explained, indicates that the message that follows is to be given special attention. The reason is that the address alerts the one being addressed. A divine speech that opens with an address is distinguished from one that comes without it. Addressing the believers with ﴿O you who believe﴾ conveys an urging (al-igra') to adhere to this address, or to adhere to what it implies. The reason is that describing a person as a believer moves him to comply. It also indicates that complying with this matter is one of the requirements of faith, and that opposing it is a deficiency in faith. He, may He be glorified and exalted, says: ﴿O you who believe﴾. We must give this address our full attention and wait to see what God directs us to, as was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "When God says, 'O you who believe,' prick up your ears, for it is either good that you are commanded or evil that you are forbidden."[[Narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur in his Tafsir (50).]]

Then He said: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume your wealth﴾. The prohibition came: ﴿do not consume one another's wealth unjustly﴾. Here "la" is a prohibitive particle, which is why the verb after it is in the jussive mood with the nun dropped.

﴿Do not consume your wealth﴾ means: whatever you hold as property, whether little or much, whether goods or cash, whether debts or specific items. It covers all wealth in general.

His words ﴿between you﴾ mean: in dealings, because consuming wealth must necessarily occur between two or more parties. If it is from one person to another person, then that person has consumed his own wealth.

﴿Between you﴾ means: during your dealings with one another.

His words ﴿unjustly﴾: al-batil (the unjust or falsehood) in the lexicon means that which is lost in vain, that which perishes and contains no good. The intended meaning of "unjustly" here is that which contradicts the Sharia, because the Sharia is truth, and whatever contradicts it is falsehood. The meaning on this basis is: do not consume your wealth among yourselves in a manner that contradicts the Sharia, such as usury (riba), fraud, lying, deception, and the like.

﴿Except that it be﴾: "illa" (except) is a particle of exception, but what is intended by it is istidrak (a correction or contrast), meaning "but." That is: but if there is a trade, or a trade (tijara) among you by mutual consent from you, then this is permissible. We say that the exception here is disconnected (al-istithna' al-munqati'), because His words ﴿except that it be a trade by mutual consent from you﴾ are not of the same kind as consuming wealth unjustly. Rather, it is consuming by what? By right. The disconnected exception is when the excluded item (al-mustathna) is of a different kind from the item it is excluded from. Here it must be disconnected, because trade by mutual consent is not consuming unjustly, but consuming rightfully. For this reason we say that the exception in this verse is disconnected.

﴿Except that it be a trade﴾ has two canonical readings: ﴿tijaratun﴾ with the damma, and ﴿tijaratan﴾ with the fatha. With the reading of the damma there is no difficulty; that is, "except that a trade occurs among you." Here "kana" is complete, not incomplete. With the reading of the fatha, "kana" is incomplete, and ﴿tijaratan﴾ is its predicate, and its subject is a hidden pronoun. In this case a problem arises: would the subject be a hidden pronoun, understood as "it" (huwa), even though the word "consuming" (ta'kulu) that it would refer to is masculine? Can we say "except that the consuming be a trade"? That is not correct. But here there is a useful point: when a pronoun or demonstrative falls between two things, and the second is masculine while the first is feminine, or the reverse, it is permissible to take into account either the first or the second. Do you understand?

When a pronoun or demonstrative falls between two things, and the first is masculine while the second is feminine, or the reverse, it is permissible to make it masculine or feminine. It may be masculine in consideration of its earlier referent, and feminine in consideration of its later referent. Here it has been made feminine in consideration of its second, later referent. That is: except that the trade by which you consume wealth be a trade by mutual consent from you. Trade (tijara) is exchange, or the exchange among people for the sake of profit. This is trade, and from it comes the jurists' expression "trade goods" ('urud al-tijara). As for what is given as a gift, pledged, or lent, this is not trade. Likewise, what is bought to meet a need, such as buying bread to eat, is not trade, because a person does not intend profit by it.

At this point a difficulty remains in the meaning of the verse: if transactions are more numerous than trade, why were they not mentioned? It has been said that they were not mentioned, meaning dealings without the intention of trade, because the most common form of people's dealings is trade, and it is in trade that disputes over bargaining arise. As for other transactions, gifts come from the giver's good will, and likewise loans and pledges. What is bought for need usually does not lead to dispute, because a person intends by it to meet a need, not to obtain profit. Therefore trade was mentioned. Otherwise, it is well known that contracts made by mutual consent are more numerous than trade contracts.

﴿By mutual consent from you﴾: the prepositional phrase ﴿by mutual consent﴾ is attached to an omitted element whose assumed form is: "proceeding from mutual consent from you," or "resulting from it." And ﴿tarad̄in﴾ here is in the form of mutual action (tafā'ul), which shows that what is intended is mutual consent from both parties, the taker and the giver.

His words ﴿by mutual consent from you﴾ mean: proceeding from you yourselves, who are the parties to the transaction, not from others. So if a father agrees to sell his son's property while the son has not agreed, and the property belongs to the son, then the father's consent carries no weight.

Then he said:
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, yes. If a father agrees to sell his son's property without the son's agreement, his consent carries no weight.

He said: ﴿And do not kill yourselves; indeed, God is ever Merciful to you﴾. ﴿Do not kill yourselves﴾: killing is well known as taking a soul's life. But does ﴿yourselves﴾ mean the killer's own soul, so that it refers to suicide, or does it mean "your fellow believers," as in His words: ﴿And do not defame one another﴾ [al-Hujurat 11], since a person does not defame himself but defames others? Which of these is intended?

We say: it is inclusive. It is not restricted to one who kills himself, nor to one who kills others. Rather, the verse includes both. If the meaning is "do not kill yourselves," meaning you yourselves, there is no difficulty in the verse. If the meaning is "do not kill others," then why was the others expressed as "yourselves"? We say: others were expressed as "yourselves" because the believer with his brother is like one body, as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, gave this as an example: "When one of its limbs complains, the rest of the body responds to it with fever and sleeplessness."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6011), Muslim (2586/66), from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.]] Also, expressing one's brother as one's self carries urging and exhortation, as if he were yourself. This contains an incitement for a person to avoid killing others, and a summons for a person to show compassion toward his brother, or to move him to compassion toward his brother.

His words ﴿indeed, God is ever Merciful to you﴾: this clause is a reason (ta'lil) for what precedes it, giving the reason for both rulings: consuming wealth and killing souls. God, glorified and exalted, is merciful to us. Among His mercy is the prohibition of consuming one another's wealth unjustly, or the prohibition against consuming one another's wealth unjustly. The second is the prohibition against killing ourselves, for this is from God's mercy toward us. The reasoning for the first is that consuming wealth unjustly leads to disputes and conflict, and perhaps to armed clashes, and the killing of people is evident.

His words ﴿indeed, God is ever Merciful to you﴾: to whom does the address ﴿you﴾ return? To the believers, because He is addressing the believers with ﴿O you who believe﴾. This is confirmed by His saying: ﴿And He is ever Merciful to the believers﴾ [al-Ahzab 43]. Nowhere in the Quran is mercy attributed to God in relation to the disbelievers, in the general sense. The mercy by which God is described appears in the Quran either in a general form or in a particular form directed at whom? At the believers. As for a particular form directed at the disbelievers, it does not appear.

* Student: May God be gracious to you. It appears in another place, O Shaykh, His saying: ﴿And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾ [al-Baqara 195]. Shaykh, can we say that this falls under this category (...) some of you?
* Shaykh: What?
* Student: (...) some of you.
* Shaykh: Which ones? His words ﴿with your own hands﴾. Yes. Regarding the verse ﴿And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾, it has been said that what is intended is: do not abandon spending in the way of God, lest you perish. What is intended is not throwing oneself into what destroys, such as killing or exposing oneself to it. But the correct view is that the verse is general: ﴿do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾ applies to this and to that.
* Student: Can this wording, O Shaykh, be taken in its apparent sense: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾, in its apparent sense?
* Shaykh: And what is that?
* Student: The soul, meaning the agreed sense, as we said: killing others without an indicator (...). So we have abandoned the original meaning and not the meaning (...) without an indicator?
* Shaykh: No. May God bless you. The indicator is that aggression against another is like aggression against oneself, because the Messenger made the punishment of one who aggresses against himself the same as the punishment of one who aggresses against others: that he is eternally abiding in the fire of Hell and is tormented therein. Do you understand?
* Student: Is it not the case that if he kills a soul, he is killed?
* Shaykh: Do you understand?
* Student: O Shaykh, where is the indicator?
* Shaykh: The indicator is that God expresses believers toward one another as "souls." That is the indicator. That the word may bear two meanings, and carrying it on both is better than limiting it to one. But if we say that what is meant by souls here is others, not the person's own soul, that is an error. He says: why do you take it this way and not that without an indicator? But if we say it is general, there is no difficulty.
* Student: Does His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿God intends to lighten for you﴾ [al-Nisa' 28] benefit? The character of the Prophet, peace be upon him, in the hadith of 'A'isha: "He was never given a choice between two matters without choosing the easier of them"?[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6786), Muslim (2327/77), from 'A'isha.]]
* Shaykh: Yes, yes. From it we learn that the Messenger loves what God loves. But this is not in the verse for us to mention it among its benefits.
* Student: May God be gracious to you. Can we interpret the verse ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾ as meaning that consuming wealth may be (...) is that correct or not?
* Shaykh: That is not correct, because this "wa" (and) is a conjunction, and conjunction requires difference. Say: do not kill yourselves by consuming wealth. Rather, it is said that God, mighty and majestic, mentioned the prohibition regarding wealth and regarding souls.
* Student: (...) wealth?
* Shaykh: (...) Wealth: not spending in the way of God. It is not consuming another's wealth.
* Student: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾. Is it not the case that if a person kills a soul, he is killed for it?
* Shaykh: No. He is killed if the conditions are fulfilled, so it is a cause. (...)

He asks about the Salafi methodology. The Salafi methodology in what? It was eager for knowledge. The methodology of the People of the Sunna is in what? Read the commentary on al-Tahawiyya, or the commentary on al-'Aqida al-Wasitiyya.

* Student: In da'wa.
* Shaykh: In calling to God? They call to God, exalted is He, with wisdom and good admonition, and they argue with them in the best manner. They argue with the People of the Book in the best manner, except those of them who commit wrong. They do not condemn anyone for exercising independent reasoning (ijtihad) provided it does not oppose the consensus (ijma') of the Salaf, or an explicit text of the Quran or the Sunna.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in God from Satan the accursed. ﴿And whoever does that, in aggression and injustice, We will drive him into a Fire, and that is ever easy for God. (30) If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to an honorable entrance. (31) And do not wish for that by which God has made some of you exceed others. For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned. And ask God of His bounty. Indeed, God is ever Knowing of all things. (32) And for each We have appointed heirs to what is left by parents and close relatives, and those with whom your oaths have bound you, so give them their share. Indeed, God is ever Witness over all things. (33)﴾ [al-Nisa' 30–33].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in God from Satan the accursed. God, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly﴾. The discussion of the beginning of this verse has already been given, and I believe there is nothing in it that requires further discussion.
* In this verse, among its benefits: the concern for preserving wealth and avoiding aggression, from His saying: ﴿do not consume one another's wealth unjustly﴾.
* And in it: the prohibition of taking a person's property without his consent, from His saying: ﴿except that it be a trade by mutual consent from you﴾.
* And in it also: the prohibition of forbidden transactions, even if they are by mutual consent of both parties, because a forbidden transaction is consuming wealth unjustly. On this basis, if the two parties agree to a usurious transaction, that is forbidden.
* Among its benefits: that it is a requirement of faith to avoid consuming wealth unjustly, because He directed the address to whom? To the believers.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the condition of mutual consent in contracts, from His saying: ﴿except that it be a trade by mutual consent from you﴾. If consent precedes the contract, there is no difficulty in the permissibility and validity of the contract. But if it comes afterward, does the contract take effect or not? This is the matter called by the scholars the unauthorized transaction (al-tasarruf al-fudooli), meaning: if I sell a person's property without his permission and consent, but he later grants permission and consents, is the earlier contract valid or void? If we look at the generality of His saying: ﴿except that it be a trade by mutual consent from you﴾, we say that it is valid, because this trade has come to result in mutual consent.
