It does not include a young girl with whom intercourse is not possible. This will be mentioned, Allah willing, in the benefits [section].

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and you find no water﴾. The fa' here is a conjunction linking it to His saying: ﴿and if you are sick, or on a journey﴾, [then] ﴿and you find no water﴾.

The negation of finding indicates that a search has taken place, because one does not say "he did not find" except of someone who sought. You say: "I searched and did not find." As for one who did not search, it is not correct to say that he did not find.

﴿and you find no water, then seek clean earth﴾. ﴿Seek﴾ means aim, because tayammum (dry ablution with earth) in the Arabic language means intention, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not aim at the bad [part] of it to spend from it, while you would not take it yourselves unless you overlook [defects] in it﴾ [Al-Baqarah 267]. That is: do not intend the bad to spend from it, while you would not take it yourselves unless you overlook its faults. The poet said:

"I aimed for her from Adhri'at, while her people
in Yathrib, the nearest of her dwellings, were a lofty sight."

He said: "tayammamtuha" means "I aimed for her," that is, I headed toward her. As for al-sa'id, it is the surface of the earth. Al-sa'id is the surface of the earth, because it rises and is clearly visible.

As for His saying: ﴿clean﴾ (tayyiban), tayyib is the opposite of khabith (bad). Since the purpose of this tayammum is purification, tayyib becomes tahur (pure). If you wish, say: tahir (pure), and it is so. So tayyib here means tahir.

As for al-sa'id, we have said: it is everything on the surface of the earth, or it is the surface of the earth, whether it be stones, sand, dust, or something else.

﴿So wipe your faces and your hands﴾ is coordinated with ﴿seek﴾.

﴿So wipe your faces and your hands, indeed Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾. As for (the face), we say concerning its limits what we said regarding wudu'. That is, the limit of the face is from ear to ear in breadth, and from the hairline to the bottom of the chin in length. This is the face.

As for His saying: ﴿your hands﴾, here Allah has used the word hand without qualification, and when the word hand is used without qualification, what is meant is only the palm, and not what goes beyond it.

As for His saying: ﴿indeed Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾, this sentence is the reason for the rulings mentioned before. That is: because of His pardon and forgiveness, He prescribed tayammum for you when water is absent or in case of illness.

Al-'Afuww (the Pardoner) is the One who overlooks His servants' abandonment of obligations and commission of prohibited acts. The pardon of Allah, mighty and majestic, is complete pardon coupled with power, as in His saying: ﴿indeed Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent﴾ [An-Nisa' 149]. This differs from the pardon of others, which may come from inability, that is, inability to take revenge.

As for His saying: ﴿Forgiving﴾ (ghafur), al-Ghafur is the One who covers sins and overlooks them. So when pardon is joined with forgiveness, perfection is attained: pardon is for abandoning an obligation, and forgiveness is for committing a prohibited act.

* In this noble verse there are many benefits. Among them: the importance of prayer and the care that must be taken with it. The reason is that Allah, exalted is He, introduced the ruling concerning prayer with a call, in order to draw attention. Another [indication of its importance] is that Allah began the address with the attribute of faith, ﴿O you who have believed﴾. This shows the importance of prayer and the care that must be given to it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of wine (khamr). This is because of His saying: ﴿do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾, for this is a concession to people to drink wine outside the times of prayer. This was one of the stages in the prohibition of wine, because wine went through four stages: permission, a hint at abandoning it, a prohibition against drinking it near the time of prayer, and then a prohibition against drinking it altogether.

The Muslims have agreed upon the prohibition of wine, and its prohibition has become one of the clearly known matters on which there is consensus. The scholars have said that whoever denies its prohibition is a disbeliever, unless he grew up in a land far from the lands of the Muslims, in which case he is taught and then explained to.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the speech of an intoxicated person has no legal effect, because of His saying: ﴿until you know what you are saying﴾. This indicates that the intoxicated person does not know what he is saying. If he does not know what he says, his speech is vain and has no weight. This is so, and this is the preferred view: that the speech of an intoxicated person has no weight. Even if he divorces, his divorce does not take effect; if he frees a slave, his manumission is not implemented; if he makes a waqf (endowment), it is not implemented. Whatever he says has no weight, because he does not know what he is saying.

* A corollary of this benefit is that if a person becomes extremely angry, to the point that he does not know what he is saying, his speech has no weight, even if it is disbelief and extreme anger drove him to it, because of His saying: ﴿until you know what you are saying﴾. This shows that a person's ignorance of what he says affects the ruling. Likewise, if he divorces in the grip of extreme anger while not knowing what he is saying, there is no ruling. Even if he divorces while knowing what he says, but has become like one under compulsion from extreme anger, there is no ruling, because of His saying: "and the woman is not divorced by that."

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the urging to presence of heart in prayer, because of His saying: ﴿until you know what you are saying﴾. When the heart is absent, a person does not know what he says, and he says it merely out of habit. If he returned to himself, it would become clear to him that he does not know what he is saying, that is, he does not know the meaning of what he says, even if he knows that it is words.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: in it is evidence for the Prophet's ﷺ prohibition of praying in the presence of food or while one is pressed by the two kinds of excrement. The reason is that prayer in such a state diminishes the worshipper's awareness of what he is saying.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the view held by some scholars that if whisperings (waswas) overwhelm most of the prayer, the prayer is not valid. That is, if distracting thoughts (hawajis) overwhelm the prayer or most of it, the prayer is not valid, because of His exalted saying: ﴿until you know what you are saying﴾. But the correct position on this issue is that the prayer is valid, though the worshipper does not attain the full reward. The evidence for this is what the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, reported: that "when the Satan hears the call to prayer, he turns his back and has flatulence," because of how much he hears and how it weighs on his heart. When the iqamah (second call) is given, he returns and begins to say to the person: "Remember such-and-such, remember such-and-such, remember such-and-such," until one of you does not know how much he has prayed. [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (608) and Muslim (389/84), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.] This shows that whisperings during prayer do not invalidate it, but there is no doubt that they diminish it, because of his saying: "You have from your prayer only what you understood of it." [See the Fatawa of Ibn Taymiyyah (2/226), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the prohibition for one in janabah to remain in the mosque, because of His saying: ﴿nor [while you are] in a state of janabah, except those passing through [a place]﴾. This is the most correct of the opinions on this verse: that what is meant is the prohibition of a person in janabah from approaching the mosques, except those passing through. However, an exception is made for the case where the one in janabah has performed wudu'. If he has performed wudu', it is permissible for him to remain in the mosque, because there are reports from the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, that they used to do this during the lifetime of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. [Narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur in his Sunan (646), from the report of 'Ata' ibn Yasar.]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: passing through is not the same as staying. Following from this benefit: if a person passes through the mosque, we do not require him to perform the greeting prayer of the mosque, because he is passing through. This differs from the case where he stays and sits, for then we say to him: do not sit until you have prayed two rak'ahs.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the prohibition is lifted, that is, the prohibition on a person in janabah entering the mosque is lifted, when he performs ghusl, because of His exalted saying: ﴿until you have washed﴾. You have already learned a moment ago that it is also lifted by what?

* Students: By wudu'.

* Shaykh: By wudu', on the basis of the reports from the Companions.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an allusion to the well-known rule on which there is agreement: that hardship brings ease. The reason is that Allah, exalted is He, permitted the sick person to perform tayammum. But is one to perform tayammum for every illness, or only if using water would lead to death?

* Students: (...).

* Shaykh: Yes. Neither this nor that. Some scholars say: one should perform tayammum only if one fears death. But if one fears illness, or prolonged illness, or disfigurement of the body, then one does not perform tayammum. Others say: one performs tayammum for every illness. The correct view is neither this nor that. One performs tayammum for every illness in which using water is feared to prolong the illness, or increase it, or cause a wound to spread so that it affects the body, or the like. In short, whenever something harmful occurs, one performs tayammum, and there is no harm.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: if a traveler does not find water, he performs tayammum and does not wait until he finds water in a town, because of His saying: ﴿or on a journey﴾, and ﴿and you find no water, then seek [clean earth]﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is not permissible to perform tayammum while in one's home town when water is absent, because Allah, exalted is He, made the conditions for tayammum the absence of water, and He stipulated two conditions: first, the absence of water, and second, travel. The correct view, however, is that it is permissible. This is because it is established that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, performed tayammum while at home, in the case of the man who came and greeted the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he did not return the greeting until he performed tayammum at a wall and said: "I disliked to mention Allah except in a state of purity." [Narrated by Abu Dawud (17), from the hadith of al-Muhajir ibn Qunfudh, with the wording: "I disliked..." until the end of the hadith.] This is an explicit text in the dispute. Moreover, the cause is one: the absence of what?

* Student: Water.

* Shaykh: The absence of water. Suppose that water was cut off from the town and a person could not find water with which to purify himself; then he performs tayammum, because the cause is the same. But mention of travel was made because it is the usual context in which water is absent. As we have already seen, when a qualification is mainly descriptive of the usual situation, it carries no restrictive implication.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: travel has no fixed limit. The reason is the unqualified term ﴿or on a journey﴾, and He did not say: [a journey of] such-and-such distance. This is the preferred view among the scholars: travel has no limit, neither eighty kilometers, nor a hundred kilometers, nor forty kilometers. Its limit is that it be called travel. When it is called travel, the rulings of travel apply to it. Allah and His Messenger did not specify travel by a fixed distance.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: urine and feces nullify wudu', because of His saying: ﴿or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself﴾.

Are there other nullifiers besides these? There are nullifiers. Among them: sleep, when it is deep, such that if a person passed wind he would not be aware of it. As for light sleep, by which a person would be aware of himself if he passed wind, it does not nullify wudu'.

* Among them: eating camel meat, which nullifies wudu'. This is established from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. There are two authentic hadiths on it: the hadith of al-Bara' [Narrated by Abu Dawud (184), al-Tirmidhi (81), and Ibn Majah (494), from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib], and the hadith of Jabir ibn Samurah. [Narrated by Muslim (360/97), from Jabir ibn Samurah.]

How many are these? Urine, feces, sleep, and eating camel meat. Some matters remain on which there is disagreement, although sleep itself is also disputed. But the correct view is that deep sleep nullifies wudu'.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 43 (part 3 of 4):

Whatever exits from other than the two passages, if it is impure, such as blood, there is a difference of opinion among the scholars on it. The correct view is that it does not nullify wudu' (ablution), for the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) would be struck by wounds in the way of Allah, and they would also be struck by wounds outside of fighting, and no report has come from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he commanded them to perform wudu' because of that. Such matters are widespread enough that their transmission would be expected. Furthermore, we say: wudu' is established by the requirement of the legal evidence, so this purity achieved by wudu' cannot be removed except by legal evidence, and there is no evidence indicating that the exit of blood from the body, or other impurities from other than the two passages, nullifies wudu'. Accordingly, nosebleeds, even if they are heavy, and wounds, even if the bleeding from them is heavy, do not nullify wudu'.

Touching the penis, or if you wish, say: touching the private part (farj), does it nullify wudu'? Concerning it, the scholars have several views: that it nullifies wudu' absolutely; that it does not nullify wudu' absolutely; and a detailed view. The most evident view is the detailed one, and this is what is required by the reason ('illah) that the Prophet (ﷺ) gave for the non-nullification. When he was asked about a man who touches his penis during prayer, whether he must perform wudu', he said: «No, it is only a part of you» [Abu Dawud (182), al-Tirmidhi (85), and al-Nasa'i in al-Mujtaba (165), from the hadith of Talq ibn Habib]. That is, a part of you and a piece of you. So if a person touches it without desire, it is like touching the rest of his limbs; there is no wudu' upon him, and there is no difficulty in this.

But if he touches it with desire, is wudu' obligatory or recommended? Concerning it there are two views among the scholars. Some of them said it is recommended, because desire agitates the body. Others said it is obligatory. The better view, and indeed the more cautious, is that he should perform wudu'.

Among the matters on which the scholars differed also: washing the dead, touching a woman. The correct view concerning this is that it does not nullify. Accordingly, the nullifiers that we consider to be nullifiers and that the texts indicate are: urine, faeces, deep sleep, eating the flesh of camels, and touching the penis with desire as a matter of caution.

* A student: What about the emission of wind, O Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: Wind exits from the two passages, yes. For this reason, if we say "what exits from the two passages" and generalize, it would be better.
* A student: Vomiting?
* The Shaykh: Vomiting does not nullify wudu'.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: sexual intercourse with women is a minor impurity (hadath); because of His saying: ﴿or you have touched women﴾.
But is it a minor or a major impurity? We say: it is a major impurity, as the verse of al-Ma'idah indicates. Accordingly, it is obligatory upon a person who has intercourse with a woman to perform ghusl, whether he ejaculates or does not ejaculate. At the beginning of Islam, when a man had intercourse without ejaculating, he would wash his penis and what had reached the woman from it, and ghusl was not obligatory upon him. Then this was abrogated (naskh), and ghusl became obligatory from intercourse even if no ejaculation occurred. As for when ejaculation occurs, from intercourse or otherwise, ghusl is obligatory, because of the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): «Water is only from water» [Muslim (343/80), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: it is a condition for the permissibility of tayammum (dry ablution) that water be absent, or that its use would cause harm. Absence of water is derived from His saying: ﴿then you find no water﴾, and harm from its use from His saying: ﴿and if you are sick﴾. Accordingly, tayammum is not possible except when the use of water is impossible, either due to its absence or due to harm from using it.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the permissibility of performing tayammum on the entire surface of the earth, whether sand, pebbles, dust, saline ground, plaster, or other things. Whatever is on the earth may be used for tayammum; because of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿then perform tayammum with clean earth (ṣa'īd)﴾, without restriction, and because of the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): «Clean earth is the wudu' of the Muslim, even if he does not find water for ten years» [Abu Dawud (332), al-Tirmidhi (124), and al-Nasa'i in al-Mujtaba (322), from the hadith of Abu Dhar]. Clean earth (al-ṣa'īd al-ṭayyib).
The scholars differed concerning what is not of the same kind as earth, such as a tree: is it permissible to perform tayammum with it or not? Some of them permitted tayammum with it, and some said it is not permissible except when it is attached to the earth. As for a broken branch thrown on the ground, one does not perform tayammum with it. This is the closer view. Accordingly, if a person performs tayammum with the trunk of a tree attached to the earth, there is no harm. But there is no doubt that performing tayammum on the earth itself is better, more cautious, and further from disagreement.
The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, differed as to whether it is a condition that there be dust on it. Some scholars said: there must be dust, because of His saying in the verse of al-Ma'idah: ﴿then wipe your faces and your hands with it﴾ [al-Ma'idah 6], and "min" (from) indicates partitiveness, and this requires that there be dust with which to wipe.
Others said: dust is not a condition, and they cited the verse: ﴿your faces and your hands﴾ [al-Nisa' 43], where He did not say "from it," and they cited that it was reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that when he showed 'Ammar ibn Yasir how to perform tayammum, he struck his hands on the earth and blew into them [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (338) and Muslim (368/112), from the hadith of 'Ammar ibn Yasir]. Had dust been a condition, he would not have blown, because blowing necessarily makes the dust fly away. The correct view is that dust is not a condition, and that if a person performs tayammum on the earth, his tayammum is valid, whether there is dust on it or not.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: wiping is required, wiping with intention; because of His saying: ﴿then perform tayammum﴾, ﴿then wipe﴾. Accordingly, if the wind blows and carries dust, and a person stands facing the wind and endures it until his face is filled with dust, and he wipes his face, is that sufficient or not?
Some people of knowledge said: it is sufficient. The more cautious view is that it is not sufficient, because Allah commanded us to intend the surface of the earth and wipe from it.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the wisdom in the legislation. Its explanation: Allah distinguished between the purity by water and the purity by tayammum. Purity by water from major impurity (janabah) must cover what? The whole body. And from minor impurity it must cover the four limbs: the face, the two hands, the head, and the two feet.
As for the purity of tayammum, it is only in two limbs, namely the face and the two hands, and there is no distinction in it between the greater and the lesser purities. The wisdom in this is that purification by water contains cleansing, a clear physical cleansing, while purification by tayammum contains a spiritual cleansing, which is the perfection of servitude and humility before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in that a person wipes his face and palms with dust, and this is evidence of the perfection of servitude.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation of order between wiping the face in tayammum and wiping the hands. Which comes first? The face. The evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) when he approached al-Safa: «﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾ — I begin with what Allah began with» [Muslim (1218/147), from the hadith of Jabir]. In a wording of al-Nasa'i: «Begin with what Allah began with» [al-Nasa'i in al-Mujtaba (2962), from the hadith of Jabir]. If Allah began here with the faces, then we begin with them. This matter is one on which the scholars differed. Some said order is a condition in tayammum absolutely, whether one performs tayammum for a minor or a major impurity. Others said order is not a condition absolutely, whether one performs tayammum for a minor or major impurity. Others said: if it is for a minor impurity, order is obligatory, and if it is for a major impurity, it is not obligatory. They said: because if it is for a minor impurity, it is a substitute for a purity in which order is obligatory, and the substitute has the ruling of what it substitutes; and if it is for ghusl, then ghusl does not require order, so its substitute, tayammum, does not require order either. The more cautious course? The more cautious course is that he orders it, beginning with the face, then the two hands.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: wiping the forearm is not obligatory in tayammum; because of His saying: ﴿your faces and your hands﴾, and He stated it absolutely. And "hand," when stated absolutely, means the palm. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands﴾ [al-Ma'idah 38]. The scholars have agreed that the hand of a thief is cut only from the joint of the palm, not from the elbow. Here Allah stated "hand" absolutely, as He stated it absolutely in the case of cutting for theft, and when it is stated absolutely, the palm is meant.
If someone says: must wiping not extend to the elbow by analogy with wudu'? We say: analogy requires equivalence between the branch and the root, and here equivalence between the branch and the root cannot be realized because of the great difference between the purity of tayammum and the purity of water. As you see, the purity of tayammum is much lighter than the purity of water; it requires only two limbs to be purified, and purity is the same for minor and major impurity; and there is also in it no rinsing of the mouth, no snuffing of water into the nose, and no bringing of dust beneath the hair, even if it is thin. The difference between the purity by water and by tayammum is very great, and if that is the case, analogy is not valid.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of these two names of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: al-'Afuww (the Pardoner) and al-Ghafur (the Forgiving): ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾.
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of the attribute indicated by these two names, which is pardon and forgiveness.
If someone says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ — is this attribute something that Allah had and then ceased to have?
The answer: No. The word "kāna" (was) is a past-tense verb. We say: in this context and similar ones, it has been stripped of indicating time, and what is meant by it is the confirmation of the attribute that it indicates. This is frequent in the Qur'an with respect to the names and attributes of Allah.
* A student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you well, some people cite the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿your faces and your hands﴾ [al-Ma'idah 6], the verse, to argue that rinsing the mouth and snuffing water into the nose are not obligatory?
* The Shaykh: What is the point of the evidence?
* The student: They said: those who say rinsing the mouth and snuffing water into the nose are obligatory in wudu' say that the nose and mouth are part of the face. Did Allah, or was it reported from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he commanded those who performed tayammum to rinse their mouths and snuff water into their noses with dust?
* The Shaykh: Did you hear what he said? He says: some scholars or some people cited this verse to show that rinsing the mouth and snuffing water into the nose are not obligatory. We say: yes, we agree with them that rinsing the mouth and snuffing water into the nose in tayammum are not obligatory, for how could one snuff dust into the nose or rinse the mouth with it? As for wudu', the Prophet (ﷺ) was constant in rinsing the mouth and snuffing water into the nose, and no report has come from him, neither authentic nor weak, that he abandoned it. Rather, he said to Laqit ibn Sabirah: «Exaggerate in snuffing water into the nose unless you are fasting» [Abu Dawud (142), (2366), al-Tirmidhi (788), al-Nasa'i in al-Mujtaba (87), and Ibn Majah (407), from the hadith of Laqit ibn Sabirah], and he said: «When you perform wudu', rinse the mouth» [Abu Dawud (144), from the hadith of Laqit ibn Sabirah], and he said: «When one of you performs wudu', let him put water on his nose and then blow it out» [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (162) and Muslim (278/20), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. These are commands. Then we also say: the purity of tayammum has a far greater deficiency. Also, the foot is not washed in the purity of tayammum; do they say that washing the foot is not obligatory?
* A student: They do not say so. In Surat al-Nisa', ...
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: The ruling of it, its evidence is the evidence...
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: They say: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: Sunnah (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: Those who say rinsing the mouth and snuffing water into the nose are obligatory say that the face includes the nose and mouth.
* The Shaykh: Correct.
* The student: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned here, stated absolutely in the verse of tayammum.
* The Shaykh: But is it possible that a person snuffs dust or rinses his mouth with dust? If this statement is indeed reported from any of the people of knowledge, then there is something wrong in his intellect, if it is authentic.
* A student: A muezzin who became junub in the morning, is his situation during the call to prayer considered forbidden?
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: A muezzin in the mosque who wants to perform ghusl and return, does this count as (...) forbidden?
* The Shaykh: No. We say: he should perform ghusl and then call the adhan, and if you do not do so, then perform wudu' and then call the adhan.
* * *
(...)
* The Shaykh: What?
* A student: I have questions, O Shaykh. Some say (...), and it is known that the wall formerly was of mud, but does it apply to paint now?
* The Shaykh: No, paint does not fall under it except according to the second view, which says: everything on the surface of the earth is ṣa'īd.
* The student: And what is the correct view, O Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: This is the correct view.
* A student: Of course, you mentioned that dust is not a condition in tayammum, and you mentioned the evidence that the Messenger (ﷺ) blew into his hands. So what is the response to whoever says it is necessary that there be dust, and cites the verse in al-Ma'idah: ﴿from it﴾, the saying of Allah: ﴿then wipe your faces and your hands from it﴾ [al-Ma'idah 6], and that "min" (from) is partitive? What is the basis of our response to him?
* The Shaykh: The response to him is that it is said: "min" here may be partitive, and it may indicate the starting point. When a possibility is present, the argument is nullified. Who will specify for us that "min" is partitive when he says: wipe with your faces from it?
* The student: The default, O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: The default is what? Yes?
* The student: The default in ﴿from it﴾ is partitive.
* The Shaykh: No, it has several meanings, and the context determines which meaning is intended.
* A student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you well, can we derive from the entry of the Companions into the mosque while they were junub the non-obligation of tahiyyat al-masjid (greeting of the mosque)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed.
* The student: May I say: can we derive from it the non-obligation of the greeting of the mosque?
* The Shaykh: No, we do not derive that; because the greeting of the mosque is obligatory only upon one who enters the mosque while being fit for prayer. As for one who enters without being in wudu', we do not say to him: pray.
* The student: They dropped an obligation (...).
* The Shaykh: No, no. Essentially, it is not obligatory in itself. It is obligatory upon one who enters in a state of wudu' not to sit until he prays two rak'ahs. This is according to those who hold it obligatory, although what appears to us is that it is not obligatory.
* The student: The hand, when stated absolutely, is intended to mean the shoulder, restricted by (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, according to their opinion: if the thief steals, his hand is cut from the shoulder.
* A student: And the Sunnah clarifies it.
* The Shaykh: No, the verse is absolute. And who told them that when the hand is stated absolutely it means up to the shoulder?
* A student: Shaykh, does blood exiting from the two passages not nullify wudu'?
* The Shaykh: It nullifies wudu'; every exit from the two passages nullifies wudu'.
* The student: And if it exits from other than the two passages?
* The Shaykh: From other than the two passages, it does not nullify wudu'.
* A student: May Allah reward you well, according to the view you preferred, that dust is not a condition in tayammum, I say: does this not conflict with tayammum on walls coated with paint?
* The Shaykh: They say paint is not from the original earth. Paint, as is known, is from petroleum, so it resembles the garments with which walls are covered. But whoever says that everything connected to the earth is from the earth, which is the school of Malik, then tayammum on it is valid.
* The student: As for your principle, it is that it must be from the earth for tayammum to be valid on it.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* A student: May Allah reward you well, O Shaykh. It is reported from Ibn 'Umar that he «struck the earth twice for tayammum, and wiped with them his face and his hands up to the elbows» [al-Muwatta' of Malik (142)]. Is it derived from it that tayammum with two strikes is permissible, and likewise wiping...?
* The Shaykh: That is his own ijtihad, may Allah be pleased with him, but it is ijtihad against an explicit text, because it is established in the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn that «the Messenger only wiped the two palms alone».
* The student: I say: does the action of the Companions have any proof value?
* The Shaykh: Proof against the Sunnah?!
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes. It is said: this is among his ijtihadat, just as he, may Allah be pleased with him, used to wash inside his eyes during wudu' until he went blind.
* A student: Is overpowering of the intellect by fainting or intoxication a nullifier of wudu'?
* The Shaykh: Yes, like deep sleep.
* A student: Is standing (al-waqf) considered staying (al-mukth) or passing through (al-'ubur) (...)?
* The Shaykh: What do you say about this? Is standing in the mosque like passing through or like sitting?
* The students: Sitting.

* Shaykh: Sitting. This is sitting (qu'ud). The evidence for this is that the Messenger (ﷺ) forbade the menstruating woman from circumambulating the House, even though she moves around.

* Student: In the hadith, it is not permissible until she prays two rakʿahs, then (...) it is permissible.

* Shaykh: We say something like this: No, pray two rakʿahs. We say this is like sitting.

* Student: Shaykh, if one of the limbs has a wound, meaning he cannot use water, and the rest of the limbs are healthy, does he perform tayammum and set aside wuḍūʾ, or not...?

* Shaykh: Meaning, washing and wiping harm him?

* Student: No, but it harms him that...

* Shaykh: Washing and wiping, or washing only?

* Student: Yes, washing and wiping.

* Shaykh: He performs tayammum in its place, except if he has a bandage (jabīrah, lafafah) on it, in which case he wipes over the bandage.

* Student: And he washes the other limbs?

* Shaykh: He washes the other limbs, and even the rest of the same limb.

* Student: Is there evidence for this, Shaykh?

* Shaykh: ﴿Fear Allah﴾.

* Student: ﴿as much as you are able﴾.

* Shaykh: Is he able to wash the rest of the limb or not?

* Student: As for the rest of the limbs, he is able.

* Shaykh: Then it is obligatory upon him.

* Student: A person who is wounded and cannot wash or wipe it, but can wrap a bandage over it and wipe the bandage. Do we say he performs tayammum, or is it obligatory for him (...)?

* Shaykh: No, he performs tayammum, unless it is in the interest of the wound. If it is in the interest of the wound, the bandage, he wraps it over it.

* Student: Is it obligatory?

* Shaykh: If it is for his benefit, that is known, because: ﴿And do not throw yourselves into destruction with your own hands﴾ [al-Baqarah 195].

* Student: Is tayammum before or after?

* Shaykh: The correct view. As for the (Ḥanbalī) school, tayammum is done in the place of washing. If it is with the hand, then when he washes the healthy hand, he performs tayammum, then wipes his head. The correct view is that it is permissible for it to be after completing wuḍūʾ, and that order is not a condition in this.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: There is nothing wrong with it.

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They purchase error, and they wish that you would lose the way. And Allah is most knowing of your enemies, and sufficient is Allah as protector, and sufficient is Allah as helper.﴾ [An-Nisa 44–45].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture?﴾ The interrogative here is for affirmation (taqrir); that is, Allah affirms this in a manner that is witnessed and seen by the beholder.

The address in His words ﴿Have you not seen﴾ may be to the Messenger (ﷺ), and it may be to whoever the address reaches; i.e., "Have you not seen, O addressee, ﴿those who were given a portion﴾?" That is, were given a portion. Here ﴿were given﴾ takes two objects: the first object in this context is the waw (of the plural), which is the deputy subject (nā'ib al-fā'il), and the second object is His words ﴿a portion﴾. The one who gave them a portion of the Scripture is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and this portion of the Scripture is the Torah and the Gospel. On this basis it includes the Jews and the Christians, but it applies more strongly to the Jews, because they were the ones in Madinah during the time of the Messenger (ﷺ).

﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who purchase error﴾. ﴿They purchase error﴾ means they seek it by purchase. It is known that the buyer is one who desires the goods and earnestly pursues them until he obtains them by purchase, and this is more eloquent than if He had said "they take the path of error", because purchase indicates desire and seeking until a person reaches what he wants. They purchase error with what? With guidance, as Allah the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿Those are the ones who purchased error in exchange for guidance﴾ [Al-Baqarah 16].

Is this a profitable purchase? No. This is the worst kind of purchase. For this reason the Exalted said in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿So their commerce did not profit them, nor were they guided﴾ [Al-Baqarah 16].

﴿They purchase error﴾: this is considered in terms of what they choose for themselves. Is their evil limited? Listen: ﴿and they wish that you would lose the way﴾. Along with their purchasing of error, their choosing of it and their eagerness for it, they wish to transmit it to others as well. ﴿They wish that you would lose the way﴾, i.e., the path to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which is the religion of Islam. If this is their wish, they will strive to achieve their aim by every means. For this reason we find that the disbelievers, the enemies of the Muslims, strive to misguide the Muslims by every means: sometimes through moral corruption, sometimes through military destruction, and sometimes through evil and corrupt ideas. They see the weapon that is most harmful and use it, without caring; that is, if the matter led to armed aggression, they would do it, because they want us to lose the way.

If someone says: Why do they want us to lose the way? We say: Because they are astray, and every person wants people to be like himself. This is one aspect. Another aspect is that they are allies of Satan, and Satan said, addressing Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿He said: "Because You have led me astray, I will surely sit in ambush for them on Your straight path. Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left, and You will not find most of them grateful"﴾ [Al-A'raf 16–17]. Consider His words ﴿I will surely sit in ambush for them on Your path﴾, where he did not say "upon Your path" or "in Your path"; he dropped the preposition so that his sitting would include being on the path to prevent us from entering it, and being in the path to prevent us from completing the journey. Thus he sits in wait for us on the path: outside it to keep us from entering, and inside it to keep us from completing the journey. These are the allies of Satan, as Allah said: ﴿So fight the allies of Satan﴾ [An-Nisa 76]. And if they are his allies, they will support him in what he wants of misguiding the servants of Allah.

﴿And Allah is most knowing of your enemies﴾. Allah is more knowing of your enemies than you are, because we may not perceive the enemy, and his plans by which he wishes to mislead us may be hidden from us. But Allah, the Exalted, is ever watchful.

In His words ﴿And Allah is most knowing of your enemies﴾ there is consolation for us and a threat to our enemies, because when He is most knowing of our enemies, He will protect us from their evil if we turn to Allah; and if we turn away from Allah, He will give these enemies power over us.

﴿And sufficient is Allah as protector﴾: i.e., as one who manages affairs. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as helper﴾: i.e., as one who defends and supports.

* There are benefits in these two verses. First: among people is one who is given the Scripture and granted knowledge, but does not benefit from it. Such people were given a portion of the Scripture, yet they did not benefit from it; they purchased error in exchange for guidance.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever does not benefit from his knowledge resembles these people. Whoever Allah has given knowledge but who does not benefit from it resembles them. For this reason Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Whoever among our scholars is corrupt has a resemblance to the Jews, and whoever among our worshippers is corrupt has a resemblance to the Christians."[[See al-Fatawa of Ibn Taymiyyah (2/142) from the narration of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah.]] And this is sound.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: it bears witness to the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "The Qur'an is a proof for you or against you."[[Recorded by Muslim (1/223) from the hadith of Abu Malik al-Ash'ari.]] So the books of Allah which people carry are either for them or against them.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the love of these people for error and evil, from His words ﴿they purchase error﴾.

* Among its benefits: caution regarding these people, and that however they act with us, they do not wish us any good at all, from His words ﴿and they wish that you would lose the way﴾. They may lavish upon us wealth, factories, and everything else, but what do they want? They want to mislead us; they want us to lose the way. Conquest through worldly means is conquest with a deadly weapon; that is, lavishing worldly goods and comfort upon a person is conquest with a deadly weapon, because man, as Allah said of him: ﴿And you love wealth with immense love﴾ [Al-Fajr 20]. So when wealth he loves is lavished upon him, the nature of human circumstances requires that he become soft toward the one who provided and lavished that wealth upon him.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: praise of the Muslims for being upon the path, because His words ﴿that you would lose the way﴾ imply that, had they not been upon the path, they would not have tried to mislead them; for the one who is astray is astray, so what would he try to do?

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: warning against these Jews or Christians or others, because if Allah warns us against those who were given a portion of the Scripture, then our caution against those who are blind, deaf and dumb is all the more appropriate.

* Among the benefits of the second verse: affirmation of Allah's knowledge, from His words ﴿And Allah is most knowing of your enemies﴾.

* Among its benefits: the perfection of Allah's knowledge.

* Student: Because it was expressed in the comparative form.

* The Shaykh: Yes, because it was expressed in the comparative form ﴿most knowing of your enemies﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: consolation of the believers and strengthening of their resolve, because He is most knowing of our enemies, and He is our helper and our protector.

* Among its benefits: a threat and warning to the polytheists, from His words ﴿And Allah is most knowing of your enemies﴾. For if we supposed (and to Allah belongs the highest likeness) that your father said to your enemy: "I know you and your enmity," he would fear and be wary.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the Muslims must have an enemy; rather, enemies. As we mentioned earlier in commenting on the word: every non-Muslim, of whatever creed, is an enemy of the Muslims.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: praise of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, for complete sufficiency in protection and what else? And support; from His words ﴿And sufficient is Allah as protector and sufficient is Allah as helper﴾. ﴿Protector﴾ (waliyyan) is in the accusative as a specification (tamyiz), transferred from the subject, because what suffices is Allah's protection and support, so it is a specification transferred from the subject. The "bā'" in His words ﴿bi-Allah﴾ — they said it is superfluous, and that the original is: "Allah suffices as protector, and Allah suffices as helper." (...)

* Student: May Allah bless you. ﴿And Allah is most knowing of your enemies﴾: ﴿most knowing﴾ came in the form of a comparative. In the language it is known that comparison occurs only between two, so how is it explained? And it has already been mentioned, O Shaykh, that some people say "a'lam" means "'alim" (knowing)?

* The Shaykh: We have explained the falsity of this, and we said that "a'lam" is more emphatic than "'alim", because "'alim" does not prevent sharing: Allah is knowing, and so-and-so is knowing, and so-and-so is knowing.

* Student: What is the benefit of this interpretation? Why did they resort to it (...)?

* The Shaykh: Out of their assumption that if the Creator and the created share in knowledge, this would indicate resemblance; or it is in the sense of the poet's saying:

Have you not seen that the sword diminishes in worth when it is said that the sword is more cutting than the staff?
But this is an error. We say: even the life, knowledge, hearing and sight of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, share with those of the created in origin, a sharing in origin; but the Creator is more perfect than the created in this.

* Student: So comparison is permissible, then?

* The Shaykh: It is permissible; indeed Allah said: ﴿Is Allah better, or what they associate?﴾ [An-Naml 59].
