Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Or do they have a share in the kingdom? For then they would not give the people even a speck (naqir)﴾. ﴿Or do they have?﴾ How shall we parse it here?

* Student: Is ﴿am﴾ (ام) coordinating (ʿāṭifa)?

* The Shaykh: No.

* Student: It is used in the sense of (bal) (rather/nay) together with the interrogative hamza.

* The Shaykh: Yes, here it is in the sense of (bal) together with the interrogative hamza. It indicates a turning away from what preceded it (iḍrāb). It has been said that it is only interrogative, but this is a well-known disagreement among the grammarians (naḥwiyyūn). ﴿Or do they have a share?﴾ means: rather, do they have a share in the kingdom? They wish to stand between the Prophet (ﷺ) and what Allah has given him of prophethood, through which he will possess the eastern and western parts of the earth. That is to say: those who spoke these words and preferred the path of the disbelievers over the path of the believers, do they have a share of the kingdom, such that they can prevent Allah's bounty upon His Prophet and give that bounty to these disbelievers?!

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Then﴾, meaning: if they had a share of the kingdom, ﴿they would not give the people even a speck﴾. That is, they would not give people anything. ﴿The people﴾ is the first object of ﴿yu'tūn﴾, and ﴿naqīran﴾ is the second object. The naqīr is the small pit on the back of a date-stone, and it is used as a proverb for something very little. That is to say: if these people had a kingdom and a share of it, then due to their stinginess they would not give people even a naqīr, because the Jews are among the most miserly of people and the most greedy and eager for wealth.

So the meaning of the verse is: Do these people have a share of the kingdom, that they should try to prevent Allah's bounty upon His Messenger and give that bounty to these disbelievers? No. Even if it were supposed that they had a share of the kingdom, they would never give anyone among them anything. For this reason He said: ﴿Then﴾, meaning: even if they were given a share of the kingdom, they would not give people a naqīr. And what is beyond that?

* The students: It is a fortiori (min bāb awlā).

* The Shaykh: A fortiori.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that these Jews, who wanted to stand between Allah's bounty upon His Messenger and His Messenger, and to transfer this bounty to these disbelievers, have no share of the kingdom. Kingship belongs to whom? To Allah alone.

* Among its benefits: an indication that the Jews are among the most miserly of people, from His saying: ﴿Then they would not give the people even a naqīr﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 54 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾ As for ﴿أَمْ﴾ (am), we say about it what we said about the verse before: it means "bal" (rather) together with the interrogative hamza. ﴿They envy the people﴾: the people meant here are Muhammad (ﷺ), his family and his companions. ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾ Envy (hasad) by the definition of most scholars is wishing for the removal of Allah's blessing from another person, whether you wish that it come to you or that it pass to no one.

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Envy is hatred of what Allah has bestowed on another. That is, one hates what Allah has bestowed on someone else, such that when he is told that so-and-so has obtained such-and-such, his heart is agitated from hatred of what that man has obtained. On this basis, what the Shaykh (Ibn Taymiyyah) said is more general than what the majority of scholars said, because what the majority said requires that one wish for the removal of that blessing, whereas in this definition mere hatred of it counts as envy. It is well known that whoever hates something will wish for it to disappear.

And His saying ﴿for what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾ means: He gave them of His bounty. What is the bounty that was given to the Messenger?
* Student: The Quran.
* Shaykh: The Quran, or something more general?
* Student: Islam.
* Shaykh: Yes, all of Islam and the whole Shari'ah. Among the greatest things Allah gave the Messenger is prophethood and the mission.

﴿for what Allah has given them of His bounty. We had already given the family of Abraham the Book and wisdom, and We gave them a great kingdom﴾. That is: Our bounty has not ceased to exist; this is not the first bounty We have bestowed upon the servants of Allah, rather the bounty has never ceased to exist. ﴿We gave the family of Abraham the Book and wisdom﴾. The meaning of ﴿the family of Abraham﴾ here is everyone who followed his religion, and the first of them is he, peace be upon him. Allah gave them the Book and gave them wisdom, and He placed in his offspring prophethood and the Book. Most of the prophets whom Allah mentioned to us were from the offspring of Abraham, most of them from the Children of Israel, who are the descendants of Ya'qub (Jacob) son of Ishaq (Isaac) son of Ibrahim. The one unique individual among the family of Abraham is Muhammad (ﷺ), who is from the offspring of Isma'il. For this reason most of the prophets whom Allah mentioned to us were from the Children of Israel.

But this one, Muhammad (ﷺ), was sent to all of them. His religion is dominant over all religions, his message is the seal of the messages, and his nation will remain until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿the Book﴾ means the written, and all the books revealed to the prophets are written by hand. ﴿And wisdom﴾ is correctness; wisdom is correctness. So the Quran is correct, the Torah is correct, the Gospel is correct, and everything the messengers brought is correct. It is for this reason that it was said: wisdom is placing things in their proper places.

﴿And We gave them a great kingdom﴾: ("We gave") means the family of Abraham were given a great kingdom. The most eloquent example of this is what Allah, the Exalted, gave to Solomon. Allah gave him a great kingdom, to the extent that he said: ﴿Grant me a kingdom that none after me will deserve﴾. Even the rebellious devils ﴿made for him whatever he wished: sanctuaries, statues, bowls like water-troughs, and fixed cauldrons﴾. And they, the devils, were ﴿every builder and diver, and others bound together in chains﴾: a builder who builds on the land, a diver who dives into the sea to bring pearls and precious things, everything that is in the sea; and the third group were bound together in chains, because they disobeyed his command, so he bound them in chains and imprisoned them. This is a great kingdom.

Likewise, Allah subjected the wind to him, ﴿flowing gently by his command wherever he willed﴾, that is, wherever he intended. ﴿Gently﴾ means without turbulence and without hardship. It is known that wind usually involves unsettling and hardship even if it does not carry a person, let alone if there were a wind carrying him, which would involve unsettling and turbulence. But Allah, the Exalted, made it gentle even though it was a strong wind: ﴿And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind, strong, running by his command﴾. Yet despite its strength, there was no unsettling in it: ﴿gently wherever he willed﴾. The scholars said: when he wanted to head in a direction, he would place a carpet and sit upon it, along with his retinue and whoever wished to travel with him, and then he would command the wind and it would carry them and fly with them; ﴿its morning journey a month and its evening a month﴾. This is from the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is part of the kingdom given to the family of Abraham, and there is no doubt that this is a great kingdom, since the devils and the winds were subjected to him.

When he said: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ and her throne was in the south, in Yemen, while they were in the north, in al-Sham (Syria): ﴿A powerful one of the jinn said, I will bring it to you before you rise from your place﴾. He had a fixed time at which he would rise, such as after an hour or two or something similar. ﴿Indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it.﴾ ﴿One who had knowledge of the Scripture said, I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you﴾: that is, before you extend your gaze and then return it. ﴿When he saw it settled beside him, he said, This is from the bounty of my Lord﴾. Consider His saying ﴿When﴾: the fa' (then) indicates sequence and immediacy, and that he saw it instantly. Then he saw it settled, as though it had been there for decades. For this reason the word ﴿settled﴾ was used, and it did not say "when he saw it beside him." Seeing it beside him may include the time up to now after it had halted, but "settled" means it had come to stay for years. ﴿He said: This is from the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful﴾.

This statement should be on every tongue when Allah bestows a blessing upon you: say, "This is from the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful," because many people do not obtain this blessing.

* In this noble verse: an explanation of the envy that the Jews had.
* And in it: a denunciation of envy, because Allah brought this verse in condemnation of it.

What is the ruling on envy? Is it among the minor sins or the major sins? The answer: it is among the major sins, because it consumes good deeds.

Does the envious person gain anything? Never.

So there are harms in envy:
First: it is a major sin, and major sins are not forgiven except through repentance.
Second: it is an objection to Allah's decree and destiny, because your hating that Allah gives this person something is an objection to Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾
Third: it involves aggression against the envied person. This is usually the case, though not always. Envy may arise in a person's heart, yet he does not transgress against the envied person by word or deed. For this reason it came in the hadith: «If you suspect, do not verify, and if you envy, do not act upon it»[[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (3153) from the hadith of Haritha ibn al-Nu'man with the wording: "If you envy, seek forgiveness from Allah."]]. Envy may arise in a person's heart, and a person is human, but if you sense it in your heart, try to expel it from your heart until you become pure. If you are unable, then the least that is required of you is not to transgress against the one you envy, that is, not to wrong him by word or deed.

Aggression by word includes accusing the envied person with accusations and attributing to him what he did not say, or obstructing him from his work, or insulting him before his elders and officials, or insulting him before his companions and peers, or similar things. This is aggression by word.

Aggression by deed: to attack him physically so as to prevent him from what Allah has given him of His bounty, such as drowning his wealth or burning it so that he has no wealth, because he envied him for his abundance of wealth.

Fourth: resemblance to the Jews. That is, among the harms of envy is that it resembles the Jews, and how evil is a trait in which a person resembles the Jews.

Fifth: the envious person is always in anxiety, because Allah's blessings upon others keep coming one after another. Whenever a blessing is renewed for someone else, envy rises in his heart, so he is always in continuous anxiety.

Sixth: the envious person usually becomes weary and imagines that he is unable to reach the envied person, so you find him exhausted and not trying to attain virtues. But if he turned away from people and considered whoever Allah increased in bounty to be in a blessing, and he himself strove to seek blessings, he would be safe from all of this.

Among the harms of envy: it creates enmity and hatred among people, because the envious person is usually not free of aggression, and aggression against others leads to enmity and hatred. ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾ to the end of the verse.

* Student: Shaykh, now (...) the ta'ghut (false object of worship or transgression). We said that it is that which a servant transgresses beyond. Is the ta'ghut the one who is transgressed toward, or the one who transgresses?
* Shaykh: The one transgressed toward.
* Student: The one transgressed toward?
* Shaykh: Yes, whether that transgression is directed at a deity worshipped, a leader followed, or an authority obeyed.
* Student: O Shaykh, is the one transgressed toward not a ta'ghut?
* Shaykh: He may be a ta'ghut if he calls people to worship himself, and he may not be. For example, Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus son of Mary) and whoever was worshipped besides Allah among the saints and prophets are not ta'ghut, but they are the locus of ta'ghut, that is, the place of transgression.
* Student: May Allah be good to you, Shaykh. Some scholars divide envy into two categories: minor and major. They say that a person may find something in himself toward his brother without intending to harm him, and this is not among the major sins (...). As for Shaykh al-Islam, he said that there are two opinions on the matter, and he quoted a text from Shaykh al-Islam from the book "Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil," in which he defined envy as the wish for the removal of a blessing. Is this correct, O Shaykh?
* Shaykh: All forbidden envy is among the major sins. As for the envy that occurs in a person's heart while he resists it, that is neither a minor nor a major sin.
* Student: Shaykh, we said that the ta'ghut that is transgressed toward may be a ta'ghut (...). Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾. Does this mean... so what about those who are worshipped besides Allah, such as Isa ibn Maryam, 'Uzayr, and others?
* Shaykh: ﴿When the son of Maryam was cited as an example﴾. Read the verse. ﴿Your people turn away from it in dismay. And they said: Are our gods better, or he?﴾. Allah said: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather they are a quarrelsome people﴾, that is, people of contention. When Allah said: ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be its entrants. If these were gods, they would not have entered it; and all therein will abide. For them therein is a roaring, and they therein will not hear﴾, the polytheists came saying: "This is Isa ibn Maryam; do you say he is fuel for Hell?" Allah said: ﴿Indeed those for whom the best has preceded from Us are kept far from it﴾, and Isa is among those for whom Allah's best reward had preceded.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Of course it is known. Whoever is worshipped besides Allah, while being one of the prophets of Allah or His saints or the righteous, what is his sin that we should say he is a ta'ghut? Rather, he is the locus of transgression, meaning that others transgressed through him.
* Student: May Allah bless you, Shaykh. When one of them speaks, I feel that there is envy in his words, and he does not say "Mashallah." Would you remind him to say "Mashallah"?
* Shaykh: No. What does it mean? Does he describe something as similar to something else, for example (...)? Or do you mean the evil eye?
* Student: No, I mean a man speaks, and I feel that in his words there is something I fear may be envy. For example, your little child is with you and he speaks about him, saying (...) "Mashallah"?
* Shaykh: What did he say? What did he say?
* Student: He said: "This boy is handsome," for example, and said: "How beautiful is his beauty!" Without saying "Mashallah." Did he not say "Mashallah"?
* Shaykh: No, (...) envy is that a person hates Allah's blessing upon another. As for what you are pointing to, it is the evil eye (ayn). The evil eye: when a person sees what pleases him, he should invoke blessing upon it by saying, "May Allah bless you."
* Student: What if he did not say it?
* Shaykh: How?
* Student: What if he did not say "Adhkuruhu" (let me mention it)?
* Shaykh: No. Every person who senses this in himself should say, "May Allah bless you." As for a person who sees something that pleases him, of wealth or children, let him say, "Mashallah, la quwwata illa billah" (What Allah wills; there is no power except with Allah).
* Student: And if he does not say it?
* Shaykh: There is nothing wrong.
* Student: That is, he visited you in your house, and you have some good thing, so he looked at this good thing, and you felt that he wants this good for himself. Did you sense from his words...?
* Shaykh: No. People say this: if he speaks about something, they say: say "Mashallah," or say "Tabarak Allah," or something similar, and then he mentions it.
* Student: He mentions it, meaning.
* Shaykh: But merely that he saw my son with me and he is handsome or light (...), mentioning Allah is not valid.
* Student: Some people say that the hadith «Envy consumes good deeds» is a weak hadith. Does it help (...)? Is there no evidence that envy is a major sin?
* Shaykh: No. There is the fact that it is one of the traits of the Jews «And whoever imitates a people is one of them»[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4033) from the hadith of Ibn Umar.]].
* Student: O Shaykh, the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they say to those who disbelieve, "These [people]..."﴾. Who is meant by ﴿these﴾, according to the more correct view?
* Shaykh: ﴿These﴾ means the disbelievers of Quraysh. For this reason I told you that the lam may either mean "in" (fi), so that "these" retains its literal sense, or the lam is for transitivity, as when you say, "I said to so-and-so: such-and-such." Then ﴿these﴾ would mean what? "You" (antum). That is, they say openly to the disbelievers: "You are better guided in the way than those who believed."
* Student: May Allah bless you, Shaykh. If a person is envied, what should he do to protect himself from this envy? Does he have a reward with Allah? If something afflicts him, what does he have with Allah?
* Shaykh: If a person is envied, meaning he is afflicted by the evil eye, then he is rewarded without doubt for his patience. Whatever afflicts him is an expiation for his sins. But that other person, who is the one who envies, is the transgressor and the aggressor, a wrongdoer.

The scholars differed regarding whether, if something is destroyed because of the evil eye of another person, the one with the evil eye must compensate for it. The correct view is that he must compensate; that is, he is liable, because the right of a human being makes no distinction between intentional and unintentional harm. But if he struck him with the evil eye until he died, shall we kill him? Yes. Some scholars say: we kill him, because the evil eye kills. Some scholars say: yes, we kill him, but with the evil eye of another evil-eyed person. This is problematic: when does this occur? They said, according to experience: if a person challenges the one with the evil eye, the latter cannot harm him. If he says to the evil-eyed person, "Come, I challenge you," he will not harm him, because he will have a strong soul that repels the soul of the second.

* Student: Shaykh, the verse ﴿The one who said, "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you"﴾... In the verse ﴿A powerful one of the jinn said, I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it. One who had knowledge of the Scripture said, I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you﴾. What is meant by ﴿the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾? Is he from the 'Afarit (powerful jinn)?
* Shaykh: What is meant by ﴿the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾ is a believing man who asked Allah, the Exalted, and the angels brought it to him. The angels brought it, and the angels are stronger than the devils.
* Student: Is there a cure for envy if a person is envied?

* Shaykh: Yes, indeed. It has many remedies. Among them is what the Prophet ﷺ directed: that the one who is afflicted performs wudu' (ablution) and washes his *maghabin* (the places where the sweat collects, i.e., the hollows behind the knees) and similar places. Then the sick person is given it to drink and it is poured over his head, and he is healed at once by Allah's permission.[[Recorded by Ibn Majah (3509) from the hadith of Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf.]] Among them are remedies known to us through experience: one takes the *faniluh* (a small amount of the cloth or what is attached) and the *taqiyyah* (the fabric in contact with the body), the part that touches the body, and places it in water, and the afflicted person drinks it and is cured immediately.

There is also a third thing, which they say, though I do not know whether it is authentic or not: that a funeral prayer be performed over the one who causes the evil eye (*'ayn*). He is prayed over with the funeral prayer, and when he is prayed over with the funeral prayer, his eye dies and he no longer afflicts anyone with the evil eye. But I do not know this, I have not verified it.

Some of those accused of the evil eye were once asleep, and then his brothers who were in the house gathered together. When [the one leading] said, "They want to perform the absent funeral prayer for him," and when he said, "Allahu akbar," [the sleeper] said, "Allahu akbar kabira," and got up and said, "How do you do this?" They said, "Because when a person is an evil-eye causer and then the funeral prayer is performed over him, his eye is nullified." But we have not verified this.

As for the matter of taking from his *sha'ar* (what is close to his body), meaning what is adjacent to his body, this is a remedy that has been tested, widely transmitted, and well known.

* Student: What if you were to make the Sunnah correct, O Shaykh? The hadith in the story of Sahl ibn Hunayf, is it not the basis for this?

* Shaykh: Yes. But do we say: we do not go beyond what the Messenger ﷺ did, or do we say: if something is established by experience, there is no harm in using it?

* Student: Is the funeral prayer over this evil-eye causer legislated, meaning that they perform the absent funeral prayer over the evil-eye causer?

* Shaykh: No. It is not beneficial; its condition is that he be present before them.

* Student: From a legal standpoint, O Shaykh?

* Shaykh: No, I do not know, I am not aware of anything about this.

Someone says: "It was reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he used to recite in Maghrib (the sunset prayer) with *al-Tur*."[[Agreed upon; Bukhari (765) and Muslim (463/174), from the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mut'im.]] Did he recite all of it?

Yes, he recited in Maghrib with *al-Tur*. The letter *ba'* (in *bi-al-Tur*) indicates completeness (*istiab*).

* Student: And *al-A'raf*, O Shaykh?

* Shaykh: And *al-A'raf*, all of it.

Is it permissible to deposit money in banks without interest?

In any case, if it is possible to avoid depositing anything in banks, that is the best. If you are compelled to do so, there is no harm, on the condition that you do not take *riba* (usury), and be careful to deposit with the one least involved in usury.

If a scholar exercises *ijtihad* (independent legal reasoning, deriving a ruling from the sources) on a question and acts accordingly, then another opinion appears to him and he changes from the first, does his second *ijtihad* not nullify his earlier ruling that arose from his first *ijtihad*? What is its form? And what is the position of the *muqallid* (one who follows the opinion of another) regarding the two *ijtihads*?

If the scholar's *ijtihad* differs, then if he explicitly retracts the first, his statement is the second. If he does not explicitly retract, he has two opinions, and the second *ijtihad* does not demolish the first, because each of the two *ijtihads* may be an error and may be correct. As for the *muqallid*: if one of them becomes preferable to him, meaning his inclination leans toward one of the two *ijtihads*, he acts accordingly; otherwise, he is free to choose.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿So among them are those who believed in it, and among them are those who turned away from it, and Hell is sufficient as a blazing fire. Indeed, those who disbelieved in Our verses, We will drive them into a Fire. Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment. Indeed Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise. But those who believed and did righteous deeds, We will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. For them therein are purified spouses, and We will admit them into deep shade.﴾ [An-Nisa' 55–57].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who believe in *jibt* and *taghut*?﴾ and so on to the end.

Who is meant by ﴿those who were given a portion of the Scripture﴾ in this verse?

* Student: The Jews.

* Shaykh: The Jews, good. And what is meant by *jibt*?

* Student: *Jibt* is what has no benefit in religion. And according to the statement of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him: it is magic.[[Previously cited.]]

* Shaykh: Yes, either magic. And it was said that it is an idol. There are multiple opinions, which are gathered together in this: everything that has no good in religion, or everything that is harmful to religion, is *jibt*. And *taghut*?

* Student: "Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: it is Satan."[[Previously cited.]] And Ibn al-Qayyim defined it: it is everything by which a servant exceeds his limit, whether a person who is followed or obeyed.

* Shaykh: Or worshipped.

* Student: Or worshipped or obeyed.

* Shaykh: Good. And according to this, Umar's explanation, may Allah be pleased with him, is by way of example.

﴿They say to those who disbelieved﴾: what about the *lam* here?

* Student: The *lam* here has two possibilities.

* Shaykh: It may carry two meanings.

* Student: Either it means *fi* (in), so the meaning is: they say concerning those who disbelieved.

* Shaykh: And according to this, is the demonstrative (*ism al-ishara*) to be taken literally?

* Student: Literally.

* Shaykh: And according to this, the demonstrative is taken literally.

* Student: The second meaning: the *lam* is in its original function of conveying the verb to its object, so the meaning is: they say to those who disbelieved: "These (meaning you) are better guided than those who believed in terms of the way."

* Shaykh: Then the demonstrative becomes addressing, meaning: you. What do they point to? I mean, what do they intend by their saying "those who disbelieved" and by their saying ﴿more guided than those who believed in terms of the way﴾?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: And ﴿those who believed﴾?

* Student: ﴿Those who believed﴾ are the Messenger ﷺ and the Companions.

* Shaykh: Well done, exactly.

What is the recompense that Allah placed upon them?

* Student: Allah cursed them.

* Shaykh: That Allah cursed them. And what does cursing mean?

* Student: Expulsion and distancing.

* Shaykh: Expulsion and distancing from the mercy of Allah.

What is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Or do they have a share of the dominion? Then they would not give the people even a speck (*naqir*)﴾?

* Student: That is, do they have a share of dominion? That is, they have no share. And if they had a share, they would not give people even a *naqir*. The *naqir* is what is found on the back of a date pit, and it is used as a proverb for little.

* Shaykh: Well done. That is, do they have a share of dominion, so that they dispose of it and say: these are more guided and these are more wretched? Or do they give these and withhold from those? And if they had a share, then what?

* Student: They would not give people.

* Shaykh: They would not give people a *naqir*, because they are among the most miserly of people.

* From the benefits of the verse: ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾ and so on to the end: the denunciation of the people of envy, because of His saying: ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾

We mentioned in the last lesson the harms of envy. What is its remedy? We say concerning its remedy:

First: that a person be content with Allah's decree and destiny, and that he know that bounty is in Allah's hand, He gives it to whom He wills. When he knows this, he will be at peace and will not object to his Lord, Exalted and Majestic, regarding what He has given them of His bounty.

Among them: that he knows that his envy will never prevent Allah's bounty from reaching the one envied. And if it could prevent Allah's bounty from the one envied, then every person would envy another.

Among them: that he turns to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in asking Him to give him the like of what He gave this person, as Allah the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿And do not wish for what Allah has favoured some of you over others. For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned﴾, followed by ﴿And ask Allah of His bounty﴾ [An-Nisa' 32].

Among them: that he mentions the consequences of envy, its evil and its punishment, so that he fears this evil and punishment, and so he refrains.

Among them: that he knows it is one of the characteristics of the Jews.

The essential point is that when a person reflects on its harms, that reflection is a remedy by which he protects himself from envy.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the clarification that Allah bestowed favour upon these envious people through what He mentioned in His saying: ﴿We had already given the family of Abraham the Scripture and wisdom﴾ and so on to the end. There is no justification for envy along with what Allah the Exalted has given them of bounty. This is also one of the remedies by which a person treats envy: he says, for example, "Why should I envy so-and-so when Allah the Exalted has given me such-and-such?"

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the clarification of what Allah bestowed upon the family of Abraham: the Scripture, wisdom, and great dominion. For example, the Torah and the Gospel are all Scripture and wisdom. And great dominion: who is the greatest, among those you know, who was given dominion from the Children of Israel?

* Students: Sulayman, peace be upon him.

* Shaykh: Sulayman, peace be upon him. For he was given a great dominion, to the extent that he said: ﴿Grant me a dominion such as will not belong to anyone after me﴾ [Sad 35], because of its greatness.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has the right of disposal over His dominion as He wills. He withholds and He extends.

"Why should I envy so-and-so when Allah the Exalted has given me such-and-such?!"

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the clarification of what Allah bestowed upon the family of Abraham: the Scripture, wisdom, and great dominion. For example, the Torah and the Gospel are all Scripture and wisdom, and great dominion: who is the greatest, among those you see, who was given dominion from the Children of Israel?

* Students: Sulayman, peace be upon him.

* Shaykh: Sulayman, peace be upon him. For he was given a great dominion, to the extent that he said: ﴿Grant me a dominion such as will not belong to anyone after me﴾ [Sad 35], because of its greatness.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has the right of disposal over His dominion as He wills, for He withholds and He extends, because of His saying: ﴿We had already given the family of Abraham the Scripture and wisdom, and We gave them a great dominion﴾ [An-Nisa' 54].

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So among them is he who believed in it, and among them is he who averted from it﴾ [An-Nisa 55]. ﴿Among them﴾: the pronoun refers to the family of Ibrahim; meaning, not every member of the family of Ibrahim accepted this Book, this wisdom and this kingdom. ﴿Among them is he who believed in it﴾: here "min" (مِن) is for partitive (تبعيض, indicating a part). The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿and among them is he who averted from it﴾. So Allah divided them into two groups. The partitive may come with the particle indicating it in both groups, or it may come in only one of them, and be omitted from the second group, as in His saying: ﴿So among them are the wretched and the happy﴾ [Hud 105]. The meaning is: "among them are the wretched, and among them are the happy," because it is not possible for one to be both wretched and happy at the same time; but the particle was omitted from the second group or counterpart. ﴿Among them is he who believed in it﴾ and before that, and believed in the Book and the wisdom, and was grateful for the blessing of the kingdom. ﴿And among them is he who averted from it﴾: he averted from it, so he did not believe in it, and did not thank Allah for this blessing and this great kingdom.

And His saying: ﴿he who averted from it﴾. ﴿Averted (ṣadda)﴾ is used both intransitively and transitively. The intransitive meaning is that he averted from it by himself, and the transitive meaning is that he averted others from it. Both attributes are established for these people: they avert from it themselves, and they avert others from it. Even the Children of Israel claim that Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon him, was not a prophet, but a king, of vast kingdom and strong kingdom, strong authority, and not a prophet; and likewise Dawud, they consider him not a prophet but a king. The correct view is that they were among the messengers and prophets, but Allah the Exalted gave Sulayman that great kingdom.

Then He said: ﴿And Hell suffices as a blaze﴾. Meaning: how great is the blaze that will befall these people in Hell!

﴿Kafā (suffices)﴾: we have previously mentioned that it takes the particle bi (بـ) as its complement, but they say: the bi is extra in form; that is, in terms of i'rab (grammatical case-marking). As for meaning, it has a purpose, which is making (kafā) transitive to its object. They say: the bi is an extra particle of jarr (جر, genitive), and that Jahannam in this verse is the subject (fā'il); i.e., it suffices. And ﴿sa'īran (as a blaze)﴾ — what is it?

* Students: It is a tamyīz (تمييز, specification).

* The Shaykh: It is a tamyīz. And sa'īr means "the kindled" (al-mus'ʿar) or "the blazing" (al-sā'ir), and both indicate a great burning.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: people are divided, regarding the blessings of religion and worldly life that Allah grants them, into two groups: a group that believes and a group that disbelieves. This is the sunnah of Allah, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He it is who created you, so among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [At-Taghabun 2]. Had Allah willed, He would have made mankind one community, but in His mercy He made them differ, so that Allah may know the truthful from the liar, so that the banner of jihad may stand, so that enjoining good and forbidding evil may stand, and so that the believer may know the worth of Allah's blessing upon him in faith, and so that the believer may strive for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to keep him firm, lest he become like these people. The sum is that Allah, glorified and exalted, divided people into two groups for great wisdoms.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: those who did not believe in it turned away from it, and also barred people from it; due to His saying: ﴿and among them is he who averted from it﴾. We have mentioned that it is used intransitively and transitively, and that in this verse it is suitable for both meanings.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the magnitude of the burning of the Fire; due to His saying: ﴿And Hell suffices as a blaze﴾.

* Among its benefits: whoever averts from what Allah has given of the Book and wisdom, he will be fuel for Hell, and we seek refuge in Allah.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 56 (part 1 of 3):

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved in Our verses - We will surely drive them into a Fire﴾, and after it He said: ﴿But those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾. This is the method of the Qur'an, which is repetitive (mathani): that is, when the mention of the people of the Fire comes, the mention of the people of Paradise comes too; when the mention of the righteous (muttaqun) comes, the mention of the criminals (mujrimun) comes, and so on, so that a person travels toward Allah between fear and hope, and so that he does not become bored if the speech were in one uniform pattern.

He said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved in Our verses, We will surely drive them﴾. "Disbelieved in them" means they denied them and rejected them. The root of the word (kafara) is covering and concealment, and from it is named al-kufurra, which is the sheath of the date-palm spathe.

His saying ﴿Our verses﴾ includes both the cosmic verses (al-ayat al-kawniyya) and the legislative verses (al-ayat al-shar'iyya). From disbelief in the legislative verses is denying the messengers and not adhering to the laws that the messengers brought. From disbelief in the cosmic verses is attributing this universe to other than Allah, or saying that someone assisted Allah in it, or saying that someone has a share in it; all of this is denial of the verses. Among it is denying that the eclipse occurred as a warning from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and as a means of frightening; because some people say: the eclipse has an ordinary cause, and it is not so that Allah may frighten His servants with it. This is considered a type of disbelief, though not disbelief that removes one from the religion, but it is a kind of disbelief.

﴿We will surely drive them into a Fire﴾. "Sawfa" (surely/will): the grammarians say it is a particle of what?

* Student: Taswif (future of deferral).

* Shaykh: Taswif. It indicates the certainty of the occurrence of a thing, but after a period of time, because taswif means delay, and from it the saying: "He delayed (sawwafa) in repentance," i.e., he postponed it. So the meaning of "sawfa" is that they will surely burn, but after a time.

His saying ﴿We will surely drive them into a Fire﴾: that is, We will make them burn in it until it consumes them. ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will exchange them for other skins, that they may taste the punishment﴾. ﴿Roasted through (nadijat)﴾: the root nadj means reaching the utmost in completion; that is, when they are roasted through from the burning and consumed, they are replaced with other skins, different from the first, because the first was burned and gone. Why? ﴿That they may taste the punishment﴾, i.e., the pain. Because when the skin is burned, it becomes a barrier between the rest of the body and the fire, so they do not feel the fire; but when it is replaced with a new skin, then they feel the heat of the fire. We seek refuge with Allah from it, and for you. So whenever their skins are roasted, We replace them.

﴿Kullama﴾ is a conditional particle that indicates repetition; that is, they are forever and always: whenever the skins are roasted through, they are replaced with other skins, for this wisdom ﴿that they may taste the punishment. Indeed Allah is ever Mighty and Wise﴾. "The punishment" means the pain by which they are tormented.

﴿Indeed Allah is ever Mighty and Wise﴾. ﴿Kana﴾ is a past-tense verb, but it is not intended to denote time; it indicates the certainty of the attribute indicated by its predicate, without restriction to a time. For this reason they say it is stripped of time in this usage. Why? Because if we said it indicates time, then might and wisdom would have ended and passed away.

His saying ﴿ʿAzīzan (Mighty)﴾: the scholars said that al-ʿAzīz has three meanings. The first: ʿizzat al-qadr (greatness of power/worth); the second: ʿizzat al-qahr (irresistible dominance); the third: ʿizzat al-imtina' (invulnerability). As for ʿizzat al-qadr, it means He is of great worth, nothing resembles Him. As for ʿizzat al-qahr, it means He is the victor who overpowers every tyrant. As for ʿizzat al-imtina', it means He is protected from every defect, deficiency, and evil. From it is the saying: "a hard land (arḍ ʿazāz)", i.e., firm, firm and resistant to softness. All these meanings, and perhaps other meanings too, are established for Allah: ﴿So to Allah belongs all might﴾ [Fatir 10]. As for al-Ḥakīm (the Wise), it is derived from ḥikma, which is firmness and perfection, and from ḥukm, which is judgment and decision. Allah, glorified and exalted, is Wise, possessing perfect wisdom, and Ḥakīm can mean Ḥākim, the judge who decides between His servants, to whom all matters return, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, His is the judgment, and He is the swiftest of reckoners﴾ [al-An'am 62].

It should be known that the judgment of Allah, glorified and exalted, is divided into: a cosmic, decreed judgment (ḥukm kawnī qadarī), and a legislative, religious judgment (ḥukm shar'ī dīnī). As for the cosmic decreed judgment, they gave as an example His saying about one of Joseph's brothers: ﴿I will not leave this land until my father permits me or Allah judges for me﴾ [Yusuf 80]. He intends by that a decreed judgment, not a legislative judgment, because Allah did not legally prevent him from returning to his family; rather, he intends that Allah should judge for him a decreed judgment. As for the legislative judgment, its evidence and example is His saying, blessed and exalted, in Surat al-Mumtahanah, after He mentioned the rulings He mentioned: ﴿That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 10]. This is a legislative judgment. The two kinds may combine in one verse, such as His saying, blessed and exalted: ﴿To Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-Qasas 70], and His saying: ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ [al-Tin 8]. The point is that the judgment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is divided into: decreed cosmic, and second, legislative religious. We have mentioned for each one a proof and an example, and we mentioned what combines both kinds, and all of that is present in the Qur'an.

If someone asks: which of them is necessarily executed upon the servants, the cosmic or the legislative?

The cosmic decreed one. It is executed upon the servants, and no one can oppose or resist it. As for the legislative judgment, by which Allah judges between the servants, some servants accept it and act upon it, and some servants do not accept it or act upon it. Wisdom, which is one of the two meanings in His saying ﴿Ḥakīman﴾, is derived from iḥkām, which is perfecting a thing; so the firm thing is the perfected thing. Some scholars explained it as: putting things in their proper places; meaning that when you see this thing you say it is not suitable in its place except for it. Then wisdom is wisdom in the thing itself, and wisdom in the purpose of the thing; that is, the thing in itself conforms to wisdom, and secondly, its purpose is praiseworthy wisdom. Let us consider ablution, for example: its being in this manner, beginning first with the face, then the two hands, then the head, then the ears, and that some limbs are washed while others are wiped, this is without doubt wisdom; that is, its being in this specific form is wisdom. Then its purpose, which is purification from sins and purification from minor impurities, is without doubt a praiseworthy end. So wisdom exists in the essence of the thing and in its purpose, and all of this is established in the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. If we say that judgment is cosmic and legislative, and wisdom is wisdom in the essence of a thing and wisdom in its purpose, then all of it becomes how many divisions?

* The students: Four.

* Shaykh: Four divisions. God willing, the rest of the discussion of the verse will come.

* Student: O Shaykh, ﴿Had Allah willed, they would not have fought one another﴾ [al-Baqarah 253]. O Shaykh, is it among the divine sunan? That is, He makes the disbelievers believers by command, O Shaykh. How is this a decreed judgment, O Shaykh?

* Shaykh: Yes, this is a decreed judgment accomplished by the legislative judgment.

* Student: Alright, O Shaykh, if someone objects and says: Well, what does it mean? This was decreed upon them that they become disbelievers. How is the response to them?

* Shaykh: What?

* Student: If someone argues with them, O Shaykh, and says: it means Allah, glorified and exalted, judged upon them that they become disbelievers. How is the response to them?

* Shaykh: We respond to them with His saying, Exalted: ﴿Had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear; and if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were refusing﴾ [al-Anfal 23]. Last night we spoke about the Qadariyya and the Jabriyya, and we said that each of them has a suspicion (shubha), is that not so?

* The students: Yes.

* Shaykh: But are these suspicions clear to you, or shall we clarify them now?

* The students: Let us clarify them.

* Shaykh: Yes, let us clarify them; because some people said to me: Well, why did you not clarify these suspicions?

We mentioned that the suspicion of the Qadariyya is that Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those among you who strive and are patient, and We will test your reports﴾ [Muhammad 31]. ﴿Until We know﴾: so now He does what?

* The students: He does not know.

* Shaykh: He does not know? Well, the answer to this is that we say: the knowledge of Allah, glorified and exalted, is of two kinds; it is divided into two parts: knowledge of what will be, and knowledge of what has been. He knows that this servant will carry out what he was commanded, or that this servant will not carry out what he was commanded, is that not so?

Knowledge of what will be does not entail reward or punishment, because nothing was directed at the responsible person in it, so no reward or punishment follows from it. The second is knowledge of what?

* Student: Of what we know.

* Shaykh: Of what has been. This is what Allah, the Exalted, meant by: ﴿until We know﴾, that is, until We know the thing as having occurred and actualized, and at that point what follows from it is what? The recompense: reward or punishment. And what supports this is that Allah, glorified and exalted, has shown in many verses that Allah has known everything: ﴿Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heaven and the earth? Indeed that is in a Book; indeed that is easy for Allah﴾ [al-Hajj 70]. He said in the verse on fasting: ﴿Allah knew that you were deceiving yourselves﴾ [al-Baqarah 187]; and He said: ﴿Allah knew that you would remember them﴾ [al-Baqarah 235], and they had not yet remembered them: ﴿you will remember them﴾. So the summary is that we say: knowledge is divided into?

* Student: Two kinds.

* Shaykh: What are they?

* The students: Knowledge of what has been and what will be.

* Shaykh: Knowledge of what has been, and knowledge of what will be. Which of them entails punishment or reward? The knowledge of what has been, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿until We know those among you who strive and are patient﴾. Therefore some scholars explained it as meaning: until We know with the knowledge of manifestation, that is, the knowledge of the occurrence of the thing.

We remain with the answer to the Jabriyya who said: Allah said: ﴿Had your Lord willed, they would not have done it﴾ [al-An'am 112], ﴿Had Allah willed, those after them would not have fought one another after the clear proofs came to them, but they differed, so some of them believed and some of them disbelieved; and had Allah willed, they would not have fought﴾ [al-Baqarah 253]. We say: Yes, their fighting occurs by the will of Allah, without doubt, and their associating partners occurs by the will of Allah, as He said: ﴿Had Allah willed, they would not have associated; and We did not make you a guardian over them, nor are you over them a manager﴾ [al-An'am 107]. But did Allah grant them will and volition, or did He not grant them?

* The students: He granted them.

* Shaykh: He granted them: ﴿Among you is one who desires this world, and among you is one who desires the Hereafter﴾ [Al 'Imran 152]; ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its due striving﴾ [al-Isra' 19]; ﴿Whoever desires the immediate [world]﴾ [al-Isra' 18]. So volition belongs to the human being and no one denies it. What Allah has decreed upon you, you have no knowledge of before you do it, so that you can use it as an argument; is that not so? What Allah has decreed upon you, you have no knowledge of before you do it, so that you may argue by the decree of Allah. For we say to the one who argues by the decree of Allah: What informed you that Allah decreed wretchedness upon you?

Why did you not decree that Allah decreed for you what? Happiness, so that you would be happy? Then they would have no argument. And Allah has already refuted this argument in fact: ﴿Those who associated will say: Had Allah willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything. Likewise did those before them deny, until they tasted Our might﴾ [al-An'am 148]. Had they had an argument, they would not have tasted the might of Allah, because they would be excused.

* Student: ﴿Had Allah willed, they would not have fought﴾: attributing the fighting to them, does it not indicate that they have a will?

* Shaykh: Yes, it indicates that the act is theirs.

* Student: The saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿We replaced them with other skins﴾: does ﴿baddalnāhum﴾ mean replacing the skin itself by renewal, or another skin?

* Shaykh: Yes, He creates a new skin different from the first skin that was burned.

* Student: O Shaykh, we have seen in some cities people who claim knowledge, yet they do not pray, nor do they enjoin good, nor forbid evil, nor pay zakat, and they argue with His saying: ﴿Those who, if We establish them in the land﴾ [al-Hajj 41], etc. We told them that the Prophet ﷺ prayed in Makkah while he was not empowered at that time, and they said: this is by way of recommendation (istihbab).

* Shaykh: By way of what?

* Student: By way of recommendation, because the Qur'an is what clarifies.

* Shaykh: Yes. ﴿As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow what is unclear of it﴾ [Al 'Imran 7]. This is a report by Allah about something future: ﴿And Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed Allah is Strong and Mighty. Those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer, give zakat, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾ [al-Hajj 40-41]. So it is said to these people: Allah promised those who support Allah with this, with support, and you now do not enjoin good nor forbid evil, so you do not deserve support. If you want support, then do that: enjoin good, forbid evil, establish prayer, and give zakat.

* Student: May Allah bless you. You have now mentioned that they will replace them with skins other than their skins. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, will our bodies be the bodies we have now?

* Shaykh: What?

* Student: Our bodies now, the ones we are now upon; will those bodies on the Day of Resurrection be the very same?

* Shaykh: No, they will be greater, far greater.

* Student: That is, will they be sixty cubits?

* Shaykh: Greater. It has come in an authentic hadith that "the molar tooth of one of them is like the mountain of Uhud" [[Reported by Muslim (2851/44) from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, with the wording: "The molar of the disbeliever, or the fang of the disbeliever, is like Uhud..." the hadith.]], and we seek refuge with Allah; their bodies are enlarged because of the severity of the punishment.

* Student: O Shaykh, if a Qadari objects to us, O Shaykh, and says: Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me has come into effect: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together﴾ [al-Sajdah 13].

* Shaykh: Qadari or Jabari?

* Student: Jabari.

* Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: He says: this is a matter; that is, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wrote that He will fill Hell with mankind, and Paradise likewise. So then, if Allah willed, everything would be?

* Shaykh: Well (...) the river of Paradise. We do not see it being used except for the people of Paradise; it is not divided into two parts, it becomes from these, and we do not want more from you than this.

* Student: That is, on the Day of Resurrection, if they argue, they go to the Fire and say: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wrote upon me that I enter...

* Shaykh: On the Day of Resurrection they do not argue, may Allah bless you. They acknowledge the error, saying: ﴿Had we been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze﴾ [al-Mulk 10], and they ask Allah to return them, saying: if we return we will believe: ﴿So return us; we will do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Sajdah 12]. On the Day of Resurrection there is no argument in it; but the discussion now is...

* Student: Shall we not strike this on his face, O Shaykh?!

* Shaykh: Who?

* Student: This Jabari.

* Shaykh: By Allah, if you gave him a slap on the face and said: By Allah, I am compelled to this, there is no objection!

* Student: O Shaykh, ﴿So among them is one who believed in it﴾ [al-Nisa' 55]. Some people believe that the Prophet ﷺ has no valid lineage?

* Shaykh: No, we did not say it in general; the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is from the family of Ibrahim.

* Student: O Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, you mentioned that the skins are other than the first skins.

**Shaykh:** Yes, they change them.

**Student:** Yes indeed. Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, says: "Their changing is only their renewal." This was because the Jahmiyyah (a sect that denied Allah's attributes) argued against him, saying: "How can He punish skins that have committed no sin?" So he said: "Their changing is their renewal."

**Shaykh:** Yes. It is not unlikely that this is a correct meaning. That is, it is not improbable that it is a correct meaning. It may be supported by the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿On the day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾ [Ibrahim 48], even though the earth itself is the original. But the original sense of "tabdil" (change) is replacing one thing with another. These skins are not independent entities that could be punished, so that one could say they were punished without any crime. These skins are like garments for these people, so they are not counted. Therefore what Imam Ahmad said is a possible interpretation, may Allah have mercy on him.

**Student:** What Imam Ahmad said is that the skins are replaced?

**Shaykh:** Now?

**Student:** They say: "How is it punished when it has not sinned?" The skins are replaced; it is not the skin that feels. The person is the one who feels, the person is the one who perceives the punishment and the beating...

**Shaykh:** They say that doctors (but I do not know whether this is certain or not) say that what is inside the skin does not suffer, does not feel pain, and that pain belongs only to the skin. That is the opposite of what you are saying. Yes. Allah made the skin feel pain so that a person would sense what afflicts him. But now, stick a needle in: the first thing you feel is in the skin. The inner flesh you do not feel. Then, among the blessings of Allah is that the inner flesh has no sensation. If it had sensation, when this bread moves along the small intestines, could a person sleep?! Now if an ant walks on your skin, you cannot sleep. If an ant walks on your skin while you are sleeping, you cannot sleep, sleep will not come to you. But what about these things moving through the small intestines? For this reason, glory be to Allah the Mighty, whenever a person contemplates the wisdom of Allah, he sees wonders beyond wonders. When this food becomes ready to be expelled, the person feels it; that is, when it asks permission, it comes to the door and you feel it. But before that, it moves about in these small intestines, twisted one upon another, and you do not feel it at all.

**Student:** About the miracles, Shaykh, scientifically.

**Shaykh:** What?

**Student:** Some people attribute scientific miracles from medicine and other fields to verses of the Qur'an, and trace them back to the verses?

**Shaykh:** If the verses allow for these scientific miracles, there is no objection.

**Student:** The problem, Shaykh, is that there comes (...).

**Shaykh:** No, I said: if they allow it. But if it is merely an illusion, then it does not mean, for example, that when they reached the moon they said: this is indicated by the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass [through]﴾ [al-Rahman 33]. That is not correct.

**Student:** Some of them say... some of them think it allows it, as an illusion...

**Shaykh:** No, no. The indication must be established, otherwise it is not permissible. (...)

"Peace be upon you, O Prophet" (al-Salam alayka ayyuha al-Nabi): this is a supplication. "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah": a supplication. "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad," "O Allah, bless Muhammad," "I seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of Hell": all of these are supplications. Likewise between the two prostrations: "My Lord, forgive me and have mercy upon me." All of them are supplicatory sentences.

**Students:** The reasoning (ta'lil), Shaykh?

**Shaykh:** This is the one who asks: Is the testimony of a single woman accepted regarding the sighting of the crescent of Ramadan?

Answer: Yes, it is accepted, because it is a religious report, just as if she reported the sunset, for example.

He says: Shaykh, in some jurisprudential matters the disagreement of the scholars of hadith and the jurists creates difficulty for us. What is the criterion for preferring one view in such a matter?

As for the young student of knowledge and the layperson, they follow whoever they consider more trustworthy in his knowledge and religion. As for the rising student of knowledge who has taken a share of knowledge, he himself reviews the evidences of both sides until it becomes clear to him which is the stronger.

He says: I was puzzled by the saying of the one who said: "And dreams, when they are interpreted, come to pass." Does the occurrence of a dream depend on its interpretation?

No. It may occur before it is interpreted, but when it is interpreted, it occurs according to the interpretation. For this reason, a person should not, "if he sees what he dislikes, present it to anyone, because if he presents it, and it is then interpreted, it occurs by the permission of Allah. Rather, if he sees what he dislikes, he should get up and spit to his left three times, and say: 'I seek refuge in Allah from the evil of Satan and from the evil of what I have seen,' and turn over to his other side, and not tell it to anyone. This is when he sees what he dislikes, and it will be a relief once," until the Companions said: "We used to become ill when we saw a dream we disliked, until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told us this hadith, and our affair became settled."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7044), and Muslim (2261/4), from the hadith of Abu Qatadah al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

As for when you see what you love, beware of relating it to someone who does not love you. Do not tell it except to one who loves you, because Allah said about Jacob: ﴿Do not relate your vision to your brothers, lest they plot against you a scheme﴾ [Yusuf 5].

**Student:** Who is speaking, Shaykh?

**Shaykh:** Jacob says it to Joseph.

**Student:** If he presents it to a layman who does not know, Shaykh, an ignorant person?

**Shaykh:** He should not present it. Whatever he dislikes, he should not present.

**Student:** Shaykh, (...)?

**Shaykh:** No.

**Student:** So it is excused, Shaykh?

**Shaykh:** No, not at all. What you dislike, do not mention.
