* And among the benefits of this noble verse: a person may claim what he is not truthful about, as in His words: ﴿they claim that they believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you﴾.

* And among its benefits: the obligation to believe in what was revealed to the Messenger and what was revealed before him, as in His words: ﴿that they believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you﴾. This indicates that belief in what was revealed before him is equivalent to belief in what was revealed to him, although it differs in method and law (*shir'ah* and *minhaj*), as Allah said: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a method﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:48]. Otherwise, the origin of the religions is one in terms of faith and beliefs, but it differs in law and method, because Allah is All-Wise, legislating for each nation what suits it, and what its condition requires of righteousness and reform.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the perfection of Islam and of those who adhere to it, because Islam commands people to believe in everything Allah has revealed, and those who adhere to it likewise believe in everything Allah has revealed. Those who have adopted other than Islam, such as the Jews and Christians, do not believe in everything Allah has revealed, do they? As for the earlier ones among them, they believe in it only in a general, implicit way (*iman hukmi*), meaning they believe in what came after their laws in a general way, because they did not encounter it. The believers in Moses in his time and the believers in Jesus in his time believe in the Qur'an, because they find that the Messenger is written in their Torah and Gospel. But it is implicit belief. As for the belief of Muslims in the Qur'an and in the earlier laws, it is true belief, because the religion of Islam is the latest.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's elevation (*'uluw*). From where is this derived?

* Students: From the fact of sending down.

* Shaykh: From the fact of sending down? If someone says: the sender is not mentioned in ﴿what was revealed to you﴾. Did He not say "what We revealed"?

* Students: It is known.

* Shaykh: Because it is known, and what is known is like what is mentioned. For this reason Allah said: ﴿and man was created weak﴾ [an-Nisa' 4:28]. If someone asks: who created man? We say: what? Allah. The verse does not say "Allah created man." We say: because it is known that there is no creator except Allah. This is known by the created order (*kawnan*). ﴿Man was created weak﴾. And the sending down of revelation is known by the law (*shar'an*), because the one who sends down revelation is Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Therefore, from this we derive the elevation of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. This is what the Book, the Sunnah, the consensus (*ijma'*) of the early generations, sound reason, and fifthly, innate nature (*fitrah*) indicate. This is a known matter, and praise be to Allah.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that seeking judgment from other than Allah and His Messenger is seeking judgment from the false deity (*taghut*, false authority or transgressor). As in His words: ﴿they desire to seek judgment before the false deity﴾.

* And among its benefits: that seeking judgment from other than Allah and His Messenger is disbelief. From where is this derived? From their being declared liars in their claim of faith, in His words: ﴿they claim﴾, because if they were believers they would have desired to seek judgment before Allah and His Messenger.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: if desiring to seek judgment before the false deity removes one from Islam, then actually seeking judgment before it is all the more so. Whoever loves and desires that judgment be sought before the false deity, even if he does not actually seek it, is not a believer. How much more so is one who fulfills this desire and actually seeks judgment before the false deity! For this reason Allah the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided, and submit in full submission﴾ [an-Nisa' 4:65]. These are great, emphatic conditions. ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not believe﴾ is a sentence emphasized by an oath and by an extra particle in form: the oath is ﴿by your Lord﴾, and the extra particle is ﴿no﴾, because this "no" is not a negator.

﴿Until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves.﴾ This is the act. ﴿Then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided.﴾ That is: they do not find constriction regarding what you have decided. The third: ﴿and submit in full submission﴾, that is, complete submission without hesitation. A person may find within himself discomfort with a legal ruling, or may not find it, but he does not submit and hasten to comply. But he does not believe until the discomfort is removed from him and until he submits in full.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: we are commanded to disbelieve in the false deity: ﴿and they have been commanded to reject it﴾. Our faith is not complete except by disbelieving in the false deity, as His words indicate: ﴿So whoever disbelieves in the false deity and believes in Allah has grasped the most reliable handhold﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:256]. There must be disbelief in the false deity, or else faith in Allah is not valid.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that Satan has a will. From where is this derived? ﴿And Satan intends﴾. Yes, he has a will, and indeed he has a command. From where is this derived? From His words: ﴿Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you toward immorality﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:268]. He wills and he commands. Alright, can we, or is it possible for us, to repel this will and this command? By what? By seeking refuge in Allah from him, because Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you, then seek refuge in Allah﴾ [al-A'raf 7:200]. When the Companions complained to the Prophet (ﷺ) about the evil thoughts they found in their souls, he said: "Whoever finds that, let him seek refuge in Allah," and [let him] "desist" [agreed upon; reported by al-Bukhari (3276) and Muslim (134/214), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah]. This is the protection from it.

* And among the benefits of this verse: that Satan wants the children of Adam to go astray a far-off straying, not a near straying. As in His words: ﴿and Satan intends to lead them far astray﴾. But do you think that Satan orders far-off straying right from the start? What does he do?

* Students: Gradually.

* Shaykh: Gradually. He first commands immorality and minor sins, then major sins, then disbelief, may Allah protect us and you from it. For this reason the scholars said: sins are the postal route to disbelief. Do you know what a postal route (*bareed*) is? A postal route is a fixed distance of three farsakh (about 18 km). In the past they had no airplanes or telephones, so how did they deliver messages in a short time? They divided the distance into postal stages. A rider takes the messages from one station and gallops with his horse to the end of the stage. Then another rider is waiting, takes the message, and proceeds with it to the next station, and so on until they reach the destination. This is the reason it is called a postal route. The point is that the scholars say: sins are the postal route to disbelief. Satan leads a person step by step until he destroys him.

* Student: O Shaykh, may Allah bless you. Regarding those who judge by other than what Allah has revealed, there are lawyers, O Shaykh. That is, is the lawyer included in His words: ﴿They desire to seek judgment before the false deity, and they have been commanded to reject it﴾?

* Shaykh: This question is very important. In other words, if we are in a country that does not rule by the Shari'ah but by civil law, may we seek judgment before it? We say: first, if there is no necessity, we do not seek judgment before it. That is, if reform is possible, we do not seek judgment. If reform is not possible, we look to see whether there is someone we can choose to be an arbitrator between us. If we find one, it is not permissible for us to seek judgment before these courts. If we do not find one, then we seek judgment, not with the intention of accepting everything they rule, but with the intention of accepting only what agrees with the Shari'ah, because this is a necessity. Otherwise, rights would be lost. Rights are not ten riyals or twenty riyals, which does not matter, but may be property and real estate. If a person does not seek judgment before these courts, he loses his right.

So here we say: it is permissible to seek judgment, not with the intention of accepting their ruling, but with the intention of accepting what agrees with the Shari'ah. But after two preliminaries: the first is attempting reform, and the second is seeking judgment before a man who rules by the law of Allah. If that is not possible, then rights are not lost.

As for the lawyer now: this lawyer who wishes to seek judgment before a non-Shari'ah court, we say: if his intention is that, were they to rule by other than the Shari'ah, he would not accept it, then there is no harm. But if his intention is that they rule in his favor according to what he wants, whether or not it agrees with the Shari'ah, then this is forbidden, even if it is in Shari'ah courts.

Suppose a person is an excellent advocate, eloquent in pleading and argument, and he wishes to represent someone even before a Sharia court, while intending to reach his own objective rather than the objective of Allah and His Messenger. Is this forbidden or permissible? It is forbidden, and there is no doubt about this. Some people have a powerful ability to persuade in argument or in pleading. When such a person sits before the judge with a quiet, gentle opponent, he may devour him with his words, and the judge rules by what?

* Student: By what he hears.
* Shaykh: By what he hears, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said. This is the principle of every advocate who pleads while wishing to reach his own goal rather than the goal of Allah and His Messenger. Such people are not permitted to follow this method.
* Student: (...) because they come and take their in-laws, they take...
* Shaykh: That is not correct. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They are the enemy, so beware of them﴾ [al-Munafiqun 4].
* Student: If they are the in-laws of the Muslims, they take them...

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by Allah's permission. And if, when they wronged themselves, they had come to you and asked Allah's forgiveness, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance, Merciful. But no, by your Lord, they do not believe until they make you judge in what they dispute among themselves, then find within themselves no resistance to what you decide and submit in full submission. And if We had prescribed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," only a few of them would have done it. But if they had done what they were admonished, it would have been better for them and firmer in strengthening [their faith]. And then We would have given them from Us a great reward. And We would have guided them to a straight path.﴾ [al-Nisa' 64–68].
* Shaykh: Enough, praise be to Allah. I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by Allah's permission﴾. The benefits remaining from...
* Student: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows﴾.
* Shaykh: Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts﴾.
* From this noble verse it is derived that nothing that is in the breasts is hidden from Allah the Exalted, by His saying: ﴿Allah knows what is in their hearts﴾.
* Among its benefits: a person is held accountable for what the heart earns. This is not contradicted by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah has overlooked for my nation what their souls whisper about, as long as they do not act on it or speak of it."[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (5269) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] This is because the whisper of the soul (hadith al-nafs) is not settled. That is, a person may whisper to himself but it does not take hold. If it takes hold, it becomes an act.
For this reason the scholars said: the heart has an act, and the soul has a whisper. The act of the heart is to settle upon a thing and adopt it. So what is it that Allah threatened in His saying: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts﴾? The answer: it is the act of the heart, that a person acts with his heart, meaning he becomes content with the thing his soul has whispered to him.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation to turn away where speech is of no benefit, by His saying: ﴿So turn away from them﴾. Some scholars held that this verse was abrogated (naskh, the cancellation of a ruling by a later text) by the verses on jihad. That is not so. Rather, the verses on jihad concern one matter and this verse concerns another. This verse concerns disputing with the hypocrites, and the hypocrites cannot be fought with weapons, because they show that they are Muslims. They can only be struggled against with knowledge and clear explanation. So when we have explained to them and yet they persist in dispute, we turn away from them.
For this reason Imam Malik may Allah have mercy on him said: If a disputer comes to you, explain the Sunnah (the prophetic way) to him and do not dispute with him. For when you explain the Sunnah to him, you place the proof before him. If he disputes, then whom is he disputing with? He is disputing with Allah, not with you. Explain the Sunnah and do not argue about it with a disputer, because the obligation of one to whom the Sunnah has been made clear is to accept it without dispute.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: when a person turns away from these hypocrites and their like, he does not leave them without admonition. Rather he admonishes them, perhaps they will benefit, by His saying: ﴿And admonish them﴾. We have already discussed the meaning of admonition (mawiza). What is it?
* Student: Reminding of Allah combined with encouragement and warning.
* Shaykh: Reminding combined with encouragement and warning, yes.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: when a person speaks, he should speak with eloquent speech that reaches the soul, by His saying: ﴿And speak to them concerning themselves a far-reaching word﴾.
* Among its benefits also: it is part of the etiquette of the speaker to face the one he addresses, by His saying: ﴿And speak to them﴾. The word (lahum, "to them") means that the speaker should turn toward the one he addresses. So he should not speak while turning away, or speak while facing another direction. Rather, when he wants to speak with a person in admonition, his face should be turned toward that man, by His saying: ﴿And speak to them﴾.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by the permission of Allah﴾. First, the grammar (i'rab). His saying ﴿min rasulin﴾ (from a messenger): its place is in the accusative as the direct object, but the superfluous (za'idah) ﴿min﴾ has entered upon it to emphasise generality. So in its i'rab we say: ﴿rasulin﴾ is a direct object in the accusative, and its accusative sign is a presumed fatha on its final letter, its appearance being prevented by the occupation of the position by the movement of the superfluous preposition.

Know that when you say of a particle that it is superfluous (za'id), you do not mean that it is superfluous in meaning, but that it is superfluous in terms of grammatical function (i'rab). As for meaning, all superfluous particles are said to be particles of emphasis (tawkid), so every superfluous preposition is a particle of emphasis.

Second: His saying ﴿li-yuta'a﴾ (to be obeyed). The lam here is for causation (ta'lil), not for consequence (aqibah), so pay attention! Why? Because not every messenger is obeyed, but the wisdom behind sending is that he be obeyed, so the lam here is for causation.

Also His saying: ﴿And if they, when they wronged themselves, had come to you﴾. ("Idh") is an adverb of past time, not of the future, and ("idh") comes for causation rather than temporal location. An example is His saying: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you did wrong, that you will be sharing in the punishment﴾ [az-Zukhruf 39], meaning: because you did wrong. And you say: "I came to you because you came to me," even though the time of the second coming differs from the time of the first, but here ("idh") is for causation.

Also in the grammar, they say that ("law") is specific to verbs, and here it has entered upon ("anna"). So what is the answer to this rule that says "law" is specific to verbs, although here it has not entered upon a verb? The answer is to say that the verb is omitted, and the estimate is: "And if it were established that they, when they wronged themselves, came to you..." As for ﴿jaaooka﴾ (they came to you), it is the answer of ("law").

His saying: ﴿they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾. ﴿And if they, when they wronged themselves, had come to you and asked Allah's forgiveness, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾. The lam is also placed in the answer of the condition: ﴿they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾, and so on to the end.

Allah the Exalted says that He sent no messenger except to be obeyed by Allah's permission. The messengers were not sent so that they would be denied and harmed, even if the outcome may be denial and harm. But the basic purpose of sending messengers is obedience to them, as in His saying: ﴿I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they worship Me﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 56]. This means this is the basic purpose of creating jinn and mankind: that they were created for worship, not for amusement and play. But is this realised in every single human and every single jinni? No.

So this verse is like the verse in Surat adh-Dhariyat, except that the one in adh-Dhariyat relates to the testimony that there is no god but Allah, while this one relates to the testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. That one concerns tawhid, and this one concerns risalah. So the messengers were sent only to be obeyed, not to be denied, harmed, or killed; for among the messengers were some who were denied, harmed and killed, and some who were obeyed.

His saying: ﴿except to be obeyed by the permission of Allah﴾. The "permission of Allah" is divided into two kinds: kawni (universal, decreed) and shar'i (legislative). Which is meant here? The shar'i, though it may also be the kawni, meaning: to be obeyed if Allah permits that by His decree. Among the messengers who were sent to be obeyed is Muhammad ﷺ.

Therefore He followed it with His saying: ﴿And if they, when they wronged themselves, had come to you﴾, meaning: if, at the time they wronged themselves, they had come to you, that is, came to you in a state of having wronged themselves. This concerned a dispute that arose between them, so they sought judgement from someone other than the Messenger ﷺ. So if, at the time this wrong occurred, they had come to the Messenger ﷺ, ﴿and asked Allah's forgiveness, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾.

His saying: ﴿when they wronged themselves﴾, meaning when they wronged themselves through the dispute and contention that arose between them. ﴿had come to you﴾, that is, come to the Messenger ﷺ. It is known that the meaning is that they came to you during your lifetime. This is shown by His saying: ﴿and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them﴾, since after his death he cannot ask forgiveness for them, as his deeds ended with his death, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "When a person dies, his deeds come to an end."[[Narrated by Muslim (2682/13) from Abu Hurayrah.]]

﴿They came to you and asked Allah's forgiveness﴾, that is, for the wrong they had committed, ﴿and the Messenger asked forgiveness for them﴾ as confirmation of that, ﴿they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾.

Here, in His saying ﴿and the Messenger asked forgiveness for them﴾, there is an explicit noun in place of a pronoun. The original would be "and you asked forgiveness for them," but it was stated explicitly in place of the pronoun to draw attention to the fact that the Prophet ﷺ is a messenger, and that the Messenger's asking forgiveness for them has a distinction over others, since the supplication of the Messenger is answered. So for this reason he used the description of messengership instead of the pronoun, which is the original form in this place.

﴿they would have found Allah...﴾: we said the lam is in the answer of ("law"), and that ﴿jaaooka﴾ is the predicate of ("anna"). The estimate: "And if they had come to you when they wronged themselves, and asked Allah's forgiveness, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them." As for its i'rab, we restate it a second time: ("idh") is an adverb, and an adverb must have a governing element, which is ﴿jaaooka﴾.

﴿fastaghfaru Allah﴾ is conjoined to ﴿jaaooka﴾, and ﴿wastaghfara lahumu ar-rasul﴾ is conjoined to it as well. ﴿lawajadu Allah﴾: the lam is in the answer of ("law"), and on this basis the answer of ("law") is His saying ﴿lawajadu Allah﴾.

His saying: ﴿tawwaban﴾. At-Tawwab is one of Allah's names, and Allah's acceptance of repentance is divided into two kinds: repentance meaning granting the guidance to repent, and repentance meaning accepting repentance. An example of the first is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And to the three who were left behind, until when the earth was narrow for them despite its vastness, and their souls were confined to them, and they thought that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them so they might repent﴾ [at-Tawbah 118]. What follows? ﴿li-yatubu﴾ (so they might repent). What is the meaning of ﴿tab﴾?

* Students: He granted them success in repenting.

* The Shaykh: He granted them success in repenting, and decreed it for them. As for His saying: ﴿And He it is who accepts repentance from His servants﴾ [ash-Shura 25], this is evidence that "at-tawwab" comes with the meaning of "one who accepts repentance", and an example is His saying: ﴿Forgiver of sin and Acceptor of repentance﴾ [Ghafir 3]. So at-Tawwab is one of Allah's names, and it has two meanings: the first, the one who grants success in repentance; the second, the one who accepts repentance.

His saying: ﴿Merciful﴾ is also one of Allah's names, so among the names of Allah is ar-Rahim, and Allah's mercy is divided into two kinds: general (ammah) and specific (khassah). The general mercy encompasses all creation, and it is for the believer and the disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked, but only in this world. The specific mercy is for the believers only, according to His saying: ﴿And He is ever Merciful to the believers﴾ [al-Ahzab 43], and it exists in this world and in the religion as well.

Know further that the mercy of Allah is one of His attributes that are established for Him in the true sense, and it is not as the people of ta'til (denial of attributes) claim, meaning: the will to do good or good itself. For the people of ta'til do not believe that Allah has mercy, and they say: every place where mercy is mentioned means doing good or the will to do good. Why? Because they thought that the mercy which Allah affirmed for Himself is like the mercy of created beings, so they said: mercy involves a kind of tenderness, emotional response and softness, and these are not befitting to Allah.

It is said to them: these attributes or meanings you have claimed are specific to whose mercy? The created being's. As for the Creator, He is merciful along with His strength and power. Moreover, your claim that mercy is softness, gentleness and humiliation is a false claim, for a powerful ruler may exist who is full of might, and may yet have mercy. But because of their conception that the mercy Allah affirmed for Himself is like the mercy of created beings, they denied it and said: it is impossible for Allah to have mercy. This is why Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book al-Fatwa al-Hamawiyyah: "Every denier is a likener (mumaththil)."

You may find this surprising and say: how can he deny, while we say he is a likener? Because he denies only on the basis of likening, on the premise that if he affirms, he has likened. So he likened first and denied second. An example is this attribute, mercy; another example is the face. They said: it is impossible for Allah to have a face, for if He had a face it would follow that He resembles created beings, and this is impossible. We say: you have thus likened first and denied second.

* * *

In this noble verse there are benefits. First: the affirmation of wisdom for Allah, the Exalted, in sending messengers, by His saying: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by the permission of Allah﴾.

* Among its benefits: the establishment that voluntary actions subsist in Allah, the Exalted, meaning that voluntary actions occur anew for Him according to the objects of those actions. From where is this taken? From His saying ﴿arsalna﴾ (We sent), since the sending of messengers occurs successively, the first being Noah and the last being Muhammad, peace be upon them all.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation that Allah's actions are causally motivated (ta'lil). From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿except to be obeyed by the permission of Allah﴾. This is what the Ahl as-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah hold: that Allah's actions and rulings are motivated by causes, but the cause may be known to us or unknown to us, either in general or in particular.

The meaning of his saying "either in general" is that it may be unknown to all humanity, or unknown to some people but not others. Otherwise, we know that all of Allah's actions and rulings are motivated, tied to causes, wisdoms and secrets, but some of them are known to the creation and some are not.

If someone asked us: why is the noon prayer four rak'ahs, why not two or six? We say: Allah knows best; no one knows, none of mankind knows.

If someone asked: why is the eating of camel meat a nullifier of wudu'? Some scholars say: Allah knows best, because it does not come from wisdom, and they say: this is a matter of worship; we must worship Allah by performing wudu' if we eat camel meat, and not ask. Other scholars say: rather, this is motivated by a cause, namely the strength and devilry of camels; when a person eats this meat, he is affected by it, so he performs wudu' in order that this strength acquired by eating camel meat may subside. This is why a person is commanded, when angry, to perform wudu', so that wudu' may extinguish the heat of anger.

Likewise the camel pens: some scholars understood the wisdom of praying in camel pens, and some did not understand the wisdom. Scholars may also differ on the cause. Regarding the prohibition of praying in a graveyard, what is its cause? Some scholars said: the cause is that the soil of the graveyard mixes with the discharges of the dead and the impurities in it; and some scholars said: rather, the cause is fear of shirk. Which of these is more sound?

* Students: The second.

* The Shaykh: The second is certainly more sound. Firstly, because not every graveyard is dug up. Secondly, the basic rule is what: purity or impurity?

* Students: Purity.

* The Shaykh: Purity. The point is that all of Allah's actions and rulings are motivated, but some of them have a known cause, some do not have a known cause, and some are known to some people but not others.

* Among the benefits of the verse: that the legislative wisdom may have its ruling diverge. It is taken from His saying: ﴿except to be obeyed﴾. This is the legislative wisdom in sending messengers, but it may be what? It may diverge, as in His saying: ﴿I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they worship Me﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 56]. This is the legislative wisdom, and it may diverge.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of permission for Allah, the Exalted, by His saying: ﴿except to be obeyed by the permission of Allah﴾. Permission is of two kinds: legislative (shar'i) and universal (kawni). An example of the first is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Or do they have partners who have ordained for them in religion that which Allah has not permitted?﴾ [ash-Shura 21]. Is it legislative or decreed?

* Students: Legislative.

* The Shaykh: And it is not valid decreed?

* Students: It is not valid.

* The Shaykh: Yes, it is not valid; because it has occurred, Allah has permitted it decreed, but He has not permitted it legislatively. Among that is also the saying of Allah: ﴿Say: Has Allah permitted you, or do you fabricate against Allah?﴾ [Yunus 59], that is, permitted you legislatively. The universal permission is abundant, such as His saying: ﴿Who is it that intercedes with Him except by His permission?﴾ [al-Baqarah 255], and likewise this verse.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person must hasten to repentance and seeking forgiveness, by His saying: ﴿And if they, when they wronged themselves, had come to you and asked Allah's forgiveness, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them﴾.

* Among its benefits: that it is legislated for one who has wronged himself in a dispute or litigation to come to the Messenger ﷺ to ask Allah's forgiveness, and to ask the Messenger to forgive him, because the Messenger, peace be upon him, holds judgement and to him the litigation is referred. So it is legislated for them to come to the Messenger and seek Allah's forgiveness in his presence, and for the Messenger, peace be upon him, to ask forgiveness for them.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that if a person wrongs himself, he should go to the grave of the Prophet ﷺ to seek Allah's forgiveness there, so that the Messenger may ask forgiveness for him.

* Students: It is not permissible.

* The Shaykh: Not permissible? Fine, what about the verse?

* Students: During his life.

* The Shaykh: Yes, the verse is about his lifetime. Nevertheless, the people of extremism (ghulu) have cited it to argue that a person, when he commits a sin, should come to the Prophet's grave, seek Allah's forgiveness, and have the Messenger ask forgiveness for him. They support this with a fabricated story: a Bedouin of the 'Utbi tribe came to the grave of the Prophet, peace be upon him, and recited:

"O best of those buried in the valley, whose bones..." (and so on to the end of the two verses). When he slept, he saw the Prophet ﷺ, who said to him: "Indeed Allah has forgiven you."[[Mentioned by Ibn al-Jawzi in Muthir al-'Azm al-Sakin ila Ashraf al-Amakin (2/301).]] This is a fabricated story, and the verse shows the falsity of this claim, because the verse says: ﴿when they wronged themselves﴾, and is "idh" for the past or the future?

* Students: For the past.

* The Shaykh: For the past. If it had said "if they wrong themselves" there might be some doubt, but it says "when they wronged themselves." Moreover, even if it had said "if they wrong themselves," there would be no evidence in it, because His saying ﴿and the Messenger asked forgiveness for them﴾ definitively prevents this from being after his death, since the Messenger ﷺ cannot ask forgiveness for them after his death.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that whoever repents and seeks forgiveness sincerely and sincerely will find repentance and mercy, by His saying: ﴿they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾.

Is any sin excepted from this? No; with repentance no sin is excepted. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed Allah forgives all sins﴾ [az-Zumar 53]. This is a general verse, all sins.

And there is a detailed verse: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾.

The great heads of sins Allah mentioned: ﴿do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ this is shirk; ﴿and do not kill the soul﴾ aggression against the self, which is the greatest bodily aggression; ﴿and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾ aggression against honour. ﴿And whoever does that will meet a penalty. The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation, except for one who repents and believes and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ [al-Furqan 68–70].

Does this include the hypocrites?

* Students: Yes.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 64 (part 2 of 2):

* The Shaykh: Yes, it includes them, by the generality of the text, and by the words of Allah Most High concerning the hypocrites in particular: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will not find for them a helper. Except for those who repent and amend and hold fast to Allah and devote their religion to Allah. Those will be with the believers, and Allah will give the believers a great reward.﴾ [An-Nisa' 145-146].
Can it be derived from the verse that one may ask another for supplication, by saying: "O so-and-so, ask Allah's forgiveness for me"? Or can it be derived from it that a person benefits from the supplication of another?
* Students: The second.
* The Shaykh: Yes, the second. That is because the verse does not state that they asked the Messenger to seek forgiveness for them; rather, the verse states that they sought forgiveness from Allah and the Messenger sought forgiveness for them, and the verse does not mention a request. And it is known that a person benefits from the supplication of another. Indeed, the Prophet ﷺ said to the Companions: «When you say that», meaning "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah", «you have indeed greeted every righteous servant in the heavens and the earth»[[Reported by al-Bukhari (831) and Muslim (402/55), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud.]].
Likewise, Allah related of the believers that they say: ﴿Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith﴾ [al-Hashr 10]. And likewise Muslims pray over their dead and say: "O Allah, forgive them and have mercy on them, forgive him and have mercy on him." This is a matter of scholarly consensus: that a person benefits from the supplication of another.
But is it permissible to ask another to supplicate for you? This is a matter of disagreement. Some scholars said: there is no harm in asking a righteous man to supplicate for you. They cited as evidence that a man would come to the Prophet ﷺ and say: "O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah that He send us rain," and he would supplicate; and that sometimes they asked the Prophet ﷺ to supplicate to Allah for their forgiveness and he supplicated for them; and that the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, sought intercession through al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib in asking for rain[[Reported by al-Bukhari (1010) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]]; and that the Prophet ﷺ commanded whoever met Uways al-Qarani to ask him for supplication[[Reported by Muslim (2542/225) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]]; and that the Prophet ﷺ said to 'Umar: «Do not forget us, O my brother, from» -what?- «your supplication»[[Reported by Ibn Majah (2894), and Ahmad (195), from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]].
But none of these contains evidence. As for a person asking the Prophet ﷺ, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, to supplicate for him, this is specific to him. For this reason it is not reported that anyone came to Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, or 'Ali saying: "Supplicate to Allah for me."
As for seeking rain through al-'Abbas, it was because 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Stand up, O 'Abbas, and supplicate to Allah for us." He asked him to supplicate for the general body of Muslims. There is no harm in your going to a person in whom you hope for goodness and the answering of supplication and saying: "Supplicate to Allah for the Muslims that He send them rain," because you are not supplicating for yourself.
As for Uways al-Qarani, that is specific to him. For this reason we know with certainty that Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, and the jurists among the Companions are superior to him; yet the Prophet ﷺ did not command anyone to say: "Ask these people to supplicate for you." Rather, this is specific to him alone.
Based on this, the better course is that you do not ask anyone to supplicate for you. However, Shaykh al-Islam restricted this ruling to the case where you intend your own specific benefit. As for when you intend the benefit of your brother by his reward for supplicating for you, and his reward for the angel's supplication for him, for whoever supplicates for his brother in his absence, the angel says: "Amin, and for you the like of it," or "and for you the like thereof"[[Reported by Muslim (2732/85) from the hadith of Abu al-Darda'.]]. He said: if he intends this, then he intends kindness to his brother, and so he is not included in the blameworthy matter.
* Student: O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The Student: We mentioned, O Shaykh, that the supplication of the Messengers is answered.
* The Shaykh: Yes, generally.
* Student: O Shaykh, regarding ﴿bi-ma qaddamat aydihim﴾ (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, "because of what they sent forth," i.e., because of the sins they committed.
* Student: You asked me a question in the previous lesson, where is the answer to the question?
* The Shaykh: What?
* Student: The application of a part to the whole.
* The Shaykh: The application of a part to the whole. We say: when a part is mentioned and the whole is intended, this indicates that this part is a condition for the continuation of the whole. The brother raised an objection to this with His saying: ﴿bi-ma qaddamat aydihim﴾. We said: they answered this by saying that it was expressed with the hands, not because they are a condition for the rest of the body, but because they are generally the instrument of action.
* Student: O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The Student: May Allah bless you, O Shaykh. His saying ﷺ: «As long as he does not act or speak»[[Reported by al-Bukhari (5269) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. Does it not present a difficulty, O Shaykh, to what we preferred earlier, that inner speech, where a person speaks to himself and then continues, is hypocrisy? Because this one spoke to himself and then went on with it?
* The Shaykh: How?
* The Student: It was mentioned earlier, O Shaykh, in..
* The Shaykh: That it does not break the fast.
* The Student: O Shaykh, for example, this has settled in your heart and your chest, that he spoke to himself and began to continue, and every time he wanted, for example, to release his desire, he continued and said: "This is inner speech."
* The Shaykh: Yes, correct.
* The Student: Then he releases.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The Student: And satisfies his desire.
* The Shaykh: He has done nothing.
* The Student: And in the hadith: «He leaves his desire for My sake»[[Agreed upon; reported by al-Bukhari (1894) and Muslim (1151/164) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]].
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The Student: This one did not leave his desire.
* The Shaykh: He did not do it.
* The Student: But he did act, O Shaykh; he continued, this inner speech continued with him.
* The Shaykh: But did the continuing result in an action?
* The Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: No action occurred from him. Yes. For this reason we said: if an action occurred, such as moving his member for example, or rolling on the ground, his fast is invalidated.
* Student: May Allah be pleased with you, O Shaykh. Does not the one who sends greetings upon the Prophet ﷺ, Allah returns his soul to him and he returns the greeting[[Reported by Abu Dawud (2041) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]?
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The Student: The greeting?
* The Shaykh: Indeed.
* The Student: Some said: since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, returns his soul to him, and it has been reported that the prophets are not dead in their graves but they pray[[Reported by Abu Ya'la (3425) and al-Bazzar (6391) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]], that they are not dead, so should we call upon them both during their lives and after their deaths?
* The Shaykh: Is this one of the matters of the unseen or of the observable?
* The Student: The unseen.
* The Shaykh: Are matters of the unseen restricted to what we have heard, or do we bring something from our own?
* The Student: No, to what we have heard.
* The Shaykh: To what we have heard. So we say: Allah returns the Messenger's soul and he returns the greeting, but we do not go beyond this. Otherwise we would say: how have you become, how is your color today, may you be well. Then the life of the barzakh is other than the life of this world, even the martyrs are alive with their Lord, receiving provision, but the life of the barzakh is other than the life of this world. Otherwise we would say that the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, committed a great offense against the Messenger, in that they buried him while he was alive.
* Student: O Shaykh, you said: Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, who mentioned the story; how do we respond to him?
* The Shaykh: We respond that he is not infallible, not infallible, and perhaps at that time the discussion of it did not reach him with its chain of transmission.
* Student: O Shaykh, may Allah bless you, you mentioned an allusion in deriving benefits: the allusion to the people of innovation and the grave-worshippers who take refuge with the Messenger ﷺ while he is now dead. O Shaykh, if there is someone explaining this verse who has before him some people, or a group of them, or who thinks some people among them are of them, is it preferable that he present this issue to them in order to refute it?
* The Shaykh: He must present it to remove doubt from them, but he should not, for example, be harsh in criticizing them. Rather he says, for example: some people may understand from this verse such and such.
* The Student: So he does not do what you did, O Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: What?
* The Student: As if you derived it (...) first.
* The Shaykh: How?
* The Student: (...) this derivation first; we do not mention it as you mentioned, that this is a benefit and so on?
* The Shaykh: Wisdom is the lost property of the believer. Address the person in a manner suited to his condition.
* Student: O Shaykh, may Allah bless you. We have learned that the Prophet ﷺ appears in... if one of us sees the Prophet ﷺ, meaning he has seen him, as came in the hadith: «Whoever has seen me in a dream has indeed seen me, for the Shaytan cannot take my form»[[Agreed upon; reported by al-Bukhari (6993) and Muslim (2266/10) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. So if the Prophet ﷺ appeared to one of them in a dream and said to him: "So-and-so son of so-and-so has been forgiven," would this dream be true?
* The Shaykh: What do you say? He says: if the Shaytan cannot take the form of the Prophet, peace be upon him, and whoever sees the Messenger has seen the truth, and I saw the Messenger and he said: inform so-and-so that Allah has forgiven him, such and such? Should I inform so-and-so, and would this truly be that Allah has forgiven him?
The Messenger only informed that whoever sees him [has seen the truth], and did not mention anything about his speech. As I told you: in matters of the unseen we restrict ourselves to what has been reported, and we do not say, for example, that if the Messenger related a hadith to us we would act upon it. What we mentioned to you about the story of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah does not apply here, because what he mentioned is something the Sunnah has brought, namely excess in supplication; indeed the Qur'an has also brought it.

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿And if We had decreed upon them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except for a few of them. But if they had done what they were being advised to do, it would have been better for them and stronger in firmness. And then We would have given them from Us a great reward. And We would have guided them to a straight path. And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast affirmers of truth, the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions. That is the bounty from Allah, and sufficient is Allah as Knowing.﴾ [An-Nisa 66–70].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. The discussion of His, Blessed and Exalted is He, statement ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves﴾ has already passed, and we took its benefits.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if We had decreed upon them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes"﴾. We also already spoke about the beginning of this verse in terms of its tafsir (exegesis) and i'rab (grammatical analysis).

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And if We had decreed upon them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it﴾; that is because they dislike what pains and harms them in this world, and they do not care, if this matter is lifted from them, whether they are obedient or disobedient.

His statement ﴿Kill yourselves﴾ does not mean that a person kills himself; rather it means that he kills his brother, because a person's brother is like his own self. The evidence for this is the statement of Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿And do not defame one another﴾ [Al-Hujurat 11], and it is known that a person does not defame himself but rather defames his brother.

His statement ﴿or leave your homes﴾ is also among the things that are hateful to the souls: that a person be expelled from his land. This is among the most hateful things to the soul; he leaves his homeland in which he has lived, leaves his property, and leaves the land he knew. It is difficult for souls. Had We imposed that upon them, only a few of them would have submitted; only a few of them would have done it, because of their preference of this world over the Hereafter.

His statement ﴿except for a few of them﴾ is an exception, and "few" means less than half, while "many" means half or more. But what is more than half is called "more," and what is less than it is called "the fewer."

﴿And if they﴾ means: if these people who sought judgment from other than the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and who were commanded to seek judgment from the Messenger, ﴿if they had done what they were being advised to do, it would have been better for them﴾; what they are advised to do is to return to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him and his family. ﴿It would have been better for them﴾ in their present state and in their final outcome. ﴿And stronger in firmness﴾ means: firmer in establishing themselves upon the truth, because whenever a person increases in obedience to Allah, he increases in faith, certainty, and steadfastness.

* From this verse the following benefits are derived. First: the demonstration of human weakness, and that a person cannot bear everything he is commanded to do when it does not suit him, especially when faith is weak, and more so if we say that this verse was revealed concerning the hypocrites.

* Among its benefits: killing people among themselves is among the hardest things for souls.

* Among its benefits also: expulsion from homes is among the difficult things for souls, since Allah, the Exalted, made it an example here: ﴿or leave your homes﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the saved among the servants are few, by His statement ﴿except for a few of them﴾. So examine yourself: are you among those few or among the many? This ruling is supported by what is established in the two Sahihs and others: "Allah, glorified and exalted, will call out on the Day of Resurrection: 'O Adam!' He will say: 'Here I am at Your service and pleasure.' Allah will say: 'Bring forth from your progeny a group for the Fire.' He will say: 'O Lord, what is the group for the Fire?' He said: 'Out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine.'" That is, one in a thousand is from the people of Paradise and the rest of the children of Adam are from the people of the Fire. "This weighed heavily upon the Companions, and they said: 'O Messenger of Allah, which of us is that one?' He said: 'Rejoice, for you are among two nations which have never been present in anything except that they outnumbered it: Ya'juj and Ma'juj.'" Then he said: "I truly hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise, a third of the people of Paradise, and half of the people of Paradise"[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (3348) and Muslim (222/379) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]]. The Companions rejoiced at this and glorified Allah.

This indicates that the children of Adam, the very few among them, are those who are saved from the Fire, and the rest are from the people of the Fire; we seek refuge in Allah from it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: obedience to Allah, the Exalted, is the cause of every good, by His statement ﴿But if they had done what they were being advised to do, it would have been better for them﴾.

* Among its benefits: the legal rulings are admonitions; for this reason Allah called the Qur'an an admonition, saying: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord and a healing for what is in the chests, and guidance and mercy for the believers﴾ [Yunus 57].

The reason that commands and prohibitions are admonitions is that a person takes admonition from them, so he carries out the command and avoids the prohibition. Many people do not understand from the word "admonition" except what is accompanied by encouragement or warning, but this is not a condition.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the differing of ranks among the servants, by His statement?

* Student: ﴿it would have been better for them﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿it would have been better for them and stronger in firmness﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: steadfastness upon the truth varies; some of it is strong and powerful, some of it is weak, and some of it is intermediate, by His statement ﴿and stronger in firmness﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an indication of the great matter that will occur in the future, and that a person is feared to slip unless Allah makes him firm, by His statement ﴿and stronger in firmness﴾; because firmness is not mentioned in places where there is no slipping; firmness is mentioned only in the context of places of slipping.

It is known that a person encounters doubts in his life and encounters desires. Doubts erode knowledge and remove knowledge, and desires erode the will, until a person wants only what he desires. This is a calamity. A person is surrounded by two things: doubt by which knowledge departs, and desire by which willpower departs. If Allah does not make him firm with knowledge, sincere will, and resolute determination, he will perish.

Is it understood from this that faith varies?

* Student: ﴿it would have been better for them﴾.

* The Shaykh: Is it understood? I do not want you to bring the evidence.

* The student: It is understood.

* The Shaykh: It is understood. What is the reasoning?

* Student: His statement: ﴿it would have been better for them﴾.

* The Shaykh: What is its reasoning? The word "better" (khayr), what do you see in it? Is it a comparative form (ism tafdil) or not? I am asking you.

* The student: It is a comparative form.

* The Shaykh: The comparative form requires the existence of a preferred and a compared-to, and this is variation. Likewise it is understood from His statement, what? ﴿and stronger in firmness﴾ that faith varies.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if We had done so, We would surely have given them from Us a great reward (67) And We would have guided them to a straight path﴾. (Idhan) is a particle of the present time, (idh) is for the past, and (idha) is for the future. These three particles divide up time. (Idh)?

* Student: For the past.

* The Shaykh: And (idha)? Yes indeed.

* The Student: For the future.

* The Shaykh: And (idhan)?

* The Student: For the present.

* The Shaykh: For the present. That is: "And if they had done what they were admonished to do, We would surely have rewarded them for it."

﴿We would surely have given them from Us a great reward﴾. (Atā), with the long vowel, means "to give," so it is one of the sisters of what?

* Students: (kasā).

* The Shaykh: (Kasā). That is, it is one of the verbs that take two objects which were not originally a subject and predicate, unlike (zanna) and its sisters, which take two objects that were originally a subject and predicate. An example: you say, "Zayd is standing" (Zaydun qā'imun). Introduce (zanna) to it: "I thought Zayd to be standing" (ẓanantu Zaydan qā'iman). And you say, "I clothed Zayd with a robe" (kasawtu Zaydan jubbatan). Remove the verb: could you say "Zayd" as a subject and "a robe" as a predicate? It is not possible. For this reason a distinction is made between (kasā) and its sisters and (zanna) and its sisters. (Ātā) belongs to which of the two categories?

* Students: The category of (kasā).

* The Shaykh: The category of (kasā), the second category. Its first object is the pronoun ha' in His saying ﴿la-ātaynāhum﴾, and the second is ﴿ajran﴾.

﴿wa-idhan la-ātaynāhum﴾ means: We would have given them. ﴿min ladunnā﴾ means: from Our presence. ﴿ajran ʿaẓīman﴾ means: a reward. Allah, the Exalted, called the reward that He placed upon deeds "ajr" (a wage), so that it may be clear to a person that this reward will certainly be obtained, just as the wage must be obtained by one who rents a house or the like; he must receive the rent.

Here "ʿaẓīm" (great) means both abundant and intense, meaning that it is a reward which a person cannot fully comprehend, because it is great. Describing a thing as great, coming from the Great One, indicates its greatness.

That is, this verse is evidence that a person is rewarded with a reward other than the strengthening mentioned by Allah in the first verse, namely that he attains a great reward from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. All of this is to encourage doing what the servant is admonished to do.

* And in this noble verse is evidence against the claim of the Sufis who say: "Worship Allah for Allah's sake and do not worship Him for the sake of Allah's reward." The proof: if mentioning the reward had no effect on the deed, mentioning it would be what? Futile and pointless. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned the reward and encouraged action for the sake of reward only to make clear that intending the reward does not weaken the deed nor contradict sincerity. Allah described His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and those with him as seeking "a bounty from Allah and good pleasure," saying: ﴿You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and His good pleasure﴾ [al-Fath 29].

Moreover, another verse praises those who seek the Face of Allah, so this is evidence that if you desire the Face of Allah you are rewarded, and if you desire Allah's reward you are also rewarded.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the greatness of this reward, in two respects: the first is its attribution to Allah in His saying ﴿min ladunnā﴾, since the gift of the Great is great; and the second is from His saying ﴿ajran ʿaẓīman﴾.

**Ibn 'Uthaymin's Commentary (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Karim) on Surah 4, Verse 68:**

﴿And We would surely have guided them to a straight path.﴾ The word ﴿صِرَاطًا﴾ (*ṣirāṭan*, "a path") has two readings: with the letter *sīn*, ﴿سِرَاطًا﴾ (*sirāṭan*), and with *ṣād*, ﴿صِرَاطًا﴾. This construction also takes two objects (*maf'ūlān*, the direct objects of the verb), which are not originally a subject and predicate. The first object is the pronoun *hā'* in ﴿لَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ ("them"), and the second is ﴿صِرَاطًا﴾.

(**Hudā**): Guidance here includes the guidance of knowledge and instruction, and the guidance of divine success and right direction. We have already explained that when the verb is followed by ﴿إلى﴾ (*ilā*, "to"), it means guidance in the sense of indication and direction. When it is used without the preposition, it includes both meanings. We have given examples of this. Among the examples of the verb followed by ﴿إلى﴾ is the saying of Allah about His Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [al-Shūrā 52].

That is, when the verb is followed by ﴿إلى﴾, it means guidance in the sense of indication and direction, and when the preposition is dropped, it includes both meanings. We have given examples of this. Among the examples of the verb without the preposition is the saying of Allah in Surah al-Fātiḥah: ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾ [al-Fātiḥah 6]. This verse as well, ﴿And We would surely have guided them to a straight path﴾ [al-Nisā' 68], is of this kind.

* Among its benefits: whoever does what he is admonished to do and obeys Allah and His Messenger will be guided to the truth. The reward of a good deed is another good deed after it.

* Another of its benefits: if you want breadth of knowledge and firmness in knowledge, then hold fast to obedience to Allah, because whenever a person is guided by Allah's guidance, his guidance increases, as Allah says: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muḥammad 17].

The saying ﴿صِرَاطًا مُسْتَقِيمًا﴾ indicates that there are paths that are not straight. What is the straight path?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, the ways of disbelief. Allah says: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it. And do not follow [other] ways, for they will separate you from His way﴾ [al-An'ām 153]. So the ways (*subul*) that incline a person to the right and to the left are crooked. But the path of Allah, which is His way that leads to Him, is straight.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 69 (part 1 of 3):

Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast in truth (al-siddiqin), the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.﴾ [An-Nisa 69]. (مَن) here is conditional (shartiyyah), and the verb after it is in the jussive mood (majzum) because of it. The evidence of the jussive is the deletion of the yā'. The original form of (يُطع) is (يطيع).

If someone asks: Why was the yā' deleted?

We say: Because when the verb became jussive it became quiescent (sakin), and the yā' is quiescent too. The rule is that when two quiescent letters meet, if the first is a sound consonant it is given a kasra, and if it is a weak letter (harf 'illah) it is deleted. Ibn Malik says about this:

* Student: If two quiescent letters meet, vowel the one before them with kasra, and if it is a soft letter, then its deletion is required.

* The Shaykh: Correct. ("If two quiescent letters meet, vowel the one before them with kasra, and if it is a soft letter") means a weak letter, ("then its deletion is required") means delete it.

Here we say: the yā' was deleted because it is a soft letter (harf layn) and is followed by a quiescent letter, so its deletion was obligatory.

If someone says: What follows it is not quiescent, rather it is vowelled with kasra: ﴿وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ﴾?

The answer: This kasra is incidental, due to the meeting of the two quiescent letters.

Where is the answer, the answer of (مَن)? It is the clause ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.

Here we ask: Why is the fā' attached in the answer?

* Student: This fā' is a substitute for the verb.

* The Shaykh: It is a connector linking the answer. So why is the answer of the conditional attached with fā'?

* Student: Because it was not the answer..

* The Shaykh: No, the answer.

* Student: The answer of the conditional.

* Student: Because the answer of the conditional is a nominal clause.

* The Shaykh: Because the answer of the conditional is a nominal clause, and when it is a nominal clause it must be attached with fā'.

* Student:
A nominal clause, and a clause of request, and with the rigid (word), and with mā, lan, qad, and with the future particle (sa/sawfa).

* The Shaykh: There are seven positions where, when they occur as the answer of the conditional, they are attached with fā'.

As for His words ﴿مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ﴾, there are two readings: ﴿مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ﴾ with yā', and ﴿مِنَ النَّبِيئِينَ﴾ with hamza.

And (مِن) here is explanatory (bayaniyyah). So what is the ambiguous thing that (مِن) clarifies?

* Student: ﴿الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.

* The Shaykh: It is a relative pronoun (ism mawsul). The relative pronoun is ambiguous and needs clarification, and its relative clause does not clarify it.

﴿وَحَسُنَ أُولَئِكَ رَفِيقًا﴾. ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ refers to what?

* Student: ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ refers to.

* The Shaykh: That is, what is the thing pointed to?

* Student: Those pointed to: the steadfast in truth, the martyrs, and the righteous.

* The Shaykh: Only? And the prophets are excluded?!

Why did He say ﴿رَفِيقًا﴾ when the thing pointed to is plural?

* Student: A specification (tamyiz).

* The Shaykh: ﴿رَفِيقًا﴾ is a specification? A specification must be singular. Is it now a singular rafiq whose plural is rufaqa'?

* Student: Because it is on the pattern (fa'il/fa'il-type, fa'īl).

* The Shaykh: And when it is on the pattern fa'īl?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: That is, if we say qatīl, it means qatlā (the slain)?

* Student: The wording is singular, but He means by it the plural: the companions (rufaqā').

* The Shaykh: Yes. The scholars say: rafīq is singular and suitable for both the singular and the plural, meaning it is suitable for this and that. So you say: "These (one) is a companion of this group," or "companions of this group," like (جُنُب, junub) for example: the word junub is singular in form but suitable for the plural. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if you are in a state of major impurity (junuban), then purify yourselves﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 6]. Likewise al-fulk (the ship) is singular but suitable for the plural. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿until when you are in ships (al-fulk) and they sail with them﴾ [Yunus 22], and He says: ﴿Do you not see that the ships (al-fulk) sail in the sea by the favor of Allah﴾ [Luqman 31]. Examples of this are many.

I like a statement said by Ibn 'Aqil, may Allah have mercy on him, and he was one of the jurists. He said: The hunchback whose hump is like one bowing, intending bowing, is like the fulk in Arabic: it is suitable for the singular and the plural. Likewise the bending of the hunchbacked man may be natural or may be a legal bowing (ruku').

This brings us to the story of al-Kisa'i with Abu Yusuf. Al-Kisa'i used to say: When a person masters a field of knowledge with strong, excellent mastery, he understands whatever else of the sciences even if he has not studied them. He said this, and it was in the presence of al-Rashid. Abu Yusuf said to him, and Abu Yusuf was a jurist: "What do you say about a man who forgets in the prostration of forgetfulness (sujud al-sahw)?" Al-Kisa'i said: "I say: that one does not perform the prostration of forgetfulness." He said: "Do you have anything from your grammar that indicates this?" He said: "Yes, I have that the diminutive does not get diminutized."

I do not know whether this is fabricated or true. In any case, when a person connects the sciences with one another, he benefits, and he has the ability to compose, the composition of thought. For this reason you find Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, linking things that you think are distant from one another, though they are close, gathered by a single root.

Let us return to the meaning of the verse. Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ﴾ [An-Nisa 69]. Obedience (al-ta'ah) is: conforming to the command by abandoning what is forbidden and doing what is commanded. For this reason we say: whoever abandons disobedience is considered obedient, and whoever performs an obligation is obedient. So it was said about obedience: it is conformity to the command or conformity to the one obeyed.

And His words ﴿وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ﴾ and He did not say "then the Messenger" (ثم الرسول), because the command of the Messenger is part of Allah's legislation. As you know, the Prophet (ﷺ) in legislation may be joined with Allah by the conjunction "and" (wa), because what he brought is from Allah's legislation. Unlike universal (kawniyyah) matters, where it is not permissible to join with Allah except with "then" (thumma).

From this—i.e., from the branches of this rule—is the saying: "Allah and His Messenger know best" in legislative matters.

And from this is His saying: ﴿And if they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them﴾ [At-Tawbah 59], and He did not say "then His Messenger," because this is giving by legislation, so it belongs to the Law. As for destined (qadariyyah) matters, the Prophet (ﷺ) owns nothing in them. For this reason, when a man said to him: "Whatever Allah wills and you will," he said: «Have you made me an equal (nidd) to Allah?»[[Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (1839), and al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad (783), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas with the wording: "You have made me an equal to Allah."]].

And His words ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ﴾ [An-Nisa 69]: (أولئك) is a demonstrative for a plural, although the one before it is singular. But they said: (مَن) and (مَا) and similar words are suitable for both the singular and the plural. So by their wording they are singular, and by their meaning they are plural, so it is valid for the pronoun or the demonstrative to refer to them either by wording or by meaning.

Allah the Exalted has combined both in His saying: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah has certainly perfected for him provision﴾ [At-Talaq 11]. He observed the wording in the first, the meaning in the second, and the wording again in the third.

And His words ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ﴾: He used the demonstrative to indicate the high rank of those people, and did not say (فهؤلاء), to alert to the elevation of their rank.

And His words ﴿مَعَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, meaning the blessing of religion and worldly life, which is the specific blessing. Know that Allah's blessing, glory be to Him, is divided into two kinds: general blessing and specific blessing.

The general blessing is for the believer and the disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked, the upright and the corrupt. This is the general kind, and among it is the provision flowing to people: rain, plants, prosperity, and security. These are among the general blessings.

The second: the specific blessing, which is blessing in religion and in worldly life. This is specific to whom? To the believers. They are four categories, as Allah the Exalted said here: ﴿Allah has bestowed favor upon them: of the prophets, the steadfast in truth, the martyrs, and the righteous﴾. The prophets here include the messengers, because every messenger is a prophet. So when it says ﴿of the prophets﴾, the messengers are included by priority, and there is no doubt about this.

As for ﴿النَّبِيِّينَ﴾, it was said: they are those to whom a law was revealed but who were not commanded to convey it. The messenger is one to whom a law was revealed and who was commanded to convey it. This is the well-known view among the scholars.

It was said: the prophet is one to whom it was revealed that he worship according to the law of one before him, or who brings what completes it, so there must have been a messenger before him. But the correct view is that of the majority: that the prophet receives revelation of a law, but is not obligated or required to convey it.

Among these—i.e., among the prophets who were not sent—is Adam. Adam was a prophet who was spoken to, but he was not a messenger, because he was the first of mankind, so there was no nation for him to be a messenger to. Also, the people who came from him and Eve were few, and worldly life had not tempted them. They would look to their father and worship as he worshipped. When people spread and multiplied, Allah sent the messengers.

For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Mankind was one nation; then Allah sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners﴾ [Al-Baqarah 213]. This indicates that before this, no prophets were sent to them as bearers of good news and warners; rather they were prophets who worshipped Allah, and a community followed them. The word is derived from al-naba', which is news. It was also said it is from al-nubuwwah, which is elevation. As for the first, it is clear, because the prophet both informs and is informed. On this view, the word ﴿النَّبِيِّينَ﴾ with hamza (النبيئين) is a form (fa'il) in the sense of passive and active: he is one informed (munabba') and one who informs (munbi'). As for the reading with yā', it may be from naba', with the hamza dropped for lightness, or from nubuwwah, which is elevation, because of the high station of the prophets. There is no doubt that the prophets are the highest rank of Allah's righteous servants.

﴿الصِّدِّيقِينَ﴾.

* Student: May Allah be pleased with you. It has come from the Messenger (ﷺ) that on the Day of Resurrection the messengers will be terrified, held back from the Throne. In tonight's lesson the resurrection (...) that Allah the Exalted says to Adam (...).

* The Shaykh: There is no disagreement about this. I say there is no disagreement, so it does not need explanation.

* Student: Because they will be frightened in front of the messengers.

* * *

* Student: For example, a sick person says: what did he bring here? The matter is the reverse.

* The Shaykh: No, this differs. A sick person may say: "What did they bring me?" This may be a spy or not. He may not say this; he may be happy when visited, like this man, and perhaps become energized. Visiting is for those you know and those you do not know. It is not chivalrous, especially when you enter a room with people you know and people you do not know, to ask about these and not ask about the condition of the others.

* Student: May Allah be pleased with you. Is it derived from his (ﷺ) saying that a person should seek out (...)?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. From it is derived that if a person knows that this individual is harming himself, and he visits him in order to rescue him from the Fire, this is good.

* Student: May Allah bless you. Our brother, may Allah bless him, attributed the hadith «Convey from me, even if it is one verse»[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (3461), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr.]] to al-Bukhari. What is the authenticity of the hadith?

* The Shaykh: This is authentic: «Convey from me, even if it is one verse, and narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no blame».

* Student: «And narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no blame»[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (3662), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]].

* The Shaykh: Yes, all of it is authentic. But narrating does not mean affirming, because the Messenger commanded us to withhold judgment about what they narrate, unless our law testifies to it. For this reason the scholars said: reports of the Children of Israel are divided into three categories: a category our law testifies to be true, a category our law testifies to be false, and a category about which our law says nothing. The third is to be withheld from.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast in truth, the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions (69). That is the bounty from Allah, and sufficient is Allah as Knower (70). O you who have believed, take your precaution and go forth in small groups or go forth all together (71). And indeed, among you is one who will lag behind. If disaster strikes you, he says, "Allah has certainly blessed me, for I was not present with them as a witness" (72). But if bounty comes to you from Allah, he will say, as if there had been no affection between you and him, "Oh, I wish I had been with them so I could have achieved a great achievement" (73)﴾ [An-Nisa 69–73].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast in truth, the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.﴾ The beginning of this verse has already been discussed, and I think we have taken its benefits.

His words ﴿وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ﴾: is the (ال) in (الرسول) for generic reference (al-haqiqah) or for a known referent (al-'ahd)?

* Student: For a known referent.

* The Shaykh: For a known referent. If it is for a known referent, who is meant?

* Student: (...) (ﷺ).

The Shaykh: Which of the messengers? What is meant is Muhammad (ﷺ). Is there another possibility?

* Student: The possibility that what is meant is all the messengers.

* The Shaykh: That is, the genus (al-jins); what is meant is the category, meaning ﴿وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ﴾ whom He sent, whether it is Muhammad or others. This is the closest form of generality.

His words ﴿مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ﴾: is (مِن) here explanatory? Where is the ambiguous thing it clarifies? It is ﴿مَعَ الَّذِينَ﴾.

Allah says: ﴿مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ وَالصِّدِّيقِينَ﴾. The messengers are included among the prophets here, because every messenger is a prophet, but not every prophet is a messenger. So His words ﴿مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ﴾ include the messengers, and they are superior to the prophets. This is agreed upon among the scholars of the Muslims. As for the extremist Sufis, they said: the friend of Allah (wali) is superior to the prophet, and the prophet is superior to the messenger. They said: because the friend has guardianship and nearness, the prophet has reporting with distance, and the messenger is a servant. They recited in support of this:

The station of prophethood is in an isthmus, above the messenger and below the friend.

Look at this bad expression: "the station of prophethood is in an isthmus, above the messenger and below the friend." So the friend is far above them and far from them. Then, with distance, who comes after the friend? After the friend comes the prophet, then the messenger, and according to their claim there is little difference between the prophet and the messenger.

There is no doubt that this is manifest error, and we seek refuge in Allah. Because we say: every messenger is a prophet, and every prophet is a friend of Allah. The most noble of Allah's friends are the messengers and prophets. Without doubt, the most noble of the friends are the prophets, and the most noble of the prophets are the messengers. So their statement is false.

Then, whom do they mean by the friends?

They mean by "friends" the heads of the tyrants (tawaghit), their friends, who are the friends of Satan, whom they want to be worshipped and to be made infallible from every sin and every error.

As for the steadfast in truth (al-siddiqun): the siddiq is one who affirmed the truth and spoke the truth. Allah's saying clarifies it: ﴿And he who brought the truth and affirmed it—those are the righteous (al-muttaqun)﴾ [Az-Zumar 33]. So the siddiq is one who spoke the truth and affirmed the truth. The best of the steadfast in truth is Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, because this Ummah is the best of nations, and Abu Bakr is the best of this Ummah, so the best of the steadfast in truth is Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him.

﴿And the martyrs﴾. The word "shuhada'" is the plural of "shahid" (martyr, witness). The scholars differed about who is meant. It was said that the martyrs here are the people of knowledge, based on the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and so do the angels and those of knowledge, maintaining justice. There is no deity except Him, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ [Ali 'Imran 18]. It was also said that the martyrs are those who were killed in the cause of Allah, based on the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿And never think of those who were killed in the cause of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ [Ali 'Imran 169].

The correct view is that the verse is general, because the scholars are martyrs whom Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has called to witness over the creation. They bear witness to the truth and they bear witness over the creation. Who is most knowledgeable of the truthfulness of the messengers and of the law of the messengers? The scholars. So they bear witness to the truth that the messengers brought, and they bear witness over the people that the messengers delivered it.

Then we also say: this Ummah is a witness over mankind in general, based on the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced nation that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Baqarah 143]. The meaning of that is that this Ummah bears witness that the messengers came to their peoples with clear proofs, and that among those peoples some disbelieved and some believed, because there is no messenger after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and all the messengers have passed, and Allah has related to us some of their news.

As for the saying: ﴿and the righteous﴾, these are of a lower rank than those before them. Yet whoever was before them is without doubt among the righteous, so this is the case of coordinating the general with the specific. Not every righteous person is a truthful one (siddiq), not every righteous person is a martyr, and not every righteous person is a prophet or messenger. But every prophet, every siddiq and every martyr is righteous. Allah, the Exalted, said about Ibrahim: ﴿And We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed he is in the Hereafter among the righteous﴾ [al-Nahl 122].

So righteousness is a general description, and its being conjoined to what came before is by way of conjoining the general to the specific. But who is the righteous person?

The righteous (al-salih) is the opposite of the corrupt (al-fasid).
