So he is the one obedient to Allah, because the corrupt is the one who disobeys Allah, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation﴾ [al-A'raf 56]. The scholars said: meaning, do not cause corruption in it by sins, for sins are a cause of corruption on the earth.

The evidence for that is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if the people of the cities had believed and feared Allah, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth, but they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn﴾ [al-A'raf 96].

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea by what the hands of people have earned﴾ [al-Rum 41].

Based on this, the righteous person is the one who obeys Allah. Some have expressed this by saying: the righteous is the one who fulfils the right of Allah and the rights of the servants. This comes to the same meaning as the first, because the one who obeys Allah must necessarily be one who fulfils the right of Allah and the rights of the servants.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿and excellent are those as companions﴾. "Hasuna" (excellent) is a past-tense verb but it carries the sense of wonder (ta'ajjub), so it means: how excellent these companions are. The phrase ﴿those﴾ refers to these four categories. As for "rafiqan" (as companions), it was said that it means "companions" (plural), and that it is a noun used for both singular and plural. It was also said that "rafiqan" is a specification (tamyiz) for "hasuna", since it carries the sense of wonder, but the first view is more correct. That is, excellent are these as companions. The word "rafiq" applies to both the singular and the plural. The "rafiq" and the "mirfaq" is the one by whom you find comfort, companionship, help, ease and the like. For this reason, "rafiq" is said only of one who accompanies you and travels with you, whether in work, in travel, or in something else.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿That is the bounty from Allah﴾.

* Student: Shaykh, does the context not specify that the Messenger is Muhammad (ﷺ)?
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: How so?
* Student: From the beginning of the verses: ﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾ [al-Nisa' 59]. (...) identifies that the Messenger is Muhammad (ﷺ), then Allah, mighty and majestic, concluded it: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour of the prophets﴾.
* Shaykh: There is no doubt that the context of the verses before it is all about the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, but there is no objection to a general verse coming so that the Messenger is included implicitly. The Messenger Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, is included implicitly.
* Student: In His saying, the Exalted: ﴿then those are with those who﴾ and His saying: ﴿and the righteous﴾, that everyone who obeys Allah and His Messenger is among the righteous. So shall we say that "ma'a" (with) here means "min" (from)?
* Shaykh: No, because those other than these four categories are the hypocrites and the disbelievers.
* Student: With them.
* Shaykh: With them. For this reason a person may be gathered with the disbelievers even if there is some obedience in him, as a rebuke to him. And he may be gathered with the believers even if there is some disobedience in him, when Allah pardons him.
* Student: Will students of knowledge be gathered with the martyrs?
* Shaykh: Yes, on their path toward becoming martyrs.
* Student: If they die upon that?
* Shaykh: If they die upon that. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever leaves his home emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has become due from Allah﴾ [al-Nisa' 100]. His reward is completed for what he intended.
* Student: Shaykh, are the righteous (al-salihin) higher, or the reformers (al-muslihun)?
* Shaykh: Yes. Every reformer is righteous, and the righteous person in whom there is no reforming has a deficiency in his righteousness, because reforming is part of the perfection of righteousness. For this reason He said: ﴿And those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer﴾ and did not mention that they enjoin what is right. He said: ﴿And those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer – indeed, We do not waste the reward of the reformers﴾ [al-A'raf 170].
* Student: Are the reformers greater than the righteous, Shaykh?
* Shaykh: The reformer – yes, reforming is part of the perfection of righteousness. A person may be righteous yet not concerned with the righteousness of others, so he is not a reformer, and in that case we say: he is righteous but deficient in righteousness.
* Student: Shaykh, why did He not say "the reformers" in the verse?
* Shaykh: We do not say; Allah said it this way.
* Student: You mean this ordering, Shaykh?
* Shaykh: I say: Allah said it this way; we cannot change the Qur'an.
* Student: No, I mean, Shaykh, is this ordering based on preference?
* Shaykh: Based on preference.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, it is a report intended to encourage. That is, do you wish to be with these and in their company? The answer: yes. Then obey Allah and His messengers.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: That is, you say: if one obeys Allah and His Messenger, he does not go outside these categories, so you say? Fine, he is with them. I may say, for example: this man is with the believers and he is a believer.
* Student: Some people apply the word "martyrdom" to those killed in a battle, or in defending a specific cause, or by torture. Is this correct?
* Shaykh: As for the one who is killed in battle while fighting so that the word of Allah is supreme, this is a martyr without doubt. As for the one who fights for a specific cause and not so that the word of Allah is supreme, he is not in the cause of Allah and is not a martyr, and it is not permissible to call him a martyr. Indeed, even the one killed in battle is not to be called a martyr, as al-Bukhari included in his chapter heading, may Allah have mercy on him, saying: "Chapter: One should not say: so-and-so is a martyr." And as 'Umar forbade that, he said: "You say: so-and-so is a martyr and so-and-so is a martyr, but how do you know – meaning – perhaps he misappropriated (from the spoils). Rather, say: whoever dies or is killed in the cause of Allah, he is a martyr."[[Recorded by al-Nasa'i (3349) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]]
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: We mentioned this. We said: this Ummah is also a witness over the previous nations, and likewise the Ummah bears witness of some of its members over others. For this reason the preponderant view is that whoever the Ummah testifies for and agrees in praising, he is to be testified for as being among the people of Paradise.
* Student: The suicide operations now that (...) in some countries – do we say of the one killed in them: a martyr?
* Shaykh: Did he not kill himself?
* Student: But is it not derived from the hadith that the man with the date who entered the battle and fought until he was killed...
* Shaykh: No, that one did not kill himself. The one who threw away the dates and fought did not kill himself, because he was defending and wanted to kill the enemies. But this one entered as a suicide bomber, an entry of self-destruction.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: It is never permissible. This one killed himself. It is not permissible except in one specific situation, which Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned: when there is a great benefit for Islam in it. He cited the story of the boy with the king, whom the king wanted to kill; he kept sending him once to the mountains to be thrown down from them, and once to the sea to drown in it, but he returned safe. So he said to the king: "If you want to kill me, gather the people, take an arrow from my quiver, shoot me with it and say: In the name of the Lord of this boy; for you will kill me." The king did so, gathered the people, took an arrow from his quiver, shot him with it and said: "In the name of the Lord of this boy," and it reached him and killed him.[[Recorded by Muslim (3005) from the hadith of Suhayb.]] What happened? All those people began to say: "The Lord is the Lord of the boy," not you. So this is a great benefit, and it may be said: there is no harm in a person sacrificing himself for it.

* * *

* Student: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour of the prophets and the truthful and the martyrs and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions (69). That is the bounty from Allah, and sufficient is Allah as Knower (70). O you who have believed, take your precaution and go forth in small groups or go forth all together﴾ [al-Nisa' 69–71].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour of the prophets and the truthful and the martyrs and the righteous﴾. Allah mentioned three benefits for the one who does what he is admonished to do. What are they?
* Student: That he gains the safety of this world and the Hereafter (...), the great reward, guidance.
* Shaykh: Good. Can it be derived from the verse that whoever does what he is admonished to do increases in knowledge?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: From where?
* Student: From His saying: ﴿And if they had done that, We would have given them from Us a great reward﴾ [al-Nisa' 67–68].
* Shaykh: A reward, yes. ﴿And We would have guided them to a straight path﴾. There are two views; which is it?
* Students: The second.
* Shaykh: The second, yes. What is derived from the attribution in His saying: ﴿from Us﴾?
* Student: Abundance and magnificence.
* Shaykh: Abundance and magnificence. Its basis?
* Student: That Allah, mighty and majestic, attributed the reward and the recompense to Himself, the Glorified and Exalted, and did not specify its amount in this verse, so that it is a great reward.
* Shaykh: But what is its basis?
* Student: That Allah, mighty and majestic, attributed it to Himself and did not attribute it to the Messenger of Allah, because the Mighty One, when He attributes a matter to Himself, the matter becomes great, because the attributed...
Shaykh: That is, the gift of the Generous is abundant and the Great One's gift is great. Is there a parallel to this in the Sunnah? A supplication the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, taught to some of his companions?
* Student: The supplication that the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, taught Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him; he says at the end of his prayer: "So forgive me a forgiveness from You."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (834) and Muslim (2705/48).]]
Shaykh: In his prayer – not at its end: "So forgive me a forgiveness from You." Correct.
His saying: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger﴾ – who is meant by the Messenger here: is it the general or a known messenger?
* Student: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family.
* Shaykh: That is, a known messenger – the Messenger meaning Muhammad? Or is the Messenger meant as a category, including all the messengers?
* Student: It includes all the messengers.
* Shaykh: You.
* Student: The context indicates that it is specific to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him and his family.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Shaykh, if we say it is general, it would be better.
* Shaykh: Because if we say it is general, the context is not corrupted by it.
Where is the mention of the messengers? The verse only has ﴿of the prophets﴾?
* Student: Because every messenger is a prophet, and not every prophet is a messenger.
* Shaykh: So "the prophets" includes them.
* Student: It includes the prophets and the messengers.
* Shaykh: Correct.
The governing rule in the definition of the siddiq?
* Student: The siddiq is one who is truthful in his speech and affirms what is said to him; the truthful one and the one who is affirmed, who affirms others and is truthful in his speech.
* Shaykh: Truthful in his speech.
* Student: And one who affirms others.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: He is the one who believed in the truth and spoke by it.
* Shaykh: Yes. Is there a verse in the Qur'an that indicates this?
* Student: ﴿And the one who came with the truth and affirmed it – those are the righteous﴾ [al-Zumar 33].
* Shaykh: The "ma'iyyah" (being with) here in His saying: ﴿with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour﴾ – is it in this world or the Hereafter?
* Student: In the Hereafter; they are gathered in their company.
* Shaykh: And in this world?
* Student: It is not necessary that he be with them in this world.
* Shaykh: So you are not with the Messenger?
* Student: Essentially not, specifically not.
* Shaykh: Not even 'Umar and Abu Bakr specifically?
* Student: With them in this world and the Hereafter; it covers both matters, Shaykh, because obedience to the Messenger, peace be upon him, is in the company of the Messenger, peace be upon him, in life; because if one follows the Sunnah of the Messenger, peace be upon him, it enjoins obedience to him.
* Shaykh: That is, the being-with in the Hereafter is clear: he is gathered with him. In this world, because whoever adopts the path of a person is in reality with him. For this reason, the word "Al" is applied to whom? To the followers. They are called the "Al" of a person, and they are followers who may not have any kinship with him.
* Shaykh: Have we taken the benefits now?
* Students: No.
* Shaykh: From where?
* Students: ﴿And whoever obeys﴾.
* Shaykh: Good, in the name of Allah.
* Among the benefits of the verse: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger﴾. The exhortation to obey Allah and His Messenger. Its basis is the mention of the reward, because mentioning the reward for doing a thing means encouraging it and urging it.
* Among its benefits: that obedience to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, is obedience to Allah. Its basis: whoever obeys the Messenger deserves praise as one who obeyed Allah.
* Among its benefits: the permissibility of joining the Messenger with the Lord, mighty and majestic, by the conjunction "wa" (and) in obedience, and likewise in disobedience, because the command of the Messenger is the command of Allah, by His saying: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger﴾. For this reason we say: in matters relating to the law, there is no harm in a person joining the Messenger with the Lord, mighty and majestic, with "wa", because the law of the Messenger is the law of Allah. Look at this verse: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger﴾, ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Nisa' 14], ﴿And if only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them﴾ [al-Tawbah 59]. This is legislative giving. As for matters of creation, no one shares Allah, the Exalted, in His lordship, so it must be mentioned with a particle of coordination indicating sequence. For this reason, when a man said to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him and his family: "What Allah wills and you will," he said: "Have you made me an equal to Allah? Say: what Allah alone wills."[[Recorded by Ahmad in al-Musnad (1839) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, with the wording "Have you made me an equal (adl) to Allah?"]]
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour are four categories: the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs and the righteous. This verse explains the verse of al-Fatihah: ﴿the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour﴾ [al-Fatihah 7]. So those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour are these four categories.

The most excellent of the people of the Prophet's (ﷺ) time...

Let me correct that. Here is the full translation:

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Prophet is more excellent than the *siddiq* (the truthful one, a title for the most sincere believers), the *siddiq* is more excellent than the *shahid* (the martyr), and the *shahid* is more excellent than the *salih* (the righteous). This is because the order here is from the highest to the lowest.

* Among the benefits of this verse: it refutes what the philosophers among the Sufis and others have claimed, that the *wali* (the saint, one who is close to God) is more excellent than the Prophet, and the Prophet is more excellent than the Messenger. We have explained this issue and shown that every prophet is a *wali*, and every messenger is a prophet. Accordingly, the messenger is a prophet and a *wali*, but not every *wali* is a prophet or a messenger.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the praise of these four categories, may God make us and you among them, when the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And excellent are those as companions﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: companions differ. Some are companions of good and some are companions of evil. This is shown by His saying here: ﴿And excellent are those as companions﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) also warned against bad companions and said: "The likeness of a bad companion and a good companion is like the bearer of musk and the blower of the bellows (*kir*): either he will burn your clothes, or you will find from him a foul smell."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2101) and Muslim (2628 / 146), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]] Do you know what the *kir* is?

* Student: The blacksmith blows into it.

* Shaykh: Into the mouth?

* Student: The blacksmith uses it on iron.

* Shaykh: Correct, the blacksmith uses it. But what is it like, and what is it made of?

* Student: This *kir* is made of leather.

* Shaykh: Leather.

* Student: It is made of animal hide, and it is closed except for an opening or a hole through which the air comes out. There is another hole from which it takes in air. When the worker presses it like this, it takes in the air and pushes it forward, where the fire is. This *kir* blows the fire until it melts the iron. This is the old *kir*. As for the modern one, I have no knowledge of it.

* Shaykh: The old one, as he mentioned, is leather. Its end that enters the fire is narrow, and its top is wide. At its top are two pieces of wood that open. When one pulls it open, it fills with air. Then one closes it like this and presses on it. When it is pressed and full of air, where does the air go?

* Students: To the fire.

* Shaykh: It goes to the fire, and you find the fire blazing intensely.

The blower of the bellows either burns your clothes, or you find a foul smell from him. In contrast, the good companion is like the bearer of musk: either he sells you some, or he gives you some for free, or you find a pleasant smell from him.

That is the bounty from Allah, and Allah suffices as Knower. (Qur'an 4:70)

"That" refers to what has already been mentioned of Allah's favour upon these four categories, whom Allah has favoured with blessings in this world and the Hereafter. The blessing upon these four categories is a continuous blessing from this world to the next, unlike Allah's bestowal upon others among the wretched servants of Allah, for which is a blessing in this world but a loss in the Hereafter.

So "that" refers to what Allah has bestowed upon these categories. "The bounty from Allah" (al-fadl min Allah): al-fadl (bounty) may be a description (sifah) or an explanatory apposition (ʿatf bayan) to dha (that), and it may be the predicate of the subject. Had a separating pronoun (damir al-fasl) been present, it would have been certain that it is the predicate of the subject. Now, there are two possibilities for its grammatical analysis (iʿrab). The first possibility is that "dhalika al-fadl" is one unit, meaning the description and the described, and "min Allah" is a prepositional phrase serving as the predicate of the subject. It is also permissible that dha is the subject (mubtada') and al-fadl its predicate, with "min Allah" in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal) in the accusative.

"That is the bounty from Allah" means not from anyone else. They did not acquire the high rank they attained by themselves, but by the bounty of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "O Allah, do not leave me to myself, nor to anyone other than You, even for the blink of an eye" [Abu Dawud (5090), from the hadith of Abu Bakrah]. A person does not acquire virtues by himself; if he were left to himself he would be humiliated, degraded and deprived, but the bounty is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

"And Allah suffices as Knower": this is a form expressing wonder (taʿajjub). It has been said regarding its grammatical analysis that kafa is a past-tense verb, the bi is an extra (zaʾid) preposition, and the word Allah is the subject, meaning: "And Allah suffices as a witness." On this basis, ʿalIman is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause, meaning "while He is Knower." The connection of this sentence with what precedes it is to make clear that Allah, glorified and exalted, has bestowed the bounty upon these people only with knowledge; it is not arbitrary. Rather, Allah knows best where to place His message, knows best where to place righteousness, knows best where to place knowledge, and knows best where to place guidance. He, glorified and exalted, knows the place that is worthy of this bounty, so He bestows it upon it, and knows who is not worthy, so He deprives him. This is the connection of this sentence with what precedes it.

It is derived from this noble verse:

First: the explanation of Allah's blessing upon these categories, from His saying "That is the bounty from Allah," and its basis is that Allah has favoured them.

Second: that whatever bounty a person obtains is only from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not by his own power and strength. For this reason Allah destroyed those who said: "I was given this only because of knowledge I possess" [al-Qasas 78], since the bounty is in the hand of Allah.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the encouragement for a person to turn to his Lord in asking for what he seeks. Its basis is that if the bounty is from Allah, then do not ask for bounty except from the One in whose hand is bounty.

Another benefit of the noble verse: the demonstration of the vastness of the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from His saying "And Allah suffices as Knower."

Also among its benefits: the entrusting of the matter to Allah, and that when Allah favours one person over another, know that this is with knowledge, not in vain. For this reason, when the deniers said: "We will never believe until we are given the like of what was given to the messengers of Allah" [al-An'am 124], Allah refuted them, saying to them: "Allah knows best where to place His message" [al-An'am 124], and you are not worthy of the message.

Among the benefits of this verse, a benefit that is somewhat remote: the demonstration that the Arab people are, by the knowledge of Allah, the most excellent of the children of Adam. Its basis is that Muhammad ﷺ was the most noble of the servants of Allah, meaning the most noble of mankind, and he was from the Arabs. This indicates that the Arab race is superior to the non-Arab race among the children of Adam. This is an observable matter, and their morals and manners, and the great virtue they gained through supporting this religion, attest to it. Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in his book Iqtida' al-Sirat al-Mustaqim several aspects demonstrating that the Arab race is superior to the other race of humanity.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 71:

Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O you who have believed, take your precaution﴾ [An-Nisa 71]. The address here is directed to the believers. When Allah, glorified and exalted, begins an address with the particle of calling (yā', "O"), this indicates that the matter is of importance and deserves to alert the one addressed, so he is called out to so that he pays attention.

Furthermore, this address is directed to the believers to show that carrying out what it contains is a requirement of faith, and that opposing it is among the deficiencies of faith, and may even be among the nullifiers of faith depending on what one is commanded to do. Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, as is transmitted from him and well known: "When you hear Allah say: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, then lend it your hearing—meaning, listen to it carefully—for it is either good that you are commanded to do, or evil that you are forbidden from."[[Narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Tafsir (50), and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (1886), from the narration of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]] He, may Allah have mercy on him, spoke the truth. It is either good that we are commanded to do, or evil that we are forbidden from, or news that we are warned against, such as His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis and monks consume the wealth of people unjustly and avert [people] from the way of Allah﴾ [At-Tawbah 34]. This contains no command and no prohibition, but it contains a warning against the way of those rabbis and monks who turn away from the way of Allah and consume people's wealth.

And His saying: ﴿take your precaution﴾ [An-Nisa 71]. What is meant by "hizr" (precaution)? It means fear of whom?

* Students: Of our enemies.

* The Shaykh: Originally it refers to our enemies, the disbelievers, and the believer has no enemy except the disbeliever: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers and Jibril and Mika'il—then indeed, Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Baqarah 98], and ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ [Al-Mumtahanah 1]. So there is in truth no enemy of the believer except the disbeliever, and disbelievers are of degrees. The disbeliever who openly declares disbelief is less harmful than the disbeliever who conceals his disbelief, and that is the hypocrite (munafiq). For this reason Allah said in Surah al-Munafiqun, which He revealed entirely concerning the hypocrites, saying: ﴿They are the enemy, so beware of them﴾ [Al-Munafiqun 4]. Many of you know that the phrase ﴿They are the enemy﴾ is a sentence that implies exclusivity because both its parts are definite: ﴿They are the enemy, so beware of them﴾, as if there is no enemy of the Muslims except the hypocrite, because his enmity—and we seek refuge in Allah—cannot be perceived, and it cannot be guarded against.

So then, take your precaution against your enemies: from the hypocrites, from the openly declared disbelievers, from the sinners who entice you to fall into sins short of disbelief, and from everyone who averts you from the religion of Allah. Take your precaution.

We take precaution against the invasion of these people against us, whether it is by weapons, or by thought, or by morals. It is well known now that the enemies of the Muslims invade the Muslims with every kind of weapon, and they look for the weapon suited to the nation and invade it with that. If it is suitable for the nation to be invaded by weapons, they act: they fight, and they attack. If that is not possible, they consider whether they can invade us through ideas; they bring deviant, atheistic ideas, and if that is possible they do it. If that is not possible, because the nation is at a high level of awareness, monotheism, and attachment to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, they say: then we invade by a third way, which is morals, and they unleash upon it everything that corrupts its morals, such as magazines, broadcasts, and other things.

For this reason, now look at what they have done to people through the satellite channels that are received by means of the dish antennas.

* A student: The satellites.

* The Shaykh: He says: through the satellites. The satellites transmit and the dish receives.

These things they broadcast, there is no doubt—as we have heard, and we have not watched, praise be to Allah—but as we have heard, there is great evil in them. They include beneficial things in them, because they know that if they were one hundred percent corrupting, people would not accept them except those whose hearts have swerved, and we seek refuge in Allah. But they put beneficial things in them in order to lay the bait of love.

So I say: this invasion now is an invasion of morals, and perhaps there is also an invasion of thought. Sometimes I listen to a clear, high-quality radio station, among the best of the world's stations that we hear, which broadcasts Christian missionary activity, calling to Christianity. But praise be to Allah, everything you call to that is good, we find that our Shari'ah includes it, and there is no need for this call of theirs, because the Islamic Shari'ah, praise be to Allah, has encompassed it and more than what they have.

So I say: the saying of the Exalted ﴿take your precaution﴾ encompasses everything that could be a weapon against us. And it is well known that for each weapon we take what suits it. Is that correct or not? That which suits the moral weapon is that the people be made to see and be shown the bad outcome of the ruin of morals, and that, as it has been said:

"Indeed nations are their morals, as long as they remain; if their morals have gone, they too have gone."

And to explain to them the harms of bad morals, of indecencies, and other than this. Regarding ideas, one explains to people the sound creed that connects them to Allah and makes a person always with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, remembering Allah with his heart, his tongue, and his limbs, standing, sitting, and lying on his side.

There remains the armed invasion by weapons; we must prepare the means, because Allah said: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾ [Al-Anfal 60].

So precaution varies. To some of these people we may say: learn the creed, learn beneficial knowledge, and spread it among the people. And to some of these people we may say: adorn yourselves with noble morals, avoid trivialities, and explain to the people the outcome of bad morals.

And to some people we may say: learn weapons: how they are made, how they are launched, how to receive the weapon that is directed at you, and so on. So the verse is absolute: ﴿precaution﴾, and precaution is according to what suits each thing.

﴿So go forth in separate groups or go forth all together﴾ [An-Nisa 71]. Someone may say: this indicates that the intended meaning of precaution here is precaution against weapons. But this is not necessary, because the attachment of a meaning to some individual instances of a general term does not necessitate restricting it. This is a useful rule: the attachment of a meaning to some individual instances of a general term does not necessitate restriction. For example, the statement of Jabir regarding pre-emption (shufa'a): "The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, decided pre-emption in everything that has not been divided. But when boundaries are set and roads are determined, there is no pre-emption."[[Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan (2497), from the narration of Abu Hurayrah.]] If we look at the beginning of the hadith: he decided pre-emption in everything not divided, we say: pre-emption is in everything not divided, all things. So if a car is sold between me and Zayd to 'Amr, Zayd has the right of pre-emption, because the car has not been divided, is that not so? In everything not divided. So if there is a car between me and Zayd and I sell my share to 'Amr, Zayd has the right to take that which I sold to 'Amr and add it to his share, and for this it is called shufa'a, because he joins his share to the share of his partner.

The statement "when boundaries are set and roads are determined" requires that what is meant by "what has not been divided" be land, because it is land in which boundaries are set and in which roads are determined. For this reason the scholars differed: is pre-emption in everything, even movables, or is it only in immovable property? The correct view is generality, because the attachment of a meaning to some individual instances of a general term does not necessitate restriction.

Another example: ﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three menstrual periods. And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs, if they believe in Allah and the Last Day. And their husbands have more right to take them back in that [period]﴾ [Al-Baqarah 228]. The noble verse indicates at its beginning that all divorced women, even irrevocably divorced ones, wait by themselves for three periods, meaning three menstrual cycles; a woman observes three menstrual cycles when she is divorced. But His saying ﴿and their husbands have more right to take them back﴾ requires that what is meant by "divorced women" be whom? Revocably divorced women, not irrevocably divorced ones. So do we say that the generality in His saying ﴿and divorced women﴾ is specified by His saying ﴿and their husbands﴾, and that what is meant by divorced women is the revocable ones? Or do we say: divorced women is general, and the attachment of a meaning to some individual instances of a general term does not necessitate restriction?

* Students: The second.

* The Shaykh: Yes, the second. For this reason the majority of scholars, indeed it has been reported as a consensus, hold that the waiting period of a divorced woman, even if she is irrevocably divorced, is how many? Three periods, even if she is irrevocably divorced. And since the principle of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, was that every woman separated whose husband does not hold the right of return has a waiting period of one menstrual cycle, he said: except the one divorced three times, and he conditioned the statement on that by the existence of a dissenter.

Are you following? You did not understand? Shaykh al-Islam had a principle: a woman who was separated and whose husband has no right of return over her observes a waiting period of one menstrual cycle, like the one who obtained khul', the one whose marriage was annulled, and so on. Is that clear or not? And the school (madhhab)?

* Students: Three.

* The Shaykh: It must be three menstrual cycles. The case of the one divorced three times was raised against him: the one divorced three times, whose husband has no right of return over her. So does she observe one cycle or three?

According to his principle, one. But he, may Allah have mercy on him, conditioned the statement on the existence of one who holds it, because a later person cannot oppose an earlier consensus, and it has been mentioned that some of the Successors (tabi'un) held this view. So I say, may Allah bless you: the principle we established is that when a general term is mentioned and then a meaning is attached to some of its individual instances, does that constitute specification of the general term or not?

* Students: No.

* The Shaykh: We say: it does not constitute it, and this is the correct view, that it does not. So then, ﴿So go forth in separate groups or go forth all together﴾, although the apparent context suggests that His saying ﴿take your precaution﴾ means against your enemies who oppose you with weapons, we say: mentioning the ruling of some individual instances of a general term does not necessitate restriction.

* A student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. Could we say, Shaykh: the first enemy of a person is Satan, because Satan comes to a person not openly but secretly. The second enemy is like the hypocrites and the enemies of Islam, the Jews and Christians, most of whom, if they came to us with weapons, we would confront them; if they came to us with all kinds of means, have we taken our precaution?

* The Shaykh: And the third? The third enemy? The first enemy: Satan; the second: the hypocrites and disbelievers; and the third?

* A student: The self (nafs).

* The Shaykh: You forgot the self! The self is more hostile, except what my Lord has mercy upon: ﴿Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon whom my Lord has mercy﴾ [Yusuf 53].

* A student: Shaykh, we mentioned, Shaykh, that the opinions on affirming and negating causes, in defining causes, are two extremes and a middle. How do those who negate causes respond to this verse?

* The Shaykh: Which one?

* The student: ﴿take your precaution﴾?

* The Shaykh: Yes. They say: yes, take precaution, but if you take precaution you do not benefit by your precaution; rather, benefit occurs at the time of precaution and not by the precaution. They say: causes are a sign of a thing, not a cause. For example, a person who is lazy tries the shower and becomes energetic, and indeed after the shower he is energetic. They say: he did not become energetic because of the shower; he became energetic at it, not by it. That is, Allah made for him energy at the shower, not by the shower. When you strike glass with a stone and the glass breaks, the stone did not break it, but it was decreed that it would break upon the stone's contact with it. This view is incorrect, without any doubt.

* * *
* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿O you who have believed, take your precaution, then go forth in separate groups or go forth all together (71). And indeed, among you is he who will be slow. So if a disaster strikes you, he says: "Allah has favored me, for I was not a witness with them." (72) And if bounty comes to you from Allah, he will surely say, as if there had never been between you and him any affection: "Oh, I wish I had been with them so I could have achieved a great achievement"﴾ [An-Nisa 71-73].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, take your precaution﴾, and the discussion of this phrase of the verse has already passed.

Then He said: ﴿So go forth in separate groups﴾: go forth, meaning to fight in the way of Allah, that is, set out.

And His saying ﴿separate groups﴾ means dispersed, and ﴿or go forth all together﴾ means gathered. What shows us that ﴿thubat﴾ means dispersed is His saying ﴿or go forth all together﴾, as it is set against it, and the opposite of a thing is in opposition to it in meaning. So the meaning of ﴿thubat﴾ is dispersed, and ﴿or go forth all together﴾.

* In this verse there are benefits. First: the virtue of faith, in that its people deserve that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, address them, as in His saying ﴿O you who have believed﴾.

* Second, among the benefits of the verse: the obligation to take precaution against our enemies, and every enemy from whom precaution is taken in what one fears from him. Those who invade us with weapons, we take precaution against them with weapons; those who invade us with ideas, we take precaution against them with knowledge; and those who invade us with morals, we take precaution against them by rising above trivial morals. Every enemy is met with his own weapon.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: it is fitting, indeed obligatory, for a person to be astute and perceptive. For this reason it came in the hadith from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: "The believer is astute and perceptive,"[[Musnad al-Shihab al-Qada'i (1/107), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]] and the Messenger explained the astute (kayyis) as "the one who holds himself accountable and works for what comes after death,"[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2459) and Ibn Majah (4260), from the hadith of Abu Ya'la Shaddad ibn Aws.]] meaning: decisive, perceptive, and possessing caution.

* If someone says: may we reach the degree of having bad opinions of others and say this is taking precaution?

* We say: it is not permissible to think ill of one whose outward condition is uprightness, as the scholars said: it is forbidden to think ill of a Muslim whose outward condition is uprightness. As for one whose outward condition is wickedness, we may take precaution against him, lest he deceive us.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation to go forth for jihad in the way of Allah, whether we are gathered or dispersed.

If someone says: how do we reconcile this with His saying ﴿And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once. Why should there not go forth from every division of them a group﴾ [At-Tawbah 122]?

We say: the answer is that these who go forth, go forth whether they are dispersed or in a group. Based on this, the command here applies to those who go forth, since they are commanded to go forth dispersed or gathered. As for those who remain to gain understanding in the religion of Allah, these will not go forth.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 72–73 (part 1 of 2):

Then He said: ﴿And indeed, among you is he who would lag behind. So if a disaster strikes you, he says, "Allah has certainly blessed me, for I was not present among them as a witness."﴾ [An-Nisa' 72]. In this verse there are two lams: the first lam in (la-man) and the second in (la-yubatti'anna). Are they the lam of the beginning (lam al-ibtida')?

The answer: As for the first, it is the lam of the beginning (lam al-ibtida'), because it falls on the delayed subject of (inna), and it conveys emphasis. As for the second lam, it is the lam that prepares for an oath (lam al-muwatta'ah lil-qasam). Thus His saying ﴿yubatti'anna﴾ falls in the answer of the oath, and the estimate is: "And indeed among you is he who, by Allah, will lag behind," so the lam here falls in the answer of the oath.

And His saying ﴿So if a disaster strikes you﴾ is a conditional clause. The condition in it and its answer are a past verb. Do we say that it is in the jussive mood (majzum), or do we say that it is built (mabni) in a position of jussiveness? The second, because the past verb is built. The verb of the condition is ﴿asabatkum﴾, and its answer is ﴿qala qad an'ama Allahu 'alayya﴾.

And His saying ﴿idh lam akun﴾: (idh) here is for causation (ta'lil) and is not a time adverb (zarf); rather it is for causation, meaning: "because I was not present with them as a witness."

As for the meaning of the verse: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says ﴿And indeed among you﴾, and (min) here is partitive (tab'id), meaning some of you ﴿is he who would lag behind (la-man la-yubatti'anna)﴾, meaning: the one who lags behind. The meaning of (yubatti') is that he calls to delay, whether he calls others or calls himself. So His saying ﴿la-yubatti'anna﴾ includes the one who discourages others from setting out for fighting, and the one who discourages himself and is negligent until the opportunity is lost. This one who lags behind is delayed and does not go out to fight. The outcome of fighting is either booty, victory and support, or the opposite. So if a disaster strikes you, meaning a defeat and humiliation befalls you, he says ﴿Allah has certainly blessed me, for I was not present among them as a witness﴾. His speech thus contains both boasting and contempt: boasting in himself that he did not witness this disaster, and contempt for those who were struck by it. This is the utmost of estrangement. He is one of them, yet he speaks these words as if there was no affection between him and them, as if he were the farthest of people from them, when he boasts that he escaped the disaster that befell them, and belittles those who were struck, becoming like a reproacher of them.

﴿And if a bounty from Allah comes to you, he will surely say﴾, ﴿"Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I would have achieved a great achievement"﴾ [An-Nisa' 73]. ﴿And if a bounty comes to you﴾, meaning victory and booty, he will surely say ﴿"Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I would have achieved a great achievement"﴾, so he wishes vainly upon Allah after the matter has escaped him.

As for His saying ﴿as if there had not been between you and him any affection﴾: ﴿as if there had not been﴾ contains an example for our reading in grammar two nights ago, and it is the light form of (ka'anna): ﴿ka'an lam takun﴾. And (ka'anna), when lightened, I think we read it and stopped at it? Good, then let us leave it until we reach it.

The clause ﴿lam takun baynakum wa baynahu mawaddah﴾ is in a position of nominative (raf') as the predicate of (ka'anna), and its subject is an omitted pronoun of the matter (damir al-sha'n).

And His saying ﴿ka'an lam takun baynakum wa baynahu mawaddah﴾: "mawaddah" is pure love, meaning as if he were distant from you, with no bond between you and him. This clause, most exegetes assert, returns to the first situation, namely: "if a disaster strikes you, he says, as if there had not been any affection between you, 'Allah has certainly blessed me.'" But this is not correct, and its explanation will come, God willing.

* * *

Among those present, a group combined Maghrib and 'Isha' because of rain (meaning, praise be to Allah, the rains are general), and they shortened, combined and shortened while they were in the town. Is this correct?

* Student: Combining is correct.

* Shaykh: Combining is correct, and shortening is not correct. It was said to them: this is not permissible, you must pray four. Then their imam conveyed to them on the next day and said: pray two rakahs, completing the two previous rakahs. So they prayed two rakahs, completing the two previous rakahs. Subhan Allah! Such overstepping by people in giving fatwas is something strange. So what is obligatory upon them now?

* Students: Repeating the prayer.

* Shaykh: That they pray 'Isha' four rakahs. The obligation now is that they pray 'Isha' four, yes. And this is an incident, not a ruling; it actually happened the night before last.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿And if a bounty from Allah comes to you, he will surely say, as if there had not been between you and him any affection, "Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I would have achieved a great achievement." (73) So let those fight in the way of Allah who sell the worldly life for the Hereafter. And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed or achieves victory – We will give him a great reward.﴾ [An-Nisa' 73–74].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, take your precaution and go forth in parties or go forth all together.﴾

* Shaykh: What does introducing the address with a call (nida') convey?

* Student: Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When Allah, glorified and exalted, begins with the call ﴿O you who have believed﴾, then lend it your hearing.

* Shaykh: But I say: what does introducing the address with a call convey, regardless of whether it is "those who have believed" or others?

* Student: It conveys attentiveness.

* Shaykh: It conveys attentiveness, yes, to the speech directed at the addressee. How do we say that it conveys attentiveness to this?

* Student: Because the address was directed by Allah, glorified and exalted.

* Shaykh: One cannot justify a ruling by the ruling itself. You cannot say: why was ghusl obligatory? You say: because ghusl was obligatory. Why was wudu' obligatory? Because wudu' was obligatory.

* Student: Because (...) that this is among the requirements of faith.

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: Because He began it with (ya) for address: O you.

* Shaykh: Yes, indeed, but why do we say that it indicates attentiveness and care toward the address, or toward what the address requires?

* Student: Because the call conveys alerting.

* Shaykh: Correct. The call undoubtedly conveys alerting: "O so-and-so." It is not like speech thrown out without a call. It conveys alerting, and alerting conveys attentiveness to the matter and its importance.

What does its being directed to the believers indicate?

* Student: It contains an incitement to the addressees to respond, when He addresses them with the description of faith and the virtue of faith.

* Shaykh: Good. Two: an excitement to acceptance through the virtue of faith, since He singled out the believers with the call. And the third?

* Student: It contains a warning against opposing, because if this command is among the requirements of faith, then leaving it is a deficiency in faith.

* Shaykh: The fourth?

* Student: It indicates that doing what is commanded is among the requirements of faith.

* Shaykh: Yes, that doing it is among the requirements of faith and that leaving it is a deficiency in faith. What is the meaning of His saying ﴿take your precaution﴾?

* Student: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, directs the believers to take their precaution against their enemy.

* Shaykh: What is the meaning of taking precaution?

* Student: Taking precaution means: the believers take their precaution, if the enemy intended is the enemies of Allah from the hypocrites.

* Shaykh: We do not want the manner of precaution, but what is the meaning of taking precaution at all?

* Student: Beware of him means be cautious of him.

* Shaykh: Good.

* Student: Taking precaution is by fearing him.

* Shaykh: Fearing him and preparing for him.

Regarding this verse, I think I mentioned to you: "The believer is astute and discerning." Did I mention it as a hadith or as a saying?

* Students: As a saying.

* Other students: As a hadith.

* Student: It is obligatory upon the believer to be astute and discerning.

* Shaykh: In any case, whoever understood from me that I said it is a hadith, it is not authentically from the Prophet ﷺ. Regarding this verse, I think I mentioned: "The believer is astute and discerning." Did I mention it as a hadith or as a saying?

* Students: As a saying.

* Shaykh: As a hadith?

* Students: As a saying.

* Shaykh: As a saying.

* Student: As a saying, meaning the believer should be astute and discerning.

* Shaykh: In any case, whoever understood from me that I said it is a hadith, it is not authentically from the Prophet ﷺ. It is mentioned in the explanation of al-Jami' al-Saghir: "The believer is astute, discerning, and cautious," and he said: there is a liar among its narrators, so the hadith is fabricated, but its meaning is correct.

* Student: That it is obligatory upon a person, O Shaykh.

* Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: The believer or the person?

* Shaykh: No, the believer and the person, even the person.

What is the meaning of His saying ﴿go forth in parties﴾?

* Student: Go forth separately.

* Shaykh: What is the evidence that ﴿thubat﴾ here means separately?

* Student: That it came after His saying ﴿go forth in parties﴾ and ﴿go forth all together﴾.

* Shaykh: So then: go forth separately or together.

Is the address here general, meaning all people must go forth?

* Student: No.

* Shaykh: The evidence?

* Student: The verse.

* Shaykh: Which is?

* Student: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once﴾ [At-Tawbah 122].

* Shaykh: ﴿And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once. Why should not a group from every section of them go forth?﴾

What is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed among you is he who would lag behind﴾ [An-Nisa' 72]?

* Student: It means that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, informed them that among them are those who discourage the believers from fighting the enemy and from (...) or (...) toward the enemy. Discouragement is of two kinds: some discourage themselves, and some discourage other believers.

* Shaykh: Good, so the delaying here is for himself and for others.

Its parsing?

* Student: (man)...

* Shaykh: ﴿And indeed among you is he who would lag behind﴾?

* Student: (man) is a relative pronoun: "for the one who delays."

* Shaykh: Then the lam.

* Student: (...) answer of the oath.

* Shaykh: The lam in His saying ﴿la-man﴾?

* Student: The lam is the lam of the beginning, the delayed subject of inna, falling on the delayed subject of inna: ﴿inna minkum la-man﴾.

* Shaykh: And the lam in ﴿la-yubatti'anna﴾?

* Student: It prepares for the oath; the estimate is: "By Allah, he will delay."

* Shaykh: Perfect, good.

The division in His saying ﴿fa-in asabatkum﴾ [An-Nisa' 72] and ﴿wa-la-in asabakum﴾ [An-Nisa' 73] indicates what?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: What is the meaning of this division: "if he is struck" and "if he is granted"? What is the meaning of this division?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: It is not clear; the answer is not apparent. What is in the verse?

* Student: ﴿fa-in asabatkum musibah﴾.

* Shaykh: Yes, and ﴿wa-la-in asabakum fadl﴾?

* Student: That they are struck by this (...).

* Shaykh: Yes, good. What indicates that the man is a helper, or a discloser, or what?

* Student: If a disaster strikes you, he praises Allah that he was not with them.

* Shaykh: Yes, but what does he intend by this?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Good, yes.

* Student: He says: ﴿asabatkum﴾ meaning: defeat.

* Shaykh: Yes, but this division regarding this man's state, what does it indicate?

* Student: In the state of defeat, if defeat strikes the believers, he has (...). As for the other, if they are granted victory, he may be with them.

* Student: It indicates his boasting and contempt.

* Shaykh: His boasting in what?

* Student: ﴿Allah has certainly blessed me, for I was not present among them as a witness﴾ [An-Nisa' 72], and his contempt is what you mentioned; and his boasting: "so I would have achieved with them a great achievement."

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: As for his boasting, it is His saying ﴿Allah has certainly blessed me, for I was not present among them﴾ [An-Nisa' 72]; as for his contempt, it is in the verse he mentioned.

* Another student: Boasting and contempt are in the same verses; he exulted in himself and belittled others.

* Shaykh: Correct, the same verse includes this. But His saying ﴿And if a bounty from Allah comes to you﴾, is the second division for his state?

* Student: The second division shows that he is wavering: if they are granted victory, his state becomes contempt (...); if they are granted victory, he becomes regretful for not going, he becomes between regret and joy.

* Shaykh: In any case, I think the matter is clear: it indicates that the man does not want to fight in the way of Allah; he wants what? The world. If a disaster strikes them, he boasts that he escaped, and if he misses victory he says ﴿Oh, I wish I had been with them﴾ [An-Nisa' 73]. He resembles those of whom Allah said: ﴿If they are given from it they are content, and if they are not given from it, behold, they are angry﴾ [At-Tawbah 58].

Regarding His saying ﴿And if a bounty from Allah comes to you, he will surely say﴾, there is a difficulty: where is the answer of the conditional (in) ? Or have we not explained it?

* Student: We have not explained it.

* Shaykh: We have not reached it? Good.

* * *

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿And if a bounty from Allah comes to you, he will surely say, as if there had not been between you and him any affection, "Oh, I wish I had been with them"﴾ [An-Nisa' 73].

The clause is conditional and oath-based: conditional because of the presence of (in), and oath-based because of the presence of the lam. The lam in His saying ﴿wa-la-in﴾ is the lam of the oath, preparing for the oath; (in) is conditional; and ﴿la-yaqulanna﴾ falls in the answer of the oath. The condition and the oath have both claimed it, so do we make it for the oath or for the condition? Ibn Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, clarifies this in his saying:

"Omit, when condition and oath come together, the answer of whichever comes later; it is obligatory."

Where is the later one here?

* Students: The condition.

* Shaykh: The condition. So the answer of the condition is omitted, and what remains is the answer of the oath. For this reason the answer is joined with the lam and was not in the jussive as an answer of the condition. This is a rule among the grammarians: when a condition and an oath come together, the answer of the one that comes later is omitted, either the condition or the oath. You say: "By Allah, if Zayd stands," which of them is later?

* Students: The condition.

* Shaykh: The answer: "Amr will surely stand." And you say: "If Zayd stands, by Allah..."?

* Students: (...).

* Shaykh: No, (...) if Zayd stands, by Allah, 'Amr will not stand. The point is that the one that comes later is the one whose answer is omitted; this is a rule among the grammarians.

He says: ﴿And if a bounty from Allah comes to you﴾, the bounty here means victory and booty; ﴿he will surely say﴾, meaning this one who delays; ﴿as if there had not been﴾, and in another reading: ﴿as if there had not been﴾ (with yakun); the well-known reading is ﴿ka-an lam takun﴾, and the second is ﴿ka-an lam yakun﴾; ﴿between you and him any affection﴾, meaning love and companionship; ﴿"Oh, I wish I had been with them"﴾, this is the speech of the saying, the content of His saying ﴿he will surely say﴾: ﴿"Oh, I wish I had been with them"﴾, meaning: I wish I were with them ﴿so I would have achieved a great achievement﴾. The verb here is in the subjunctive by the fa' of causation, according to those who ease and facilitate, who are they? The Kufans; and by (an) implied after the fa' according to the view of the Basran grammarians who regulate; so the estimate is: "fa-an afuza fawzan 'azima," and the verb was put in the subjunctive by this because it falls in the answer of the wish (tamanni).

The meaning of the verses is that this category of people, who delay themselves and delay others, and so do not go out to fight in the way of Allah, remains a spectator. If a disaster strikes you, he boasts and belittles you for being in a state in which you were forsaken, and he boasts that he escaped from what? From this disaster. And if a bounty befalls you, then he wishes to be with you to achieve the bounty, which is victory and booty. Then we know that this man does not intend fighting in the way of Allah, but intends only the world.

As for His saying ﴿as if there had not been between you and him any affection﴾, the clause, it is not hidden that it is a parenthetical clause (jumlah mu'taridah), but is this its place?

The answer: Many exegetes have said that its place is what precedes it, and the meaning is: he said, as if there had never been any affection between you and him: "God has blessed me." But the correct view is that there is no transposition in it, and that its place is its own place. Nothing is more eloquent than the Book of God, and He says: ﴿As if there had never been any affection between you and him﴾. This means that it is as if he does not wish to make clear that his wish to have been with them was not out of the affection between us and him, but rather because of the bounty that was obtained, which is victory and spoils. As for affection, it is as if it were severed, even in this state in which success in victory is attained, as if there had never been any affection between you and him.

The success in His words ﴿then I would have achieved a great success﴾ is because he sees the greatest thing as being only worldly success. The truth is that the supreme success, beyond which there is no greater success, is what God mentioned in His words: ﴿Whoever is spared from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed succeeded. And the worldly life is not but the enjoyment of delusion﴾ [Al-Imran 185].

Summary of the two verses: among people there is the hypocrite who does not desire fighting in the way of God, but fights only for the sake of this world. If a calamity of defeat and humiliation befalls you, he boasts over you, belittles you, and says: ﴿God has bestowed favor upon me, for I was not a witness with them﴾. But if the opposite occurs and you achieve victory and a bounty from God reaches you, then he wishes he were with you so that he might attain the great success, which is the ultimate goal of his aspiration, namely gaining from this world.

* Benefits we take:

* First: In His words, Exalted is He, ﴿And indeed, among you is one who will surely lag behind﴾ [An-Nisa 72] there is evidence that laziness in good and turning back from it is among the causes of hypocrisy. This is so. Lagging behind from good and being sluggish about it is not only a cause of hypocrisy, but is also a cause of misguidance, blindness, and we seek refuge in God, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [Al-An'am 110]. And God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Rather, they denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused matter﴾ [Qaf 5]. Therefore, whenever the truth becomes clear to a person, he must adopt it and not be negligent, lest he suffer what those suffered. Rather, he should hasten and act. How excellent is the one who ends up where his predecessors did.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the description of a category of people who do not wish to fight in the way of God but desire this world. When those whom they were about to go out with are struck by a calamity, they boast that they were saved from that. And if these people are reached by bounty and victory, they wish they had been with them. Thus their aim is the world and not fighting in the way of God. As for the one whose aim is fighting in the way of God, he is the opposite of that: if he is struck by a calamity and is martyred, he moves from one state to a better one; ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of God as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ [Al-Imran 169]. And if bounty and victory reach him, he praises God, the Mighty and Majestic, asks God to grant him of His bounty, and regards this as an aid to his obedience.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 72–73 (part 1 of 2):

Then He said: ﴿And indeed, among you is he who would lag behind. So if a disaster strikes you, he says, "Allah has certainly blessed me, for I was not present among them as a witness."﴾ [An-Nisa' 72]. In this verse there are two lams: the first lam in (la-man) and the second in (la-yubatti'anna). Are they the lam of the beginning (lam al-ibtida')?

The answer: As for the first, it is the lam of the beginning (lam al-ibtida'), because it falls on the delayed subject of (inna), and it conveys emphasis. As for the second lam, it is the lam that prepares for an oath (lam al-muwatta'ah lil-qasam). Thus His saying ﴿yubatti'anna﴾ falls in the answer of the oath, and the estimate is: "And indeed among you is he who, by Allah, will lag behind," so the lam here falls in the answer of the oath.

And His saying ﴿So if a disaster strikes you﴾ is a conditional clause. The condition in it and its answer are a past verb. Do we say that it is in the jussive mood (majzum), or do we say that it is built (mabni) in a position of jussiveness? The second, because the past verb is built. The verb of the condition is ﴿asabatkum﴾, and its answer is ﴿qala qad an'ama Allahu 'alayya﴾.

And His saying ﴿idh lam akun﴾: (idh) here is for causation (ta'lil) and is not a time adverb (zarf); rather it is for causation, meaning: "because I was not present with them as a witness."

As for the meaning of the verse: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says ﴿And indeed among you﴾, and (min) here is partitive (tab'id), meaning some of you ﴿is he who would lag behind (la-man la-yubatti'anna)﴾, meaning: the one who lags behind. The meaning of (yubatti') is that he calls to delay, whether he calls others or calls himself. So His saying ﴿la-yubatti'anna﴾ includes the one who discourages others from setting out for fighting, and the one who discourages himself and is negligent until the opportunity is lost. This one who lags behind is delayed and does not go out to fight. The outcome of fighting is either booty, victory and support, or the opposite. So if a disaster strikes you, meaning a defeat and humiliation befalls you, he says ﴿Allah has certainly blessed me, for I was not present among them as a witness﴾. His speech thus contains both boasting and contempt: boasting in himself that he did not witness this disaster, and contempt for those who were struck by it. This is the utmost of estrangement. He is one of them, yet he speaks these words as if there was no affection between him and them, as if he were the farthest of people from them, when he boasts that he escaped the disaster that befell them, and belittles those who were struck, becoming like a reproacher of them.

﴿And if a bounty from Allah comes to you, he will surely say﴾, ﴿"Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I would have achieved a great achievement"﴾ [An-Nisa' 73]. ﴿And if a bounty comes to you﴾, meaning victory and booty, he will surely say ﴿"Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I would have achieved a great achievement"﴾, so he wishes vainly upon Allah after the matter has escaped him.

As for His saying ﴿as if there had not been between you and him any affection﴾: ﴿as if there had not been﴾ contains an example for our reading in grammar two nights ago, and it is the light form of (ka'anna): ﴿ka'an lam takun﴾. And (ka'anna), when lightened, I think we read it and stopped at it? Good, then let us leave it until we reach it.

The clause ﴿lam takun baynakum wa baynahu mawaddah﴾ is in a position of nominative (raf') as the predicate of (ka'anna), and its subject is an omitted pronoun of the matter (damir al-sha'n).

And His saying ﴿ka'an lam takun baynakum wa baynahu mawaddah﴾: "mawaddah" is pure love, meaning as if he were distant from you, with no bond between you and him. This clause, most exegetes assert, returns to the first situation, namely: "if a disaster strikes you, he says, as if there had not been any affection between you, 'Allah has certainly blessed me.'" But this is not correct, and its explanation will come, God willing.
