Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 74 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So let those fight in the way of Allah who sell the worldly life for the Hereafter﴾ [An-Nisa 74]. ﴿So let them fight﴾: the fa (فاء) is the conjunctive fa, which indicates that what follows is connected to what precedes it. The connection is clear, because the preceding verses mention those who do not want to fight in the way of Allah, whereas this verse mentions the other category, those who fight in the way of Allah.

The lam in His words ﴿fa-l-yuqatil﴾ is the lam al-amr (the imperative lam). It is pronounced with a sukun even though it is normally kasra, because it comes after the fa. The imperative lam is given a sukun when it follows fa, wa (و), or thumma (ثم), as in His words here, ﴿fa-l-yuqatil﴾, and His words: ﴿Thumma l-yaqdu tafathahum wa l-yufu nudhurahum﴾ [al-Hajj 29], "Then let them end their state of unkemptness and fulfill their vows." Here, لْيَقْضُوا and لْيُوفُوا carry the sukun. This differs from the lam of purpose, called lam kay (لام كي), which must always be pronounced with a kasra, as in His words: ﴿li-yakfuru bima ataynahum wa li-yatamatta'u﴾ [al-'Ankabut 66], "so that they may disbelieve in what We have given them and enjoy." You must pronounce it with a kasra; do not say wa-l-yatamatta'u, because if you say that, the meaning changes.

As for His words ﴿alladhina yashuruna﴾: alladhina is the subject (fa'il) of yuqatil. The word yashuruna means "they sell," even though in our colloquial language it is used to mean "they buy." That is not the case here: yashuruna means "they sell." Among its uses is His words: ﴿And among the people is one who sells himself seeking the approval of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah 207]. Yashri nafsahu means "he sells himself." When the one receiving is meant, one says ishtara (اشترى): the giver is sha'in (شارٍ, seller) and the receiver is mushtarin (مشترٍ, buyer).

﴿alladhina yashuruna l-hayata d-dunya bi-l-akhirah﴾ means: those who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter. They make the exchange, the replacement for the worldly life, to be the Hereafter. These are the people who truly profited from their lives, because they took the Hereafter in exchange for this world. They were not like those about whom Allah said: ﴿But you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ [al-A'la 16-17].

﴿wa man yuqatil﴾ [An-Nisa 74]: man here is conditional (شرطية), the verb after it is jussive, and the answer of the condition is His words: ﴿fa-sawfa nu'tihi ajran 'azima﴾, "then We will give him a great reward." As for ﴿fa-yuqtal aw yaghlib﴾, it is coordinated with the conditional verb.

﴿wa man yuqatil fi sabili llah﴾ means: whoever, of any person, fights in the way of Allah, that is, who fights so that the word of Allah is supreme, as the Prophet ﷺ explained.

﴿fa-yuqtal aw yaghlib﴾: if he is killed, he is a martyr (shahid); if he is victorious, he is successful (fa'iz). His victory does not nullify his reward, and for this reason He said: ﴿then We will give him a great reward﴾. He profits in every case: if he is killed, he is killed as a martyr, and if he is victorious, he is victorious and blessed. This is like His words: ﴿Say, "Do you await for us except one of the two best outcomes?" — and we await for you that Allah will afflict you with punishment from Him or at our hands﴾ [at-Tawbah 52]. The two best outcomes are martyrdom, or victory and triumph.

﴿fa-yuqtal aw yaghlib fa-sawfa nu'tihi ajran 'azima﴾ [An-Nisa 74]: that is, a great reward. Allah the Exalted called the reward ajr (أجر, wage), likening it to the wage of a worker whom a person hires to do something and then pays. The point is that Allah has committed Himself to rewarding this worker, just as the employer commits himself to paying the worker his wage. For this reason Allah called the deed given to Him a loan (qard), although Allah has no need of anything, and He called the reward for it a wage, as though He had hired a worker to pay him his wage.

His words ﴿ajran 'azima﴾ refer to the reward of Paradise, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah has prepared one hundred levels in Paradise for those who strive in His way." [Reported by al-Bukhari (2790) from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.] That is, in Paradise, and this is the great reward.

* In this noble verse there are benefits:
* Among them: the obligation to fight the enemies, based on His words: ﴿So let them fight﴾.
* Among them: the obligation to make the intention sincere in fighting, based on His words: ﴿in the way of Allah﴾. The reasoning is that among those who fight there are those who fight out of bravery, those who fight out of zeal (ḥamiyyah), meaning partisanship for their nation or homeland, and those who fight to be seen, meaning for show. The Prophet ﷺ was asked about this and said: "Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is supreme, he is in the way of Allah." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (123) and Muslim (1904/150) from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.] So fighting in the way of Allah is fighting so that the word of Allah is supreme.

Is the meaning: "so that people may believe"?
The answer: No. It is so that the word of Allah is supreme, either through faith, the faith of those fought against, or through their humiliation and their payment of the jizyah (tax), as in His words: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day, and who do not prohibit what Allah and His Messenger have prohibited, and who do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture, until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled﴾ [at-Tawbah 29].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: showing the high aspiration of these fighters, that they sell the worldly life for the Hereafter. This is from the strength of their faith, the truth of their resolve, and the height of their aspiration, because they believe that there is a Hereafter, and they have a strong resolve by which they overcome their desires. Otherwise, how many people prefer the worldly life and say: "A dirham in hand is better than a thousand promised" (and Allah forbid). There is no doubt that this indicates the absence of faith in such a person. If he were a believer, the promised reward, which is better than what is given in hand, would be what he works for, and he would know that between him and that promise there is only a little time, and that what he gets in hand is worth nothing compared to what is promised. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The place of one of your whips in Paradise is better than this world and all that is in it." [Reported by at-Tirmidhi (1664) from Sahl ibn Sa'd.] The whip is not long, and yet it is better than the entire world and all that is in it. And it is not your world, or the world of the era you live in, but the world from Adam, from its beginning, even before Adam, from its beginning to its end. The place of one of our whips in Paradise is better than the world and all that is in it. This is the wise, resolute, sincere believer.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the one who fights in the way of Allah is successful in every case, based on His words: ﴿And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed or achieves victory﴾. He profits and succeeds in every case, whether he is killed or victorious, and he has a great reward.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: showing the greatness of the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, based on His words: ﴿fa-sawfa nu'tihi﴾ ("We will give him"). The reason is the plural pronoun. We know that Allah is one God, so whatever pronouns in the plural are attributed to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are meant to express glorification.

* A student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. If the one who fights in the way of Allah has obligations to people (huquq al-'ibad), what will be his fate?

* The Shaykh: His fate is that the Prophet ﷺ was asked about martyrdom and said: "It expiates everything." Then the questioner left, and he called him back and said: "Except debt; Jibril told me that just now." [Reported by an-Nasa'i in al-Mujtaba (3155) from Abu Hurayrah.] This shows that the rights of people are not nullified by martyrdom. That is so, because the rights of people must be paid to them. However, it is established from the Prophet ﷺ that "whoever takes the property of people intending to repay it, Allah will repay on his behalf." [Reported by al-Bukhari (2387) from Abu Hurayrah.]

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes.

* A student: May Allah be good to you, Shaykh. A person wanted to go to fight, or to go to a certain land for jihad in the way of Allah, and another came and said to him: "(...) in these lands, or (...)." Would this man be considered one who discourages others, and what is the definition of discouraging?

* The Shaykh: If he said it as sincere advice, then it is not discouragement. But if he said it wanting to dishearten him, while knowing that if he went to that place he would benefit and benefit others, then he falls under the verse. Sometimes a man consults you and you know it is not in his interest to go, either because it would be useless or for other reasons. This is not discouragement; it is sincere advice. Sometimes you say, "Do not go," not for this purpose, but you want to dishearten him, and this is not permissible.

* A student: Some scholars held that the addressees in His words ﴿from among you﴾ and His words ﴿as if there had never been between you and him any affection﴾ are believers. So what is the answer?

* The Shaykh: The answer is that Allah addresses people in general, and the hypocrites, as you know, show that they are believers. So they are "from you" outwardly, though not in reality.

* The student: Do we say the intended addressees here are the general public?

* The Shaykh: The generality.

* The student: The generality? So the believer who discourages others is included?

* The Shaykh: And the hypocrite.

* The student: And the hypocrite?

* The Shaykh: Yes.

(...)

* * *

* The Shaykh: (...) Why did Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, not state the verb in His words ﴿and those in authority among you﴾ [An-Nisa 59]?

* A student: Because obedience to the rulers is part of obedience to Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, and follows from obedience to Allah.

* The Shaykh: And is it not?

* The student: It is not independent.

* The Shaykh: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turn away from you with aversion﴾ [An-Nisa 61]. Why did He not say, "you see them"?

* A student: It is the explicit noun in place of the pronoun, and it has benefits.

* The Shaykh: This is the explicit noun in place of the pronoun. What are its benefits?

* The student: Showing the cause: that they turned away because of their desires.

* The Shaykh: Excellent, that is one.

* The student: And to alert the addressee that they are hypocrites.

* The Shaykh: No.

* A student: Recording the judgment on the referent of the pronoun.

* The Shaykh: How?

* The student: Recording the judgment on the referent of the pronoun.

* The Shaykh: With what?

* The student: That if there were a pronoun, it would be...

* The Shaykh: No.

* A student: Recording a judgment on the place of the pronoun by a description, and it also indicates generality.

* The Shaykh: By the description, and that they are hypocrites. If He had said, "you see them," it would not have been clear to us that they are hypocrites. But when He said, ﴿you see the hypocrites﴾, the meaning is that He has recorded against them that they are hypocrites. If you wish, say: a judgment is passed on the referent of the pronoun by this attribute, namely hypocrisy.

The third?

For the causation of the ruling, and the passing of a judgment on the referent of the pronoun by this attribute.

* A student: Generality.

* The Shaykh: Generality; meaning that everyone who turns away...

* The student: From the Messenger is a hypocrite.

* The Shaykh: He is a hypocrite. Well done.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, swore that faith is not complete except with three matters concerning the judgment of the Messenger ﷺ.

* A student: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged and submit in full submission﴾ [An-Nisa 65].

* The Shaykh: What is the difference between these three?

* The student: The first thing is taking him as judge.

* The Shaykh: Taking him as judge.

* The student: Taking him as judge.

* The Shaykh: So that they do not seek judgment from anyone else, however great his intellect and intelligence. That is one.

* The student: The discomfort is this matter (...).

* The Shaykh: ﴿Find within themselves no discomfort﴾ means no tightness (dīq).

* The student: Tightness regarding this judgment.

* The Shaykh: The third?

* The student: Submission: outward compliance.

* The Shaykh: Submission: outward compliance, such that no opposition arises from them.

* The student: Regarding the judgment.

* The Shaykh: Excellent, may Allah bless you.

In His words, blessed and exalted: ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it﴾ [An-Nisa 66]. The word law (لو) here requires an answer to the condition. So what is the answer in this verse?

* A student: The answer to the condition is omitted; its estimate is: "and if it were established that they..."

* The Shaykh: The answer to the condition is omitted?

* The student: No, that is the condition clause (fi'l al-shart).

* The Shaykh: I am asking about its answer.

* The student: ﴿And if they had, when they wronged themselves...﴾ [An-Nisa 64].

* The Shaykh: No, ﴿And if We had decreed for them...﴾.

* The student: ﴿And if We had decreed for them...﴾ ﴿they would not have done it﴾.

* The Shaykh: A clause?

* The student: ﴿Ma fa'aluhu﴾ ("they would not have done it").

* The Shaykh: ﴿Ma fa'aluhu﴾.

* The student: The answer to the condition.

* The Shaykh: Why was the lam not attached to the answer of law, although it may be attached to it, or although the answer may take the lam?

* The student: Because the clause here is negative.

* The Shaykh: Because the clause here is negated.

* The student: Negated, and the lam indicates the affirmation and emphasis of the matter, while negation contradicts that.

* The Shaykh: So from this we take a rule: when the answer of law begins with the negative ma, it does not take the lam.

If it is affirmative, may it take the lam or not?

* The student: Both options are permissible.

* The Shaykh: Both are permissible.

* The student: With the lam or without the lam.

* The Shaykh: With the lam and without it. Recite to me two verses of the Qur'an that show this.

* The student: Surat al-Waqi'ah: His words, ﴿If We willed, We would have made it salty﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 70], and secondly: ﴿If We willed, We would have made it broken debris﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 65].

* The Shaykh: Correct. Yes, ﴿If We willed, We would have made it broken debris﴾, ﴿If We willed, We would have made it salty﴾.

His words, exalted be He: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor﴾. Who is meant by "the Messenger"?

* A student: The Prophet ﷺ.

* The Shaykh: Do you mean the generality or Muhammad specifically?

* The student: It is more appropriate that it means the category of messengers; (...) the Prophet ﷺ (...) the context.

* The Shaykh: One of the rules of tafsir: if two explanations conflict, one specific and the other general, which do we take?

* The student: (...) the general.

* The Shaykh: Why?

* The student: Because (...).

* The Shaykh: Because the specific (...) the general, and not the reverse? Or no? Have you understood this rule: if two interpretations conflict, one general and the other specific, we take the general, because it – that is, the general – includes the specific, and not the reverse.

What does His words, ﴿That is the bounty of Allah, and sufficient is Allah as Knower﴾, indicate from the behavioural (ethical) perspective?

* A student: A reference to sincerity: that a person should not take pride in himself.

* The Shaykh: It indicates that a person should not take pride in himself, but should believe that the bounty is from Allah, unlike the one who said: ﴿I was only given it on account of knowledge I have﴾ [al-Qasas 78].

* * *

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.

Allah, blessed and exalted, said in Surat an-Nisa: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners, and when you judge between people to judge with justice. Excellent is that which He instructs you. Indeed, Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing﴾ [An-Nisa 58]. The scholars derived from this verse that a trustee must safeguard the trust in a suitable place, must not transgress regarding it, and must not neglect it. How did they derive that? Answer.

* A student: Because the rendering of a trust differs according to the type of trust (...).

* The Shaykh: No.

* A student: Because of His words ﴿to its owners﴾; just as its owners protect it, it must...

* The Shaykh: No.

* A student: Shaykh, it is impossible to render the trust unless one has preserved it.

* The Shaykh: Correct. It is impossible to render it except by preserving it and not transgressing against it.

Now, His words: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you?﴾ [An-Nisa 60]. Who are these people?

* A student: The Jews, the People of the Book.

* The Shaykh: The People of the Book. Do you agree with this? Who?

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 74 (part 2 of 2):**

* Student: The verse is general (...) the hypocrites.
* The Shaykh: It includes the People of the Book and the hypocrites. How do we know that it includes the hypocrites?
* Student: The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture?﴾ [an-Nisa' 51].
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they have believed in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you?﴾ [an-Nisa' 60].
* The Shaykh: Yes, but this does not indicate the inclusion of the hypocrites.
* Student: Shaykh, because the hypocrites outwardly show Islam, so when they say to us, "We believe in what was revealed to the Messenger (ﷺ)," they likewise believe in what was revealed to those before him.
* Another student: It is understood from His words ﴿in what has been revealed to you﴾ that they claim they believed in Muhammad (ﷺ).
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: That the People of the Book did not believe in the Messenger (ﷺ).
* The Shaykh: There is no god but Allah!
* Student: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger"﴾ [an-Nisa' 61] (...) the hypocrites.
* Another student: The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turn away from you with aversion.﴾
* The Shaykh: Correct, yes, this is ﴿you see the hypocrites turn away from you with aversion﴾. Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, says in al-Fatwa al-Hamawiyya: the speculative theologians (al-Mutakallimun, the scholars of kalam, i.e. speculative theology) resemble those whom Allah spoke of in the four aspects. How is that?
* Student: Yes, they say: "We intended goodness and reconciliation."
* The Shaykh: Do not start from the end; start from the beginning.
* Student: The first aspect: if...
* Another student: The first aspect: the People of the Book, in their plunging into this inquiry, claim that they seek the truth. They claim it. Likewise these hypocrites in this matter also claim that. They share the claim of seeking the truth, and they are liars in that. This is the first.
The second: ﴿They wish to seek judgment from the false deities, while they were commanded to reject them﴾ [an-Nisa' 60]. Also, each of them has taken a false deity from the false deities as a guide on his path. So the people of kalam have made their desires the judge, and the hypocrites have also made what they made... I mean...
* The Shaykh: Made their desires the judge.
* The student: Their desires. The third...
* Another student: (...) with the Book and the Sunnah, adding the Book and the Sunnah, unlike (...) from the Book and the Sunnah.
* The Shaykh: And the speculative theologians, when they are called to the Book and the Sunnah and to affirming what Allah and His Messenger affirmed, you see them turn away, and they do not like inquiry into this.
* Student: The fourth: His words: ﴿We intended nothing but goodness and reconciliation﴾ [an-Nisa' 62].
* The Shaykh: That is, when they are discovered, they say...
* The student: ﴿We intended nothing but goodness and reconciliation.﴾
* The Shaykh: That is: "We intended nothing but goodness and reconciliation." How is "reconciliation" (tawfiq) in relation to the speculative theologians?
* The student: They say (...) we reconcile between (...) and reason.
* The Shaykh: Between revelation (al-sam') and reason. Correct.

Regarding the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by permission of Allah﴾ [an-Nisa' 64]. If someone says: this has been contradicted, because among the messengers there were those who were not obeyed but were rather denied.
* Student: (...) The response to them is that whoever denies the messengers is denying the truth, and this is not an argument for them; it is an argument against them, not for them.
* The Shaykh: But the verse says: ﴿except to be obeyed﴾. We did not send him except so that he would be obeyed.
* The student: No messenger was sent from among the messengers except to be obeyed by permission of Allah.
* The Shaykh: And how many a messenger was not obeyed?
* The student: (How many a messenger) is not an argument against the verse, Shaykh. The argument is that the Messenger (ﷺ), according to the people of truth, does not lie under any circumstances.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Allah the Exalted restricted it. He said: "except by permission of Allah."
* The Shaykh: ﴿to be obeyed by permission of Allah﴾, that is fine, but it informs that he must be obeyed; everything is by the permission of Allah.
* Student: The permission of Allah the Exalted is divided into two types: a universal permission (kawni)...
* The Shaykh: No.
* The student: Shaykh, what prevents it?
* The Shaykh: No, no.
* Student: The lam is not the lam of consequence (al-lam al-'aqibah); here it is the lam of causation in His words ﴿so that he would be obeyed﴾, for causation: meaning, in order that he be obeyed. As for whether he is obeyed or not obeyed, that is another matter.
* Another student: Shaykh, in it there is a legislative will (irada shar'iyyah): Allah, Mighty and Majestic, willed that He be obeyed legislatively, but everything Allah wills legislatively occurs universally (kawnan).
* The Shaykh: Yes. Is there a parallel to it in the Qur'an?
* The student: ﴿Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him﴾ [al-Isra' 23].
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: Shaykh, ﴿And Allah wants to accept your repentance﴾ [an-Nisa' 27].
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾.
* The Shaykh: Yes, ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾, and yet many of them did not worship Him more than those who did not worship Him. But this is what? A legislative will, whose object may fail to be realized. This is the correct view.
* Student: The lam of consequence, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: Even if it were the lam of consequence, in reality the consequence is not like that. No. It is good to say: it is a legislative will; Allah willed that the messengers be obeyed, Allah willed that He be worshipped, but what was willed did not occur.

Some of them said this is like your saying: "I sharpened the pencil in order to write with it." Sometimes you write and sometimes you do not write. That is: this is my intention, and it may happen or may not happen. But what we have mentioned is better.

Regarding the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Kill yourselves or leave your homes﴾ [an-Nisa' 66], there are two readings?
* Student: Kasr of the nun and its damma.
* Another student: There is a reading: ﴿ani-qtuluu﴾ (with kasra on the nun and qitlu) and a reading: ﴿anu-qtuluu﴾.
* The Shaykh: With a damma on the nun.
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Good. The second: ﴿or leave your homes﴾ [an-Nisa' 66]?
* Student: ﴿awi-khruju﴾, ﴿awu-khruju﴾.
* The Shaykh: Kasra on the waw and damma on the waw, correct. So: kasra on the nun and damma on it, and kasra on the waw and damma on it.

﴿Only a few of them did it﴾ also has two readings.
* Student: ﴿qaliilan﴾ and ﴿qaliilun﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿qaliilan﴾ and ﴿qaliilun﴾.
* The student: And the answer is that the exception here... we say that the exception is complete and negated.
* The Shaykh: The exception from a complete negated statement.
* The student: And for an exception from a complete negated statement, both possibilities are permitted: the accusative as an exception, or agreement (al-ittiba') with what precedes it.
* The Shaykh: Good, what is the agreement here?
* The student: On the nominative, we make it agree with what precedes it.
* The Shaykh: And that is?
* The student: ﴿And if We had decreed for them﴾, ﴿did it﴾ on the pronoun in ﴿fa'aluhu﴾.
* The Shaykh: (...) where is the waw?
* The student: The waw is the pronoun of the subject, and on the accusative it is an exception.
* The Shaykh: An exception. Well done, may Allah bless you.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – they will be with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous﴾. Some people said: "with" (ma'a) means what?
* Student: You say "ma'a"? What is its meaning?
* The Shaykh: Yes, with the meaning of what?
* Student: (...) they will be gathered with them on the Day of Resurrection.
* The Shaykh: No, "ma'a" means what?
* Student: "min" means "min".
* The Shaykh: With the meaning of "min" (from); so they are from those upon whom Allah bestowed favor.
Must "ma'a" necessarily mean "min"?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, must "ma'a" necessarily mean "min", or may it stay in its original sense, which is accompaniment?
* The student: The second.
* The Shaykh: That is, it is permitted. So it is permitted for it to mean "min" and also for it to be accompaniment in its original sense: ﴿they will be with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor﴾. And if they are with them as companions, then they are of them, and in that case we do not take the word out of its apparent meaning, but the meaning returns to the second view, which is the meaning of "min".

﴿The martyrs (al-shuhada')﴾: there are two opinions?
* Student: The scholars; the martyrs are those who fight in the cause of Allah (...).
* The Shaykh: Those who fight in the cause of Allah, or those who are killed in the cause of Allah?
* The student: Those who are killed in the cause of Allah.
* The Shaykh: What supports the first, that they are the scholars?
* Student: In Surat Al 'Imran: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge﴾ [Al 'Imran 18] (...) the testimony.
* The Shaykh: Correct, yes. And what supports that they are the martyrs, that is, those who were killed in the cause of Allah?
* Student: The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And do not think of those who have been killed in the cause of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision. Rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty, and rejoicing for those who have not yet joined them from behind them – that no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve﴾ [Al 'Imran 169, 170].
* The Shaykh: The word "shahada" (martyrdom) is not mentioned in it.
* Student: Does a hadith suffice?
* The Shaykh: Yes, a hadith, but in the Qur'an there is nothing that indicates this.
* Student: Its being paired with the truthful and the righteous, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Allah has certainly blessed me, for I was not present with them as a witness﴾ [an-Nisa' 72].
* The Shaykh: That is: present.
Did Allah not say in Surat Al 'Imran: ﴿and that He may take from among you martyrs﴾ [Al 'Imran 140]? That is: those who are killed in the cause of Allah.
Now, do we have a principle that clarifies the two meanings?
* Student: That if a word can bear two meanings with no contradiction between them, it is understood as both together.
* The Shaykh: Correct. And then we say?
* Student: The verse includes the martyrs of battle and the martyrs among the scholars.
* The Shaykh: Good, correct.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And indeed among you is one who will surely lag behind﴾. The (min)?
* Student: The min here is for partitive.
* The Shaykh: For partitive. What is the sign of the partitive min?
* Student: It is known that we say: "inna..." That is, ﴿And indeed among you is one who will surely lag behind﴾ means: some of you will surely lag behind.
* The Shaykh: That is, that it can take its place?
* Student: "Some."
* The Shaykh: "Some," good.
The lam in His words ﴿la-man﴾, and in His words ﴿la-yubatti'anna﴾?
* Student: The first is for emphasis; the first is the one that comes at the beginning of the speech.
* The Shaykh: The first is the lam of initiation (lam al-ibtida').
* Student: Yes, and it conveys emphasis. As for the second, it is for the oath, and if the word Allah were placed in its position, it would be permissible.
* The Shaykh: So the second lam falls in the answer to the oath, and the first lam is the lam of initiation, which is for emphasis.
Here there is a difficulty: how do we say it is the lam of initiation when it is not at the beginning of the speech?
* Student: It came with the postponed subject of "inna."
* The Shaykh: How?
* Student: It came with the postponed subject of "inna."
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: That is, they are not combined; the lam of emphasis is not combined with "inna."
* The Shaykh: That is, they postponed it so that two emphatic particles would not combine at the beginning of the speech. For this reason some call it the displaced lam (al-lam al-muzahlaqah), meaning the one that has been pushed from its place.

If someone says: what is the benefit of the oath in the Qur'an, when it is true and sincere without the oath?
* Student: It clarifies the addressee's doubt, so it is emphasized by this, or (...) the thing sworn to and its importance.
* The Shaykh: That is, the Qur'an is in the Arabic tongue, and the Arabs emphasize reports by means of oaths.

**Part 1 of 3**

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verses 75–76

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan (Satan). ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah and [for] the oppressed men, women, and children who say, "Our Lord, take us out of this city whose people are oppressors, and appoint for us from Yourself a protector, and appoint for us from Yourself a helper"? (75) Those who believe fight in the way of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the way of Taghut (false deities). So fight against the allies of Shaytan. Indeed, the plot of Shaytan is ever weak.﴾ [An-Nisa' 75–76].

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. When Allah the Exalted and Glorified commanded fighting in the way of Allah, He directed the command to those who sell (yashrun) the worldly life for the Hereafter; that is, they sell the worldly life for the Hereafter. He also explained the virtue of fighting in the way of Allah, and that the one who fights in the way of Allah, whether he is killed or victorious, has a reward from Allah: ﴿And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed or conquers, We will give him a great reward﴾ [An-Nisa' 74]. Allah then rebuked those who refrain from fighting, saying: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah﴾. The word "ma" here is interrogative, and its meaning is disapproval (inkar). It may also carry both disapproval and wonder; that is, its meaning is a rebuke of those who did not fight, and an expression of amazement at their condition.

As for His saying ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, it has been explained many times before: fighting in the way of Allah is fighting so that the word of Allah alone is supreme.

His saying ﴿and [for] the oppressed men﴾ may be conjoined to the word "Allah" (in the phrase "the way of Allah"), meaning: "and in the way of the oppressed." It may also be conjoined to the word "way" (sabil), meaning: "and for the oppressed men." Both meanings flow into one channel, whether we say "in the way of the oppressed" or "for the oppressed themselves." The oppressed men are those who cannot leave this city which subjects them to a wretched torment.

﴿And [for] the women﴾ is conjoined either to "the oppressed" or to "the men." Which is preferable? If we say it is conjoined to "the men," the meaning is that women are divided into two groups: an oppressed group and a group that is not oppressed, and the verse refers to the oppressed group. If we say it is conjoined to "the oppressed," then women are not divided into two groups but are one category, and a woman is not obliged to emigrate. But the first meaning is better, because among women there are those who emigrated and did not remain in the abode of humiliation and degradation.

His saying ﴿and [for] the children﴾: this is the one that we can say is conjoined to His saying "the oppressed." This is because children cannot emigrate or leave, and they are wronged in these places; they have no strategy and cannot find a way. So it is an obligation upon us to fight in the way of Allah the Exalted, and for these oppressed men, women, and children.

His saying ﴿who say, "Our Lord, take us out"﴾: ﴿who﴾ is an adjective (sifa) describing everything preceding it, both the conjoined and the conjoined-to. ﴿say﴾ means each one of them says it, or the verb "say" is used in the sense of the group, even though this statement was not uttered by each individual; this is because a group that shares one goal and one path, the statement of one of them is considered the statement of all.

﴿Our Lord, take us out of this city﴾: the pointed-to city is the one they inhabit and remain in, and it is Makkah, because the Quraysh subjected whoever embraced Islam to a wretched torment.

His saying ﴿whose people are oppressors﴾: ﴿oppressors﴾ here is a descriptive adjective (na't). For what?

Student: For "city."

Student: For "its people" (ahl).

Shaykh: For the demonstrative in ﴿this﴾. But how can it be an adjective when the meaning belongs to other than the described noun? Because He said ﴿whose people are oppressors﴾ and did not say "oppressive" (feminine)?

The answer to this is that the adjective is of two types: the real (haqiqi) and the causative (sababi).

The real adjective is one where the attribute returns to the described noun, as when you say: "I passed by Zayd the virtuous." Here "virtuous" is an attribute returning to whom? To Zayd.

The causative adjective is one where the attribute returns to other than the described noun, but has a connection to it, as when you say: "I passed by Zayd, whose father is virtuous." Here the virtue does not return to Zayd but to his father, yet there is a relation and link between them, and therefore it was attributed to him, so it is said "his father." The pronoun in "his father" returns to Zayd. ﴿whose people are oppressors﴾ belongs to this category. Is the adjective here causative or real?

Student: Causative.

Shaykh: Causative. ﴿whose people are oppressors﴾. Accordingly we say: ﴿oppressors﴾ is an adjective of ﴿this﴾, and "people" (ahl) is the agent of the active participle "oppressors." ﴿oppressors﴾ is an active participle, and ﴿its people﴾: "people" is the agent, "people" is in construct form, and "ha'" (its) is the genitive pronoun attached to it.

Why are they oppressors in ﴿whose people are oppressors﴾? Is the intended oppression the aggression against the rights of these believers, or is it something more general, such as their wronging through polytheism and also aggression?

Student: The second.

Shaykh: The second. The people of this city are oppressors with respect to the right of Allah, by associating others with Him, and Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Indeed, association [of others with Allah] is a great injustice﴾ [Luqman 13]. These people are also oppressors with respect to their aggression against these believers, since they used to harm them and subject them to a wretched torment.

﴿And appoint for us from Yourself a protector﴾: the "wa" here is a conjunctive particle, and ﴿appoint﴾ is conjoined to ﴿take us out﴾. That is, they also say: ﴿appoint for us from Yourself﴾, meaning "from Your presence," ﴿a protector﴾, and ﴿appoint for us from Yourself a helper﴾. "Appoint for us a protector" means one who takes charge of us, who manages our affairs, and ﴿helper﴾ means one who supports us against our enemies.

Notice that the word ﴿appoint﴾ came twice, because the setting is one of supplication, and the setting of supplication calls for expansiveness, because the supplicant is communicating intimately with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The intimate speech of a beloved with his beloved, the more it increases, the stronger the love becomes. For this reason, you find that when a person loves someone, he wishes to speak with him at length, and sometimes he sits talking with him for a long period, which seems to him far shorter than it is.

﴿And appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper﴾. The helper (nasir) is the one who defends and repels your enemy from attacking you.

If someone says: Doesn't "protection" (wilaya) also come with the meaning of "support"?

We say: Yes. But, as we mentioned before, the setting of supplication calls for expansiveness.

* * *

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿Those who believe fight in the way of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the way of Taghut. So fight against the allies of Shaytan. Indeed, the plot of Shaytan is ever weak (76). Have you not considered those who were told, "Restrain your hands, establish prayer, and give zakah"? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a faction of them fear men as they should fear Allah or with greater fear, and say, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed for us fighting? If only You would delay us to a near term." Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, and you will not be wronged even a [thread of] date-fiber"﴾ [An-Nisa' 76–77].

Shaykh: We seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan.

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah and [for] the oppressed﴾. What type of interrogation is this here?

Student: Disapproving (inkari), and it may be disapproval and wonder.

Shaykh: Yes, disapproval and wonder.

His saying ﴿and [for] the oppressed men﴾ is conjoined to what?

Student: (...) conjoined to the word "Allah."

Shaykh: Yes indeed. And what would the estimated (taqdir) construction be?

Student: "In the way of Allah and in the way of the oppressed."

Shaykh: Or conjoined to "way"?

Student: (...) Allah, and the oppressed men.

Shaykh: That is: "and in [the rescue of] the oppressed, to free them."

Good. What is meant by "city" in His saying ﴿the city whose people are oppressors﴾?

Student: Makkah.

Shaykh: Makkah. Is there evidence that it is Makkah?

Student: From the verse?

Shaykh: Yes, from the verse or from outside the verse.

Student: The reality, O Shaykh, at the time the verses were revealed.

Shaykh: Is there not a verse that indicates this?

Student: Another verse?

Shaykh: Yes.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: No.

Student: ﴿And how many a city was stronger in power than your city﴾... [Muhammad 13].

Shaykh: Well done, exactly.

His saying ﴿and appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper﴾: what is the difference between the protector (wali) and the helper (nasir)?

Student: The protector is the one who takes charge of a person's affairs, the guardian of affairs.

Shaykh: By bringing him benefit and warding off...?

Student: Harm.

Shaykh: And the helper?

Student: The helper is the one who assists you and supports you.

Shaykh: Yes. That is, he also prevents His enemies from him, because victory (nasr) means prevention, as in His saying: ﴿So who will protect us from the might of Allah if it should come to us?﴾ [Ghafir 29].

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those who believe fight in the way of Allah.﴾ When Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, rebuked and expressed wonder at those who do not fight in the way of Allah, He clarified that the fighters are divided into two groups, saying: ﴿Those who believe fight in the way of Allah.﴾ This is a sentence composed of a subject and a predicate: the subject is ﴿those who﴾ and the predicate is ﴿fight﴾.

His saying ﴿fight in the way of Allah﴾ means: they fight the disbelievers.

His saying ﴿in the way of Allah﴾ means: in His religion and His law; that is, for His sake. The Prophet (ﷺ) clarified fighting in the way of Allah: it is the fighting of one who fights so that the word of Allah is supreme. This is fighting in the way of Allah, and whatever else is not in the way of Allah.

﴿And those who disbelieve fight in the way of Taghut.﴾ This sentence is composed of a subject and a predicate: the subject is ﴿those who﴾, and the predicate is the clause ﴿fight in the way of Taghut.﴾

﴿Taghut﴾ is an intensive form (sigha mubalagha) from transgression (tughyan). The ta' in it is like the ta' in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was a [whole] nation﴾ [An-Nahl 120]; the ta' is for intensification. Just as they say: "So-and-so is an 'allama" (one who knows very much), the ta' is also for intensification. Accordingly, the last letter of the word, that is, the last of its root letters, is the waw in "taghut," and the ta' is an added letter for intensification. Who is the Taghut?

The meaning is known by mentioning its opposite. The Taghut is the opposite of the one who fights in the way of Allah. So everyone who fights for other than the way of Allah is fighting in the way of Taghut, whether we say it is Shaytan, or the allies of Shaytan, or tribal partisanship, or something else. The important point is that we understand that what is meant by "the way of Taghut" is whatever is for other than the way of Allah, by way of contrast. We have already had a useful principle regarding this: a thing may be known by knowing its opposite. We have already encountered from it His saying: ﴿So go forth in separate groups or go forth all together﴾ [An-Nisa' 71].

And His saying ﴿Taghut﴾ means: everything by which a person exceeds his limit, is transgression and taghut.

﴿So fight against the allies of Shaytan.﴾ The fa' is for consequence based on what preceded; that is: fight, O fighters in the way of Allah, against the allies of Shaytan, who have taken Shaytan as a protector, so he deceived and misguided them, and they are those who fight not so that the word of Allah is supreme.

﴿Indeed, the plot of Shaytan is ever weak.﴾ When He commanded fighting against the allies of Shaytan, He clarified that they are overcome, and that the fighter against the allies of Shaytan is victorious. This is derived from the reasoning in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the plot of Shaytan is ever weak.﴾ If his plot is weak, then he has no ability to oppose the truth.

His saying ﴿Indeed, the plot of Shaytan﴾: if the plot of Shaytan is weak, while it is that which comes by way of deceit and trickery, then what is open is even more so. Shaytan has plots and schemes; he plots against man, but he is weak. When Allah is mentioned, he withdraws. Otherwise, he plots even outside of fighting. He plots against man in acts of worship: he first approaches him through negligence in worship, making it seem easy to him, and says: "If you leave it this time, you can do it another time." Then when he intends to do it another time, he whispers to him and discourages him. He makes disobedience seem trivial to him, saying: "This is a minor sin, and no one sees you; there is no one with you but Allah, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful," and similar things. So he makes it easy for him and beautifies it through his scheming. Nevertheless, his plot is weak, because it never withstands the truth.

* There are several issues and benefits in this verse.

* First: a clarification that people are divided into two groups regarding jihad...

Student: The previous verse, O Shaykh.

Shaykh: The previous one? ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight﴾?

* ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight﴾ contains benefits:
* First: a rebuke of those who are negligent in jihad, based on His saying: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah﴾.
* Among its benefits also: mentioning what encourages fighting from the psychological side, based on His saying: ﴿and [for] the oppressed men, women, and children﴾, because mentioning what stirs a person and rouses him is something desirable. Without doubt, when a person is told that there are oppressed men, children, and women, he will certainly increase in resolve and readiness.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the disbelievers have oppressed these people and humiliated them.
* Among its benefits: the obligation to defend the oppressed against the disbelievers, because Allah the Exalted rebuked for two matters: for abandoning fighting in the way of Allah, and for abandoning fighting in the way of these oppressed people to free them. This is an obligation upon every Muslim who has the ability: to free the captive Muslims and to lift the oppression from them to the extent of his capacity, based on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [At-Taghabun 16].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of seeking a means (tawassul) through a state of affairs, based on His saying: ﴿take us out of this city whose people are oppressors﴾. They sought a means to Allah the Exalted by mentioning the condition of the people of this city, that they are oppressors toward them. Mentioning a condition, that a person is wronged, creates tenderness and compassion.

Know that seeking a means to Allah the Mighty and Majestic can be done through several matters:

The first matter: seeking a means to Allah through His names, based on His saying: ﴿And to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so invoke Him by them﴾ [Al-A'raf 180]. So you say: "O Forgiving, forgive me," and "O Merciful, have mercy on me." Here, it is fitting, out of good manners, intelligence, and discernment, that one should not seek a means for a matter except through the name suitable to it. If he wants to ask Allah for forgiveness, he seeks a means through what? Through "the Forgiving." Provision, through "the Provider." Seizing the wrongdoer, through "the Severe in punishment," and similar things.

The second: seeking a means to Allah the Exalted through His attributes, including what is in the transmitted hadith: "O Allah, by Your mercy I seek help" [1]. This is a means to Allah the Exalted through one of His attributes. Likewise: "O Allah, by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation, cause me to live if You know life is good for me" [2]. Likewise: "O Allah, I seek Your choice by Your knowledge, and I seek Your power by Your power" [3].

[1] Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (3524) from the hadith of Anas, with the wording: "O Living, O Self-Subsisting, by Your mercy I seek help."
[2] Recorded by al-Nasa'i in al-Mujtaba (1305) from the hadith of 'Ammar ibn Yasir.
[3] Recorded by al-Bukhari (1162) from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah.

The third: seeking a means (tawassul) to God through His actions. Actions are a type distinct from attributes, even though they are sometimes counted among them. An example is your saying: "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim." The correct view is that the particle *kaf* here indicates cause (ta'lil), meaning: "because You sent blessings upon Ibrahim." It is not strange for *kaf* to indicate cause. It does so in His saying: ﴿And remember Him as He has guided you﴾ [al-Baqarah 198], meaning "because of His guiding you," according to one of the two interpretations. When we say that the *kaf* in "kama sallayta 'ala Ibrahim" [[Reported by al-Bukhari (3370) from the hadith of Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, and (4798) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]] is causal, the difficulty that many scholars raise is removed. That difficulty is how one could liken the blessing upon Muhammad ﷺ to the blessing upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim, when Muhammad and his family are more excellent than Ibrahim and his family. If we take the *kaf* as causal, the difficulty disappears. If we take it as comparative, which is not valid but is considered for argument's sake, then according to some scholars this is a case of mentioning the blessing upon the Prophet ﷺ twice: once as a request, and once as a report. The request is "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad," and the report is "as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim" [[Reported by al-Bukhari (3370) from the hadith of Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah.]]. Muhammad is undoubtedly from the family of Ibrahim, by lineage and by following him, as Allah, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, the most worthy of Ibrahim among the people are those who followed him, and this Prophet and those who believed﴾ [Al 'Imran 68]. So he is of his family ﷺ by lineage and by following. But what we mentioned first, what category is it? It is seeking a means to Allah through His actions, which is preferable.

The fourth: seeking a means to Allah through the state of the supplicant. That is, a person mentions his condition to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and presents it. Mentioning a state that calls for compassion and kindness is a means of tawassul. Among its examples is the saying of Musa, peace be upon him: ﴿My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need﴾ [al-Qasas 24].

The fifth: seeking a means to Allah through faith in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger. Among its examples is His saying: ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire"﴾ [Al 'Imran 16].

The sixth: seeking a means to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, through the supplication of the righteous. That is, a person seeks a means to Allah through the supplication of a righteous man, such as the saying of 'Ukkasha ibn Mihsan: "Ask Allah to make me one of them." He said: "You are one of them" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5811) and Muslim (261/369) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. Another example is the entry of the Bedouin man who said: "O Messenger of Allah, wealth has perished and the roads have been cut off, so ask Allah to give us rain" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1013) and Muslim (897/8) from the hadith of Anas.]]. Among its examples is the supplication of the believers. Is the supplication of the believers for those who preceded them of this type, or not? Is there a means in it? No, there is no tawassul in it. In truth, there is no tawassul in it.

The seventh: seeking a means to Allah, Exalted is He, through righteous deeds, such as the seeking of a means by the three men whom the cave closed upon. "Three men were sheltered by the night and entered a cave. Then a rock slid down and closed over them, and they were unable to move it. So they sought a means to Allah, Exalted is He, through their righteous deeds: one of them by his dutifulness to his parents, the second by his chastity, and the third by his fulfilment of trust. Then the rock was moved aside, and they came out walking" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2272) and Muslim (2743/99) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar.]]. These are the categories of permissible tawassul.

As for forbidden tawassul, its rule is that a person seeks a means to Allah through something that is not a means. This is a kind of mockery and ridicule of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because a means (wasilah) is that by which one reaches the sought goal. If you present something before your supplication while it is not a means, this becomes like mockery of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. An example is that a person seeks a means through the very person of a righteous man, saying: "O Allah, I ask You by so-and-so." Among this, according to the preferred opinion, is seeking a means through one's status (jah): "O Allah, I ask You by the status of so-and-so." This tawassul is haram, because it is a seeking of a means to Allah through what is not a means. For this reason we have prohibited a person from hanging amulets (tama'im) if they are not from the Qur'an. Why? Because they are an invalid means. Whoever seeks a means to Allah through an invalid means, his tawassul is haram.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: permission to speak openly of evil (al-jahr bil-su') for one who has been wronged. You may say: "So-and-so wronged me, so-and-so took my wealth," and similar things. This is not considered backbiting (ghibah), based on His saying: ﴿the people of which are wrongdoers﴾. Allah, blessed and exalted is He, has said: ﴿Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech except by one who has been wronged﴾ [an-Nisa' 148].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the hands of the disbelievers have authority over what is under them. That is, if a disbeliever has a land, a city, or something similar, he has authority over it, based on His saying: ﴿the people of which are wrongdoers﴾, for He made them its people. Yet in reality they are not its people, as Allah says: ﴿They were not its protectors. Its protectors are only the righteous, but most of them do not know﴾ [al-Anfal 34].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: permissibility for a person to supplicate his Lord to bring him out of the town whose people are wrongdoers, based on His saying: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers﴾. If he has the ability, let him leave. But is the meaning of ﴿whose people are wrongdoers﴾ those who transgressed against us, or those who transgressed against the right of Allah?

The apparent meaning is the first. That is, it is not permissible for a person to supplicate Allah to bring him out of the land unless its people have wronged him by preventing him from his religion and from practising it. As for when they are wrongdoers to themselves but do not harm any Muslim, emigration is not obligatory, and he should not supplicate Allah, Exalted is He, to bring him out of it unless he fears for his religion.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that a person may ask Allah, Exalted is He, for a protector from Himself, based on His saying: ﴿And make for us from Yourself a protector﴾. One should not say that you must say "O Allah, make me a protector." Rather, you either supplicate Allah that He take you as a protector, or that He facilitate a protector for you. Similarly, it is said: ﴿And make for us from Yourself a helper﴾. Know that when the protector (wali) and the helper (nasir) are combined, the protector is for what benefits and the helper is for averting what harms. When one of them is mentioned alone, it includes the other. If "protector" is said without "helper," the meaning is one who brings you good and averts evil from you. If "helper" is said without "protector," the meaning is one who averts evil and brings good. When both are combined, the protector is for one who brings good, and the helper is for one who averts evil.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the demonstration of the high aspiration of those people, when they said: ﴿from Yourself﴾ regarding the protector, and ﴿from Yourself﴾ regarding the helper. For a protector who comes from Allah, and likewise a helper, is the one who benefits. As for a protector who does not come from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, but whom zealotry and partisanship have moved, such a one may benefit or may not.

* Also in the verse: seeking a means through lordship (rububiyyah), based on His saying: ﴿Our Lord﴾. Of which of the seven types of tawassul that we mentioned is this?

* Students: Attributes.

* The Shaykh: In attributes. Supplication that includes tawassul is most often through lordship, because lordship is that by which sovereignty, creation, and management belong. Although it may come through divinity (uluhiyyah), as in "Allahumma," most often it is through lordship.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of ...﴾ [an-Nisa' 76].

* A student: Seeking a means through the status (jah) of the Prophet ﷺ and through the status of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?

* The Shaykh: As for through the status of the Prophet, it is not permissible, because it is not a means. The status of the Prophet, peace be upon him, is a lofty rank for the Messenger that does not benefit me. Do you understand? As for the status of Allah, seeking a means through it is not permissible. To whom would you seek a means?! Unless by "status" he means "face" (wajh), and says: "I seek a means through an attribute of Allah." Do you understand?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Like: "I seek refuge in Allah the Mighty and in His noble Face" [[Reported by Abu Dawud (466) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As.]].

* The student: Some scholars prohibited seeking a means through the status of Allah.

* The Shaykh: Yes, that is correct, so long as one does not intend by "status" the "face." The status of Allah is with whom?! Because status means rank with others. So-and-so has status with so-and-so, meaning a high rank. Who is higher than Allah?!

* The student: No one.

* The Shaykh: Good.

* The student: Then seeking a means through the status of Allah diminishes from His essence?

* The Shaykh: Yes, this is not permissible. But if a person intends the face, there is no harm in it, because it is from seeking a means through attributes.

* A student: Seeking a means through the testimony that there is no god but Allah, because Allah loves it and it is among the attributes of tawhid?

* The Shaykh: Seeking a means through the testimony that there is no god but Allah is from righteous deeds. As for seeking a means through "There is no god but Allah," it is from seeking a means through an attribute. Do you understand?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Who knows the difference? Seeking a means through the testimony that there is no god but Allah is from seeking a means through a righteous deed, and seeking a means through "There is no god but Allah" is from seeking a means through an attribute?

* A student: Shaykh, seeking a means through the testimony that there is no god but Allah is a means through a deed, on the basis that one testifies that there is no god but Allah...

* The Shaykh: Through a human action.

* The student: And seeking a means through "There is no god but Allah" is a means through an attribute, because it is among the attributes of Allah, blessed and exalted is He...

* The Shaykh: His singularity in divinity.

* A student: Shaykh, is (...) derived from the verse?

* The Shaykh: From where is this?

* The student: ﴿its people﴾.

* The Shaykh: Is "ahl" (people/owners) only used for possession? Is "ahl" only ever attributed to an owner?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: People of praise and glory; that is, a companion or one deserving. Do you understand? But in any case, were it not that there are sunan (established precedents) indicating otherwise, we would say this is the apparent sense: when "ahl" is attributed to a created being, "ahl" means the owner. This is the basic meaning.

As for the houses of Mecca, there is disagreement. The correct view is that they can be owned in their own right, but the land cannot be owned. Then they differed as to whether they can be owned in their structures and their benefits. The established school (madhhab) holds that they cannot be owned either in their structures or in their benefits. For this reason they prohibited the people of Mecca from renting out houses. They said: a man from Mecca may not rent out his house, and even if he rents it, he may not let another person rent it from him, because if he is wronged he cannot prevent the wrong from himself by wronging someone else.

Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, chose the permissibility of sale but not of rent. He said: sale, because he owns the building itself, so it is his property, and he may sell it. As for the benefits, people are equal in the Sacred Mosque.

The school of al-Shafi'i holds the permissibility of both sale and rent, and this is what is practised now. But hoarding them (ihtikar) is what is forbidden. That is, when the season comes, we increase their rent because people need them. This is what is forbidden.

For this reason it is regrettable that during the season of pilgrimage (in past times, though I do not know about them now) people raise the prices of consumer goods. If bread is four for a riyal, they make it two for a riyal.

* A student: Three for a riyal.

* The Shaykh: And outside the season?

* The student: Four for a riyal.

* The Shaykh: Four for a riyal. That means a quarter more, and this is contrary to the practice of the Jahiliyyah. The people of the Jahiliyyah served the pilgrims and gave them nabidh (date drink) for free.

* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands, establish prayer, and give zakah"? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a group of them fear men as they should fear Allah or even more intensely. And they say, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed for us fighting? If only You would delay us to a near term." Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, and you will not be wronged even a thread."﴾ [an-Nisa' 77].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. We have already mentioned the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the Taghut﴾ [an-Nisa' 76]. What is meant by the taghut here?

* A student: Words are known by their opposites. Here He contrasted the taghut with the cause of Allah, so whatever is not in the cause of Allah is taghut.

* The Shaykh: So it is taghut? Even if he fights out of zealous partisanship?

* The student: If he fights out of zealotry, all of that is taghut, and the taghut in its definition too...

* The Shaykh: Do you have evidence for this rule you claim? That is, another example that supports it, so that from the multiplicity of examples we can derive a rule?

* The student: Many examples have passed with us, such as His saying: ﴿So go forth in separate groups or go forth all together﴾ [an-Nisa' 71].

* The Shaykh: Yes. The word ﴿separate groups﴾ may confuse a person, but when it is joined with this, you understand it. Many things of this kind, or close to it.

From His saying: ﴿Indeed, the plan of Satan is ever weak﴾ [an-Nisa' 76] it is derived that in urging jihad one should show the weakness of the enemy. This is the opposite of what the jurists said: that one prevents the one who discourages (al-mukhadhdhil) and the one who spreads fear (al-murjif). From where? The purpose here is to incite the Muslims to fight. The opposite of that is what? The one who spreads fear says: "The enemy is strong, we have no strength against him, and we cannot face him," and similar things. I say: this is the opposite. So it is derived from this that the enemy's condition should be mentioned as weak, so that the person's resolve is strengthened and his side grows stronger.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse, ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah﴾: showing that faith entails sincerity (ikhlas), based on His saying: ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah﴾. We can analogize the rest of the righteous deeds to this. Those who believe seek knowledge to preserve the Shari'ah of Allah and spread it among the servants of Allah. Those who believe worship Allah, Exalted is He, through prayer, charity, and other things, seeking nearness to Allah. The opposite of this is the case of those who disbelieve.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: praise of the believers for their sincerity, because Allah related this as praise of them.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: showing that whoever fights outside the cause of Allah has in him a trait of disbelief, based on His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the Taghut﴾. Even if he is a believer who prays, fasts, pays zakah, and performs Hajj, if he fights out of zealotry or partisanship, there is in him a resemblance to the disbelievers and a trait of disbelief.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation of fighting the allies of Satan. From where is this derived?

* A student: From ﴿So fight the allies of Satan﴾.

* The Shaykh: From His saying: ﴿So fight the allies of Satan﴾. So Allah, Exalted is He, commanded fighting the allies of Satan.

Benefits of this noble verse: mentioning what motivates compliance, which is drawn from His words ﴿the allies of Satan﴾, because in it there is encouragement and incitement to fight them.

Another benefit of this noble verse: that the disbelievers who wage war are among the allies of Satan, based on His words ﴿the allies of Satan﴾. And how were they his allies? We have already explained this: they comply with his commands and his prohibitions. If he commands them to indecency, they comply; if he forbids them from righteousness, they comply. By this they became his allies.

Another benefit of this noble verse: the demonstration of the weakness of Satan, or, in more general terms, the demonstration of the weakness of what Satan does, whether by scheming or otherwise. For if his scheming is weak, then what he does not scheme with is weaker still, based on His words ﴿Indeed, the scheming of Satan is ever weak﴾.

Another benefit of this noble verse: a person should not fear or be afraid of the allies of Satan, because the allies of Satan are weak, just as Satan, who is their patron, has weak scheming.

Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan schemes against the human being, based on His words ﴿Indeed, the scheming of Satan﴾. So beware of his scheming, and do not let him deceive you. Perhaps he whispers to you to neglect the required worship, or to engage in forbidden acts of disobedience, and says: "Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, the matter is easy; do it and repent," until he schemes against you and you fall into his traps. So beware of his scheming.

**Part 1 of 3**

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verses 75–76

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan (Satan). ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah and [for] the oppressed men, women, and children who say, "Our Lord, take us out of this city whose people are oppressors, and appoint for us from Yourself a protector, and appoint for us from Yourself a helper"? (75) Those who believe fight in the way of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the way of Taghut (false deities). So fight against the allies of Shaytan. Indeed, the plot of Shaytan is ever weak.﴾ [An-Nisa' 75–76].

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. When Allah the Exalted and Glorified commanded fighting in the way of Allah, He directed the command to those who sell (yashrun) the worldly life for the Hereafter; that is, they sell the worldly life for the Hereafter. He also explained the virtue of fighting in the way of Allah, and that the one who fights in the way of Allah, whether he is killed or victorious, has a reward from Allah: ﴿And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed or conquers, We will give him a great reward﴾ [An-Nisa' 74]. Allah then rebuked those who refrain from fighting, saying: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah﴾. The word "ma" here is interrogative, and its meaning is disapproval (inkar). It may also carry both disapproval and wonder; that is, its meaning is a rebuke of those who did not fight, and an expression of amazement at their condition.

As for His saying ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, it has been explained many times before: fighting in the way of Allah is fighting so that the word of Allah alone is supreme.

His saying ﴿and [for] the oppressed men﴾ may be conjoined to the word "Allah" (in the phrase "the way of Allah"), meaning: "and in the way of the oppressed." It may also be conjoined to the word "way" (sabil), meaning: "and for the oppressed men." Both meanings flow into one channel, whether we say "in the way of the oppressed" or "for the oppressed themselves." The oppressed men are those who cannot leave this city which subjects them to a wretched torment.

﴿And [for] the women﴾ is conjoined either to "the oppressed" or to "the men." Which is preferable? If we say it is conjoined to "the men," the meaning is that women are divided into two groups: an oppressed group and a group that is not oppressed, and the verse refers to the oppressed group. If we say it is conjoined to "the oppressed," then women are not divided into two groups but are one category, and a woman is not obliged to emigrate. But the first meaning is better, because among women there are those who emigrated and did not remain in the abode of humiliation and degradation.

His saying ﴿and [for] the children﴾: this is the one that we can say is conjoined to His saying "the oppressed." This is because children cannot emigrate or leave, and they are wronged in these places; they have no strategy and cannot find a way. So it is an obligation upon us to fight in the way of Allah the Exalted, and for these oppressed men, women, and children.

His saying ﴿who say, "Our Lord, take us out"﴾: ﴿who﴾ is an adjective (sifa) describing everything preceding it, both the conjoined and the conjoined-to. ﴿say﴾ means each one of them says it, or the verb "say" is used in the sense of the group, even though this statement was not uttered by each individual; this is because a group that shares one goal and one path, the statement of one of them is considered the statement of all.

﴿Our Lord, take us out of this city﴾: the pointed-to city is the one they inhabit and remain in, and it is Makkah, because the Quraysh subjected whoever embraced Islam to a wretched torment.

His saying ﴿whose people are oppressors﴾: ﴿oppressors﴾ here is a descriptive adjective (na't). For what?

Student: For "city."

Student: For "its people" (ahl).

Shaykh: For the demonstrative in ﴿this﴾. But how can it be an adjective when the meaning belongs to other than the described noun? Because He said ﴿whose people are oppressors﴾ and did not say "oppressive" (feminine)?

The answer to this is that the adjective is of two types: the real (haqiqi) and the causative (sababi).

The real adjective is one where the attribute returns to the described noun, as when you say: "I passed by Zayd the virtuous." Here "virtuous" is an attribute returning to whom? To Zayd.

The causative adjective is one where the attribute returns to other than the described noun, but has a connection to it, as when you say: "I passed by Zayd, whose father is virtuous." Here the virtue does not return to Zayd but to his father, yet there is a relation and link between them, and therefore it was attributed to him, so it is said "his father." The pronoun in "his father" returns to Zayd. ﴿whose people are oppressors﴾ belongs to this category. Is the adjective here causative or real?

Student: Causative.

Shaykh: Causative. ﴿whose people are oppressors﴾. Accordingly we say: ﴿oppressors﴾ is an adjective of ﴿this﴾, and "people" (ahl) is the agent of the active participle "oppressors." ﴿oppressors﴾ is an active participle, and ﴿its people﴾: "people" is the agent, "people" is in construct form, and "ha'" (its) is the genitive pronoun attached to it.

Why are they oppressors in ﴿whose people are oppressors﴾? Is the intended oppression the aggression against the rights of these believers, or is it something more general, such as their wronging through polytheism and also aggression?

Student: The second.

Shaykh: The second. The people of this city are oppressors with respect to the right of Allah, by associating others with Him, and Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Indeed, association [of others with Allah] is a great injustice﴾ [Luqman 13]. These people are also oppressors with respect to their aggression against these believers, since they used to harm them and subject them to a wretched torment.

﴿And appoint for us from Yourself a protector﴾: the "wa" here is a conjunctive particle, and ﴿appoint﴾ is conjoined to ﴿take us out﴾. That is, they also say: ﴿appoint for us from Yourself﴾, meaning "from Your presence," ﴿a protector﴾, and ﴿appoint for us from Yourself a helper﴾. "Appoint for us a protector" means one who takes charge of us, who manages our affairs, and ﴿helper﴾ means one who supports us against our enemies.

Notice that the word ﴿appoint﴾ came twice, because the setting is one of supplication, and the setting of supplication calls for expansiveness, because the supplicant is communicating intimately with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The intimate speech of a beloved with his beloved, the more it increases, the stronger the love becomes. For this reason, you find that when a person loves someone, he wishes to speak with him at length, and sometimes he sits talking with him for a long period, which seems to him far shorter than it is.

﴿And appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper﴾. The helper (nasir) is the one who defends and repels your enemy from attacking you.

If someone says: Doesn't "protection" (wilaya) also come with the meaning of "support"?

We say: Yes. But, as we mentioned before, the setting of supplication calls for expansiveness.

* * *

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿Those who believe fight in the way of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the way of Taghut. So fight against the allies of Shaytan. Indeed, the plot of Shaytan is ever weak (76). Have you not considered those who were told, "Restrain your hands, establish prayer, and give zakah"? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a faction of them fear men as they should fear Allah or with greater fear, and say, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed for us fighting? If only You would delay us to a near term." Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, and you will not be wronged even a [thread of] date-fiber"﴾ [An-Nisa' 76–77].

Shaykh: We seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan.

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah and [for] the oppressed﴾. What type of interrogation is this here?

Student: Disapproving (inkari), and it may be disapproval and wonder.

Shaykh: Yes, disapproval and wonder.

His saying ﴿and [for] the oppressed men﴾ is conjoined to what?

Student: (...) conjoined to the word "Allah."

Shaykh: Yes indeed. And what would the estimated (taqdir) construction be?

Student: "In the way of Allah and in the way of the oppressed."

Shaykh: Or conjoined to "way"?

Student: (...) Allah, and the oppressed men.

Shaykh: That is: "and in [the rescue of] the oppressed, to free them."

Good. What is meant by "city" in His saying ﴿the city whose people are oppressors﴾?

Student: Makkah.

Shaykh: Makkah. Is there evidence that it is Makkah?

Student: From the verse?

Shaykh: Yes, from the verse or from outside the verse.

Student: The reality, O Shaykh, at the time the verses were revealed.

Shaykh: Is there not a verse that indicates this?

Student: Another verse?

Shaykh: Yes.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: No.

Student: ﴿And how many a city was stronger in power than your city﴾... [Muhammad 13].

Shaykh: Well done, exactly.

His saying ﴿and appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper﴾: what is the difference between the protector (wali) and the helper (nasir)?

Student: The protector is the one who takes charge of a person's affairs, the guardian of affairs.

Shaykh: By bringing him benefit and warding off...?

Student: Harm.

Shaykh: And the helper?

Student: The helper is the one who assists you and supports you.

Shaykh: Yes. That is, he also prevents His enemies from him, because victory (nasr) means prevention, as in His saying: ﴿So who will protect us from the might of Allah if it should come to us?﴾ [Ghafir 29].

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those who believe fight in the way of Allah.﴾ When Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, rebuked and expressed wonder at those who do not fight in the way of Allah, He clarified that the fighters are divided into two groups, saying: ﴿Those who believe fight in the way of Allah.﴾ This is a sentence composed of a subject and a predicate: the subject is ﴿those who﴾ and the predicate is ﴿fight﴾.

His saying ﴿fight in the way of Allah﴾ means: they fight the disbelievers.

His saying ﴿in the way of Allah﴾ means: in His religion and His law; that is, for His sake. The Prophet (ﷺ) clarified fighting in the way of Allah: it is the fighting of one who fights so that the word of Allah is supreme. This is fighting in the way of Allah, and whatever else is not in the way of Allah.

﴿And those who disbelieve fight in the way of Taghut.﴾ This sentence is composed of a subject and a predicate: the subject is ﴿those who﴾, and the predicate is the clause ﴿fight in the way of Taghut.﴾

﴿Taghut﴾ is an intensive form (sigha mubalagha) from transgression (tughyan). The ta' in it is like the ta' in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was a [whole] nation﴾ [An-Nahl 120]; the ta' is for intensification. Just as they say: "So-and-so is an 'allama" (one who knows very much), the ta' is also for intensification. Accordingly, the last letter of the word, that is, the last of its root letters, is the waw in "taghut," and the ta' is an added letter for intensification. Who is the Taghut?

The meaning is known by mentioning its opposite. The Taghut is the opposite of the one who fights in the way of Allah. So everyone who fights for other than the way of Allah is fighting in the way of Taghut, whether we say it is Shaytan, or the allies of Shaytan, or tribal partisanship, or something else. The important point is that we understand that what is meant by "the way of Taghut" is whatever is for other than the way of Allah, by way of contrast. We have already had a useful principle regarding this: a thing may be known by knowing its opposite. We have already encountered from it His saying: ﴿So go forth in separate groups or go forth all together﴾ [An-Nisa' 71].
