And His saying ﴿Taghut﴾ means: everything by which a person exceeds his limit, is transgression and taghut.

﴿So fight against the allies of Shaytan.﴾ The fa' is for consequence based on what preceded; that is: fight, O fighters in the way of Allah, against the allies of Shaytan, who have taken Shaytan as a protector, so he deceived and misguided them, and they are those who fight not so that the word of Allah is supreme.

﴿Indeed, the plot of Shaytan is ever weak.﴾ When He commanded fighting against the allies of Shaytan, He clarified that they are overcome, and that the fighter against the allies of Shaytan is victorious. This is derived from the reasoning in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the plot of Shaytan is ever weak.﴾ If his plot is weak, then he has no ability to oppose the truth.

His saying ﴿Indeed, the plot of Shaytan﴾: if the plot of Shaytan is weak, while it is that which comes by way of deceit and trickery, then what is open is even more so. Shaytan has plots and schemes; he plots against man, but he is weak. When Allah is mentioned, he withdraws. Otherwise, he plots even outside of fighting. He plots against man in acts of worship: he first approaches him through negligence in worship, making it seem easy to him, and says: "If you leave it this time, you can do it another time." Then when he intends to do it another time, he whispers to him and discourages him. He makes disobedience seem trivial to him, saying: "This is a minor sin, and no one sees you; there is no one with you but Allah, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful," and similar things. So he makes it easy for him and beautifies it through his scheming. Nevertheless, his plot is weak, because it never withstands the truth.

* There are several issues and benefits in this verse.

* First: a clarification that people are divided into two groups regarding jihad...

Student: The previous verse, O Shaykh.

Shaykh: The previous one? ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight﴾?

* ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight﴾ contains benefits:
* First: a rebuke of those who are negligent in jihad, based on His saying: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah﴾.
* Among its benefits also: mentioning what encourages fighting from the psychological side, based on His saying: ﴿and [for] the oppressed men, women, and children﴾, because mentioning what stirs a person and rouses him is something desirable. Without doubt, when a person is told that there are oppressed men, children, and women, he will certainly increase in resolve and readiness.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the disbelievers have oppressed these people and humiliated them.
* Among its benefits: the obligation to defend the oppressed against the disbelievers, because Allah the Exalted rebuked for two matters: for abandoning fighting in the way of Allah, and for abandoning fighting in the way of these oppressed people to free them. This is an obligation upon every Muslim who has the ability: to free the captive Muslims and to lift the oppression from them to the extent of his capacity, based on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [At-Taghabun 16].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of seeking a means (tawassul) through a state of affairs, based on His saying: ﴿take us out of this city whose people are oppressors﴾. They sought a means to Allah the Exalted by mentioning the condition of the people of this city, that they are oppressors toward them. Mentioning a condition, that a person is wronged, creates tenderness and compassion.

Know that seeking a means to Allah the Mighty and Majestic can be done through several matters:

The first matter: seeking a means to Allah through His names, based on His saying: ﴿And to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so invoke Him by them﴾ [Al-A'raf 180]. So you say: "O Forgiving, forgive me," and "O Merciful, have mercy on me." Here, it is fitting, out of good manners, intelligence, and discernment, that one should not seek a means for a matter except through the name suitable to it. If he wants to ask Allah for forgiveness, he seeks a means through what? Through "the Forgiving." Provision, through "the Provider." Seizing the wrongdoer, through "the Severe in punishment," and similar things.

The second: seeking a means to Allah the Exalted through His attributes, including what is in the transmitted hadith: "O Allah, by Your mercy I seek help" [1]. This is a means to Allah the Exalted through one of His attributes. Likewise: "O Allah, by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation, cause me to live if You know life is good for me" [2]. Likewise: "O Allah, I seek Your choice by Your knowledge, and I seek Your power by Your power" [3].

[1] Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (3524) from the hadith of Anas, with the wording: "O Living, O Self-Subsisting, by Your mercy I seek help."
[2] Recorded by al-Nasa'i in al-Mujtaba (1305) from the hadith of 'Ammar ibn Yasir.
[3] Recorded by al-Bukhari (1162) from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah.

The third: seeking a means (tawassul) to God through His actions. Actions are a type distinct from attributes, even though they are sometimes counted among them. An example is your saying: "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim." The correct view is that the particle *kaf* here indicates cause (ta'lil), meaning: "because You sent blessings upon Ibrahim." It is not strange for *kaf* to indicate cause. It does so in His saying: ﴿And remember Him as He has guided you﴾ [al-Baqarah 198], meaning "because of His guiding you," according to one of the two interpretations. When we say that the *kaf* in "kama sallayta 'ala Ibrahim" [[Reported by al-Bukhari (3370) from the hadith of Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, and (4798) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]] is causal, the difficulty that many scholars raise is removed. That difficulty is how one could liken the blessing upon Muhammad ﷺ to the blessing upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim, when Muhammad and his family are more excellent than Ibrahim and his family. If we take the *kaf* as causal, the difficulty disappears. If we take it as comparative, which is not valid but is considered for argument's sake, then according to some scholars this is a case of mentioning the blessing upon the Prophet ﷺ twice: once as a request, and once as a report. The request is "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad," and the report is "as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim" [[Reported by al-Bukhari (3370) from the hadith of Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah.]]. Muhammad is undoubtedly from the family of Ibrahim, by lineage and by following him, as Allah, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, the most worthy of Ibrahim among the people are those who followed him, and this Prophet and those who believed﴾ [Al 'Imran 68]. So he is of his family ﷺ by lineage and by following. But what we mentioned first, what category is it? It is seeking a means to Allah through His actions, which is preferable.

The fourth: seeking a means to Allah through the state of the supplicant. That is, a person mentions his condition to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and presents it. Mentioning a state that calls for compassion and kindness is a means of tawassul. Among its examples is the saying of Musa, peace be upon him: ﴿My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need﴾ [al-Qasas 24].

The fifth: seeking a means to Allah through faith in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger. Among its examples is His saying: ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire"﴾ [Al 'Imran 16].

The sixth: seeking a means to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, through the supplication of the righteous. That is, a person seeks a means to Allah through the supplication of a righteous man, such as the saying of 'Ukkasha ibn Mihsan: "Ask Allah to make me one of them." He said: "You are one of them" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5811) and Muslim (261/369) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. Another example is the entry of the Bedouin man who said: "O Messenger of Allah, wealth has perished and the roads have been cut off, so ask Allah to give us rain" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1013) and Muslim (897/8) from the hadith of Anas.]]. Among its examples is the supplication of the believers. Is the supplication of the believers for those who preceded them of this type, or not? Is there a means in it? No, there is no tawassul in it. In truth, there is no tawassul in it.

The seventh: seeking a means to Allah, Exalted is He, through righteous deeds, such as the seeking of a means by the three men whom the cave closed upon. "Three men were sheltered by the night and entered a cave. Then a rock slid down and closed over them, and they were unable to move it. So they sought a means to Allah, Exalted is He, through their righteous deeds: one of them by his dutifulness to his parents, the second by his chastity, and the third by his fulfilment of trust. Then the rock was moved aside, and they came out walking" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2272) and Muslim (2743/99) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar.]]. These are the categories of permissible tawassul.

As for forbidden tawassul, its rule is that a person seeks a means to Allah through something that is not a means. This is a kind of mockery and ridicule of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because a means (wasilah) is that by which one reaches the sought goal. If you present something before your supplication while it is not a means, this becomes like mockery of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. An example is that a person seeks a means through the very person of a righteous man, saying: "O Allah, I ask You by so-and-so." Among this, according to the preferred opinion, is seeking a means through one's status (jah): "O Allah, I ask You by the status of so-and-so." This tawassul is haram, because it is a seeking of a means to Allah through what is not a means. For this reason we have prohibited a person from hanging amulets (tama'im) if they are not from the Qur'an. Why? Because they are an invalid means. Whoever seeks a means to Allah through an invalid means, his tawassul is haram.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: permission to speak openly of evil (al-jahr bil-su') for one who has been wronged. You may say: "So-and-so wronged me, so-and-so took my wealth," and similar things. This is not considered backbiting (ghibah), based on His saying: ﴿the people of which are wrongdoers﴾. Allah, blessed and exalted is He, has said: ﴿Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech except by one who has been wronged﴾ [an-Nisa' 148].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the hands of the disbelievers have authority over what is under them. That is, if a disbeliever has a land, a city, or something similar, he has authority over it, based on His saying: ﴿the people of which are wrongdoers﴾, for He made them its people. Yet in reality they are not its people, as Allah says: ﴿They were not its protectors. Its protectors are only the righteous, but most of them do not know﴾ [al-Anfal 34].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: permissibility for a person to supplicate his Lord to bring him out of the town whose people are wrongdoers, based on His saying: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers﴾. If he has the ability, let him leave. But is the meaning of ﴿whose people are wrongdoers﴾ those who transgressed against us, or those who transgressed against the right of Allah?

The apparent meaning is the first. That is, it is not permissible for a person to supplicate Allah to bring him out of the land unless its people have wronged him by preventing him from his religion and from practising it. As for when they are wrongdoers to themselves but do not harm any Muslim, emigration is not obligatory, and he should not supplicate Allah, Exalted is He, to bring him out of it unless he fears for his religion.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that a person may ask Allah, Exalted is He, for a protector from Himself, based on His saying: ﴿And make for us from Yourself a protector﴾. One should not say that you must say "O Allah, make me a protector." Rather, you either supplicate Allah that He take you as a protector, or that He facilitate a protector for you. Similarly, it is said: ﴿And make for us from Yourself a helper﴾. Know that when the protector (wali) and the helper (nasir) are combined, the protector is for what benefits and the helper is for averting what harms. When one of them is mentioned alone, it includes the other. If "protector" is said without "helper," the meaning is one who brings you good and averts evil from you. If "helper" is said without "protector," the meaning is one who averts evil and brings good. When both are combined, the protector is for one who brings good, and the helper is for one who averts evil.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the demonstration of the high aspiration of those people, when they said: ﴿from Yourself﴾ regarding the protector, and ﴿from Yourself﴾ regarding the helper. For a protector who comes from Allah, and likewise a helper, is the one who benefits. As for a protector who does not come from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, but whom zealotry and partisanship have moved, such a one may benefit or may not.

* Also in the verse: seeking a means through lordship (rububiyyah), based on His saying: ﴿Our Lord﴾. Of which of the seven types of tawassul that we mentioned is this?

* Students: Attributes.

* The Shaykh: In attributes. Supplication that includes tawassul is most often through lordship, because lordship is that by which sovereignty, creation, and management belong. Although it may come through divinity (uluhiyyah), as in "Allahumma," most often it is through lordship.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of ...﴾ [an-Nisa' 76].

* A student: Seeking a means through the status (jah) of the Prophet ﷺ and through the status of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?

* The Shaykh: As for through the status of the Prophet, it is not permissible, because it is not a means. The status of the Prophet, peace be upon him, is a lofty rank for the Messenger that does not benefit me. Do you understand? As for the status of Allah, seeking a means through it is not permissible. To whom would you seek a means?! Unless by "status" he means "face" (wajh), and says: "I seek a means through an attribute of Allah." Do you understand?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Like: "I seek refuge in Allah the Mighty and in His noble Face" [[Reported by Abu Dawud (466) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As.]].

* The student: Some scholars prohibited seeking a means through the status of Allah.

* The Shaykh: Yes, that is correct, so long as one does not intend by "status" the "face." The status of Allah is with whom?! Because status means rank with others. So-and-so has status with so-and-so, meaning a high rank. Who is higher than Allah?!

* The student: No one.

* The Shaykh: Good.

* The student: Then seeking a means through the status of Allah diminishes from His essence?

* The Shaykh: Yes, this is not permissible. But if a person intends the face, there is no harm in it, because it is from seeking a means through attributes.

* A student: Seeking a means through the testimony that there is no god but Allah, because Allah loves it and it is among the attributes of tawhid?

* The Shaykh: Seeking a means through the testimony that there is no god but Allah is from righteous deeds. As for seeking a means through "There is no god but Allah," it is from seeking a means through an attribute. Do you understand?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Who knows the difference? Seeking a means through the testimony that there is no god but Allah is from seeking a means through a righteous deed, and seeking a means through "There is no god but Allah" is from seeking a means through an attribute?

* A student: Shaykh, seeking a means through the testimony that there is no god but Allah is a means through a deed, on the basis that one testifies that there is no god but Allah...

* The Shaykh: Through a human action.

* The student: And seeking a means through "There is no god but Allah" is a means through an attribute, because it is among the attributes of Allah, blessed and exalted is He...

* The Shaykh: His singularity in divinity.

* A student: Shaykh, is (...) derived from the verse?

* The Shaykh: From where is this?

* The student: ﴿its people﴾.

* The Shaykh: Is "ahl" (people/owners) only used for possession? Is "ahl" only ever attributed to an owner?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: People of praise and glory; that is, a companion or one deserving. Do you understand? But in any case, were it not that there are sunan (established precedents) indicating otherwise, we would say this is the apparent sense: when "ahl" is attributed to a created being, "ahl" means the owner. This is the basic meaning.

As for the houses of Mecca, there is disagreement. The correct view is that they can be owned in their own right, but the land cannot be owned. Then they differed as to whether they can be owned in their structures and their benefits. The established school (madhhab) holds that they cannot be owned either in their structures or in their benefits. For this reason they prohibited the people of Mecca from renting out houses. They said: a man from Mecca may not rent out his house, and even if he rents it, he may not let another person rent it from him, because if he is wronged he cannot prevent the wrong from himself by wronging someone else.

Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, chose the permissibility of sale but not of rent. He said: sale, because he owns the building itself, so it is his property, and he may sell it. As for the benefits, people are equal in the Sacred Mosque.

The school of al-Shafi'i holds the permissibility of both sale and rent, and this is what is practised now. But hoarding them (ihtikar) is what is forbidden. That is, when the season comes, we increase their rent because people need them. This is what is forbidden.

For this reason it is regrettable that during the season of pilgrimage (in past times, though I do not know about them now) people raise the prices of consumer goods. If bread is four for a riyal, they make it two for a riyal.

* A student: Three for a riyal.

* The Shaykh: And outside the season?

* The student: Four for a riyal.

* The Shaykh: Four for a riyal. That means a quarter more, and this is contrary to the practice of the Jahiliyyah. The people of the Jahiliyyah served the pilgrims and gave them nabidh (date drink) for free.

Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, chose the permissibility of sale but not of rent. He said: sale, because he sometimes owns the building, so it is his property, and he may sell it. As for the benefits, people are equal in the Sacred Mosque.

The school of al-Shafi'i: the permissibility of both sale and rent, and this is what is practised now. But hoarding them is what is forbidden, meaning that when the season comes we increase their rent, because people need them. This is what is forbidden. For this reason it is regrettable that during the season (in past times, though I do not know about them now) people raise the prices of consumer goods. If bread is four for a riyal, they make it two for a riyal.

* A student: Three for a riyal.

* The Shaykh: And outside the season?

* The student: Four for a riyal.

* The Shaykh: Four for a riyal, yes indeed. I seek refuge in Allah! Normally, if it is sold for three riyals in the season, how much is it sold for outside the season?

* A student: Four riyals.

* The Shaykh: Four riyals. That means a quarter more, and this is contrary to the practice of the Jahiliyyah. The people of the Jahiliyyah served the pilgrims and gave them nabidh for free.

* * *

* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands, establish prayer, and give zakah"? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a group of them fear men as they should fear Allah or even more intensely. And they say, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed for us fighting? If only You would delay us to a near term." Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, and you will not be wronged even a thread."﴾ [an-Nisa' 77].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. We have already mentioned the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the Taghut﴾ [an-Nisa' 76]. What is meant by the taghut here?

* A student: Words are known by their opposites. Here He contrasted the taghut with the cause of Allah, so whatever is not in the cause of Allah is taghut.

* The Shaykh: So it is taghut? Even if he fights out of zealous partisanship?

* The student: If he fights out of zealotry, all of that is taghut, and the taghut in its definition too...

* The Shaykh: Do you have evidence for this rule you claim? That is, another example that supports it, so that from the multiplicity of examples we can derive a rule?

* The student: Many examples have passed with us, such as His saying: ﴿So go forth in separate groups or go forth all together﴾ [an-Nisa' 71].

* The Shaykh: Yes. The word ﴿separate groups﴾ may confuse a person, but when it is joined with this, you understand it. Many things of this kind, or close to it.

From His saying: ﴿Indeed, the plan of Satan is ever weak﴾ [an-Nisa' 76] it is derived that in urging jihad one should show the weakness of the enemy. This is the opposite of what the jurists said: that one prevents the one who discourages (al-mukhadhdhil) and the one who spreads fear (al-murjif). From where? The purpose here is to incite the Muslims to fight. The opposite of that is what? The one who spreads fear says: "The enemy is strong, we have no strength against him, and we cannot face him," and similar things. I say: this is the opposite. So it is derived from this that the enemy's condition should be mentioned as weak, so that the person's resolve is strengthened and his side grows stronger.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse, ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah﴾: showing that faith entails sincerity (ikhlas), based on His saying: ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah﴾. We can analogize the rest of the righteous deeds to this. Those who believe seek knowledge to preserve the Shari'ah of Allah and spread it among the servants of Allah. Those who believe worship Allah, Exalted is He, through prayer, charity, and other things, seeking nearness to Allah. The opposite of this is the case of those who disbelieve.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: praise of the believers for their sincerity, because Allah related this as praise of them.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: showing that whoever fights outside the cause of Allah has in him a trait of disbelief, based on His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the Taghut﴾. Even if he is a believer who prays, fasts, pays zakah, and performs Hajj, if he fights out of zealotry or partisanship, there is in him a resemblance to the disbelievers and a trait of disbelief.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation of fighting the allies of Satan. From where is this derived?

* A student: From ﴿So fight the allies of Satan﴾.

* The Shaykh: From His saying: ﴿So fight the allies of Satan﴾. So Allah, Exalted is He, commanded fighting the allies of Satan.

Benefits of this noble verse: mentioning what motivates compliance, which is drawn from His words ﴿the allies of Satan﴾, because in it there is encouragement and incitement to fight them.

Another benefit of this noble verse: that the disbelievers who wage war are among the allies of Satan, based on His words ﴿the allies of Satan﴾. And how were they his allies? We have already explained this: they comply with his commands and his prohibitions. If he commands them to indecency, they comply; if he forbids them from righteousness, they comply. By this they became his allies.

Another benefit of this noble verse: the demonstration of the weakness of Satan, or, in more general terms, the demonstration of the weakness of what Satan does, whether by scheming or otherwise. For if his scheming is weak, then what he does not scheme with is weaker still, based on His words ﴿Indeed, the scheming of Satan is ever weak﴾.

Another benefit of this noble verse: a person should not fear or be afraid of the allies of Satan, because the allies of Satan are weak, just as Satan, who is their patron, has weak scheming.

Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan schemes against the human being, based on His words ﴿Indeed, the scheming of Satan﴾. So beware of his scheming, and do not let him deceive you. Perhaps he whispers to you to neglect the required worship, or to engage in forbidden acts of disobedience, and says: "Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, the matter is easy; do it and repent," until he schemes against you and you fall into his traps. So beware of his scheming.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 77 (part 1 of 3):

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Have you not seen those to whom it was said, "Restrain your hands"?﴾ and so on to the end. The interrogative here is an interrogative of wonder; that is, marvel at the state of these people.

His words ﴿seen﴾ may be a seeing of knowledge or a seeing of sight, and the apparent meaning is that it is a seeing of knowledge; that is, be amazed at the state of these people with your heart and your thinking.

﴿Have you not seen those to whom it was said, "Restrain your hands"?﴾ The one who said it is not specified, and the apparent meaning is that it was the Prophet (ﷺ).

His words ﴿Restrain your hands﴾ mean: withhold them from fighting. This is because some of the Companions who were in Makkah, when the Quraysh wronged them and restricted them, said: "Shall we not fight them? Why do they confine us and wrong us? Shall we not fight them?" So it was said to them: ﴿Restrain your hands﴾, do not fight them, because fighting out of its proper place is destruction. So do not fight them; restrain your hands. You know that the people in Makkah were oppressed and wronged, having no strength and no state, so fighting was absolutely unfitting. Therefore it was said to them: ﴿Restrain your hands﴾, that is, from fighting. The proof that what is meant is from fighting is the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah﴾ [al-Fath 24], that is, He restrained them from fighting, ﴿Restrain your hands﴾.

﴿And establish the prayer and give zakah﴾: that is, perform the particular acts of worship which involve neither fighting nor jihad.

﴿Establish the prayer﴾: this is an act of worship specific to the person, which does not extend to others.

﴿And give zakah﴾: this is an act of worship which extends to others, yet it is still worship. Zakah, for example, is not meant merely as kindness to the poor; the most important thing in it is to worship Allah by spending of what one loves, which is wealth, in order to attain what is sought. For this reason whoever understands from zakah that it is intended only as mere benefit to the entitled ones is mistaken; that is not the aim. The aim is worship of Allah by giving up what you love, and all of us love wealth, as Allah said: ﴿And you love wealth with immense love﴾ [al-Fajr 20], and He said: ﴿And indeed, he is intense in his love of good [wealth]﴾ [al-'Adiyat 8].

So He says: ﴿Establish the prayer﴾, which is a particular act of worship that does not extend beyond the person. ﴿And give zakah﴾, which is an act of worship that extends beyond him. The prayer is well known; it is worship, or the worship of Allah, the Exalted, through known sayings and actions, opened with the takbir and concluded with the taslim. Here you must add to the definitions that the jurists gave for acts of worship the element of worship of Allah. In the books of the jurists we find, for example: "Prayer is known sayings and actions." That is not sufficient, because if a person were to say these sayings and do these actions without worshipping Allah, it would not become prayer. So what must we add? Worship of Allah through known sayings and actions, opened with the takbir and concluded with the taslim.

Second: zakah. We say: it is worship of Allah by giving up a portion of wealth in a specific, known manner from the Sunnah.

As for His words ﴿give zakah﴾: we know that (ātā, to give) takes two objects. Their origin is?
* Students: Their origin is not subject and predicate.
* The Shaykh: Their origin is not subject and predicate; rather it is of the type of (kasā, to clothe). Thus in ﴿give zakah﴾ the second object is omitted; the estimate is: its recipients, or its people.

﴿So when fighting was prescribed for them﴾: that is, when it was obligated. Writing (al-katb) here means obligation, as in His words: ﴿O you who have believed, fasting has been prescribed for you﴾ [al-Baqarah 183], and His words: ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times﴾ [an-Nisa' 103], that is, an obligation. ﴿Was prescribed﴾ means obligated. And when was it obligated?

It was obligated when the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions migrated to Madinah, and when they had a state and strength they were commanded to wage jihad, and ﴿Permission has been given to those who are being fought because they were wronged, and indeed, Allah is competent to give them victory﴾ [al-Hajj 39]. The obligation of jihad was in the second year after the Hijrah; jihad was obligated upon the Muslims. ﴿When fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a faction of them feared men as they should fear Allah or with greater fear﴾ [an-Nisa' 77].

﴿A faction of them﴾: from whom? From those who had asked to fight while they were in Makkah. When fighting was prescribed for them in Madinah, a group of them held back, and the resolve they had in Makkah departed. ﴿A faction of them﴾: that is, a group of them.

﴿They fear men as they should fear Allah or with greater fear﴾: "fear" (yakhshawna) means they are afraid of them and guard against them.

﴿As they should fear Allah﴾: that is, as they fear Allah. For this reason we ask: is this verbal noun (maṣdar) added to its object or to its subject?
* Students: To its object.
* The Shaykh: To its object; the estimate is: as their fear of Allah.

﴿Or with greater fear﴾: ﴿or﴾ is a conjunction. But is it for doubt, or for distribution, or for correction? As for doubt, no, why? Because doubt cannot occur in the information of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; Allah has knowledge, whereas a person doubts and says: "This is like that, or better." Is it for distribution, meaning that some of them fear men as they fear Allah and some fear men with greater fear? That is possible. Or is it for correction, meaning: "Rather, with greater fear"? That is also possible. Or is it for confirming what preceded?

That too is possible. For this reason, when Allah said: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾ [as-Saffat 147], the scholars said: how can it be ﴿or more﴾? Does Allah not know? He, Mighty and Majestic, knows that they are a specific number, so how did He say ﴿or more﴾? We say: there is no doubt here; ﴿or﴾ is definitely not for doubt. Some said it is for correction, meaning "rather, they are more." Others said it is for confirming what preceded, as you say: "This is like that, if it is not like it then it is higher than it," for example. So ﴿or﴾ is for confirming what preceded. As for distribution in the verse ﴿We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾, it does not apply, because it is a single group, and distribution is not possible in it.

In any case, ﴿or﴾ in a context like this cannot be taken to mean doubt, because doubt cannot occur in the report of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿Or with greater fear﴾: that is, with higher and greater fear. Know that fear (khashyah) and dread (khawf) are near-synonyms, meaning that one of the two words (that is, one of the two terms) often comes in the place of the other. But they said there is a subtle difference between them. Among the differences: khashyah is based on knowledge, unlike khawf, which may arise from illusion without any reality. Khashyah is from knowledge. A person may see a shadow from afar and think it is an enemy, and so he fears it. Do we say this is khawf or khashyah? Khawf, because it is based on illusion; it may be a tree, not an enemy. But when he sees that it is an enemy, armed, then he fears it with khashyah. They cited for their view the words of Allah: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah﴾ [Fatir 28].

It was objected to them with the words of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ [an-Nahl 50], where there is khawf. It was answered that His words ﴿above them﴾ prevent this fear from being an illusion; rather it is fear from knowledge. Likewise they said: khashyah arises from the greatness of the one feared, while khawf arises either from the greatness of the one feared or from the weakness of the one fearing. Accordingly, if a boy of seven years fears a boy of ten years, do we say this is khashyah or khawf? Khawf, because the ten-year-old is weak and not to be feared, but because of the weakness of the seven-year-old he fears him. So we say this is khawf, not khashyah. The khashyah of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is khashyah without doubt, because it stems from the greatness of the One feared, the Mighty and Majestic, and everything other than Allah is weak in comparison to Him, as Allah said: ﴿As for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the land without right and said, "Who is mightier than us in strength?" Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength?﴾ [Fussilat 15].

They also said: khashyah is stronger than khawf, and they cited for this etymology, saying: the letters shin, ya', and kha' in all their derivations indicate harshness. From it comes (al-shaykh, the elder): shin, ya', kha', which indicates age and advanced years. When a person grows old and advanced in years, his frame becomes stiff; if you wish to straighten it, what is in it breaks. But the young is pliant and can be straightened if it bends. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ), when he advised the raiding parties and expeditions, said: "Kill the elders of the polytheists and spare their youth" [narrated by Abu Dawud (2670) and al-Tirmidhi (1583) from the hadith of Samurah ibn Jundub], meaning their young men. They also said: it derives from (al-khish, coarse cloth).

* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: There is no objection (kha', ya', shin). Khish is coarse, or silk?
* A student: Khish.
* The Shaykh: They said it is coarser, and this indicates that khashyah is greater and stronger.

He says: ﴿They fear men as they should fear Allah or with greater fear, and they said: "Our Lord, why have You prescribed for us fighting?"﴾ Glory be to Allah! Yesterday you were seeking it, and now you object to it?! This shows the weakness of a person, however high his station.

﴿Why have You prescribed for us fighting?﴾ The interrogative ﴿why﴾ here is either for wonder, which better suits the state of the Companions, or for denial, which is far from the state of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them.

﴿Why have You prescribed for us fighting? Why did You not delay us to a near term?﴾ ﴿Why did You not﴾ means (halla, would that), so it is for urging.

﴿Delay us to a near term﴾: they did not say "a distant term," because the whole world is near, however long a life may extend for a person; it is near. This shows cowardice and weakness, because it does not follow from the obligation of fighting that they must die. How many a person has fought, struggled, plunged into the thick of battle, and cut through the ranks of enemies without being killed, among them Khalid ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him! How much he fought and how much he waged war, and yet he died on his bed! He said: "Here I am dying on my bed as a donkey dies; may the eyes of the cowards never sleep" [Tarikh Dimashq (16/273), from Abu al-Zinad]. So it is said: it does not follow from fighting that a person is killed; jihad is obligated upon him, and he wages it and is saved.

﴿Why did You not delay us to a near term﴾: here it is possible that "near" is part of their own speech, meaning they do not want a long extended life, because they know the whole world is near. It is also possible that their speech ended at His words ﴿to a term﴾, but Allah clarified that whatever the term is, it is near.

﴿Say﴾: the address is to the Messenger (ﷺ).

﴿The enjoyment of this world is little﴾: indeed, by Allah, the enjoyment of this world is little, neither in its kind, nor in its type, nor in its duration. Everything in this world of bliss is incomparable to the bliss of the Hereafter, as Allah said: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾ [as-Sajdah 17]. Even what exists in this world and has a counterpart in the Hereafter, the difference is enormous; the difference between them is like the difference between this world and the Hereafter. ﴿In both of them is fruit and palm trees and pomegranates﴾ [ar-Rahman 68]: meat, wine, milk, water, honey; but is this like that? Never. You cannot imagine what is in the Hereafter: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾.

Also, it is little in terms of its duration; however long it is, it is little. Those who remained in their cave three hundred years said: ﴿We remained a day or part of a day﴾ [al-Kahf 19]. And he whom Allah caused to die for a hundred years and then revived said: ﴿I have remained a day or part of a day﴾ [al-Baqarah 259]. And Allah said: ﴿Have you seen if We let them enjoy for years, then what they were promised comes to them, what they were enjoying will not avail them﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 205–207]. However long the duration in this world, it is little. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The place of a whip of one of you in Paradise is better than this world and all that is in it" [narrated by al-Bukhari (2892) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd].

For this reason He said: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah﴾. The Hereafter is better; better than what? Than this world. The word is an elative from which the hamzah of (af'al) has been dropped for lightness, due to its frequent occurrence in people's speech; similarly sharr (worse), similarly al-nas (the people), whose origin is unas, and similarly Allah, whose origin is al-Ilah. The Arabs sometimes drop some letters from a word due to its frequent use.

﴿Better﴾ in what respect? Better in its kind, its type, and its duration. For this reason He said in Surah (Sabbih): ﴿But you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ [al-A'la 16–17].

His words ﴿for those who fear Allah﴾ are a necessary condition, because the Hereafter is not better for those who do not fear Allah; rather it is evil for them. It is better only for those who fear Allah. Taqwa (fear of Allah) originates from wiqayah (protection); the origin of ittaqa is (awtaqa), but the waw was changed to ta' for a morphological reason, then the ta' was assimilated into the ta'. Here taqwa is mentioned. Note that when taqwa is mentioned alone, it includes birr (righteousness), and when birr is mentioned alone, it includes taqwa. When both birr and taqwa are mentioned together, birr becomes the performance of acts of obedience and taqwa the abstention from prohibited acts. So His words ﴿Cooperate in righteousness and piety﴾ [al-Ma'idah 2]: birr is the performance of obedience, taqwa is abstention from what is prohibited. Here ﴿for those who fear Allah﴾ includes both birr and taqwa.

His words ﴿better for those who fear Allah﴾ mean that as for one who does not fear Allah, it is not better for him.

﴿And you will not be wronged a fibre﴾: there are two readings: ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾ and ﴿and you will not be wronged a fibre﴾. Also there is a word earlier in which three readings occur: ﴿alayhim﴾ in ﴿When fighting was prescribed for them (alayhim)﴾, which has (the hā' and mīm pronounced with damma), (the hā' with kasra and the mīm with damma), and (both with kasra).

The first: ﴿alayhum﴾; the second: ﴿alayhim﴾; the third: ﴿alayhim﴾ with both vowels kasra.

* A student: The second, O Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: The second: the hā' with kasra and the mīm with damma, ﴿alayhimu al-qital﴾. This is the well-known reading in the Mushaf now: hā' with kasra and mīm with damma.

﴿And they will not be wronged a fibre﴾; in another reading: ﴿And you will not be wronged a fibre﴾. If it is with the ta', it is part of the speech which Allah commanded His Prophet to say.

﴿And you will not be wronged a fibre﴾: that is, say to them: you will not be wronged a fibre. If it is with the ya', it is the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, meaning ﴿and they will not be wronged a fibre﴾, from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The fatil (fibre) is the thread which is inside the date stone. Do you know? The stone has three things which are used as a proverb for smallness: the naqir, the qitmir, and the fatil. The fatil is the thread inside the stone. Do you know the date stone? This unripe date, the date; inside it there is a thread. Do you know?
* A student: (...) external.
* The Shaykh: Yes, external; it is not in its middle. This is called fatil. Over it there is a skin called qitmir. On its back there is a small pit called naqir; from this pit the sprout emerges when you bury it in the earth, and when Allah wills it to grow, the sprout comes out of this pit and spreads in the earth. After a time, all the pulp inside it has gone and drawn away, leaving only the shell, which is its skin, not the qitmir.

These three things are used as a proverb for the smallness and insignificance of a thing; that is, no one is wronged even a fibre; each is repaid for his deeds. But there remains the question: what is the lifespan of the disbeliever in this world? Let us say a hundred years. His remaining, apart from this community, how long does he stay in the Fire? Forever and ever. If someone says: this is injustice, since how can the recompense be eternal while the deed is limited to a hundred years or so?

We say: his wrongdoing and disbelief covered his whole life in this world, so his recompense covers all his remaining existence in the Hereafter. Moreover, he was given an excuse and it was made clear to him; he has no excuse. The matter is not vague, so that it could be said that it is injustice.

**Student:** There is another opinion (...).

**Shaykh:** Am I the one who said it, everyone? Am I the one who said it? (...) Me? No, perhaps I transmitted it from someone else.

**Student:** The more likely is dates.

**Shaykh:** Yes, the more likely is dates, because this one, if he washes himself with soap and scrubs, nothing will remain.

**Student:** Shaykh, may Allah bless you, we were taught that definitions must be comprehensive and exclusive. We said, regarding the meaning of *ṭāghūt* in this verse, that it is one who fights outside the cause of Allah. But Shaykh, there are hadiths showing that one who fights, for example, in defence of himself, or in defence of his honour, is rewarded, and even if he dies he dies as a martyr, though he is not fighting in the cause of Allah?

**Shaykh:** No, my brother. How is this "not in the cause of Allah"?

**Student:** Is he in the cause of Allah?

**Shaykh:** Yes, indeed. Because you are commanded to preserve yourself and defend it. That is, "in the cause of Allah" is not restricted to fighting the disbelievers. Here it is correct to say "in the cause of Allah": everything that Allah has commanded is in His cause.

**Student:** Raising the word of Allah.

**Shaykh:** Yes, and the Muslim's remaining alive in it is raising the word of Allah.

**Student:** (...) that the disbeliever will abide forever, because his intention in this world is to remain in disbelief, because his intention to remain in disbelief persists...

**Shaykh:** That is not correct, because on the Day of Resurrection they will acknowledge faith and truly believe.

**Student:** Shaykh, if we say that the reading "﴿and they will not be wronged a whit﴾" — Shaykh, if we say that Allah, glorified and exalted, and in the verse which (...)

**Shaykh:** We said: (...) this is part of the continuing address: ﴿Say: The enjoyment of this world is little﴾; that is, say to them: the enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, and you will not be wronged a whit.

If we say that it is from Allah, ﴿and you will not be wronged a whit﴾ becomes an address even to the Messenger, while the address now is with the disbelievers.

**Student:** We said: ﴿aw﴾ is for *idrāb* (a particle of transition or retraction), to confirm what came before, and we said it came in (...) the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

**Shaykh:** No, it came in other than the speech of Allah.

**Student:** It came in the speech of Allah (...).

**Shaykh:** No, it does not come there. Yes.

**Student:** For variety and *idrāb*...

**Shaykh:** That is, some of them are like the fear of Allah, and some of them are more intense.

**Student:** No, in *idrāb*, Shaykh. That is, "up to one hundred thousand, rather they exceed (that)." Someone might say: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knew that they were one hundred thousand, then it became clear to Him that they exceed that, so He said: "Rather they exceed." This statement may be raised, saying: now we have the speech of the creature, who says: this thing, in number, is ten; then it becomes clear to him that he was mistaken, so he says: No, rather twelve.

**Shaykh:** But is this possible in the speech of Allah?

**Student:** It is not possible. But how do we respond to (...)? If we say that it comes for *idrāb*?

**Shaykh:** *Idrāb* is of two kinds: *idrāb ibṭālī* (cancelling retraction), and *idrāb intiqālī* (transitional retraction). This one is transitional. It does not mean that he cancelled the first and brought the second. The meaning, for the sake of confirming this matter, is that they cannot be fewer than one hundred thousand.

**Student:** And for confirmation, for example, Shaykh.

**Shaykh:** This is what Ibn al-Qayyim chose.

**Student:** Is there not mentioned in it (...)?

**Shaykh:** No, this (...) the meaning is that they are one hundred thousand and no more.

**Student:** Confirmation of what came before.

**Shaykh:** If we say: for confirmation of what came before, then the meaning is that they are one hundred thousand and no more. But He brought the statement ﴿or they exceed﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt 147] as confirmation of what came before.

**Student:** That means they do not decrease?

**Shaykh:** That means they do not decrease.

**Student:** Those who said that this verse is about the hypocrites.

**Shaykh:** Which of them?

**Student:** They cited three signs. They said: among them (...) for other than Allah, and this is a sign of the hypocrite. Second: their objection to Allah: ﴿Why have You prescribed fighting for us?﴾ Third: (...).

**Shaykh:** We say: the occasion of revelation. The scholars have discussed this and named those who said these words. Since the matter is an actual event, that the Muslims in Makkah had strong zeal against the Quraysh, who humiliated and oppressed them, and then their souls weakened afterward, because the hypocrites in fact did not request fighting. They did not even request fighting so that it would be said to them: "Restrain your hands." The phrase ﴿it was said to them: Restrain your hands﴾ means that they had requested it, but it was said: ﴿Restrain your hands﴾.

* * *

**Student:** If it is transitive to one object, then it is visual (*baṣariyya*). Then why do we say: it may be, and it may be, we look? If it is transitive to two objects, we say...?

**Shaykh:** Sometimes it governs an accusative and the second is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial accusative). If you say: "I saw Zayd standing with my own eyes," you put it in the accusative now. But the second, what do we say? A *ḥāl*.

**Student:** (...) educational gatherings, Shaykh. What is your opinion?

**Shaykh:** My opinion is this is correct. But you have heard me on more than one occasion speak about educational gatherings, in which we urge you to good and virtuous manners, and to greeting one another, both initiating and returning the greeting. But we have not found application. We always speak about this, but now we see the students: one passes by his brother and does not greet him.

* * *

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are within fortified towers. And if good befalls them, they say, "This is from Allah," but if evil befalls them, they say, "This is from you [O Muhammad]." Say, "All is from Allah." So what is [the matter] with these people that they fail to understand any statement? (78) Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself. And We have sent you to mankind as a messenger, and sufficient is Allah as witness.﴾ (79)

**Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿Have you not seen those to whom it was said, "Restrain your hands and establish prayer"?﴾ And so on to the end.

What is the word in this verse that has three readings?

**Student:** The word ﴿ʿalayhim﴾.

**Shaykh:** The word ﴿ʿalayhim﴾, yes. The readings?

**Student:** The one found in the Mushaf: kasra on the *hā'* and ḍamma on the *mīm*.

**Shaykh:** Kasra on the *hā'* and ḍamma on the *mīm*. Recite it.

**Student:** ﴿ʿalayhim﴾. The second: with kasra on the *hā'* and kasra on the *mīm*: ﴿ʿalayhim﴾. The third: ḍamma on the *hā'* and ḍamma on the *mīm*: ﴿ʿalayhum﴾.

**Shaykh:** Well done, excellent. And which word has two readings?

**Student:** ﴿wa lā tuẓlamūn﴾ and ﴿wa lā yuẓlamūn﴾.

**Shaykh:** That is, with the *tā'* and the *yā'*, the vowels are the same.

Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Have you not seen those to whom it was said, "Restrain your hands and establish prayer and give zakah"?﴾

* In this verse there are benefits. Among them: wonder, or the call to wonder at what is a matter of wonder, because we mentioned that the interrogative is for expressing amazement.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: a person may hasten toward something, and when it befalls him he recoils from it. These people hastened to fight, and when they were commanded to it, some of them recoiled. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "Do not wish for encounter with the enemy, but ask Allah for well-being. But when you meet them, then be patient, for Paradise is under the shade of the swords."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhārī (2966) and Muslim (1742/20) from the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā.]]

* And it follows from this benefit that a person should not involve himself in a matter from which he is unable to extricate himself. For this reason a saying was transmitted: "None of you should humiliate himself." They said: "How does he humiliate himself?" He said: "He speaks on a matter, then cannot get out of it."[[Recorded by al-Tirmidhī (2254) and Ibn Mājah (4016) from the hadith of Ḥudhayfah.]] This report, or its meaning, and the reason this is self-humiliation is that when a person undertakes something, then becomes unable to do it and falls behind, his standing among people falls, and they say: "This is a hasty man, this is a rash man. How can he enter into a matter when he does not know how to get out of it?"

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: if a person is unable to engage in *jihād*, then let him do good deeds or specific acts of worship, because he has been commanded to them, by His saying: ﴿Restrain your hands and establish prayer and give zakah﴾.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: fighting is obligatory. Fighting the disbelievers is obligatory, by His saying: ﴿When fighting was prescribed for them﴾. And here are questions.

The first: is it an individual obligation (*farḍ ʿayn*) or a collective obligation (*farḍ kifāya*)?

We say: the principle is that it is a collective obligation. This is the principle, and it becomes an individual obligation, according to what the scholars said, in four situations.

The first situation: when the two lines meet. Then it becomes necessary for him to fight. If he turns away, that is among the major sins, because of the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, when you meet those who have disbelieved advancing [for battle], do not turn your backs to them. And whoever turns his back to them that day, unless swerving [as part] of battle or joining [another] company, he has certainly returned with anger from Allah, and his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾ [al-Anfāl 15–16]; "and because the Prophet ﷺ made turning away on the day of the advance one of the destructive sins."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhārī (2766) and Muslim (1742/20) from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah.]]

The second situation: when the enemy besieges him. Then it is obligatory for him to defend, because if he is routed before the enemy, this becomes a great trial in religion, and Allah says: ﴿Fight them until there is no more fitnah and the religion is for Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah 193].

The third: when his land is besieged, then it becomes necessary for him to defend his land and not surrender as far as he is able.

The fourth: when the ruler calls him, when the ruler summons him to march, then it is obligatory for him to respond. Note that the enemy besieging a group and the enemy besieging a person are equal; that is, if a group is besieged in a wilderness, or a city is besieged, it counts as one. When the ruler calls him, it is obligatory to respond, by the saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, what is [wrong] with you that when it is said to you, "Go forth in the cause of Allah," you adhere heavily to the earth? Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter?﴾ [al-Tawbah 38]. This is a rebuke to them when it is said to them, "Go forth in the cause of Allah," and they adhere heavily to the earth.

The fourth [as I said]: we said that besieging him or besieging his land is one matter. I counted them as two, but they are one matter.

The fourth: when he is needed, such as when he has knowledge of a type of weapon that no one else knows. Here it becomes obligatory on him to advance and fight. The principle is that fighting is a collective obligation, and it becomes individual in these four matters.

The second question: is fighting to compel people to enter the religion of Allah, or fighting to raise the word of Allah?

**Students:** The second.

**Shaykh:** The second. So fighting is not to compel people to enter the religion. Fighting is so that the word of Allah is supreme, such that no one stands to oppose it or resist it. The evidence for this is what Muslim recorded in his Ṣaḥīḥ[[Recorded by Muslim (1731/3) from the hadith of Buraydah.]] from the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Ḥuṣayb: "that the Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, when he appointed a commander over an army or a detachment, would instruct him to fear Allah and to be good to those Muslims with him." And in it: "If they refuse Islam, he invites them to pay the *jizya* (poll tax on protected non-Muslims). If they pay it, he withholds from them." This shows that fighting is not to compel people to become Muslim, because giving the *jizya* does not mean Islam, but giving the *jizya* means submission and not opposing. So when the whole religion is for Allah, and the religion of Allah is the dominant and prevailing one, the people have fulfilled their duty.

The third question: is this fighting a matter of repelling an aggressor, so that I do not kill, or do not proceed to kill except when what is less than it is impossible; or is it not of this category?

**Students:** The second.

**Shaykh:** The second. Fighting the disbelievers is not a matter of repelling an aggressor. For this reason we finish off their wounded, pursue their fleeing, and kill them, and kill the wounded and the fleeing. As for fighting the rebels (*ahl al-baghy*), this is a matter of repelling an aggressor. For this reason, if a group rises against the ruler and fights them, it is not permitted to finish off the wounded or pursue the one fleeing, unless we know that he has fled in order to re-arm himself anew. Then we may pursue him, but without killing him; we detain him so that his evil does not arise again.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: condemnation of one who fears people as he fears Allah or more intensely, by His saying: ﴿Then when a party of them fear men as they fear Allah or [even] more intensely﴾. The sign of this is that a person abandons what Allah has obligated upon him out of fear of people, or commits what is forbidden out of fear of people. This is blameworthy, and it may sometimes reach the point of associating partners with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So it is obligatory that you not fear people as you fear Allah, because people, as the Prophet ﷺ said to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: "Know that if the nation were to gather to benefit you with something, they would not benefit you except with what Allah has written for you; and if they gathered to harm you with something, they would not harm you except with what Allah has written against you."[[Recorded by al-Tirmidhī (2516) from the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās.]] But you are commanded to take the means that lead you to benefit and to leave the means that lead you to harm. As for that being at the expense of your religion, this is not permitted.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: condemnation of one who objects to Allah's legislative rulings, as in this verse: ﴿Why have You prescribed fighting for us?﴾, and [objects to] His cosmic decrees, by His saying: ﴿Why did You not delay us to a near term?﴾. This includes both the legislative ruling and the cosmic decree. So it is not permitted for a person to object to Allah's legislative rulings, nor to His cosmic decrees. Rather he must submit. As for the legislative rulings, some people submit and some do not submit. As for the cosmic decrees, all are submitting: ﴿And to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, willingly or unwillingly﴾ [al-Raʿd 15]. This is the cosmic prostration. Every person is humbled and subject to Allah's cosmic decree; no one can ever repel it. Allah says: ﴿Then why, when it [the soul] reaches the throat, and you at that time are watching—and We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see—then why, if you are not to be recompensed, do you not return it, if you are truthful?﴾ [al-Wāqiʿah 83–87]. Up to this point? It is impossible.

So we must submit, and we have no right to object. But "why" (*lima*) is prohibited both legally and in terms of decree. "When" (*matā*) is not prohibited except when the motive for asking is denial, as in His saying: ﴿When is this promise, if you are truthful?﴾ [al-Mulk 25].

"Where" (*ayna*) is not prohibited. You ask where the place of a legislative or cosmic ruling is. There is no harm in that. Indeed, the Messenger ﷺ said to the slave girl: "Where is Allah?"[[Recorded by Muslim (537/33) from the hadith of Muʿāwiyah ibn al-Ḥakam al-Sulamī.]] So the interrogative varies.

"How" (*kayfa*), when it concerns a ruling, is not prohibited. When it concerns matters of the unseen, it is prohibited, as the righteous predecessors (*al-salaf al-ṣāliḥ*) said regarding one who asked about the modality of Allah's attributes, Mighty and Majestic.

**Ibn 'Uthaymin's commentary on surah 4, verse 77 (part 3 of 3):**

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is encouragement to renounce worldly attachment (*tazhid*), based on His saying: ﴿Say: The enjoyment of this world is little﴾. And Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth: the enjoyment of this world is little. Ask someone who has lived a hundred years, for example, "How much of your life do you estimate has passed?" What will he say? It is nothing. Right now, at this moment, it is as if I were only just born. Everything that has passed is gone, so it is little. Likewise, whatever bliss exists in this world is also little and insignificant compared with the Hereafter. If you consider fruits, for example, you find they come for a time and then disappear for another time. The same is true of fruits, crops and rain. All of it is little. This is from the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because if Allah had perfected for us the blessings of this world in every respect, we would have been deluded by them. Allah pointed to this in His saying: ﴿And were it not that mankind would become one community [in disbelief], We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver roofs for their houses and stairways [of silver] by which they could ascend, and for their houses doors and couches [of silver] on which they could recline, and ornaments of gold. But all that would be nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life. And the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous﴾ [al-Zukhruf 33–35]. This is from the wisdom of Allah, that the world should not be complete, lest we be deluded by it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the permissibility of comparing two things that are utterly different. His saying: ﴿and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah﴾ is an example. There is no comparison between this world and the Hereafter, but since this world is immediate and the soul is inclined to love what is immediate, comparing the two becomes appropriate. So the Hereafter is better for those who are mindful of Allah. A similar example is the Exalted's saying: ﴿The companions of Paradise that Day will be better in resting place and finer in place of repose﴾ [al-Furqan 24], even though the companions of the Fire have no goodness at all. This is for the sake of (...) in it, and because the companions of the Fire think they are in some good.

* * *

Suppose a man buys a garment, for example, as a gift for his father, and says to the seller: "I want a large garment as a gift for my father." What is the ruling on the sale here?

There is nothing wrong with it. Is there a problem? What is the problem you see?

* Student: Don't mention it at the time of purchase.

* Shaykh: No, no. May Allah bless you. He bought it for him; he (the father) is the one who pays its price. As for this being a gift, there is nothing wrong with it.

You say: There are women from the Tabligh Jama'at who come to me and say: "Come with us to invite people to Allah's way." Is it permissible for me to go out with them when I have no knowledge?

A woman must have a mahram (a male relative whom she may never marry) with her. She may not go out to call people to Islam except with a mahram, because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A woman should not travel except with a mahram." [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (1086) and Muslim (1338 / 413), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar.] So if the women are accompanied by male mahrams, there is no harm. Otherwise, it is not permissible for them to go out. As for travelling without knowledge, what is the benefit? If a person does not have knowledge with which to call people, there is no benefit.

Someone says: The Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Hold fast to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the Rightly-Guided Caliphs" [related by Abu Dawud (4607) and al-Tirmidhi (2676), from the hadith of al-'Irbad ibn Sariyah]. Do we understand from this that the Rightly-Guided Caliphs, may Allah be pleased with them all, have a Sunnah to be followed apart from the Sunnah of the Messenger (ﷺ), because they are guided and rightly-guided? Or what? And what is the meaning of our saying that they have a Sunnah to be followed?

The meaning is that the Messenger (ﷺ) undoubtedly has the Sunnah that is to be followed. If the Sunnah of the Rightly-Guided Caliphs is supposed to contradict his Sunnah, then the Sunnah of the Messenger takes precedence. But if there is something that no text from the Prophet (ﷺ) has addressed, and no known Sunnah, and the Rightly-Guided Caliphs introduced it as a Sunnah, then it is to be followed. For example, the first call to prayer on Friday is from the Sunnah of 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him. The Prophet (ﷺ) had no Sunnah about it, so it is followed.

* Student: And if they disagreed?

* Shaykh: They disagreed about what? The caliphs? We know that when they disagree, the ruling is what the text supports.

What is the wisdom in a woman breaking the prayer when a donkey or a black dog passes in front of the worshipper, especially when we know that 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, objected when she said: "You have compared us to donkeys and dogs"? [related by Muslim (512 / 270)].

The answer to this is that when the Prophet (ﷺ) says something, our position on it is to say: "We hear and we obey." We have no right to pay attention to the objection of 'Aisha or anyone else. Moreover, 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said this as a form of rejection regarding a matter that was not objectionable, and the matter is not as she claimed, may Allah be pleased with her. The Messenger (ﷺ) said: "It breaks the prayer of a Muslim man when [something] passes in front of him" [related by Muslim (511 / 266), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, in similar wording]. She argued that the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed while she was lying across in front of him. Is this passing in front? No. So there is no basis for her objection.

As for her saying: "You have compared us to donkeys and dogs," we say: Far from it, and God forbid. Rather, we say: Allah has favoured the children of Adam over many of those He created, with a clear preference. But the ruling of Allah and His Messenger is a matter that must be accepted. This is not because of any impurity, so that we would say "he compared us." Rather, it is because when a woman who has reached puberty passes between a man and what is in front of him, it may be a cause of temptation and attachment of the heart to her, so that he becomes distracted from his prayer. So Allah pardoned her for this objection.

I was praying the 'Asr prayer at home. During the first tashahhud (the sitting recitation in prayer), my daughter, who is a child of one year and four months, came to me, took hold of my hand and put some food in it. So I turned to the right in order to put the food on something raised from the ground. Is this correct?

Did you turn or did you look sideways?

* Student: I turned to the right.

* Shaykh: With your whole body?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: Then repeat the prayer, because turning with the whole body invalidates the prayer. Repeat it, may Allah reward you with good.

* Student: News about our brothers in Bosnia?

* Shaykh: By Allah, I have not heard. Their custom is to call us on Thursday; that is their habit. We heard that things are calm, praise be to Allah. But the problem is that a group of Muslims has appeared fighting the government of Bosnia. However, praise be to Allah, they have overrun them... a problem.

* Student: (...) Yemen (...).

* Shaykh: This is a great trial. We ask Allah to extinguish it by His grace and generosity, and to spare the Muslims this evil.

* Student: Is it true that among the communists...?

* Shaykh: As for me, I have not tested either these or those, do you understand?

I say: I have not tested these people or those people. I did not go to al-Bidh or to Abdullah Salih and say: "Come, everyone, what is your creed?" So we do not know. But in itself, it is undoubtedly a trial, and in reality it is a calamity, because it cannot be free of evil. It is evil now, and the affairs and the future are in the hands of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. We ask Allah to protect the Muslims from its evil.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Wherever you are, death will overtake you, even if you should be within lofty towers. And if a good come to them, they say, "This is from Allah"; but if an evil come to them, they say, "This is from you [O Muhammad]." Say, "All is from Allah." So what is [wrong] with these people that they hardly understand any statement? Whatever good comes to you [O man] is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself. And We have sent you [O Muhammad] to mankind as a messenger, and sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾ [al-Nisa 78–79].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. It was mentioned in the previous verse that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿When fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a party of them feared men as they should have feared Allah, or with even greater fear, and they said, "Our Lord, why have You decreed for us fighting? If only You would delay us to a near term"﴾. They said that to flee from death; this is the apparent meaning, and the discussion of this verse has already been covered.

We said that some people have said: ﴿Our Lord, why have You decreed for us fighting? If only You would delay us to a near term﴾, meaning so that we would have time to prepare for fighting and then fight. But this contradicts the apparent meaning of the verse.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in fortified towers.﴾ Let us begin first with the grammar. (ʾAyna) here is a conditional noun of unconditional sense (ism shart jazim), and (mā) is an extra particle for emphasis (zā'ida lil-tawkīd). The conditional verb is ﴿takūnū﴾ and ﴿yudrikkumu﴾ is the response of the condition (jawab al-shart).

﴿And even if you were in fortified towers﴾: (law) here is a conditional particle, and its conditional verb is ﴿kuntum﴾. We do not find a response of the condition for (law), so it was said: the response of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, and the sense is: "And even if you were in fortified towers, death would overtake you." It was also said that in this context it does not need a response. This is the view of Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, in his book Aqsam al-Qur'an: that in such a context it does not need a response, and that if a response were supplied the speech would be awkward and not eloquent. This occurs frequently in the Qur'an: you find a conditional clause referring back to what came before, meaning its response is understood from what preceded it; in that case we say it needs no response, and supplying a response makes the speech clumsy.

As for the rest of the verse, there is apparently no difficulty in it, except that His saying ﴿lā yakādūna yafqahūna ḥadīthan﴾ (yakād) is one of the verbs of approximation (af'al al-muqarabah), and it works like (kāna and its sisters): it raises the noun and puts the predicate in the accusative.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says in response to those who said: ﴿Why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had delayed us to a near term﴾. He says: if you say this for the sake of enjoying a little in this world, then you will not escape death: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you﴾, whether you are in the air, or in the sea, or on the earth, or in fortified towers, or in crumbling houses, or in a barren wilderness. ﴿Wherever you may be﴾, and (ʾayna) is well known to indicate place.

His saying ﴿death will overtake you﴾ means: it will not miss you, and you cannot escape it. Rather, in another verse there is something stronger and more eloquent, where He the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Say: Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 8]. He did not say "it will reach you (lāḥiqukum)"; He said ﴿meet you (mulāqīkum)﴾. And what do you think of a thing from which you flee, and which meets you? Without doubt you will be quicker to reach it than if it were merely pursuing you! Because your fleeing and your meeting combine, and so that is swifter. Thus He the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in fortified towers.﴾ And what comes after death? After death is meeting Allah the Mighty and Majestic, with good or with evil. And when does it occur? We do not know when death will come, or in which land. We do not know. ﴿And no soul knows in what land it will die﴾ [Luqman 34]. So let us prepare, and let us always be vigilant, so that when death overtakes us we are in the state with which our Lord is pleased, the Mighty and Majestic.

His saying ﴿in fortified towers﴾: (burūj) is the plural of (burj), which is a high building, and from it come the burūj in the sky, which are twelve zodiacal signs, to which Allah alluded in His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky zodiacal signs﴾ [al-Furqan 61]. The seasons of the year revolve through these burūj: spring, summer, autumn, and winter; each season has three of them. The best and most beneficial of the burūj for the body is the sign of Aries (al-Hamal), which occurs at the beginning of spring, for bodies are at their healthiest then. This is from the standpoint of it being a sign; but there are matters that befall a person in which his body is healthy or sick, according to circumstances. Yet in terms of time, the best season is spring.

So what is meant by burūj here? High buildings, since they resemble the zodiacal signs in their height and elevation. As for one who said that what is meant is the celestial burūj, he has strayed far and erred, because Allah said ﴿fortified (mushayyadah)﴾, and this description never applies to celestial burūj; it applies only to lofty palaces.

His saying ﴿mushayyadah﴾ means: well-fortified and firmly built. To this is added that they are plastered with (shīd), which is (gypsum), i.e., whitewashed; because whiteness is loved by the soul and protects from the heat of the sun, which is why palaces are built with it. ﴿And even if you were in fortified towers﴾.

﴿And if good befalls them, they say: "This is from Allah"; and if evil befalls them, they say: "This is from you [O Muhammad]."﴾ The pronoun in His saying ﴿if it befalls them﴾ refers to those who denied the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. By evil (sayyi'ah) here is meant what distresses, not evil deeds; rather, what distresses a person, such as drought, sickness, poverty, and the like. Drought from the sky, when it does not rain, and barrenness from the earth, when it does not grow; poverty and sickness. If evil befell them, they said: "This is from you." And if good befell them—its opposite: fertility, rain, wealth, health—when these befell them, they said: "This is from Allah," meaning you have no merit in it. And in the case of evil they said: "This is from Muhammad; he is the one who brought it. May Allah not bring him near us," thereby taking omen from him, peace and blessings be upon him. This is like the saying of the Children of Israel to Musa: ﴿We have taken an omen from you and those with you. He said: Your omen is with Allah; rather, you are a people being tested﴾ [al-Naml 47].

Likewise the peoples said to their messengers: ﴿We take an omen from you. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and a painful punishment will surely touch you from us﴾ [Ya-Sin 18]. Thus taking omens was a habit of those who denied the messengers: they said that whatever drought, barrenness, sickness, or poverty befell them was from you; and if the opposite befell them, which was pleasing to them, they said: "This is from Allah."

Allah the Mighty and Majestic responded to them: ﴿Say﴾, i.e., O Muhammad: ﴿All is from Allah﴾. Good and evil are from Allah, because Allah is the One who decrees them, not from the coming of the messengers. Rather, the coming of the messengers brings nothing but good; but they use these doubts as an argument against the messengers in order that people will deny them and shun them.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: All is from Allah﴾. It is He who decrees good and decrees evil. This answer is a sound answer, because none can bring rain except Allah, none can withhold rain except Allah, none can bring health except Allah, and none can bring sickness except Allah the Mighty and Majestic; so all is from Allah.

﴿What is wrong with these people that they can hardly understand any statement?﴾ (mā) is an interrogative of wonder: that is, how strange these people are. ﴿They can hardly﴾, i.e., they do not come close to. ﴿Understand any statement﴾, i.e., they do not come close to understanding the statement, knowing the rulings and the wisdom, since they said this false statement.

His saying ﴿lā yakādūna﴾ means "they do not come close," and it is known that negating coming close is a negation of the act itself, and more so. So if they can hardly understand, then all the more so are they—what?—not understanding at all and not even near to understanding. And ﴿ḥadīthan﴾ means: what is related/spoken to them.

* This noble verse contains several benefits.
* The first benefit: there is no escape from death, however strong a person may be in his authority and in his fortresses; he has no escape from it. This is drawn from His saying: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you﴾.
* Among the benefits of this verse: it is obligatory for a person to prepare for death, since there is no escape from it; and since there is no escape, let us prepare for it so that we may act.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the attribution of overtaking to death.
* And it follows from this: that it is valid to attribute a thing to causes, but on condition that one believes these causes do not act by themselves, and that they are only from Allah the Mighty and Majestic.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: fortresses do not avail against the decree of Allah; by His saying: ﴿even if you were in fortified towers﴾.
* Among its benefits: the use of hyperbole in speech, and that this is one of the methods of the Arabic language; by His saying: ﴿even if you were in fortified towers﴾.
* Among its benefits: the permissibility of omitting what is known, and that this does not count as a defect in speech; by His saying: ﴿even if you were in fortified towers﴾.
* And this branches from this benefit: what occurs in contracts—contracts of sale, hire, pledge, endowment (waqf), and the like. For example, if someone says: "I have endowed this for so-and-so even if he is rich," the meaning is: even if he is rich, it is an endowment for him; and accordingly the endowment is valid for this beneficiary under every circumstance.
* Among the benefits of this verse: it is the custom of people to protect themselves against death with what? With lofty, well-built palaces. If there were an enemy who wanted to attack you, would you seek refuge from him in a tent of cloth? In a building of wood? No, in towers: lofty, strong towers, so that nothing from him reaches you.
