A believer is not made to abide eternally in the Fire. So it was said: the verse is to be understood as referring to one who considers that lawful, meaning: one who deems the intentional killing of a believer lawful. But this view is baseless, because one who deems the intentional killing of a believer lawful is a disbeliever whether he killed or did not kill. For this reason, when this interpretation was offered to Imam Ahmad, he smiled and said: if he deems killing him lawful, he is a disbeliever, whether he killed him or not.

This interpretation is similar to the interpretation of those who explained the hadiths about the disbelief of one who abandons the prayer as referring to one who deems it lawful. It is said: one who deems abandoning the prayer lawful is a disbeliever, whether he abandoned it or not. So restricting the texts on the disbelief of one who abandons the prayer to the one who deems it lawful, and does not believe it obligatory, is a distortion of the text in two ways. The first: diverting the wording from its apparent meaning. The second: imposing upon the text a meaning that it does not indicate. So the violation against the texts in this matter is in two respects.

Some scholars said: the verse is based on an omitted element, and the implied sense is: this is his recompense if He requites him; and if He does not requite him, then Allah's bounty is vast: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills﴾. But this interpretation does not get us out of the difficulty, because our discussion concerns the case where He requites him: will he abide eternally or not? And Allah, mighty and majestic, mentioned in the verse that He will requite him with this, so this interpretation is weak.

The third aspect: this warning is attached to a cause, and a cause may have an impediment that prevents its effect, because things are not completed except by the existence of their causes and the absence of their impediments. It is said: this is his recompense, but if the texts indicate that there is an impediment that prevents permanent abiding, we adopt that impediment.

Have you considered the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And for his parents, to each one of them is a sixth of what he leaves, if he has a child﴾ [an-Nisa' 11]? If one of the parents were a disbeliever, would he be entitled? No, although the apparent meaning of the verse is generality. So it is said: the texts of the Sharia qualify one another, and this aspect is the safest if khuluud means permanent stay. But if we say khuluud means long stay, then nothing of what we have mentioned is an objection to the verse.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of anger for Allah, mighty and majestic.

Anger is one of the attributes of action (sifat fi'liyyah) that occur by the will of Allah, exalted is He, and every attribute attached to a cause is an attribute of action, because it exists when that cause exists and is absent when it is absent. But is anger upon its apparent meaning? Is anger an attribute in the one who is angry that entails vengeance, or is it a separate thing from the angry one and what is meant by it is vengeance? We say: as for the salaf, they say: anger is an attribute in the one who is angry that entails vengeance, and it is not vengeance itself. This is shown by the fact that this is the apparent wording, and that Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So when they angered Us, We took vengeance upon them﴾ [az-Zukhruf 55].

If it were said that anger is vengeance, the meaning of the verse would be: "When We took vengeance upon them, We took vengeance upon them," and this is a meaning from which the speech of Allah is free. The verse is clear that vengeance had anger as its cause, and the cause is other than the effect.

So anger is an attribute subsisting in Allah, mighty and majestic, and it is not vengeance. As for the people of negation (ta'til) and distortion (tahrif), they say: anger is vengeance or the will of vengeance. But the people of the Sunnah say: we oblige you to say that anger is an attribute subsisting in Allah, because He does not take vengeance except upon one with whom He is angry; so vengeance is a necessary consequence of anger, and the will of vengeance likewise, since Allah did not take vengeance upon them, nor will to take vengeance upon them, except because they angered Him. Accordingly, it is incumbent upon us to believe that Allah, exalted is He, becomes angry.

If someone says: anger is a coal that Satan casts into the heart of the son of Adam, from which the blood of the heart boils, the veins swell, the face reddens, and the hair bristles, do you affirm this for Allah? We say: no, this is the anger of the created being; as for the anger of the Creator, we do not know its modality, but we believe that He, majestic and exalted, becomes angry.

If it is said: anger is a deficiency, as evidenced by the fact that the Prophet ﷺ forbade it when a man said: "Advise me." He said: "Do not become angry." The man repeated it several times, and he said: "Do not become angry." [Related by al-Bukhari (6116).] We say: it is a deficiency with respect to the created being; but with respect to the Creator it is an attribute of perfection, because it indicates perfection of authority and perfection of power. For this reason, if you wrong a person stronger than you, he becomes angry, and if you wrong a person below you, he grieves: the first becomes angry because he is capable of vengeance, and the second grieves because he is incapable of vengeance.

* Student: O Shaykh, may Allah bless you. In the previous verse we said that His saying: ﴿And if he was from a people between you and them is a covenant﴾ (...) What prevents, O Shaykh, that a believer may be from a people between us and them is a covenant, from a tribe between us and them is a covenant (...) returns to the first verse: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ ﴿And whoever kills a believer﴾, so does the context of the verse indicate it?

* Shaykh: No, no, if the one killed is from a people who are not believers. For this reason we mentioned that the verse indicates three types: the believer, the mu'ahad, and the believer from a people of disbelievers with whom there is no covenant between us and them.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: The original ruling is that this believer, whether he is from those between us and them who have a covenant or not, if his family is not disbelievers, there is blood-money for him; and if we said what you said, it would have left silent about the one between us and them who has a covenant.

* Student: (...) Is there a rule that says: if Allah mentions "abiding therein" and does not mention "forever," then it is an abiding that falls short of the eternal?

* Shaykh: If we say that khuluud in the Arabic language means a long stay, this rule is correct, built on this, with disagreement over whether khuluud requires perpetuity or not.

* Student: O our Shaykh, is it not, by greater reason, that deliberate killing has an expiation (kaffarah) in general, as in accidental killing, if he kills him?

* Shaykh: It is not by greater reason, because Allah distinguished between them, and we have pointed to the wisdom in that: deliberate killing is not expiated by expiation, because it is greater.

* Student: If someone says (...) what diverted it from the Muslim to the disbeliever (...)?

* Shaykh: The Sunnah related on that, the Sunnah came on this, and perhaps Allah will facilitate it, since we have a study on the subject of blood-money.

* Student: (...) in the explanation of Muslim (...) concerning one who kills himself deliberately (...).

* Shaykh: That the one who kills himself deliberately, in it he is one who abides, eternally, it is explicitly stated with perpetuity.

* Student: It is not a problem, because he is a believer.

* Shaykh: No, because perhaps at that hour he does not have faith.

* Student: Would it not be specified by the verses of repentance and the general texts?

* Shaykh: Whoever repents?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: Whoever repents, there is no difficulty; whoever repents, there is no difficulty. The discussion is about one who died while being a deliberate killer of a soul. As for one who repents, Allah forgives all sins and there is no difficulty in it.

* Student: My intention is: whoever kills a believer intentionally.

* Shaykh: Whoever kills a believer intentionally and repents, Allah accepts his repentance.

* Student: O Shaykh, may Allah bless you, is knowledge of the punishment a condition for carrying out retaliation (qisas)?

* Shaykh: No. He says: is knowledge of the punishment a condition for carrying out retaliation? We say: it is not a condition, and this is general in everything: whenever a person knows that something is forbidden, its effect is applied to him. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ obligated expiation upon the one who had intercourse with his wife in Ramadan, even though he did not know; he came asking what was incumbent upon him.

* Student: Is what is attributed to Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah bless you, authentic, that the repentance of the killer is not accepted?

* Shaykh: Yes, it is authentic. But Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, says that the deliberate killer has no repentance, but his statement is to be understood as meaning he has no repentance with respect to the right of the one killed, because deliberate killing involves three rights: the right of Allah, the right of the heirs of the one killed, and the right of the one killed.

As for the right of Allah, there is no doubt that it is dropped by repentance, by the text of the Qur'an: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse; and whoever does that will meet a penalty. Its punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated, except for those who repent﴾ [al-Furqan 68-70].

As for the right of the heirs of the one killed, it is dropped by the killer surrendering himself to them, because their right is that they kill him, and he has surrendered himself.

As for the right of the one killed, the one killed has died, so his right remains, because his forgiveness is not known. So what came from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, is to be understood as: he has no repentance with respect to the right of the one killed. However, the correct view is that he has repentance even with respect to the right of the one killed, because Allah, exalted is He, will compensate on his behalf on the Day of Resurrection, since he repented a sincere repentance.

* Student: Now, if a person kills someone and then that victim dies, and all of his heirs agree on killing him, except one young child?

* Shaykh: The young child waits until he reaches maturity. But if one of the heirs, who inherits only one thousandth, forgives, the retaliation falls; because of His saying: ﴿And whoever is pardoned by his brother anything﴾, and "anything" (shay') is indefinite in a conditional context and includes the little and the much.

* Student: Does not the argument of those who take the verse and the hadiths about one who abandons the prayer as referring to one who deems it lawful lead, by their interpretation, to rendering the texts void of benefit?

* Shaykh: Yes; for this reason we say: the text remains with no benefit from it.

* Student: What if a killer is killed and dies in prison before the ruling is carried out upon him?

* Shaykh: If he dies in prison, the blood-money is fixed on his property.

* Student: And if he has no property, does the 'aqilah (paternal kin) bear anything of it?

* Shaykh: No, the 'aqilah bears nothing in deliberate killing, but if he has no property, then either it is dropped or it is taken from the public treasury (bayt al-mal).

* Student: O Shaykh, may Allah bless you, we mentioned that blood-money is due upon the 'aqilah in accidental killing. Does this statement conflict with the saying of Allah: ﴿And that man has only what he strives for﴾ [an-Najm 39], and His saying: ﴿No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ [al-An'am 164]?

* Shaykh: Yes, it does not conflict with it, because this is from the aspect of mutual assistance, since accidental killing happens frequently, so it was of the mercy of Allah, mighty and majestic, that these people bear it as they share in the maintenance.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No, it is not specified. That is, this is after the people of the Fire who deserve punishment have been taken out, and then after everything has ended, death will be brought and slaughtered between Paradise and the Fire, and it will be said: "O people of Paradise, abiding with no death; and O people of the Fire, abiding with no death." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4730) and Muslim (2849/40) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]

* Student: O Shaykh, we did not hear the question, O Shaykh.

* Shaykh: He asks: does his saying "abiding, with no death" not indicate the view that khuluud is a lasting stay? We say: it is not specified.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: But is he permitted to shoot a person? Was he permitted to shoot the person?

* Student: No, he is the one who came.

* Shaykh: No, he is not the one who came. But we know, if we suppose that this man, after seeing a person wanting to kill the game, leapt until he was in the mouth of a cannon, for example, there is no harm; he is the one who killed himself.

* Student: (...) Would it be deliberate (...)?

**The Shaykh:** Intentional, you mean? It is deliberate, but he is not killed in retaliation for a Muslim, because according to the jurists this is a deliberate killing. It is not permissible to kill a *mu'ahad* (a non-Muslim living under a covenant of protection with the Muslims). Some doubt remains about this, because the sanctity of a *mu'ahad* is not the same as the sanctity of a Muslim. Also, a Muslim is not killed for a *mu'ahad*. So this is referred to the opinion of the imam: if he sees fit to have him killed, he is killed.

* * *

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿O you who believe, when you go forth in the cause of Allah, investigate carefully, and do not say to one who offers you peace, "You are not a believer," seeking the goods of worldly life. For with Allah are abundant gains. Thus were you before, and Allah conferred His favor upon you, so investigate carefully. Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted. (94) Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers, other than those with a disability, and those who strive in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit [at home] by a degree. And to each Allah has promised reward, but Allah has preferred the strivers over those who sit [at home] with a great reward, (95) [as] degrees from Him and forgiveness and mercy. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [An-Nisa' 94–96].

**The Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, when you go forth in the cause of Allah﴾ and so on to the end.

In the previous verse it was mentioned that Allah the Exalted threatened the one who kills a believer deliberately with certain things. Can you enumerate them for us?

**Student:** His recompense is Hell, abiding therein; that he enters Hell, and the abiding, and the wrath, and the curse, and the painful punishment.

**The Shaykh:** How many?

**Student:** Five things.

**The Shaykh:** Good. We have already discussed the refutation of the Negators (*ahl al-ta'til*), those who say that Allah does not become angry and does not become pleased, at His saying: ﴿And Allah became angry with him﴾. So what do the evidences support?

**Student:** The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And Allah became angry with him and cursed him﴾, and other verses.

**The Shaykh:** And other verses, such as?

**Student:** The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Say, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that as to what is due from Allah? [Worse is] those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He was angry and made from them apes and swine and slaves of Taghut."﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 60].

**The Shaykh:** Any other?

**Student:** His saying the Exalted: ﴿And when they angered Us (āsafūnā), We took retribution from them﴾.

**The Shaykh:** ﴿āsafūnā﴾ means: they angered Us.

**Student:** ﴿Other than those who have earned anger (al-maghḍūb 'alayhim)﴾.

**The Shaykh:** It does not explicitly state that the anger is from Allah.

**Student:** The verse of mutual cursing (*mula'anah*), O Shaykh: ﴿That the anger of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful﴾ [An-Nur 9].

**The Shaykh:** Its occurrence in several places in the Qur'an, and it not being interpreted as punishment, indicates what? Its occurrence in the Qur'an in several places, and it does not occur in a single place where it is meant as retaliation. What does that indicate?

**Student:** It indicates that anger is established for Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, by these verses.

**The Shaykh:** It indicates that by anger is meant the actual reality of anger. Yes, correct.

Why did these Negators deny that Allah be described as angry?

**Student:** They said: because anger is an ember that Satan throws into the heart of the son of Adam, and this is something from which Allah is to be exalted.

**The Shaykh:** Yes. They said: anger is the boiling of the blood of the heart, and this is not befitting for Allah. So what is the response to them?

**Student:** The answer: it is said that this anger belongs to the creature. As for the Creator, Glorified and Exalted is He, anger is for Him an attribute of perfection, not resembling the anger of creatures.

**The Shaykh:** It is an anger that does not resemble the anger of creatures. Our evidence is His saying the Exalted: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [Ash-Shura 11].

Why did they interpret anger as the intention of retribution, or as retribution itself?

**Student:** They turn away from this reality, because this is necessarily connected with anger; retribution is also necessarily connected with anger, so they interpreted it with that.

**The Shaykh:** No.

**Student:** Because they negate the voluntary attributes of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

**Another student:** Because they say: if we affirm the attribute of anger, it would be originated, and originated things do not subsist except…

**The Shaykh:** But why do they interpret it as will, as the intention of retribution or as retribution?

**Student:** Either they attach it to pre-eternity, or they attach it to the effect of the continuous state.

**The Shaykh:** Yes.

**Student:** Because they divert the originated anger to something else.

**The Shaykh:** Yes.

**Student:** They affirm the attribute of will.

**The Shaykh:** Correct. Because they affirm the attribute of will, the meaning of anger becomes the intention of retribution.

And why did they interpret it as retribution itself?

**Student:** (...) the real attribute (...).

**The Shaykh:** But why did they permit themselves to interpret anger as retribution?

**Student:** What the brothers mentioned: they say that if they affirmed it, it would necessarily entail, for example, that anger is the boiling of the blood of the heart, and so on. They say: and it would follow that this is also for Allah. And they, in their own view, want to exalt Allah above it.

**Another student:** Because retribution is an attribute separate from Allah, the Exalted.

**The Shaykh:** Correct. Retribution is the punishment, and punishment is separate from Allah; it is not an attribute in His essence. Therefore they affirmed it (as such).

Some scholars mentioned that the greatest thing we refute them with is His saying the Exalted: ﴿And when they angered Us, We took retribution from them﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 55]. What is the basis of that?

**Student:** That if anger is retribution, the verse would have no benefit, and the meaning would be: when We retributed against them, We retributed against them.

**The Shaykh:** Well done, correct. And the verse is explicit that the cause of the retribution is anger.

We have mentioned a principle on this subject: that everything Allah has described Himself with, it is obligatory upon us to affirm it and to believe that it does not resemble the attributes of creatures. This is what is obligatory upon us. As for diverting it from its apparent meaning to other meanings that we determine by our intellects, and you see them as contradictory, that is because we have said: whoever affirms one attribute and negates another is contradictory, because the statement regarding some attributes is like the statement regarding the others, as the scholars have established.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: whoever kills a believer deliberately, his recompense includes that he is cursed, that he is expelled from the mercy of Allah; by His saying: ﴿and cursed him﴾.

* Branching from this benefit: is it permissible for us to curse the killer by name, and say: "You are cursed, you are one upon whom anger rests," or not? The answer: No. Rather we say: you are one who has killed a believer deliberately, and whoever kills a believer, his recompense is Hell, to the end of the verse. So we distinguish between judging this man as cursed or not, because it is possible that he repents and the curse is removed.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah the Exalted has prepared punishment for whoever deserves it; by His saying: ﴿and prepared for him a great punishment﴾.

* Branching from this benefit: that the Fire exists now, and so it is. The Fire with which the disbelievers are punished exists now, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Baqarah 24]. And the Prophet (ﷺ) saw it during the prayer of the eclipse[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (86) and Muslim (905/11), from the hadith of 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her).]].

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the greatness of the punishment of the Fire; by His saying: ﴿great﴾. And "great", when a thing is described as great, it becomes according to the greatness of the one who describes it; that is, it is a thing great with a very great greatness.

* Student: The benefits of His saying the Exalted: ﴿And if he was from a people at enmity with you and he is a believer, then [the penalty is] the freeing of a believing slave﴾. We forgot them, O Shaykh; we did not mention its benefits.

* **The Shaykh:** Did we not pay attention to what? Or did we not mention its meaning?

* **Student:** We mentioned its meaning.

* **The Shaykh:** What is its meaning? Its meaning is: give me it.

* **Student:** "If he was from a people…" — that the man (i.e., the victim) has relatives who are numerous, so freeing a believing slave, and there is no blood money.

* **The Shaykh:** And there is no blood money. Why?

* **Student:** Because they are disbelievers and do not deserve blood money.

* **The Shaykh:** Why?

* **Student:** And there is no covenant between us and them.

* **The Shaykh:** Because if this man were one of those disbelievers, and he were of them (i.e., a disbeliever like them), blood money would be due to him if there were a covenant between us and them.

* **Student:** We said, O Shaykh: a disbeliever cannot be a Muslim.

* **The Shaykh:** And also, if we gave them (blood money), they would become strong with it against us.

* So, from the benefits of this noble verse: if the believing person killed has heirs who are disbelievers, then they have no blood money. First, because they cannot inherit from him while they are disbelievers, since a disbeliever does not inherit from a Muslim. Second, because if we gave it to them, they would be strengthened by it against us.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 94 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, blessed and exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who believe, when you go forth in the cause of Allah, investigate carefully﴾, to the end of the verse.

What is the benefit of introducing the address with the vocative? Because this has already passed over us?

* Student: (...) the address; second, this quality which (...) is one of the qualities of the hypocrite.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: Encouragement (al-ighra').
* Shaykh: This ighra' is for alerting (al-tanbih), no, no, yes.
* Student: (...) the address.
* Shaykh: This (...) the addressee mentioned it, mention this.
* Student: Indicating its importance.
* Shaykh: Correct, indicating the importance of the matter, and for this reason it is introduced with what calls for attentiveness. And what is the benefit of directing the call to the believers?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: First?
* Student: (...).
* Student: To indicate that complying with what is mentioned, whether a command or a prohibition, is among the requirements of faith.
* Shaykh: An alert that complying with what is mentioned, whether a command or a prohibition, is among the requirements of faith; and for this reason it is addressed to the believer. Second?
* Student: Second: that failing to comply with this command indicates a deficiency in the faith of one who does not carry it out.
* Shaykh: Yes, an indication that opposing this is among the deficiencies of faith, that is, among the things that diminish faith. Third?
* Student: Third, "and those who believe."
* Shaykh: Yes, directing the call to the believers.
* Student: Encouragement.
* Shaykh: Correct, encouragement; because when you describe the person: "O so-and-so, O believer," this urges him and makes him move forward, just as if you say: "O man, O you man," you urge him, saying: "The requirement of your manhood is such and such." So the benefits become how many? Three. We will not explain them now, because they were explained before.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, when you go forth in the cause of Allah﴾, meaning: when you go out as fighters (mujahidin) in the cause of Allah; because "striking" (ḍarb) occurs on the earth and intentions differ in it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And others travel through the land seeking of the bounty of Allah﴾ [al-Muzzammil 20]. These are the merchants. These, ﴿when you go forth in the cause of Allah﴾, meaning: you went out as fighters in the cause of Allah. ﴿Then investigate carefully﴾. This was revealed concerning a people who went out for jihad and encountered a people who said: "We have become Muslim," but they did not say it in this wording; rather they said: "Ṣabanā" (we have turned away). They thought that the meaning of their saying "ṣabanā" was "we have remained Ṣābiʾūn," that is, not Muslims, so they fought them. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Then investigate carefully﴾. There is also a reading: ﴿fatathabbatū﴾ in both places. That is, you recite: ﴿fatabayyanū﴾, then the one at the end of the verse: ﴿fatabayyanū﴾; or you recite ﴿fatathabbatū﴾ first, and recite ﴿fatathabbatū﴾ second. On this basis there are only two readings, not four readings. Meaning that if you recite the first as ﴿fatabayyanū﴾, then recite the second as ﴿fatabayyanū﴾, and if you recite the first as ﴿fatathabbatū﴾, then recite the second as ﴿fatathabbatū﴾. It is not permissible to differ: reciting the first ﴿fatabayyanū﴾ and the second ﴿fatathabbatū﴾, or the reverse. So the reading is two readings only.

And His saying: ﴿fatabayyanū﴾ means: seek to clarify the matter. Clarification (tabayyun) is the result of deliberation (tathabbut); for this reason the two readings are like the two meanings, one of which follows from the other. Which follows from the other: clarification or deliberation? Clarification; because you deliberate first so that the matter becomes clear to you. So in the two verses, that is in their combination, there is a great benefit: that you deliberate, and through deliberation the matter becomes clear, so you do not hasten. We have previously mentioned the blame of those hasty people in His saying, blessed and exalted: ﴿And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear, they spread it. And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, those who draw conclusions from them would have known it﴾ [an-Nisa' 83].

He says: ﴿fatabayyanū﴾, meaning: deliberate, and do not proceed to do something you will regret. How often a person regrets when he proceeds to something before clarification, even in his own personal affairs. If he intends to do an act, then merely upon something arising in his soul or heart he acts before he has considered the matter, before he has looked at the outcomes, and you find him regretful. How much more so if the act is related to another!

Often a person enters his house and finds the child crying out. "What is wrong with you, my son?" He says: "My brother hit me." Then the father strikes the brother whom the child claimed had hit him; and when the matter becomes clear, the mistake was from whom? From the child. We say: deliberate, do not proceed until the matter is clarified.

The reason for that is that a person is seized by jealousy (ghayra) and rushes forward. Jealousy, when it is not bound by a limit from the Sharia and a limit from reason, becomes ghayra... Do you know ghayra? Ghayra: the spoiling of food in the stomach, so that when a person belches a foul smell appears to him, as if it were rotten meat. So jealousy must be restrained by a limit of what? The Sharia and reason. For this reason He said: ﴿tabayyanū﴾.

﴿And do not say to him who offers you peace, "You are not a believer"﴾. The word "al-salām" has two readings: ﴿al-salam﴾ and ﴿al-salām﴾.

His saying: ﴿to him who offers you peace﴾ means: extends to you peace and conveys it to you; because he is a Muslim. So "al-salām" here means Islam. Do not say to him, "You are not a believer"; rather take him by what? By the apparent state of his condition; because this is what is obligatory upon us: to apply the rulings in this world according to the apparent state, since we do not know what is in the hearts. As for the Hereafter, the rulings are applied according to what? 
* Students: The hearts.
* Shaykh: According to what is in the hearts, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿On the Day when the secrets are tested﴾ [at-Tariq 9], and He said: ﴿Does he not know that when what is in the graves is scattered, and what is in the breasts is obtained?﴾ [al-'Adiyat 9, 10]. For this reason a person must be more concerned with the work of the heart than with the work of the limbs; because the work of the limbs may be corrupted by desire, a person may feign his deed for the world, to gain people's regard, for status, for wealth, or for something else. But the work of the heart cannot be feigned by a person, since it is not established except with sincerity, if it is sound.

His saying: ﴿You seek the goods of this worldly life﴾ — it is as if Allah, mighty and majestic, is alluding to the rebuke of those people who hastened. Among them were some who desired the spoils: ﴿seeking the goods of this worldly life﴾; because everything in this world is "ʿarad" (transient), meaning something that passes away, as is the reality. There is no doubt that the world is transient, and that it passes away or a person passes away from it. Either you lose the world or the world loses you; every person either becomes poor and loses what he has of the world, or he dies and wealth is lost to him. For this reason Allah, glorified and exalted, named the enjoyment of the world "ʿarad" (transient goods). Why? Because it passes away.

So what is the lasting thing? It is the reward of the Hereafter. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more lasting﴾ [al-A'la 16, 17]. ﴿With Allah are abundant spoils﴾. Glory be to Allah! When He rebuked them for desiring spoils in this incident that had occurred, He promised them that there are abundant spoils, as He said in Surah al-Fath: ﴿Allah has promised you many spoils that you will take﴾ [al-Fath 20]. So Allah, glorified and exalted, has abundant spoils, and how many spoils the Muslims gained in their campaigns! They gained great wealth, to the extent that it is said that dinars would be brought and placed in the mosque as if they were a spread of food, not in bags or hides; they were placed like that on the ground as if they were a spread of food or a mound of sand. And people gained great and abundant spoils in the time of the Islamic conquests.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Thus you were before﴾, meaning: like the state of these people. ﴿You were before﴾, meaning: Muslims or disbelievers? Disbelievers; you yourselves were disbelievers before you became believers, fighting the disbelievers so that the word of Allah would be supreme.

﴿Thus you were before, then Allah conferred favour upon you﴾. Favour (mann) is giving without price; that is, Allah, glorified and exalted, gave you a gift without price except gratitude, and gratitude in reality is not a price, not a price for the blessing; because Allah the Exalted does not benefit from it. Who benefits from it? The grateful servant. So Allah's blessing upon you in enabling you to give thanks is a blessing upon you; and if Allah willed, you would not have been grateful. On this the poet says:

If my thanks is a blessing from Allah, a blessing upon me for which thanks is due in its like...
How could thanks be fulfilled except by His grace, even if days are long and life continues?

So when Allah grants you success toward good, when He gives you a religious or worldly good and you then thank Him, your being enabled to thank is a blessing, which requires thanks; when you thank for this enablement, it becomes another blessing, and when you thank for that, it becomes another blessing. Therefore you cannot thank Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; you cannot reach full gratitude. For this reason among the remembrances reported from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was his saying: "Glory be to You, I cannot enumerate praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself" [Muslim (486/222), from the hadith of 'A'isha]. Yet despite that, Allah bestows favour upon us through Islam, we submit, and He rewards us for it. Then He says: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ [ar-Rahman 60]. Glory be to Allah! You are the one who does good to us first and last, and our works are not in comparison to Your goodness; rather our works are also from Your goodness. And He says: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾, and He says: ﴿This has been for you a reward, and your effort has been appreciated﴾ [al-Insan 22]. Glory be to Allah! Who enabled us for this striving? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; He thanks us for it, and He is the one who enabled us to it. The reality is that a person is, so to speak, filled with the favour of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; he cannot count the favour of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿If you should count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾ [an-Nahl 18]. For this reason He said: ﴿Then Allah conferred favour upon you, so investigate carefully﴾, repeating it for emphasis regarding the importance of the matter; and emphasis on a thing indicates its importance. For this reason He said: ﴿So investigate carefully; indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾, an indication that even if you hasten and claim, or show people, that you are deliberate, Allah is not hidden from your state; He knows your state. Al-Khabir is the One who knows the inner aspects of matters.

* In this noble verse there are many benefits:
* First: the importance of the ruling mentioned in it. What is its indication? The introduction with the vocative.
* Second: that complying with it is among the requirements of faith, because it is introduced by directing the address to the believers.
* Third: the virtue of the believers, in that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, addresses them with whatever rulings He wills. There is no doubt that Allah addressing a person by his person or his description is indeed an honour. People jostle at the courts of worldly kings; if this king says, "How are you this morning, so-and-so?" Just that, "How are you, so-and-so?" How do they count it? They count it an honour. So when Allah directs the address to the believers, that is an honour for them.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation of deliberation in matters, even in jihad in the cause of Allah; you must deliberate. What is the indication of that? His saying: ﴿fatabayyanū﴾, which is an imperative verb, and the basic principle of the imperative is obligation, especially in such grave matters.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that it is obligatory upon us to deal with people according to the apparent; by His saying: ﴿And do not say to him who offers you peace, "You are not a believer"﴾. He did not say "you are not a Muslim," because he offered peace and submitted; but do not say, "You are not a believer," meaning: faith has not entered his heart.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a warning against those people who accuse Muslims of showing off in their deeds. Some people—may Allah protect us—when they dislike a person and he is praised in their presence for performing good deeds, say: "This is a show-off (murā'in)." By this statement they become heirs to the hypocrites; because the hypocrites are ﴿those who slander the volunteers among the believers concerning charity, and those who find nothing but their effort﴾ [at-Tawbah 79].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that it is not permissible for us to go beyond the apparent that shows from a person, even if there are indications that point to the contrary of his apparent state. The evidence is ﴿And do not say to him who offers you peace, "You are not a believer"﴾.

An applied example of this occurred in the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family: "Usama ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, who was beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, overtook a man from among the polytheists and struck him with the sword. When Usama came upon him and overtook him, the man said: 'There is no god but Allah,' but Usama killed him." He thought, what? That he said it out of fear of death, and did not say it from his heart. This was reported to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, and he began to say: "Did you kill him after he said: There is no god but Allah? How will you deal with 'There is no god but Allah' when it comes on the Day of Resurrection?" Allahu Akbar! He kept repeating this until Usama said: "I wished that I had not become Muslim before that day" [Muslim (97/160), from the hadith of Jundub ibn 'Abdullah al-Bajali; its origin is in the Two Sahihs from the hadith of Usama ibn Zayd]; meaning: I wished that this had been in the state of my disbelief, so that I would become Muslim and what had passed would be forgiven me; because whoever becomes Muslim, Allah forgives him what preceded in his disbelief, whatever it was.

So I say: this indicates a warning and caution against judging people in a way that contradicts the apparent. We are not burdened with what we cannot bear. By Allah, if Allah had made our judgment of people according to the inner state, we would have perished. Who can verify the inner state? It is not possible. We have nothing but the apparent.

* Student: May Allah bless you. We said in the verse (...) that there are four readings (...)?
* Shaykh: No, I did not say, meaning in every case similar to this place. No; it may be, for example, that there are two alternating readings, but in this place they have stated: if he recites ﴿fatabayyanū﴾ in the first, he recites in the second.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: No, these are attributes; apparently there is no harm, but it does not change in one tashahhud.
* Student: If the disbelievers use Muslims as human shields, what do we do with them?
* Shaykh: He says: if the disbelievers use Muslims as shields, what do we do? Is it permissible to proceed to kill them or not? There is a difference of opinion among the scholars. Some say: if we cannot reach killing the disbelievers except by that, then the Muslim is killed and he is a martyr. Others say: no, because averting harms takes precedence over securing benefits. The closer view is that one looks at the public interest in that matter: they may shield with ten when they are a thousand, and they may shield with a thousand when they are ten, for example, and one looks to the public interest.
* Student: Were the three readings established in both places ﴿fatabayyanū﴾, in the first and the second?
* Shaykh: No, no, they are all one; there are only two readings. If you recite "tabayyanū" in the first, recite in what remains.

(...) This one whose name was not mentioned, and whoever is not named is unknown, and among the conditions for accepting a report is that the reporter be known, and among the conditions for answering a question is that the questioner be known. In any case, the answer. Let us read. Who is next?

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Those who sit at home among the believers, other than those with a harm, and those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives are not equal. Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit at home by a degree; and to each Allah has promised the best reward; and Allah has preferred those who strive over those who sit at home with a great reward, degrees from Him, and forgiveness and mercy. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.' Those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves, [the angels] will say, 'In what [condition] were you?' They will say, 'We were oppressed in the land.' [The angels] will say, 'Was not the earth of Allah spacious enough for you to emigrate therein?' For those, their refuge is Hell, and evil it is as a destination. Except the oppressed among men, women, and children who are unable to devise a plan and are not able to find a way. For those, perhaps Allah will pardon them, and ever is Allah Pardoning and Forgiving.﴾ [An-Nisa 95–99].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of Allah, investigate carefully, and do not say to one who gives you [a greeting of] peace, "You are not a believer"﴾.
What is the meaning of ﴿fatabayyanu﴾?
* Student: The other reading explains it, which is at-tathabbut, so verify (fatathabbatu).
* Shaykh: So there are two readings: ﴿tabayyanu﴾ and ﴿tathabbatu﴾. What is the meaning of ﴿tabayyanu﴾?
* Student: At-tabayyun is seeking clarity about a matter and verifying it.
* Shaykh: How? And ﴿tathabbatu﴾?
* Student: The same meaning.
* Shaship: No, we mentioned that there is a difference between them.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: At-tabayyun, at-tar'ruth (deliberation), and at-tathabbut.
* Student: At-tathabbut is seeking a general truth.
* Shaykh: The reality of the situation.
* Student: And at-tabayyun is the attainment of that and its becoming clear.
* Shaykh: So the two verses, or the two readings, are a premise and a result. ﴿Tathabbatu﴾ means seeking the reality of the matter and the situation, and ﴿tabayyanu﴾ means the matter becoming clear after verification, and this is the result: that a person's matter becomes clear to him. So the two readings are one for the premise and the second for the result.
Are the two readings distributed over each word individually, or do they apply to all?
* Student: The first ﴿tabayyanu﴾ ﴿tabayyanu﴾ or ﴿tathabbatu﴾ ﴿tathabbatu﴾.
* Shaykh: And the second is repeated?
* Student: Meaning: if you read the first as ﴿tabayyanu﴾, the second is ﴿tabayyanu﴾, and if you read the first as ﴿tathabbatu﴾, the second is ﴿tathabbatu﴾.
* Shaykh: No, it means that if you read one of them with one of the two readings, the second is the same reading. So there are only two readings. If we said they were distributed, there would be four readings.
The statement of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿seeking the fleeting goods of the worldly life﴾. What is the meaning of ﴿tabtaghuna﴾?
* Student: You desire.
* Shaykh: Does (ibtagha) mean (arada, to desire)?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Do you have evidence that ibtigha' here means desire? Is there evidence from the Qur'an?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: The statement of the brothers of Joseph: ﴿They said, "O our father, what could we desire?"﴾ [Yusuf 65], meaning what do we want.
* Shaykh: Any other?
* Student: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾ [Ali 'Imran 85].
* Shaykh: No, brother, I want an explanation of the verse exactly: ﴿tabtaghuna 'arada al-hayat al-dunya﴾. Is there in the Qur'an an exact parallel expressed with desire?
* Student: ﴿And others travel through the land seeking of the bounty of Allah﴾ [Al-Muzzammil 20].
* Shaykh: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You desire the goods of this world, while Allah desires the Hereafter﴾ [Al-Anfal 67].
Why was what is in this world called ʿaraḍ (goods)?
* Student: ʿaraḍ (...) because it presents itself and passes away.
* Shaykh: ʿaraḍ; because it presents itself and passes away. How many a rich person has become poor, and how many a poor person has become rich. Then a person either dies or his wealth is destroyed.
The statement of Allah: ﴿With Allah are abundant spoils﴾. What is the meaning relation of this sentence to what precedes it?
* Student: In meaning?
* Shaykh: Yes, in meaning (...).
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Well done, so that they may be reassured that Allah the Exalted has abundant spoils with Him.
Did this occur?
* Student: It occurred.
* Shaykh: Do you recall something?
* Student: What happened in the battle of Khaybar.
* Shaykh: Likewise, the wealth of Bahrain came and was piled up in the mosque, and likewise the Islamic conquests afterward; speak and there is no harm.
The statement: ﴿Thus you were before, then Allah conferred favour upon you﴾. What is the meaning relation of this sentence to what precedes it?
* Student: It reminds them that their condition was like the condition of these disbelievers.
* Shaykh: Well done; it reminds them that your condition was like the condition of these disbelievers: you were disbelievers and then you embraced Islam.
What is the difference between al-khabir and al-alim?
* Student: al-Khabir is the one who places a thing in its proper place.
* Shaykh: You mean the wise (al-hakim), this is the wise; I want al-khabir.
* Student: al-Khabir is the knower of matters.
* Shaykh: And al-alim?
* Student: al-Khabir is specific to the inner aspects of matters, and al-alim to their outward aspects.
* Shaykh: Correct. That is: al-alim, when mentioned alone, includes knowledge of inner and outer aspects; when mentioned with al-khabir, al-khabir is the knower of inner aspects and al-alim the knower of outward aspects, as in His statement: ﴿He said, "The Knowing, the Acquainted has informed me"﴾ [At-Tahrim 3].
The statement of Allah: ﴿Indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾. Why was the object placed first? Is the intent to convey exclusivity as the rule states, or is the intent something else? And what prevents the first meaning?
* Student: The intent here is not exclusivity, because Allah knows what man does and what others do.
* Shaykh: Exactly; what prevents it is that Allah is Acquainted with what they do and with other things. So what is the intent?
* Student: The intent is a threat.
* Shaykh: The intent is a threat to these people, as if He said, and Allah is far above what I assume: as if He said, "If I did not know anything, I would still be Knowing of what you do." So the benefit of this is not exclusivity, because Allah knows what these people do and others. The intent is a threat: that is, supposing I knew nothing, I would still be Knowing of what?
* Students: Of what you do.
* Shaykh: Of what you do. Pay attention to this benefit.
* From the benefits of the noble verse: Allah's knowledge of inner matters, by His statement: ﴿Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾. This is also supported by His statement: ﴿He is the First and the Last, the Apparent and the Hidden﴾ [Al-Hadid 3]. The Prophet (ﷺ) explained "the Hidden" as that beyond which there is nothing. Is that clear?
* From the benefits of the noble verse: a warning to a person against doing what does not please Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Do not think that if you do something it will be hidden from Allah; never. Whoever believes in this, and we ask Allah to make me and you among those who believe in it, will not undertake anything Allah does not approve, because he knows that He knows it, even in his heart. It guards his heart from deviation and being swept away when he knows that Allah the Exalted is Acquainted with what he does.
But these matters require discernment, and that a person be always watchful of Allah, fearful of Him. Whenever he intends something, he should remember the greatness of Allah and His knowledge of what he is about to do, so that he refrains. We ask Allah to revive our hearts with this, for we are heedless of these matters; desire overcomes guidance. You find a person, when he desires something, does it, and does not consider that he has a watchful recorder, nor that Allah the Exalted at that moment knows what he does. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "An adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer," meaning if he had faith he would not have committed adultery, because he knows that Allah sees him.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verses 95–96 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those who sit at home among the believers, other than those with a harm, are not equal to those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives.﴾ (Lā) here is a negation particle. ﴿Yastawī﴾ is a present-tense verb, ﴿al-qā'idūn﴾ is its subject, and ﴿al-mujāhidūn﴾ is conjoined to ﴿al-qā'idūn﴾. That is because some people wish for vain desires from Allah, wishing to be like those who strive in the way of Allah while they sit at home, and this is not possible. For this reason Allah negated equality, saying: ﴿Those who sit at home among the believers are not equal.﴾ Sitting at home from what? From jihad.

Then He said: ﴿other than those with a harm.﴾ There are two readings (qira'at) of ﴿ghayru﴾. The first is the nominative, ﴿ghayru﴾, as an adjective (ṣifah) of ﴿al-qā'idūn﴾. The second is the accusative, ﴿ghayra﴾, as an exception (mustathnā). Both are authentic readings of the seven recognised readings, so it is permissible to recite ﴿ghayru ulī al-ḍarar﴾ or ﴿ghayra ulī al-ḍarar﴾.

This is for you to know between yourself and yourself, or between yourself and your students who are people of knowledge and understanding. But with the general public, do not mention to them two readings, because in that there are two corruptions: a particular one and a general one. The particular one is that they will accuse you of error. We prayed behind an imam who made a grammatical error, saying: ﴿Lā yastawī al-qā'idūna min al-mu'minīna ghayra ulī al-ḍarar﴾, while what is in the Mushaf is ﴿ghayru ulī al-ḍarar﴾. So this imam is not fit for what? Because he makes errors in grammar.

The second is the general corruption: if people are told that he did not make an error but followed a second reading, it may diminish the greatness of the Qur'an in their souls. How can the Qur'an differ? The Qur'an, glory be to Allah, differs? Therefore it should not be said to every person that there are two readings in this. Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: «Speak to the people in what they know, that is, what their minds can grasp without aversion. Do you want Allah and His Messenger to be denied?»[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (127).]] The answer is no. So speak to people with what their minds can reach and what they can digest and understand. The meaning of his saying «Speak to the people in what they know» is not that you should tell them what they already know, because that has no benefit. What they already know needs no telling, except as a reminder after heedlessness, and that is possible.

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿other than those with a harm.﴾ And what is the harm? It is that which removes the obligation of jihad. Allah explained it in His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick﴾ [al-Fath 17]. These are the three excuses. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Tawbah 91]. The condition is ﴿when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger﴾. These are the people of excuses.

﴿And those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives.﴾ The mujāhid is the one who exerts his effort, that is, his capacity, in attaining what he seeks.

His saying ﴿in the way of Allah﴾ means in the law of Allah. This includes intention and action. The intention was explained by the Messenger (ﷺ) in his saying: «Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is the highest, he is in the way of Allah»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (123) and Muslim (1904 / 149), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]]. The action is that the jihad be in accordance with the Shari'ah, so that we undertake it when it is an obligation or a recommended act, and we refrain from it when its harm is greater than its benefit. Pay attention. For example, if the Islamic nation has a deficiency in weapons, in equipment, and also in numbers, while the nations opposing it are stronger in weapons and greater in numbers, is it commendable for us to fight? No. For this reason Allah did not make fighting obligatory upon the Islamic nation except when it was what? Prepared and capable: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you can of power﴾ [al-Anfal 60].

So ﴿in the way of Allah﴾ includes two meanings. The first meaning: intention, that the mujāhid's aim is to establish the law of Allah so that the word of Allah is the highest. The second meaning: that it be in accordance with the Shari'ah, because (fī) indicates location, and what is located is what? The way of Allah. This is the located thing. If you say: "The water is in the cup," the container is the cup and the contained is the water. Here the jihad in the way of Allah must be in the way of Allah, that is, in His law which He legislated.

His saying ﴿with their wealth and their lives﴾: the bā' here is like your saying: "I cut with the knife" and "I struck with the stick." It is for instrumentality, meaning that it indicates the instrument by which the jihad occurs. Jihad occurs with wealth and occurs with lives. Allah mentioned jihad with wealth first for two reasons. The first reason is that it is easier for a person, is it not? Fighting with wealth is generally easier for a person. The second thing is that its benefit may be greater, because a person himself fights and kills whom Allah wills, but if he is a man of great wealth and spends great sums, how many mujahideen can he support? Dozens, or hundreds, or more. ﴿And their lives﴾ means their selves.

Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic explained the aspect of the negation of equality, saying: ﴿Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit at home by a degree﴾. This degree Allah did not specify, but His saying the Exalted ﴿And for each are degrees according to what they did﴾ [al-An'am 132] indicates that this degree is a great and significant degree, not a small one. The Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned: «Indeed, in Paradise there are one hundred degrees which Allah the Exalted has prepared for those who strive in His way»[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (2790), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]].

﴿And to each Allah has promised the best reward.﴾ Here ﴿kullan﴾ may raise a question for us: why is it in the accusative?

* Student: A fronted object (mafʿūl muqaddam).
* Shaykh: A fronted object of what?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: And ﴿al-ḥusnā﴾?
* Student: A second object.
* Shaykh: A second object or first? A second object. And this is not from the construction of ishtighāl (verbal preoccupation). Why is it not from ishtighāl? Because the verb was not occupied with a pronoun of the object.

﴿And to each Allah has promised the best reward.﴾ ﴿Al-ḥusnā﴾ is Paradise, as the Prophet (ﷺ) explained it in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more﴾ [Yunus 26]. He said: «The best reward is Paradise, and the increase is looking at the Face of Allah»[[Narrated by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15 / 65), Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir (6 / 1495), and al-Daraqutni in Kitab al-Ru'yah (p. 156), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]]. So al-ḥusnā is Paradise. It is a description of a deleted noun, whose estimate is: "the promised good reward," Allah promised the good promise. It is a superlative (ism tafḍīl), as you know, meaning there is no ultimate goodness beyond it. Every goodness that exists is below it, because al-ḥusnā is the superlative form of the highest degree of goodness.

﴿And Allah has preferred those who strive over those who sit at home with a great reward.﴾ Look at the degree in the first verse, and the second ﴿Allah has preferred the mujāhidīn over the qā'idīn with a great reward.﴾ The first is in rank, and the second is in the reward, in its magnitude, the magnitude of the reward and the recompense.

﴿Allah has preferred those who strive over those who sit at home with a great reward (95). Degrees from Him, and forgiveness and mercy, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Allahu akbar. ﴿Degrees﴾ is either an apposition (badal) or an explanatory appositive (ʿaṭf bayān) of His saying ﴿reward﴾.

﴿Degrees from Him﴾: they are left vague in the verse, but the Messenger (ﷺ) said: «Indeed, in Paradise there are one hundred degrees which Allah has prepared for the mujāhidīn in the way of Allah»[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (2790), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]].

﴿And forgiveness﴾ means forgiveness of sins. ﴿And mercy﴾ means facilitation of what is sought. With the combination of forgiveness and mercy, what is feared is removed and what is sought is attained. What is feared is removed by forgiveness, meaning forgiveness of a sin for which one deserved punishment and was then forgiven. Mercy is the attainment of what is sought, and it is above forgiveness. For this reason forgiveness generally comes before mercy, because, as they say, "clearing comes before adorning." Forgiveness is repeated in the Noble Qur'an and in other than the Qur'an as well. We have passed that it is derived from what?

* Student: From al-mighfar.
* Shaykh: From al-mighfar, and what is it? What is al-mighfar?
* Student: It covers (...).
* Shaykh: The turban, meaning?
* Student: No, no, a cover (...).
* Shaykh: Meaning it is worn on the body?
* Student: It is not worn on the body.
* Shaykh: On what?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Meaning it is worn on the head? Made of wood?
* Student: A sword.
* Shaykh: A sword worn on the head? That is not the sword.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: It covers with what? Is the mighfar of wood or of pottery?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Leather. Does leather prevent a sword?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: And swords too, but of what material?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, correct. It is called the helmet (khūdhah), and it is a thing like a vessel worn on the head, made of iron, so that one is protected from arrows and protected from the sword. So it is derived from (al-mighfar). Then what is the meaning of the forgiveness of sins?
* Student: It means covering the sin and overlooking it.
* Shaykh: Well done. Covering the sin and overlooking it, because this is what derivation requires. Those who say that ghafr in the language is covering, did they encompass the meaning or not?
* Student: They encompassed it.
* Shaykh: They encompassed it. So is this skullcap considered a mighfar, because it covers?
* Student: It does not encompass.
* Shaykh: So it must be completed?
* Student: With protection.
* Shaykh: With protection. Well done. Not every covering is a protection.

﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

* In this noble verse there are several benefits:
* Among them: the negation of equality among people. It is strange that we hear someone who often repeats, saying: "The religion of Islam is a religion of equality." This is an error against the religion of Islam. The religion of Islam is not a religion of equality, but a religion of justice, which is giving each person what he deserves. For this reason you find in the Noble Qur'an that most of the Qur'an is the negation of equality, not its affirmation: ﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ [al-An'am 50], ﴿Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ [al-Zumar 9], ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought﴾ [al-Hadid 10], and so on.

The claim that Islam is a religion of equality may in reality lead to a dangerous principle. First: equating males with females, and that preferring males over females is considered contrary to the religion of Islam. Second: socialism, equalizing people in sustenance, so that we take from the wealth of the rich and give it to the poor, because the religion is a religion of equality. If they had said the religion is a religion of consolation (mu'āsāh), it would have been correct. For this reason condolences are legislated in calamities and similar things.

* Student: Does the indefiniteness of ﴿darajah﴾ indicate magnification or belittlement?
* Shaykh: Apparently it indicates magnification, meaning a great degree. For this reason He later explained it as degrees.
* Student: In other contexts, outside the Qur'an, it comes to indicate diminution.
* Shaykh: In any case, the indefiniteness of a word has many meanings according to what it is described with. An indefinite noun may be described by what indicates paucity or by what indicates abundance.
* Student: The saying ﴿Degrees from Him, and forgiveness and mercy﴾, is it an explanation of His saying ﴿a great reward﴾ or an explanation of His saying ﴿a degree﴾?
* Shaykh: No, apparently it is for ﴿a great reward﴾, because forgiveness and mercy do not come in the rank.
* Student: (...) So how can we (...) it is obligatory upon us (...) ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were humiliated﴾.
* Shaykh: This is a special matter. And ﴿How many a small company has overcome a large company﴾ [al-Baqarah 249]. But this is a special matter concerning Badr. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, and He knows that among you is weakness. So if there are among you one hundred who are patient, they will overcome two hundred﴾ [al-Anfal 66], and He permitted the people to flee from their enemy when they were outnumbered more than two to one.
* Student: Do such verses support the view of the one who says: when jihad occurs in the Book and the Sunnah, what is meant by it is fighting the disbelieving enemies, so that the verse ﴿Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ is understood as generally applying, and that the scholarly jihad is achieved by carrying out these verses?
* Shaykh: No. The hypocrites: jihad against the hypocrites is not possible except with knowledge.
* Student: By way of parallelism (mushākalah)?
* Shaykh: No, no, by way of reality. He said in the Qur'an: ﴿And strive against them with it a great striving﴾ [al-Furqan 52].
* Student: Is it by way of naming?
* Shaykh: No, by way of truth. How many a person exhausts you in debating him in religion?
* Student: We benefited from the previous verse that it is not permissible to transgress a person's outward appearance, even with peers.
* Shaykh: Transgress?
* Student: A person's outward appearance.
* Shaykh: A person's outward appearance, what is its color?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: A person's outward appearance, or the outward state?

* Student: In other contexts, outside the Qur'an, it comes to indicate diminution.
* Shaykh: In any case, the indefiniteness of a word has many meanings according to what it is described with. An indefinite noun may be described by what indicates paucity or by what indicates abundance.
* Student: The saying ﴿Degrees from Him, and forgiveness and mercy﴾, is it an explanation of His saying ﴿a great reward﴾ or an explanation of His saying ﴿a degree﴾?
* Shaykh: No, apparently it is for ﴿a great reward﴾, because forgiveness and mercy do not come in the rank.
* Student: (...) So how can we (...) it is obligatory upon us (...) ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were humiliated﴾.
* Shaykh: This is a special matter. And ﴿How many a small company has overcome a large company﴾ [al-Baqarah 249]. But this is a special matter concerning Badr. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, and He knows that among you is weakness. So if there are among you one hundred who are patient, they will overcome two hundred﴾ [al-Anfal 66], and He permitted the people to flee from their enemy when they were outnumbered more than two to one.
* Student: Do such verses support the view of the one who says: when jihad occurs in the Book and the Sunnah, what is meant by it is fighting the disbelieving enemies, so that the verse ﴿Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ is understood as generally applying, and that the scholarly jihad is achieved by carrying out these verses?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 95–96 (part 2 of 2):

* The Shaykh: No, the hypocrites. Jihad against the hypocrites is not possible except through knowledge.
* The student: By way of mushakalah (similarity of expression)?
* The Shaykh: No, no. It is by way of reality, for He said in the Quran: ﴿So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with it, a great striving﴾ [al-Furqan 52].
* The student: Is it by way of naming?
* The Shaykh: No, it is by way of truth. How many a person exhausts you in debating him concerning the religion.
* The student: We benefited from the previous verse that it is not permissible to go beyond a person's outward appearance, even by means of indicators.
* The Shaykh: Go beyond?
* The student: A person's outward appearance.
* The Shaykh: A person's outward appearance, what is it like?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Is it the person's outward appearance or the outward state?
* The student: The outward state. We established earlier that it is a condition in the matter of circumstantial evidence (...) oaths and vows.
* The Shaykh: It enters under verification (tabayyun). Acting on circumstantial evidence falls under verification.
* The student: Even if circumstantial evidence appears here (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes. But people's accountability in Islam is according to the outward, their accountability is according to the outward. As for matters of rulings and judging between them, one acts on circumstantial evidence; but as between them and Allah, one acts on the outward.
* * *
* Student: ﴿They will say, "In what were you?" They will say, "We were oppressed in the land." The angels will say, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious that you could emigrate therein?" For those, their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination. (97) Except for the oppressed among men, women and children who are unable to devise a plan and do not find a way. (98) For those, it is hoped that Allah will pardon them; and Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.﴾ [an-Nisa' 97–99].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. We discussed the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers, other than those with a disability﴾, and in it there are two readings, ﴿ghayru﴾ and ﴿ghayra﴾. On the reading of raf', it is an adjective (sifah); on the reading of nasb, it is an exception (istithna').

I think we had begun extracting benefits and reached...?
* Student: The equality.
* The Shaykh: One benefit, which is the negation of equality or parity between those who sit out from fighting and those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their selves.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the wisdom of the Shari'ah, in that it does not equate between those who differ, just as it does not differentiate between those who are equal. The Islamic Shari'ah comes from One who is All-Wise and All-Aware. You will not find in it two contradictory rulings, nor will you find in it two things alike that then differ in ruling, never. Rather, if it appears to you that two things are alike while they differ in ruling according to the Shari'ah, then reconsider, reconsider again and again until it becomes clear to you. If it does not become clear, then suspect your understanding, and do not accuse the Shari'ah rulings.
* Among the benefits of these noble verses: that whoever sits out from jihad due to a harm is like one who performed jihad, based on His saying: ﴿Not equal are those who sit [at home]﴾ ﴿and the strivers﴾, then He made an exception saying: ﴿other than those with a disability﴾. So those with a disability are, therefore, equal to the strivers. This is supported by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) at the Battle of Tabuk: "Indeed, in Medina there are people; you have not traveled any journey nor crossed any valley except that they were with you." They said: "How, O Messenger of Allah, when they are in Medina?" He said: "They are in Medina; the excuse has held them back." [Reported by al-Bukhari (4423), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]
Does this apply to everyone who is prevented from an act of worship by an excuse? The answer is: Yes. For this reason, in the authentic hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever falls ill or travels, there is recorded for him what he used to do while healthy and resident." [Reported by al-Bukhari (2996), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the virtue of jihad in the way of Allah with wealth and self, and its basis: they are of a higher rank than those who sit out and do not strive.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that reward is of the same kind as the deed. Mention to me the evidence from the verse. What is the reason?
* Student: That Allah, Glorified and Exalted, (...).
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: That Allah rewarded them for (...).
* The Shaykh: ﴿Allah has preferred those who strive﴾ is explicit: ﴿Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their selves over those who sit [at home] by a degree.﴾ It follows from this benefit that the difference in reward indicates the difference in the doer.
It may also be derived from it a second benefit: its use as evidence for the position of the People of the Sunnah that faith increases and decreases; it increases by obedience and decreases by disobedience, as is well known, and by other causes.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the fine precaution (ihtiras) in the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Its basis: when Allah mentioned the virtue of the strivers over those who sit [at home], one might imagine that the rank of the believers who sit [at home] has been lowered, so Allah removed this illusion by saying: ﴿And to each Allah has promised the best﴾. This is the method of the Quran.
Look at the second example that matches this: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest; those are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterwards. But to each Allah has promised the best﴾ [al-Hadid 10]. And look at a third example: ﴿And [mention] David and Solomon when they judged concerning the field when the sheep of a people grazed therein by night, and We were witnesses to their judgment. And We gave understanding of it to Solomon, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge﴾ [al-Anbiya' 78–79]. The evidence is in His saying: ﴿and to each We gave judgment and knowledge﴾. So these three examples show that it is part of the eloquence of speech to apply precaution by removing what might be imagined.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the good tidings to the general body of believers, both those who sit [at home] and the strivers, of the best (al-husna), based on His saying: ﴿And to each Allah has promised the best﴾.
Does it follow from this benefit that we testify for every believer that he is in Paradise? The answer: In general terms, yes. In specific terms, we stop at what the text has stated. For example, we say: all the Companions, Allah promised them Paradise, both the striver and the one who sat out. But a specific individual cannot be testified for unless the Prophet (ﷺ) has testified for him. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, added: Whoever is praised with good by the people, we testify for him with Paradise. He cited as evidence the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Baqarah 143], and he cited what is established in the Sunnah: "A funeral procession passed by, and those present praised the deceased with good, so the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'It is obligatory.' Then another passed, and they spoke ill of it, and he said: 'It is obligatory.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is obligatory?' He said: 'As for the first, you praised him with good, so Paradise became obligatory for him; and as for the second, you spoke ill of him, so the Fire became obligatory for him.' Then he said: 'You are the witnesses of Allah on earth.'" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1367) and Muslim (949/60), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.] So Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, derived that testimony is permissible for one whom the Ummah agrees in praising, and he gave as examples the well-known imams attested to for justice, faith and piety, such as the four imams: Imam Ahmad, al-Shafi'i, Malik and Abu Hanifah, and Sufyan al-Thawri, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, and others whom the Ummah has agreed in praising.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that there is no virtue greater than Paradise. From where is this derived? From His saying: ﴿al-husna﴾, because (al-husna) is the feminine superlative of (ahsan).
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the encouragement to jihad in the way of Allah. The indication: Allah's preference of the strivers over those who sit [at home] by a degree, rather by degrees.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the magnitude of Allah's favor upon the servants, in that He made their recompense for deeds like the wage a person deserves as an obligation on the employer; based on His saying: ﴿a great reward﴾. He called it a wage (ajr) just as the worker's wage, although the favor belongs to Allah, Exalted, first and last. It is He who enabled you to act, and He who bestowed upon you the reward for it.
If someone asks: Is there any support for this meaning you have mentioned?
We say: Yes. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed upon Himself mercy: that whoever of you does evil in ignorance and then repents after that and corrects himself, indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-An'am 54]. He prescribed mercy, prescribed upon Himself. He, Glorified and Exalted, obligates upon Himself and upon His servants whatever He wills, and no one objects to Him.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the greatness of the ranks of the strivers in the way of Allah. The basis of this is His saying: ﴿degrees from Him﴾. He attributed them to Himself. It is known that a gift is greater in proportion to the greatness of the giver. If you say, for example: "So-and-so gave charity," and he is among the richest of people, your mind goes to his having given a great deal. If you say: "So-and-so gave charity," and he is poor, your mind goes only to his having given a small amount. For this reason He said: ﴿degrees from Him﴾. Attributing a thing to Allah indicates its greatness. Among that is the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying in the supplication he taught Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) to recite in his prayer: "So forgive me with forgiveness from You, and have mercy upon me." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (834) and Muslim (2705/48), from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.]
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of forgiveness for Allah, based on His saying: ﴿and forgiveness﴾.
Is forgiveness established for other than Allah? Yes, it is established for others. Allah said: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon and overlook and forgive, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [at-Taghabun 14]. And Allah said: ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [ash-Shura 43].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of mercy for Allah. Mercy which Allah attributed to Himself is of two types: an attribute, and a created thing. That is, of two types: one of them is an attribute of Allah, and another is a creation of Allah's creations that Allah named mercy. From the first is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And your Lord is the Forgiving, Possessor of mercy﴾ [al-Kahf 58]; this is an attribute. From the second is His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain after they have despaired and spreads His mercy﴾ [ash-Shura 28]; here the meaning of mercy is what is the effect of the rain of plants and other than plants.
And from that also is His saying, Glorified and Exalted: ﴿As for those whose faces will be whitened, they will be in the mercy of Allah, wherein they will abide eternally﴾ [Aal 'Imran 107]. What is meant by mercy here? Paradise, by the evidence of His saying: ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire﴾ [Hud 106]. Is this mercy created or uncreated? It is created. And from it is His saying in the divine hadith about Paradise: "You are My mercy; I have mercy upon whom I will through you."  [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4850) and Muslim (2846/34), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]
Thus it becomes clear that mercy is divided into what? Two types: created and attribute. The created is among the totality of creations, something separate from Allah, attributed to Him only as an attribution of creation and bringing into existence, yet it is one of the effects of the mercy which is the attribute. As for the mercy which is an attribute, it is an attribute inseparable from the Essence, that is, the Essence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of these two names for Allah, and they are what? Al-Ghafur (the Forgiving) and al-Rahim (the Merciful), ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾, and their explanation has already passed.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verses 95–96 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those who sit at home among the believers, other than those with a harm, are not equal to those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives.﴾ (Lā) here is a negation particle. ﴿Yastawī﴾ is a present-tense verb, ﴿al-qā'idūn﴾ is its subject, and ﴿al-mujāhidūn﴾ is conjoined to ﴿al-qā'idūn﴾. That is because some people wish for vain desires from Allah, wishing to be like those who strive in the way of Allah while they sit at home, and this is not possible.
