[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1494) and Muslim (1076/174), from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]], and when they said: "We have nothing," he said: "Did I not see the cooking pot on the fire?" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5097) and Muslim (1504/14), from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]], and he did not know, perhaps it was water boiling. The Prophet (ﷺ) does not know the unseen at all.

Allah, exalted, has said a general statement in His great Book: ﴿He is the Knower of the unseen, and He does not reveal His unseen to anyone, except to a messenger whom He has chosen. Then indeed He makes a guard go before him and behind him﴾ [al-Jinn 26-27]. He does not give him knowledge of everything, even the Hour. Jibril came to the Messenger and asked: When is the Hour? What did he say? He said: "The one asked about it knows no more than the one asking" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (50) and Muslim (9/5), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]].

So the most noble of the messengers among the angels, and the most noble of the messengers among mankind, both do not know the unseen; neither knows when the Hour will be.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of Allah's favour upon His Messenger (ﷺ) and its greatness, based on His saying: ﴿and the favour of Allah upon you has been great﴾.

* This may branch from this benefit: that the greatest favour Allah bestows upon the servant is knowledge, and there is no doubt in this. Then this is good news for the people of knowledge: when Allah teaches them from His law what He has taught them, they are indeed the heirs of the Prophet (ﷺ), since He has taught them from his law what they did not know.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 114 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk, except for those who enjoin charity, or what is right, or reconciliation between people.﴾

His saying: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk.﴾ The word (najwa) (secret talk). First: the grammatical analysis (i'rab). ﴿There is no good﴾: this is (la) of generic negation (la nafiya lil-jins), and its noun is ﴿khayra﴾. What is its i'rab?
* Student: A noun of la of generic negation.
* Shaykh: Complete.
* Student: (...) indeclinable.
* Shaykh: Complete.
* Student: (La) is the la of generic negation, and khayr is the noun of la, indeclinable, based on..
* Shaykh: The noun of (la) is indeclinable, built on the fatha, in a position of nasb?
* Student: In a position of nasb..
* Shaykh: In a position of nasb, built on the fatha in a position of nasb.
And ﴿fi kathirin﴾ is its predicate.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, "there is no good in much of such-and-such."
His saying: ﴿min﴾ and ﴿illa man﴾: this is a substitution (badal). His saying: ﴿min najwahum﴾ may be a plural, as in His saying: ﴿There is no secret conference of three but that He is their fourth﴾ [al-Mujadila 7], so (najwa) here means those conferring in secret (mutanajjin).
﴿There is no secret conference of three but that He is their fourth﴾, meaning: there is no gathering of three secretly conferring but that He is their fourth. It may also be a verbal noun (masdar), and on this reading the meaning is: there is no good in much of the private conversation of those who confer secretly. This is in terms of grammar; in terms of meaning it is one and the same, without difference. The meaning is that much of what these people confer about in secret contains no good, and only the little of it contains good.
His saying: ﴿illa man amara﴾: is (man) in need of a supposed noun (taqdir al-mudaf), so that we say the estimate is: "except the secret talk of one who..."? Or is it not in need? We say: this depends on the word (najwahum). If we say it is a verbal noun, it needs the estimate, meaning: except the secret talk of whoever..; and if we say (najwa) means those conferring in secret, then (man) here does not need an estimate, because the meaning is: there is no good in much of those conferring in secret except whoever enjoins, for in them there is good.
What is najwa? Whether we say it means those conferring or that it is a verbal noun, najwa is speech which a person whispers to his companion. This is najwa, and its ruling will be explained, God willing.
﴿except for those who enjoin charity﴾, meaning: except the secret talk of one who enjoins. This is if we say the first (najwa) is a verbal noun; and if we say it is a verbal noun in the sense of plural, then no estimate is needed. That is: except one who enjoins charity, or good conduct, or reconciliation between people, three things.
﴿man amara bi-sadaqa﴾ means: he said to another: "Give charity." This word (taṣaddaq) (give charity), if it is spoken by one above, it is a command (amr); if by an equal, it is a request and counsel. It includes both this and that: whether the one who gives the command has authority over the one addressed, or the one who gives the command has no authority but says it by way of what? Sincere advice and pointing the way.
His saying: ﴿bi-sadaqa﴾ is indefinite (munakkar), and indefiniteness indicates generality, so it includes the little and the much.
﴿or what is right﴾: al-ma'ruf is what is not blameworthy (munkar), and it is more general than charity, because charity is a kindness, while al-ma'ruf is what people recognize as good even if it is not charity, such as enjoining forbearance, enjoining keeping ties of kinship, enjoining kindness, if it does not fall under charity; and if we restrict charity to the charity of wealth.
﴿or reconciliation between people﴾: reconciliation (islah) is the removal of corruption between people, such as when there is enmity between two persons and someone strives to remove that enmity. This is reconciliation, and it is among the best deeds that bring one near to Allah.
His saying: ﴿between people﴾ includes Muslims and non-Muslims. Reconciliation between people is good, whether you reconcile between Muslims, or between disbelievers, or between Muslims and disbelievers. From where is the generality taken? From His saying: ﴿people﴾.
Then He said: ﴿And whoever does that﴾, the referent being what preceded: the command to charity, what is right, and reconciliation.
﴿seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾: (ibtigha') means seeking. ﴿the pleasure of Allah﴾ means: seeking that Allah be pleased with him.
﴿then We will give him a great reward﴾: the fa' here is the connecting particle for the response (jawab), the response of (man) in His saying: ﴿And whoever does that﴾. So why is the response joined with fa'?
* Student: Because it is joined with the verb of the condition.
* Shaykh: Because the response is joined with (sawfa). Can you give us a verse that includes that, that is, what must be linked with fa'?
* Student:
Nominal and imperative, and with ja'mid, with ma, qad, la, and with tanfis.
* Shaykh: Well done, these are seven things. Ibn Malik, however, gave a rule for it. What is it?
* Student:
Join with fa' definitely the response if it is made the condition for "in" or other than it, which does not take it.
* Shaykh: Well done.
Join with fa' definitely the response if it is made the condition for "in" or other than it, which does not take it.
Meaning: whatever cannot properly follow "in" must be joined with fa'. This is a rule, and what our brother indicated in the verse is detail. But what Ibn Malik mentioned has a benefit, namely the indication that it must be joined with fa'. So what is the reason?
The reason is that it cannot properly be a verb of the condition; and when it cannot be a verb of the condition, it cannot be a response, and therefore it must be joined with fa'. Is that clear, everyone? The verse:
Join with fa' definitely the response if it is made the condition for "in" or other than it, which does not take it.
What is its general meaning? Its meaning is that when the response cannot properly be a verb of the condition, it must be joined with fa'. This is the ruling. Why? Because what cannot be a condition cannot be a response, so it must be joined with fa'.
﴿then We will give him a great reward﴾. In His saying ﴿nu'tihi﴾ there are two Sab'i readings: ﴿nu'tihi﴾ and ﴿yu'tihi﴾. As for the reading ﴿yu'tihi﴾, it follows the flow of the speech, because His saying is: ﴿seeking the pleasure of Allah, then He will give him﴾, meaning Allah, ﴿a great reward﴾.
If it is ﴿yu'tihi﴾, it follows the flow of speech, because the whole speech is in the third person; and if He says ﴿then We will give him﴾, then it has departed from the flow of speech, and this is called iltifat (shift of person), and every shift must have a benefit according to the context.
* This noble verse contains many benefits. First: that much of people's speech contains no good. So what is the criterion for what contains good and what does not? The criterion was stated by the Prophet (ﷺ) in his saying: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say what is good or keep silent" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6018), (47/75), from Abu Hurayra]. This is one. And in his saying (ﷺ): "Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him" [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2317) and Ibn Majah (3976), from Abu Hurayra], and "in his prohibition (ﷺ) of qil wa qal (gossip) and excessive questioning" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6473), and Muslim (593/12), from al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba]. These are three hadiths, all showing what the good in speech is. The first?
* Student: The saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say what is good or keep silent."
* Shaykh: And the second?
* Student: "Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him."
* Shaykh: The second.
* Student: The saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him."
* Shaykh: This is what we said, the second, brothers. This is the second?
* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: The third?
* Student: "He forbade qil wa qal."
* Shaykh: Yes, he forbade qil wa qal and excessive questioning.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of charity. Its basis is that if the one who commands charity has good in his command, then the one who gives charity is more deserving of it, without doubt.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: encouraging a person to command good and kindness, from His saying: ﴿except for those who enjoin charity, or what is right, or reconciliation between people﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of commanding reconciliation between people.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk, except for those who enjoin charity, or what is right, or reconciliation between people. And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah, We will give him a great reward (114). And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers, We will leave him in what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination﴾ [an-Nisa' 114-115].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. His exalted saying: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk, except for those who enjoin charity, or what is right﴾ to the end. What is meant by najwa in His saying: ﴿of their secret talk﴾?
* Student: Najwa admits of one of two meanings: either it is a plural, as in His saying: ﴿There is no secret conference of three﴾, or it is a verbal noun, meaning: there is no good in much of their private conversation.
* Shaykh: Their private conversation, correct. And based on this, is ﴿except for those who enjoin﴾ an exception?
* Student: ﴿Except for those who enjoin﴾: if we say najwa is a verbal noun, then the estimate is a noun being supplied.
* Shaykh: The estimate?
* Student: The estimate: except the private conversation of one who enjoins; and if we say it is a plural, then no estimate is needed.
* Shaykh: Well done. His saying: ﴿except for those who enjoin charity, or what is right, or reconciliation between people﴾: these three things, what is the difference between them?
* Student: Al-ma'ruf is more general, including charity and reconciliation. Charity here relates to the body, and reconciliation relates to wealth, and reconciliation relates to..
* Shaykh: What relates to wealth?
* Student: Charity.
* Shaykh: Charity. Good. Al-ma'ruf is more general, whether it is by wealth or by action. ﴿Or reconciliation between people﴾?
* Student: Between two groups, as in His saying, glorified and exalted: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make reconciliation between them﴾ [al-Hujurat 9].
* Shaykh: So reconciliation between people is something whose benefit extends to others. All these three things extend their benefit to others: charity, what is right, and the third, reconciliation between people. What is derived from His saying: ﴿And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾?
* Student: That worship must have two conditions: sincerity to Allah, and following (the Prophet's way).
* Shaykh: The obligation to take care with sincerity, that without sincerity there is no good in it, and that without sincerity no great reward is produced by it even if there is good in it, because it is transitive; but the great reward is not attained by it.
We have taken four benefits, I think as you said, I forgot them. What are they?
* Student: The first: that much of people's speech contains no good.
The second: the virtue of charity.
The third: encouraging people to command charity.
The fourth: the matter of commanding reconciliation between people.
* Shaykh: Yes. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse also: the virtue of commanding what is right; since Allah the Exalted joined it with commanding charity, from His saying: ﴿except for those who enjoin charity﴾. What is al-ma'ruf? Al-ma'ruf is everything the Shari'a recognizes and approves; and everything it denies and forbids is munkar.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the clarification that these three matters contain good even if a person does them without intending to seek the face of Allah. Its basis is that when Allah the Exalted negated good from much of the secret talk, He made an exception of these three, then said: ﴿And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah, then We will give him a great reward.﴾
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that it is valid to apply the verb (fa'ala, to do) to speech. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿And whoever does that﴾, although what occurred was a command to charity, what is right, or reconciliation. This holds if we say the referent is the command understood from (amara); but if we say the referent is charity, what is right, and reconciliation, then it is an act and there is no difficulty, because the referent is disputed, as we mentioned earlier.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's pleasure, the Mighty and Majestic, from His saying: ﴿seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾. Is pleasure an attribute of action (sifa fi'liyya) or an essential attribute (sifa dhatiyya)? It is said: it is an attribute of action, because every attribute connected to Allah's will, which He may do or not do, is an attribute of action. This is the criterion, and pleasure is connected to will, because its cause is the act with which Allah is pleased, and the act with which Allah is pleased follows what? Allah's will; since it is the act of the servant, and the act of the servant occurs by Allah's will. So pleasure is among the attributes of action. It should be known that the attributes of action, taken as a genus, are all essential attributes, but their types and individual instances are those that occur; as for their root, which is the act itself, it is an attribute of what? Essential.
The proof: Allah the Exalted has never ceased and never ceases to act; but what is renewed is the types or individual instances of action. For example, istiwa' (settling) on the Throne: is its type something that occurred or not? It is something whose type occurred, because we know of no act that is istiwa' except what is specific to the Throne, and what is specific to the Throne certainly occurred after the creation of what? After the creation of the Throne.
Descent to the lowest heaven is also of a type that occurred, and its individual instances occur too, because Allah descends every night. Istiwa' on the Throne is absolute and general; that is, it is not limited to a night, nor a day, nor a week, nor a month; but descent occurs every night. So it is clear now that the root of the attributes of action is what? Essential. Why? Because Allah has never ceased and never ceases to act. If you ask: what is the proof of this? We say: because action is perfection, and if we said that a time could pass over Him when He was not acting, that would be a deficiency in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; for if we said of one over whom a time passed that he was not acting, why? Because he was unable?!
If you say: unable, this is problematic; and if you say: able, we say: bring the proof for the limitation; for limiting what no evidence establishes is arbitrariness. From what moment did the act become possible for Him? So we say that the root of the attributes of action is what? Essential, because Allah has never ceased and never ceases to act; and as for their types and individual instances, they are attributes of action, because they are connected to His will, blessed and exalted.
According to the people of ta'til (denial of attributes), such as the Ash'aris, the Mu'tazilites, the Jahmites, and those who resemble them, they say: Allah has no pleasure. But they do not deny it with outright denial, only with denial by interpretation (ta'wil). For example, when they say: He has no pleasure.
We say: if you deny pleasure by outright denial, this is a rejection of the Qur'an, and one who rejects the Qur'an is a disbeliever. But if they say: yes, Allah has pleasure, but by pleasure is meant such-and-such, this is called denial by interpretation, and they are not declared disbelievers for that, unless the innovation is a major one that causes disbelief; but that is another matter.
How do they explain pleasure? They say: pleasure is reward. It is said: reward is not pleasure, because reward is a separate act distinct from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So He rewards those with whom He is pleased, rewarding them with something separate and distinct from Allah: with Paradise and its bliss, with a good life in this world, and similar things. Therefore their explanation of pleasure as reward is wrong. We say: if you explain it as reward, it necessarily follows that pleasure is established; for one cannot reward except one with whom he is pleased. He never rewards one he is angry with; he rewards only one he is pleased with. Therefore, however much they flee from denying pleasure, it will necessarily be implied for them, and despite their struggle and distortion, they can never escape it at all.

Among the most comfortable and easiest of the creeds is the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah (the People of the Sunnah and the Community), the creed of the Salaf (the righteous predecessors), who say: "What Allah has affirmed for Himself, we affirm, and what He has negated of Himself, we negate." So they say, for example: "We affirm for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the attribute of being pleased, as He affirmed it for Himself, and we negate of Him likeness, as He negated it of Himself, when He said: ﴿There is nothing like Him﴾ [Ash-Shura 11]. And what harm does that do us?" They also negate takyif (specifying the modality of the attributes), because we have no knowledge of it, and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge﴾ [Al-Isra 36]. So you find the creed of the Salaf easy, with no anxiety in it and no contradiction. Contradiction is found only with the people of tahrif (distortion), such as the Mu'tazilah (a rationalist school that denied the attributes of Allah) and others.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse also: the affirmation of the attributes of action, in His saying: ﴿We will give him a great reward﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a person should not hasten to seek the reward, since Allah may delay the reward for a wisdom. From where is this taken? From the word "sawfa" (soon/will), which indicates postponement. It indicates certainty, but it also indicates that the matter is not expected to come soon, rather it may be far off. For this reason, do not hasten Allah's reward, nor even His answering of supplication, as in the hadith: «One of you is answered so long as he does not hasten, saying: "I supplicated, but I was not answered."» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6340) and Muslim (2735/90), from Abu Hurayrah.]

Likewise, do not hasten to expect the reward. Furthermore, a person should also, and we ask Allah to help us and you to do so, when he does a righteous deed, not hasten to seek the reward of this world, so that he does not become one who desires the world. For example, whoever believes and does righteous deeds, Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾ [An-Nahl 97].

If you do a deed in order that Allah give you a good life, this is without doubt good. But better than that is that you intend the reward of the Hereafter, and the reward of this world comes to you. If you desire the reward of both this world and the Hereafter, there is no harm, because Allah did not mention the reward of this world to us in vain, but to stir up determination and move souls. Otherwise, every reward that Allah mentioned in this world would be considered, what? Vain and meaningless. So there is no blame on a person for intending the reward of this world and the Hereafter together. But if he intends only the reward of this world, this is without doubt a deficiency in sincerity.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the greatness of the one who does that seeking the Face of Allah; the greatness of his reward, due to His saying: ﴿We will give him a great reward﴾, because the magnification of a thing from the Great indicates its greatness.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of the grace of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, toward His servants, in that He named their reward for deeds an ajr (wage), in the position of the wage of a hired worker, which must be given to him when he is entitled to it. This is one of the blessings of Allah: that He names the reward He has made for deeds, He names it what? An ajr (wage), in the position of what? The obligatory wage of a hired worker. Yet Allah is the One who granted the deed, and He is the One who granted the reward. With this, the difficulty in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him﴾ [Al-Baqarah 245] is removed. This verse is among the mutashabih (ambiguous verses). Who followed it? The Jews followed it, and they said: "Allah is poor, and the proof that He is poor is that He asked for a loan," and He said: ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan﴾. So it is said to them: Woe to you! Allah is free of need of us, of the servants, before He created them and after He created them. But He likened the deed to a loan out of kindness, and to show that He, Mighty and Majestic, has bound Himself to reward the obedient.

If someone says: Your explanation here implies that something has become obligatory upon Allah, and Allah the Exalted has nothing obligatory upon Him?

The answer: Yes, nothing is obligatory upon Him from the side of people. People do not make anything obligatory upon Allah. But He made it obligatory upon Himself, and when He makes something obligatory upon Himself, it is from His perfection. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy: that whoever of you does evil in ignorance and then repents after that and corrects himself, indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Al-An'am 54]. So He is the One who prescribed for Himself that He reward the obedient, and that whoever does evil in ignorance and then repents, Allah will accept his repentance. For this reason, when the poet said:

"Nothing is due to the servants from Him as an obligation,
no, nor any deed of theirs is lost before Him.
If they are punished, it is by His justice,
or if they are granted bliss, it is by His grace, and He is the Generous, the All-Encompassing."

When this poet said that, Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) said a similar statement, but he restricted it and clarified it, saying:

"Nothing is due to the servants from Him as an obligation;
He made obligatory upon Himself the great reward.
If they are punished, it is by His justice,
or if they are granted bliss, it is by His grace, and grace belongs to the Bestower."

So may Allah have mercy on him, he made clear that nothing is obligatory upon Allah toward the servants except what He made obligatory upon Himself. And when Allah makes something obligatory upon Himself, it is from His grace, Mighty and Majestic.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 115 (part 1 of 3):

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers – We will give him what he has turned to and drive him into Hell, and evil is it as a destination.﴾

"Man" (مَن) here is conditional (shartiyyah), not relative (mawsulah), because the verb after it is in the jussive mood (majzum), so it is conditional. Unassimilating the doubled letter here (fakk al-idghaam) is permissible; had it been assimilated, it would have been said: "wa-man yushaqqi al-Rasul."

In ﴿the Messenger﴾, the definite article (al) is for prior reference (al-'ahd al-dhihni), meaning the Messenger who was sent to this Ummah, who is Muhammad ﷺ.

﴿From after﴾ is connected to "opposition" (mushaqqah); that is, his opposition is established. ﴿After guidance has become clear to him﴾: that is, the truth became clear to him and manifest. The guidance (al-huda) is the knowledge that the Prophet ﷺ brought, and it is well known that the Prophet ﷺ was sent with guidance and the religion of truth. So guidance is beneficial knowledge, and the religion of truth is righteous action.

﴿And follows other than the way of the believers﴾ is conjoined to ﴿opposes﴾; that is, he combines two matters: opposing the Messenger, and following other than the way of the believers. And what is the meaning of mushaqqah? Mushaqqah means being on a side other than the side of the Messenger ﷺ. It is derived from (al-shiqq) [side], not from (al-mashaqqah) [hardship].

As for His saying ﴿other than the way of the believers﴾, we may take (ghayr) as an adjective of an omitted noun, meaning: "and follows what?" a path other than the path of the believers; and we may take it as a direct object without estimating a noun. The way of the believers is their path, and it is well known that the believers have no path to Allah except through His law.

﴿We will give him﴾ is the answer of the condition.

﴿We will give him what he has turned to﴾: that is, We will abandon him and leave his affair to what he has taken as his ally, like the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever's migration was for worldly gain that he may obtain, or for a woman he may marry, his migration is to what he migrated for."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2529) and Muslim (1907/155), from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]]

The meaning of ﴿We will give him what he has turned to﴾ is: We will leave him, so We do not take him as an ally, and it is said: "What you have chosen is yours." Whoever clings to something is left to it.

﴿And drive him into Hell﴾: that is, We cause him to enter Hell so that he burns in it; (salyuhaa) means being burned by it.

﴿And evil is it as a destination﴾: this is a sentence of invective (insha'iyyah lil-dhamm), meaning: how evil is it as a destination! And "destination" (masir) means "return." This is the meaning of the verse.

So this verse contains a threat and a warning against whoever opposes the Messenger ﷺ and follows other than the way of the believers: that Allah, the Exalted, punishes him for that with two punishments. The first punishment is what? That Allah gives him what he has turned to and abandons him. The second punishment is that Allah drives him into Hell, and Hell (Jahannam) is one of the names of the Fire.

* From this verse we learn, first: the prohibition of opposing the Messenger, and that it is among the major sins, since the punishment is attached to it: abandonment and being driven into Hell.

If someone says: is this general for every opposition, or is it restricted according to what the texts require? What?

The answer: the second, because some sins do not take a person out of the religion, nor is this punishment attached to them. Yes, if a person intends by his sin to oppose the Messenger openly and to be dissatisfied with this ruling, then he disbelieves, not because of the sin he committed, but because of the opposition and contradiction and his failure to adhere to what the Messenger brought.

* Among the benefits of this verse: excuse by ignorance, based on His saying ﴿after guidance has become clear to him﴾. So if a person denies something the Messenger ﷺ brought, and begins to argue against it, but he is ignorant, he is excused, because the verse is explicit: ﴿after guidance has become clear to him﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that what the Prophet ﷺ brought is guidance and light. But how does it become clear? It becomes clear when a person reflects upon what the Messenger ﷺ brought of acts of worship, morals, dealings, and other things.

[Repetition in the source text omitted here, as it duplicates the preceding point.]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that what the Prophet ﷺ brought is guidance and light. But how does it become clear? It becomes clear when a person reflects upon what the Messenger ﷺ brought of acts of worship, morals, dealings, and other things. If he reflects upon it with knowledge and justice, meaning fairness, then the truth becomes clear to him, and he recognizes that what the Messenger ﷺ brought is true.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that with hesitation the proof is not established, based on His saying ﴿after it has become clear﴾. But a person must seek clarity, and must not say: "Enough, by Allah, the truth has not become clear to me and I will not search." Rather, he must search.

This applies to some Muslim lands where there are common people who commit clear shirk without any ambiguity, worshipping graves, seeking help from the dead, and other things of major shirk that they do, and they are told that this is shirk, yet they do not investigate. These people are not excused by their ignorance. Why? Because they did not seek clarity, and they are without doubt negligent.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the proof of consensus (ijma'), based on His saying ﴿and follows other than the way of the believers﴾. From this it is inferred that the way of the believers is true, and so it is: that is, if the Ummah agrees upon something, it is true. It is impossible for this Ummah, which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, chose and made a witness over mankind, ﴿that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Baqarah 143], and which bears witness to their actions and the rulings of their actions, that its consensus could be false ever. Rather, its consensus on something is true.

But what remains is establishing the consensus (tahqiq al-ijma'); this is the difficulty, establishing the consensus. Sometimes you see noble scholars narrating a consensus while disagreement exists and is widespread. Some scholars, may Allah pardon them, do not say "I know of no dissenter," which would have been an excuse, but they say "by consensus," or "they agreed upon such-and-such," while disagreement is abundant.

Among the strange things: he narrated a consensus that the testimony of a slave is rejected, and narrated another consensus that the testimony of a slave is accepted. Is this possible? It is not possible; its cause is failure to verify and to review the statements of the people of knowledge.

Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned a large group in his book al-Sawa'iq al-Mursalah of consensus-claims that were narrated by him and by eminent imams, yet there was no consensus.

As an example, besides the matter of the slave's testimony: some scholars narrated a consensus that a triple divorce in one utterance makes the woman irrevocably separated, and said: "This is agreed upon, and whoever says it does not separate has left the consensus and opposed the way of the believers. Have you understood?"

This consensus can never be sound, neither after the era of 'Umar nor before the era of 'Umar. As for before the era of 'Umar, radiyallahu 'anhu, it is certainly not sound, for Ibn 'Abbas, radiyallahu 'anhuma, said: "Triple divorce was (counted as) one in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, in the time of Abu Bakr, and for two years of 'Umar's caliphate."[[Narrated by Muslim (1472/15), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]

It was one: that is, if a man says "You are divorced, you are divorced, you are divorced," it counts as one. "And for this reason the Prophet ﷺ said to Rukanah when he said: 'I divorced her three times in a single session.' He said: 'In a single session?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'That is one, so take her back.'"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2196), and Ahmad (2387), with his wording, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]

It is clear that he repeated it: "You are divorced, you are divorced, you are divorced." But he asked him: "In a single session?" Because if it was in two sessions, it is possible he took her back between the two divorces, and if he took her back between the two divorces, the second becomes what? Effective.

In any case, I want to illustrate that some scholars narrated a consensus that she is separated by triple divorce, whether pronounced separately or together, and we say: this is not sound, because if in the time of the Messenger ﷺ, in the time of Abu Bakr, and for two years of 'Umar's caliphate triple divorce was one, how can the consensus be sound?!

For this reason some scholars said: the consensus is that it does not take effect except as one, and that this is an ancient, earlier consensus; and the one who said this is closer to the correct view than the one who said that the consensus is that the woman is separated by it. There is no doubt about the era of the Messenger, the era of Abu Bakr, and two years of 'Umar's caliphate.

The point is that these are matters in which a person needs to verify (tahrir) the issue and to have complete knowledge. It is known that some scholars were lax in narrating consensus, and their excuse in that was that they had not encountered a dissenter, so they were lenient in the matter.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the way of the believers is obedience to the Messenger ﷺ, because He said: ﴿opposes﴾ ﴿and follows other than the way of the believers﴾. So the way of the believers is the absence of opposition, and so it is.

The more faith a person has, the stronger his following of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, until it is as if he sees the Messenger before him following his trace. When a person follows this method, he attains comfort, tranquility, and strength of faith; whenever he does something, it is as if the Messenger is before him guiding him by his word or his deed. This is a matter we must be attentive to, and not let our deeds be lost in vain. For most of us have general following, praise be to Allah, but specific following in every act he does or says is greatly lacking among us, so we must be attentive to it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the punishment of whoever opposes the Messenger and follows other than the way of the believers, that he is left to what he turned to, and is lost. This is the reality; for this reason Allah, the Exalted, said in another verse: ﴿But if they turn away, know that Allah only wants to afflict them for some of their sins﴾ [al-Ma'idah 49]. So one sin is a cause of another sin, and whenever a person commits a sin, let him prepare for another sin as a punishment for him, unless he repents.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of the Fire and of punishment by it, based on His saying ﴿We will drive him into Hell, and evil is it as a destination﴾.

As for the question about this Fire, may Allah protect us and you from it: does it now exist? The answer?

* Students: Yes.

* Shaykh: And is it everlasting?

* Students: Yes.

* Shaykh: Yes, this is what the People of the Sunnah and the Community hold, and no disagreement is known from anyone on this except odd statements that carry no weight; because Allah explicitly stated its perpetuity in three verses of the Noble Qur'an: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted [others] from the way of Allah have certainly gone far astray (167). Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged – never will Allah forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path (168), except the path of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Nisa' 167–169]; His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blaze (64), abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Ahzab 64–65]; and His saying: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger – then indeed, for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Jinn 23]. May Allah protect us and you from it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah's praise, through censure and disparagement, of the Fire; based on His saying ﴿and evil is it as a destination﴾. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, speaks truly, for the worst destination a person can arrive at is the Fire. O Allah, protect us.

* Student: Does the principle of excuse by ignorance not become problematic in light of His saying: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not reason (22). And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were refusing﴾ [al-Anfal 22–23]? Is this verse not problematic for it?

* Shaykh: No, it does not create a problem. This verse is among the ambiguous (mutashabih) verses, and the other verse is clear and explicit. The meaning of ﴿If Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear﴾ is: hearing from which they would benefit. But even if He had made them hear in a way that benefits them, the deviation in their hearts would prevent them from being able to follow.

* Student: Now, the disbelievers (...) in the world (...) to whom the call has not reached, does the verse of al-Anfal not apply to them?

* Shaykh: As for these, may Allah bless you, it is said: their affair is with Allah, because these do not adhere to Islam, so they are treated like the people of fatrah [the interval without a messenger]. But if one professes Islam but holds shirk out of ignorance, here we say: he is a Muslim excused by his ignorance, because there is a difference between one who adheres to disbelief and shirk and does not want Islam, and another person who says he is a Muslim, testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, but holds shirk; the result is clear in this. As for those to whom the call has not reached, the correct view is that their affair is with Allah, and that we do not classify them with the Muslims outwardly; if they die among us, we do not pray over them nor bury them with us. As for the Hereafter, their affair is with Allah.

* Student: If the Ummah agrees on an opinion in a matter, and five or ten dissent, does this dissent not harm the way of the believers, and is consensus still formed despite the dissent of these five or ten?

* Shaykh: No, there is no consensus with the dissent of five or ten, nor even with the dissent of one or two, except according to some scholars. Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, holds that the dissent of one or two does not nullify consensus. The correct view is that the agreement of all the mujtahids is required. Common people we do not count, and muqallids we do not count, because the scholars agreed that the muqallid is not among the scholars, so his statement is not considered, for the muqallid is a copy of a book written in this school.

* Student: "And follows other than the way of the believers" – he says: there is no indication of consensus in this verse, because consensus comes from the mujtahids, and here "the believers" includes the commoner, the muqallid, and the scholar; so restricting "the believers" to the mujtahids requires evidence?

* Shaykh: Yes indeed. We say: the way of the believers includes the commoner; the commoner follows (...), he has no opinion in reality and it is not counted. That is why you find a commoner in a town following the scholar of his town, and even before the present complete communication among people, if it was said, for example, in Riyadh, "the Shaykh in Riyadh said such-and-such," and then it was said, "the Shaykh in another city said such-and-such," they would not consider the second statement, because the commoner follows the shaykh of his town.

* Student: It is narrated from Imam Ahmad that he said, regarding Allah's saying ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited﴾ [al-A'raf 204], that they agreed it refers to prayer. And it is narrated from him that he said: whoever claims consensus has lied; perhaps they disagreed?

* Shaykh: How do we reconcile his statement in this and that?

It is said: his saying "they agreed that it refers to prayer" means that it is not obligatory for me to listen to the recitation of a reciter beside me, for example; this is what is meant, and this consensus is evident, with no difficulty in it.

As for the consensus he denied, it is the consensus that has no basis, and the origin of this statement was said in refutation of the Mu'attilah (those who deny Allah's attributes), whose speaker says: "This is the consensus of the People of Truth," and similar things.

(...) What is hijrah?

* Student: Hijrah linguistically is: leaving.

Legally it is: leaving lands where a person cannot practice his religion for lands where he can practice his religion. Some defined it as: moving from a land of shirk to lands of Islam.

* Shaykh: Well said. ﴿yuhajir﴾ – why was it not (yuhajiru)?

* Student: It is the verb of the condition.

* Shaykh: The verb of the condition; because "man" is conditional and it puts the verb in the jussive, so it is the verb of the condition.

Read ﴿And when you are among them﴾ – the second group ﴿and let them take their precaution and their weapons﴾. Why was precaution not mentioned for the first group?

* Student: Because in the second group the enemy may have become alert and perhaps attacked them while they were praying, so Allah commanded them to take precaution and weapons.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 115 (part 2 of 3):**

* The Shaykh: Well done. The second group: the enemy will have become alert, so they may attack them. Therefore He said: ﴿And let them take their precaution and their weapons﴾.
This feature departs from what is usual in prayers. In how many respects?
* The student: In several respects. Among them: that (...).
* The Shaykh: Among them: the second rak'ah is longer than the first. And the default?
* The student: The default is that the first is longer than the second.
* The Shaykh: The default is that the first is longer than the second. Correct. And among them?
* The student: That it is permissible for the followers (ma'mumin) to separate from the Imam.
* The Shaykh: Yes, the permissibility of the followers separating from the Imam. Complete.
* The student: And among them: the second group follows an Imam, prays, and waits.
* The Shaykh: They make up what they missed before the Imam's salam.
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Which of the two groups was with the Imam, the first or the second?
* The student: The second was with the Imam.
* The Shaykh: The second. What is the evidence?
* The student: The evidence is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And let another group who have not yet prayed come and pray with you﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Let them pray with you﴾. And what did He say about the first?
* The student: About the first: ﴿When you have established the prayer for them, let a group of them stand with you and let them take their weapons. And when they have prostrated, let them be behind you﴾. Because the first group ended up behind, and the second...
* The Shaykh: But what is derived from the noble verse, that the second is the one with the Imam, is His saying: ﴿Let them pray with you﴾. This is correct. But what is the evidence that the first did not pray with him?
* The student: The evidence is that the Imam had preceded...
* The Shaykh: The evidence, not the reason. You said "that the Imam," and that word means the reason.
* The student: His saying: ﴿Let them pray with you﴾.
* Another student: His saying: ﴿When they have prostrated﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿When they have prostrated﴾, so He affirmed their separation: ﴿When they have prostrated, let them be behind you﴾.
Can the first group be judged to have attained the congregational prayer, as a ruling?
* A student: As a ruling, yes.
* The Shaykh: As a ruling, yes. What is the evidence?
* The student: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Let them pray with you﴾.
* The Shaykh: But He said: ﴿When they have prostrated﴾.
* The student: The first group?
* The Shaykh: Yes, the first group.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: As a ruling?
* A student: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When you have established the prayer for them, let a group of them stand with you and let them take their weapons﴾. His saying, after ﴿When you have established the prayer for them﴾: ﴿let a group of them stand with you﴾?
* The Shaykh: The hadith: "Whoever catches one rak'ah of the prayer has caught the prayer."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (580) and Muslim (607/161), from Abu Hurayrah.]] I did not say, "What is the evidence from the verse," so that you can argue against me. The evidence in general.
* A student: His saying: ﴿with you﴾.
* The Shaykh: But He said: ﴿let a group of them stand with you﴾ and did not say "let them pray." They did stand, but as a ruling they caught the congregational prayer, because of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Whoever catches one rak'ah of the prayer has caught the prayer."
Is carrying weapons in this situation obligatory?
* A student: The preferred view...
* The Shaykh: I do not want the preferred view or what is preferred. We are now taking from the verse.
* A student: The verse indicates...
* The Shaykh: It indicates obligation. What is the evidence?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No. That may be for recommendation, because the default is that a person carrying something that occupies him in his prayer is prohibited. So the lam here stands in contrast to the prohibition.
* A student: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And there is no blame upon you if there is discomfort from rain or if you are ill, that you put down your weapons﴾. So the negation of blame...
* The Shaykh: Wait, complete it.
* A student: ﴿that you put down your weapons﴾.
* The Shaykh: Well done. From His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And there is no blame upon you if there is discomfort from rain or if you are ill, that you put down your weapons﴾. The implication of the noble verse: if this situation does not exist, then blame falls upon you.
Some scholars hold that it is permissible in this situation to carry a najis (impure) weapon out of necessity?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: This is outside the meaning of the verse, because the verse does not mention it. And this is the closer view: that it is permissible to carry a najis weapon out of necessity.
Does the noble verse indicate that the disbelievers are eager to keep the Muslims unarmed, as is the case now in Bosnia and Herzegovina?
* A student: It is indicated.
* The Shaykh: From where?
* The student: His saying: ﴿The disbelievers wish that you would be negligent of your weapons and your belongings, so they could come upon you in one attack﴾.
* The Shaykh: Well done, may Allah bless you. This is correct. The disbelievers wish that we would be negligent of our weapons. So how would they give them to us?
Does the verse indicate the severity of the disbelievers' rage in regard to raiding us?
* A student: From the verse.
* The Shaykh: Which verse?
* The student: ﴿The disbelievers wish that you would be negligent of your weapons and your belongings﴾.
* The Shaykh: No.
* A student: His saying: ﴿so they could come upon you in one attack﴾.
* The Shaykh: His saying: ﴿so they could come upon you in one attack﴾.
You confined yourself to...
* A student: I said: the verse.
* The Shaykh: No. What suits the matter is that the verse must contain the proof. Pay attention to this, as you may miss it. That is: someone is asked for a specific ruling, then he recites the beginning of the verse and does not mention what indicates the specific ruling. This does not count as anything.
His saying: ﴿one attack﴾, meaning: a prepared assault that would finish you off?
* A student: His saying about the disbelievers: ﴿The disbelievers wish﴾.
* The Shaykh: Yes. The proof is: ﴿so they could come upon you in one attack﴾. It indicates their rage, their intense fury, and that they come forward with strength.
* * *
* The student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿So when you have finished the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides. And when you are secure, establish the prayer. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specified times﴾ [an-Nisa 103]. ﴿And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy. If you are suffering, indeed they are suffering as you suffer, but you hope from Allah that for which they do not hope. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [an-Nisa 104].
* The Shaykh: What is the wisdom in His saying: ﴿When you have finished the prayer, remember Allah﴾? What is the wisdom in commanding His remembrance after finishing the prayer?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Other than this.
* The student: Remembrance keeps the servant constantly connected to his Lord, Glorified and Exalted. So when the prayer is finished and there was no remembrance, it is as if the servant has separated from his Lord (...). He remembers Allah so that he remains constantly connected to his Lord, Glorified and Exalted.
* The Shaykh: It is as if He is saying: do not make your connection with Allah and your remembrance of Him only in the prayer, saying: "Finished, the prayer is over," and become negligent of the remembrance of Allah. Similar to this is what came regarding Friday: ﴿And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse through the land and seek from the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah often﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 10]. Do not be negligent. This is an important warning.
A man prayed after the time had expired, deliberately. What do you say about his prayer?
* A student: His prayer is invalid.
* The Shaykh: Invalid? After the time, not before the time? He prayed after the time, deliberately, without an excuse, and his prayer is invalid?
* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: From where do you take this?
* A student: ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specified times﴾.
* The Shaykh: Is the evidence compound? It requires another evidence to support this, combined with it.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: He cited this, but we said: another evidence must be added to this.
* A student: This verse together with the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) and Muslim (1718/18), the wording of Muslim, from 'A'ishah.]]
* The Shaykh: Well done. This verse indicates invalidity when combined with the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected." Because this one who left the prayer until its time expired has done an action for which there is no command from Allah and His Messenger, rather there is a prohibition from Allah and His Messenger upon it. So his prayer is invalid.
Is this out of mercy toward him or out of punishment?
* A student: This one who left the prayer and its time expired...
* The Shaykh: Until its time expired, and we said: do not make it up?
* A student: Out of punishment.
* The Shaykh: Out of punishment, or out of mercy so that he does not tire?
* The student: Out of punishment only.
* The Shaykh: What is the reasoning?
* The student: Even if he made it up a thousand times, it would not suffice and would not be valid for him.
* The Shaykh: Yes. But what is the reason it is a punishment and not mercy? Because now we have two men: one forgot five prayers and we said: make them up. And the second deliberately left five prayers and we said: rest, do not make them up?
* A student: The first knows that they are (...), and in the second (...).
* The Shaykh: Until now we have not prepared an answer, you have not identified the answer.
* A student: As for the one who leaves the prayer, if he leaves it deliberately (...).
* The Shaykh: This means it is like turning away from him and not being pleased with his act. He turned away from him and was not pleased with his action. In contrast to the one to whom it was said: pray, and this prayer is an expiation, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no expiation for it except that."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (597) and Muslim (684/314), from Anas ibn Malik.]]
Does failing to observe the prescribed times contradict the completeness of faith?
* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: What is the evidence from the verse?
* A student: ﴿upon the believers﴾.
* The Shaykh: The evidence is His saying: ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specified times﴾, and the believer will observe this decreed writing at its specified times.
What is the wisdom of the verse that follows: ﴿And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy﴾, to the end? That is, what is meant by it?
* A student: When He mentioned the ruling on the prayer...
* The Shaykh: No, I do not want the connection of this to what precedes it. I want: what is the wisdom in mentioning this?
* The student: A prohibition against the believers becoming weak and fainthearted in pursuing the disbelievers.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Consoling the believing fighters, consoling them. He says: ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people﴾ [Al 'Imran 140]. ﴿If you are suffering, indeed they are suffering as you suffer﴾. But the outcome? ﴿But you hope from Allah that for which they do not hope﴾. Therefore, when Abu Sufyan said at the battle of Uhud: "A day for a day, Badr, and war is in turns." The Muslims answered him: "No equality. Our dead are in Paradise, and your dead are in the Fire."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (4043) from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, and Ahmad (2609), the wording of Ahmad, from Ibn 'Abbas.]] There is no doubt that this contains consolation and strengthening for the believers in pursuing their enemies.
Is there an indication in the verse that one cannot testify that a martyr is in Paradise?
* A student: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿but you hope from Allah that for which they do not hope﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿You hope﴾. Hope may be fulfilled and may not be fulfilled. Therefore we are forbidden to say of a specific person that he is a martyr, except one whom the Messenger (ﷺ) has testified for. So whoever the Messenger testified to be a martyr, we testify for him, and likewise whoever the Qur'an testified for, as at the battle of Uhud when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿and that He may take from among you martyrs﴾.
In the hadith about Uhud: when the Prophet (ﷺ) ascended the mountain, and they trembled with them, and with him were Abu Bakr, 'Umar, and 'Uthman, he said: "Be steady, Uhud, for upon you are a Prophet, a Siddiq, and two martyrs."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3675) from Anas ibn Malik.]] That is, the four categories of creation: of them on this mountain, how many categories were found? Three: a Prophet, a Siddiq, and a martyr.
Now we testify that 'Umar is a martyr, and that 'Uthman is a martyr, and we also testify that Thabit ibn Qays, may Allah be pleased with him, is a martyr, because the Messenger said to him: "You will live praiseworthy, you will be killed as a martyr, and you will enter Paradise,"[[Narrated by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (7167), al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (5105), and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1311), from Thabit ibn Qays.]] in a well-known story: "When the verse of Allah, Exalted is He, was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet or speak to him loudly as you speak loudly to one another, lest your deeds be nullified while you perceive not﴾, he, may Allah be pleased with him, had a strong, booming voice, and therefore he was an orator and a poet for the Messenger (ﷺ), combining oratory and poetry. He hid himself in his house weeping, fearing that his deeds would be nullified while he did not perceive it, may Allah be pleased with him." (But by Allah, he feared punishment only because he felt secure from it; whoever fears Allah's punishment, Allah makes him secure from it.) "The Prophet (ﷺ) missed him and asked about him. He was told that he was in his house, and he sent for him and was informed of the reason. He said: Allah says: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet...﴾ and I, O Messenger of Allah, fear that my deeds will be nullified while I do not perceive it. So he said to him: 'Rather, you will live praiseworthy, you will be killed as a martyr, and you will enter Paradise.'"[[Narrated by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (7167) from Thabit ibn Qays; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (5107) from the daughter of Thabit ibn Qays; al-Tabarani in Musnad al-Shamiyyin (2582) from Anas; and its origin is in Muslim (119/187) from Anas in abridged form.]] So he lived praiseworthy, was killed as a martyr, and we testify that he will enter Paradise, may Allah be pleased with him.
Regarding his death there is a strange story: "When he, may Allah be pleased with him, was killed, one of the soldiers passed by him and took the coat of mail he was wearing. It was at the edge of the army, so he placed it under a *burmah*" (Do you know the *burmah*? A pot of fired clay, made of baked earth, which is of stone...) "He placed the coat of mail under it. Then one of Thabit's companions saw Thabit in a dream and he said to him: 'So-and-so, or a man' (I forgot whether he specified the man or said 'a man') 'passed by me and took the coat of mail and placed it under a *burmah* at the edge of the army, and beside it is a horse neighing. Inform Khalid that I bequeath such-and-such, so let this reach Abu Bakr.' When morning came, the man came to Khalid ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, and informed him of the matter. They went to the place he had mentioned, and there was the coat of mail under the *burmah* with the horse neighing beside it. He took it, and his bequest reached Abu Bakr, and he executed it."[[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1320) from Thabit ibn Qays.]]
The scholars said: No one's bequest was executed after his death except Thabit ibn Qays. He bequeathed after his death and it was carried out. The conclusion is that we do not testify to anyone being a martyr except one whom the Messenger (ﷺ) testified for. It is established from the Prophet (ﷺ): "That the one who dies in a fire is a martyr, that the one who drowns is a martyr, that the one with a stomach ailment is a martyr, that the one who dies of plague is a martyr, and that whoever dies under a collapsed building is a martyr."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (3111) and al-Nasa'i (1846) from Jabir ibn 'Atik, with the wording: "Martyrdom is of seven kinds apart from being killed in the way of Allah: the one who dies of plague is a martyr, the drowned is a martyr, the one with pleurisy is a martyr, the one with a stomach ailment is a martyr, the one who dies in a fire is a martyr, the one who dies under a collapse is a martyr, and the woman who dies in childbirth is a martyr."]] So if someone dies from these causes, do we say he is a martyr in a specific sense?

Ibn 'Uthaymin: Commentary on Surah 4, verse 115 (part 3 of 3)

No, but we hope that he is a martyr (shahid). That is because appearance may differ from reality. We say: we hope he is among the martyrs. Praise be to Allah, our testimony is not a condition for his being a martyr if he is among the martyrs, is it not so? And our not testifying for him does not prevent him from being a martyr if he is among the martyrs. It suffices for us to hope that he is among the martyrs.

* Student: What is the meaning of (yastin)?
* Shaykh: "Yastanu al-faras" (the horse stands) means: when it stands on three legs, it is said that it "yastin."

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. "Indeed We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the treacherous. (105) And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful. (106) And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not like one who is a betrayer, sinful." [An-Nisa' 105-107].
* Shaykh: In this noble verse, "Indeed We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you," does it indicate that the Prophet (ﷺ) does not judge by his own opinion?
* Student: His saying: "that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you..."
* Shaykh: "Indeed We have sent down to you the Book in truth." What is the point of the inference?
* Student: Almighty and Majestic Allah said: "by what Allah has shown you."
* Shaykh: And He did not say "by what"?
* Student: He did not say "by what you see."
* Shaykh: "By what you see." And also, He made his judgment founded upon the sending down of the Book.

This actual event supports this. The Prophet (ﷺ) permitted some of the hypocrites who asked his permission, and Allah said to him: "Allah pardon you. Why did you give them permission until those who were truthful became clear to you and you knew the liars?" [At-Tawbah 43]. Yet Allah addressed him with this gentle reproach, placing pardon before blame or reproach. All of this is out of respect for the Messenger (peace be upon him). A parallel to this is His saying: "He frowned and turned away (1) that the blind man came to him (2). And what would make you know? Perhaps he would purify himself" [Abasa 1-3]. He did not say "you frowned," out of dislike of addressing him with a matter for which he would be blamed. We ask Allah to make me and you among those who honour Him and His Messenger.

His saying: "And do not be an advocate for the treacherous." Does this indicate that this had occurred from him, so he was forbidden from it?
* Student: It does not indicate that.
* Shaykh: It does not indicate that. Why? "And do not be an advocate for the treacherous"?
* Student: This is like His saying, Mighty and Exalted is He: "If you were to associate others with Allah, your deeds would surely be nullified" [Az-Zumar 65].
* Shaykh: And shirk?
* Student: It is far from him (ﷺ).
* Shaykh: Impossible. Correct, may Allah bless you.

His saying: "treacherous, sinful." If someone asked: is the word (sinful, athim) a restrictive qualifier (sifah qayd) or a descriptive qualifier (sifah kashf)? That is, is it a restrictive adjective or an explanatory adjective?
* Student: Restrictive.
* Shaykh: Restrictive? Because a treacherous person may not sin, does he? If it is restrictive, its meaning is that the treacherous divides into two kinds: sinful and not sinful.
* Student: Explanatory.
* Shaykh: Explanatory. Do you agree with this? Yes, it is an explanatory adjective, because every treacherous person is sinful, indeed he is sinning.

A parallel to this in the explanatory adjective is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: "O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life" [Al-Anfal 24]. He calls us only to that which gives us life. Likewise His saying, Exalted is He: "O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you" [Al-Baqarah 21]. For it is well known that if we made "who created you" a restrictive qualifier, there would be a lord who did not create us, and that is not the case. Rather, this is an explanatory qualifier, and an explanatory qualifier generally serves to clarify a fact or give the reason for a ruling. This is the usual case.

What is the story to which these verses refer: "They hide from people, but they cannot hide from Allah" and so on?
* Student: (...) a man from the hypocrites stole a coat of mail (...) with the Jew (...).
* Shaykh: A man from the Ansar stole a coat of mail or a sack of flour, according to differing reports, and he accused a man from the Jews, and the man was innocent. His people wanted the Prophet (peace be upon him) to argue on his behalf to dispel this accusation, which was a disgrace to these people. So Allah sent down these verses [[See Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi (1/183).]].

What is derived from these verses is the justice of Islam, and that it is built upon justice. What is the basis for this?
* Student: That the one accused of theft was a Jew, and that the one who defended him was the Prophet (ﷺ) (...). Had there been injustice in Islam, it would not have given the Muslim his due against (...).
* Shaykh: That is, his defending this innocent Jew indicates that this religion is built upon justice, and it is so: "Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct and giving to relatives" [An-Nahl 90].

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. "Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with; but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates with Allah has certainly strayed far astray. (116) They invoke not besides Him except female [deities], and they invoke not but a rebellious Satan. (117) Allah has cursed him, and he said, 'I will take from Your servants an appointed portion. (118) And I will mislead them, and I will arouse in them desires, and I will order them so they will slit the ears of cattle, and I will order them so they will alter the creation of Allah.' And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly suffered a clear loss. (119) He promises them and arouses desires in them, but Satan promises them only delusion. (120) Those - their refuge is Hell, and they will not find from it an escape." [An-Nisa' 116-121].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: "Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with." The discussion of His saying "And whoever opposes the Messenger..." and so on has already passed, and we took its benefits, did we not? Let us discuss them.

First: Where is the response (jawab) of the conditional in His saying: "And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him"?
* Student: His saying: "We will give him what he has turned to."
* Shaykh: His saying: "We will give him."
If someone said to you: the response of the conditional should be jussive (majzum), and this is not jussive?
* Student: It is jussive.
* Shaykh: Jussive by what?
* Student: By the deletion of the weak letter.
* Shaykh: By the deletion of the weak letter, well done.

What is the meaning of His saying: "We will give him what he has turned to"?
* Student: That is, that We grant him what he wanted...
* Another student: That is: We leave him and abandon him, and entrust him to what he has taken up.
* Shaykh: Perfect, correct. That is: We abandon him and entrust him to what he has taken up, or to whoever has taken him up.

His saying: "and evil it is as a destination" (sa'at masiran). What is in the accusative position of "masiran"?
* Student: A specification (tamyiz).
* Shaykh: Tamyiz, transferred from what?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Wrong.
* Student: From the subject (fa'il).
* Shaykh: From the subject, and the original is: "evil was its destination" (sa'at maseeruh).

Is there in the verse evidence for excuse by ignorance?
* Student: "after guidance has become clear to him."
* Shaykh: The question is not "where is the evidence?" Is there in it evidence for excuse by ignorance?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: From where is it derived?
* Student: That "whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him..." means...
* Shaykh: "after guidance has become clear to him." What did you understand from it?
* Student: That whoever has not had guidance made clear to him, there is no punishment upon him.
* Shaykh: There is no punishment upon him, and this implies excuse by ignorance.

Is there a basis for distinguishing between the fundamentals (usul) and the branches (furu') regarding excuse by ignorance?
* Student: There is no basis for it, because the general evidences indicating excuse by ignorance are absolute, whether in the fundamentals or the branches.
* Shaykh: Absolutely? Fine.

Consider: if a Muslim who identifies with Islam, who fasts, prays and gives charity, but calls upon other than Allah, believing that this is permissible and a means of seeking nearness to Allah, what do you say about him?
* Student: He bears no burden.
* Shaykh: Why?
* Student: Because guidance has not been made clear to him.
* Shaykh: Because guidance has not been made clear to him, so he is excused by his ignorance.

Consider: if it were said to this man, "This action of yours is shirk," and he said, "This is what I found my fathers upon, and I will not turn away from it"?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: If the one who informed him is not a trustworthy source in his eyes?
* Student: It is obligatory upon him to seek the truth, because he has (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, well done. That is, the layman may say, "I do not trust you; he does this and his scholars see it and say nothing to him, so I do not trust you." We say: then it is obligatory upon him to do what? To search. Since he has been told, and this is a serious matter, once he has been told "this is shirk," it is obligatory upon him to search, and if he does not, he becomes negligent and not fulfilling the obligation.

Here He attributed the path (sabil) to the believers, and in some verses the path is attributed to Allah, to Himself. How is the combination?
* Student: (...) Glory be to Him, in the sense that it is an attribution of guidance (...).
* Shaykh: Correct. It is attributed to Allah because He is the one who established it for the servants and legislated it for them, and because it leads to Him. That is for two reasons: that He is the one who established it for the servants and legislated it, and that it leads to Allah. As for its attribution to the believers, it is because they are the ones who walk upon it.

The Almighty said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills.﴾ The explanation of this verse has already been covered in full. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, repeated it twice in this surah, and between the two occurrences He mentioned killing, the killing of a soul. It has already been noted that the scholars said the killer of a soul can repent, and they cited as evidence that Allah mentioned the killing of a soul between two verses, both of which indicate that Allah forgives everything other than shirk.

The earlier discussion concerned ﴿مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ﴾ (mā dūna dhālik). Does it mean "what is other than that" or "what is less than that"?

* Student: "What is other than that."

* The Shaykh: "What is other than that." That is, "what is less than it," or is the meaning "what is other than that"?

* Students: "What is less than it."

* The Shaykh: Good. What follows from that?

* Student: It has an implication for whether someone commits something greater than shirk.

* The Shaykh: And what is greater than shirk?

* Student: On the first reading, there is nothing greater than shirk, so everything other than shirk is forgiven.

* The Shaykh: So when we say ﴿مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ﴾ means "what is other than it," disbelief that is not shirk falls under it. When we say it means "what is less than it," what does that exclude? It includes the minor sins that are below shirk, and it excludes the major sins of disbelief and other things.

The main point is this: is ﴿مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ﴾ "what is other than it" or "what is less than it"? We say it means "what is less than it," because if you said "what is other than that," disbelief that is not shirk would be subject to Allah's will, and that is not the case. Rather, the meaning is what is below shirk.

Does the verse contain anything indicating that shirk is not forgiven even if it is minor (ashghar)? Yes. How is this derived? When you take ﴿أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ﴾ as a verbal noun (maṣdar), the construction becomes: Allah does not forgive the association of partners with Him. In that case, it is an indefinite noun in a negative context, which makes it general. For this reason Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: shirk is not forgiven even if it is minor. This may be supported by the saying of Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him): "For me to swear falsely by Allah is more beloved to me than to swear truthfully by other than Him."[[Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzāq in his Muṣannaf (15929), and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (8902), from the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd.]] Thus he regarded the evil of shirk as greater than the evil of a false oath.

As for His words: ﴿وَمَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ ("Whoever associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray"), and in the first verse: ﴿فَقَدِ افْتَرَى إِثْمًا عَظِيمًا﴾ ("he has indeed fabricated a tremendous sin") [al-Nisāʾ 48]. From the two verses together, it is derived that the polytheist is a fabricator and one who has gone astray. This is indeed the case, because his claim that Allah has a partner is a lie and a great fabrication. And his building upon this claim by associating others with Allah is error. Merely saying "Allah has a partner" is fabrication, and then putting that into practice is considered error. So from these two noble verses it is derived that the polytheist is a fabricator and one who has gone astray. His words ﴿بَعِيدًا﴾ ("far") are due to the magnitude of his sin and offense.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 117–120 (part 1 of 2):

Then He said: ﴿They invoke, besides Him, none but females, and they invoke none but a rebellious devil.﴾ (In) here means (ma) (not), and the sign of this—that is, the sign that (in) means (ma)—is that (illa) (except) comes after it. This is the sign that it means (ma). ﴿It is not but a manifest magic﴾ [al-Ma'idah 110]. The meaning: "This is not..." ﴿This is not but a noble angel﴾ [Yusuf 31]. The meaning: "This is not but a noble angel." ﴿You are only a warner﴾ [Fatir 23], i.e., "You are not but a warner." So (in) comes in the sense of (ma), and its sign is what? That (illa) comes after it.

Also, (in) has several meanings, and there is no harm in mentioning them now so that our brothers who have not previously studied them may know them. It comes as a negation. It also comes as the lightened form of the heavy (inna), affirmative, the opposite of the negating (in), since the lightened form of the heavy is affirmative; for the lightened form of the heavy conveys emphasis, as it is in fact (inna) but lightened, so it is for what? For emphasis, unlike (in), which is for negation. The poet said:

...................... ∗∗∗ "And indeed Malik was of noble origins"

He boasts of his people and says:

...................... ∗∗∗ "And indeed Malik was of noble origins"

That is: "And indeed Malik was of noble origins."

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And indeed they were before that in manifest error﴾ [Al 'Imran 164]. (In kanu) means (inna). Where is its noun? They say: it is a pronoun of the matter (damir al-sha'n) which is omitted whenever it occurs, and the estimate is: "and indeed He" (wa innahu), i.e., the matter, or "and indeed they" (wa innahum), i.e., the people. Some of them say: we do not estimate a pronoun of the matter; we estimate a pronoun suited to the context. So if they are a group, we say the estimate is "indeed they" (innahum), and there is no harm in this.

In any case, this (in) is the lightened form of the heavy, and it is the opposite of the negating (in), because it is for affirmation and the emphasis of affirmation, unlike the negating (in).

(In) comes as a conditional, and this is very common, such as: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they desist, what has passed will be forgiven them﴾ [al-Anfal 38].

It comes as an extra particle, meaning its presence is like its absence, as in the poet's verse:

"You, Banu Ghudanah, are not gold ∗∗∗ nor silver, but indeed you are clay"

The poet is satirizing these people, saying: you are neither gold nor silver, rather you are clay. And "People are like mines" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3493) and Muslim (2526 / 199) from Abu Hurayrah], as the Prophet ﷺ said: a good mine and a bad mine. How many divisions are there? The divisions are four. Count the five?

* Student: Negating.
* Shaykh: Negating.
* Student: And extra.
* Shaykh: And extra. Count?
* Student: Lightened from the heavy.
* Shaykh: Lightened from the heavy.
* Student: Negating.
* Shaykh: And negating.
* Student: In the sense of (ma).
* Shaykh: It is the negating; it does not come as the lightened form of the heavy.

In any case, in this noble verse, ﴿They invoke, besides Him, none but females﴾, we say: (in) is negating, i.e., these polytheists do not invoke, besides Allah—that is, other than Allah—anything but females.

What is the meaning of His saying ﴿none but females﴾? It is said: the names of these idols are feminine names: al-Lat, al-'Uzza, Manat; these are all feminine names. The feminine is inferior to the masculine, not in its strength, nor its rank, nor its standing, nor in everything, ﴿and the men have a degree over them﴾ [al-Baqarah 228].

It is also said: the meaning of ﴿They invoke, besides Him, none but females﴾ is: they invoke none but something like females, which cannot repel harm from itself, so how could it repel harm from others?

According to this view, the masculine idols such as Hubal are included. Hubal is masculine, and yet he is worshipped besides Allah. On this basis, this view is closer to the truth, because it is more general, and because it shows the reality of these idols, that they cannot repel anything from themselves, so how could they repel it from others?

﴿And they invoke none but a rebellious devil﴾, i.e., they invoke none but a rebellious devil.

Here "invoking" (du'a') means worship, i.e., they worship none but the devil, and "worship" here means obedience: they obey the devil, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a manifest enemy. And that you worship Me; this is a straight path﴾ [Ya Sin 60–61]. So the devil commands them to associate partners, and they associate. So their associating with the devil is what kind of association?

* Students: Obedience.
