* Shaykh: Association of obedience. And their associating with the idols is association of worship, as they worship them. A people in this state have no good in them; they worship only what does not benefit them, and they obey only the command of the devil.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾; the pronoun refers to the devil.

﴿Marid﴾: ﴿a rebellious devil﴾. (Al-marid) is one who has reached the utmost limit in transgression and insolence.

The devils are of kinds: among them is the marid, and among them is one who is not marid. For this reason, in some wordings of the hadith about the devils being chained in Ramadan it says: "The rebellious devils are chained" [al-Nasa'i (2106) and Ahmad (7917), the wording being his, from Abu Hurayrah], i.e., the stubborn people, the devils who are stubborn and strong in their defiance.

﴿Allah has cursed him﴾. Cursing (al-la'n) means expulsion and removal from the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Is this a statement or a supplication?

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, it must be a statement, because it comes from whom? From Allah, and Allah does things and does not supplicate against anyone. So Allah, the Exalted, informs that Allah has cursed him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense﴾ [Sad 78], and the second verse: ﴿And indeed upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense﴾ [al-Hijr 35]. So the curse of Allah and the curse of those who curse are upon Iblis until the Day of Recompense.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah has cursed him, and he said: "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion"﴾. ﴿And he said﴾: the subject is whom?

* Student: The devil.
* Shaykh: No, the subject is—﴿Allah has cursed him and he said﴾ is conjoined to what?

* Student: Resumption (istinaf).
* Shaykh: The waw is for resumption. Well done, the waw is for resumption. For this reason it is necessary to stop at your saying: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾. Stop. ﴿And he said﴾, i.e., the devil, ﴿and he said: "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion."﴾

The content of the saying is the clause ﴿I will surely take﴾, and this clause—as you see—is emphasized with how many emphases?

* Student: The lam, the nun of emphasis, and the implied oath.
* Shaykh: The lam, the nun of emphasis, and the implied oath. So with three emphases.

﴿He said﴾, i.e., to Allah. ﴿I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion﴾: ﴿a portion﴾ is the object of (atakhadha). The meaning: I will take them as allies; I will befriend them and they will befriend me.

And (al-nasib) is a part of a thing. So what is this portion? This portion is much greater than the earlier portion, because the Prophet ﷺ informed that Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection: "O Adam! He will say: At your service, and at your pleasure. He will say: Bring forth from your offspring a group to the Fire. He will say: O Lord, and what is the group of the Fire? He will say: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3348) and Muslim (222 / 379) from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri].

But we must know that the devil did not say: "I will take from among the children of Adam." He said: ﴿from among Your servants﴾, and "Your servants" is what? More general and comprehensive than the children of Adam; for this reason He said: ﴿an appointed portion﴾, and these are those whom he led astray from the children of Adam, and in relation to the children of Adam they are what? Much more.

So we say: is the intended meaning of "servants" here the children of Adam? Let us see. If it is said: they are the children of Adam, then it becomes a case of the general used to mean the specific, and then this appointed portion is much more than those who were spared from his misguidance.

If we say: the intended meaning of "servants" is what includes all creation, the angels are among the servants of Allah, as He said of them that they are ﴿honoured servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 26]. Likewise, all created things are humbled before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, either by legal humility or by decreed humility. On this basis the appointed portion relative to the servants in general is small, it is small; but relative to the children of Adam it is great, because of the nine hundred and ninety-nine out of every thousand, all of them are in the Fire, and one out of the thousand is in Paradise.

His saying ﴿an appointed portion﴾: "fard" means decisive determination, i.e., decreed and fixed. Allah the Mighty and Majestic gave him that and empowered him to mislead the children of Adam for a wisdom which He, glory be to Him, intended. But He threatened whoever follows him, saying: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you of them, all together﴾ [Sad 85].

﴿And I will surely mislead them﴾: he takes them as allies, befriends them, and they befriend him, and he also misleads them from what? From the path of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, whether from this nation or from others. The clause here is emphasized with the same emphases as the clause before it, i.e., with three emphases. ﴿And I will surely mislead them﴾, i.e., from the straight path.

﴿And I will surely excite in them desires﴾: i.e., I will promise them with false hopes. And indeed this happened to Adam, when the devil said to him: ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ [Ta-Ha 120], and ﴿He swore to them both: "Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisers"﴾ [al-A'raf 21]. So Adam, peace be upon him, forgot that Allah had forbidden him, saying: ﴿Do not approach this tree﴾ [al-A'raf 19], but he promised them with false hopes and said: ﴿I will direct you to the tree of eternity﴾, i.e., to the tree which, if you eat from it, you will be made eternal and will have a kingdom that does not decay.

So the devil excites in the children of Adam desires, exciting them with many desires; among them: he makes the act of disobedience easy for him. He says: this is easy, this is minor; it will be expiated by the prayers, it will be expiated by the 'umrah, and so on. And the poor soul misled by the devil does not know that the prayers and 'umrah up to 'umrah, and what resembles them of that which expiates sins, must be complete; and who is it that brings the completion of the prayer?!

Most people now, their prayers reach the level of what? The level of being valid (al-ijza'), and perhaps they do not even reach that level.

Likewise, he says: this is easy: "Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that to whom He wills" [al-Nisa' 48]. He excites desire in him, saying: even if it were decreed that you die persisting in disobedience, you have righteous children who will pray for you, and "When a person dies, his deeds are cut off except from three" [Muslim (1631 / 14) from Abu Hurayrah], and so on. In short, he casts false hopes into their souls in many forms.

﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely cut off the ears of the cattle﴾: "I will command them" with a clear command face to face, or a command of inspiration from within the self? The second. And perhaps the devil appears in a human form and commands them with a clear command, but the basic principle is an inner command: he commands them to do such and such; for this reason He said: ﴿so they will cut off the ears of the cattle﴾. The fa' here is coordinating, and it is coordinated with (amurannahum). It will come, Allah willing, in the benefits (al-fawa'id) that it indicates complete submission on their part.

﴿so they will cut off the ears of the cattle, and I will surely command them, so they will alter the creation of Allah﴾. (Yubattikunna) means: they will cut. What is the grammatical analysis of (yubattikunna)?

* Student: The fa' is resumptive (tafri'iyya).
* Shaykh: Its analysis?
* Student: It is derived from what precedes it (mufarra'a).
* Shaykh: No, no, it is not derived; it is coordinating. The one who derives (mufarri') is one whose speech branches its end from its beginning. The fa' is coordinating, indicating sequence and immediacy. The lam?
* Student: The lam is the lam of initiation.
* Shaykh: Does it enter upon the subject so that it is the lam of initiation? The lam of initiation is the one that enters upon the subject (mubtada').
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Some say: it is preparatory to the oath, i.e., it prepares for the oath, because the oath is presumed before it. Continue.
* Student: (yubattikunna) is an imperfect verb.
* Shaykh: (yubattikunna) is all an imperfect verb?!
* Student: (yubattik) is an imperfect verb, and the subject is a hidden pronoun.
* Shaykh: Analyse first; complete the analysis of the verb before.
* Student: (yubattik) is an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the nun that is omitted to avoid the succession of similar sounds; and the nun is for emphasis.
* Shaykh: Why was the verb not built, given that it has the nun of emphasis?
* Student: Because it is not direct.
* Shaykh: Not direct. Then the omitted nun must be estimated, to avoid the succession of similar sounds. And the waw?
* Student: It is omitted to avoid the meeting of two quiescent letters.
* Shaykh: And the waw omitted for the meeting of two quiescent letters? And what? An object?!
* Student: It is the subject.
* Shaykh: The subject. Fine. And the nun?
* Student: The nun is omitted.
* Shaykh: No, the nun is present.
* Student: The nun is the nun of emphasis.
* Shaykh: The original of this word is: fa-layubattikunna adhan al-an'am. The first nun was dropped out of dislike for the succession of similar sounds, but the nun of emphasis was not dropped, because it was brought as a sign; if it were dropped, the sign would be lost. Then the waw was dropped, because when the first nun was dropped, the second nun met the quiescent waw, so two quiescent letters met. Ibn Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, says:

"If two quiescent letters meet, vowel the first; and if it is a soft letter, its deletion is deserved."

And here, is the first one soft or not soft? Soft, i.e., one of the letters of prolongation, so it is deleted.

The meaning of ﴿fa-layubattikunna﴾ is: so they will cut the ears of the cattle. And the mere cutting is not what is included in the verse; rather, they cut the ears of the cattle as a sign that they are forbidden, because they forbid what Allah has permitted and permit what Allah has forbidden. They have known rules and regulations, man-made laws, not legislated by Sharia.

When a she-camel bears such-and-such number of offspring, then she must be released; the sign? Cutting the ear. This is what is mentioned in His saying: ﴿Allah did not prescribe any baheerah, sa'ibah, wasilah, or ham﴾ [al-Ma'idah 103]. But it is explained: this cutting—they do not cut it as a sign and evidence that it belongs to so-and-so, as if they branded it; no, they cut it out of a false belief that it has become free, not to be ridden, not to be burdened, not to be given water from its milk, nor other things.

And al-an'am is the plural of na'am, like asbab the plural of sabab, and na'am applies to three things: camels, cows, and sheep.

﴿and I will surely command them, so they will alter the creation of Allah﴾.

* Student: Shaykh, you said it is emphasized with three emphases; the emphasis is implied, is it not present?
* Shaykh: How? What word do you mean?
* Student: ﴿He said: I will surely take﴾ — the implied one, O Shaykh, or the deleted one, does it not negate the emphasis? Is the emphasis mentioned?
* Shaykh: No, no. If a proof indicates the deleted element, it is as if it were present, and here there is a proof. Ibn Malik said in the Alfiyya, as one of the rules: what is known may be omitted... ∗∗∗ ......................
And although this was said about the subject and predicate, it should be general.

* Student: Those in the Fire, the nine hundred and ninety-nine, is this before the eternal abiding, so it includes the sinful Muslims, or after the eternal abiding, so it refers to the disbelievers?
* Shaykh: No, this is meant after the eternal abiding. What is meant by nine hundred and ninety-nine are those who will abide forever in the Fire.

* Student: You mentioned that His saying ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾ is a declarative sentence. The rhetoricians say that a declarative sentence is what can be described as true or false; it admits truth, so is this (...)?
* Shaykh: No, it is in itself, regardless of what it reports. For this reason, Musaylimah's saying "He is a messenger" does not admit truth.
And Muhammad's saying "He is a messenger" does not admit falsehood (...).

* * *

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely alter the creation of Allah.﴾ This is joined to what came before, to His words: ﴿I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion﴾, up to His words: ﴿And I will surely command them.⁠﻿ The meaning is that Satan commands the servants of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to alter the creation of Allah. So what is meant by "the creation of Allah"? Does it mean the fitrah (the innate disposition) upon which people were created, so that the meaning is that he alters the innate disposition of people from monotheism to polytheism, and from certainty to doubt, as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [This is] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be to the creation of Allah⁠﻿﻿? "What?" ﴿to the creation of Allah﴾ [Ar-Rum 30].

Or does "altering the creation of Allah" mean al-wasm (tattooing), al-washr (filing the teeth), an-namṣ (plucking the facial hair), and similar things?

Scholars hold two opinions, and the correct view is that it is inclusive. This is based on the well-known principle of tafsir (exegesis): whenever two interpretations are mentioned for a verse, they do not contradict each other, and the verse can bear both, then the verse must be understood as having both meanings together. Accordingly, He commands them to alter the creation of Allah, which is the fitrah upon which people were created, and the creation of Allah is also the physical alteration through filing the teeth, tattooing, filing (washr), and other such things, because this meaning is more general.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly suffered a clear loss.﴾ Allah has spoken the truth. ﴿Whoever takes Satan﴾ means: makes him ﴿an ally﴾, that is, one whose guardianship is accepted; that is, takes Satan as a protector ﴿instead of Allah, has certainly suffered a clear loss.⁠﻿﻿

Taking Satan as a protector happens through obeying him. Whoever obeys Satan and disobeys the Most Merciful has certainly suffered a clear loss. Loss is the opposite of profit. Indeed, the one who loses is the one who did not even retain his capital; he did not gain, but lost.

As for His words ﴿mubīnan﴾ ("clear"), it is derived from (abāna). It is a derivative of a quadriliteral verb, and its original form is (mubyin). But the vowel of the yā' was transferred to the preceding sound consonant, and the sukūn (absence of vowel) of the letter that preceded it was transferred to the yā', so it became (mubīnan).

I say: it derives from (abāna), and (abāna) can be intransitive or transitive. You say: "bāna al-fajr" (the dawn appeared) and "abāna al-fajr" (the dawn made itself clear). If we take it as intransitive, ﴿mubīnan﴾ means "clear and evident". If we take it as transitive (abāna al-shay' means "he made the thing manifest"), the meaning becomes that it is a loss that manifests and becomes evident in the one who suffers it.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires, but Satan does not promise them except delusion.﴾ In ﴿He promises them﴾, the pronoun, the subject pronoun, refers back to ﴿Satan﴾. The hā' (the "them" suffix) is the object pronoun, referring to the servants whom Satan led astray.

What does he promise them? He promises them things they desire and hope for, and so they follow him. For example, he says to him: "Commit this sin and repent to Allah afterwards," "Commit this sin, for it is minor," "Commit this sin and you will get such-and-such." Just as he said to Adam: ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that will never decay?⁠﻿﻿

﴿And arouses their desires﴾ means he raises their hopes and opens before them false expectations.

﴿But Satan does not promise them except delusion﴾. Here the noun is repeated in place of a pronoun. The context required him to say "but Satan does not promise them except delusion," but he used the noun in place of the pronoun to highlight his enmity, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy⁠﻿﻿ [Fatir 6].

His words ﴿except delusion﴾ mean: except deception and falsehood.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires, but Satan does not promise them except delusion (120). Those – their refuge is Hell, and they will not find from it any means of escape (121). But those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is truth, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement? (122) It is not by your wishful thinking or the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper (123). And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer – those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged even the speck on a date seed (124). And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend (125).⁠﻿﻿ [An-Nisa' 120–125].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [idols], and they invoke none but a rebellious Satan﴾.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: an explanation of the reality of idols, and that they belong to the weak category; this is shown by His words: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [idols]﴾. We have already discussed in tafsir whether the meaning is that they name the idols with female names, or that these idols, because of their weakness, are like females in relation to males.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: obedience is called invocation (du'a') and worship ('ibadah); this is shown by His words: ﴿And they invoke none but a rebellious Satan﴾.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan misleads the children of Adam to such an extent that he makes them his servants.
Called invocation and worship; this is shown by His words: ﴿And they invoke none but a rebellious Satan﴾.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan misleads the children of Adam to such an extent that he makes them his servants. We have previously discussed whether the word (marīd, rebellious) is a descriptive (explanatory) adjective or a restrictive adjective; that is, whether all devils are rebellious, or whether they are divided. We mentioned two views on this. It is possible that it is an explanatory adjective, and the meaning is that every devil is rebellious. It is also possible that it is a restrictive adjective, meaning that devils are divided into the rebellious ones and others.

Then He said: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾, and so on to the end.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: Allah cursed Satan; this is shown by His words: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: a warning against submitting to the commands of the one whom Allah has cursed, because this clause serves as the reason for condemning them when they worshipped Satan.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan swore that he would take an appointed portion from the servants of Allah; this is shown by His words: ﴿And [Satan] said, "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion."⁠﻿﻿

* And among its benefits: affirmation that Satan speaks, and that he speaks as he also acts. The Prophet (ﷺ) informed that "he eats and drinks with his left hand" [[Recorded by Muslim (2020/106) with the wording: "Indeed Satan eats with his left hand and drinks with it," from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]]. So he speaks and acts, and he creates desires, promises, and deceives.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan's portion of the servants of Allah is appointed, meaning decreed, and it must happen. This is like His words, Exalted is He, in Surah Hud: ﴿And for that He created them, and the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together."⁠﻿﻿ [Hud 119].

Then He said: ﴿And I will surely mislead them, and I will surely arouse their desires, and I will surely command them⁠﻿﻿, and so on to the end.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: Satan swore with an emphatic oath that he would mislead those portions that were allotted to him, and this oath has its implications.

* Consequently: we must be wary of the whisperings of Satan, because they are all misguidance.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: this misguidance which Satan causes among the children of Adam is accompanied by desires, meaning that he introduces wishful thinking to them, that they will receive good, that sins will not harm them, that repentance is near, and similar things.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: caution against one who misleads you and introduces false desires into you, because all misguidance is evil.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: the prohibition of slitting the ears of livestock when it is done in the manner used by the people of ignorance (jahiliyyah). It has been mentioned previously that the people of ignorance used to slit the ears of livestock to indicate that they were forbidden and set free. So can it be said, based on this, that if a person slits the ears of livestock for a worldly benefit, is it permissible or not? The answer: it is permissible, because this is not one of the commands of Satan.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan commands the children of Adam, and they alter the creation of Allah; this is shown by His words: ﴿and they will surely alter the creation of Allah.⁠﻿﻿ Does "altering the creation of Allah" refer to slitting livestock ears, or is it general?

The correct view: it is general. This has been discussed earlier in tafsir, and we pointed to the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: the original rule regarding altering the creation of Allah is what? Prohibition, because it is among the commands of Satan. When we say "the original rule," this is to exclude alterations of Allah's creation that Allah has commanded, such as shaving the pubic area, trimming the moustache, plucking the armpit hair, and similar things. These are alterations, but they are permitted, so they do not fall under the commands of Satan, since Satan only commands immorality.

Does dyeing something black count as altering the creation of Allah?
The answer: yes, because the one who dyes himself black wants to make himself look young again, so he alters the creation of Allah from old age to youth. For this reason, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded changing grey hair with something other than black [[Recorded by Muslim (2102/79) with the wording: "Change this with something, and avoid black," from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah.]].

Does altering the creation of Allah include tattooing, filing the teeth, and plucking facial hair? Yes, all of this is included.

Does altering the creation of Allah include shaving the beard? Yes, it may be said that it is included, especially if a person persists in it and continues doing it. It may also be said that this is not an alteration, because the beard grows, and if it grows, the creation has not been altered. But most of those afflicted with shaving the beard continue in it, so their action here is an attempt to alter the creation of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Some scholars have explicitly stated that shaving the beard is an alteration of the creation of Allah.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: a warning against taking Satan as a protector; this is shown by His words: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly suffered loss.⁠﻿﻿

If someone asks: how do we know whether this person is an ally of Satan or not?

We say: everyone who disobeys Allah is an ally of Satan, but the alliance may be general or specific. If one obeys Satan in disbelief and polytheism, the alliance is general. If one obeys him in some sin, the alliance is specific. It should be known that a person's allegiance to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is reduced to the extent that he allies himself with Satan.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: an explanation that most of creation has suffered loss, because most of creation has taken Satan as an ally instead of Allah.

* Another benefit of His words ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires﴾, and so on to the end: emphasis on warning against Satan, his promises, and his desires. So the final clause ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires⁠﻿﻿ serves as an emphasis on His words: ﴿and I will surely arouse their desires, and I will surely command them, and they will surely slit the ears of livestock.⁠﻿﻿

* Another benefit of this noble verse: a warning against the delusion of Satan and the introduction of wishful thinking and hope; this is shown by His words: ﴿But Satan does not promise them except delusion.⁠

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 117–120 (part 1 of 2):

Then He said: ﴿They invoke, besides Him, none but females, and they invoke none but a rebellious devil.﴾ (In) here means (ma) (not), and the sign of this—that is, the sign that (in) means (ma)—is that (illa) (except) comes after it. This is the sign that it means (ma). ﴿It is not but a manifest magic﴾ [al-Ma'idah 110]. The meaning: "This is not..." ﴿This is not but a noble angel﴾ [Yusuf 31]. The meaning: "This is not but a noble angel." ﴿You are only a warner﴾ [Fatir 23], i.e., "You are not but a warner." So (in) comes in the sense of (ma), and its sign is what? That (illa) comes after it.

Also, (in) has several meanings, and there is no harm in mentioning them now so that our brothers who have not previously studied them may know them. It comes as a negation. It also comes as the lightened form of the heavy (inna), affirmative, the opposite of the negating (in), since the lightened form of the heavy is affirmative; for the lightened form of the heavy conveys emphasis, as it is in fact (inna) but lightened, so it is for what? For emphasis, unlike (in), which is for negation. The poet said:

...................... ∗∗∗ "And indeed Malik was of noble origins"

He boasts of his people and says:

...................... ∗∗∗ "And indeed Malik was of noble origins"

That is: "And indeed Malik was of noble origins."

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And indeed they were before that in manifest error﴾ [Al 'Imran 164]. (In kanu) means (inna). Where is its noun? They say: it is a pronoun of the matter (damir al-sha'n) which is omitted whenever it occurs, and the estimate is: "and indeed He" (wa innahu), i.e., the matter, or "and indeed they" (wa innahum), i.e., the people. Some of them say: we do not estimate a pronoun of the matter; we estimate a pronoun suited to the context. So if they are a group, we say the estimate is "indeed they" (innahum), and there is no harm in this.

In any case, this (in) is the lightened form of the heavy, and it is the opposite of the negating (in), because it is for affirmation and the emphasis of affirmation, unlike the negating (in).

(In) comes as a conditional, and this is very common, such as: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they desist, what has passed will be forgiven them﴾ [al-Anfal 38].

It comes as an extra particle, meaning its presence is like its absence, as in the poet's verse:

"You, Banu Ghudanah, are not gold ∗∗∗ nor silver, but indeed you are clay"

The poet is satirizing these people, saying: you are neither gold nor silver, rather you are clay. And "People are like mines" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3493) and Muslim (2526 / 199) from Abu Hurayrah], as the Prophet ﷺ said: a good mine and a bad mine. How many divisions are there? The divisions are four. Count the five?

* Student: Negating.
* Shaykh: Negating.
* Student: And extra.
* Shaykh: And extra. Count?
* Student: Lightened from the heavy.
* Shaykh: Lightened from the heavy.
* Student: Negating.
* Shaykh: And negating.
* Student: In the sense of (ma).
* Shaykh: It is the negating; it does not come as the lightened form of the heavy.

In any case, in this noble verse, ﴿They invoke, besides Him, none but females﴾, we say: (in) is negating, i.e., these polytheists do not invoke, besides Allah—that is, other than Allah—anything but females.

What is the meaning of His saying ﴿none but females﴾? It is said: the names of these idols are feminine names: al-Lat, al-'Uzza, Manat; these are all feminine names. The feminine is inferior to the masculine, not in its strength, nor its rank, nor its standing, nor in everything, ﴿and the men have a degree over them﴾ [al-Baqarah 228].

It is also said: the meaning of ﴿They invoke, besides Him, none but females﴾ is: they invoke none but something like females, which cannot repel harm from itself, so how could it repel harm from others?

According to this view, the masculine idols such as Hubal are included. Hubal is masculine, and yet he is worshipped besides Allah. On this basis, this view is closer to the truth, because it is more general, and because it shows the reality of these idols, that they cannot repel anything from themselves, so how could they repel it from others?

﴿And they invoke none but a rebellious devil﴾, i.e., they invoke none but a rebellious devil.

Here "invoking" (du'a') means worship, i.e., they worship none but the devil, and "worship" here means obedience: they obey the devil, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a manifest enemy. And that you worship Me; this is a straight path﴾ [Ya Sin 60–61]. So the devil commands them to associate partners, and they associate. So their associating with the devil is what kind of association?

* Students: Obedience.
* Shaykh: Association of obedience. And their associating with the idols is association of worship, as they worship them. A people in this state have no good in them; they worship only what does not benefit them, and they obey only the command of the devil.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾; the pronoun refers to the devil.

﴿Marid﴾: ﴿a rebellious devil﴾. (Al-marid) is one who has reached the utmost limit in transgression and insolence.

The devils are of kinds: among them is the marid, and among them is one who is not marid. For this reason, in some wordings of the hadith about the devils being chained in Ramadan it says: "The rebellious devils are chained" [al-Nasa'i (2106) and Ahmad (7917), the wording being his, from Abu Hurayrah], i.e., the stubborn people, the devils who are stubborn and strong in their defiance.

﴿Allah has cursed him﴾. Cursing (al-la'n) means expulsion and removal from the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Is this a statement or a supplication?

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, it must be a statement, because it comes from whom? From Allah, and Allah does things and does not supplicate against anyone. So Allah, the Exalted, informs that Allah has cursed him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense﴾ [Sad 78], and the second verse: ﴿And indeed upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense﴾ [al-Hijr 35]. So the curse of Allah and the curse of those who curse are upon Iblis until the Day of Recompense.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah has cursed him, and he said: "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion"﴾. ﴿And he said﴾: the subject is whom?

* Student: The devil.
* Shaykh: No, the subject is—﴿Allah has cursed him and he said﴾ is conjoined to what?

* Student: Resumption (istinaf).
* Shaykh: The waw is for resumption. Well done, the waw is for resumption. For this reason it is necessary to stop at your saying: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾. Stop. ﴿And he said﴾, i.e., the devil, ﴿and he said: "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion."﴾

The content of the saying is the clause ﴿I will surely take﴾, and this clause—as you see—is emphasized with how many emphases?

* Student: The lam, the nun of emphasis, and the implied oath.
* Shaykh: The lam, the nun of emphasis, and the implied oath. So with three emphases.

﴿He said﴾, i.e., to Allah. ﴿I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion﴾: ﴿a portion﴾ is the object of (atakhadha). The meaning: I will take them as allies; I will befriend them and they will befriend me.

And (al-nasib) is a part of a thing. So what is this portion? This portion is much greater than the earlier portion, because the Prophet ﷺ informed that Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection: "O Adam! He will say: At your service, and at your pleasure. He will say: Bring forth from your offspring a group to the Fire. He will say: O Lord, and what is the group of the Fire? He will say: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3348) and Muslim (222 / 379) from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri].

But we must know that the devil did not say: "I will take from among the children of Adam." He said: ﴿from among Your servants﴾, and "Your servants" is what? More general and comprehensive than the children of Adam; for this reason He said: ﴿an appointed portion﴾, and these are those whom he led astray from the children of Adam, and in relation to the children of Adam they are what? Much more.

So we say: is the intended meaning of "servants" here the children of Adam? Let us see. If it is said: they are the children of Adam, then it becomes a case of the general used to mean the specific, and then this appointed portion is much more than those who were spared from his misguidance.

If we say: the intended meaning of "servants" is what includes all creation, the angels are among the servants of Allah, as He said of them that they are ﴿honoured servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 26]. Likewise, all created things are humbled before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, either by legal humility or by decreed humility. On this basis the appointed portion relative to the servants in general is small, it is small; but relative to the children of Adam it is great, because of the nine hundred and ninety-nine out of every thousand, all of them are in the Fire, and one out of the thousand is in Paradise.

His saying ﴿an appointed portion﴾: "fard" means decisive determination, i.e., decreed and fixed. Allah the Mighty and Majestic gave him that and empowered him to mislead the children of Adam for a wisdom which He, glory be to Him, intended. But He threatened whoever follows him, saying: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you of them, all together﴾ [Sad 85].

﴿And I will surely mislead them﴾: he takes them as allies, befriends them, and they befriend him, and he also misleads them from what? From the path of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, whether from this nation or from others. The clause here is emphasized with the same emphases as the clause before it, i.e., with three emphases. ﴿And I will surely mislead them﴾, i.e., from the straight path.

﴿And I will surely excite in them desires﴾: i.e., I will promise them with false hopes. And indeed this happened to Adam, when the devil said to him: ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ [Ta-Ha 120], and ﴿He swore to them both: "Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisers"﴾ [al-A'raf 21]. So Adam, peace be upon him, forgot that Allah had forbidden him, saying: ﴿Do not approach this tree﴾ [al-A'raf 19], but he promised them with false hopes and said: ﴿I will direct you to the tree of eternity﴾, i.e., to the tree which, if you eat from it, you will be made eternal and will have a kingdom that does not decay.

So the devil excites in the children of Adam desires, exciting them with many desires; among them: he makes the act of disobedience easy for him. He says: this is easy, this is minor; it will be expiated by the prayers, it will be expiated by the 'umrah, and so on. And the poor soul misled by the devil does not know that the prayers and 'umrah up to 'umrah, and what resembles them of that which expiates sins, must be complete; and who is it that brings the completion of the prayer?!

Most people now, their prayers reach the level of what? The level of being valid (al-ijza'), and perhaps they do not even reach that level.

Likewise, he says: this is easy: "Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that to whom He wills" [al-Nisa' 48]. He excites desire in him, saying: even if it were decreed that you die persisting in disobedience, you have righteous children who will pray for you, and "When a person dies, his deeds are cut off except from three" [Muslim (1631 / 14) from Abu Hurayrah], and so on. In short, he casts false hopes into their souls in many forms.

﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely cut off the ears of the cattle﴾: "I will command them" with a clear command face to face, or a command of inspiration from within the self? The second. And perhaps the devil appears in a human form and commands them with a clear command, but the basic principle is an inner command: he commands them to do such and such; for this reason He said: ﴿so they will cut off the ears of the cattle﴾. The fa' here is coordinating, and it is coordinated with (amurannahum). It will come, Allah willing, in the benefits (al-fawa'id) that it indicates complete submission on their part.

﴿so they will cut off the ears of the cattle, and I will surely command them, so they will alter the creation of Allah﴾. (Yubattikunna) means: they will cut. What is the grammatical analysis of (yubattikunna)?

* Student: The fa' is resumptive (tafri'iyya).
* Shaykh: Its analysis?
* Student: It is derived from what precedes it (mufarra'a).
* Shaykh: No, no, it is not derived; it is coordinating. The one who derives (mufarri') is one whose speech branches its end from its beginning. The fa' is coordinating, indicating sequence and immediacy. The lam?
* Student: The lam is the lam of initiation.
* Shaykh: Does it enter upon the subject so that it is the lam of initiation? The lam of initiation is the one that enters upon the subject (mubtada').
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Some say: it is preparatory to the oath, i.e., it prepares for the oath, because the oath is presumed before it. Continue.
* Student: (yubattikunna) is an imperfect verb.
* Shaykh: (yubattikunna) is all an imperfect verb?!
* Student: (yubattik) is an imperfect verb, and the subject is a hidden pronoun.
* Shaykh: Analyse first; complete the analysis of the verb before.
* Student: (yubattik) is an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the nun that is omitted to avoid the succession of similar sounds; and the nun is for emphasis.
* Shaykh: Why was the verb not built, given that it has the nun of emphasis?
* Student: Because it is not direct.
* Shaykh: Not direct. Then the omitted nun must be estimated, to avoid the succession of similar sounds. And the waw?
* Student: It is omitted to avoid the meeting of two quiescent letters.
* Shaykh: And the waw omitted for the meeting of two quiescent letters? And what? An object?!
* Student: It is the subject.
* Shaykh: The subject. Fine. And the nun?
* Student: The nun is omitted.
* Shaykh: No, the nun is present.
* Student: The nun is the nun of emphasis.
* Shaykh: The original of this word is: fa-layubattikunna adhan al-an'am. The first nun was dropped out of dislike for the succession of similar sounds, but the nun of emphasis was not dropped, because it was brought as a sign; if it were dropped, the sign would be lost. Then the waw was dropped, because when the first nun was dropped, the second nun met the quiescent waw, so two quiescent letters met. Ibn Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, says:

"If two quiescent letters meet, vowel the first; and if it is a soft letter, its deletion is deserved."

And here, is the first one soft or not soft? Soft, i.e., one of the letters of prolongation, so it is deleted.

The meaning of ﴿fa-layubattikunna﴾ is: so they will cut the ears of the cattle. And the mere cutting is not what is included in the verse; rather, they cut the ears of the cattle as a sign that they are forbidden, because they forbid what Allah has permitted and permit what Allah has forbidden. They have known rules and regulations, man-made laws, not legislated by Sharia.

When a she-camel bears such-and-such number of offspring, then she must be released; the sign? Cutting the ear. This is what is mentioned in His saying: ﴿Allah did not prescribe any baheerah, sa'ibah, wasilah, or ham﴾ [al-Ma'idah 103]. But it is explained: this cutting—they do not cut it as a sign and evidence that it belongs to so-and-so, as if they branded it; no, they cut it out of a false belief that it has become free, not to be ridden, not to be burdened, not to be given water from its milk, nor other things.

And al-an'am is the plural of na'am, like asbab the plural of sabab, and na'am applies to three things: camels, cows, and sheep.

﴿and I will surely command them, so they will alter the creation of Allah﴾.

* Student: Shaykh, you said it is emphasized with three emphases; the emphasis is implied, is it not present?
* Shaykh: How? What word do you mean?
* Student: ﴿He said: I will surely take﴾ — the implied one, O Shaykh, or the deleted one, does it not negate the emphasis? Is the emphasis mentioned?
* Shaykh: No, no. If a proof indicates the deleted element, it is as if it were present, and here there is a proof. Ibn Malik said in the Alfiyya, as one of the rules: what is known may be omitted... ∗∗∗ ......................
And although this was said about the subject and predicate, it should be general.

* Student: Those in the Fire, the nine hundred and ninety-nine, is this before the eternal abiding, so it includes the sinful Muslims, or after the eternal abiding, so it refers to the disbelievers?
* Shaykh: No, this is meant after the eternal abiding. What is meant by nine hundred and ninety-nine are those who will abide forever in the Fire.

* Student: You mentioned that His saying ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾ is a declarative sentence. The rhetoricians say that a declarative sentence is what can be described as true or false; it admits truth, so is this (...)?
* Shaykh: No, it is in itself, regardless of what it reports. For this reason, Musaylimah's saying "He is a messenger" does not admit truth.
And Muhammad's saying "He is a messenger" does not admit falsehood (...).

* * *

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely alter the creation of Allah.﴾ This is joined to what came before, to His words: ﴿I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion﴾, up to His words: ﴿And I will surely command them.⁠﻿ The meaning is that Satan commands the servants of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to alter the creation of Allah. So what is meant by "the creation of Allah"? Does it mean the fitrah (the innate disposition) upon which people were created, so that the meaning is that he alters the innate disposition of people from monotheism to polytheism, and from certainty to doubt, as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [This is] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be to the creation of Allah⁠﻿﻿? "What?" ﴿to the creation of Allah﴾ [Ar-Rum 30].

Or does "altering the creation of Allah" mean al-wasm (tattooing), al-washr (filing the teeth), an-namṣ (plucking the facial hair), and similar things?

Scholars hold two opinions, and the correct view is that it is inclusive. This is based on the well-known principle of tafsir (exegesis): whenever two interpretations are mentioned for a verse, they do not contradict each other, and the verse can bear both, then the verse must be understood as having both meanings together. Accordingly, He commands them to alter the creation of Allah, which is the fitrah upon which people were created, and the creation of Allah is also the physical alteration through filing the teeth, tattooing, filing (washr), and other such things, because this meaning is more general.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly suffered a clear loss.﴾ Allah has spoken the truth. ﴿Whoever takes Satan﴾ means: makes him ﴿an ally﴾, that is, one whose guardianship is accepted; that is, takes Satan as a protector ﴿instead of Allah, has certainly suffered a clear loss.⁠﻿﻿

Taking Satan as a protector happens through obeying him. Whoever obeys Satan and disobeys the Most Merciful has certainly suffered a clear loss. Loss is the opposite of profit. Indeed, the one who loses is the one who did not even retain his capital; he did not gain, but lost.

As for His words ﴿mubīnan﴾ ("clear"), it is derived from (abāna). It is a derivative of a quadriliteral verb, and its original form is (mubyin). But the vowel of the yā' was transferred to the preceding sound consonant, and the sukūn (absence of vowel) of the letter that preceded it was transferred to the yā', so it became (mubīnan).

I say: it derives from (abāna), and (abāna) can be intransitive or transitive. You say: "bāna al-fajr" (the dawn appeared) and "abāna al-fajr" (the dawn made itself clear). If we take it as intransitive, ﴿mubīnan﴾ means "clear and evident". If we take it as transitive (abāna al-shay' means "he made the thing manifest"), the meaning becomes that it is a loss that manifests and becomes evident in the one who suffers it.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires, but Satan does not promise them except delusion.﴾ In ﴿He promises them﴾, the pronoun, the subject pronoun, refers back to ﴿Satan﴾. The hā' (the "them" suffix) is the object pronoun, referring to the servants whom Satan led astray.

What does he promise them? He promises them things they desire and hope for, and so they follow him. For example, he says to him: "Commit this sin and repent to Allah afterwards," "Commit this sin, for it is minor," "Commit this sin and you will get such-and-such." Just as he said to Adam: ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that will never decay?⁠﻿﻿

﴿And arouses their desires﴾ means he raises their hopes and opens before them false expectations.

﴿But Satan does not promise them except delusion﴾. Here the noun is repeated in place of a pronoun. The context required him to say "but Satan does not promise them except delusion," but he used the noun in place of the pronoun to highlight his enmity, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy⁠﻿﻿ [Fatir 6].

His words ﴿except delusion﴾ mean: except deception and falsehood.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires, but Satan does not promise them except delusion (120). Those – their refuge is Hell, and they will not find from it any means of escape (121). But those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is truth, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement? (122) It is not by your wishful thinking or the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper (123). And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer – those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged even the speck on a date seed (124). And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend (125).⁠﻿﻿ [An-Nisa' 120–125].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [idols], and they invoke none but a rebellious Satan﴾.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: an explanation of the reality of idols, and that they belong to the weak category; this is shown by His words: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [idols]﴾. We have already discussed in tafsir whether the meaning is that they name the idols with female names, or that these idols, because of their weakness, are like females in relation to males.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: obedience is called invocation (du'a') and worship ('ibadah); this is shown by His words: ﴿And they invoke none but a rebellious Satan﴾.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan misleads the children of Adam to such an extent that he makes them his servants.
Called invocation and worship; this is shown by His words: ﴿And they invoke none but a rebellious Satan﴾.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan misleads the children of Adam to such an extent that he makes them his servants. We have previously discussed whether the word (marīd, rebellious) is a descriptive (explanatory) adjective or a restrictive adjective; that is, whether all devils are rebellious, or whether they are divided. We mentioned two views on this. It is possible that it is an explanatory adjective, and the meaning is that every devil is rebellious. It is also possible that it is a restrictive adjective, meaning that devils are divided into the rebellious ones and others.

Then He said: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾, and so on to the end.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: Allah cursed Satan; this is shown by His words: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: a warning against submitting to the commands of the one whom Allah has cursed, because this clause serves as the reason for condemning them when they worshipped Satan.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan swore that he would take an appointed portion from the servants of Allah; this is shown by His words: ﴿And [Satan] said, "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion."⁠﻿﻿

* And among its benefits: affirmation that Satan speaks, and that he speaks as he also acts. The Prophet (ﷺ) informed that "he eats and drinks with his left hand" [[Recorded by Muslim (2020/106) with the wording: "Indeed Satan eats with his left hand and drinks with it," from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]]. So he speaks and acts, and he creates desires, promises, and deceives.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan's portion of the servants of Allah is appointed, meaning decreed, and it must happen. This is like His words, Exalted is He, in Surah Hud: ﴿And for that He created them, and the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together."⁠﻿﻿ [Hud 119].

Then He said: ﴿And I will surely mislead them, and I will surely arouse their desires, and I will surely command them⁠﻿﻿, and so on to the end.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: Satan swore with an emphatic oath that he would mislead those portions that were allotted to him, and this oath has its implications.

* Consequently: we must be wary of the whisperings of Satan, because they are all misguidance.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: this misguidance which Satan causes among the children of Adam is accompanied by desires, meaning that he introduces wishful thinking to them, that they will receive good, that sins will not harm them, that repentance is near, and similar things.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: caution against one who misleads you and introduces false desires into you, because all misguidance is evil.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: the prohibition of slitting the ears of livestock when it is done in the manner used by the people of ignorance (jahiliyyah). It has been mentioned previously that the people of ignorance used to slit the ears of livestock to indicate that they were forbidden and set free. So can it be said, based on this, that if a person slits the ears of livestock for a worldly benefit, is it permissible or not? The answer: it is permissible, because this is not one of the commands of Satan.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan commands the children of Adam, and they alter the creation of Allah; this is shown by His words: ﴿and they will surely alter the creation of Allah.⁠﻿﻿ Does "altering the creation of Allah" refer to slitting livestock ears, or is it general?

The correct view: it is general. This has been discussed earlier in tafsir, and we pointed to the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: the original rule regarding altering the creation of Allah is what? Prohibition, because it is among the commands of Satan. When we say "the original rule," this is to exclude alterations of Allah's creation that Allah has commanded, such as shaving the pubic area, trimming the moustache, plucking the armpit hair, and similar things. These are alterations, but they are permitted, so they do not fall under the commands of Satan, since Satan only commands immorality.

Does dyeing something black count as altering the creation of Allah?
The answer: yes, because the one who dyes himself black wants to make himself look young again, so he alters the creation of Allah from old age to youth. For this reason, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded changing grey hair with something other than black [[Recorded by Muslim (2102/79) with the wording: "Change this with something, and avoid black," from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah.]].

Does altering the creation of Allah include tattooing, filing the teeth, and plucking facial hair? Yes, all of this is included.

Does altering the creation of Allah include shaving the beard? Yes, it may be said that it is included, especially if a person persists in it and continues doing it. It may also be said that this is not an alteration, because the beard grows, and if it grows, the creation has not been altered. But most of those afflicted with shaving the beard continue in it, so their action here is an attempt to alter the creation of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Some scholars have explicitly stated that shaving the beard is an alteration of the creation of Allah.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: a warning against taking Satan as a protector; this is shown by His words: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly suffered loss.⁠﻿﻿

If someone asks: how do we know whether this person is an ally of Satan or not?

We say: everyone who disobeys Allah is an ally of Satan, but the alliance may be general or specific. If one obeys Satan in disbelief and polytheism, the alliance is general. If one obeys him in some sin, the alliance is specific. It should be known that a person's allegiance to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is reduced to the extent that he allies himself with Satan.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: an explanation that most of creation has suffered loss, because most of creation has taken Satan as an ally instead of Allah.

* Another benefit of His words ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires﴾, and so on to the end: emphasis on warning against Satan, his promises, and his desires. So the final clause ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires⁠﻿﻿ serves as an emphasis on His words: ﴿and I will surely arouse their desires, and I will surely command them, and they will surely slit the ears of livestock.⁠﻿﻿

* Another benefit of this noble verse: a warning against the delusion of Satan and the introduction of wishful thinking and hope; this is shown by His words: ﴿But Satan does not promise them except delusion.⁠

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 117–120 (part 1 of 2):

Then He said: ﴿They invoke, besides Him, none but females, and they invoke none but a rebellious devil.﴾ (In) here means (ma) (not), and the sign of this—that is, the sign that (in) means (ma)—is that (illa) (except) comes after it. This is the sign that it means (ma). ﴿It is not but a manifest magic﴾ [al-Ma'idah 110]. The meaning: "This is not..." ﴿This is not but a noble angel﴾ [Yusuf 31]. The meaning: "This is not but a noble angel." ﴿You are only a warner﴾ [Fatir 23], i.e., "You are not but a warner." So (in) comes in the sense of (ma), and its sign is what? That (illa) comes after it.

Also, (in) has several meanings, and there is no harm in mentioning them now so that our brothers who have not previously studied them may know them. It comes as a negation. It also comes as the lightened form of the heavy (inna), affirmative, the opposite of the negating (in), since the lightened form of the heavy is affirmative; for the lightened form of the heavy conveys emphasis, as it is in fact (inna) but lightened, so it is for what? For emphasis, unlike (in), which is for negation. The poet said:

...................... ∗∗∗ "And indeed Malik was of noble origins"

He boasts of his people and says:

...................... ∗∗∗ "And indeed Malik was of noble origins"

That is: "And indeed Malik was of noble origins."

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And indeed they were before that in manifest error﴾ [Al 'Imran 164]. (In kanu) means (inna). Where is its noun? They say: it is a pronoun of the matter (damir al-sha'n) which is omitted whenever it occurs, and the estimate is: "and indeed He" (wa innahu), i.e., the matter, or "and indeed they" (wa innahum), i.e., the people. Some of them say: we do not estimate a pronoun of the matter; we estimate a pronoun suited to the context. So if they are a group, we say the estimate is "indeed they" (innahum), and there is no harm in this.

In any case, this (in) is the lightened form of the heavy, and it is the opposite of the negating (in), because it is for affirmation and the emphasis of affirmation, unlike the negating (in).

(In) comes as a conditional, and this is very common, such as: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they desist, what has passed will be forgiven them﴾ [al-Anfal 38].

It comes as an extra particle, meaning its presence is like its absence, as in the poet's verse:

"You, Banu Ghudanah, are not gold ∗∗∗ nor silver, but indeed you are clay"

The poet is satirizing these people, saying: you are neither gold nor silver, rather you are clay. And "People are like mines" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3493) and Muslim (2526 / 199) from Abu Hurayrah], as the Prophet ﷺ said: a good mine and a bad mine. How many divisions are there? The divisions are four. Count the five?

* Student: Negating.
* Shaykh: Negating.
* Student: And extra.
* Shaykh: And extra. Count?
* Student: Lightened from the heavy.
* Shaykh: Lightened from the heavy.
* Student: Negating.
* Shaykh: And negating.
* Student: In the sense of (ma).
* Shaykh: It is the negating; it does not come as the lightened form of the heavy.

In any case, in this noble verse, ﴿They invoke, besides Him, none but females﴾, we say: (in) is negating, i.e., these polytheists do not invoke, besides Allah—that is, other than Allah—anything but females.

What is the meaning of His saying ﴿none but females﴾? It is said: the names of these idols are feminine names: al-Lat, al-'Uzza, Manat; these are all feminine names. The feminine is inferior to the masculine, not in its strength, nor its rank, nor its standing, nor in everything, ﴿and the men have a degree over them﴾ [al-Baqarah 228].

It is also said: the meaning of ﴿They invoke, besides Him, none but females﴾ is: they invoke none but something like females, which cannot repel harm from itself, so how could it repel harm from others?

According to this view, the masculine idols such as Hubal are included. Hubal is masculine, and yet he is worshipped besides Allah. On this basis, this view is closer to the truth, because it is more general, and because it shows the reality of these idols, that they cannot repel anything from themselves, so how could they repel it from others?

﴿And they invoke none but a rebellious devil﴾, i.e., they invoke none but a rebellious devil.

Here "invoking" (du'a') means worship, i.e., they worship none but the devil, and "worship" here means obedience: they obey the devil, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a manifest enemy. And that you worship Me; this is a straight path﴾ [Ya Sin 60–61]. So the devil commands them to associate partners, and they associate. So their associating with the devil is what kind of association?

* Students: Obedience.
* Shaykh: Association of obedience. And their associating with the idols is association of worship, as they worship them. A people in this state have no good in them; they worship only what does not benefit them, and they obey only the command of the devil.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾; the pronoun refers to the devil.

﴿Marid﴾: ﴿a rebellious devil﴾. (Al-marid) is one who has reached the utmost limit in transgression and insolence.

The devils are of kinds: among them is the marid, and among them is one who is not marid. For this reason, in some wordings of the hadith about the devils being chained in Ramadan it says: "The rebellious devils are chained" [al-Nasa'i (2106) and Ahmad (7917), the wording being his, from Abu Hurayrah], i.e., the stubborn people, the devils who are stubborn and strong in their defiance.

﴿Allah has cursed him﴾. Cursing (al-la'n) means expulsion and removal from the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Is this a statement or a supplication?

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, it must be a statement, because it comes from whom? From Allah, and Allah does things and does not supplicate against anyone. So Allah, the Exalted, informs that Allah has cursed him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense﴾ [Sad 78], and the second verse: ﴿And indeed upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense﴾ [al-Hijr 35]. So the curse of Allah and the curse of those who curse are upon Iblis until the Day of Recompense.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah has cursed him, and he said: "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion"﴾. ﴿And he said﴾: the subject is whom?

* Student: The devil.
* Shaykh: No, the subject is—﴿Allah has cursed him and he said﴾ is conjoined to what?

* Student: Resumption (istinaf).
* Shaykh: The waw is for resumption. Well done, the waw is for resumption. For this reason it is necessary to stop at your saying: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾. Stop. ﴿And he said﴾, i.e., the devil, ﴿and he said: "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion."﴾

The content of the saying is the clause ﴿I will surely take﴾, and this clause—as you see—is emphasized with how many emphases?

* Student: The lam, the nun of emphasis, and the implied oath.
* Shaykh: The lam, the nun of emphasis, and the implied oath. So with three emphases.

﴿He said﴾, i.e., to Allah. ﴿I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion﴾: ﴿a portion﴾ is the object of (atakhadha). The meaning: I will take them as allies; I will befriend them and they will befriend me.

And (al-nasib) is a part of a thing. So what is this portion? This portion is much greater than the earlier portion, because the Prophet ﷺ informed that Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection: "O Adam! He will say: At your service, and at your pleasure. He will say: Bring forth from your offspring a group to the Fire. He will say: O Lord, and what is the group of the Fire? He will say: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3348) and Muslim (222 / 379) from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri].

But we must know that the devil did not say: "I will take from among the children of Adam." He said: ﴿from among Your servants﴾, and "Your servants" is what? More general and comprehensive than the children of Adam; for this reason He said: ﴿an appointed portion﴾, and these are those whom he led astray from the children of Adam, and in relation to the children of Adam they are what? Much more.

So we say: is the intended meaning of "servants" here the children of Adam? Let us see. If it is said: they are the children of Adam, then it becomes a case of the general used to mean the specific, and then this appointed portion is much more than those who were spared from his misguidance.

If we say: the intended meaning of "servants" is what includes all creation, the angels are among the servants of Allah, as He said of them that they are ﴿honoured servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 26]. Likewise, all created things are humbled before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, either by legal humility or by decreed humility. On this basis the appointed portion relative to the servants in general is small, it is small; but relative to the children of Adam it is great, because of the nine hundred and ninety-nine out of every thousand, all of them are in the Fire, and one out of the thousand is in Paradise.

His saying ﴿an appointed portion﴾: "fard" means decisive determination, i.e., decreed and fixed. Allah the Mighty and Majestic gave him that and empowered him to mislead the children of Adam for a wisdom which He, glory be to Him, intended. But He threatened whoever follows him, saying: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you of them, all together﴾ [Sad 85].

﴿And I will surely mislead them﴾: he takes them as allies, befriends them, and they befriend him, and he also misleads them from what? From the path of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, whether from this nation or from others. The clause here is emphasized with the same emphases as the clause before it, i.e., with three emphases. ﴿And I will surely mislead them﴾, i.e., from the straight path.

﴿And I will surely excite in them desires﴾: i.e., I will promise them with false hopes. And indeed this happened to Adam, when the devil said to him: ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ [Ta-Ha 120], and ﴿He swore to them both: "Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisers"﴾ [al-A'raf 21]. So Adam, peace be upon him, forgot that Allah had forbidden him, saying: ﴿Do not approach this tree﴾ [al-A'raf 19], but he promised them with false hopes and said: ﴿I will direct you to the tree of eternity﴾, i.e., to the tree which, if you eat from it, you will be made eternal and will have a kingdom that does not decay.

So the devil excites in the children of Adam desires, exciting them with many desires; among them: he makes the act of disobedience easy for him. He says: this is easy, this is minor; it will be expiated by the prayers, it will be expiated by the 'umrah, and so on. And the poor soul misled by the devil does not know that the prayers and 'umrah up to 'umrah, and what resembles them of that which expiates sins, must be complete; and who is it that brings the completion of the prayer?!

Most people now, their prayers reach the level of what? The level of being valid (al-ijza'), and perhaps they do not even reach that level.

Likewise, he says: this is easy: "Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that to whom He wills" [al-Nisa' 48]. He excites desire in him, saying: even if it were decreed that you die persisting in disobedience, you have righteous children who will pray for you, and "When a person dies, his deeds are cut off except from three" [Muslim (1631 / 14) from Abu Hurayrah], and so on. In short, he casts false hopes into their souls in many forms.

﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely cut off the ears of the cattle﴾: "I will command them" with a clear command face to face, or a command of inspiration from within the self? The second. And perhaps the devil appears in a human form and commands them with a clear command, but the basic principle is an inner command: he commands them to do such and such; for this reason He said: ﴿so they will cut off the ears of the cattle﴾. The fa' here is coordinating, and it is coordinated with (amurannahum). It will come, Allah willing, in the benefits (al-fawa'id) that it indicates complete submission on their part.

﴿so they will cut off the ears of the cattle, and I will surely command them, so they will alter the creation of Allah﴾. (Yubattikunna) means: they will cut. What is the grammatical analysis of (yubattikunna)?

* Student: The fa' is resumptive (tafri'iyya).
* Shaykh: Its analysis?
* Student: It is derived from what precedes it (mufarra'a).
* Shaykh: No, no, it is not derived; it is coordinating. The one who derives (mufarri') is one whose speech branches its end from its beginning. The fa' is coordinating, indicating sequence and immediacy. The lam?
* Student: The lam is the lam of initiation.
* Shaykh: Does it enter upon the subject so that it is the lam of initiation? The lam of initiation is the one that enters upon the subject (mubtada').
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Some say: it is preparatory to the oath, i.e., it prepares for the oath, because the oath is presumed before it. Continue.
* Student: (yubattikunna) is an imperfect verb.
* Shaykh: (yubattikunna) is all an imperfect verb?!
* Student: (yubattik) is an imperfect verb, and the subject is a hidden pronoun.
* Shaykh: Analyse first; complete the analysis of the verb before.
* Student: (yubattik) is an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the nun that is omitted to avoid the succession of similar sounds; and the nun is for emphasis.
* Shaykh: Why was the verb not built, given that it has the nun of emphasis?
* Student: Because it is not direct.
* Shaykh: Not direct. Then the omitted nun must be estimated, to avoid the succession of similar sounds. And the waw?
* Student: It is omitted to avoid the meeting of two quiescent letters.
* Shaykh: And the waw omitted for the meeting of two quiescent letters? And what? An object?!
* Student: It is the subject.
* Shaykh: The subject. Fine. And the nun?
* Student: The nun is omitted.
* Shaykh: No, the nun is present.
* Student: The nun is the nun of emphasis.
* Shaykh: The original of this word is: fa-layubattikunna adhan al-an'am. The first nun was dropped out of dislike for the succession of similar sounds, but the nun of emphasis was not dropped, because it was brought as a sign; if it were dropped, the sign would be lost. Then the waw was dropped, because when the first nun was dropped, the second nun met the quiescent waw, so two quiescent letters met. Ibn Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, says:

"If two quiescent letters meet, vowel the first; and if it is a soft letter, its deletion is deserved."

And here, is the first one soft or not soft? Soft, i.e., one of the letters of prolongation, so it is deleted.

The meaning of ﴿fa-layubattikunna﴾ is: so they will cut the ears of the cattle. And the mere cutting is not what is included in the verse; rather, they cut the ears of the cattle as a sign that they are forbidden, because they forbid what Allah has permitted and permit what Allah has forbidden. They have known rules and regulations, man-made laws, not legislated by Sharia.

When a she-camel bears such-and-such number of offspring, then she must be released; the sign? Cutting the ear. This is what is mentioned in His saying: ﴿Allah did not prescribe any baheerah, sa'ibah, wasilah, or ham﴾ [al-Ma'idah 103]. But it is explained: this cutting—they do not cut it as a sign and evidence that it belongs to so-and-so, as if they branded it; no, they cut it out of a false belief that it has become free, not to be ridden, not to be burdened, not to be given water from its milk, nor other things.

And al-an'am is the plural of na'am, like asbab the plural of sabab, and na'am applies to three things: camels, cows, and sheep.

﴿and I will surely command them, so they will alter the creation of Allah﴾.

* Student: Shaykh, you said it is emphasized with three emphases; the emphasis is implied, is it not present?
* Shaykh: How? What word do you mean?
* Student: ﴿He said: I will surely take﴾ — the implied one, O Shaykh, or the deleted one, does it not negate the emphasis? Is the emphasis mentioned?
* Shaykh: No, no. If a proof indicates the deleted element, it is as if it were present, and here there is a proof. Ibn Malik said in the Alfiyya, as one of the rules: what is known may be omitted... ∗∗∗ ......................
And although this was said about the subject and predicate, it should be general.

* Student: Those in the Fire, the nine hundred and ninety-nine, is this before the eternal abiding, so it includes the sinful Muslims, or after the eternal abiding, so it refers to the disbelievers?
* Shaykh: No, this is meant after the eternal abiding. What is meant by nine hundred and ninety-nine are those who will abide forever in the Fire.

* Student: You mentioned that His saying ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾ is a declarative sentence. The rhetoricians say that a declarative sentence is what can be described as true or false; it admits truth, so is this (...)?
* Shaykh: No, it is in itself, regardless of what it reports. For this reason, Musaylimah's saying "He is a messenger" does not admit truth.
And Muhammad's saying "He is a messenger" does not admit falsehood (...).

* * *

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely alter the creation of Allah.﴾ This is joined to what came before, to His words: ﴿I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion﴾, up to His words: ﴿And I will surely command them.⁠﻿ The meaning is that Satan commands the servants of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to alter the creation of Allah. So what is meant by "the creation of Allah"? Does it mean the fitrah (the innate disposition) upon which people were created, so that the meaning is that he alters the innate disposition of people from monotheism to polytheism, and from certainty to doubt, as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [This is] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be to the creation of Allah⁠﻿﻿? "What?" ﴿to the creation of Allah﴾ [Ar-Rum 30].

Or does "altering the creation of Allah" mean al-wasm (tattooing), al-washr (filing the teeth), an-namṣ (plucking the facial hair), and similar things?

Scholars hold two opinions, and the correct view is that it is inclusive. This is based on the well-known principle of tafsir (exegesis): whenever two interpretations are mentioned for a verse, they do not contradict each other, and the verse can bear both, then the verse must be understood as having both meanings together. Accordingly, He commands them to alter the creation of Allah, which is the fitrah upon which people were created, and the creation of Allah is also the physical alteration through filing the teeth, tattooing, filing (washr), and other such things, because this meaning is more general.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly suffered a clear loss.﴾ Allah has spoken the truth. ﴿Whoever takes Satan﴾ means: makes him ﴿an ally﴾, that is, one whose guardianship is accepted; that is, takes Satan as a protector ﴿instead of Allah, has certainly suffered a clear loss.⁠﻿﻿

Taking Satan as a protector happens through obeying him. Whoever obeys Satan and disobeys the Most Merciful has certainly suffered a clear loss. Loss is the opposite of profit. Indeed, the one who loses is the one who did not even retain his capital; he did not gain, but lost.

As for His words ﴿mubīnan﴾ ("clear"), it is derived from (abāna). It is a derivative of a quadriliteral verb, and its original form is (mubyin). But the vowel of the yā' was transferred to the preceding sound consonant, and the sukūn (absence of vowel) of the letter that preceded it was transferred to the yā', so it became (mubīnan).

I say: it derives from (abāna), and (abāna) can be intransitive or transitive. You say: "bāna al-fajr" (the dawn appeared) and "abāna al-fajr" (the dawn made itself clear). If we take it as intransitive, ﴿mubīnan﴾ means "clear and evident". If we take it as transitive (abāna al-shay' means "he made the thing manifest"), the meaning becomes that it is a loss that manifests and becomes evident in the one who suffers it.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires, but Satan does not promise them except delusion.﴾ In ﴿He promises them﴾, the pronoun, the subject pronoun, refers back to ﴿Satan﴾. The hā' (the "them" suffix) is the object pronoun, referring to the servants whom Satan led astray.

What does he promise them? He promises them things they desire and hope for, and so they follow him. For example, he says to him: "Commit this sin and repent to Allah afterwards," "Commit this sin, for it is minor," "Commit this sin and you will get such-and-such." Just as he said to Adam: ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that will never decay?⁠﻿﻿

﴿And arouses their desires﴾ means he raises their hopes and opens before them false expectations.

﴿But Satan does not promise them except delusion﴾. Here the noun is repeated in place of a pronoun. The context required him to say "but Satan does not promise them except delusion," but he used the noun in place of the pronoun to highlight his enmity, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy⁠﻿﻿ [Fatir 6].

His words ﴿except delusion﴾ mean: except deception and falsehood.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires, but Satan does not promise them except delusion (120). Those – their refuge is Hell, and they will not find from it any means of escape (121). But those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is truth, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement? (122) It is not by your wishful thinking or the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper (123). And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer – those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged even the speck on a date seed (124). And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend (125).⁠﻿﻿ [An-Nisa' 120–125].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [idols], and they invoke none but a rebellious Satan﴾.
