* From the benefits of this noble verse: an explanation of the reality of idols, and that they belong to the weak category; this is shown by His words: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [idols]﴾. We have already discussed in tafsir whether the meaning is that they name the idols with female names, or that these idols, because of their weakness, are like females in relation to males.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: obedience is called invocation (du'a') and worship ('ibadah); this is shown by His words: ﴿And they invoke none but a rebellious Satan﴾.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan misleads the children of Adam to such an extent that he makes them his servants.
Called invocation and worship; this is shown by His words: ﴿And they invoke none but a rebellious Satan﴾.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan misleads the children of Adam to such an extent that he makes them his servants. We have previously discussed whether the word (marīd, rebellious) is a descriptive (explanatory) adjective or a restrictive adjective; that is, whether all devils are rebellious, or whether they are divided. We mentioned two views on this. It is possible that it is an explanatory adjective, and the meaning is that every devil is rebellious. It is also possible that it is a restrictive adjective, meaning that devils are divided into the rebellious ones and others.

Then He said: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾, and so on to the end.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: Allah cursed Satan; this is shown by His words: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: a warning against submitting to the commands of the one whom Allah has cursed, because this clause serves as the reason for condemning them when they worshipped Satan.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan swore that he would take an appointed portion from the servants of Allah; this is shown by His words: ﴿And [Satan] said, "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion."⁠﻿﻿

* And among its benefits: affirmation that Satan speaks, and that he speaks as he also acts. The Prophet (ﷺ) informed that "he eats and drinks with his left hand" [[Recorded by Muslim (2020/106) with the wording: "Indeed Satan eats with his left hand and drinks with it," from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]]. So he speaks and acts, and he creates desires, promises, and deceives.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan's portion of the servants of Allah is appointed, meaning decreed, and it must happen. This is like His words, Exalted is He, in Surah Hud: ﴿And for that He created them, and the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together."⁠﻿﻿ [Hud 119].

Then He said: ﴿And I will surely mislead them, and I will surely arouse their desires, and I will surely command them⁠﻿﻿, and so on to the end.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: Satan swore with an emphatic oath that he would mislead those portions that were allotted to him, and this oath has its implications.

* Consequently: we must be wary of the whisperings of Satan, because they are all misguidance.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: this misguidance which Satan causes among the children of Adam is accompanied by desires, meaning that he introduces wishful thinking to them, that they will receive good, that sins will not harm them, that repentance is near, and similar things.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: caution against one who misleads you and introduces false desires into you, because all misguidance is evil.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: the prohibition of slitting the ears of livestock when it is done in the manner used by the people of ignorance (jahiliyyah). It has been mentioned previously that the people of ignorance used to slit the ears of livestock to indicate that they were forbidden and set free. So can it be said, based on this, that if a person slits the ears of livestock for a worldly benefit, is it permissible or not? The answer: it is permissible, because this is not one of the commands of Satan.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan commands the children of Adam, and they alter the creation of Allah; this is shown by His words: ﴿and they will surely alter the creation of Allah.⁠﻿﻿ Does "altering the creation of Allah" refer to slitting livestock ears, or is it general?

The correct view: it is general. This has been discussed earlier in tafsir, and we pointed to the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: the original rule regarding altering the creation of Allah is what? Prohibition, because it is among the commands of Satan. When we say "the original rule," this is to exclude alterations of Allah's creation that Allah has commanded, such as shaving the pubic area, trimming the moustache, plucking the armpit hair, and similar things. These are alterations, but they are permitted, so they do not fall under the commands of Satan, since Satan only commands immorality.

Does dyeing something black count as altering the creation of Allah?
The answer: yes, because the one who dyes himself black wants to make himself look young again, so he alters the creation of Allah from old age to youth. For this reason, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded changing grey hair with something other than black [[Recorded by Muslim (2102/79) with the wording: "Change this with something, and avoid black," from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah.]].

Does altering the creation of Allah include tattooing, filing the teeth, and plucking facial hair? Yes, all of this is included.

Does altering the creation of Allah include shaving the beard? Yes, it may be said that it is included, especially if a person persists in it and continues doing it. It may also be said that this is not an alteration, because the beard grows, and if it grows, the creation has not been altered. But most of those afflicted with shaving the beard continue in it, so their action here is an attempt to alter the creation of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Some scholars have explicitly stated that shaving the beard is an alteration of the creation of Allah.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: a warning against taking Satan as a protector; this is shown by His words: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly suffered loss.⁠﻿﻿

If someone asks: how do we know whether this person is an ally of Satan or not?

We say: everyone who disobeys Allah is an ally of Satan, but the alliance may be general or specific. If one obeys Satan in disbelief and polytheism, the alliance is general. If one obeys him in some sin, the alliance is specific. It should be known that a person's allegiance to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is reduced to the extent that he allies himself with Satan.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: an explanation that most of creation has suffered loss, because most of creation has taken Satan as an ally instead of Allah.

* Another benefit of His words ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires﴾, and so on to the end: emphasis on warning against Satan, his promises, and his desires. So the final clause ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires⁠﻿﻿ serves as an emphasis on His words: ﴿and I will surely arouse their desires, and I will surely command them, and they will surely slit the ears of livestock.⁠﻿﻿

* Another benefit of this noble verse: a warning against the delusion of Satan and the introduction of wishful thinking and hope; this is shown by His words: ﴿But Satan does not promise them except delusion.⁠

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 117–120 (part 1 of 2):

Then He said: ﴿They invoke, besides Him, none but females, and they invoke none but a rebellious devil.﴾ (In) here means (ma) (not), and the sign of this—that is, the sign that (in) means (ma)—is that (illa) (except) comes after it. This is the sign that it means (ma). ﴿It is not but a manifest magic﴾ [al-Ma'idah 110]. The meaning: "This is not..." ﴿This is not but a noble angel﴾ [Yusuf 31]. The meaning: "This is not but a noble angel." ﴿You are only a warner﴾ [Fatir 23], i.e., "You are not but a warner." So (in) comes in the sense of (ma), and its sign is what? That (illa) comes after it.

Also, (in) has several meanings, and there is no harm in mentioning them now so that our brothers who have not previously studied them may know them. It comes as a negation. It also comes as the lightened form of the heavy (inna), affirmative, the opposite of the negating (in), since the lightened form of the heavy is affirmative; for the lightened form of the heavy conveys emphasis, as it is in fact (inna) but lightened, so it is for what? For emphasis, unlike (in), which is for negation. The poet said:

...................... ∗∗∗ "And indeed Malik was of noble origins"

He boasts of his people and says:

...................... ∗∗∗ "And indeed Malik was of noble origins"

That is: "And indeed Malik was of noble origins."

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And indeed they were before that in manifest error﴾ [Al 'Imran 164]. (In kanu) means (inna). Where is its noun? They say: it is a pronoun of the matter (damir al-sha'n) which is omitted whenever it occurs, and the estimate is: "and indeed He" (wa innahu), i.e., the matter, or "and indeed they" (wa innahum), i.e., the people. Some of them say: we do not estimate a pronoun of the matter; we estimate a pronoun suited to the context. So if they are a group, we say the estimate is "indeed they" (innahum), and there is no harm in this.

In any case, this (in) is the lightened form of the heavy, and it is the opposite of the negating (in), because it is for affirmation and the emphasis of affirmation, unlike the negating (in).

(In) comes as a conditional, and this is very common, such as: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they desist, what has passed will be forgiven them﴾ [al-Anfal 38].

It comes as an extra particle, meaning its presence is like its absence, as in the poet's verse:

"You, Banu Ghudanah, are not gold ∗∗∗ nor silver, but indeed you are clay"

The poet is satirizing these people, saying: you are neither gold nor silver, rather you are clay. And "People are like mines" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3493) and Muslim (2526 / 199) from Abu Hurayrah], as the Prophet ﷺ said: a good mine and a bad mine. How many divisions are there? The divisions are four. Count the five?

* Student: Negating.
* Shaykh: Negating.
* Student: And extra.
* Shaykh: And extra. Count?
* Student: Lightened from the heavy.
* Shaykh: Lightened from the heavy.
* Student: Negating.
* Shaykh: And negating.
* Student: In the sense of (ma).
* Shaykh: It is the negating; it does not come as the lightened form of the heavy.

In any case, in this noble verse, ﴿They invoke, besides Him, none but females﴾, we say: (in) is negating, i.e., these polytheists do not invoke, besides Allah—that is, other than Allah—anything but females.

What is the meaning of His saying ﴿none but females﴾? It is said: the names of these idols are feminine names: al-Lat, al-'Uzza, Manat; these are all feminine names. The feminine is inferior to the masculine, not in its strength, nor its rank, nor its standing, nor in everything, ﴿and the men have a degree over them﴾ [al-Baqarah 228].

It is also said: the meaning of ﴿They invoke, besides Him, none but females﴾ is: they invoke none but something like females, which cannot repel harm from itself, so how could it repel harm from others?

According to this view, the masculine idols such as Hubal are included. Hubal is masculine, and yet he is worshipped besides Allah. On this basis, this view is closer to the truth, because it is more general, and because it shows the reality of these idols, that they cannot repel anything from themselves, so how could they repel it from others?

﴿And they invoke none but a rebellious devil﴾, i.e., they invoke none but a rebellious devil.

Here "invoking" (du'a') means worship, i.e., they worship none but the devil, and "worship" here means obedience: they obey the devil, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a manifest enemy. And that you worship Me; this is a straight path﴾ [Ya Sin 60–61]. So the devil commands them to associate partners, and they associate. So their associating with the devil is what kind of association?

* Students: Obedience.
* Shaykh: Association of obedience. And their associating with the idols is association of worship, as they worship them. A people in this state have no good in them; they worship only what does not benefit them, and they obey only the command of the devil.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾; the pronoun refers to the devil.

﴿Marid﴾: ﴿a rebellious devil﴾. (Al-marid) is one who has reached the utmost limit in transgression and insolence.

The devils are of kinds: among them is the marid, and among them is one who is not marid. For this reason, in some wordings of the hadith about the devils being chained in Ramadan it says: "The rebellious devils are chained" [al-Nasa'i (2106) and Ahmad (7917), the wording being his, from Abu Hurayrah], i.e., the stubborn people, the devils who are stubborn and strong in their defiance.

﴿Allah has cursed him﴾. Cursing (al-la'n) means expulsion and removal from the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Is this a statement or a supplication?

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, it must be a statement, because it comes from whom? From Allah, and Allah does things and does not supplicate against anyone. So Allah, the Exalted, informs that Allah has cursed him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense﴾ [Sad 78], and the second verse: ﴿And indeed upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense﴾ [al-Hijr 35]. So the curse of Allah and the curse of those who curse are upon Iblis until the Day of Recompense.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah has cursed him, and he said: "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion"﴾. ﴿And he said﴾: the subject is whom?

* Student: The devil.
* Shaykh: No, the subject is—﴿Allah has cursed him and he said﴾ is conjoined to what?

* Student: Resumption (istinaf).
* Shaykh: The waw is for resumption. Well done, the waw is for resumption. For this reason it is necessary to stop at your saying: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾. Stop. ﴿And he said﴾, i.e., the devil, ﴿and he said: "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion."﴾

The content of the saying is the clause ﴿I will surely take﴾, and this clause—as you see—is emphasized with how many emphases?

* Student: The lam, the nun of emphasis, and the implied oath.
* Shaykh: The lam, the nun of emphasis, and the implied oath. So with three emphases.

﴿He said﴾, i.e., to Allah. ﴿I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion﴾: ﴿a portion﴾ is the object of (atakhadha). The meaning: I will take them as allies; I will befriend them and they will befriend me.

And (al-nasib) is a part of a thing. So what is this portion? This portion is much greater than the earlier portion, because the Prophet ﷺ informed that Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection: "O Adam! He will say: At your service, and at your pleasure. He will say: Bring forth from your offspring a group to the Fire. He will say: O Lord, and what is the group of the Fire? He will say: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3348) and Muslim (222 / 379) from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri].

But we must know that the devil did not say: "I will take from among the children of Adam." He said: ﴿from among Your servants﴾, and "Your servants" is what? More general and comprehensive than the children of Adam; for this reason He said: ﴿an appointed portion﴾, and these are those whom he led astray from the children of Adam, and in relation to the children of Adam they are what? Much more.

So we say: is the intended meaning of "servants" here the children of Adam? Let us see. If it is said: they are the children of Adam, then it becomes a case of the general used to mean the specific, and then this appointed portion is much more than those who were spared from his misguidance.

If we say: the intended meaning of "servants" is what includes all creation, the angels are among the servants of Allah, as He said of them that they are ﴿honoured servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 26]. Likewise, all created things are humbled before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, either by legal humility or by decreed humility. On this basis the appointed portion relative to the servants in general is small, it is small; but relative to the children of Adam it is great, because of the nine hundred and ninety-nine out of every thousand, all of them are in the Fire, and one out of the thousand is in Paradise.

His saying ﴿an appointed portion﴾: "fard" means decisive determination, i.e., decreed and fixed. Allah the Mighty and Majestic gave him that and empowered him to mislead the children of Adam for a wisdom which He, glory be to Him, intended. But He threatened whoever follows him, saying: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you of them, all together﴾ [Sad 85].

﴿And I will surely mislead them﴾: he takes them as allies, befriends them, and they befriend him, and he also misleads them from what? From the path of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, whether from this nation or from others. The clause here is emphasized with the same emphases as the clause before it, i.e., with three emphases. ﴿And I will surely mislead them﴾, i.e., from the straight path.

﴿And I will surely excite in them desires﴾: i.e., I will promise them with false hopes. And indeed this happened to Adam, when the devil said to him: ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ [Ta-Ha 120], and ﴿He swore to them both: "Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisers"﴾ [al-A'raf 21]. So Adam, peace be upon him, forgot that Allah had forbidden him, saying: ﴿Do not approach this tree﴾ [al-A'raf 19], but he promised them with false hopes and said: ﴿I will direct you to the tree of eternity﴾, i.e., to the tree which, if you eat from it, you will be made eternal and will have a kingdom that does not decay.

So the devil excites in the children of Adam desires, exciting them with many desires; among them: he makes the act of disobedience easy for him. He says: this is easy, this is minor; it will be expiated by the prayers, it will be expiated by the 'umrah, and so on. And the poor soul misled by the devil does not know that the prayers and 'umrah up to 'umrah, and what resembles them of that which expiates sins, must be complete; and who is it that brings the completion of the prayer?!

Most people now, their prayers reach the level of what? The level of being valid (al-ijza'), and perhaps they do not even reach that level.

Likewise, he says: this is easy: "Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that to whom He wills" [al-Nisa' 48]. He excites desire in him, saying: even if it were decreed that you die persisting in disobedience, you have righteous children who will pray for you, and "When a person dies, his deeds are cut off except from three" [Muslim (1631 / 14) from Abu Hurayrah], and so on. In short, he casts false hopes into their souls in many forms.

﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely cut off the ears of the cattle﴾: "I will command them" with a clear command face to face, or a command of inspiration from within the self? The second. And perhaps the devil appears in a human form and commands them with a clear command, but the basic principle is an inner command: he commands them to do such and such; for this reason He said: ﴿so they will cut off the ears of the cattle﴾. The fa' here is coordinating, and it is coordinated with (amurannahum). It will come, Allah willing, in the benefits (al-fawa'id) that it indicates complete submission on their part.

﴿so they will cut off the ears of the cattle, and I will surely command them, so they will alter the creation of Allah﴾. (Yubattikunna) means: they will cut. What is the grammatical analysis of (yubattikunna)?

* Student: The fa' is resumptive (tafri'iyya).
* Shaykh: Its analysis?
* Student: It is derived from what precedes it (mufarra'a).
* Shaykh: No, no, it is not derived; it is coordinating. The one who derives (mufarri') is one whose speech branches its end from its beginning. The fa' is coordinating, indicating sequence and immediacy. The lam?
* Student: The lam is the lam of initiation.
* Shaykh: Does it enter upon the subject so that it is the lam of initiation? The lam of initiation is the one that enters upon the subject (mubtada').
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Some say: it is preparatory to the oath, i.e., it prepares for the oath, because the oath is presumed before it. Continue.
* Student: (yubattikunna) is an imperfect verb.
* Shaykh: (yubattikunna) is all an imperfect verb?!
* Student: (yubattik) is an imperfect verb, and the subject is a hidden pronoun.
* Shaykh: Analyse first; complete the analysis of the verb before.
* Student: (yubattik) is an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the nun that is omitted to avoid the succession of similar sounds; and the nun is for emphasis.
* Shaykh: Why was the verb not built, given that it has the nun of emphasis?
* Student: Because it is not direct.
* Shaykh: Not direct. Then the omitted nun must be estimated, to avoid the succession of similar sounds. And the waw?
* Student: It is omitted to avoid the meeting of two quiescent letters.
* Shaykh: And the waw omitted for the meeting of two quiescent letters? And what? An object?!
* Student: It is the subject.
* Shaykh: The subject. Fine. And the nun?
* Student: The nun is omitted.
* Shaykh: No, the nun is present.
* Student: The nun is the nun of emphasis.
* Shaykh: The original of this word is: fa-layubattikunna adhan al-an'am. The first nun was dropped out of dislike for the succession of similar sounds, but the nun of emphasis was not dropped, because it was brought as a sign; if it were dropped, the sign would be lost. Then the waw was dropped, because when the first nun was dropped, the second nun met the quiescent waw, so two quiescent letters met. Ibn Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, says:

"If two quiescent letters meet, vowel the first; and if it is a soft letter, its deletion is deserved."

And here, is the first one soft or not soft? Soft, i.e., one of the letters of prolongation, so it is deleted.

The meaning of ﴿fa-layubattikunna﴾ is: so they will cut the ears of the cattle. And the mere cutting is not what is included in the verse; rather, they cut the ears of the cattle as a sign that they are forbidden, because they forbid what Allah has permitted and permit what Allah has forbidden. They have known rules and regulations, man-made laws, not legislated by Sharia.

When a she-camel bears such-and-such number of offspring, then she must be released; the sign? Cutting the ear. This is what is mentioned in His saying: ﴿Allah did not prescribe any baheerah, sa'ibah, wasilah, or ham﴾ [al-Ma'idah 103]. But it is explained: this cutting—they do not cut it as a sign and evidence that it belongs to so-and-so, as if they branded it; no, they cut it out of a false belief that it has become free, not to be ridden, not to be burdened, not to be given water from its milk, nor other things.

And al-an'am is the plural of na'am, like asbab the plural of sabab, and na'am applies to three things: camels, cows, and sheep.

﴿and I will surely command them, so they will alter the creation of Allah﴾.

* Student: Shaykh, you said it is emphasized with three emphases; the emphasis is implied, is it not present?
* Shaykh: How? What word do you mean?
* Student: ﴿He said: I will surely take﴾ — the implied one, O Shaykh, or the deleted one, does it not negate the emphasis? Is the emphasis mentioned?
* Shaykh: No, no. If a proof indicates the deleted element, it is as if it were present, and here there is a proof. Ibn Malik said in the Alfiyya, as one of the rules: what is known may be omitted... ∗∗∗ ......................
And although this was said about the subject and predicate, it should be general.

* Student: Those in the Fire, the nine hundred and ninety-nine, is this before the eternal abiding, so it includes the sinful Muslims, or after the eternal abiding, so it refers to the disbelievers?
* Shaykh: No, this is meant after the eternal abiding. What is meant by nine hundred and ninety-nine are those who will abide forever in the Fire.

* Student: You mentioned that His saying ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾ is a declarative sentence. The rhetoricians say that a declarative sentence is what can be described as true or false; it admits truth, so is this (...)?
* Shaykh: No, it is in itself, regardless of what it reports. For this reason, Musaylimah's saying "He is a messenger" does not admit truth.
And Muhammad's saying "He is a messenger" does not admit falsehood (...).

* * *

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely alter the creation of Allah.﴾ This is joined to what came before, to His words: ﴿I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion﴾, up to His words: ﴿And I will surely command them.⁠﻿ The meaning is that Satan commands the servants of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to alter the creation of Allah. So what is meant by "the creation of Allah"? Does it mean the fitrah (the innate disposition) upon which people were created, so that the meaning is that he alters the innate disposition of people from monotheism to polytheism, and from certainty to doubt, as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [This is] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be to the creation of Allah⁠﻿﻿? "What?" ﴿to the creation of Allah﴾ [Ar-Rum 30].

Or does "altering the creation of Allah" mean al-wasm (tattooing), al-washr (filing the teeth), an-namṣ (plucking the facial hair), and similar things?

Scholars hold two opinions, and the correct view is that it is inclusive. This is based on the well-known principle of tafsir (exegesis): whenever two interpretations are mentioned for a verse, they do not contradict each other, and the verse can bear both, then the verse must be understood as having both meanings together. Accordingly, He commands them to alter the creation of Allah, which is the fitrah upon which people were created, and the creation of Allah is also the physical alteration through filing the teeth, tattooing, filing (washr), and other such things, because this meaning is more general.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly suffered a clear loss.﴾ Allah has spoken the truth. ﴿Whoever takes Satan﴾ means: makes him ﴿an ally﴾, that is, one whose guardianship is accepted; that is, takes Satan as a protector ﴿instead of Allah, has certainly suffered a clear loss.⁠﻿﻿

Taking Satan as a protector happens through obeying him. Whoever obeys Satan and disobeys the Most Merciful has certainly suffered a clear loss. Loss is the opposite of profit. Indeed, the one who loses is the one who did not even retain his capital; he did not gain, but lost.

As for His words ﴿mubīnan﴾ ("clear"), it is derived from (abāna). It is a derivative of a quadriliteral verb, and its original form is (mubyin). But the vowel of the yā' was transferred to the preceding sound consonant, and the sukūn (absence of vowel) of the letter that preceded it was transferred to the yā', so it became (mubīnan).

I say: it derives from (abāna), and (abāna) can be intransitive or transitive. You say: "bāna al-fajr" (the dawn appeared) and "abāna al-fajr" (the dawn made itself clear). If we take it as intransitive, ﴿mubīnan﴾ means "clear and evident". If we take it as transitive (abāna al-shay' means "he made the thing manifest"), the meaning becomes that it is a loss that manifests and becomes evident in the one who suffers it.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires, but Satan does not promise them except delusion.﴾ In ﴿He promises them﴾, the pronoun, the subject pronoun, refers back to ﴿Satan﴾. The hā' (the "them" suffix) is the object pronoun, referring to the servants whom Satan led astray.

What does he promise them? He promises them things they desire and hope for, and so they follow him. For example, he says to him: "Commit this sin and repent to Allah afterwards," "Commit this sin, for it is minor," "Commit this sin and you will get such-and-such." Just as he said to Adam: ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that will never decay?⁠﻿﻿

﴿And arouses their desires﴾ means he raises their hopes and opens before them false expectations.

﴿But Satan does not promise them except delusion﴾. Here the noun is repeated in place of a pronoun. The context required him to say "but Satan does not promise them except delusion," but he used the noun in place of the pronoun to highlight his enmity, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy⁠﻿﻿ [Fatir 6].

His words ﴿except delusion﴾ mean: except deception and falsehood.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires, but Satan does not promise them except delusion (120). Those – their refuge is Hell, and they will not find from it any means of escape (121). But those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is truth, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement? (122) It is not by your wishful thinking or the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper (123). And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer – those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged even the speck on a date seed (124). And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend (125).⁠﻿﻿ [An-Nisa' 120–125].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [idols], and they invoke none but a rebellious Satan﴾.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: an explanation of the reality of idols, and that they belong to the weak category; this is shown by His words: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [idols]﴾. We have already discussed in tafsir whether the meaning is that they name the idols with female names, or that these idols, because of their weakness, are like females in relation to males.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: obedience is called invocation (du'a') and worship ('ibadah); this is shown by His words: ﴿And they invoke none but a rebellious Satan﴾.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan misleads the children of Adam to such an extent that he makes them his servants.
Called invocation and worship; this is shown by His words: ﴿And they invoke none but a rebellious Satan﴾.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan misleads the children of Adam to such an extent that he makes them his servants. We have previously discussed whether the word (marīd, rebellious) is a descriptive (explanatory) adjective or a restrictive adjective; that is, whether all devils are rebellious, or whether they are divided. We mentioned two views on this. It is possible that it is an explanatory adjective, and the meaning is that every devil is rebellious. It is also possible that it is a restrictive adjective, meaning that devils are divided into the rebellious ones and others.

Then He said: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾, and so on to the end.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: Allah cursed Satan; this is shown by His words: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: a warning against submitting to the commands of the one whom Allah has cursed, because this clause serves as the reason for condemning them when they worshipped Satan.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan swore that he would take an appointed portion from the servants of Allah; this is shown by His words: ﴿And [Satan] said, "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion."⁠﻿﻿

* And among its benefits: affirmation that Satan speaks, and that he speaks as he also acts. The Prophet (ﷺ) informed that "he eats and drinks with his left hand" [[Recorded by Muslim (2020/106) with the wording: "Indeed Satan eats with his left hand and drinks with it," from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]]. So he speaks and acts, and he creates desires, promises, and deceives.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan's portion of the servants of Allah is appointed, meaning decreed, and it must happen. This is like His words, Exalted is He, in Surah Hud: ﴿And for that He created them, and the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together."⁠﻿﻿ [Hud 119].

Then He said: ﴿And I will surely mislead them, and I will surely arouse their desires, and I will surely command them⁠﻿﻿, and so on to the end.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: Satan swore with an emphatic oath that he would mislead those portions that were allotted to him, and this oath has its implications.

* Consequently: we must be wary of the whisperings of Satan, because they are all misguidance.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: this misguidance which Satan causes among the children of Adam is accompanied by desires, meaning that he introduces wishful thinking to them, that they will receive good, that sins will not harm them, that repentance is near, and similar things.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: caution against one who misleads you and introduces false desires into you, because all misguidance is evil.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: the prohibition of slitting the ears of livestock when it is done in the manner used by the people of ignorance (jahiliyyah). It has been mentioned previously that the people of ignorance used to slit the ears of livestock to indicate that they were forbidden and set free. So can it be said, based on this, that if a person slits the ears of livestock for a worldly benefit, is it permissible or not? The answer: it is permissible, because this is not one of the commands of Satan.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Satan commands the children of Adam, and they alter the creation of Allah; this is shown by His words: ﴿and they will surely alter the creation of Allah.⁠﻿﻿ Does "altering the creation of Allah" refer to slitting livestock ears, or is it general?

The correct view: it is general. This has been discussed earlier in tafsir, and we pointed to the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: the original rule regarding altering the creation of Allah is what? Prohibition, because it is among the commands of Satan. When we say "the original rule," this is to exclude alterations of Allah's creation that Allah has commanded, such as shaving the pubic area, trimming the moustache, plucking the armpit hair, and similar things. These are alterations, but they are permitted, so they do not fall under the commands of Satan, since Satan only commands immorality.

Does dyeing something black count as altering the creation of Allah?
The answer: yes, because the one who dyes himself black wants to make himself look young again, so he alters the creation of Allah from old age to youth. For this reason, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded changing grey hair with something other than black [[Recorded by Muslim (2102/79) with the wording: "Change this with something, and avoid black," from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah.]].

Does altering the creation of Allah include tattooing, filing the teeth, and plucking facial hair? Yes, all of this is included.

Does altering the creation of Allah include shaving the beard? Yes, it may be said that it is included, especially if a person persists in it and continues doing it. It may also be said that this is not an alteration, because the beard grows, and if it grows, the creation has not been altered. But most of those afflicted with shaving the beard continue in it, so their action here is an attempt to alter the creation of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Some scholars have explicitly stated that shaving the beard is an alteration of the creation of Allah.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: a warning against taking Satan as a protector; this is shown by His words: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly suffered loss.⁠﻿﻿

If someone asks: how do we know whether this person is an ally of Satan or not?

We say: everyone who disobeys Allah is an ally of Satan, but the alliance may be general or specific. If one obeys Satan in disbelief and polytheism, the alliance is general. If one obeys him in some sin, the alliance is specific. It should be known that a person's allegiance to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is reduced to the extent that he allies himself with Satan.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: an explanation that most of creation has suffered loss, because most of creation has taken Satan as an ally instead of Allah.

* Another benefit of His words ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires﴾, and so on to the end: emphasis on warning against Satan, his promises, and his desires. So the final clause ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires⁠﻿﻿ serves as an emphasis on His words: ﴿and I will surely arouse their desires, and I will surely command them, and they will surely slit the ears of livestock.⁠﻿﻿

* Another benefit of this noble verse: a warning against the delusion of Satan and the introduction of wishful thinking and hope; this is shown by His words: ﴿But Satan does not promise them except delusion.⁠

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Those—their refuge is Hell, and they will not find from it any escape﴾ [An-Nisa 121]. ﴿Those﴾ refers to those who obeyed Satan and followed him.

﴿Their refuge is Hell﴾, i.e., their place of return. ﴿Jahannam﴾ (Hell) is one of the names of the Fire. It was so named because it is—we seek refuge in Allah—deep and dark, and gloomy, so it is entirely jahmah (gloomy, grim). ﴿And they will not find from it any escape﴾: i.e., they will not find any refuge or place of flight from it. Rather, they will abide therein eternally, ﴿and they will never be removed from it﴾ [Al-Hijr 48], as in another verse.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the return of those who obey Satan is Hell, and it is not possible for them to leave it. This is to be understood as applying to those who obeyed him with absolute obedience. As for those who obeyed him in some sins, the position of the People of the Sunnah and the Community is that they are not made to abide eternally in the Fire, but are punished according to their deeds and then leave the Fire.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the affirmation of Jahannam, which is the Fire, by His saying: ﴿Those—their refuge is Hell﴾.

* Among its lessons: the people of Hell cannot be saved from it, and by its people is meant the disbelievers who left Islam for disbelief.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 122 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿But those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is true, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement?﴾ [An-Nisa' 122].

The connection of this verse to what precedes it: the Noble Qur'an is *mathani* (oft-repeated, paired), in which meanings are paired. When a warning comes, a promise comes; when the Fire is mentioned, the Garden is mentioned; when the believers are mentioned, the disbelievers are mentioned, and so on. This is so that a person is not perpetually fearful, such that despair overtakes him, nor perpetually hopeful, such that he feels secure from the plotting of Allah, but rather he is between these two.

As for His saying: ﴿those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, faith alone is not sufficient; there must be faith and action. In what do they believe? They believe in everything that faith in the unseen requires, and the Prophet (ﷺ) clarified the foundations of that in the hadith of Jibril, where he said: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and destiny, its good and its evil." [Recorded by Muslim (8/1) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]

As for His saying: ﴿did righteous deeds﴾, the intended meaning of *al-salihat* (the righteous [deeds]) is the actions. For this reason the grammarians said: *al-salihat* (الصالحات) is an adjective of a deleted noun, and the implied phrase is "the righteous deeds." The deletion of the modified noun is common in the language and in the Qur'an as well, as in His saying: ﴿that make full coats of mail﴾ [Saba' 11], meaning: coats of mail that are full (*dira'an sabighat*).

So what are the righteous deeds? The righteous deeds are that which is sincere (*khalis*) and correct (*sawab*). Sincerity is that which is for Allah alone, with no partnership for anyone in it, and correctness is that which conforms to the Law of Allah. By this, *shirk* (association of partners) is negated and innovation (*bid'ah*) is negated. By what is *shirk* negated?

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: By sincerity. And innovation?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: By following (*mutaba'ah*). Following cannot be realized unless the act conforms to the Law in six matters, which are: the cause (*sabab*), the kind (*jins*), the quantity (*qadr*), the form (*hay'ah*), the time (*zaman*), and the place (*makan*). If the act conforms to the Law in these six matters, following is realized in it; if any one of them is lacking, there is no following.

First: the cause. If a person worships Allah the Exalted with an act tied to a cause that Allah did not make a cause, there is no following. Among this is what happens at the birth celebration of the Prophet (ﷺ) of prayers upon him, remembrances, and other things, even if they are permissible; they do not conform to the Law. Why? Because the passing of the time in which he was born is not a cause for instituting this act of worship.

Likewise, some people, when they belch, say: "Al-hamdu lillah." Do you know what belching is?

* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: Clear. He says, "Al-hamdu lillah." This is not valid, because belching is not a cause for praise. Otherwise, the release of wind from the rear would be a cause for praise, and no one says this, not even the common folk. So we say: this is not following the Messenger (ﷺ).

Some people, when you give them incense, say: "Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad," making their fumigation a cause for prayer upon the Prophet (ﷺ). We say: this is not following, because the Prophet (ﷺ) used to perfume himself, and it is not reported from him that whenever he perfumed himself he prayed upon the Prophet.

Also among this: when someone yawns, some people say, "A'udhu billahi min al-shaytan al-rajim." This has no basis and is not from the Law, because the Prophet (ﷺ) guided us as to what to do when yawning: that a person suppress it as much as he can, and if he cannot, he places his hand over his mouth. [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6226) and Muslim (2994/56) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.] This is one.

Second: that the act conform to the Law in its kind. If one worships Allah with something of which Allah has not made its kind a means of worship, it is not accepted and is not from the Law. An example: sacrificing a horse. The horse is permissible, but if he sacrificed it, his sacrifice would not be accepted, why? Because it contradicts the Law in its kind, since sacrifices are only from the livestock animals (*bahimat al-an'am*).

Third: its quantity. If he prays five [rak'ahs] in a four-rak'ah prayer, or four in a three-rak'ah prayer, or three in a two-rak'ah prayer, his worship is not valid, because he has exceeded the prescribed quantity. Likewise, if he performs ablution four times, this excess is not rewarded, because he has exceeded the prescribed command. Likewise, if he circumambulates eight rounds, the excess is not from the Law, and he is not rewarded for it.

Fourth: its form, that it be in the manner that was reported. If a person prays and prostrates before bowing, having performed the bowing but after the prostration, it is not accepted, because it contradicts the Law in its form.

Likewise, if he performs ablution in reverse, beginning with washing the foot, then wiping the head, then washing the hands up to the elbows, then washing the face, this ablution is not valid.

Fifth: the time. If a person prays one minute before the time, his prayer is not valid, because it was not at the time that the Law prescribed. And if a person sacrifices - that is, slaughters his sacrifice - on the ninth day of Dhu al-Hijjah, it is not accepted, because it is at other than the time that the Law prescribed.

Sixth: its place. If he performs i'tikaf (seclusion) in his house instead of the mosque, his i'tikaf is not accepted, because it is not in the prescribed manner.

So the righteous deed is that in which the Prophet (ﷺ) is followed, and following is not realized until the worship is in the manner of the Law in these six matters.

As for His saying: ﴿We will admit them﴾, this sentence is the predicate of the subject; the predicate of ﴿those who﴾. The *sin* (سين) in it is for certainty and nearness. As for certainty, there is no difficulty. As for nearness - though it is distant - because its occurrence is certain, it is as if it were near. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾ [An-Nahl 1], where He expressed the future with the past, because of the certainty of its occurrence. A person might object to us, saying: "*sanudkhiluhum*" - if you say that *sin* is for certainty and nearness, a person may remain in this world eighty years before he dies? We say: what is certain is like what is near. Moreover, the future is near however distant it is; there is no doubt that the future is near however far it is, while the past is distant however near it is.

﴿We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾: "gardens" (*jannat*). Sometimes the expression appears as the singular "*jannah*," and there is no contradiction: it is a garden with respect to the genus, and gardens with respect to the types, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Two gardens of gold, their vessels and what is in them, and two gardens of silver, their vessels and what is in them." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4878) and Muslim (180/296) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.] What, then, is the Garden? Some people say: the Garden is an orchard with many dense trees. If we define it with this definition, it may diminish its value in the eyes of the common people especially, so we say: the gardens are the great abode that Allah the Exalted prepared for the righteous, in which is "what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4780) and Muslim (2824/2) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]

As for His saying: ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾, does ﴿from beneath them﴾ mean from beneath its land? No, rather from above the ground, but beneath the palaces and trees. Flowing water, a river flowing from beneath the trees and palaces, has a beautiful and attractive appearance. May Allah make us and you among its people, by His grace and generosity.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿But those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is true, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement? (122) It is not by your wishful thinking, nor the wishful thinking of the People of the Book: whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper. (123) And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer - those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged even the speck on a date-seed. (124) And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend. (125) And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever, of all things, Encompassing.﴾ [An-Nisa' 122-126].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. When Allah, glorified and exalted is He, mentioned the threat against those who oppose Him among the disbelievers and hypocrites, and that their refuge is Hell, from which they will find no escape, He mentioned the reward of the believers, saying: ﴿But those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them﴾. The discussion of this sentence and of His saying: ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever﴾ has already preceded. This is the recompense of the righteous who established faith and righteous deeds.

Then He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿The promise of Allah﴾. *Wa'da* (وعد) is a verbal noun whose governing verb is the meaning of the preceding sentence; it is a verbal noun emphasizing the meaning of the sentence. For this reason it is not correct to mention its governing verb with it, because if the governing verb of the verbal noun is mentioned with it, the emphasis remains on that verb, not on the sentence, and the aim is to emphasize the sentence, i.e., that this report is from Allah, mighty and majestic, a promise ﴿the promise of Allah﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿ḥaqqan﴾ (truly), it is said that it is a verbal noun emphasizing the verbal noun before it, i.e., this promise is true. It is also said that it is a verbal noun for a deleted verb, the implied meaning being: "Is that true? Truly." *Al-haqq* (the truth) is the established thing, and its opposite is falsehood, which is that which vanishes and is lost in vain. As for the truth, it is established and is not lost; rather it is intended in itself, and has its great fruits.

﴿The promise of Allah, true; and who is more truthful than Allah in statement?﴾ *Man* (من) is an interrogative particle, but it is imbued with the meaning of negation, so it is more emphatic than a bare interrogative, and more emphatic than a bare negation. We have mentioned previously that when the interrogative is imbued with the meaning of negation, it is what?

* Student: For challenge.

* Shaykh: Yes, imbued with the meaning of challenge: i.e., if you claim that anyone is more truthful than Allah in statement, then bring him.

As for His saying: ﴿man aṣdaq﴾ (who is more truthful), *aṣdaq* (أصدق) is a comparative noun derived from *ṣidq* (truthfulness), and truthfulness is the report of what agrees with reality; its opposite is lying, which is the report of what contradicts reality.

As for His saying: ﴿qīlan﴾ (in statement), it means "qawlan" (in speech), and it is a specification (*tamyiz*) following the comparative noun, as in His saying: ﴿I am more numerous than you in wealth and mightier in men﴾ [Al-Kahf 34].

* In this noble verse there is an explanation of the recompense of those who believe and do righteous deeds.
* Among its benefits: that faith alone is not sufficient, but there must be action; and that action alone is not sufficient, but there must be faith. Thus none deserves Paradise except one who combines faith and righteous deeds. When the reward of Paradise is mentioned restricted or conditioned by faith alone, what is meant is faith that includes righteous deeds.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that action benefits its doer only if it is righteous. You have known what the righteous is: it is the sincere and correct, that is, that which is done seeking the face of Allah and in accordance with the Law of Allah.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that we testify for every believer who does righteous deeds that he will enter Paradise, based on His saying: ﴿We will admit them﴾, then He said: ﴿The promise of Allah, true﴾. This is in general terms; we testify for every believer who does righteous deeds that he will enter Paradise.

But do we apply this testimony to all individuals of the general category, meaning that we specify one particular person? The answer: No, except for one whom Allah has testified for with this, or whom His Messenger (ﷺ) has testified for, or upon whom the Ummah has unanimously agreed. These are three:

The first: one whom Allah informed about as being among the people of Paradise.
The second: one whom the Messenger (ﷺ) informed about.
The third: one upon whom the Ummah has unanimously agreed, i.e., on praising him, and that he is among the people of goodness and the people of truth.

From the first is Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him). The saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿So I have warned you of a Fire flaming. None will enter it but the most wretched, who denied and turned away. But the most righteous will be spared it, who gives his wealth to purify himself, and for whom there is not [given] for anyone a favor that will be recompensed, except seeking the Face of his Lord, the Most High. And he is going to be satisfied﴾ [Al-Layl 14-21]. Most of the exegetes say: these were revealed concerning Abu Bakr. Based on this, the verse indicates testimony, indicates the information that he (may Allah be pleased with him) will be spared the Fire, and if he is spared the Fire, he will be among the people of Paradise, since there are only two abodes.

As for those whom the Prophet (ﷺ) testified to be in Paradise, they are many. For example, all the wives of the Messenger are in Paradise, because his wives in this world are his wives in the Hereafter. Among them also are the ten promised Paradise: Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Sa'id, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and so on; and among them Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, for the Prophet (ﷺ) testified to him of Paradise; and among them Bilal, to whom the Prophet (ﷺ) testified of Paradise; and among them 'Ukashah ibn Mihsan, to whom the Prophet (ﷺ) testified of Paradise. Examples of this are many.

As for what the Ummah has unanimously agreed upon, its evidence is that "a funeral bier passed by the Prophet (ﷺ) and they praised it well, so he said: 'It is obligatory,' then another passed by him and they spoke ill of it, so he said: 'It is obligatory.' They said: 'What is obligatory, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'As for the first, you praised him well, so Paradise became obligatory for him; and as for the second, you spoke ill of him, so the Fire became obligatory for him. You are the witnesses of Allah on His earth.'" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1367) and Muslim (949/60) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]

But one whose outward appearance is faith and righteous deeds, we say: whoever believes and does righteous deeds is among the people of Paradise, but we do not say: this particular person is, because we do not know how he will be concluded - we ask Allah to conclude for us and for you with goodness. He does not know. This man who was with the Prophet (ﷺ) in a military campaign, and was a brave, bold hero who left no enemy alone or single, "the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'He is among the people of the Fire,' and he was a fighter, he fought; 'this was great and grievous to the Companions, and a man from among the Companions said: I will certainly stay with him,' meaning: I will stay with him until I see what his end will be. 'So he stayed with him, and an arrow from the enemy struck this man, and he became very distressed, so he drew his sword, placed its tip on his chest, and leaned upon it until it came out through his back - and we seek refuge in Allah - and he died. The man who had stayed with him came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah. He said: 'Why?' He said: The man you said, "He is among the people of the Fire," such and such happened to him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, a man may work the work of the people of Paradise in what appears to people, and he is among the people of the Fire'" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2898) and Muslim (112/179) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd] - we seek refuge in Allah. Therefore it is not permissible for us to testify that a specific person is in Paradise, even if we see that his deeds are the deeds of the people of Paradise.

Among the lessons of this noble verse: Allah, Exalted is He, says, and "qawl" (saying) is an audible utterance. Therefore Allah, glory be to Him, speaks a true speech. Is it audible? The answer is yes; otherwise it would not be called speech, because speech that is inward self-talk must be qualified, as in His saying: ﴿And they say to themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"﴾ [al-Mujadila 8]. When it is stated without qualification, what is meant is audible speech. This is the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah): that Allah speaks with audible speech, that He speaks with sound, and that He speaks with letters. This implies no deficiency and no resemblance to creation; rather, it is perfection. Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) mentioned other positions, which you may consult in the abridgement of al-Sawa'iq al-Mursalah, reaching eight opinions concerning the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. The best known of them is the position of the Ash'aris (al-Ash'ariyyah), that the speech of Allah is the meaning subsisting in His essence, and that what is heard is created sounds which Allah created to express what is in His essence.

The Jahmiyyah said: rather, the speech of Allah is created, and its attribution to Allah is one of honour, not of description. They said: the speech of Allah is like the rest of created things. Which of them opposed the Sunnah? Both opposed the Sunnah, and the Ash'aris are further from the Sunnah than the Mu'tazilah, because all of them agree that what is heard is created. But the Mu'tazilah said: it is the speech of Allah; the Ash'aris said: it is not the speech of Allah, but rather an expression of the speech of Allah, and the speech of Allah is the meaning subsisting in His essence. According to their words, speech would mean knowledge entirely. All of this is false.

Among the lessons of this noble verse: the description of Allah's speech as truthful, the description of His speech and saying as truthful, by His saying: ﴿And who is more truthful in statement than Allah?﴾. Can it be described as false? No, by Allah, it cannot.

If someone says: Do not the rhetoricians say that a report (khabar) is that which admits of truth and falsehood? We say: Yes, but they qualify this, saying: that which admits of truth and falsehood in itself, i.e., regardless of its speaker. For some speech is certainly false, and some speech is certainly true, and neither admits the other.

Among the lessons of this noble verse: it is valid for us to place the superlative form (ism al-tafdil) between the attributes of Allah and the attributes of creation, so we say: the speech of Allah is the most truthful speech; the knowledge of Allah is what? The broadest knowledge; and Allah is more knowing than others.

Some people have thought that if you pair a description with the superlative form, you have likened Allah to creation, so they went on to interpret the saying of Allah: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am 124], and His saying: ﴿And your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Isra' 55], explaining them as meaning "knowing." They say: "a'lam" means "'alim" (knowing). Glory be to Allah! They fled from one deficiency but fell into something more deficient, because the superlative form indicates the exaltedness of Allah's attributes, that they are the highest attributes, with no deficiency in any respect.

They say "'alim" (knowing), and when you say "'alim," it does not preclude sharing and equality, does it not? For you say: "'Amr is knowing, Zayd is knowing, Muhammad is knowing, Bakr is knowing," and they are equal. But all of this befalls a person when he holds a creed and then tries to bend the texts toward it, and so falls into deviation. We ask Allah for well-being.

So, "a'lam" in the names and attributes of Allah is what? It is on its own basis; "a'lam" is on its own basis. Indeed Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Is Allah better, or what they associate with Him?﴾ [al-Naml 59]. Everyone would answer: Allah is better. Even the polytheists, with their idols, say that Allah is better. It is related that the Prophet ﷺ asked Husayn, Abu 'Imran ibn Husayn, saying to him: "How many gods do you worship?" He said: "Seven: six on earth and one in heaven." He said: "To whom do you turn for your desire and your fear?" He said: "The One in heaven."[[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (3483) from the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn.]] How do you worship others? They acknowledge that Allah, Exalted is He, is above everything, and even the polytheists acknowledge this.

Student: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself, besides Allah, any protector or helper. And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer—those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged even the speck on a date-seed.  And who is better in religion than one who submits himself completely to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend. And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever, of all things, encompassing.﴾ [An-Nisa 123–126].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture.﴾

The address in His words ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking﴾ is to this Ummah.

﴿Nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture﴾ means the Jews and the Christians. This is because the Jews and the Christians said: "We are the People of the Scripture, we are earlier than you, we are the friends and beloved of Allah," and so on, wishing to make themselves superior to this Ummah. This Ummah says: "Our Messenger is the Seal of the Prophets, and this Ummah has been preferred over the people," and it wants to be better than the People of the Scripture. So Allah separated between them and judged between them with a just judgment, saying: The matter is not by your wishful thinking, O Muslims, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Matters are not given according to a person's wish, such that whenever he wishes, what he wishes for is obtained, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Or does man have whatever he wishes? But to Allah belongs the Hereafter and the first life.﴾ [An-Najm 24–25].

His words ﴿the People of the Scripture﴾ mean the Jews and the Christians, and "the Scripture" refers to the Torah for the Jews and the Gospel for the Christians.

Then the ruling came: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ ﴿Whoever does﴾ — "man" here is conditional (shartiyyah), ﴿does﴾ is the verb of the condition (fi'l al-shart), and ﴿will be recompensed﴾ is the response of the condition (jawab al-shart). ﴿For it﴾ means: for its evil, whether from you, O this Ummah, or from the People of the Scripture: ﴿whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾

When we consider this ruling, we find that it applies to the People of the Scripture more than to this Ummah, because the People of the Scripture did evil by denying Muhammad ﷺ, so they are recompensed for it.

﴿And he will not find for himself﴾ is conjoined to the response of the condition: ﴿and he will not find for himself, besides Allah, any protector or helper.﴾ ﴿Besides Him﴾ means: other than Him. ﴿A protector﴾ is one who takes charge of him by bringing about benefits; ﴿nor a helper﴾ is one who defends him against harms and corruptions.

* From the benefits of this verse: wishful thinking benefits nothing, as in His words ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture.﴾ This supports what is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The intelligent one is he who holds himself accountable and works for what comes after death, and the incapable one is he who follows his desires and wishes vainly upon Allah."[[Narrated by at-Tirmidhi (2459) and Ibn Majah (4260) from the hadith of Shaddad ibn Aws.]]

* From the benefits of this noble verse: justice between disputants, even if one of them is upon truth and the other upon falsehood; justice is obligatory, and each is to be given what he deserves. What is the basis of this? The negation of the matter being by wishful thinking, with regard to the Muslims, the Jews and the Christians, then the affirmation that whoever does evil is recompensed for it, and this is the utmost justice. For this reason Allah said: ﴿O you who have believed, be persistent in standing firmly for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness.﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 8].

* From the benefits of this noble verse: a warning to whoever does evil, by His words ﴿whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, for his deed will not be lost and he will certainly be recompensed for it. The verse is unrestricted: is the recompense in this world, or in the Hereafter, or in both?

We say: if the punishment in this world is a legal punishment (ʿuqubah shar'iyyah), then he is not punished twice for it. For this reason it is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ that "whoever commits a crime and is then given its prescribed punishment in this world, it is an expiation for him."[[Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (18) and Muslim (1709/43) from the hadith of ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit; Musnad al-Shamiyyin (2267), the wording being his, from the hadith of Thabit ibn al-Dahhak.]] As for non-legal punishments, which are the decreed punishments that Allah sends upon a person, such as sickness, poverty, or other things, these may expiate sins, and nothing remains against him in the Hereafter; and they may not expiate all sins.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of not carrying out a threat (ikhlaf al-wa'id). This is because ﴿whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ is a threat, but Allah the Exalted said in His Book: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾, and this shows that whoever does evil—what? —may be forgiven by Allah, apart from shirk.

If someone asks: how do we answer this verse, ﴿whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, when it is a statement of information? We say: it is meant as a threat, and it belongs to the category of warning, and pardoning a threat is a matter of generosity, which is praiseworthy and not blameworthy. For this reason a poet praised himself by saying:

"And indeed I, even if I threaten him, or promise him, ∗∗∗ I am one who breaks my threat and fulfills my promise."

* From the benefits of this noble verse: a person is not recompensed with more than the evil he has done, as shown by His words ﴿will be recompensed for it﴾; the particle "bi" here indicates exchange or substitution. This is unlike one who does good, who is given more, as in other verses.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the perfection of Allah's power and dominion, as shown by His words ﴿and he will not find for himself, besides Allah, any protector or helper.﴾ Similar verses are repeated often in the Qur'an, such as His words: ﴿And you have not, besides Allah, any protectors; then you would not be helped﴾ [Hud 113], and His words: ﴿Abiding therein forever; they will not find a protector or a helper﴾ [al-Ahzab 65]. This is frequent, because Allah, glorified and exalted, is perfect in power and perfect in dominion; no one can prevent Him, and no one can repel Him.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: worldly calamities are expiations, because they are a kind of recompense. The Prophet ﷺ informed that no distress, nor worry, nor grief afflicts a servant except that Allah expiates it for him, even a thorn that pricks him, Allah expiates for him by it.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (5641) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abu Hurairah, and Muslim (2572/49) from the hadith of ʿAʾishah.]]

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer—those will enter Paradise, and they will not be wronged even the (smallest) speck.﴾ ﴿And whoever does﴾: this is a conditional (sharti) construction; the conditional verb is ﴿does﴾ (ya'mal), and the response of the condition is ﴿those will enter Paradise﴾. It is joined by the fa' (fa), because the response is a nominal sentence.

As for His saying ﴿whoever does﴾: we have said it is conditional, and the conditional particle conveys generality. This generality is emphasised by His saying ﴿whether male or female﴾.

As for His saying ﴿of righteous deeds﴾, some have claimed that (min) is extra (za'idah), saying that the intended meaning is "and whoever does righteous deeds." This view is not correct, because (min) is only added in a negative context or something resembling it, as Ibn Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

"And it is added after a negation or its like, causing a indefinite noun to be in the genitive, like (mā li-bāghin min mafar)."

Moreover, its presence is more complete than its absence, because (min) here serves to specify the kind of deed that is left general in His saying ﴿whoever does﴾; so (min) here is explanatory (bayaniyyah).

As for His saying ﴿of righteous deeds﴾, it means: of righteous deeds. You will find this style frequently in the Qur'an: the qualified noun is omitted and the qualifier is kept. The reverse is rare; that is, omitting the qualifier is rare while omitting the qualified noun is common, because the qualifier indicates the qualified noun, but not the reverse.

He says ﴿of righteous deeds﴾, meaning: of righteous deeds. So what are the righteous ones? The righteous deeds are those that combine two conditions. The first condition: sincerity (ikhlas). The second: following the Law of Allah, whether it is the Law of Muhammad (ﷺ) if it is from this Ummah, or a part of the law of the earlier Messengers that remains in force.

As for His saying ﴿whether male or female﴾, this (min) is an explanation of (man) in His saying ﴿and whoever does of righteous deeds, whether male or female﴾, and this is detailing after a general statement; otherwise it is well known that (man) is general, encompassing male and female.

As for His saying ﴿while being a believer﴾, the clause is a circumstantial clause (hal), a circumstance of the subject of ﴿does﴾, meaning: and the situation being that he is a believer. This is an indispensable condition, since righteous deeds do not benefit in the absence of faith; and whenever a person's faith increases, his strength in righteous deeds increases.

﴿Those will enter Paradise﴾. In another reading it is ﴿yudkhalūna﴾ (they will be made to enter). According to the reading in our Mushaf, ﴿Paradise﴾ is the direct object; according to the other reading, ﴿yudkhalūna al-jannah﴾ has ﴿al-jannah﴾ as a second object of ﴿yudkhalūna﴾, and the deputy subject occupies the position of the first object.

As for His saying ﴿those will enter Paradise﴾: may one say that this is the explicit noun used in place of the pronoun, and that it could have said "they will enter Paradise"? The answer: yes; because the demonstrative is among the apparent (explicit) nouns, not the pronouns.

If someone asks: what is the purpose of this explicit usage? We say: to show the elevated rank of these people, since He pointed to them with the demonstrative of distance, ﴿those﴾ (ulā'ika).

As for His saying ﴿will enter Paradise﴾: Paradise is the abode that Allah, the Exalted, has prepared for His righteous friends, and "therein is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4780), and Muslim (2824/2) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. I ask Allah to make me and you among its people, Amin.

As for His saying ﴿and they will not be wronged even the (smallest) speck﴾: His saying ﴿will enter﴾ and ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾ means that every person will be in the place he deserves without any deficiency. The naqir is the small pit that is on the back of a date-stone.

In the date-stone there are three things, all used as examples of very small quantity: the fatil, the naqir, and the qitmir. As for the fatil, it is the thread that runs in the groove inside the stone; as for the naqir, it is the small pit on its back; and as for the qitmir, it is what? The membrane that covers it. All of them are meant as examples.

Allah, the Exalted, said ﴿will enter Paradise and will not be wronged even the speck﴾ so that no one supposes that if a person is at a rank, he might be lowered from his rank for some reason. The matter is not so.

Let us give an example of this. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith—We will join them with their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾ [at-Tur 21]. Here "descendants" means those who follow their fathers while they are young. These follow their fathers. If the son's rank is lower than the father's rank, the son is raised to the father's rank, and the father is not lowered in exchange for the son's elevation. That is, it is not said, for example, that if the distance is twenty degrees, the father is lowered ten degrees and the son raised ten degrees. No; rather the son is raised twenty degrees and joins the father, without any deficiency to the father. So this, and Allah knows best, is the benefit in His saying ﴿and they will not be wronged even the speck﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Noble Qur'an, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, described it, is ﴿mathani﴾ (oft-repeated), meaning matters are paired within it: when the believer is mentioned, the disbeliever is mentioned; when the reward of the disbeliever is mentioned, the reward of the believer is mentioned, and so on. Reflect on this and you will find it most common in the Qur'an.

The wisdom in this is that a person travels to Allah between what? Between fear and hope; because if he recalls what Allah has prepared for the righteous, his hope prevails, and if he recalls what Allah has prepared for the disbelievers, what? his fear prevails. It is better that his fear and his hope be equal.

The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, have differed: is this always so, that a person's fear and hope should be equal in every state, or only in some states? And is it in every deed or in some deeds?

Some scholars say: if the person is ill, it is better to give precedence to hope, so that he meets his Lord thinking well of Him, following the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "None of you should die except while thinking well of his Lord"[[Narrated by Muslim (2877/82), and Ahmad (14481), with this wording, from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah.]].

Some scholars say: if he intends an evil deed, he should give precedence to fear until he refrains; and if he does a righteous deed, he should give precedence to hope that the One who enabled him to do it will accept it from him.

In any case, the scholars differ on this, so we say: every person knows his own soul. If you see that fear has overcome you until you reach despair of Allah's mercy, whether in matters of religion or matters of worldly life, then at that point correct yourself and adjust yourself. And if you see that you give precedence to hope, correct yourself also; because some sinners, when you say, "Fear Allah, brother, and desist from sin," reply, "Allah is Forgiving and Merciful," and so give precedence to hope—and this is an error. Among people there is also the opposite: if he commits even the slightest sin, he despairs and loses hope in Allah's mercy, and so gives precedence to fear.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: there is no difference between men and women in what they deserve of reward. The indication is His saying ﴿whether male or female﴾, then He mentioned the reward: ﴿those will enter Paradise﴾. However, with respect to deeds there is a difference between them, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "I have not seen anyone more deficient in intellect and religion who takes away the understanding of a prudent man than one of you"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (1462) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and Muslim (79/132) with this wording from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar.]]. Then he explained the deficiency of her religion: when she menstruates, she does not pray and does not fast. As for the reward for deeds, they are equal.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: for a deed to be accepted it must be righteous, based on His saying ﴿and whoever does of righteous deeds﴾. If there is shirk in it, it is not accepted. Why? Because the condition, which is sincerity, is lacking. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said in the Hadith Qudsi: "I am the most independent of partners from partnership; whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his partnership"[[Narrated by Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. And whoever performs an innovated deed with complete sincerity but not according to the Messenger's Law, it is not accepted from him, because it is not in accordance with the following (ittiba'). The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697), and Muslim (1718/18) with this wording, from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a righteous deed must be founded upon faith, a faith with no doubt in it, based on His saying ﴿while being a believer﴾. As for one who does righteous deeds outwardly but whose heart is not believing—may Allah protect us and you from that—his righteous deed will not benefit him; like a sincere man who seeks the pleasure of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and follows the Messenger, but is doubtful: despite his sincerity, he is doubtful, and so it is not accepted from him.

But here is a matter that must be watched for: when the heart is sincere and pure, Satan is given power over it, so that he causes it to fall either into shirk or into doubt. The more a person's faith is pure, the more Satan increases his arrows and his doubts and the like. So be on your guard, turn away from this, cease it, and seek refuge in Allah from it; for it will not harm you. For this reason we often hear someone complaining of this condition, and we say to him what the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Seek refuge in Allah"—what?—"then cease."
