"Seek refuge in Allah": this is turning to Allah regarding what you cannot do; no one can free you from Satan except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so seek refuge in Allah. "And cease": this is about what you can do; cease meaning: turn away from this, do not think about it. You are now going to pray; if someone asked you, "Why did you go to pray?" you would say, "In faith in Allah, and seeking His bounty," and you have no doubt about this.

So whatever Satan throws upon your heart, do not pay attention to it. You will easily know how to free yourself: by saying that you came to the mosque, performed ablution, and abstained from food, drink and intercourse while fasting only as a believer in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, believing in His reward and fearing His punishment. By such matters a person can be helped to drive away these whisperings; otherwise, if a person lets himself drift with them, they may destroy him.

But—praise be to Allah—the Messenger (ﷺ) has given us this effective remedy: "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan," then I cease, and I look at the work I am engaged in; I attend to my work: if it is worship, then it is worship; if it is a worldly matter, then it is a worldly matter. The main thing is that I ignore that thing and do not drift with it; for if you drift with it you will be ruined, even though it is a whisper with no reality. For this reason the verse came: ﴿while being a believer﴾. So settle yourself upon faith, and let there be in your heart nothing of shirk; for simply put, you tell yourself: why did I perform ablution? Why did I pray? Why did I fast? Why did I give charity? And the like.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the elevated rank of those characterized by this quality, namely righteous deeds together with faith, is derived from His saying ﴿those will enter Paradise﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is permissible for us to testify that everyone who does righteous deeds while being a believer is in Paradise, because this is a report from Allah, and Allah, the Exalted, does not break His promise.

If someone says: Do we testify for each individual by name? The answer: No; because there is a difference between generality and specificity, and between absolute and restricted statements. So we do not testify for anyone by name except one for whom the Messenger (ﷺ) or Allah has testified; then we believe this and say: so-and-so is in Paradise. For example, the wives of the Messenger, peace be upon him: do we testify that they are in Paradise? Yes, because they are his wives in the Hereafter, and they will be with him. So we testify to Paradise for them. Likewise the Ten (promised Paradise), Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, Bilal, 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, and others: whoever the Messenger testified for by name, we testify for by name; and when he has not testified for someone by name, we testify for him in a general way.

The same applies to disbelief: we say, "Whoever slaughters to other than Allah is a disbeliever and a polytheist." But do you testify that every person who slaughters to other than Allah is a polytheist? No; because he may be acting out of ignorance, or through interpretation, or the like. So there is a difference between specifying and generalizing, and between absolute and restricted statements. Few people grasp this matter: they take general statements and apply them to every individual, and this is not correct. The one whom we have judged to be a believer according to outward appearance may be among the people of the Fire; for the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A man may do the deeds of the people of Paradise in what appears to people, while he is in fact one of the people of the Fire"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2898), and Muslim (112/179) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd.]].

Likewise the reverse: a man may do what would make him a disbeliever, yet he does not know it, while he claims to be Muslim, prays, pays zakat, fasts and performs Hajj, but he has a trait of shirk of which he is unaware. We do not say that he is one of the people of the Fire; rather we say: whoever does this is one of the people of the Fire, but this particular man, no—because of the possibility, as I mentioned, of ignorance or interpretation.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the negation of injustice, ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾. Who could possibly be wronged? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He could be wronged in terms of divine decree (qadar), but in terms of the Law and wisdom it is impossible. So His saying ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾: injustice is negated of whom? Of Allah, in whose hand is the recompense. Is this negation a negation of something impossible, or a negation of something possible?

* A student: The second.

* The Shaykh: The second; for if it were of something impossible, it would not be a perfection, since the negation of the impossible is not a perfection. Rather it is something possible, but because of the perfection of Allah's justice it is, in fact, not possible. Accordingly it is possible in terms of decree: had Allah willed, He could have punished one who does not deserve punishment; but according to Allah's wisdom and mercy it is not possible.

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.﴾ (125) ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever, of all things, Encompassing.﴾ (126) ﴿And they ask you concerning women. Say, "Allah gives you a decision concerning them and [also] what is recited to you in the Book concerning orphan girls to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them and whom you desire to marry, and [concerning] the oppressed among children and that you should maintain justice for orphans. And whatever good you do – indeed, Allah is ever Knowing of it."﴾ [An-Nisa 125–127].

* **Shaykh:** It is better to stop here, at ﴿and you desire to marry them﴾.

* **Student:** ﴿and you desire to marry them, and [concerning] the oppressed among children, and that you should maintain justice for orphans. And whatever good you do – indeed, Allah is ever Knowing of it.﴾ (127) [An-Nisa 125–127].

* **Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. The Blessed and Exalted Allah said: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.﴾ Here "man" (مَن) is an interrogative particle, and what is meant by it is negation. We have said several times that negation expressed in the form of a question is more emphatic than explicit negation, because when it comes in the form of a question it takes on the sense of a challenge. It is as if the speaker is saying: "Bring me someone better than this; bring me someone more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah," and similar expressions.

His saying ﴿dīnan﴾ (religion) here is in the accusative as a *tamyīz* (specification), because it came after the *ism al-tafḍīl* (comparative/superlative form).

If someone asks: "It specifies what?" We say: it specifies the word ﴿aḥsanu﴾ (better), because ﴿aḥsanu﴾ is ambiguous; we do not know what it is being attached to. So when an accusative noun follows it, it specifies it and clarifies it. "Dīn" here means "deed" (ʿamal). We say this because *dīn* is used in the sense of "recompense," as in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Master of the Day of Recompense﴾ [Al-Fatihah 4], and in the sense of "deed," as in this verse, and as in His words: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾ [Al-Kafirun 6], and as in His words: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 3].

So ﴿dīnan﴾ means "deed." The deed which its doer seeks to be repaid for is called *dīn*.

﴿Min man aslama wajhahu lillāh﴾: ﴿aslama﴾ (submitted) here means *ikhlāṣ* (sincerity), i.e., he entrusted his affair to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This means sincerity of intention.

﴿wa huwa muḥsin﴾ is a circumstantial clause (*jumlah ḥāliyyah*) referring back to "man" in His words ﴿min man aslama﴾. *Iḥsān* here means conformity to the Sharia. So in this verse there is evidence for the two conditions of worship, which are: sincerity (*ikhlāṣ*) and following the Prophet's way (*mutābaʿah*). Sincerity is in His words ﴿min man aslama wajhahu lillāh﴾, and following is in His words ﴿wa huwa muḥsin﴾, because the goodness of a deed is its conformity to the Sharia.

﴿wa ittaba'a millata Ibrāhīma ḥanīfā﴾: this is a clause conjoined to what came before for the sake of *tawkīd maʿnawī* (emphasis of meaning), because the religion (*millah*) of Abraham, peace be upon him, is sincerity and upholding the Sharia. So this clause is as though it emphasizes what came before and includes it.

His saying ﴿Ibrāhīm﴾ refers to the father of the prophets, because the prophets after him were from his offspring. It has two readings: ﴿Ibrāhīm﴾ and ﴿Ibrāhām﴾, i.e., replacing the *yā'* with an *alif*. When the *yā'* is replaced by an *alif*, the *hā'* must be pronounced with a *fatḥah*.

His saying ﴿ḥanīfā﴾ may be a circumstantial accusative (*ḥāl*) of the subject of ﴿ittaba'a﴾, or a circumstantial accusative of ﴿Ibrāhīm﴾. Have you understood? Which of them is more likely? The second is more likely, because of the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Then We revealed to you, "Follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah"﴾ [An-Nahl 123]. It is well known that if Abraham was *ḥanīf* and we were commanded to follow his religion, then we will be *ḥunafāʾ* (those who incline toward truth).

﴿wa ittakhadha Allāhu Ibrāhīma khalīlā﴾: the *wāw* here is *istiʾnāfiyyah* (resumptive), not conjunctive. It is as though the Mighty and Majestic resumed in order to explain the rank of Abraham, whom we were commanded to follow, because Allah took him as a *khalīl*. The *khalīl* is one who has pure love, and he was named so because love encompassed his entire body until it penetrated his veins. On this, a poet says:

*You have permeated the passage of the spirit within me,*
*and by this was the one who is khalīl named "khalīl."*

* In this verse there are benefits. First: encouragement to sincerity, by His words ﴿min man aslama wajhahu lillāh﴾.
* Among them: encouragement to following (the Prophet's way), by His words ﴿wa huwa muḥsin﴾.

* Among its benefits: no one is better in religion than one described in this manner. Accordingly, if the Christians say that they are better in religion than the Muslims, what do we say? We say: this is a lie, because they lack both sincerity and following. The Christians are known to hold the doctrine of the Trinity, and they also have not followed the Sharia of Allah, since they disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ) and his family.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the excellence of Abraham, peace be upon him, since we were commanded to follow him. This means he is an imam; for this reason, scholars call him by the title: "Imam of the ḥunafāʾ."

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah took Abraham as a *khalīl*, and this is a great virtue for him. Did He take anyone else? Yes, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, Allah has taken me as a *khalīl*, just as He took Abraham as a *khalīl*."[[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra (1058) from the hadith of Jundub, and Ibn Majah (141) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr.]]

* Among its benefits: an indication that *khullah* (intimate friendship) is a higher rank than *maḥabbah* (love), because it is specific to Abraham and Muhammad (ﷺ). If it were of the same meaning or the same rank as love, it would be established for all who deserve love. It is well known that it is not correct to say that Allah took the believers as *akhillā'* (intimate friends), because *khullah* is exclusive. From this we know the error of one who says: "Abraham the *Khalīl* and Muhammad the *Ḥabīb* (Beloved)," because this is a belittling of the Messenger (ﷺ), since it lowers his rank from *khullah* to *maḥabbah*, which is shared even by the believer who is pious, just, and patient.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the actions of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by His words ﴿wa ittakhadha Allāhu Ibrāhīma khalīlā﴾. *Ittikhādh* (taking) is an event that occurs after the existence of its cause. This is what the people of knowledge express as *qiyām al-ḥawādith bi-Llāh* (the occurrence of events in Allah), meaning that the Blessed and Exalted does what He wills whenever He wills. This is in contrast to those who said that voluntary actions do not subsist in Him, and that no action renews for Him, neither speech, nor creation, nor anything else. There is no doubt that this is a false doctrine, and its implication is a deficiency in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, since He would not be doing what He wills whenever He wills.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and ever is Allah, of all things, Encompassing.﴾ Glorified and Exalted is He.

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens﴾: This sentence is a declarative sentence composed of a subject and predicate, in which the predicate has been placed first for the purpose of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens﴾, and no one contests Him in that, ﴿Say, "Call upon those you claim besides Allah. They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, nor do they have therein any partnership, nor is there for Him from among them any helper." And intercession will not benefit with Him except for one whom He permits﴾ [Saba' 22-23]. So to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.

Here He said ﴿whatever (mā) is in the heavens﴾ and did not say ﴿whoever (man) is in the heavens﴾. Some of them said: this is by way of giving precedence to non-rational beings, because (man) in the Arabic language is used for rational beings, i.e., those possessing intellect, and (mā) for non-rational beings, and non-rational creatures are more numerous than rational ones. It is also possible that He used (mā) to encompass those persons and attributes, because the specification of (man) for rational beings and (mā) for non-rational beings applies only to entities; but (mā) is used for entities and attributes. Do you not see His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So marry what seems good to you of women﴾ [An-Nisa' 3], where He said ﴿mā﴾, and it is known that women are rational beings, but since the one married is not married for her own essence, rather she is married for the attributes that subsist in her, and attributes are meanings and not intellects, He said ﴿what seems good to you of women﴾. And this view is more preferable than the first view; I mean, that ﴿whatever is in the heavens﴾ used (mā) rather than (man) in order to encompass what? The persons and the attributes.

﴿whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾: In some verses He says ﴿whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al-Hadid 1], and the apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that this is from the variation of context and styles, because the meaning does not differ; since the conjoined has the same ruling as the conjoined-to. So if He says ﴿whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, it is as if He said ﴿whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth﴾. Variation in context occurs much in the Qur'an, as one perceives when reciting the stories that appear in the Qur'an for several messengers, finding much variation in expression.

﴿and whatever is on the earth and ever is Allah, of all things, Encompassing﴾: Allah was encompassing of all things. Here (kāna) is stripped of the indication of time, because if it retained indication of time, Allah's encompassing of all things would be a past, bygone encompassing, whereas He has not ceased and does not cease to be encompassing of all things. Rather, it comes in such a context to establish the ruling, so this is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa' 152]; the meaning is not that forgiveness and mercy are renewed for Him. ﴿And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise﴾ [An-Nisa' 92]; knowledge and wisdom are not renewed for Him, nor is it something past that has ceased. Rather, what is this for? To emphasize His being characterized by this attribute.

As for His saying ﴿Encompassing of all things﴾: what kind of encompassing? All things, encompassed by Him in knowledge, power, hearing, sight, management, and other meanings of His lordship, exalted is He.

From this noble verse: the generality of Allah's dominion. Is it derived?

* A student: The supposition of the verb.

* The Shaykh: No, from the relative (mā), because all relative nouns convey generality.

* And from it: the exclusivity of the dominion of whatever is in the heavens and the earth to Allah, exalted is He. It is derived from the fronting of the predicate, because fronting what should be delayed conveys what? It conveys restriction.

* And among the benefits of this verse: that the heavens are of a number. From where is this derived?

* A student: The heavens is plural.

* The Shaykh: From ﴿the heavens﴾, which is plural. So what is this number? This has been explained in the Qur'an and the Sunnah. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Say, "Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Great Throne?"﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 86], and ﴿And We built above you seven strong [heavens]﴾ [An-Naba' 12]. Likewise the Sunnah came, and the people agreed upon that.

* And among the benefits of this verse: that the earth is one, from His saying ﴿and whatever is on the earth﴾, and He did not say ﴿and whatever is on the earths﴾; so the earth is one. Do you understand?

* A student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: Yes, this is the apparent wording, but this apparent meaning has been explained in several places that the intended singular here is the genus, not unity, i.e., the genus of earth. The Sunnah has explicitly come that the earths are seven, and the Qur'an has apparently come that the earths are seven. In the Sunnah: "Whoever unjustly takes a span of land, it will be placed around his neck from seven earths on the Day of Resurrection" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2452), and Muslim (1610/137), from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Zayd]. And in the Qur'an, apparently: ﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾ [At-Talaq 12]. So the likeness here may be in attribute, and it may be in number. The first possibility is impossible because of the evident difference between the heavens and the earth, so the second possibility remains, namely likeness in number.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the encompassing of Allah, exalted is He, of all things; from His saying ﴿and ever is Allah, of all things, Encompassing﴾.

From this benefit follows an important behavioral benefit: when you know Allah's encompassing of all things, you fear Him, have awe of Him, and watch over yourself, because wherever you are, Allah encompasses you. When you believe this, you fear the Lord of the worlds who encompasses all things.

Does fear of Allah in the heart follow from this? Yes, because Allah is encompassing; even what is in your heart, He encompasses it, exalted is He.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 127 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Exalted said: ﴿They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say: "Allah gives you a ruling concerning them."﴾ ﴿They ask you for a ruling (yastaftunaka)﴾: they ask you to issue a fatwa (iftaʾ). Iftaʾ (issuing a fatwa, i.e., giving a religious ruling) is informing about a legal ruling. This is iftaʾ, and it is a clarification of the ruling, not an obligation to comply with it. By this, a distinction is made between qadaʾ (judicial judgment) and iftaʾ. Qadaʾ is the clarification of the legal ruling together with the enforcement of it, because the judge says to the two litigants: "The truth is with you, O so-and-so," and this is a clarification of the truth, "so give it to your opponent." What is this? This is enforcement. The mufti cannot enforce even if he issues a fatwa. But must one be bound by what he issues? There is detail on this. The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: If the one seeking a fatwa asks a scholar in whose words he is confident, believing that his words are true, then he is obligated to act upon it and not to seek another's opinion, because Allah said: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl 43]. The benefit of asking them is to act upon what they say; otherwise that would be pointless. Yes. If you asked a scholar in a village, and in your view no one is more knowledgeable than him, and your intention is that when you reach the city where scholars are abundant you will ask, then in this case you are bound by this scholar's fatwa with a restricted or temporary commitment, and you may ask again when you reach the abundant sources.

﴿They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say: "Allah gives you a ruling concerning them."﴾ [al-Nisa 127] Allahu akbar. The one asked is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the one who gives the ruling is Allah, because what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rules is what Allah the Mighty and Majestic rules. ﴿Say: "Allah gives you a ruling concerning them."﴾ Allah the Mighty and Majestic did not specify on what matter the asking falls. Is the intended meaning ﴿concerning women﴾ regarding their marriage, regarding enabling them to buy and sell, or regarding anything at all? But the verse was revealed for a known cause: it was problematic for a man who had an orphaned girl under his guardianship, perhaps from his paternal uncle or the like, that he would wrong her and withhold her (from marriage) for himself or for his son or the like, thus wronging her. This matter became difficult for them, so they asked the Messenger (ﷺ) what they should do, and Allah gave them a ruling: ﴿Say: "Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and what is recited to you in the Book"﴾. That is, Allah gives you a ruling concerning them; that is, the Quran gives a ruling, because it is the speech of whom? The speech of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. The conjunction "wa" here is coordinating, but it is not a coordination of difference, because the Book is the means by which we reach knowledge of Allah's ruling, since Allah does not speak and rule in the manner of a direct voice, but He speaks through the Quran, and the ruling is contained in it. So the coordination here is not complete difference, because what is in the Book is the document that guides us to Allah's ruling, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And what is recited to you in the Book﴾: the intended meaning of "the Book" here is the Quran, and the "al" in it is for mental (already known) reference. ﴿Concerning the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them while you desire to marry them﴾ [al-Nisa 127]. The orphan girl under his guardianship, he does not give her what has been prescribed for her, he does not give her what is due to her. A suitable suitor comes, meaning one who should be given (her), but he holds power over her, so he does not give them what has been prescribed for them, withholding out of self-interest, because he desires to marry her. Here He said: ﴿while you desire to marry them﴾. So which of the two particles should we assume: fi (in) or ʿan (from)?
* Students: (fi).
* The Shaykh: Do you desire to marry them, or to refrain from marrying them?
* Students: (fi).
* The Shaykh: We say: the verse is open to both meanings, and this is from the eloquence and conciseness of the Quran, because one may be averse to her and not want her, yet not want her to belong to someone else; and one may be desirous of her and not want her to belong to someone else. So the verse includes both matters together.

﴿And the oppressed among the children﴾ [al-Nisa 127]. That is: and Allah gives you a ruling, ﴿and what is recited to you in the Book﴾ [al-Nisa 127] concerning the oppressed among the children: what is their condition and their affair? Is one sinful for not emigrating, for example? Is it permissible to wrong them? Everything related to their affairs, Allah has ruled on and clarified.

He said: ﴿And that you stand up for orphans with justice﴾ [al-Nisa 127]. In this verse, the apparent estimate is: and He obligated upon you that you stand up for orphans with justice. Yatama (orphans) is the plural of yatim, who is one whose father died before he reached maturity. That is, before the maturity of the father or of the child? 
* Students: The child.
* The Shaykh: What about the father?
* Students: The child.
* The Shaykh: Why would it not be the father?
* Students: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, the child's arrival at maturity indicates that he has reached it, necessarily. So the scholars' statement, "he is one whose father died before he reached maturity," undoubtedly has the pronoun referring to the child.

﴿And that you stand up for orphans with justice﴾: qist is justice. From qasata, yaqsitu, qasṭan, and the noun is qisṭ, and what is meant by it is justice. As for iqsat, what is meant by it is injustice, oppression. Therefore, if it is from the triliteral form it has one meaning, and if it is from the quadriliteral form it has another meaning: aqsata means he acted unjustly, and qasata means he acted justly. Yes, we erred: aqsata means he acted justly, and qasata means he acted unjustly. For this reason Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly﴾ [al-Ma'idah 42], and He said: ﴿And as for the unjust, they will be fuel for Hell﴾ [al-Jinn 15]. ﴿And that you stand up for orphans with justice﴾, that is, with justice, with justice in everything, even in your dealings with them regarding food, because the Companions were scrupulous about mixing with orphans in food, so Allah permitted them that. Do you understand? So this applies to every matter concerning orphans. ﴿And whatever good you do, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of it﴾. Is "mā" here conditional or relative?
* A student: Conditional.
* The Shaykh: Conditional, as evidenced by its response being joined with the fa.

His saying: ﴿And whatever you do﴾, that is, ﴿of good﴾, includes any good, whether it is transitive or intransitive, and whether it is good in wealth, knowledge, body, or any other good. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing of it﴾: this is the response clause, and it is joined with fa because the clause is nominal, and whenever the response of the conditional is a nominal clause it must be joined with fa; but it may occasionally be omitted, following the saying of the poet:
Whoever does good deeds, Allah will reward them ∗∗∗ ........................
The original is: then Allah will reward them. If someone says that the fa was dropped here out of necessity of meter, we say: there is no necessity, because if the line had been said as (man yafʿali al-hasanāt fa-llāhu yashkuruhā), with the ta' made sukūn, there would have been no necessity. In any case, the fa may be omitted in the response of a conditional, but that is rare.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing of it﴾: Knowing when it is done, or before it is done?
* Students: Both are possible, O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: Before and after, because Allah's knowledge precedes the known, unlike creatures' knowledge, which is concurrent with the created. Good. If we say that it includes knowledge, then what is the answer to the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those who strive among you and the patient﴾ [Muhammad 31]? ﴿Until We know﴾, because "ḥattā" here is for causation. ﴿And We will surely test you﴾ means: We will test you, so that We may know the patient. What is the answer?
* A student: The knowledge of Allah is of two kinds (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, Allah's knowledge is of two kinds: knowledge that precedes the act, and knowledge that follows. So the meaning is: until We know with a knowledge by which the thing becomes manifest, so We know it after its occurrence. This is one aspect. Another aspect is that the intended meaning is the knowledge upon which reward is based, and for this He said: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know﴾, and the knowledge upon which reward is based is only after the act, is it not? This aspect is clearer and more preponderant, and every person understands it: that we say Allah's knowledge is of two kinds: knowledge that a thing will occur, which is prior, and knowledge that it has occurred, which is what the reward is based upon.

His saying: ﴿And whatever good you do, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of it﴾. He did not say: "indeed Allah will reward you," as one would expect. It is said that mentioning knowledge has a benefit, which is that He does not waste for you any good whatsoever, because Allah's knowledge encompasses it, so this known matter is established for you. And it is known from many other verses that Allah the Most High says: ﴿Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah 7-8].
* A student: May Allah bless you. You said that the one who seeks a fatwa is bound to act on it once the heart is satisfied with the scholar. But many people are not reassured by the people of righteousness, especially in the lands of the grave-worshippers, and their hearts are reassured by the people of innovation and desires. Are these not bound by the fatwa of the people of righteousness?
* The Shaykh: These, may Allah bless you, sought fatwas from ignoramuses, and our discussion concerns one who sought a scholar. As for one who sought an ignoramus, these disbelievers say: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion﴾ [al-Zukhruf 22], and they do not accept the truth. I think we said: whoever seeks a scholar (...), or not?
* Students: Yes.
* A student: The saying of Allah: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ [Al 'Imran 109]. Shaykh, some astronomers and scholars divided the heavens into categories and placed locations without evidence... 
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: They placed locations without evidence. For example, he says the atmosphere is in the first heaven, the sun in the second, the moon the third, and so on. Should this be refuted, and do they say it is disbelief and baseless claim?
* The Shaykh: There is no doubt. And these layers they speak of are all subject to the earth, but they certainly differ according to their nearness to the earth and their distance from it.
* A student: The saying of Allah, the Majestic and Exalted: ﴿And who is better in religion﴾ [al-Nisa 125], one who submits, meaning sincerity to Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, ﴿while he is a doer of good﴾. We said, O Shaykh, by following. Would the implication of the noble verse not be that whoever does not submit his face to Allah or does not follow the Prophet (ﷺ) in following him is not one who is better in religion, O Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: The discussion here is that the Muslims combined sincerity and following, and following may be complete or incomplete, so the goodness belonging to the follower is according to his following.
* A student: May Allah be good to you, O Shaykh: in His saying, ﴿And that you stand up for orphans﴾, is the waw conjunctive?
* The Shaykh: No, the apparent reading is that it is coordinated with something implied, meaning: and He commanded you that you stand up for orphans with justice.
* A student: May Allah be good to you. In explaining His saying, ﴿with justice﴾, we said qist is justice, from qasata yaqsitu, and finally we said: from (aqsata)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, not from (aqsata yuqsitu); that is the correct one.
* A student: May Allah be good to you. If someone says to us: is not preference between the superior and the inferior...?
* The Shaykh: Is not what?
* The student: The comparative (ahsan) between the superior and the inferior...
* The Shaykh: Is not what?
* The student: The comparative verb (ahsan) between the superior and the inferior. So if someone says to us: from this verse we understand that the one who has not submitted his face to Allah, while being a doer of good, they say: there is also virtue in it.
* The Shaykh: There is good in it.
* The student: There is good in it. Is this correct, O Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: Does this necessarily follow? Does not Allah say: ﴿The companions of Paradise on that Day are better in resting place and finer in resting place﴾ [al-Furqan 24], and where is the goodness in the abode of the people of the Fire?
* The student: There is no good in it.
* The Shaykh: More emphatic than this is: ﴿Is Allah better, or what they associate?﴾ [al-Naml 59], where He used the comparative and then sought equivalence.
* A student: The saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And We will surely test you﴾. Shaykh, does the disbeliever get tested with good and the believer with evil?
* The Shaykh: No, rather even the believer is tested with good and tested with evil. Allah the Most High said: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial﴾ [al-Anbiya 35].
* The student: I say: I want to explain the tafsir according to this...
* The Shaykh: Which of them? Testing with good, as Solomon said: ﴿This is from the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful﴾ [al-Naml 40]. And testing with evil is that Allah tests a person with evil to know whether he will be patient or not.
* A student: Shaykh, the hadith of Sa'id: "Whoever takes a span of land unjustly, Allah will encircle him with it from seven earths" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3198), and Muslim (1610/137), with his wording, from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl.]]. I say: someone may say there is an unclear indication, because seven earths here, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "seven earths," to magnify the warner? Vocalize the dhal?
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: To magnify the warner?
* The Shaykh: To magnify what?
* Student: The warner.
* The Shaykh: Yes, the original is the opposite.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say: "Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them while you desire to marry them, and the oppressed among the children, and that you stand up for orphans with justice. And whatever good you do, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of it."﴾ [al-Nisa 127].
* The Shaykh: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say: "Allah gives you a ruling concerning them"﴾. What is istiftaʾ?
* Student: Istiftaʾ?
* The Shaykh: What is istiftaʾ?
* Student: It is seeking a fatwa.
* The Shaykh: Seeking a fatwa. And what is fatwa?
* The student: Informing about a ruling...
* The Shaykh: Legal, without? Without enforcing it, because enforcement belongs to the judiciary. Is it valid to say that we inform about Allah as a mufti?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Yes. The evidence?
* The student: ﴿Say: Allah gives you a ruling﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning them﴾, and likewise ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalālah﴾ [al-Nisa 176].

His saying: ﴿And what is recited to you in the Book﴾: is "mā" coordinated with what? With the divine name (Allah), or is it a sentence?
* The student: With the divine name.
* The Shaykh: With the divine name. Does anyone have agreement or disagreement on this? ﴿Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning them and what is recited to you in the Book﴾? The answer: it is a sentence coordinated with the first sentence, so ﴿what is recited to you﴾ ("mā") is a subject, and its predicate is omitted, its estimate being: and what is recited to you in the Book gives you a ruling concerning them. It cannot be coordinated with the divine name, because the first sentence was already complete, ﴿Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning them﴾, so what follows it is a sentence coordinated with a sentence. Do you understand?

His saying: ﴿Concerning the orphan women﴾: this idafah (construction) is of the type of idafah...
* Student: idafah...
* The Shaykh: ﴿Concerning the orphan women﴾.
* The student: Idafat bayan (explanatory construction).
* The Shaykh: Yes?
* The student: Idafat bayan.
* The Shaykh: Explanatory idafah?!
* The student: As it is itself.
* The Shaykh: Yes, but of the type of idafah what?
* The student: That is, the explanatory idafah, called idafat al-bayan.
* The Shaykh: Is it the idafah of a thing to its part, or to its whole, or to what is separate from it?
* The student: No, to itself.
* The Shaykh: To itself? Then how can it be to itself?
* The student: Yatama are the women...
* The Shaykh: It is the idafah of an attribute to the thing described.

What is meant by His saying: ﴿those to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them﴾?
* Student: The dower (mahr).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 127 (part 2 of 2):

* The Shaykh: Yes. Some of them would deprive the orphan girl under their guardianship, so they would not give her what had been prescribed for her.
The Shaykh: His saying, ﴿وَتَرْغَبُونَ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾ ("and you desire to marry them"). What is the omitted particle that we should supply?
* A student: It may be (عن) ("about/from") and it may be (في) ("in").
* The Shaykh: Yes. Does the meaning differ?
* The student: If it is (عن), then it means he does not want to marry her, but he takes her either out of envy or out of jealousy.
* The Shaykh: Good.
* The student: And if it is (في), then he wants her for himself, but he deprives her of her right of the dowry.
* The Shaykh: So he does not give her the obligatory dowry. Correct.
The Shaykh: His saying, ﴿وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الْوِلْدَانِ﴾ ("and the oppressed among the children"). It is coordinated with what?
* A student: ﴿وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الْوِلْدَانِ﴾ is coordinated with ﴿يُفْتِيكُمْ﴾: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ وَمَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾. That is, "and the oppressed among the children" is coordinated with "the women."
* The Shaykh: Does the meaning hold? ﴿فِي يَتَامَى النِّسَاءِ﴾ ("concerning the orphan women") ﴿وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الْوِلْدَانِ﴾?
* The student: It may be an object, with the verb omitted.
* The Shaykh: Who knows?
* A student: ﴿فِي يَتَامَى النِّسَاءِ﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿فِي يَتَامَى النِّسَاءِ﴾. And what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women, and what is recited to you in the Book concerning the oppressed among the children. Yes. It is permissible, but it is a remote possibility that it is coordinated with the pronoun in His saying ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾, meaning: and concerning the oppressed among the children.
The Shaykh: His saying, ﴿وَأَنْ تَقُومُوا لِلْيَتَامَى بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ ("and that you stand firm for orphans with justice"). It is coordinated with what?
* A student: It is coordinated with ﴿يُفْتِيكُمْ﴾.
* The Shaykh: "He gives you a ruling (that you...)"?
* The student: It is coordinated with an omitted verb; it obligates you...
* The Shaykh: That is, (أنْ) is a verbal-masdar particle, and its governing verb is omitted, meaning: "and He commands you that you stand firm for orphans with justice." So this is coordination of one clause with another.
﴿وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِهِ عَلِيمًا﴾ ("And whatever good you do, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of it"). Why did the fa' (فَ) occur in the predicate of the subject in ﴿وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِهِ عَلِيمًا﴾?
* A student: We said it is conditional.
* The Shaykh: On the basis that (ما) is conditional. And if we make it relative?
* The student: It is deleted..
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: The fa' is deleted.
* The Shaykh: No, it cannot be deleted; this is the Qur'an. If we make it relative, how did the fa' occur in the predicate of the subject?
* The student: A relative noun resembling (...).
* The Shaykh: The relative noun resembles the conditional noun in generality, so it is given its ruling in some respects, though not in every respect, so its predicate is linked with the fa'.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the eagerness of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, to know the legal rulings, as shown by His saying ﴿يَسْتَفْتُونَكَ﴾. But we must know that the Companions' asking the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a ruling was a request in order to act upon it and implement it. Therefore, when they knew the rulings, they acted upon them. This contrasts with some people today who ask for a fatwa in order to see what the scholar has, and then, if they wish, act upon it, and if they wish, ask another scholar. The latter is considered toying with the religion of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; for when you ask a scholar, you have made him the intermediary between you and Allah, and you have made what he gives you as a fatwa the path to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So if it permits what you want, you follow it, and otherwise you seek another. This is one who follows his own desire. Therefore the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: "Whoever pursues the concessions becomes a sinner."
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Companions' concern with the affairs of women, and indeed Allah's concern with them is even greater, as shown by His saying ﴿وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ فِي النِّسَاءِ قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ﴾. The one asking is the Companions, the one giving the fatwa is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the intermediary between the one giving the fatwa and the one asking is who? The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. This shows the concern of the Shari'ah with women. Based on this, we know that every ruling the Shari'ah has legislated concerning women is for their benefit, even if foolish and ignorant people think it is a diminishing of their rights and an injustice; they are mistaken.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: returning to what is in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that what is in the Book of fatwa is issued from Allah, as shown by His saying ﴿وَمَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾. And this is so, because the Book is ordained by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; He is the One who spoke it and sent it down upon Muhammad ﷺ and commanded him to convey it to the people. And He Himself, blessed and exalted, undertook to explain it: ﴿فَإِذَا قَرَأْنَاهُ فَاتَّبِعْ قُرْآنَهُ (١٨) ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا بَيَانَهُ﴾ [al-Qiyamah 18, 19].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the care for orphan women. First, care for women in general, and then this more specific care for orphan women, because the orphan woman combines two weaknesses: weakness due to her sex, since the female sex is weaker than men, and weakness due to the loss of a supporter, who is who?
* Students: The father.
* The Shaykh: The father. Therefore Allah enjoined care for her.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the tyranny of the people of ignorance, in that they unleashed the full force of their oppression upon these orphan women, so that they do not give them what was prescribed for them, and they also control them and their destiny, as shown by His saying ﴿اللَّاتِي لَا تُؤْتُونَهُنَّ مَا كُتِبَ لَهُنَّ وَتَرْغَبُونَ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾.
* Also among the benefits of this noble verse: that a woman's dowry is obligatory for her, as shown by His saying ﴿مَا كُتِبَ لَهُنَّ﴾. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿وَآتُوا النِّسَاءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ﴾ [an-Nisa' 4]. Accordingly, the owner of the dowry is the woman, not her guardian, even if he is her father. The dowry belongs to her; its amount is set and its type specified, and she may waive it if she is sensible and mature.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is permissible for a person to marry his ward (mawliyyatahu), because these orphans are under the guardianship of those who desire to marry them, and he has the most right to marry her. If he wishes to marry her, do we say that it is not permissible because he is a guardian dealing with himself on his own behalf, just as an agent may not buy from his own property for his principal, or from his principal's property for himself? The answer is no. That is, it is permissible for the guardian of an orphan girl, if she is lawfully permitted to him, to marry her. But he must fear Allah and not wrong her or diminish her rights. But how is the marriage contracted if he is himself the guardian? He brings two witnesses and says: "I call you to witness that I have married myself to the daughter of my paternal uncle by legal guardianship." He says, "I accept." Or does he not need to?
He does not need to say, "and I accept," because this offer already includes acceptance. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Safiyyah: «I have freed you and made your freedom your dowry»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (371), and Muslim (1365 / 84), from Anas, with the wording: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ freed Safiyyah and made her freedom her dowry.]], and he did not require an offer or acceptance, because the meaning is understood.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: care for the oppressed among children. The oppressed child, whether because of his youth, illness, insanity, or any other cause that makes him weak, care for him is undoubtedly a sign of a person's mercy. The Prophet ﷺ said: «Show mercy to those on earth, and He who is in heaven will show mercy to you»[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4941), and al-Tirmidhi (1924), and the wording is his, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr.]], and he said: «Those who show mercy, the Merciful will show mercy to them»[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4941), and al-Tirmidhi (1924), and the wording is his, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr.]]. For this reason, one of the greatest causes of obtaining mercy in the heart is compassion for the young, playing with them, and bringing joy to them. A person finds tenderness and mercy in his heart. If he remained studying volumes to bring mercy into his heart, it would not be achieved for him.
Look at the Messenger's ﷺ treatment of children. Once, «Al-Hasan climbed on his back while he was prostrating in prayer with the people, and he lengthened his prostration. After he finished, he informed the people that his son had made him a mount, and that he wished to fulfill his need»[[Narrated by al-Nasa'i (1141) from Shaddad ibn al-Had.]]. "Made him a mount" means he made him a riding animal, since he saw him prostrating in a receptive state, and the child is a child; he rode on him and made him a mount for himself. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, approved of this. Yet if one of the imams of people today had his son climb on him, he would shake him off violently and not set him down gently, may Allah grant us well-being. This is an error.
Likewise, «Umamah bint Zaynab was crying, so the Prophet ﷺ went out with her to the mosque and began carrying her during the prayer»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (516), and Muslim (543 / 41), from Abu Qatadah al-Ansari.]]. «When al-Hasan and al-Husayn came out wearing garments that tripped them, he came down from the minbar and carried them before him»[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (1109), al-Tirmidhi (3774), al-Nasa'i (1413), and Ibn Majah (3600), from Buraydah al-Aslami.]]. Examples of this are many. He would say: «O Abu 'Umayr, what did the little sparrow do?»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6129), and Muslim (2150 / 30), from Anas.]] He would joke with him and bring joy to him. If we walked in these manners, much good would result from it. O Allah, guide us.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation to stand firm for orphans with justice. This is a general command, obligating every person to stand firm for Allah as a witness with justice. But orphans have a particular matter: one must be just toward them, because the orphan has no one to defend him, and his guardian may consume his property without his noticing. For this reason I counsel regarding them.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that whatever good we do, whether small or great, Allah knows it. A consequence of this benefit is caution against neglecting what is obligatory, because if He knows the good that we do, He also knows the good that we do not do.
* And also in this noble verse: encouragement to do good, because when you know that Allah knows it and that He will reward you for it, you become active, your resolve strengthens, and you act.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 128 (part 2 of 3):

* Student: Three hundred.
* The Shaykh: No, no, a hundred and fifty. Because there is a second wife, and if a third came, it would be reduced. In any case, if she agrees to waive her right to the turn (qasm) in exchange for something, there is no harm. As for the saying of some scholars that it is not valid in exchange for something, because consideration (iwad) must be something of property, this is not correct. For Allah stated it absolutely, saying: ﴿that the two of them make a settlement, a settlement﴾, and this is the purpose of the indefiniteness in His words ﴿a settlement (sulhan)﴾, because the meaning of "a settlement" is any settlement whatsoever. This is from the eloquence of the Quran: ﴿that they make a settlement﴾, ﴿a settlement﴾, meaning any settlement at all. If He had said, "that they make a settlement between them," one might say that there must be restrictions and conditions. But when He said ﴿a settlement﴾, it became general: whatever the two agree upon, there is no harm.
Is it permissible if they agree that she gets one day and the other gets two days? It is valid. So there is no restriction in this, except for one thing, which is what came in the hadith from the Prophet ﷺ: "Reconciliation is permissible among the Muslims, except a reconciliation that makes lawful what is unlawful or makes unlawful what is lawful" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (3594) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. That is, for example, if he said to her, God forbid, "Choose: either I have anal intercourse with you, or I divorce you," and she said, "There is no objection." Is this settlement permissible?
* Student: No.
* The Shaykh: Why?
* Student: Because it is forbidden.
* The Shaykh: Because it makes lawful what is unlawful. So if it entails making lawful what is unlawful, it is not permissible.
If they agree that he divorces his other wife?
* Student: It is not permissible.
* The Shaykh: She said, "There is no harm, but divorce the other one." It is not permissible, because it makes lawful what is unlawful, since in this there is aggression and injustice. Thus the settlement that does not make lawful what is unlawful nor makes unlawful what is lawful is permissible absolutely, without restriction.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: this great principle from the Lord who is over all things powerful: ﴿Settlement is best﴾. Some people may think that if a person humbles himself and gives up a right, that is a diminishing of his right, and that the outcome will not be good. But Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in whose hand is the dominion of the heavens and the earth, says, what? ﴿Settlement is best﴾.
If you want an example of this, reflect on the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah between the Prophet ﷺ and the Quraysh. Apparently the settlement involved a great humiliation for whom? For the Muslims. But He in whose hand is the dominion of the heavens and the earth turned this settlement, by Allah's permission, into a good for the Muslims. Who abandoned the right to return a Muslim who came to the Muslims from the disbelievers? Who? The Quraysh, to whom it belonged; they were the ones who waived it. And who waived the condition of war between them for ten years? The Quraysh, because they broke the covenant by aiding their allies against the allies of the Prophet ﷺ. So you, my brother, do not look at matters in their present state; believe in the promise of Allah, and the end belongs to you.
Here, do we say: settlement is best in what concerns the spouses, or do we say: the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the particularity of the cause?
* Student: The second.
* The Shaykh: The second. So settlement in all circumstances is good, because through it there is generosity of soul and affection. If the dispute led to litigation, some bitterness would remain in the souls, for the one judged against would have something in his heart toward his opponent, and perhaps toward the judge as well, and perhaps toward the witnesses, so enmity would spread. But when settlement occurs, everyone yields with generosity of soul and tranquility.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an indication that settlement is heavy on the souls, but the believer finds the heaviness easier when he believes that settlement is good. It is taken from His words: ﴿and the souls are made present to stinginess﴾. By human nature, a person will not give up what he wants or overlook his right. This is human nature. But reconciliation, which is good, requires a price to be paid, which is pressing upon the soul that has been made present to stinginess until it agrees to settle.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the exhortation to good conduct and God-consciousness, by the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And if you do good and fear God﴾, and complete it.
* Student: ﴿And if you do good and fear God﴾...
* The Shaykh: Surah an-Nisa. We are now reading in Surah an-Nisa. Good, what is meant by this? ﴿If you do good and fear God, then indeed Allah is ever...﴾...
* Students: The exhortation to...
* The Shaykh: The exhortation to good conduct and God-consciousness, because Allah said: ﴿...is ever Acquainted with what you do.﴾
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the comprehensiveness of Allah's knowledge of everything, even of what we do. Is Allah's knowledge of what we do prior to our action or subsequent to it?
* Student: Prior.
* The Shaykh: Prior, there is no doubt it is prior, because Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heaven and the earth? Indeed that is in a Book. Indeed that is easy for Allah﴾ [al-Hajj 70].
If someone says: Does not Allah say: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those among you who strive and the patient﴾ [Muhammad 31], and ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet known those of you who fought and known the patient?﴾ [Ali Imran 142]?
We say: Yes, Allah said this, and the One who said this is the One who said: ﴿Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heaven and the earth? Indeed that is in a Book. Indeed that is easy for Allah.﴾ So how do we reconcile them?
We say: The sound method here is that you believe in this and in that, and do not imagine that there is a contradiction. You say: We believe that Allah, glorified and exalted, knows what we will do before He created the heavens and the earth by fifty thousand years, and even before that. But the writing was before the creation of the heavens and the earth by fifty thousand years. And you believe that Allah, the Exalted, tests us, that He examines us in order to know. Thus. But the soul may not be content with bare submission.
So we say: the knowledge of Allah, glorified and exalted, which comes after our action and after our being tested, is a knowledge upon which reward or punishment is based, because a servant cannot be rewarded or punished unless he is tested. As for prior knowledge, He, glorified and exalted, knows that He will test us and that we will act or abstain. But when the thing occurs, the trial and the test, and then the person disobeys or obeys, this is the knowledge which is what? Upon which reward and punishment are based, meaning that the recompense depends upon it. This is the knowledge that is restricted to the trial and examination. Some scholars made another distinction and said: Allah's knowledge of what we have not yet done is knowledge that it will be; and His knowledge of what we have done is knowledge that it has been. Thus the first knowledge relates to what will be, a knowledge of something not yet occurred, and the knowledge relating to what has been is knowledge that it has occurred. This is not objectionable, but the first is the foundation.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a threat may be by words and may be by meaning. By words: that he says, "If you do such and such, then upon you is such and such." This is a threat by words. By meaning: when Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the comprehensiveness of His awareness of what we do, this means that we should not oppose Him, out of caution lest He know from us what does not please Him. Just as the legal rulings are derived through command and prohibition, and through encouragement and warning: when rulings come accompanied by encouragement, this is evidence that they are commanded, even if there is no explicit command; and when warning comes, we know that they are forbidden.
It is related that a Bedouin heard a reciter reading: "And the thief, male and female, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they earned, as a punishment from Allah; and Allah is Mighty and Wise," and the Bedouin said: "That is not the verse; read it." He repeated it and said: "And the thief, male and female, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they earned, as a punishment from Allah; and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." The Bedouin said: "That does not work. Read the verse properly." He read it a third or fourth time and said: ﴿as a recompense for what they earned, a punishment from Allah; and Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾ [al-Ma'idah 38]. He said: "Now, now you have got it right, because He, the Mighty and Majestic, is Mighty, and so He cut off the hand, by His might, dominance, overpowering and sovereignty; and by His wisdom He cut it off. Had He forgiven and shown mercy, He would not have cut it off" [[See Khizanat al-Adab and Ghayat al-Arab by Ibn Hijjah al-Hamawi (1/176), and al-Kashkul (2/112). It has a witness from the words of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The error is not to recite some of the Quran in place of some, nor to end a verse of 'Forgiving, Merciful' with 'Knowing, Wise' or 'Mighty, Wise'; rather the error is to recite what is not in it, or to end a verse of mercy with a verse of punishment, or a verse of punishment with a verse of mercy." Musannaf of Abd al-Razzaq (5985).]]. Look at this Bedouin.
This statement is correct, and for this reason the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: If a highway robber repents before he is captured, the prescribed punishment (hadd) is dropped from him. If a highway robber who took people's property and killed them repents, the prescribed punishment is dropped from him. They cited for this the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Except those who repent before you gain power over them; so know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ma'idah 34]. He did not say, "Do not lift the penalty from them." He did not say that. But His saying that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful means that He forgave these people and showed them mercy, so the penalty is dropped from them. However, the penalty connected to the right of Allah is dropped, whereas the penalty connected to the right of the human being, such as retaliation (qisas) and the guarantee of the property they took, remains, because it is a right of the human being.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, would you kindly explain the meaning of the words ﴿Settlement is best, and the souls are made present to stinginess﴾? The meaning is clear, Shaykh, but what is the meaning of ﴿and the souls are made present to stinginess﴾?
* The Shaykh: When He said ﴿Settlement is best﴾, and settlement necessarily involves some yielding of right and some humbling of the person, because if a person receives everything he wants, the other loses everything he wants. Settlement requires two or more parties. If we gave a person everything he wants, the other would lose everything he wants; and if we give him only some of what he wants, he may become stingy and say: "Why should I concede? Let us go to the judge, either this or that." Is this not likely? This is the meaning of His words ﴿and the souls are made present to stinginess﴾; meaning: overcome your souls and reconcile, even if the soul demands its full right.
* Student: The phrase's construction (...) ﴿and the souls are made present to stinginess﴾: who...?
* The Shaykh: Allah made the souls present. But when Allah attributes a blameworthy thing to Himself, He uses the form of the passive participle (ism al-maf'ul). That is, Allah made the souls present to stinginess by their nature. Look at the saying of the jinn. The jinn would not be more knowledgeable than— do I say "than you"? Is there any objection?
* The Student: No, there is no objection.
* The Shaykh: ﴿And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on the earth, or whether their Lord intends for them guidance﴾ [al-Jinn 10]. They said: ﴿evil is intended for those on the earth﴾, out of courtesy toward Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and it is known that the one who intends is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And regarding guidance: ﴿or whether their Lord intends for them guidance﴾, He attributed it to Allah because it is good. That is, if Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, had said, "and Allah made the souls present to stinginess," the sentence would have been fine. But since stinginess is a blameworthy matter, He said: ﴿and the souls are made present to stinginess﴾. So "the souls" is the deputy of the subject, standing in place of the first object, and ﴿stinginess﴾ is the second object.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. We said that the verse ﴿indeed Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾ contains a fronting of the object before the verb, and this would be a problem, because it would mean that Allah knows only what we do. What is the answer to this problem, which I did not understand?
* The Shaykh: We said that this is in the category of threat. That is, as if nothing is known to Allah except this action, and so this is a restrictive exclusion (hasr idafi) for the threatening of these addressees.
* Student: May Allah bless you. We mentioned that settlement is permissible so long as it does not make lawful what is unlawful. The settlement...
* The Shaykh: Or makes unlawful what is lawful.
* The Student: An objection arises: if he waives the division for the wife, and Allah commanded justice among wives, we say: how...?
* The Shaykh: Why did He command justice? For whose right?
* The Student: The wife's.
* The Shaykh: If she waives it?
* The Student: Perhaps this is...
* The Shaykh: No, there is absolutely no problem. ﴿Give full measure when you measure﴾ [al-Isra 35] is obligatory. But if the holder of the right agrees to say, "Measure out for me a quarter of a sa'," is that permissible or not?
* The Student: It is permissible.
* The Shaykh: It is permissible.
* Student: Is the turn (qasm) for the wife obligatory?
* The Shaykh: What?
* The Student: The turn for the wife.
* Students: The turn, is it obligatory?
* The Shaykh: What is meant?
* Student: The turn.
* The Shaykh: The turn is well known, it is obligatory. The husband must divide equally among his wives, and it will come in the next verse, ﴿And you will never be able to be just between wives﴾ [an-Nisa 129], God willing.
* The Student: May Allah be good to you. Is the knowledge of faith in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, which comes after action, not for the purpose of clear evidence and testing, as in His words: ﴿that those who perish might perish by clear evidence, and those who live might live by clear evidence﴾ [al-Anfal 42]?
* The Shaykh: Read what comes before it? That is, Allah explained things to us so that those who perish might perish by clear evidence and those who live might live by clear evidence. This relates to the created being: the purpose is that the creature has the proof established against him and has no excuse left. It has no connection with knowledge.
* Student: Between nushuz and i'rad?
* The Shaykh: What?
* The Student: Nushuz and i'rad?
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The Student: Shaykh, we said nushuz is when he lifts himself above her, and i'rad is when he turns away from her. Is there a common element between them?
* The Shaykh: Nushuz is in abandoning an obligation, and i'rad is in doing a prohibited act.
* Student: You spoke about the closing, or the appropriateness of the closing, of Allah's words: ﴿a punishment from Allah; and Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾, and what is the appropriateness of closing with His words: ﴿If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [al-Ma'idah 118].
* The Shaykh: A valid question. He said regarding Jesus that he said to Allah, the Exalted: ﴿If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise﴾, and he did not say "indeed You are the Forgiving, the Merciful." Does anyone among you have an answer?
* Student: That Allah, the Exalted, was angry at that time.
* The Shaykh: What?
* The Student: That at that time He was angry.
* The Shaykh: The Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.
* The Student: Jesus showed courtesy toward Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so he mentioned might and wisdom.
* Student: Shaykh, he says: ﴿And if You forgive them, indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise﴾; so Your forgiveness of them does not entail punishment, and entails (...) Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, after His forgiveness and pardon.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Shaykh, forbearance and forgiveness come after ability to punish. So if Jesus, peace be upon him, wished to affirm to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, forgiveness, and that if He forgives them it is not out of weakness.
* The Shaykh: The verse, in reality, is not pure forgiveness. ﴿If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise﴾. These are two matters, punishment and forgiveness, and both together entail might and wisdom; for it is part of wisdom that Allah forgives whom He wills, and part of might that He punishes whom He wills. Since the verse is not on a single subject, it closes with what suits both.
* Student: May Allah be good to you, can we say that...
* Student: Preference, with evidence that the verb which is (...).
* The Shaykh: How?
* The Student: Can we say that (ma) in His words: ﴿And whatever good you do﴾ is conditional, with evidence from the deletion of the nun of...
* The Shaykh: But this is not the verse; this is not the wording of the verse. What we have is ﴿And if you do good and fear God﴾.
* Student: No, the verse before it.
* The Shaykh: How?
* The Student: The verse before it, with evidence that the relative (ma) is accompanied by (...).
* The Shaykh: No, it does not do; a conditional noun is required, with evidence from the jussive. Then we said it is relative, so that is a mistake or a slip of the tongue; it is conditional, without doubt.
* Student: There is a question, Shaykh.
* * *

Shaykh: As for newspapers and magazines, which are prepared, or whose content is mostly pictures, these may not be kept in the house. As for those in which a picture appears, such as the photograph of the author of an article or something similar, these pictures are unintended, and, God willing, they do no harm.

I am strict about this matter of remarks (al-mulahazat), because a person, when he undertakes a task, should perfect it. That is the most important thing.

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so. So do not incline completely [away from one], leaving her as if suspended. And if you amend and fear Allah, indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful. And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance, and ever is Allah all-Encompassing and Wise.﴾ [An-Nisa 129, 130].

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion, there is no blame upon them for effecting a settlement between themselves in reconciliation﴾. We have finished this verse along with its benefits.

He says: ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾.

﴿Lan﴾ here is for negation; it is a negating particle, and it is also a particle of nasb (accusative), putting the verb in the subjunctive, and of istiqbal (futurity), meaning it makes the present-tense verb refer purely to the future. Its counterpart is (lam), which makes the present-tense verb refer to the past. So when you say: lam yaqum Zayd (Zayd did not stand), this refers to the past. (Lan) and (lam) share negation, but they differ in their governing effect and in shifting the verb from the present/future to the past.

﴿Lan tastatee'oo﴾ means: it will not be within your capacity. ﴿An ta'diloo bayn al-nisa'﴾: ﴿an ta'diloo﴾ here is a present-tense verb preceded by (an) al-masdariyyah (the verbal-noun 'an'), and the phrase after (an) is interpreted as a verbal noun, so that in this verse it is the object of ﴿lan tastatee'oo﴾. That is: you will not be able to achieve justice between the wives, even if you strive to do so. And justice (al-'adl) is the opposite of inclination (al-mayl).

﴿So do not incline completely [away from one], leaving her as if suspended﴾. When the words of the Exalted ﴿so do not incline completely﴾ came, the difficulty raised by His saying, blessed and exalted, ﴿So marry what seems good to you of women, two, three, or four; but if you fear that you will not be just, then [marry only] one﴾ [An-Nisa 3] was resolved. Thus what was mentioned in the earlier verse is interpreted as meaning: you will not be able to be just in the attainable degree of justice, because a justice that is impossible cannot be imposed upon a person.

As for His saying ﴿even if you should strive to do so﴾: (law) here is a conditional particle, and its conditional clause is ﴿harastum﴾. Where, then, is the response (jawab) of the condition? It has been said: the response of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, and the estimated meaning is: "even if you strive, you will still not be able to." It has also been said, and the correct view is, that (law), (in) and similar conditional particles in this kind of context do not require a response; rather, they serve merely as a restriction on what was previously stated, and so they need no response. This is the view that Ibn al-Qayyim, as I recall, preferred, and it is correct: in such a context it does not require a response. If you say: "Honour Zayd if he honours you," do not say that the response of the condition in "if he honours you" is omitted and indicated by what precedes it; rather say that it requires no response, but is merely a restriction on what came before.

﴿Even if you should strive to do so﴾: that is, if you exert effort for justice, you will still not be able to achieve it. But ﴿do not incline completely [away from one]﴾. He did not say "do not incline the inclination" but said ﴿completely﴾, meaning: do not incline with the entire inclination. As for some inclination, there is no blame, since it falls within the negation of ability.

﴿So leaving her as if suspended﴾: To whom does the pronoun in ﴿tadharoohā﴾ refer? To the one toward whom he inclined, or the one from whom he inclined?

Students: From whom he inclined.

Shaykh: Undoubtedly the one from whom he inclined, because the one toward whom he inclined has been attended to and honoured. But the one from whom he inclined completely, when he turns away entirely, becomes like one suspended between heaven and earth. This is an indication that she is left unsettled, for one suspended between heaven and earth does not settle: he is not in the heavens to be at rest, nor on the earth to be at rest. This woman from whom he has completely turned away remains suspended: she is neither a widow nor a married woman. That is, he has not divorced her so that she may find rest and Allah grant her someone else, nor is she a married woman who enjoys marriage like others. Allah has likened her to this as a warning against complete inclination, which makes such a woman like one suspended.

﴿And if you amend and fear Allah, indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Here He said ﴿and if you amend and fear Allah﴾, while in the preceding verse He said ﴿and if you do good and fear Allah﴾. The difference is that this man has two wives: one from whom he has completely turned away, and the other toward whom he has turned. Such a situation will create discord between the two wives, so He said ﴿and if you amend﴾, indicating that if discord or other troubles arise between the two wives, he should reconcile between them, since this is a natural matter. Then He said ﴿and fear Allah﴾, meaning, be mindful of Allah in reconciling, so that you do not incline toward one to the exclusion of the other. ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

He forgives what has occurred of discord and inclination and the like; ﴿Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa 129], meaning: possessor of vast mercy.

In this noble verse there are many benefits. Among them: Allah, glorified and exalted, removed hardship from the human being even in his dealings with others, by His saying ﴿and you will never be able to be equitable﴾. This is a statement about a natural matter that entails the lifting of blame, because the legal principle is that a person is not obligated to do what he cannot do.

Also among them: the knowledge of Allah, glorified and exalted, of the states and inner dispositions of His servants, by His saying ﴿and you will never be able to be equitable between wives﴾. This is a matter known necessarily: that Allah, glorified and exalted, knows everything, including what a person whispers to himself.

Also among the benefits: a person must be just in what he is able to do, since Allah negated ability in order to lift hardship from it. Its implication is that when a person is able, he must be just. What he must be just in has already been mentioned: he must be just between wives in everything, in everything within his power. As for love and what arises from it, this is a difficult matter, so a person is not burdened with it.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: a person should not burden himself with what he cannot bear and what would be difficult for him, by His saying ﴿even if you should strive to do so﴾, as if He said: do not burden yourselves with what you cannot do.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the prohibition of complete inclination with respect to justice between wives, by His saying, exalted is He, ﴿So do not incline completely [away from one]﴾.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person, in his speech, should use whatever produces aversion toward what is to be disliked or encouragement toward what is to be desired, since this is part of the method of wisdom; by His saying ﴿leaving her as if suspended﴾.

Also among the benefits of this verse: appealing to compassion in a situation where compassion is due, since when a person imagines that this wife from whom he turned away is like one suspended between heaven and earth, this obliges him to show compassion, tenderness and mercy toward her.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: reconciliation and piety are a cause of forgiveness, by His exalted saying ﴿And if you amend and fear Allah, indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾. And so it is; I mean, and so it is, that its reasoning is clear, since reconciliation is good, and ﴿good deeds remove evil deeds﴾ [Hud 114], and because reconciliation is good and good deeds bring mercy.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, the Forgiving and the Merciful. By forgiveness the disliked is removed, and by mercy the sought-after is attained. This is why Allah joins the Forgiving with the Merciful in many places. Because by forgiveness what?

Students: the disliked is removed.

Shaykh: The disliked is removed, and by mercy what is sought is attained. How so? Forgiveness is the forgiving of sins and the removal of their effects; mercy is the attainment of what is desired and loved. This is why Allah named Paradise, calling it mercy, and said to it: "You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whom I will."[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4850) and Muslim (2846/36), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Is forgiveness a real attribute, or is it an expression for lifting accountability and punishment?

Answer: It is a real attribute which entails the lifting of accountability and punishment. The same applies to mercy: is it a real attribute by which Allah is characterized, or is it an expression for beneficence, bestowal, and bringing about benefits?

Answer: The first. This is the position of the righteous predecessors and the imams of this Ummah after them. As for one who says that Allah is not described with forgiveness or mercy, he has gone astray with manifest error. His argument is rational-seeming but in reality imaginary: he says that forgiveness entails an act, and an act is a characteristic of created beings, since by his claim a happening can only subsist in a happening; and by his claim mercy is not fitting for Allah, since it involves tenderness and emotional response toward the one shown mercy, which is not fitting for Allah, exalted is He. It is well known that this is analogy opposed to the text, and it closely resembles the analogy of Iblis when Allah addressed him and commanded him to prostrate, and he said: ﴿I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay﴾ [Al-A'raf 12]. That is: "I am better than him, so how shall I prostrate when he is beneath me?" Whoever makes reason the judge against the text resembles Iblis entirely, and his conduct is inspired by Iblis. We say: the mercy which is tenderness and emotional response for the sake of gentleness toward the one shown mercy is only the mercy of the servant. As for the mercy of Allah, it belongs to the Essence of Allah, and we cannot describe its modality.

As for his saying that reason does not indicate it: we say this is an error. Reason indicates it: ﴿Whatever blessing you have is from Allah﴾ [An-Nahl 53]. All these blessings are effects of mercy; were it not for Allah's mercy He would not have bestowed any blessing upon His servants. It is remarkable that they argue for the affirmation of the Will by a matter that some students do not understand, let alone the common people, yet they deny affirming mercy by reason, even though common people understand it. If you asked any layman: rain fell, watered the earth, and made the earth grow; what does this indicate?

Student: It indicates the mercy of Allah.

Shaykh: It indicates the mercy of Allah, yes. But as for the Will, they say: the specification of created things with what is peculiar to them is evidence of the Will; that a human is human, a camel is a camel, the sun is the sun, and so on, indicates the Will, for otherwise there would be no distinction among creatures.
