We say: we agree with you on this indication, but it is a hidden indication, more hidden than the indication of blessings for mercy. But ﴿whoever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light﴾ [An-Nur 40].

Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance﴾ [An-Nisa 130]. ﴿If they separate﴾: to whom does the pronoun refer? It refers to the spouses: to the wife who feared from her husband ill-treatment (nushuz) and aversion, and to the wife whom her husband has left like one hanging in suspense. It is well known that he would not turn away from her except out of his dislike for her, and he would not leave her like one hanging in suspense except out of his dislike for her. Then separation occurs. If they separate, Allah, Glorified and Exalted, will facilitate for each of them what brings about richness from Allah's abundance. ﴿Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance﴾: with what?

Some of them said: He will enrich the husband with a righteous wife in whom he finds happiness, and He will enrich the wife with a righteous husband in whom she finds happiness; meaning, the husband finds a woman and the wife finds a husband.

Others said: ﴿Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance﴾ is by replacing the first spouse, or by consolation and forgetting, so that the matter becomes as if it had never been. But this view is weak, because consolation and not mentioning one another to each other is not enrichment. Enrichment is that there be found that by which a person becomes self-sufficient, and this does not occur except with what? Except with a spouse: a husband for the wife and a wife for the husband. This is a promise from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, a promise from the Capable who is able to send the woman a husband in whom she finds happiness, or to the man a wife in whom he finds happiness. It is a promise that is true and sincere, because who is the One who promised it?
* The students: Allah.
* The Shaykh: Allah, who does not break His promise, is capable of everything. But at times this is not fulfilled because of a person's doubt, his lack of trust and his lack of faith, so this impediment occurs and the promised thing does not come to pass.

﴿And Allah is ever Vast, Wise﴾: ﴿Vast﴾ means possessing great vastness in all attributes: vast in His knowledge, ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾ [Ghafir 7]; vast in His power, ﴿Indeed Allah is over all things competent﴾ [Al-Baqarah 20]; vast in His wisdom, and for this reason wisdom is joined with it; vast in His hearing and sight, in all of His attributes, Mighty and Majestic; and vast in His encompassing, encompassing everything. ﴿And to Allah belongs the east and the west; so wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah. Indeed, Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing﴾ [Al-Baqarah 115]. The point is that He, Majestic and Exalted, is vast in the fullest sense, to the greatest extent possible. ﴿Wise﴾ means possessing wisdom, and what else? And judgment. He is the One who has both the cosmic (kawni) and the legislative (shar'i) judgment, and He is the One who has the formal or the final wisdom. Have you understood this?

First: judgment belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿The judgment is only for Allah﴾ [Al-An'am 57]. The judgment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is cosmic and legislative. Whatever He decrees over His creation is cosmic, and whatever He legislates for His creation is legislative. This is the rule: the cosmic judgment is what Allah decrees over His creation, and the legislative judgment is what Allah has prescribed for His creation, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿Prohibited to you is carrion﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 3]: this is a legislative judgment. ﴿He created the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al-An'am 1]: this is a cosmic judgment. As for an example of the same word in this root, the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in Surat al-Mumtahanah: ﴿That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you﴾ [Al-Mumtahanah 10]; this is a legislative judgment. And He said: ﴿Do they then seek the judgment of ignorance? And who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain?﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 50]. And this is what kind of judgment?
* The students: Legislative.
* The Shaykh: This is legislative. ﴿Do they then seek the judgment of ignorance...﴾ And the saying of my brother Yusuf: ﴿I will not leave this land until my father permits me or Allah judges for me﴾ [Yusuf 80]?
* The students: Cosmic.
* The Shaykh: This is cosmic. Good. ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ [At-Tin 8]?
* The students: Cosmic and legislative.
* The Shaykh: Cosmic and legislative, may Allah bless you. Wisdom may be a thing's wisdom in the form in which Allah created it, and it may be wisdom in its purpose: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat 56]. This is a wisdom explaining the praiseworthy purpose in the creation of mankind and jinn. ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾ [At-Tin 4]: this is a formal wisdom, meaning that its form is not meaningless; "formal" means that He fashions it in this particular form. This is among the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The rising of the sun to this extent, the rising of the moon to this extent, the alternation of night and day in this manner: all of this is formal wisdom, meaning that its being in this form is the wisdom, and if it differed, the wisdom would be lost.

Based on this, we say: the aspects here are four: wisdom in the legislation, wisdom in the decree, wisdom in the form, and wisdom in the purpose.

When you believe in this, you know that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cannot bring about anything, even the greatest evil and the greatest harm, except for a wisdom. These wars that have occurred and are occurring now are all for a wisdom. When we believe this, we are patient and await relief, and relief comes by Allah's permission. We do not say, "Why did Allah decree this?" or become resentful, or say, "There is no wisdom in it." No, we must believe that it is for a wisdom, because it is the decree of Allah, and the decree of Allah is undoubtedly for a wisdom. Likewise in the legislation: if Allah commands us to do something or forbids us from something, even if we do not know its wisdom, we must know that it has a wisdom, because this is part of the requirement of the name Al-Hakim. Allah created the devils and gave them power over whomever He wills of His servants, and Allah created evil, diseases, poverty and other things. Is this wisdom?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Undoubtedly wisdom; because we know that Allah does not decree anything except for a wisdom, so we are content and submit. The reality is that not being content with the decree means impugning the wisdom of Allah. The benefit of a person knowing the wisdom of Allah is that he is content, submits, and knows that what Allah legislated is true and what He decreed is true, and then he fully surrenders to the decree and destiny.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an allusion to separating the spouses when they are incompatible. The reasoning: Allah promised good upon separation, saying: ﴿And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance﴾. This is the truth: when we cannot find a path to reconciliation and harmony between the spouses, the only path is separation, so that each of them may find happiness in their life. We have evidence for this from the Sunnah: "The wife of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, may Allah be pleased with him" came, and Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, may Allah be pleased with him, is among those given glad tidings of Paradise, meaning his station is elevated. "She came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I do not blame Thabit ibn Qays regarding his character or his religion" (or she said: "I do not reproach him"). He is an upright man in his character and upright in his religion. "But I dislike disbelief in Islam." The meaning of disbelief here is ingratitude to the spouse (kufr al-'ashir), meaning not fulfilling one's duty toward him, because of her dislike for him; she dislikes him intensely. He said to her: "Will you return his garden to him?" And what is the garden? It was a dower he had given her, a garden, an orchard. Yes; but Allah knows that orchards were cheap at that time, lest the women argue against us, saying, "An orchard is worth millions."
He said: "Will you return his garden to him?" She said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." The Messenger ﷺ said to Thabit: "Accept the garden and divorce her with one divorce." So he accepted it and divorced her.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (5273) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]

Some scholars have adopted this view and said: if a woman says, "I cannot remain with the husband at all, and if you keep me with him I will burn myself," then the judge compels the husband to divorce her if she returns his dower. This view is not far from correct. Allah, the Exalted, indicated in this verse that separation is what? It is better and more excellent, because Allah promised good with it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, toward His servants: that when a woman and a man are broken by separation, Allah consoles them with what? With enrichment: He enriches each of them from His abundance.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: closing the door of despair for the separated spouses, yes, closing the door of despair from the mercy of Allah, in that He said: ﴿from His abundance﴾ and did not say merely "He will enrich each," but said ﴿from His abundance﴾, as an indication that the bounty of Allah is vast, and that you should not despair even if you find it unlikely that Allah will replace you with someone better, or that Allah will replace her with a better husband. Do not consider it unlikely, for Allah will enrich you from what? From His abundance.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, the Exalted, is Vast and Wise, as in His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Vast, Wise﴾, and this is part of His wisdom.

* Among its benefits: that this vastness through which Allah promised enrichment is founded upon wisdom. It seems, and Allah knows best, to be an indication that if this promised thing does not occur, it will not fail except for a wisdom. Sometimes Allah, Glorified and Exalted, withholds from a person what he loves for a great benefit; sometimes He tests him with what fills his heart with constant grief and worry, but for a great wisdom. What is it? That what a person suffers of worry, grief, and the loss of a beloved thing, Allah expiates for him by it. We know that life goes on and a person forgets what happened to him, but he finds its reward and benefit with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For this reason, when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, informed that "fever expiates sins," one of the Companions, whose name I have forgotten, said: "O Messenger of Allah, but if I am afflicted with fever, meaning it does not prevent me from prayer in congregation or from doing good, will Allah expiate for me by it?" He said: "Yes." So he asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to afflict him with a fever that does not prevent him from prayer or fasting, meaning nor from good, in order that it might expiate for him.[[Narrated by al-Tahawi in Mushkil al-Athar (2219).]] But this is a matter of personal reasoning (ijtihad), and it is better that you ask Allah for well-being, for well-being is certainly broader than punishment.

However, in any case, if the promise in His saying, ﴿Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance﴾, does not occur, we know that it did not occur for a great wisdom, the fruits of which a person may find in the future, either in this world or in the Hereafter.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of wisdom for Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
From this follows a great methodological and practical benefit: contentment with what? With the decree of Allah and the legislation of Allah. You are content because you know that it is for a wisdom. Even if you lose your wealth or your child, know that it is for a wisdom, and when you believe this, every calamity will become easier for you, every calamity will be easier when you know that what befalls you is from Allah and that Allah, the Exalted, possesses great wisdom in what He decrees.

* Student: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿So do not incline completely [to one] and leave her as if suspended﴾. ﴿Fa-tadharuha﴾: is it in the accusative or the jussive?
(...)
* Student: Shaykh, ﴿fa-tadharuha﴾: is it jussive or accusative (...)?
* The Shaykh: What do you say, brothers? The fa' in His saying ﴿fa-tadharuha﴾: is it the fa' of causation, with the verb after it in the accusative, or the fa' of coordination, with the verb after it in the jussive?
* Student: The second.
* The Shaykh: Which one?
* The Student: Coordination.
* The Shaykh: Good.
* Student: Accusative, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: The closer one is the first; there are two opinions.
* Student: Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: Yes?
* The Student: Accusative after (...).
* The Shaykh: Hoping... yes, that is apparent. The brother's apparent view is that it is accusative, and "lest you leave her" is because of your leaving her. Yes.
* Student: ﴿fa-tadharuha ka-l-mu'allaqah﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿So do not incline completely [to one]﴾, so that because of your complete inclination you leave her as one suspended; this is based on what precedes.
* Student: May Allah be good to you. We explained His saying, Exalted, "enrichment" as replacing the husband or consolation. Would this not be a restriction of the vast, given that Allah, Majestic and Exalted, did not restrict or define it? Could it not be, for example, with something good that the soul finds comfort in from both spouses? Replacement may be...?
* The Shaykh: But the enrichment in place of what is lost is usually with something similar to it; this is the usual case.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, a question: in the hadith of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, did his command to him, peace and blessings be upon him, to accept the garden and divorce her, mean a binding command, or was it like his intercession for the slave-woman's husband Mughith?
* The Shaykh: No. Regarding Barirah and Mughith: Barirah said to him, "Are you ordering me? Then hearing and obeying. Or are you advising me? I have no need of him." But here the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, knew that the situation would not be reconciled between them, so his command was a binding command.
* The Student: A binding command occurs because of a reason that is accepted.
* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed it occurs.
* Student: If the husband is of bad character, is this a sufficient reason for separation, and does the woman then enter [the separation]...?
* The Shaykh: First we say: if he is ugly in appearance, and if she cannot bear to look at him at all, and her chest tightens, then yes. Character is also a great defect, and for this she said: "I do not blame him for character or religion." This also indicates that if a woman finds fault in her husband's character or religion, she may ask for divorce.
* Student: If a woman does not want her husband at all, but her father makes her return to him, does his guardianship lapse?
* The Shaykh: Yes. This happens often: the father wants his daughter to remain with her husband in any case, while she does not want him at all. We say: the father is set aside, and we go to the judge.
* Student: A woman with whom a marriage contract was made but who was not consummated: is justice required between her and the other woman?
* The Shaykh: No; because Allah commanded justice, but Allah said in the Noble Qur'an: ﴿Live with them in kindness﴾ [An-Nisa 19], and by custom, if he has not gone in to her, she has no turn.
* Student: In everything?
* The Shaykh: Yes?
* Student: In gifts?
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And We had already instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and [now] you, to fear Allah. And if you deny, then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and ever is Allah Free of need and Praiseworthy. And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs. If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others; and ever is Allah competent to do that. Whoever desires the reward of this world — then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And ever is Allah Hearing and Seeing﴾ [An-Nisa 131–134].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed. We have previously discussed His saying: ﴿And you will never be able to be just between wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾, and we explained its benefits. Does this verse contradict what came earlier at the beginning of the surah?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It does not contradict it. How is the reconciliation?
* Student: We said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So do not incline completely﴾, so it became clear that what is prohibited is the total inclination; as for when one leans only partly, there is no sin on him.
* The Shaykh: There is no sin on him in combining two wives. Do you agree with that?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: His saying: ﴿And if you do good and fear Allah﴾, and in the verse before it: ﴿And if you do good and fear Allah﴾?
* Student: When a man has two wives, he will incline toward one over the other, so it is certain that discord and dispute will occur between the husband and the wife, and so Allah, Blessed and Exalted, commands him here to... 
* The Shaykh: Urges him.
* The Student: Urges him to reconciliation, reconciling the wife with the wife, whereas in the first (...) he said: man seeks reconciliation.
* The Shaykh: This is not clear; whoever has a clearer answer than this?
* Student: In the second verse, ﴿And if you reconcile and fear Allah﴾: a man has two wives, he inclines toward one over the other, so discord and dispute arise between them, and he needs to reconcile between them. As for the first verse, it concerns discord between a man and his wife, so it requires kindness.
* The Shaykh: And the situation calls for kindness; complete.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 130 (part 2 of 2):

Regarding His saying, ﴿And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance﴾: what does it indicate?

* Student: It indicates that separation is preferable and better if reconciliation is not possible, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, promised enrichment in return for it, enriching each one of the two of them.
* The Shaykh: So it points to the fact that if agreement is not possible, then what?
* The students: Then separation is preferable.
* The Shaykh: Then separation is preferable, yes.

Why did Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, say ﴿from His abundance﴾ and not say "from His presence" [or "from Himself," i.e., ʿindah]?

* Student: ﴿from His abundance﴾ so that it shows the greatness of the bounty that Allah gives them.
* The Shaykh: How so?
* The student: The livelihood of each of them will become broad.
* The Shaykh: Because, with the discord, their livelihood would be...
* The student: Miserable.
* The Shaykh: Miserable and constricted, so He said: ﴿Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 131:

﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And We have certainly instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and [you], [saying], "Fear Allah."﴾ To the end of the verse.

﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.﴾ Similar expressions have come before us many times. In it, the fronting of the predicate, ﴿لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ﴾ (lillah ma fi al-samawat, "to Allah belongs what is in the heavens"), conveys restriction (hasr): it belongs exclusively to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The dominion over the heavens and the earth encompasses everything in them, whether physical things, benefits, or otherwise. All of it belongs to Allah; no one shares in it with Him. For this reason, no one can dispose of anything in the heavens and the earth except by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, either the cosmic permission (al-idhn al-kawni) or the legislated permission (al-idhn al-shar'i).

He says: ﴿وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ ("And We have certainly instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and [you]"). Having mentioned what pertains to lordship (rububiyyah), which is the all-encompassing dominion, He mentioned what pertains to divinity (uluhiyyah) and worship, which is what? Taqwa (God-consciousness). So He said: ﴿وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ﴾. ﴿وَصَّيْنَا﴾ (wassayna, "We instructed"): wasiyyah (instruction) is a commitment to something with emphasis. That is, it is not merely saying, "O so-and-so, do such-and-such"; that is not a wasiyyah. Rather, when it is said "wassa," its meaning is that a commitment to the matter has been made to him with emphasis.

﴿الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ ("those who were given the Scripture before you"): who are those who were given the Scripture before us? It has been said: the Jews and the Christians. But the correct view is that it is more general, and that every person to whom Allah sent a scripture was instructed by Him to have taqwa. It is well known that every messenger came with a scripture, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear evidences and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance﴾ [al-Hadid 25].

So ﴿أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ﴾ here is not restricted to the Jews and Christians; rather, everyone to whom Allah gave the Scripture was instructed by Allah, Exalted, with what? With taqwa: ﴿أَنِ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ ("that fear Allah"). The grammarians call this (an) "explanatory" (tafsiriyyah). Its sign is that it comes after a verb that contains the meaning of saying without its letters. If (an) comes after a verb that contains the meaning of saying without its letters, you parse it as explanatory; or if you wish, say: what can replace it is (i.e.), then it is explanatory. Here, ﴿وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ means "i.e., fear Allah," so ﴿اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ is, as it were, an explanation of what Allah, Exalted, instructed those before us and this nation.

﴿وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ أَنِ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾. Here, if someone says: He said ﴿وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾; is it not possible to say: "And We have instructed you and those who were given the Scripture before you," so that the pronoun is not separated?

We say: Yes, but since those people preceded us, the chronological order requires that they be mentioned first, just as whoever precedes another in rank is placed before him. And if attaching the pronoun were possible, as in His saying: ﴿They expel the Messenger and you﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 1], one could ask: why was the statement not "they expel you and the Messenger"? Because there is no separation where joining is possible, as Ibn Malik said in the Alfiyya:

"And in preference, the detached [pronoun] does not come, when the attached one can come."

We say: Yes, it is possible for it to be so, but the purpose would be lost. Here, those who were given the Scripture are not better than us, but they are earlier than us in time. In ﴿They expel the Messenger and you﴾ it is the order of rank: the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is mentioned so that he is not a follower of someone else, lest it be said: "they expel you and the Messenger."

He says: ﴿الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ أَنِ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾. This is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, instructed the earlier and later peoples. The taqwa of Allah has also passed by us many times and repeatedly, as: taking a shield against the punishment of Allah by doing His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. Taqwa is sometimes attributed to Allah, as here, and sometimes attributed to creatures, as in: ﴿And fear the Fire, which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾ [Aal-Imran 131], and sometimes attributed to time, as in: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah 281]. Taqwa attributed to other than Allah is not like taqwa attributed to Allah, because taqwa attributed to Allah is taqwa with worship and humility before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. As for guarding against the Fire and guarding against the Day on which we return to Allah, this is like our guarding against beasts of prey and wolves and the like: we fear them with a natural fear, not a fear of worship nor a taqwa of worship. There is a report: "Fear the evil of the one to whom you have done good" [al-Sakhawi said in al-Maqasid (1/60): "I do not know it; it may be a saying of some of the early generations."]. Guard against his evil is not taqwa of worship. So every taqwa attributed to other than Allah is not taqwa of worship, and taqwa attributed to Allah is taqwa of worship, meaning that a person guards against disobeying Allah, Mighty and Majestic, out of love for Him and exalting Him.

﴿وَإِنْ تَكْفُرُوا فَإِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ ("And if you disbelieve, then indeed to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth"). That is: and you will not harm Allah. If all creation disbelieves, they will not harm Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because He is free of need of them. In the famous hadith qudsi of Abu Dharr, Allah, Exalted, said: "O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of one man among you, it would not diminish anything of My dominion" [Narrated by Muslim (2577/55) from the hadith of Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him]. And what diminishes Allah? Obedience benefits whom? Its doer. Sin harms its doer. As for the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, He is not harmed by disobedience nor benefited by obedience. For this He said: ﴿And if you disbelieve, then indeed to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, so He is free of need of them all.

﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَنِيًّا حَمِيدًا﴾ ("And Allah has ever been Free of need and Praiseworthy"). This has also passed by us many times and repeatedly: that (kana, "was") in this construction conveys permanence, continuity, and the attribution of its subject with the attribute mentioned after it. That is, its subject is described with the attribute added to it: ﴿كَانَ اللَّهُ غَنِيًّا حَمِيدًا﴾ and He has never ceased to be Free of need and Praiseworthy. Al-Ghani is the one who possesses a self-sufficiency by which he is independent of others, and al-Hamid means al-mahmud (the one praised), so He is Free of need and is praised for His self-sufficiency. But is every rich person praised for his riches? No. The rich miser is exactly like the poor man, indeed worse than the miser, because the rich miser is in a worse state than the poor man, since the rich miser is blamed while the poor man is not blamed. But al-Ghani al-Hamid means the one who benefits others with his wealth, and this is the one who is praised. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is free of need by His essence from all creatures, and then He is praiseworthy for what He does for His servants of goodness and blessings, the removal of calamities, and other things.

(Hamid) here: shall we take it to mean (hamid, "one who praises") or to mean (mahmud, "one who is praised")?

* The students: Both.

* The Shaykh: Yes, both meanings together.

If someone says: Is this not the use of a homonym (mushtarak) in two meanings?

We say: What harm is there in using a homonym in two meanings if there is no contradiction between them? What is the meaning of mushtarak? A word that is suitable for two meanings in their literal sense, like the word (ayn) which is applied to gold:

"Andan or Na'tan or Yanbariln, a youth like the blade of the sword, Mizt its striker..."

So gold is called ayn; flowing water is called ayn in its literal sense; the eye that sees is called ayn in its literal sense. Here, if the word (ayn) came, could it bear all three meanings?

* The students: No.

* The Shaykh: We say: No, if they cannot be combined. But if they can, then we bear it. Here (hamid) is on the pattern fa'il, which comes in the sense of fa'il and comes in the sense of maf'ul: jarih (wounded) in the sense of majruh, sami' (hearing) in the sense of sami' (one who hears). Shall we use (hamid) here in the sense of mahmud and in the sense of hamid?

The answer: Yes. If an objector raises the objection and says: This is from the use of a homonym in two meanings.

We say: What harm is there in that if the two meanings are not contradictory.

So He is hamid, that is, mahmud, praised for His complete attributes, praised for His favours and His actions that revolve between justice and beneficence. He is also hamid (one who praises) those among His servants who deserve praise, and for this Allah, Glorified and Exalted, praises those who deserve praise, such as the prophets, the messengers, and the chosen ones, and the like.

* In this verse there are benefits. Among its benefits: the generality of Allah's dominion, Glorified and Exalted, from His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾.

* Among its benefits also: the exclusivity of the general dominion to Allah, whether it is general in its inclusion of physical things or general in its inclusion of actions. Its inclusion of physical things means that all existing things belong to Allah; its inclusion of actions means that He does what He wills with these existing things. Does such a thing hold for any created being?

* The students: No.

* The Shaykh: No. No one has comprehensive dominion over existing things or over actions and dispositions, because my ownership is limited, which you do not own, and your ownership is limited, which I do not own. Then, is my ownership of what I own a dominion over all dispositions so that I may dispose of it as I wish? No, it is a limited dominion. So what did we say?

* A student: That it is a dominion that is not (...).

* The Shaykh: Limited. Good.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the importance of taqwa, the importance of the taqwa of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Why? Because He instructed it to the earlier and later peoples: ﴿And We have certainly instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and [you], [saying], "Fear Allah."﴾

If someone says: Is taqwa achieved by doing the commands and avoiding the prohibitions?

We say: Yes. Then what is the answer regarding His saying: ﴿And cooperate in righteousness and taqwa﴾ [al-Ma'idah 2], and righteousness (birr) is everything Allah has commanded, so it is righteousness?

The answer: some words have one meaning when they stand alone and another meaning when they are joined with other words. So taqwa, when it stands alone, includes righteousness, and righteousness, when it stands alone, includes taqwa. When the two are combined, righteousness becomes doing the commands and taqwa becomes avoiding the prohibitions.

Here is an intervening statement: he says, the benefits of the importance of taqwa are that Allah instructed it to the earlier and later peoples.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that opposing taqwa does not harm Allah at all, from His saying... answer.

* The students: ﴿لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿وَإِنْ تَكْفُرُوا فَإِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, al-Ghani and al-Hamid, from which are derived two of Allah's attributes, self-sufficiency (ghina) and praiseworthiness (hamd).

From joining one of them to the other comes the benefit of their combination: self-sufficiency alone is a perfection, praise alone is a perfection, and their combination produces a higher perfection.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾. This is a repetition, but an important one: the first shows His self-sufficiency from His creation, ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَنِيًّا حَمِيدًا﴾, and the second shows His watchfulness over His creation. The final verse contains a warning against opposition, and the first contains a command to obedience.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 132:

He said: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is sufficient as Disposer of affairs.﴾ The wakil (trustee, one who takes charge) is the one who watches over and disposes of affairs. Hence a person's wakil is one who disposes of what he has been entrusted with and who watches over him.

In this verse there is, from the generality of Allah's dominion, what there was in the first verse.

And in this verse there is the perfection of Allah's watchfulness over His servants, as shown by His saying: ﴿and Allah is sufficient as Disposer of affairs.﴾

If someone says: The wakil is usually of lower rank than the one who appoints him, so how can we say that Allah is a wakil?

We say: The wakil who is usually of lower rank than the one who appoints him is the one who acts on behalf of another by that other's command, or not? Your wakil is lower in rank than you, because he acts for you by what? By your command, so he is beneath you. As for the wakil in the sense of the watchful overseer, his rank is higher than the one he watches over, because He, glorified and exalted, watches over all the servants and reckons their deeds upon them.

In the verse there is also: the perfection of Allah's watchfulness, and that in it is sufficiency from every need of watching over.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others; and Allah is ever capable of that.﴾ The sentence ﴿If He wills, He can remove you﴾ is not hidden from any of us: it is a conditional sentence, and both its condition and its answer are verbs in the present tense (muḍāriʿ), which is why both are in the jussive mood: ﴿If He wills [yashaʾ], He can remove you [yudhibkum]﴾. ﴿Yudhibkum﴾ means He will cause you to cease to exist, so that you are no longer in existence.

His saying ﴿O people﴾ is a vocative (munādā) with which Allah opened this sentence to draw attention, and ﴿the people﴾ here includes both the disbeliever and the believer.

﴿And bring others﴾: others who fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and carry out His command. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be like you﴾ [Muhammad: 38]. This is a warning from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that anyone who opposes His commands will be replaced.

﴿And Allah is ever capable of that﴾: ﴿Allah is ever capable of that﴾, i.e., of removing you and bringing others, ﴿capable [qadīran]﴾. Qudrah (capability, power) is an attribute by which the one who is capable is enabled to act. Is it "without ..."?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No.

* Students: Without incapacity.

* Shaykh: Without incapacity. Power (qudrah) is an attribute by which the doer is enabled to act without incapacity, and strength (quwwah) is an attribute by which one is enabled to act without weakness.

The evidence for this is that the opposite of qudrah is ʿajz (incapacity), and the opposite of quwwah is ḍaʿf (weakness), as the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, shows: ﴿Allah is the One who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair﴾ [ar-Rum: 54]. And He, Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth; indeed, He is ever Knowing, Competent [qadīran]﴾ [Fatir: 44]. He did not say "Knowing, Strong [qawiyyan]," because what stands opposite to incapacity is qudrah.

﴿If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others﴾: ﴿and bring others﴾. If we want to parse (ākharīn), how do we parse it?

* Student: ākharīna is in the genitive, marked by the yāʾ, because it is a sound masculine plural.

* Shaykh: Because it is?

* Student: A sound masculine plural.

* Shaykh: Has anything been omitted from this word: ﴿bi-ākharīna﴾?

* Student: ﴿bi-ākharīna﴾.

* Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: Nothing was omitted.

* Shaykh: Nothing was omitted.

* Student: Something was omitted.

* Shaykh: Something was omitted?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: Say it with a jazm [i.e., complete the thought]. What is the implied phrase?

* Student: "With a people [biqawmin] others."

* Shaykh: "With a people others." So what has been omitted here, the modified noun or the modifier?

* Students: The modified noun.

* Shaykh: The modified noun. Good.

* Student: What is meant by this word?

* Shaykh: We do not know the intention; none knows the intentions except the Lord of the servants. On this is the statement of Ibn Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him:

"And the modified noun and the modifier, if understood, may be omitted; but omitting the modifier is rare."

The modified noun is omitted often, as in ﴿Make full coats of mail [sābighāt]﴾ [Saba: 11] and similar examples; omitting the modifier is rare.

﴿And Allah is ever capable of that﴾: capable of that, or of other things? Of other things as well. The fronting here does not indicate restriction (ḥaṣr); rather, fronting it emphasises His capability over it, and this is the point of dispute between those who deny capability and those who affirm it. Therefore the object was fronted for its importance, and a similar case has passed us recently.

* Among the benefits of the verse: affirming the will (mashīʾah) of Allah, derived from ﴿If He wills [yashaʾ], He can remove you﴾.

Is the will established for Allah an absolute will, detached from wisdom, or is it a will connected with wisdom?

The second. Every matter that Allah has linked to His will refers to the will that wisdom requires. The evidence is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And you will not will except that Allah wills; indeed Allah is ever Knowing, Wise﴾ [al-Insan: 30], which shows that the will of Allah is connected with knowledge and wisdom.

* Among its benefits: showing the capability of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that He is able to remove all people and bring others. You know that Noah, peace be upon him, is the second father of mankind, because Allah destroyed his people except those who were with him. The historians have said that all those who remained of mankind are the descendants of Noah, and that the descendants of Noah were Sām, Ḥām and Yāfith; from these three the children of Adam branched out after Allah drowned the people of the earth. Here Allah removed the people of the earth and brought others, and the earth was populated with its inhabitants until Muhammad (ﷺ), upon whom and whose family be peace and blessings, was sent, and he was the seal of the prophets.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming that Allah is capable of everything; everything, Allah is capable of it.

Is He, Mighty and Majestic, capable of annihilating what exists?

* Students: Yes.

* Shaykh: Because it is a thing. Capable of bringing into being what does not exist?

* Students: Yes.

* Shaykh: Because it is a thing. Everything, Allah is capable of it. Is He capable of descending to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains?

* Students: Yes.

* Shaykh: Yes, He is capable. Capable of coming to judge between the servants? He is capable. Capable of speaking? He is capable. Everything, Allah is capable of it.

Some scholars said: but capability relates to a possible thing; as for an impossible thing, capability does not relate to it.

This was problematic for some people, who said: "Is Allah capable of everything?" Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, answered that the impossible is not a thing, because it will neither exist nor be annihilated; it is not a thing, so it cannot be said that it has left the generality of the verse, and if it is not a thing, it does not enter the generality, so we do not say that this is an error. For this reason al-Saffarini said in his creed:

"By a power that relates to the possible..."

Good. Does the knowledge of Allah relate to an impossible thing or not?

* Students: It relates.

* Shaykh: Yes, it relates to an impossible thing. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya: 22]. It is impossible that there be in them gods other than Allah, yet Allah's knowledge encompasses the outcome if it were so: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾, and this is an impossible thing.

If someone asked: Is Allah capable of creating something like Himself? We say: this is impossible; it is impossible that He create the like of Himself, because He, Majestic and Exalted, has no like, as He informed about Himself; and since He has no like, it is impossible that this be the case, because the statement of Allah, Exalted, is true, does not fail, and does not change.

Some people express it as "Allah is capable of whatever He wills." Is this expression correct?

It is not correct, because it restricts capability to what Allah wills; what He does not will, He is capable of, and the implication of this statement is that He is not capable of it. So we say: first, this phrase "Allah is capable of whatever He wills" is not found in the Qur'an or the Sunnah; and second, it gives a corrupt meaning.

Some scholars drew from this and said: it gives the impression of the doctrine of the Mu'tazilah, who denied that the will of Allah relates to the act of the servant and said that the servant acts by his own choice and the will of Allah has no connection to it, so that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would be incapable of the actions of the servants on that basis, since He does not will them.

In any case, we restrict ourselves to what came in the Qur'an and Sunnah: ﴿Indeed, Allah is capable of everything﴾. If a person cannot grasp the meaning of the impossible or the non-impossible, let him say: "Allah is capable of everything," and be silent. But we have explained to you; those before us are all students of knowledge, God willing, and they will understand. However, to the layman we may not say this; we may not say "capability relates to the possible," because what is not possible, namely the impossible, is not a thing, since he will never understand it.

It is related that Satan, the father of the devils, who has a throne on the sea and sends his armies and detachments to lead creation astray, was asked by his offspring: "Why do you rejoice at the death of a scholar more than at the death of a worshipper?" He said: "Because the scholar guides people and directs them, and I cannot mislead him; but the worshipper, I can—matters are obscure to him." They said: "How so?" He said: "I will test them for you." So he sent one of his soldiers to say to a worshipper: "Can Allah place the heavens and the earth inside an egg?" The egg is understood, and the heavens and the earth likewise. The worshipper thought about it—a worshipper who worships Allah night and day—and thought, and said: "He cannot." The emissary returned and said: "He says, 'He cannot.'" He said: "Look now, the man has disbelieved, and he does not even know it." Then he sent him to the scholar and said to him: "Can Allah, Mighty and Majestic, place the heavens and the earth in an egg?" He said: "Yes, He can: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82]. If He said to the heavens, 'Be within the egg,' either the egg would have to grow or the heavens and earth would have to shrink." He returned to his devil and told him this. He said: "Look, this one escaped, and that poor man disbelieved." This story is mentioned in some earlier books[[Mentioned by al-Qurtubi in Jami' Bayan al-'Ilm wa Fadlih (1/127), attributed to Ibn 'Abbas.]].

But I say: Allah is capable of everything. Tell the layman: "Allah is capable of everything," and do not tell him: "capability relates to the possible, nor to the impossible, nor to the permissible or the obligatory"—this is my intent, and this is the better course.

* Student: Shaykh, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿And We have certainly enjoined those who were given the Scripture before you and you [to fear] Allah﴾ [an-Nisa: 131]. Should we count from this verse that Allah enjoined the earlier and later peoples, and peoples who do not know, as part of the verse?

* Shaykh: Is it counted among its benefits, meaning?

* Student: That is, it is expressed from...

* Shaykh: They are expressed, and in what way is it expressed from the verse?

* Student: They are expressed, meaning people in the argument [hujjah], people with..., Allah, Blessed and Exalted, enjoined the earlier and later peoples so that it would be a proof against them.

* Shaykh: There is no harm in translating it by its meaning; there is no harm.

* Student: And on this reading, is "an" (أن) a verbal (maṣdariyyah) particle and not the nominal "an"?

* Shaykh: Allah enjoined...?

* Student: The earlier and later peoples, with the fear of Allah.

* Shaykh: With the fear of Allah—the meaning changes, because "bi-taqwa Allah" now omits the "an."

* Student: With a special part...

* Shaykh: Now you have converted it into a verbal noun; there is no "an" in it.

* Student: The "an" and it was converted...

* Shaykh: And you also brought in the bāʾ, because the entry of the bāʾ on "an" converts it.

* Student: Into a verbal noun.

* Shaykh: Into a maṣdariyyah, yes. But the verse does not have "an"; I mean it does not have the bāʾ.

* Student: It is possible that it is circumstantial (ḥāl).

* Shaykh: That is not valid. You must parse it as explanatory (tafsiriyyah), like ﴿We revealed to him, "Build the ship"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 27].

* Student: Shaykh, if we build on His saying: ﴿And He is, when He wills, capable of gathering them﴾ [ash-Shura: 29] (...)?

* Shaykh: This one has nothing in it. One says: how do we answer His saying ﴿And He is, when He wills, capable of gathering them﴾? It is said: the will here is conditioned on the gathering, meaning if He wills to gather them, nothing prevents Him; so the will here is a condition on the gathering, not a condition on capability.

* Student: His saying ﴿capable of that﴾. Some exegetes say that fronting the object to the verb does not here imply restriction, and they say it was fronted for the fitness of the verse's endings (ru'ūs al-āyāt)?

* Shaykh: Yes, this is a verbal fitness, and we mentioned that it was fronted not for restriction, that Allah is capable of this and of other things.

* Student: They say it was found for the fitness of the verse endings...

* Shaykh: No, this is a verbal fitness. It is true that verbal fitness does occur, but we have mentioned to you a semantic fitness, which is the concern with this matter that is denied or about to be denied.

* Student: Some of them went far with this and said: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ [ar-Rahman: 46], and said: the intended meaning is one garden, and the intended meaning here is the fitness of the verse endings?

* Shaykh: This is wrong, a great error. How can it be "two gardens" when He says ﴿therein﴾ [ar-Rahman: 50]? Is this dual or singular?

* Student: Dual.

* Shaykh: Then this is an error.

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world — with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And Allah is ever Hearing, Seeing.﴾ (134) O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So do not follow your desires, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted. (135) O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book which He has sent down upon His Messenger and the Scripture which He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly strayed far off. (136) Indeed, those who believed then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief - never will Allah forgive them or guide them to a way. (137) [An-Nisa 134-137].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world — with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter.﴾

Grammatical analysis (i'rab): ﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world﴾ is a conditional sentence (jumlah shartiyyah). Its condition (shart) is the word "kāna" (was/is), and its response (jawab al-shart) is the phrase ﴿with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter﴾. The response is preceded by the letter "fa" (fa' al-jawab, the response-marking "fa") because it cannot function as a verb for the condition; and every response that cannot serve as a verb for the condition must necessarily be preceded by "fa", as Ibn Malik (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

"And necessarily precede with fa a response that is made the condition of 'in' or another particle, if it cannot be made so."

This is the governing rule, and what falls under it has been enumerated in seven categories, mentioned in his words:

"Nominal, imperative, and with jamid, and with ma, qad, la (lan), and with the future (sin/sawfa)."

His words ﴿with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter﴾ form a declarative sentence (jumlah khabariyyah) in which the predicate has been placed first to convey restriction (hasr), since one of the principles of rhetoric is that placing what should come later earlier implies restriction. ﴿And Allah is ever Hearing, Seeing﴾ – its i'rab is clear.

Allah says: ﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world﴾, meaning its recompense, its enjoyments and its splendour, then he has missed a great deal of good, because he has been deprived of what is with Allah of the reward of both this world and the Hereafter. For this reason He did not say, "Whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him from it," as is stated in another verse: ﴿We give him of it, but he has in the Hereafter no share﴾ [Ash-Shura 20]. Rather, the answer came contrary to what the listener would expect, meaning: it is as if he has gained nothing.

This verse has many parallels: whoever desires this world, both this world and the Hereafter escape him. Does he then attain what he desires of this world?

The answer: No, because of Allah's saying: ﴿Whoever desires the immediate [life], We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We intend. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will enter, blameworthy and rejected. And whoever desires the Hereafter and exerts the effort due to it while he is a believer - those are the ones whose effort is appreciated﴾ [Al-Isra 18-19]. Then, does the one who desires the Hereafter lose this world? No. For this reason the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his harvest; and whoever desires the harvest of this world, We give him thereof, but he has in the Hereafter no share﴾ [Ash-Shura 20].

So whoever desires the Hereafter, this world does not escape him; whoever desires this world, both this world and the Hereafter may escape him; and if this world comes to him, he is given only what is written for him, not everything he wants. This is the outcome regarding intentions. As for one who desires both this world and the Hereafter together, do we say that he is between two ranks? Or do we say that he attains the reward of the second rank, which is desiring the Hereafter? Here we say: which of the two predominates in one who desires both? If the Hereafter predominates, he attains the reward of both this world and the Hereafter; if this world predominates, his reward of the Hereafter is reduced by the measure of what he intended of the Hereafter. Yes, by the measure of what he intended of the Hereafter: if he intended the whole Hereafter, he obtains the whole reward; if he intended part of it, he obtains less.

The hadiths also bear witness to this. On the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Actions are only by intentions, and every person will have only what he intended. Whoever's migration was to Allah and His Messenger, his migration is to Allah and His Messenger; and whoever's migration was for worldly gain he would acquire or a woman he would marry, his migration is to what he migrated for."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1), and Muslim (1907/155), from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

Thus we find that those who desire this world are sometimes granted success in this world and attain their aim or part of it, and sometimes they do not attain it and are poorer than the Muslims.

And the Mighty and Majestic's saying: ﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world, with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter﴾ means that he has missed what he desires, because in reality he may be given what he wants or part of it, but even if it is given, it will not last; rather he will die or lose what he was given.

﴿And Allah is ever Hearing, Seeing﴾ means that this name is established in an eternal and everlasting manner, indeed these two names, the Hearing and the Seeing, and what they include of attributes, namely hearing and sight.

It has already passed us that hearing attributed to Allah the Exalted is divided into two types, and many subdivisions branch from these two types; I think we need not lengthen by repeating what has preceded.

* This noble verse contains several benefits. First: the linking of reward and recompense to intention, by His saying: ﴿Whoever desires﴾. On this basis, a person must purify his intention completely, and must not intend in acts of the Hereafter anything but the Hereafter; as for acts of this world, they are for this world.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the refutation of the Jabriyyah, by affirming volition for the servant. The Jabriyyah say that the servant has no will and is compelled in his actions, so he has no volition; this verse and others refute them.

* Among them: clarifying the lowliness of the rank of this world before Allah the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason He said: ﴿with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter﴾. Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) said in his Nuniyyah:

"Were the world to equal the wing of a gnat, He would not have given its water to the one who disbelieves; but it is, by Allah, more contemptible in His sight than the wing of a flying creature that cannot fly."

Meaning: if the world were worth the wing of a gnat, Allah would not have given a drop of it to any disbeliever, nor bestowed anything upon them for their disbelief; but they enjoy it because it is nothing in Allah's sight, whether His allies or His enemies enjoy it. This is the reality: if this world is not a means to the Hereafter, there is no good in it, and even if a person is pampered in it, that pleasure is a hell. For this reason you find the people most afflicted with burning, grief, sorrow and anxiety are the people of this world. Do not be deceived by what they have of clothing, palaces, luxury, cars and other things; by Allah, their hearts are in a worse state than the poorest of the Muslims. For this reason some of the Salaf said: "If the kings and the sons of kings knew what we are in, they would fight us over it with swords."[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Zuhd al-Kabir (1/81).]]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the one who gives reward is Allah the Mighty and Majestic, not anyone else: ﴿with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter﴾.

Following from this principle: in what we hope for of the reward of this world and the Hereafter, we should rely on none but whom? None but our Lord the Mighty and Majestic, for He is the one in whose hand the affairs are. The Messenger (ﷺ) even said to his cousin Abdullah ibn Abbas: "Know that if the whole nation gathered to benefit you with something, they would not benefit you except with what Allah has already written for you."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2516) from the hadith of Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both).]]

* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of the Hereafter. We did not say "the affirmation of this world", why? Because it is not needed; if we said "the affirmation of this world, the reward of this world", it would be of the category of idle speech: "The sky is above us and the earth beneath us," and:

"As if we, with water all around us, are a people sitting around whom is water."

May Allah reward him with good for this great benefit!

Yes, I say: this verse indicates what we have mentioned, the affirmation of the Hereafter, that it is coming and inevitable, and that it is the goal of every living being. For this reason we must feel that we in this world are travellers, exactly like a traveller, indeed quicker than a traveller; for the traveller journeys and rests, descends, sleeps, relaxes, lets his camels rest; but the living person in this world never rests: he is travelling by night and day, standing, sitting, lying down, moving in every state. So we must make ourselves feel this, lest we take it as a homeland. And among the blessings of Allah the Exalted upon man, upon all the servants, is that He has not made the bliss of this world complete, but has made it troubled, so that a person does not take it as a permanent abode and homeland; rather he knows it is not a place of settlement: its purity is turbid, its comfort is toil. By this we say: the Hereafter is the more important.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, namely: the Hearing and the Seeing, and the affirmation of what follows from them of attributes, namely:

* Student: Hearing and sight.

* The Shaykh: And the affirmation of what follows from them of effect?

* Student: That Allah the Exalted hears and sees.

* The Shaykh: That Allah hears and sees; meaning He is not Hearing without hearing, nor possessing sight without seeing, nor possessing hearing without hearing.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 135 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Most High said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. Who is addressed? All the believers, and we, God willing, are among them. So the address is directed to us and to everyone else who believes: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. Know that God Most High opening the address with a call (nida') indicates its importance, because a call draws the listener's attention and makes him turn toward the one calling: "What do you want?" ﴿O you who have believed﴾.

Then know that restricting the call to the believers indicates that they are the people fit for this address, because they are believers who carry out God's command when it is a command, abstain from His prohibition when it is a prohibition, and take on His character when it is a character. So they are worthy of being addressed. Faith is honor enough, that God directs His address to those who possess it: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. It is a great honor that the Lord of the worlds addresses you with ﴿O you who have believed﴾.

Also, its restriction to the believers indicates that what is mentioned is among the requirements of faith, and that opposing it diminishes faith.

﴿O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah﴾. ﴿Qawwamin﴾ (persistently standing firm) is on the pattern fa''alin, meaning it is an intensive form (sigha mubalagha). It may also be taken in the sense of attribution, i.e., "those possessing qawwama (steadfast uprightness)": ﴿persistently standing firm in justice﴾. And qist is justice, as God Most High said: ﴿and those who order justice among the people﴾ [Al 'Imran 21]. So qist is justice. And iqsat?

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Is it oppression (jawr) or injustice (zulm)?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Oppression (jawr). What is your evidence?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Iqsat? Qist means justice, correct? And as for aqsata, what does it mean?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Aqsata means "he acted justly," and qasata means "he acted unjustly." That is why, for the first, the active participle comes on the pattern mufqil: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly﴾ [al-Ma'ida 42]. And the active participle of the second comes on the pattern fa'il: ﴿And as for the unjust, they will be fuel for Hell﴾ [al-Jinn 15]. ﴿Witnesses with justice﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the subject of ﴿persistently standing firm﴾. It may also be a second predicate for His saying ﴿be﴾, but the circumstantial reading is preferable.

﴿Witnesses for Allah﴾: that is, you bear witness to justice for the sake of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Let neither show-off (riya'), nor reputation (sum'a), nor worldly gain, nor anything else move you to this. Be witnesses for Allah alone, as in His saying: ﴿and establish testimony for Allah﴾ [al-Talaq 2].

﴿Even if it be against yourselves﴾. Is bearing witness against oneself possible? Yes indeed. Bear witness against yourself before He bears witness against you. Witness against oneself is confession: that a person says, "I did such-and-such, and I did such-and-such, and I did such-and-such." This witness against oneself is confession. ﴿Or parents﴾: that is, the mother and the father. Even against the mother and the father, bear witness. But will the mother become upset? Even if she becomes upset? Because the pleasure of Allah takes precedence over the pleasure of the parents. ﴿And relatives﴾, such as brothers, sons, grandfathers, paternal uncles, maternal uncles, aunts, and relatives who are not the closest; that is included a fortiori. But Allah specified this explicitly because the self may incline toward them and so not bear witness with justice: ﴿even if it be against yourselves, or parents and relatives﴾.

Then Subhanahu wa Ta'ala pointed out an important matter that might influence testimony for or against the one concerned, and said: ﴿whether he is rich or poor﴾. Who is meant: the one testified against or the one testified for? ﴿Whether he is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both﴾. This is because some people bear witness for the rich because of his wealth, or for the poor because of his poverty, or bear witness against the rich because of his wealth or against the poor for some reason. So Allah commanded us to bear witness against these people even if the person is rich or poor, because their affair is up to their Creator, the Mighty and Majestic. That is why He said: ﴿Allah is more worthy of both﴾. Do not be concerned; do not say, "I will testify for the poor because he is poor and needy and has a family." We say: Allah's guardianship of them is better than your testimony.

Then He said: ﴿So do not follow [your] desire﴾, do not follow desire, meaning the desire of the self, which is a person's inclination toward what contradicts the Shari'a. This is the blameworthy desire: that a person inclines toward what contradicts the Shari'a. He says: ﴿do not follow desire﴾.

And His saying: ﴿lest you deviate﴾. Or is it: ﴿if you deviate﴾?

* The students: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes. Not as we have it ﴿lest you deviate﴾. Does the meaning here mean "out of dislike that you should act justly" or "for the sake of your acting justly"?
* Student: The first.
* Shaykh: No one wants to dislike justice. But when God commanded testimony against oneself, parents and relatives, and explained that God is the One who takes care of everyone, and forbade following desire, He said: ﴿lest you deviate﴾, meaning: if you want justice, do not follow desire. On this basis it is permissible to say that the estimate is "out of dislike that you should act justly," meaning: we commanded you, or forbade you, from following desire out of dislike that you should act justly, or for the sake of your acting justly?
* The students: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes (...). It does not allow this reading; it means "for the sake of your acting justly." Justice is uprightness, and what is meant by it in matters of rulings is judging by what the Book and the Sunnah indicate.

﴿And if you distort [testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾. ﴿If you distort﴾: that is, you deviate in testimony, so you add to it, subtract from it, or refuse to give testimony so that you do not deliver it. This is the threat: ﴿indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾. And what happens when Allah is acquainted with what we do? Recompense. This is among the most severe threats, because whoever knows that Allah is acquainted with his deeds will never dare oppose the command of Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

* Student: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing﴾. This verse often comes up for us, and we say that the ﴿kana﴾ (was) here is stripped of time. Is this an initial misconception, or does Arabic have this usage?
* Shaykh: No, Arabic has this usage. For example: "So-and-so was hospitable," to establish that he is generous and hosts people.
* Student: (...) the verse with His saying: ﴿lest you deviate﴾, so the estimate would be: "Do not follow your desire (...)"?
* Shaykh: Good.
* Student: Some shaykhs interpret whatever is mentioned, any statement, neither praise nor blame.
* Shaykh: What?
* Student: They do not mention in their tafsir, I mean some of them interpret the Qur'an and mention only his own words. They do not say "Ibn Kathir said" or "Shaykh al-Islam said" or "so-and-so said." Even the Prophet ﷺ, the tafsir of the Companions from the Prophet ﷺ, they do not mention it (...).
* Shaykh: Mufassirun (commentators) divide into two kinds: those who interpret by reasoning (tafsir bil-nazar) and those who interpret by transmitted reports (tafsir bil-athar). The one who interprets by transmitted reports must mention the reports, such as, at their head, Muhammad ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him. The one who interprets by reasoning interprets according to what his reasoning requires.
* Student: Meaning according to what he sees?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. But that does not mean that his tafsir is necessarily invalid.

* Student: ﴿And even if it be against yourselves﴾ [al-Nisa' 135]. O Shaykh, may Allah reward you well, "law" (even if) is a conditional particle. What is its protasis (fi'l al-shart) and apodosis (jawab)?
* Shaykh: Has this come up before, O people? (...)? This came up before, and we said that the correct view is that it does not need an apodosis.
* Student: And it was, O Shaykh, a verb...
* Shaykh: This is not a problem. "Even if it were against yourselves" is not a problem.
* Student: ﴿And even if it be against yourselves﴾.
* Shaykh: The prepositional phrase is attached to an omitted element.
* Student: And its apodosis?
* Shaykh: As for the apodosis, it was said that the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The estimate: "Even if it were against yourselves, then be persistently standing firm," and the correct view is that it does not need one.
* Student: In His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if you distort [testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾ [al-Nisa' 135]. His saying: ﴿then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾: is it the response of the condition, or is the response omitted and this takes its place?
* Shaykh: No. The correct view is that it is not omitted. The ruling is derived from such passages as His saying: ﴿except for those who repent before you have power over them. So know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ma'ida 34].
* Student: May Allah be good to you. Many usuliyyun (scholars of the principles of jurisprudence) argue, or take as evidence, the saying of Allah: ﴿O you who have believed﴾ [al-Baqara 104], that the disbelievers are not addressed (...)?
* Shaykh: This is simple. We answer him with His saying in many verses: ﴿O mankind﴾ [al-Baqara 21]. And restricting some individuals of a general term does not indicate restriction of the whole.
* Student: We said that aqsata means "acted justly," as in His saying: ﴿And if they return, then make settlement between them with justice and act justly﴾ [al-Hujurat 9]. Here, is there synonymy between "fa'dilu" (be just) and "aqsitu" (act justly)?
* Shaykh: Where is the synonymy?
* Student: ﴿And if they return, then make settlement between them with justice﴾ [al-Hujurat 9], and "be just"?
* Shaykh: Yes, this is reconciliation (sulh).
* Student: How does it say it, I mean?
* Shaykh: Does repetition prevent establishing the ruling? Because the matter is serious. We cannot imagine how it would be when two large groups of believers fight, and one of them transgresses against the other. It is a grave matter, so emphasis is necessary.

* * *

The saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah﴾. What is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits﴾?
This is interrogation.
* Student: That is: none is better.
* Shaykh: That is: none is better.
* Student: When interrogation carries the meaning of negation...
* Shaykh: That is, it is an interrogation with the meaning of negation.
Why is one turned away from expressing it by negation, which is the original form, to interrogation?
* Student: Because it is more forceful, since it conveys a challenge.
* Shaykh: More forceful in what?
* Student: In meaning.
* Shaykh: What is the meaning here?
* Student: That none is better.
* Shaykh: That is, more forceful in negation. As if the speaker challenges the addressee, saying: "Show me something better." And on what is His saying ﴿religion﴾ put in the accusative?
* Student: As a specifier (tamyiz) for ﴿better﴾.
* Shaykh: As a specifier for ﴿better﴾. Can we derive from this a rule that whatever is put in the accusative after "better" (af'al al-tafdil) is a specifier?
* Student: Every accusative after the comparative form (af'al al-tafdil) is in the accusative of specification.
* Shaykh: If it clarifies it, correct? Good. May Allah bless you.

﴿And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance﴾ [al-Nisa' 130]. Does this sentence encourage separation, or what?
* Student: Yes indeed. Because Allah, glorified and exalted, explained that if they separate, Allah, glorified and exalted, will enrich each of them from His abundance, meaning if...
* Shaykh: But is it to encourage separation, or to console at the time of separation?
* Student: To console at the time of separation.
* Shaykh: Have you retracted the first view?
* Student: No. If the situation between the spouses becomes difficult, then separation is better than... Yes indeed.
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. We did not understand anything!
* Student: Warding off despair.
* Shaykh: Yes, that is: so console them at the time of separation. But if someone said that it is encouragement to separation?
* Student: O Shaykh, it may be said: it is encouragement to separation for whoever cannot live together. That is, between the spouses, if living and companionship in goodness becomes impossible, then at that time...
* Shaykh: That means: if each of them desires separation, then this...?
* Student: Then it is better for them to separate.
* Shaykh: It is better that they separate.
* Student: And it is an encouragement to them...
* Shaykh: To separation.
* Student: Separation in a situation where living together is not possible, where their being together is, for example, something that...
* Shaykh: Increases the matter in severity.
* Student: Yes. Then they are encouraged to separate, and this is contrary to the Christians.
* Shaykh: We have not yet reached the matter of disagreement and agreement! The point is, in any case, the verse can bear this and that, meaning according to the situation?
* Student: Just so.
* Shaykh: If both of them have regretted, or one of them has regretted, or fears the breaking of the bonds between them, then it is said: Allah, glorified and exalted, has decreed separation; but He promises you both that He will enrich each of you from His abundance. But if separation is good, then it is an encouragement to separation. So the verse here depends on the situation.

* Student: ﴿And We will drive him into Hell﴾ [al-Nisa' 115].
* Shaykh: And ﴿nuwallihi﴾.
* Student: And ﴿nuwallihi﴾ likewise.
* Shaykh: ﴿We will leave him to what he has turned to, and drive him into Hell﴾ [al-Nisa' 115]. This is the sukun (pausal vowel reduction) for lightening.

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret conversation, except for one who orders charity or what is right or reconciliation between people﴾ [al-Nisa' 114]. ﴿Except for one who orders﴾: is the one who orders part of the secret conversation, so that the exception is valid? "Except for one who orders," meaning there is no good in much of their conversation except for one who orders. How can the person be excepted from the meaning?
* Student: Because the person orders the meaning.
* Shaykh: No, the person is the person; ﴿man﴾ is a relative pronoun.
* Student: So it is "except for one who orders something": except for one who orders charity or what is right; he orders charity or what is right.
* Another student: If we interpret the secret conversation as meaning "those conversing privately," then the exception is according to the basic sense. But if we interpret the secret conversation as a verbal noun, then the estimate here is "except a secret conversation of one who orders..."
* Shaykh: Or "a conversation about the command." If we say that the secret conversation here is the name of those conversing privately, then the exception stays as it is, since it is an exception of a person from a person.
But if we make the secret conversation here from the verb, which is conversing privately, then the estimate is "except a secret conversation of one who orders charity."
His saying: ﴿except for one who orders charity﴾ implies that whoever orders charity, in his command there is good in any case, although the secret conversation other than the command to charity and what is mentioned with it is largely not good.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: Now, the secret conversation of the children of Adam, the speech of the children of Adam: there is no good in much of them.
* Student: Except for one who orders charity, or what is right, or reconciliation between people.
* Shaykh: So every command to charity contains good?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Good. Does every command to what is right contain good?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Does every reconciliation between people contain good?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Correct. Then what is the benefit of His saying: ﴿And whoever does that seeking the approval of Allah, We will give him a great reward﴾ [al-Nisa' 114]?
* Student: Because ordering charity, ordering what is right, and reconciling between people has beneficial effects that extend to others.
* Shaykh: So it is good.
* Student: It is good in itself. If he seeks the face of Allah, the good for him increases; otherwise the benefit remains extending to others.
* Shaykh: Yes. The goodness remains in the extended benefit; if that is seeking the approval of Allah, the reward increases. May Allah bless you.

Does the verse imply that it is preferable to speak little?

* Student: Yes, because "there is no good in much of their secret talk."
* Shaykh: Well done.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan. ﴿O you who believe, believe in God and His Messenger, and the Scripture He sent down to His Messenger, and the Scripture He sent down before. Whoever disbelieves in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly strayed far astray. Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief, God will not forgive them nor guide them to a way. Give good tidings to the hypocrites that there is a painful punishment for them. Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek honor with them? Indeed, all honor belongs to God.﴾ [an-Nisa' 136-139].
* Shaykh: Well done. I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan. God, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, believe in God and His Messenger.﴾ The benefits (of this verse). No, let us begin. From where? We begin with the benefits of the previous verse, and we ask God for inspiration and success. God the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, be steadfast in upholding justice, witnesses for God.﴾ [an-Nisa' 135].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation to uphold testimony, based on His saying: ﴿be steadfast in upholding justice, witnesses for God.﴾
* Among its benefits: the obligation to be just in it, neither increasing nor decreasing it, and not refusing to give it when it is needed, because all of this is included in His saying: ﴿steadfast (qawwamin).﴾
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: justice is obligatory in giving testimony, and among it is what is mentioned in His saying: ﴿even if it be against yourselves.﴾
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an indication of sincerity in giving testimony, based on His saying: ﴿witnesses for God.﴾ So do not think that testimony is merely testimony for another or against another. No, seek it as a means of drawing near to God, Mighty and Majestic, sincere to Him in complying with His command to give it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of acknowledgment (iqrar, admitting a right) upon one who owes a right, based on His saying: ﴿even if it be against yourselves.﴾ So a person must acknowledge the right that he owes, even if it is bitter.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that acknowledgment is a form of testimony, based on His saying: ﴿even if it be against yourselves.﴾ This is because a person in reality either attributes a thing to himself, or against himself, or to another against another.
These are three types: either he attributes a thing to himself, or against himself, or to another against another.
The first is a claim (da'wa). If he attributes a thing to himself, he says: "This is mine," or "I am claiming from you one hundred riyals," or the like. This is a claim that requires evidence (bayyina) and a method of judgment according to what the Sharia requires.
Or he attributes a thing against himself, and this is acknowledgment, such as saying: "I owe so-and-so such-and-such."
Or he attributes a thing to another against another, and this is testimony, where he testifies for a person against another. All of these are considered testimony.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation to testify against parents and close relatives in what binds them, based on His saying: ﴿whether it be against parents or relatives.﴾ Accordingly, is the testimony of a child against his parents accepted? And is it accepted for them, for the parents?
On this there is a difference among the scholars:
