Some of them said: it is not accepted, closing the door and averting suspicion.
Others made a distinction, saying: if it is known that the parents are people of piety and righteousness, and that they will not claim what is not theirs, and that the child is also of great piety and trustworthiness, then testimony for the parents is accepted, because the cause, which is suspicion, is absent in such a case.
But most scholars, in my opinion, hold that a person's testimony for his parents is rejected, closing the door, and because the measure of trustworthiness or untrustworthiness is a difficult matter.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: God, glorified and exalted, forbade favoritism toward the rich or the poor. From where? 
* Student: ﴿If he is rich or poor, God is more entitled to both of them.﴾
* Shaykh: Among its benefits: God, glorified and exalted, is the Protector of everyone, so do not favor anyone because of his wealth or his poverty, for God is the Protector of all.
From here we derive the jurisprudence of what is related about Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, may God have mercy on him, when he was asked: "Will you not bequeath to your children?" He said: "I will not bequeath to them. If my children are righteous, then God protects the righteous, and His protection of them is better than my protection. If they are not righteous, I will not help them in their wickedness." This is from his jurisprudence, may God have mercy on him, in contrast to what people do now, favoring relatives, children, and parents, even if they are among the most wicked of God's servants.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the prohibition of what is called socialism (al-ishtirakiyya), because the advocates of socialism, and praise be to God that their fire has been extinguished, say: "We want to show mercy to the poor by taking from the wealth of the rich and giving it to the poor out of compassion for them." It is said in reply: God is more entitled to him than you are. God, Mighty and Majestic, has wisdom in making some people poor and others rich, and God indicated this in His saying: ﴿And We raised some of them above others in degrees, so that some of them may take others in service.﴾ [az-Zukhruf 32].
﴿in service (sukhriyyan)﴾ means that some of them make others serve them. For if people were all equal, affairs would not be set right. Who would build your house if all people were rich? And who would build your house if they were all poor, since you would have nothing to build with? So God, Mighty and Majestic, has wisdom in the difference of classes. Yet He did not neglect the rights of the poor. He made zakat obligatory, made the relief of need obligatory, made the maintenance of relatives obligatory, made the maintenance of spouses obligatory, and the like. All of this meets the needs of many of the poor.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the prohibition of following desire that opposes justice, based on His saying: ﴿So do not follow desire, lest you deviate from justice.﴾ Desire is not blamed absolutely, nor praised absolutely. If desire follows what the Messenger brought, it is praiseworthy. If it opposes it, it is blameworthy. This is why He said: ﴿Do not follow desire lest you deviate from justice,﴾ meaning: lest you be averse to being just.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a warning against injustice, based on His saying: ﴿lest you deviate from justice.﴾ This includes every situation in which justice is required. For example, it includes justice between children in giving gifts and other than gifts, to the extent that the early generations (salaf) would be just between their children in kissing (al-qubul, kissing). That is, if he kissed one child, he would kiss the other. It also includes justice between wives, justice between two litigants before a judge, and the like.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a warning to one who turns away from giving testimony and justice, or distorts it, based on His saying: ﴿And if you distort or turn away, then indeed God is ever, of what you do, Acquainted.﴾
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the comprehensive knowledge and awareness of God, based on His saying: ﴿of what you do, Acquainted.﴾ For the word (ما, ma) here is a relative pronoun (ism mawsul) that includes everything that the children of Adam do.
* And among its benefits: a warning against opposing God, because every believer who knows that God is aware of his deeds must avoid what would cause punishment and seek what would cause reward.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 136:

The words of the Most High: ﴿O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾ [An-Nisa 136]. Whenever you see an address beginning with ﴿O you who have believed﴾, pay attention to it, as is related from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "When you hear Allah say: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, then give it your ear, for it is either good that you are commanded to do, or evil that you are forbidden from."[[Az-Zuhd by Ibn al-Mubarak (1/12) and Hilyat al-Awliya' (1/130), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]]

We have already mentioned the benefits of opening an address with ﴿O you who have believed﴾, so there is no need to repeat them, since they are well known.

As for His words: ﴿O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾, someone may say: how can He say ﴿O you who have believed﴾ and then say ﴿believe﴾, when commanding something already present is vain? Addressing them as believers and then commanding them to believe seems to be a command to something that already exists?

It is said: No, this understanding is mistaken. What is meant by His words ﴿believe﴾ is: make your belief true and firm, and persist in it. Thus the command to believe in His words ﴿believe﴾ is a command with two matters:

The first: making the belief true, i.e., striving to perfect it in every respect.

The second: steadfastness upon it, for how many a believer slips and falls short.

As for His words ﴿in Allah and His Messenger﴾, the Messenger here refers to Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him), as shown by what follows.

So what is belief in Allah?

We mentioned belief in Allah earlier, and there is no harm in repeating it now: belief in Allah includes four matters: belief in His existence, belief in His lordship, belief in His divinity, and belief in His names and attributes. Whoever denies any one of these has not believed in Allah.

Belief in the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) includes believing that he is truly the Messenger of Allah, and that he brought the truth, so one believes him in what he reports, obeys his command in what he commands, and refrains from what he forbids and warns against.

﴿And the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger﴾. What is meant here is the Qur'an. ﴿And the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger﴾; He expressed its revelation with the word ﴿sent down﴾ because it was revealed piece by piece, as the Most High said: ﴿And [it is] a Qur'an which We have separated [in revelation] that you might recite it to the people over a prolonged period. And We have sent it down in stages﴾ [Al-Isra 106].

﴿And the Book which He sent down before﴾. Here "the Book" (al-kitab) is a generic noun, and the definite article (al) is for comprehensiveness, i.e., every book sent down before. He expressed the earlier scriptures with the word ﴿sent down﴾ because they were sent down all at once.

Belief in the Book of Allah means that you believe it is truly from Allah, that what it contains of reports is true, what it contains of rulings is just, and that it is dominant over the earlier scriptures and abrogates them.

Belief in the Book sent down before means that you believe every messenger to whom Allah sent a book, and that you believe in the books specifically named, such as the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the scrolls of Abraham and Moses, and that you believe they are from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that you believe in whatever report in them is authentically established.

We restricted it to whatever report in them is authentically established, because distortion, alteration, and change have entered them. As for rulings, you are not commanded to follow them except where your Sharia commands you.

The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, have differed concerning the law of those before us: is it a law for us, or is it not a law?

The verified position is that it is a law for us, based on the Most High's words: ﴿So follow their guidance﴾ [Al-An'am 90], unless our Sharia has come with something contrary to it, in which case it is abrogated. Moreover, acting upon the rulings in the books that are now in the hands of the People of the Book is not safe, because they have distorted, altered, and changed them.

Then He said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly strayed far astray﴾. How many of these are the pillars of faith?

Five. The remaining pillar, belief in divine decree, is mentioned in other verses. Whoever disbelieves in Allah, by denying Him, or denies what is established for Him of rights, names, or attributes, has strayed far astray. Likewise whoever disbelieves in the angels.

The angels are an unseen world that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created to carry out His obedience, and He assigned them duties, each according to what the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, requires. They are nobler, stronger, and greater than the jinn, for "the Prophet ﷺ saw Gabriel in his true form, which he was created in, having six hundred wings, which filled the horizon."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3232) and Muslim (174/282) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, without the words "which filled the horizon."]]

This is a great thing. The ifrit of the jinn said to Solomon: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place﴾ [An-Naml 39], and the angel brought it before his glance returned to him. This is stronger and greater.

Among the angels are those we know by their individual names, such as Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, Malik the keeper of the Fire, and Ridwan, the keeper of Paradise, if it is authentically established, and Munkar and Nakir, if it is authentically established; they are the two who question a person when he is buried.

As for 'Azra'il, it is not authentically established, though it is famous among the common people as the sun is famous at midday. So who is he?

The angel of death is called 'Azra'il by the common people, and this name is better known among them than the name Gabriel; but it has not been authentically reported from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) that he bore this name.

We also believe in what we know of their works and attributes. We know that Gabriel (peace be upon him) is entrusted with revelation, in which is the life of spirits and hearts; that Israfil is entrusted with blowing the trumpet, in which is the life of the Hereafter when he blows into the trumpet and the spirits come out to return to their bodies; and Michael is entrusted with rain and plants, in which is the life of the earth.

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to begin the night prayer with the words: "O Allah, Lord of Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil,"[[Narrated by Muslim (770/200) from the hadith of 'A'isha.]] because each of these three angels has a specific kind of life. We are now at the beginning of the day, and the beginning of the day after sleep is considered a new life, as the Most High said: ﴿It is He who takes you in death by night and knows what you have committed by day. Then He revives you therein﴾ [Al-An'am 60].

Likewise the books; belief in the books has already been explained.

The messengers: we also believe in the messengers of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in general and in particular. For those whom we know by name, we believe in them specifically; not all the messengers are known to us, as the saying of Allah, Blessed and Most High, indicates: ﴿And messengers We have related to you before, and messengers We have not related to you﴾ [An-Nisa 164]. ﴿And We certainly sent messengers before you; among them are those We related to you, and among them are those We did not relate to you﴾ [Ghafir 78]. However, we believe in them in general.

As for those specifically named, we believe in them individually. And how do we believe in them?

We believe that they are messengers of Allah, that they are truthful in what they reported about Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that they were sent to their peoples, and that they conveyed the message. Therefore, on the Day of Resurrection they will be called as witnesses for themselves and against their nations, as the Most High said: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [Al-Baqarah 143].

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿and the Last Day﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection. It is called the Last Day because it is a day after which there is no other day.

The worldly life has three stages: the stage of the embryo, the stage of life, and the stage of the barzakh; and the fourth is the end, the stage of resurrection. For this reason it is called the Last Day.

﴿has certainly strayed far astray﴾: this is the answer to the condition. The condition of whom? ﴿has certainly strayed far astray﴾, and has entered distant wildernesses, because these matters are manifest, so denying and rejecting them is far astray and a remote place.

* The noble verse contains benefits:

* First: the obligation of steadfastness upon faith, from His words: ﴿O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾ to the end.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse also: the obligation of perfecting faith, based on His words ﴿believe﴾ meaning: persist and make faith true by perfecting it.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation of believing in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, His Messenger, and His Book, from His words: ﴿Believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the Qur'an is sent down, from His words: ﴿the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger﴾.

Concerning Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, it indicates that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, since it was sent down from Him, so it is His speech.

And the exaltedness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, also, from His words ﴿sent down﴾, since sending down is from above to below. All of this is well known in the creed you have studied, praise be to Allah, and there is no need to elaborate on it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Qur'an was sent down upon Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him), from His words ﴿upon His Messenger﴾. And where does its descent end? In the heart of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), as the Most High said: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara 193-194]. It settled in the heart of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), he memorized it and explained it, and not a single letter escaped him, as the Most High said: ﴿So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation. Then upon Us is its clarification﴾ [Al-Qiyamah 18-19].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the noble Qur'an was sent down in portions, from His words: ﴿sent down upon His Messenger﴾. We cited the noble verse: ﴿And [it is] a Qur'an which We have separated [in revelation] that you might recite it to the people over a prolonged period. And We have sent it down in stages﴾ [Al-Isra 106].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of believing in the earlier books, from the Most High's words: ﴿And the Book which He sent down before﴾.

So if someone said: "I believe in the Qur'an, but the Torah and the Gospel were not sent down to our Messenger, so I will not believe in them"?

We say: you are now a disbeliever, an apostate, because you must believe in the Book sent down before, as Allah has commanded you.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that this noble Qur'an is the seal of the books; from where are they taken? ﴿which He sent down before﴾, and He did not say "after," indicating that there is no book after this noble Qur'an.

* Following from this benefit: there is no messenger after Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him), because if it were established that there was a messenger after him, it would necessitate that a book be sent down to him.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a warning against disbelief, from His words: ﴿has certainly strayed far astray﴾.

* Among its benefits: that partial faith is not valid, meaning believing in some and disbelieving in others, from His words: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly strayed far astray﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation of believing in what is mentioned, which are five of the six pillars of faith.

* Among its benefits: the obligation of believing in everything Allah reports, or His Messenger reports, concerning what will happen on the Last Day; for belief in the Last Day is not merely believing that it will occur, but believing in everything that takes place in it, as come in the Book and the Sunnah. Indeed Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: among what is included in belief in the Last Day is belief in everything the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) reported that happens after death.

Thus he made belief in the punishment of the grave part of belief in the Last Day, and his saying is true, because whoever dies has finished with the world and has entered the Last Day.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that misguidance varies, some of it being worse than others, from His words: ﴿has certainly strayed far astray﴾. So there is misguidance that is not far, and it is so; misguidance varies, faith varies, and deeds vary: ﴿And for each are degrees according to what they did﴾ [Al-An'am 132]. For example, the genus of the obligatory is better than the genus of the recommended; the obligatory prayer is better than its supererogatory counterpart; reciting al-Fatihah is better than reciting the surah after it, because al-Fatihah is a pillar and what follows it is not a pillar; fasting Ramadan is better than voluntary fasting at any time, and so on.

The genus of the obligatory is better than what, than the genus of the supererogatory? The evidence for this is the words of Allah in the sacred hadith: "My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (6502) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]] Then the genera of deeds differ: some are pillars of Islam, some are emphasized, some are less than that, and some are not pillars of Islam at all. So the deeds of the people of goodness and the deeds of the people of evil all vary, and upon this variation is built the variation of faith and the variation of wickedness: this one is stronger in faith and that one weaker, and this one's wickedness is greater and that one's less. The perpetrator of a major sin is greater in wickedness than the perpetrator of a minor sin when he commits it. This is the principle upon which Ahl as-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah rest: that deeds vary, and that doers differ, whether in righteousness or in evil.

Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and then disbelieved, then believed and then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief﴾ [An-Nisa 137].

How many times did faith occur among them?

* Students: Twice.

* The Shaykh: Twice. And disbelief?

* Students: Three times.

* The Shaykh: Three times. These people believed, they entered into faith, but faith did not settle in their hearts, so they apostatized, and we seek Allah's refuge. ﴿They believed, then disbelieved﴾, because faith did not settle in the heart. Had faith settled in their hearts, they would not have disbelieved. But it did not settle, and we seek Allah's refuge. As the Most High said: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers﴾ [Al-Baqarah 8]. ﴿Then they believed, then disbelieved﴾. Notice the vacillation: after they disbelieved the first time following belief, they believed again, and then they disbelieved and increased in disbelief, we ask Allah for well-being, because of their toying with the religion. The final disbelief became graver than what preceded it, because they are players and vacillators; they do not remain firm on any decision. The Most High said: ﴿Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path﴾. This is the predicate of (inna): "Indeed, those who disbelieved, ﴿Allah will not...﴾".

Here ﴿lam yakun﴾ is a negated present verb, and the lam in His words ﴿liyaghfira lahum﴾ is called the lam of negation or the lam of denial (lam al-juhud). According to some grammarians it is superfluous (za'idah), and according to others it is not superfluous. Those who say it is superfluous say the sense is: "Allah would not forgive them." Those who say it is not superfluous say that ﴿lam yakun Allahu liyaghfira lahum﴾ is based on an implied will, meaning He did not will their forgiveness. Whichever view is taken, in His words ﴿lam yakun Allahu liyaghfira lahum﴾ there is despair for them regarding forgiveness, and we seek Allah's refuge, and that they will remain upon their disbelief until the day they meet Him.

﴿Nor will He guide them to a path﴾. ﴿Sabilan﴾ means a way. To good or to evil? To good. Allah cannot guide them to a path of good. In the verse at the end of the surah: ﴿Nor will He guide them to a way, except the way of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ [An-Nisa 168-169], He said this of those who disbelieved and wronged.

So for those in whom this happened, Allah has closed off the door of forgiveness and the door of mercy: the door of forgiveness in His words ﴿lam yakun Allahu liyaghfira lahum﴾, and the door of mercy in His words ﴿wa la liyahdiyahum sabilan﴾.

* A student: Does this noble verse ﴿O you who believe, believe﴾ yield another benefit, namely that faith increases and decreases?

* The Shaykh: Perhaps it can be taken from it that faith increases and decreases. We said: ﴿Believe﴾ means: remain steadfast in faith and realize it.

* The student: So it increases in faith?

* The Shaykh: Yes.

* A student: Does the far-off misguidance apply to everyone who disbelieves in these four, or in one of them?

* The Shaykh: The far-off misguidance applies to everyone who disbelieves in the four or in one of them, because one who believes in some and disbelieves in others is like one who disbelieves in all, as the Most High said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and want to differentiate between Allah and His messengers, and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and want to adopt a way between that. They are the disbelievers in truth﴾ [An-Nisa 150-151].

* A student: Shaykh, some say that if a Muslim apostatizes, he is asked to repent; if he repents and then apostatizes again...

* The Shaykh: We have not reached the rulings.

* A student: Shaykh, Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, applied the name of disbelief to whoever disbelieves in Him, and we said, O Shaykh, that disbelieving in Allah includes disbelieving in His attributes, and many people, O Shaykh, disbelieve in Allah's attributes. Is it correct to apply the name of disbelief...?

* The Shaykh: Disbelief regarding Allah's attributes is of two types: disbelief of denial (takdhib) and disbelief of interpretation (ta'wil). More precisely, denying Allah's attributes divides into two parts: denial by interpretation and denial by rejection. As for denial by rejection, it is disbelief, because it is a rejection of the report. For example, if one says regarding the Most High's words ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha 5]: "Allah did not establish Himself upon the Throne," this person is a disbelieving apostate. Why?

* A student: He denied the istiwa'.

* The Shaykh: Because he denied the report. But if he says ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ and means "established" in the sense of "gained control," this is denial by interpretation. This is not disbelief unless he interprets it in a way that cannot be sustained as a meaning. Do you understand?

* A student: Does it necessarily follow from Allah sending a messenger that a book is sent down to him?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. The evidence, O brothers, is the Most High's words: ﴿Mankind was one community, then Allah sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners, and sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between people concerning that over which they differed﴾ [Al-Baqarah 213]. Also another verse: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Book and the Balance﴾ [Al-Hadid 25].

* A student: The Most High said: ﴿Allah will not forgive them﴾. And He said in another verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾ [Az-Zumar 53]. How (...)?

* The Shaykh: It will come to us, God willing; we have not yet mentioned the benefits.

* A student: Are the messengers to whom Allah sends down books, where the word "messenger" here includes the prophets; that is, does every prophet also receive a book?

* The Shaykh: Not apparently. The apparent view is that prophets are not sent down books; books are only for messengers, because they are the ones charged with conveying their Lord's message to creation.

* The student: What is the preferred view on distinguishing between a messenger and a prophet, Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, there is a difference between them.

* The student: What is the preferred view in it?

* The Shaykh: However, everything mentioned with the word "prophet" in the Qur'an is a messenger.

* A student: You said, may Allah preserve you, that the law of those before us is law for us unless a text states otherwise...

* The Shaykh: Unless our law contradicts it, yes.

* The student: Does fasting every other day fall under that?

* The Shaykh: Every other day?

* Another student: Fasting one day and breaking the fast the next.

* The Shaykh: Fasting one day and not fasting the next. The Messenger ﷺ approved this, saying: "The most excellent fasting is the fasting of Dawud" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5052), Muslim (1159/189), the wording being al-Bukhari's, from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr].

* The student: Why did he ﷺ not do it?

* The Shaykh: You know, may Allah bless you, that the Messenger ﷺ was the imam of the Ummah, its sultan, and its commander, and he was occupied with many matters more important than this. Sometimes a funeral passed by while he was speaking with his companions, and he did not stand up with the funeral, although following funerals is among the most excellent deeds. But the Messenger ﷺ considered other interests that were superior to saying "this is the most excellent thing."

* A student: May Allah bless you all. Some scholars say that every name ending in (-il) means "servant of Allah"; Jibril, for example. Is this statement correct?

* The Shaykh: By Allah, that is what they said, and Allah knows best; that is, apparently it is Hebrew.

* A student: The Karubiyyun (...)?

* The Shaykh: I do not know, by Allah. It has been said that the Karubiyyun are the bearers of the Throne, those whom Allah mentioned: ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it﴾. That is, those around these are the Karubiyyun. Allah knows best.

* A student: May Allah reward you with good. If a man was praying, then abandoned prayer, then prays (...)?

* The Shaykh: The benefits have not come yet.

* A student: Shaykh, regarding the category of sins, do shirk, innovation, and sin differ in degree?

* The Shaykh: Yes, there is no doubt they differ.

* The student: Can a person have a light innovation, for example?

* The Shaykh: Shirk is major and minor. Innovations too: some of them are sinful (mufassiq) and some are disbelief-making (mukaffir).

* The student: So, a light one, for example...?

* The Shaykh: Yes, there is no doubt about it; they differ. (...)

* * *
We have reached His words, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and then disbelieved﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse, ﴿Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief﴾: that one who vacillates between faith and apostasy will end up increasing in disbelief, as shown by His words ﴿then increased in disbelief﴾, and that is, Allah knows best, because faith never entered his heart.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: some scholars have used it to argue that one whose apostasy is repeated will not have his repentance accepted, saying: because Allah said: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief, Allah will not forgive them﴾. Is this inference correct?

Someone may say it is not correct, because what is the final state of these people? That they increased in disbelief, and Allah did not mention their repentance. But if we compare this with the Most High's words: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾ [Az-Zumar 53].

We say: this verse overrides what those scholars said, who held that the repentance of one whose apostasy is repeated is not accepted, because the verse says: ﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾.

If someone says: we do not claim that his repentance would not be accepted, but that it is unlikely he will repent; that is why the final state of these people was that they increased in disbelief. So we do not say that if he repented it would not be accepted; rather we say it is unlikely he will repent. Accordingly, we say: if the one whose apostasy has repeated shows sound faith, uprightness, and good condition, we accept it from him, and that is not difficult for Allah.

This is the more correct view: that one whose apostasy is repeated must be deliberate in accepting his repentance, until we know his sincerity in repentance, his righteousness, his uprightness, and that he has repented a sincere repentance.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a refutation of the Qadariyyah and a refutation of the Jabriyyah. The refutation of the Jabriyyah, who say that a person is compelled in his deeds and that his actions are attributed to him only metaphorically. The refutation of them is from His words: ﴿believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief﴾, where He attributed the actions to whom? To them.

There is also a refutation of the Jabriyyah, since for the Jabriyyah the servant has no voluntary act. The Jabri says: the servant has no voluntary act; he is compelled in action like a fallen leaf moved by the winds. When it was said to them: how can that be, when Allah rewards the obedient and punishes the disobedient? What wisdom is there in rewarding the obedient and punishing the disobedient, when each of them does the act without his choice?

They said: we do not dispute with Allah; He does what He wills. Injustice is a person's disposal of what is not his, and everything belongs to Allah; so when He disposes of His property as He wills, even by punishing the obedient and granting bliss to the disobedient, it is His property.

Accordingly, they negated wisdom in Allah's acts and said: Allah has no wisdom in His acts; He acts merely by will.

* Also in it: a refutation of the Qadariyyah, from His words ﴿nor will He guide them to a path﴾. This shows that guidance is in Allah's hand, and the servant does not possess it independently.

The Qadariyyah say: a person is independent in his act; Allah has no will or creation in it.

Their extremists say: nor knowledge, nor writing (decree).

So their extremists deny all levels of qadar: knowledge, writing, will, and creation.

Their moderate ones deny two of the levels of qadar: will and creation. They say: Allah knows and has written what will be, but He does not will it; the person is independent in his deed.

Both groups are extreme and excessive: the Qadariyyah went to extremes in affirming the servant's act, and overreached in affirming Allah's creation and will, while the Jabriyyah are the opposite.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a person must beware of wavering and fluctuation, for generally one in this state is not blessed in his lifespan or his work, having a different opinion each day and a different deed each day. Undoubtedly this wastes his time and he gains nothing from his life. For this reason it is reported from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Whoever is blessed in something, let him stick with it" [Cited by the author of al-Asrar al-Marfu'ah (p. 337): Ibn Taymiyyah said it is from the words of some of the Salaf. Ibn Majah (2147) narrated it with the wording "Whoever attains something, let him keep to it," from Anas ibn Malik as a marfu' report]. This is general in everything: in work, and even in a car: if it is blessed for you, keep it; and if it breaks down on you every day, then leave it. Do you leave it or keep it? Leave it.

In any case, this is evidence that a person should not vacillate but remain firm. However, our saying this does not mean that he should persist in falsehood after he sees that it is false. Rather, when it becomes clear to him that something is false, he must take up the truth, as 'Umar wrote to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari: "Let not a judgment you gave yesterday prevent you from judging by the truth today, for returning to the truth is better than persisting in falsehood" [Narrated by al-Daraqutni (4472) from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: when Allah, glorified and exalted, knows of a servant's state that he will not go straight, He will not forgive him nor guide him, because these people believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief.

Following from this benefit indicated by this verse, and also indicated by the Most High's words: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [As-Saff 5].

* It follows from this verse: good deeds bring about good deeds, and bad deeds bring about bad deeds. So if Allah bestows a good deed upon you, rejoice that He will bestow another deed to follow it.

* * *
* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿Give good news to the hypocrites that for them is a painful punishment (138). Those who take disbelievers as allies instead of believers. Do they seek honor with them? Indeed, honor belongs entirely to Allah﴾ [An-Nisa 138-139].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. We discussed the previous verse, its benefits and rulings, which is His words: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and then disbelieved﴾. We explained the disagreement of the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, over whether the repentance of one whose apostasy is repeated is accepted, and that there are two views among the people of knowledge:

Some of them said: his repentance is not accepted, and that if his apostasy is repeated three times, then at the third it is not accepted, because he is a player; if we accepted it today, when he has already apostatized twice before, he may apostatize again. They cited this verse as evidence.

But the preferred view is that if his sincerity in repentance becomes clear, his repentance is accepted, because of the general evidences for accepting repentance.

As for the noble verse, its ending says: ﴿then increased in disbelief﴾, so the final state of these people is an increase in disbelief, not repentance.

And it made clear the need to beware of a person's vacillation.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Give the hypocrites the good news that there is for them a painful punishment.﴾

﴿Give good news﴾ (bashshir) is an address to the Messenger, may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, though it can also be taken as general, applying to anyone the address is directed to, whether the Messenger (ﷺ) or others. Originally, bushra (good news) means informing someone of what pleases them. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good news, and a warner﴾ [al-Ahzab 45]. So tabshir (giving good news) is informing of what pleases. How, then, does He say: ﴿Give the hypocrites the good news that there is for them a painful punishment﴾? Does a painful punishment please anyone?

No. Some scholars answered that this is a case of sarcasm (tahakkum) directed at them. This is common in people's speech: when one sees a rebellious person, he says: "Receive good news of disappointment, receive good news of punishment," and the like. Among its examples is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Then pour over his head the torment of boiling water. Taste! Indeed, you were the mighty, the noble﴾ [ad-Dukhan 48-49].

Some scholars said that the meaning of His saying ﴿Indeed, you were the mighty, the noble﴾ is sarcasm.

Others said: ﴿Indeed, you were the mighty, the noble﴾ refers to [your status] in the worldly life, and this is your recompense in the Hereafter.

As for the second answer, they said: bushra is the informing of something by which the face changes, whether for good or for evil, and it was named so because the skin (bashrah) changes. When a person is told what pleases him, his face brightens, and when he is told what displeases him, his face darkens and becomes gloomy.

On this basis, there is no difficulty in the verse, and it is not necessary to ask whether this was said sarcastically or literally.

Rather, it was said literally.

And His saying ﴿the hypocrites﴾ means those who were hypocrites by displaying Islam and concealing disbelief. The word is derived from (nafaqa' al-yarbu') , meaning its burrow. The jerboa has a burrow with an open entrance; it digs a trench in the ground and then places at the end of the burrow a thin layer of earth. Thus, when one comes at it from the burrow's entrance, it is easy for it to push up this thin layer with its head and escape.

This is the origin of hypocrisy (nifaq), from the nafaqa' of the jerboa.

Hypocrisy was not known before Islam, nor at the beginning of Islam, because at the beginning of Islam the Muslims had no power that people feared. But when the Muslims gained strength and became powerful, which was after their victory at the Battle of Badr in the second year [of the Hijrah], hypocrisy began to appear.

The hypocrites said: "His affair has become strong and has manifested, so we must flatter him and must show that we are with him, so that he does not harm us." And they achieved what they wanted, for the Messenger ﷺ did not harm them, to the extent that he was asked permission to kill them, and he said: «People should not say that Muhammad kills his companions» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4905) and Muslim (2584/63), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah].

But this did not benefit them. So when did hypocrisy first appear? When the Muslims became strong after the Battle of Badr.

﴿Give the hypocrites the good news that there is for them a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿bi-anna﴾ is connected to ﴿bashshir﴾, ﴿'adhaban﴾ is the noun of (inna), and ﴿lahum﴾ is its predicate, placed first.

﴿a painful punishment﴾ means painful, causing pain. What is this painful punishment?

Allah the Exalted will mention it at the end of the verses: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the Fire, and you will not find for them a helper﴾ [an-Nisa' 145].

* In this noble verse: we should speak plainly to the hypocrites, giving them the good news, whether by saying "Receive good news!" or by saying "Know that there is for you a painful punishment," so that they may refrain from their hypocrisy.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the hypocrites deserve the painful punishment, as shown by His saying ﴿for them﴾, where the lam is for entitlement (istihqaq).

* Also among the benefits of this verse: their punishment is painful and agonizing.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 139:

Then He explained one of their attributes, which He mentioned in His words: ﴿Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers﴾. This is one of the signs of hypocrisy: that a person allies himself with the disbelievers rather than the believers, because he finds the believers weak, with no power (shawkah), while the disbelievers are strong, possessing power and authority, so he takes them as allies. He loyalizes to them, supports them, and flatters them, even at the expense of the religion, as is found today among some people regarding the alliance with disbelievers instead of believers. Rather, you find him a drawn sword against the Muslims, and against the disbelievers you find him cool water: he allies with them and supports them. This is one of the attributes of the hypocrites.

﴿Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers﴾: allies in what?

In loyalty in all matters: allies in love, allies in victory and support, even by speech, allies in strengthening their economy, allies in flattering them and not confronting them over what they are upon. The point is that the ways of alliance are many.

And His words: ﴿instead of the believers﴾. The particle (min), which indicates distance of relation between him and the believers, is used, as in the Almighty's words: ﴿And between us and you is a barrier﴾ [Fussilat 5]. It is more eloquent than saying: "between us and you is a barrier." Likewise, ﴿instead of the believers﴾ indicates the distance of relation between the believers and the hypocrites.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do they seek honour with them?﴾ That is: do they seek honour from the disbelievers, meaning dominance, strength, and subjugation?

This is what happens with some of those who ally themselves with the disbelievers: they seek honour from them, that they may be exalted through them. So God nullified this seeking by His words: ﴿Indeed, honour belongs to God entirely﴾. What is honour with the disbelievers? This is like the Almighty's words about the hypocrites themselves: ﴿They say: If we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble﴾ [al-Munafiqun 8]. This is true, but who is the more honourable?

﴿And honour belongs to God, and to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾. Here He did not say: "God is the most honourable, and His Messenger, and the believers," because if He had said, "God is more honourable," this would establish some honour for them. Rather He said: ﴿And honour belongs to God﴾, in a form that implies restriction through the fronting of the predicate, so that it becomes clear that the hypocrites have no honour. How could they have honour, when they fear (for their safety), flatter, and deceive?

﴿Indeed, honour belongs to God entirely﴾. The word ﴿entirely (jami'an)﴾ is a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of "honour," and it indicates that there are kinds of honour. Thus the scholars said: honour is of three kinds: honour of rank (qadr), honour of dominance (qahr), and honour of invulnerability (imtina'). God alone is the Subduer of everything, the Victor over everything; God alone is the possessor of great rank to which nothing is comparable; and God alone is the One against whom every deficiency and every defect is impossible. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, honour belongs to God entirely﴾.

* Among the lessons of this verse: the clarification of an ugly attribute of the hypocrites, which is what?

* A student: That they take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers.

* The Shaykh: Correct; taking the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. So whoever allies with the disbelievers instead of the believers, there is hypocrisy in it.

* And among the lessons of the noble verse: whoever seeks honour apart from God is humiliated, by His words: ﴿Do they seek honour with them?﴾, for this is a question of denunciation.

* And among its lessons: honour belongs to God alone, by His words: ﴿Indeed, honour belongs to God entirely﴾. He is the Mighty, who bestows honour on whom He wills and humbles whom He wills.

* And among its lessons: it is fitting for a person to sever his attachments to creatures, and to attach his heart to whom?

To God, Mighty and Majestic. He seeks from Him honour, seeks from Him victory, seeks from Him the removal of calamity, seeks from Him the facilitation of affairs. Thus, attach your heart to your Lord.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when﴾ [an-Nisa' 140].

* A student: Shaykh, I understood this: ﴿instead of the believers﴾, the (min) of connection indicates distance (...)?

* The Shaykh: Yes. When you say ﴿instead of﴾ there is a distance created by the word ﴿min﴾; that is, as if there is a distance between them and the believers. Had He said ﴿dūna al-mu'minīn﴾ without min, there would have been a possibility that they were close to the believers; so it indicates the distance.

I have already given you an example of a clearer verse than this: ﴿And between us and you is a barrier﴾ [Fussilat 5]. He did not say, "between us and you is a barrier," because if He had said, "between us and you is a barrier," it would be possible that there is nothing between them except the barrier alone. But ﴿And between us and you﴾ means that there is a distance before we reach the barrier between us and these people.

* A student: Shaykh, may God reward you well, in the tafsir, is there a difference between "painful" (al-alim) and "piercing" (al-muji') in the punishment?

* The Shaykh: "Painful" in the punishment, and what?

* The student: "Painful" and "piercing"?

* The Shaykh: Yes, "painful" means "piercing."

* The student: The same meaning?

* The Shaykh: Yes, the same meaning.

* A student: May God reward you, Shaykh. If someone asks us: when does one who allies with the enemies of God, the Mighty and Majestic, become a disbeliever?

* The Shaykh: One becomes a disbeliever if he allies with them by supporting them against the Muslims, or loves their victory over the Muslims, or the victory of falsehood over truth.

As for mere alliance by covenant or alliance by dealings, this does not take him out of Islam, and it may not even be blameworthy, let alone being something that expels one from Islam.

* A student: One who grieves over their calamities and their tragedies?

* The Shaykh: There is no doubt that this is a form of alliance, but as regards the matter of disbelief, disbelief is serious. Yet there is no doubt that this is alliance. However, a person may feel sorrow at their calamities because he sees that they harm him, since the people's relationship with this state may be stronger and more beneficial to them than their relationship with the other state. The Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God﴾ [ar-Rum 4-5], referring to the victory of the Romans over the Persians.

* A student: May God reward you well. Some scholars said that the word "glad tidings" here means mockery (tahakkum). What is the meaning of mockery?

* The Shaykh: Which one?

* The student: ﴿Give the hypocrites glad tidings﴾?

* The Shaykh: "Glad tidings," mockery: that is, he is ridiculed by it, since the painful thing is made to appear as if it were something desired and beloved.

* A student: Shaykh, may God bless you, is there a difference between alliance (muwalah) and flattery (mudahanah), and is there a kind of flattery that is permissible?

* The Shaykh: Alliance, as we said: that he supports them, helps them, and takes them as his allies, becoming one of their allies.

Flattery: that he remains silent about their falsehood, but without a bond of alliance between him and them. Flattery is forbidden, and alliance is more severe. But tolerance (mudarah) is not objectionable when there is a need for it.

* A student: May God bless you, Shaykh. You said that we should make the hypocrites aware of the glad tidings of punishment, although hypocrisy is a matter of the heart. How is this done?

* The Shaykh: No, it has a sign. God the Exalted said: ﴿And had We willed, We would have shown them to you, and you would have recognised them by their marks; and you will surely recognise them by the tone of their speech﴾ [Muhammad 30].

* A student: Is the motive for alliance the dominance of the disbeliever over the Muslim?

* The Shaykh: Meaning?

* The student: Meaning that he is the strong one, so he allies with him to guard against his evil. Which of the types mentioned earlier is this?

* The Shaykh: No, this is not alliance. It may be flattery, or it may also be tolerance; perhaps it is tolerance. Is it not permissible for us to give from our zakat, the obligation of Islam, to a disbeliever in order to guard against his evil?

* A student: Yes.

* Another student: Shaykh, may God bless you. Some Muslims place their money in the banks of the disbelievers. Is this alliance?

* The Shaykh: If he does so out of need, there is no harm; it is for his own need. He does not intend to benefit those people; he intends his own benefit.

* The student: It is known, Shaykh, that they benefit too?

* The Shaykh: He also benefits; he benefits by keeping it safe.

* A student: Shaykh, may God preserve you, what is the meaning of major and minor hypocrisy?

* The Shaykh: Yes. Major hypocrisy is that which shows Islam and conceals disbelief; that is, he is a disbeliever who has not believed in God or His Messenger, but he pretends before people that he is a believer. Minor hypocrisy is what is below that, and it is the hypocrisy that they call practical hypocrisy.

* A student: But the hypocrite remains with minor hypocrisy.

* The Shaykh: No, what is meant here in the verse is major hypocrisy.

* The student: No, does the hypocrite who has minor hypocrisy remain a believer?

* The Shaykh: Yes, he remains a believer; he combines a characteristic of faith and a characteristic of hypocrisy.

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: I have told you: if he conceals disbelief and shows Islam, this is major hypocrisy.

And if he does not conceal disbelief, such as concealing treachery, so that when he makes a covenant he betrays it, this is minor hypocrisy, which does not expel him from the religion.

* A student: Shaykh, may God bless you, is it established in the sira, that is, the biography of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, that he used to give the hypocrites glad tidings of painful punishment, or was it generally, in general terms?

* The Shaykh: Here is a principle we should understand: when textual statements (nusus lafziyyah) come, the basic rule is that they are put into practice. This is the basic rule. But if we say: textual statements are not acted upon unless we know that they were acted upon, this is a dangerous and corrupt principle.

Some people say: textual statements are not acted upon unless we know that the Companions acted upon them.

We say: the basic rule regarding textual statements is that they are acted upon. So here we do not need to say: prove to us that the Messenger used to give them glad tidings?

The basic rule is that when it was said to him: "Give glad tidings," he gave glad tidings.

* The student: So the basic rule is that it was acted upon?

* The Shaykh: Yes.

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being denied and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in a different conversation; indeed, then you would be like them. Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hellfire, all together (140). Those who wait in expectation concerning you: if you have a victory from Allah, they say, "Were we not with you?" And if the disbelievers have a share, they say, "Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?" Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers (141). Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, but He is the One who deceives them. When they stand up to pray, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering Allah except a little (142), wavering between that and this, belonging neither to these nor to those. And whoever Allah leaves astray, you will not find for him a way (143).﴾ [an-Nisa' 140–143].

* **Shaykh:** Well done. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being denied and mocked, do not sit with them.﴾

His words ﴿And He has already sent down to you﴾: the subject is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and *nazzala* and *anzala* have the same meaning.

It has been said: *anzala* is used for what came all at once, and *nazzala* for what came in installments. But the verses of the Mighty Book indicate that there is no difference. Whoever reflects on the Qur'an sees that there is no difference, for Allah, Exalted, sometimes expresses the sending down of the Qur'an by *inzal* and sometimes by *tanzil*. Yes, when it is distinguished, as in His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?" Thus [it was], that We may strengthen your heart with it﴾ [al-Furqan 32]. The meaning is: We sent it down. ﴿...that We may strengthen your heart with it﴾, so it is according to what occurred.

﴿And He has already sent down﴾, i.e., Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿to you in the Book﴾, i.e., in the Qur'an.

If we interpret *al-Kitab* as "the Qur'an," this is an interpretation by the intended meaning (*tafsir bil-murad*).

If we interpret *al-Kitab* as "that which is written," this is an interpretation by the wording (*tafsir bil-lafz*).

*Tafsir bil-lafz* is the interpretation of a word by what agrees with its derivation (*ishtiqaq*).

*Tafsir bil-murad* is the interpretation of a word by what is intended by it, regardless of its derivation.

So when you say, "*al-Kitab* means that which is written," this is a verbal interpretation by the wording. And when you say, "What is meant by it is the Qur'an," this is an interpretation by the intended meaning.

This occurs frequently in the Noble Qur'an: sometimes a word is interpreted by its intended meaning, and sometimes it is interpreted by what agrees with its derivation.

In any case, *al-Kitab* here is on the pattern *fi'al* in the sense of *maf'ul*, i.e., "written." It is called "written" because it is written in the Preserved Tablet, because it is written in the mushafs that are in our hands, and because it is written by the hands of the noble, righteous scribes (*safara*).

He says: ﴿that when you hear﴾. Here *an* is a masdariyya (verbal) particle, and it may also be a tafsiriyya (explanatory) particle, because *tanzil* includes the meaning of speech without its letters.

The explanatory *an* is the one that comes to explain what contains the meaning of speech without its letters.

So "the meaning of what is written": this is a verbal interpretation by the wording. And when you say, "What is meant by it is the Qur'an," this is an interpretation by the intended meaning. This occurs frequently in the Noble Qur'an: sometimes a word is interpreted by its intended meaning and sometimes by what agrees with its derivation. In any case, ﴿al-Kitab﴾ [an-Nisa' 140] here is *fi'al* in the sense of *maf'ul*, i.e., "written." It is called written because it is written in the Preserved Tablet, because it is written in the mushafs in our hands, and because it is written by the hands of the noble, righteous scribes.

He says: ﴿that when you hear﴾ [an-Nisa' 140]. This *an* is masdariyya, and it may be tafsiriyya, because *tanzil* includes the meaning of speech without its letters. The explanatory *an* is the one that explains what contains the meaning of speech without its letters. The thing sent down now is: ﴿that when you hear the verses of Allah being denied and mocked, do not sit with them.﴾

The verse to which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, referred is His saying: ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses, turn away from them until they engage in a different conversation. And if Satan should cause you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-An'am 68]. That is, if you see anyone engaging in [discussion of] the verses of Allah, whether by disbelief, mockery, or otherwise, do not sit with him. But if you forget, there is no blame on you, except when what? 

* **Student:** You remember.

* **Shaykh:** You remember. That is why He said: ﴿Do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-An'am 68].

﴿when you hear the verses of Allah﴾: the intended meaning of "verses" here is apparently the legislative verses (*ayat shar'iyya*), but there is no objection to saying that it also includes the cosmic verses (*ayat kawniyya*). The legislative verses are what the messengers brought from the books sent down to them, and the cosmic verses are the created beings.

So if you see someone trying to make Nature the Creator and Manager, this is disbelief in the cosmic verses of Allah. As for the legislative verses, disbelief in them is either by denial, or by disobedience and opposition. But disobedience and opposition are either major disbelief, or less than that.

His words ﴿and mocked﴾: i.e., taken as a jest and derision, whether that concerns the verses themselves, or the rulings they bring, or what they report of events, such as mocking the Day of Resurrection, or mocking Adam, or mocking the stories of the earlier prophets, or mocking the legislative rulings. All of this is included in His saying: ﴿and mocked﴾.

﴿do not sit with them﴾: the intended meaning of "sitting" is remaining, whether that is sitting, standing, or reclining. The intended meaning of sitting is not merely the opposite of standing or reclining.

﴿until they engage in a different conversation﴾: *hatta* here indicates a limit (*ghaya*), i.e., until they engage in a conversation other than it. He expressed it with ﴿they engage﴾ because those who disbelieved in the verses of Allah and mocked them are unlikely to have speech that is serious; rather they are always engaged in vain talk and play: ﴿Those who are in vain talk, playing﴾ [at-Tur 12].

Nevertheless, if this vain talk does not harm the religion, there is no harm in our remaining with them. And *hatta* here, I said, indicates a limit. Does it come for other than a limit? We say: yes, it often comes for other than a limit; it comes for causation (*ta'lil*), such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse"﴾ [al-Munafiqun 7]. Here *hatta* is for what?

* **Student:** For causation.

* **Shaykh:** No. The question is specific: why can it not be for a limit? The question is for you.

* **Student:** (...)

* **Shaykh:** You gave the ruling as the cause just now; that is not useful. Why can it not be a limit? ﴿Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse﴾ [al-Munafiqun 7]? Because the meaning, O brothers, would differ. If it said, "Do not spend until they disperse," the verse would indicate that when they disperse, then spend on them, because the limiting *hatta* (*al-ghaya*) is the one that can be replaced by "until" (*ila an*): "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse. So when they disperse, spend." But that is not the intended meaning. Rather the meaning is: do not spend in order that they disperse.

As for the one before us, ﴿until they engage in a different conversation﴾, it is a limit: ﴿until they engage in a different conversation﴾, i.e., other than the talk in which they disbelieve in the verses of Allah and mock them.

﴿indeed, then you would be like them﴾: the sentence is emphasized with *inna*, and the meaning is: indeed, if you sit with them, then you are like them, as His words indicate: ﴿then you would be like them﴾, i.e., like these engaging in vain talk.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hellfire, all together﴾ [an-Nisa' 140] on the Day of Resurrection. It has already been stated that the hypocrite is the one who displays Islam and conceals disbelief, and the disbeliever is the one who openly declares his disbelief.

* In this noble verse: there is an affirmation that the Qur'an is sent down from Allah, by His saying: ﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book﴾.
* From this benefit it follows that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, because if it is sent down from Him, it must be speech, since speech is an attribute and not a self-subsisting entity, but rather an attribute among the attributes.
* From this also follows: an affirmation of Allah's highness (*uluww*), because if the speech is from Him and it descends, this indicates that the speaker is exalted.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the ruling is attached to hearing, by His saying: ﴿when you hear﴾, just as it is attached to sight and to the heart. Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — about all those one will be questioned﴾ [al-Isra' 36].
* Among the benefits of this verse: it is not obligatory to denounce the disbeliever in the verses of Allah and the one who mocks them. Do you agree?
* **Student:** No, no.
* **Shaykh:** Yes?
* **Student:** No, (...).
* **Shaykh:** Are we now interpreting the verse itself, setting aside the other evidences?
* **Student:** Its apparent meaning is yes.
* **Shaykh:** Its apparent meaning is yes, because it only forbade sitting with them and did not command denouncing them. But the answer to this is: Allah, Exalted, only intended to clarify the ruling for those who participate, and forbidding them from that — i.e., from this evil — is understood from our being forbidden to sit with them. Our being forbidden to sit with them means that we should not approve of the evil. So the correct view is that this verse does not indicate the lifting of the prohibition of this evil; and if it indicates it or is silent about it, we have other texts that indicate the obligation to denounce evil.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: rulings revolve around their causes (*'illal*). From His saying: ﴿Do not sit with them until they engage in a different conversation﴾: when they disbelieved in the verses of Allah and mocked them, we were forbidden to sit with them; then we were permitted to sit with them when they engaged in a different conversation.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: one who participates with the perpetrator of evil is like the perpetrator, ﴿indeed, then you would be like them﴾. We said "participates," and the verse does not indicate participation; it indicates that the one sitting with them has the ruling of the doer. So we say: if the one sitting — i.e., the one remaining with them — has the ruling of the doer, then the participant is more so.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation to leave the place where the verses of Allah are disbelieved in and mocked; the obligation of separation. A person may not remain and say, "I denounce it in my heart." The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; and if he is not able, then with his tongue; and if he is not able, then with his heart" [Muslim (49/78), from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri]. And I now denounce it in my heart to the utmost extent of denunciation.

We say: if you were truthful in that, you would have stood up, since the limbs follow the heart. If the heart disliked that, the limbs would dislike it too. But this does not suffice you; you must separate, or else you are like them.

If someone says: then forbid a person from sitting with one who shaves his beard, since shaving the beard is forbidden?

The answer: it is obligatory for us to leave the place when we see him actually shaving it. But once the act has ended and only its trace remains, we are not obliged to leave the place where he is.

Similarly, if someone says: if I smell the smell of smoke on a person, I must separate from him, since the trace of smoke is in his mouth. What is the answer?

The answer: it is not obligatory. Yes, if you see him smoking, then you forbid him; if he complies, well, otherwise you stand up. The trace of a sin is not like the act of sin.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the prohibition of cooperation in sin and transgression. Its basis is that if sitting with the perpetrator of evil is forbidden, then assisting him is more so. For example, preparing the place for them, sprinkling it, perfuming it, bringing the vessels, pouring them coffee or tea: this is forbidden all the more.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the companionship of the righteous who do righteous deeds is like them. From where do we take this? From the reverse analogy (*qiyas al-'aks*): since one is burdened with sin by sitting with the disobedient, one is rewarded by sitting with the obedient. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, himself used this analogy when he said: "And in the intercourse of one of you is a charity" — meaning, when a man goes to his wife, he has a charity — and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, when one of us fulfills his desire, will he have a reward for it?" He said: "Do you see that if he placed it in the unlawful, would he bear a burden for it?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Likewise, if he places it in the lawful, he has a reward" [Muslim (1006/53), from Abu Dharr].

What kind of analogy is this? It is the reverse analogy: this is like it. For since Allah sins those who sit with the perpetrator of evil, His bounty is broader and greater, and He rewards those who sit with the righteous and the people of obedience.

From here arises a benefit: caution regarding bad companions, and encouragement toward good companions. This is what the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, indicated when he said: "The example of the good companion is like the bearer of musk." Musk is a type of perfume; it is said that it comes from the blood of a particular gazelle. Al-Mutanabbi, praising — I think it is Sayf al-Dawla — said:

*Though you surpass mankind while being one of them,*
*musk is but a part of the blood of the gazelle.*

So we say: the Messenger said: "The example of the good companion is like the bearer of musk: either he will give you some (gratis), or he will sell it to you, or you will find a good scent from him. And the example of the bad companion is like the blower of the bellows: either he will burn your clothes, or you will find a foul odor from him" [agreed upon: al-Bukhari (5534) and Muslim (2628/146), from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari].

Do you know what the *kir* (bellows) is? The *kir* is a skin that is tied together, and there is a nozzle on it that enters a pipe connected to the embers. At the end of this skin — which is soft leather — there are two pieces of wood, like this, that open and close. When one pulls it, they open and the skin fills with air; then one closes them and pushes, and then there is air entering with the pipe onto the charcoal, and the fire ignites. This is the *kir*. They used to use it in the past; we saw them. He said: the bearer of the bellows "either will burn your clothes" — when? When sparks fly onto the clothes — "or you will find a foul odor from him."

So the noble verse indicates the meaning of this hadith: beware of bad companions, and hold to good companions, for you will never lack good from good companions, and you will never lack evil from bad companions.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the Fire is for two categories of the world. Tell us them.
* **Student:** That the Fire is for two categories of...
* **Shaykh:** Explain them. Who are the two categories?
* **Student:** The ones in the verse: the hypocrites and the disbelievers.
* **Shaykh:** That is enough: the hypocrites and the disbelievers. There remains a third category: the believers. And these three categories are those mentioned at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of the Fire, and that it is vast. What is the proof of this? ﴿Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers together in Hell﴾. The reason it is vast is that "it will hold nine hundred and ninety-nine out of every thousand of the children of Adam in the Fire"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3348), and Muslim (222 / 379), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]]. And what about the jinn? ﴿I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men, all together﴾ [Hud 119]. It is apparent that the jinn are more numerous than the children of Adam in the Fire, and for this reason they are mentioned first in the verse.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: can we say that it contains iltifat (a shift in grammatical person mid-discourse)? Does it contain iltifat?

* Student: After saying ﴿So do not sit with them﴾, He used a pronoun here, then He said ﴿Indeed Allah will gather the hypocrites﴾, and used the apparent noun.

* Shaykh: Yes, indeed, it may be said so. Using the apparent noun in place of the pronoun has benefits:

* Student: Generality.

* Shaykh: Intending generality, yes.

* Student: Upon the cause for which this ruling applies to them, and the intention of stating the cause and generality.

* Shaykh: That is one.

* Student: (...) for alerting attention.

* Shaykh: Good. ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers, and Jibril and Mika'il, then indeed Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah 98]. He did not say "an enemy to Him", although this is what the context requires. But this shows that ﴿whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers, and Jibril and Mika'il﴾ is a disbeliever, and it alerts to the cause of enmity, namely enmity toward Allah, which is disbelief. And so that the meaning is more comprehensive: that is, Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers who disbelieve by being hostile, and also to those who disbelieve by other means.

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Those who wait and watch for you: if a victory comes to you from Allah, they say, "Were we not with you?" And if the disbelievers have a share, they say, "Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?"﴾ [An-Nisa 141]. They are, then, gatherers, withholders, liars, and deceivers. Note ﴿Those who wait and watch for you﴾. At-tarabbus (تربص) means waiting. From it is the words of Allah, ﴿And divorced women shall wait [remain in waiting] by themselves﴾ [Al-Baqarah 228], meaning they wait. Wait for what? For misfortunes (الدوائر, ad-dawa'ir), waiting for misfortunes to befall you, whether they fall upon you or upon them.

He says: ﴿If a victory comes to you from Allah﴾, they say, "We want a share of this victory. We are with you, so do not deprive us of the spoils."

﴿And if the disbelievers have a share﴾, He did not say "victory," because what the disbelievers are given is not a victory but a trial (mihnah). ﴿If the disbelievers have a share, they say﴾, meaning: to the disbelievers.

﴿Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?﴾ Meaning: "Were it not for us, the believers would have destroyed you. But we shielded you from them, gained mastery over you, and became a shield for you." Look at how the hypocrite behaves, may Allah protect us: if victory belongs to the believers, what do they say?

* Student: ﴿Were we not with you?﴾

* Shaykh: ﴿Were we not with you?﴾, meaning: "Since we were with you, give us our share, give us from the spoils." And if the matter is reversed?

* Student: They gain mastery over the believers.

* Shaykh: They gain mastery over the believers and protect them from the believers?!

* Student: They say, "Praise be to Allah that we were not with them"?

* Shaykh: "Praise be to Allah that we were not with them"?! No.

* Student: ﴿They say, "Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?"﴾

* Shaykh: Yes. ﴿We gained mastery over you﴾, meaning: we took control, we were a shield for you, and we protected you from the believers. It does not say "against the believers" but "from the believers." Meaning: we are the ones who defended you from the believers, and were it not for us, the believers would have killed you. They claim to be with the believers and seek the spoils, and they claim to be protectors of the disbelievers so that they may be their allies.

Allah said: ﴿So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection﴾. The fa' here is for sequence (lit. "separation" in the sense of a consequence). The noble name of Allah is the subject (mubtada'), and ﴿He will judge﴾ with its clause is the predicate (khabar).

﴿So Allah will judge between you﴾, meaning: between these hypocrites and the disbelievers as well.

﴿On the Day of Resurrection﴾ is connected to ﴿will judge﴾. The Day of Resurrection is the Day of Raising (yawm al-ba'th). It is so named for several reasons. What are they?

* Student: Because it is the day on which the witnesses will stand.

* Shaykh: Because it is the day on which the witnesses will stand.

* Student: Because it is the day on which justice will be established.

* Shaykh: Because it is the day on which justice will be established.

* Student: The day (...).

* Shaykh: Yes, well done.

﴿So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾. Subhan Allah! Is the opponent informed of the outcome of the judgment before the case is heard? Now, God willing, we are the ones who are opposing the disbelievers, because Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾, after He said: ﴿So Allah will judge between you.﴾ What judgment could be more eloquent than this? It is said to the opponent: "The judge is decided, and your opponent has no authority over you." So judgment is given in favor of the opponent before the hearing, because the matter is clear and final: ﴿And Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of the severity of the hypocrites' enmity toward the believers, since they wait and watch for misfortunes to befall them, waiting for the moment when harm will fall upon the believers. But Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿The evil turn of fortune is against them, and Allah is angry with them and has cursed them and prepared for them Hell, and it is an evil destination﴾ [Al-Fath 6].

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the hypocrites have a share of the booty. From where is it taken? His words: ﴿Were we not with you?﴾ This shows that the hypocrite is treated according to the outward appearance, so he is given what a Muslim is given.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the hypocrites have pride and arrogance in their noses. If victory belongs to the Muslims, they demand the spoils; if it belongs to the disbelievers, they claim favor over them: ﴿And if the disbelievers have a share, they say, "Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?"﴾, meaning: "So give us a share."

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the false claim of the hypocrites, because they are the ones who kept the disbelievers away from the believers, since they increased the disbelievers' numbers, helped them secretly, and comforted their hearts with what? With victory.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of recompense and judgment among people, from His words: ﴿So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection﴾, and this is a judgment after which there is no other judgment.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation that the disbeliever has no way over the believer, whatever the circumstances. The disbeliever has no way. Have you considered: if a Muslim burned their palm trees and killed their animals, would he sin? No, he does not sin.

* Student: The disbelievers? Yes.

* Shaykh: As long as they are disbelievers, of course, as long as they are disbelievers at war (harbiyyin), he does not sin, because their property is permissible. But the protected one (ma'sum), who is the dhimmi (a non-Muslim living under Muslim protection), and second, the mu'ahad (one under a treaty), and third, the musta'min (one given temporary safe conduct), their property is sacred.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, glorified and exalted, is the judge among His servants, as shown by His words: ﴿And Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers.﴾ So Allah judges and He will never grant. On this basis, there is no judgment on the Day of Resurrection for anyone, not even for the Messenger (ﷺ). He cannot judge, and for this reason, at the time of intercession, the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) cannot intercede without seeking permission from Allah.

* Can it be inferred from this noble verse that the judgment between disbelievers and believers in this world may sometimes favor the disbeliever? It may be. What is its basis?

* Student: That on the Day of Resurrection there is no way (for the disbelievers).

* Shaykh: Yes. Allah negated that they would have any way on the Day of Resurrection. As for other than the Day of Resurrection, all people are under justice.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you: did you not say the benefit in the hypocrites' false claim is their claim that they increased the numbers of the disbelievers and kept them away from the believers?

* Shaykh: Yes indeed. The falsehood lies in their claim that this increase was the cause of the share the disbelievers received.

* Student: O Shaykh, does it not seem apparent that they intend, for example, to help them, to betray the believers and discourage them, and so become a cause of victory?

* Shaykh: But is this itself the thing by which the disbelievers obtained a share?

* Student: It is among the causes.

* Shaykh: Yes, among the causes, but not everything.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, can it be inferred from the previous verse, ﴿Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers﴾, that He mentioned the hypocrites first, meaning that they are worse and more wicked than the disbelievers?

* Shaykh: Yes, it indicates that. In all verses where the hypocrites and disbelievers are mentioned together, Allah puts the hypocrites first: ﴿That Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women﴾ [Al-Ahzab 73], except in one case or one verse, for a reason, which is His words: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ [At-Tawbah 73]. That is because striving against the disbelievers is by the sword, openly; striving against the hypocrites is by knowledge and clarification, not by fighting.

* Student: The disbeliever and the one who mocks.

* Shaykh: From where?

* Student: ﴿Until they engage in a conversation other than that﴾.

* Shaykh: Yes. We said in the tafsir lesson that the ruling revolves around its cause ('illah).

* Student: Shaykh, if someone is told that the gathering will involve mockery of the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, should he go and let the mockery happen, or is it better to refrain?
