* Shaykh: If he knows that this gathering will involve mockery or disbelief, we look: if he is able to change it, it is obligatory for him to attend; if he is not able to, it is forbidden for him to attend, because attending and then leaving is only extra hardship, and it may cause evil and strife.

* Student: Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿When you hear the signs of Allah being disbelieved in and mocked﴾. Someone may say, Shaykh: is mocking the signs not disbelief?

* Shaykh: No. But engaging (in such talk) has two types: outright disbelief and mockery.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them. And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering Allah except a little (142). Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those. And whomever Allah leaves astray, you will never find for him a way (143). O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah an clear authority against yourselves?﴾ [An-Nisa 142–144].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Those who wait and watch for you﴾. What is the meaning of at-tarabbus? Waiting. Meaning? ﴿So wait, and I will be with you among those who wait﴾ [At-Tawbah 24]. And what do they wait and watch for against the Muslims?

* Student: They wait for misfortunes to befall them.

* Shaykh: They wait for misfortunes to befall them, meaning they wait for the evil turn of fortune to fall upon the believers.

What is the meaning of His words: ﴿If a victory comes to you from Allah, they say, "Were we not with you?"﴾?

* Student: It means that if there is a victory for the Muslims, they say, "Were we not with you?" meaning, "We were not ... (...)" and we were with you in this (...).

* Shaykh: And what do they intend by this statement?

* Student: That they share the spoils with them.

* Shaykh: That they participate with them in the booty. ﴿And if the disbelievers have a share, they say, "Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?"﴾

* Student: His words: ﴿Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?﴾ mean: "Did we not hold you back and protect you from the defeat the believers would inflict upon you?" By this they intend to deceive the other party into thinking that they were the reason for their victory over the believers.

* Shaykh: His words: ﴿And Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾, is this in the Day of Resurrection or now?

* Student: In this world, and it may include this world and the Hereafter.

* Shaykh: It may carry both meanings. What do you mean by both meanings? Read the verse so you understand the context.

* Student: ﴿And Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾, in this world.

* Shaykh: Read what comes before this sentence.

* Student: ﴿Those who wait and watch for you: if a victory comes to you from Allah, they say, "Were we not with you?" And if the disbelievers have a share, they say, "Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?" So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers.﴾

* Shaykh: What has become clear now?

* Student: It becomes clear that it is in this world.

* Shaykh: That it is in this world, because Allah judges between them on the Day of Resurrection, and He will never give them a way in this world.

* Student: In His words: ﴿And if the disbelievers have a share﴾.

* Shaykh: But ﴿So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: This is the Day of Resurrection, because He said: ﴿So Allah will judge﴾, then He said: there is no way for the disbelievers over the believers. So this is on the Day of Resurrection. But some scholars made its ruling general, as we mentioned to you, and we explained the benefits of this verse.

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites try to deceive Allah, but it is He who deceives them.﴾ The sentence is emphasized with (inna) to explain the condition of these hypocrites and how they deal with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. "They try to deceive Allah" means they also deceive the believers, as Allah said in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿They think to deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive none except themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah 9]. And with what do they deceive? With displaying Islam. Whoever sees them and sees their attendance at prayer and their charity says, "They are believers," so they deceive Allah by this.

He said: ﴿but it is He who deceives them.﴾ That is, Allah responds to their deception with a deception from Him. And how is His deceiving them? He gives them respite so that they continue in this and become accustomed to it, so they remain disbelievers with their devils, and Muslims with the believers. By this hypocrisy they protect their blood and their wealth. This is Allah's deception of them: He gives them respite so that they persist in their hypocrisy, and then, as a consequence, He seals their end with an evil ending.

﴿And when they stand up for prayer, they stand up lazily,﴾ ﴿when they stand up for prayer﴾, whatever prayer it may be, they stand up lazily. The one who is lazy (kaslan) is the one who has languor and lack of energy for action. So when they stand, they stand lazily; you find them dragging their feet in performing ablution, dragging their feet going to the mosque, dragging their feet in the prayer itself, and that is due to their lack of desire for prayer. The reason is that whoever is eager for something must stand up to it energetically.

﴿They show off to the people,﴾ that is, although they stand lazily, they are not sincere in their standing; rather, they show off to people, meaning they display themselves in this appearance so that people see them and say, "They are Muslims." ﴿And they remember Allah only a little,﴾ ﴿they do not remember Allah﴾ means: they do not pray, or they do not remember Allah in their prayer? The second; that is, even when they pray, they remember Allah only a little.

The intended meaning is that they do not remember Allah with their tongues, their limbs and their hearts, except a little. They do not remember Allah with their tongues, because they do not perform what is obligatory of takbir, tasbih, tashahhud and others. Likewise, they do not remember Allah with their actions: they are not at ease in prayer, they peck at it like a crow pecks, because it is burdensome to them and they do not perform it out of desire. And they do not remember Allah with their hearts, because their hearts are heedless and negligent; they perform the prayer like a machine performs its work, without feeling that they are communing with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Thus ﴿they do not remember Allah﴾ in prayer, ﴿except a little﴾, meaning with the heart, tongue and limbs.

* In this noble verse: affirmation of the deception of the hypocrites, and that they are a people of deceit and cunning. For this reason, among the characteristics of hypocrites is that when they make a covenant they betray it, when they dispute they transgress, when they speak they lie, and when they promise they break it, because all of this involves deception.

* Among its benefits: the noble verse affirms deception for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, meaning that He, exalted is He, deceives those who deceive Him, by His saying: ﴿but it is He who deceives them.﴾ Is deception a attribute of blame or of praise?

On this there is detail: if it is in response to one who deceives, it is an attribute of praise, because it indicates the strength of the one who deceives and that his enemy will not outwit him, for He is stronger in cunning than his enemy and more powerful in deception, as Allah said: ﴿Say: Allah is swifter in plotting﴾ [Yunus 21], and He said: ﴿And Allah is the best of planners﴾ [Ali 'Imran 54].

As for when it has no cause and is deception in a position of trust, it is not called deception but betrayal (khiyanah), and this is a defect in every case. For this reason Allah is not described as a betrayer absolutely, even those who betray Allah, Allah does not meet them with betrayal, as Allah said: ﴿They had already betrayed Allah before, so He gave (the Prophet) power over them﴾ [al-Anfal 71], and He did not say "so He betrayed them." The reason is that betrayal is deception in a position of trust. Indeed the Messenger ﷺ said: "Do not betray the one who betrayed you"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (3535) and al-Tirmidhi (1264) from Abu Hurairah.]], because this is blameworthy, so Allah is not described with it.

If someone asks: Is Allah described with deception absolutely, so that it is said that Allah is "one who deceives" or "a deceiver"? We say: No. He is described with it only in response to the deception of His enemies. Likewise plotting, scheming, mockery and similar attributes that are praiseworthy in some situations and not in others: it is not permissible to describe Allah with them in an unrestricted manner.

Based on this, we say: meanings and attributes are either pure perfection, and then Allah is described with them; or pure blame and deficiency, and then Allah is not described with them at all; or praiseworthy in one situation and blameworthy in another, and then Allah is described with them when they are praiseworthy, and not described with them when they are blameworthy.

Based on this, if anyone describes Allah with incapacity, we say: this is forbidden in every case, because incapacity is an attribute of blame. Likewise, if they describe Him with betrayal, we say: this is forbidden in every case, because betrayal is blameworthy in every case. Good. Speech? Speech is perfection, so Allah is described as speaking, and as willing, likewise ﴿Doer of what He wills﴾ [Hud 107], because all of these are attributes of perfection.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the hypocrites do pray, but will their prayer be accepted? No, it is not accepted, because Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And nothing prevented their contributions from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and they do not come to prayer except while lazy﴾ [al-Tawbah 54]. Even though the benefit of spending is transferable, it is still not accepted; so how about an act of worship whose benefit is not transferable? It is all the more fitting that it should not be accepted. So their prayer is not accepted, but they pray to be seen by people.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: when they perform prayer for show, they perform it how? With laziness, coldness and lack of energy.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: whoever performs prayer in a manner of laziness has a resemblance to the hypocrites, so beware of resembling the hypocrites. Perform the prayer with energy, joy and happiness. By Allah, the true believer truly rejoices when prayer comes, because he will stand before Allah communing with Him. If one of us rejoices that he will meet his friend or companion and prepares for that, then what of meeting Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and communing with Him?

For this reason, if you find laziness in your prayer, accuse yourself, for you undoubtedly resemble the hypocrites in this trait. But accuse yourself, correct your course toward Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and do not be lax, because perhaps you have some laxity now, a slight laxity, but it increases until prayer becomes the heaviest thing for you.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever shows off his good deeds to people has a resemblance to whom? To the hypocrites. Showing off has a wide scope; it is not only in prayer, charity, fasting or Hajj. No, it is broader than this: even if a person wears tattered clothes to appear to people as an ascetic, he is a show-off. Therefore do not think that showing off is restricted to pure acts of worship; it may be in anything. Everything you display to people to show that you draw near to Allah so that people see you is showing off, may Allah protect us, a showing off that nullifies the deed, because Allah says in the hadith qudsi: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in needing partners. Whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I abandon him and his association."[[Narrated by Muslim (2985/46) from Abu Hurairah.]] Allah is independent of us, while we are in need of Him, and He is in complete independence from us. So if we associate anyone with Allah, we seek refuge in Allah from shirk, He will not accept it from us. He is the most self-sufficient of partners from partnership.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: warning against showing off to people. Why do you show off to people? Do people benefit you? No, nor do they harm you. Rather, the One who benefits and harms you is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Whatever blessing you have is from Allah; then when harm touches you, to Him you cry for help﴾ [al-Nahl 53]. Do not concern yourself with people; whether they praise you or disparage you, the most important thing is to look to the pleasure of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Keep far away from showing off.

But here is a question: Satan comes to a person and says: "If you pray, you have shown off; if you improve your prayer, you have shown off." And he is far from this. So should one leave off improving the prayer out of fear of this? Or leave off worship out of fear of this? No. This is one of Satan's discouragements to a person. Rather, let him press on along his path and continue, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, and not pay attention to these whisperings, because Satan wishes that we not worship Allah, since he disobeyed Allah, so he wants people to disobey their Lord as well.

So do not abandon worship for fear of showing off. Then, if it occurs to you that you improve it because people see you, and if you are a student of knowledge who is looked up to, intend that you improve it so that people may follow you, and in this state you are a worshipper and a teacher. The Messenger ﷺ, when a delegation came to him asking him to explain to them how to pray, would say: "Pray as you see me pray"[[I have not found a hadith with this meaning; what we found is the hadith about asking about the prayer times, narrated by Muslim (613/176) from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb.]]. He would climb the pulpit when it was built for him, and he would stand and pray upon it, and say: "I did this so that you may follow me and learn my prayer."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (377) and Muslim (544/44) from Sahl ibn Sa'd.]] By this, Satan is driven away from you.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the remembrance of Allah by the hypocrites is little. We said that remembrance occurs with the heart, the tongue and the limbs; they do not remember Allah except a little, even in the outward limbs that are visible to people they remember Allah only a little.

* Among its benefits: if you find in yourself little remembrance of Allah, then there is in you a resemblance to the hypocrites. For this reason Allah described the believers of understanding as those who ﴿remember Allah standing, sitting and on their sides﴾ [Ali 'Imran 191]. And what harms you if you remember Allah? Does the tongue tire? There is no organ like the tongue in not tiring. So if that is so, then increase in the remembrance of Allah. It is related from the Prophet ﷺ that a man came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the obligations of Islam have become many for me" -meaning: and I have grown old- "so the Messenger ﷺ said to him: 'Let your tongue never cease to be moist with the remembrance of Allah.'"[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3375) and Ibn Majah (3793) from Abdullah ibn Busr.]] That is, persevere in the remembrance of Allah.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse also: the hypocrites do remember Allah, but what? But their remembrance is little.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 143 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those﴾. "Wavering" (mudhabdhabin) means vacillating, going back and forth; Satan sways them, once here and once there. ﴿Wavering between that, belonging neither to these﴾ means: neither to the believers nor to the hypocrites. Outwardly they are Muslims, and inwardly they are disbelievers. So when they come to the disbelievers, they say: "Indeed, we are with you," and when they come to the Muslims, they say: "Indeed, we are with you."
﴿Were we not with you?﴾ as has passed. So they are, may God protect us, wavering, not settling on any opinion. This is because they did not believe the first time, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-An'am 110].
Therefore, beware of accepting the truth only while hesitating. Beware of this. Whenever the truth becomes clear to you, say: "We hear and we obey," and believe, fearing that your heart and sight may be turned if you do not accept the truth the first time. Of this, or something close to it, is what some people do today: when you say, "The Messenger ordered such-and-such," or "God ordered such-and-such," they say: "Is the command for obligation?" As if he is saying: if it is not obligatory, I will not do it. This is a mistake. When you hear God command, or the Messenger command, say: "We hear and we obey," whether it is for recommendation (istihbab) or for obligation (wujub).
Only when a person neglects this command and abandons it is it appropriate to ask whether it is obligatory, so that he may make it up, or non-obligatory, so that he is not sinful for not making it up. But before you act, the perfection of servitude is to say: "We hear and we obey." Then, if it was obligatory, you have obtained the reward of the obligation and the discharge of your duty; and if it was not obligatory, you have obtained good and reward. You will not regret it. What causes regret is hesitating, saying: "Is it obligatory or not?"
I do not know that the Companions, may God be pleased with them, asked the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, when he commanded them: "Is this obligatory or a sunnah?" except in one case, the case of Barirah. When the Messenger ordered her to remain with her husband, Mughith, she said: "If you are commanding me, then I hear and obey" (and she did not say: "If you are commanding me by way of obligation"), "if you are merely advising me, then I have no need for it." Barirah had been freed, and when a wife is freed she is given the choice between remaining with her husband and annulling the marriage. "When she was freed, the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, gave her the choice, saying: 'If you wish, you may remain with the husband, and if you wish, you may annul the marriage.'"[[This is the meaning of a hadith narrated by al-Bukhari (5283) from Ibn 'Abbas.]] So she chose annulment.
The Lawgiver gave her the choice because she now possessed herself with complete ownership, whereas at the time of the contract she had been a slave with no disposal over herself. Now she had been freed, and therefore the choice was given to her, and she chose annulment, choosing herself. "Her husband would follow her through the markets of Madinah, weeping, wanting her to return. The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, would marvel and say: 'Do you not marvel at Mughith's love for Barirah, and Barirah's hatred for Mughith?'"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (5273) from Ibn 'Abbas.]]
It is indeed right to marvel at this, because the custom is that hearts are witnesses, as they say, exchanging hatred and love; but this one, glory be to God, refused, like the wife of Thabit ibn Qays, who was testified to be among the people of Paradise, who came to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, seeking khul' (separation). "She said: 'I do not blame him for his character or his religion, but I dislike disbelief after Islam.' So the Messenger ﷺ commanded him to divorce her in exchange for her garden, and she returned it to him."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (5273) from Ibn 'Abbas.]] This is among the wondrous things.
The point is that we say: we do not know of the Companions questioning the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding his command, saying: "Is it an obligation, O Messenger of God, or a voluntary act?" Not at all. So be like the Companions: say, "We hear and we obey," and praise God that the Mighty and Majestic has legislated this command for you; for were it not that God had legislated it for you, your performing it would be an innovation that would increase you only in misguidance and distance from God.
He says: ﴿Belonging neither to these nor to those﴾, ﴿wavering﴾, ﴿And whomever God sends astray, you will not find for him a way﴾ [an-Nisa' 143]. This sentence is conditional, and there is a difficulty in it: the conditional "man" (whoever), as we know, makes the verb jussive, and another difficulty is that the verb does not take the kasra, meaning it is not in the genitive, yet here it is kasra. So these are two difficulties?
* Student: It is kasra because of the meeting of two sukun (sakinayn).
* Shaykh: That is, it is jussive but took an incidental kasra due to the meeting of two sukun. And the second difficulty?
* Student: It is the same.
* Shaykh: No, it is not the same. Does the genitive enter the verb?
* Student: It does not enter; here it did not enter.
* Shaykh: Yes. Why this kasra?
* Student: This is to avoid the meeting of two sukun.
* Shaykh: That is, it is not an inflectional kasra, correct. Rather, it is to avoid the meeting of two sukun. As for the response, it is His saying: ﴿then you will not find for him a way﴾.
That is, any person whom God, glory be to Him, has decreed to be astray, you will not find for him a way to guidance. "A way" means a path. ﴿And whomever God sends astray, you will not find for him a way﴾. These hypocrites, God has sent them astray, so you will not find a way to guide them, may God protect us. Yet perhaps God bestows His favor upon some of them and they become guided, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Was it God and His signs and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief. If We pardon a faction of you, We will punish another faction﴾ [at-Tawbah 65-66].
* From the benefits of this verse: the state of the hypocrites is wavering between disbelief and belief, but their judgment in the Hereafter is that they are disbelievers; in this world, however, they are judged by their outward appearance, because rulings in this world are based on outward matters.
* And from the benefits of this noble verse: if you see yourself wavering between acceptance and denial, know that there is in you a resemblance to whom? To the hypocrites, because the believer cannot be wavering, nor have a choice in what God and His Messenger have decreed, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair﴾ [al-Ahzab 36]. Rather, they do not waver; they accept and submit.
* And from the benefits of this noble verse: tranquility and stability are required; for this reason we find the most steadfast and tranquil of people are the believers. He said: ﴿He said: Yes, but that my heart may be reassured﴾ [al-Baqarah 260].
* And from the benefits of this noble verse: whomever God has sent astray, no one can guide. This is because of His saying: ﴿And whomever God sends astray﴾.
If someone says: why does God send one astray and guide another? We say to him: did the one whose guidance was withheld, was it withheld from him unjustly or justly? The answer: justly, without doubt; and He showed favor to the other and guided him. He has not withheld from anyone his right; rather, He has shown favor to this one and guided him.
Then know that misguidance will only occur because of a cause from the servant, for God, the Exalted, said: ﴿So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [as-Saff 5]. And as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights, as they did not believe in it the first time﴾ [al-An'am 110]. So if they had believed the first time and remained steadfast on the path, God would never have sent them astray.
With this we know that the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him: "Indeed one of you may act with the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is between him and it only an arm's length, and then the Decree overtakes him, and he acts with the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it,"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3208) and Muslim (2643/1) from Ibn Mas'ud.]] does not mean that there is no more between him and Paradise than an arm's length in terms of his deeds; rather, there is no more between him and Paradise than an arm's length in terms of his term (ajal). For if his deeds had brought him to the point where only an arm's length remained between him and Paradise, God would never have forsaken him. But there is a thorn (haskah) in his heart, as in the other hadith: "Indeed a man may act with the deeds of the people of Paradise in the sight of people, while he is of the people of the Fire,"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2898) and Muslim (112/179) from Sahl ibn Sa'd, with a story at its beginning.]] and this interpretation is required: we say that "until there is only an arm's length between him and it" is with regard to the term; that is, when his term draws near and death approaches, he manifests and declares that he is of the people of the Fire, may God protect us.
* And from the benefits of this noble verse: an indication of turning to God, the Mighty and Majestic, in seeking guidance; from His saying: ﴿And whomever God sends astray, you will not find for him a way﴾. Accordingly, if we call someone to the truth but he refuses and wavers, we turn to God to guide him, for God is capable of all things. How many people were the most wretched of the people and became the most happy, and the most corrupt became the most righteous. Was 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, the second man among the followers of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, far from that? Khalid ibn al-Walid, 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl: what was their state at Uhud? Answer me.
* The students: They were disbelievers.
* Shaykh: They were disbelievers, hostile to Islam, wanting to eliminate the people of Islam, wanting to kill the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and to kill the Companions. Yet after this, what were they? They became leaders and were brave in supporting Islam and defeating the disbelievers. So God, glory be to Him, guides whom He wills. When God knows goodness in a person's heart, and we ask God to make our hearts and yours like this, He guides him to Islam. ﴿O Prophet, say to those among your captives: If God knows any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you and will forgive you﴾ [al-Anfal 70]. When God knows goodness in a servant's heart, He grants him success and guides him, and even if he strays, what is the outcome? Guidance; the outcome is that God guides him.
﴿And whomever God sends astray, you will not find for him a way﴾. ﴿A way﴾ is an indefinite noun in a context of negation, ﴿then you will not find for him a helper﴾ [an-Nisa' 52], so it encompasses every way. There can be no way for one whom God wills to be astray; we ask God to guide us and you to His straight path, and to set right our hearts and our deeds.
* Student: Shaykh, this was difficult for me: the mention of God, blessed and exalted, [that] they "do not remember God except a little," and although the hypocrites are not [...], how do they remember?
* Shaykh: Yes, perhaps something flickers in their hearts to some extent. As for remembrance by the tongue and the limbs, there is no difficulty; God mentions their remembrance by tongue and limbs without difficulty. But remembrance of God by the heart, which is what we said occurs in the heart, may occur to his mind. This is why He said: ﴿That is because they believed and then disbelieved﴾ [al-Munafiqun 3].
* Student: Is a hypocrite permitted to marry believing women [...]?
* Shaykh: Whoever's hypocrisy is known, no.
* Student: How, when we have judged him to be a Muslim?
* Shaykh: Outwardly. But when we know his hypocrisy, we know this man who leaves our gatherings of remembrance and goes to the disbelievers and the wicked and is with them. Therefore whoever's hypocrisy is known, it is obligatory to kill him. Is his repentance accepted or not? There is a difference of opinion among the scholars, and the correct view is that it is accepted.
However, the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, knew some hypocrites with certainty, yet he did not kill them, out of fear of repelling people from Islam; for this reason he said: "The people should not say that Muhammad kills his companions."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4905) and Muslim (2584/63) from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah.]] This is a point that must be noticed: if we know the hypocrisy of a person, it is obligatory to apply to him the rulings of apostasy; but we should not say what the Messenger ﷺ said. As for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, he had the right to refrain from killing them, for this great benefit.
* Student: Shaykh, may God bless you. It is known that the category of actions is broader than the category of attributes. So what is the criterion for the attributes that are applied to God, the Mighty and Majestic, derived from actions?
* Shaykh: Every action from which an attribute can be applied to Him.
* Student: Then what is His attribute in some of them? The category of actions is broader.
* Shaykh: The category of actions is known; every action from which an attribute is derived. When He says: ﴿God mocks them﴾ [al-Baqarah 15], it affirms the attribute of mockery.
* Student: Can we say: God is the Mocker, meaning the one who mocks?
* Shaykh: Yes, that is valid.
* Student: Shaykh, cursing: can we say God is the Curser?
* Shaykh: "Cursing one" (la'in), yes. God curses, and we say He is the one who curses those who deserve the curse, and we say the curse of God is upon those who deserve it.
* Student: So the category of actions is like the category of attributes.
* Shaykh: It is the same; this verb is derived from the attribute. "Striking" (darib) is derived from where?
* Student: From striking.
* Shaykh: That is it.
* Student: "Wavering between that" — what does the referent of "that" (...)?
* Shaykh: "Between that" is explained by his saying, that is, between that state, which is that they are at times with the disbelievers and at times with the believers.
* Student: Shaykh, may God bless you. Suppose someone says: it is incumbent upon us to know whether God's address and His Messenger's address imply obligation or something less, such as recommendation and permissibility; because we would be strict with ourselves regarding obligations and lenient regarding what is below them. The Companions, by their understanding and their knowledge of the Arabic language, knew that this implies obligation.
* Shaykh: The commands are before us. The main point is that the first time you do not ask. As I told you: when something has occurred, when a violation has occurred, there is no harm in investigating, or when there is some kind of hardship, there is no harm in investigating, so that it may fall away from the person. But as for one who, at the very first, we say: "Do this; the Messenger commanded this; is it obligatory or recommended?" There is no doubt that this is hesitation.
* Student: Shaykh, regarding students of knowledge: do you advise them to ask about the easier option, since they might go to laypeople and be asked, and if they do not ask the scholars about this...
* Shaykh: Let me tell you about myself. I say: this is forbidden. If he says: is it prohibited? I say: this is forbidden, that is all. Likewise, they constantly press a person: "Is it haram?" I say: the Messenger forbade it, or God forbade it, and I am not responsible. If you are truly a listener and an obeyer, avoid it.
* Student: Shaykh, regarding His saying: ﴿then you will not find for him a way﴾, the subject, Shaykh, what is its estimated form: "you," referring to the Prophet ﷺ or to his community?
* Shaykh: We mentioned a rule about this: the address from God is either one for which evidence establishes that it is general to the Messenger and others, or that it is specific to the Messenger, or there is no evidence either way. The scholars differed on whether it includes the community, and the correct view is that it includes the community, either through the wording or through the ruling.
* Student: Shaykh, Ibn al-Qayyim al-Jawziyyah mentioned in his book Shifa' al-'Alil, in the chapter on guidance and misguidance, that he says: God guides only one whose locus is receptive to guidance, and sends astray one whose locus is not receptive to guidance.
* Shaykh: Yes, correct.
* Student: What is meant here by "locus"?
* Shaykh: That is, the heart. That is, whoever is a receptive locus for guidance, and whoever is a receptive locus for misguidance is led astray. This is like His saying: ﴿God knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am 124].
* Student: Shaykh, he cited the hadith: "When God, glory be to Him, created Adam, He took a handful of earth, and the children of Adam came according to the earth's variety: among them the wicked and among them the good-natured."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4693) and al-Tirmidhi (2955) from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]]
* Shaykh: Correct.
Student: How is it, Shaykh, that a person is created wicked and another created good?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. It may be that his nature from the origin is that he dislikes Islam, dislikes the commands, and the like.
