**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.

﴿O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah a clear case against yourselves?﴾ (144)

﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will not find for them a helper.﴾ (145)

﴿Except for those who repent, amend themselves, hold fast to Allah, and purify their religion for Allah. Those are with the believers, and Allah will give the believers a great reward.﴾ (146)

﴿What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And Allah is ever Appreciative and Knowing.﴾ (147) [An-Nisa 144–147]

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers﴾. The first: have we taken its benefits?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. Discussion of this kind of expression has preceded, and we mentioned that opening with the address (nida') serves to alert, and that opening with this description, the description of faith, indicates that complying with it is among the requirements of faith, and that opposing it is a deficiency in faith.

﴿O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers﴾, meaning: do not make them allies, because (ittakhadha) means (ja'ala), made or appointed. From it is the Almighty's saying: ﴿And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend﴾ [An-Nisa' 125], meaning He made him His intimate friend. Do not make them allies, meaning do not take them as protectors, trust them, support them, and attach your affairs to them, instead of the believers. This is because some believers may be weak in faith and weak in reliance upon Allah, so they lean on these disbelievers because of their strength, and take them as allies, and think that the believers do not reach their level. Without doubt this is a deficiency in faith and reliance. Allah has already said: ﴿Do they seek honor with them? Indeed, honor belongs entirely to Allah﴾ [An-Nisa' 139].

His saying ﴿instead of the believers﴾ means: other than them.

﴿Do you want to give Allah against yourselves a clear authority?﴾ This is an interrogative used in the sense of denunciation. It means: do you want, by taking the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, ﴿to give Allah﴾, that is, to make for Him, ﴿against yourselves a clear authority﴾, that is, a manifest, evident proof. This is because your being believers requires that you ally with the believers, not the disbelievers. So if you turn away from this obligation to allying with the disbelievers, you have made for Allah against you a clear authority by which you deserve Allah's punishment.

* In this noble verse there is evidence for the prohibition of taking disbelievers as allies, because Allah forbade it and warned against it. He forbade it in His saying ﴿do not take﴾, and warned against it in His saying ﴿Do you want to give Allah against yourselves a clear authority?﴾.

* Among the benefits of this verse: two loyalties cannot be combined, the loyalty to the disbelievers and the loyalty to the believers, because of His saying ﴿instead of the believers﴾. This does not mean that if they took both them and the believers as allies, that would be permissible. Rather, we say that His saying ﴿instead of the believers﴾ means that if you take the disbelievers as allies, you have turned away from the loyalty to the believers.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, glorified and exalted, has authority and proof over those who oppose His command. This is indicated by the Almighty's saying when mentioning the sending of the messengers: ﴿So that mankind will not have an argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [An-Nisa' 165].

So here, if He had not sent the messengers, the argument would belong to people against Allah. And when the messengers are sent and the rulings are explained, the argument belongs to Allah against whom? Against the believers.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of allying with the believers and supporting them, because the believers are brothers. Whatever befalls one of them has befallen the other, and any harm that occurs must be removed by all the believers according to their capacity and ability.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire﴾. The connection of this verse with the one before it is that those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers resemble the hypocrites, and the hypocrites are those who took the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Whoever takes them as allies has resembled the hypocrites, and the hypocrites have no share at all in the Hereafter, because they are in the lowest depth of the Fire, where they will abide; they will remain in it and will not come out of it.

Al-Darak (the lowest depth, a place of utmost descent) means the lowest place, beneath which there is nothing: ﴿the lowest depth of the Fire﴾. This does not mean that others will not be in it, but the hypocrites are in it with certainty, whereas others may be in it or may be in what is above it.

﴿And you will not find for them a helper﴾. To whom is the address in ﴿you will not find﴾? It is either to the Messenger (ﷺ), or to anyone to whom the address may be directed.

I have a reading: ﴿fi al-darki﴾, ﴿fi al-darakī﴾, meaning the opening of the rā' instead of its sukun (vowel-less pronunciation), and it is a Sab'i (canonical seven-fold) reading.

﴿In the lowest depth of the Fire, and you will not find for them a helper﴾, i.e., you will not find anyone who will prevent the punishment from them or help them in this state.

From this noble verse, there are the following points:

* It is evidence that the hypocrites are among the people of the Fire, because of His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites are in the lowest depth﴾.

* Also in it: that the Fire has levels (darakat), and the darak, as we have said, is the place of destruction; so every place that is lower than what is above it corresponds to the severity of the punishment.

* Also in it: that these hypocrites are in its lowest level. Does this mean that others do not share it with them? No, others may share it with them, but we are certain that the hypocrites are in the lowest level, whereas as for anyone else, we do not know; they may be in it, or they may not be in it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the hypocrites have no helper. In this world they may prevail through deception and trickery, but in the Hereafter they will not prevail, nor will they find anyone to help them; because of His saying: ﴿And you will not find for them a helper﴾.

Then He says: ﴿Except for those who repent, amend, hold fast to Allah, and devote their religion sincerely to Allah.﴾

﴿Except for those who repent﴾ from hypocrisy, meaning they return from hypocrisy to pure faith and sincere faith. ﴿And amend﴾, meaning they reform their deeds: instead of having been corrupters, they become reformers. This is because the saying of Allah the Exalted was already mentioned in Surah al-Baqarah: ﴿Verily, they are the corrupters﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:12]. So when they reform instead of having been corruptors, this is the second condition.

﴿And hold fast to Allah﴾: they hold fast to Him, meaning they rely upon Him and do not turn to anyone else for refuge, because the hypocrites' habit is to return to the disbelievers, to exalt the disbelievers and to seek protection with them. Here, they hold fast to Allah instead of holding fast to the disbelievers.

﴿And devote their religion sincerely to Allah﴾: ﴿their religion﴾ means their worship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so they do not associate anyone with Him in it. It has already been mentioned that among the characteristics of the hypocrites is that they ﴿show off to the people﴾. So when they remove this trait and devote their religion sincerely to Allah, He says: ﴿Then those will be with the believers﴾. They will not reach the rank and station of the believers except through these four attributes: the first attribute is repentance from hypocrisy; the second is amendment; the third is holding fast to Allah; and the fourth is devoting religion sincerely to Allah, ﴿they devote their religion sincerely to Allah﴾. He says: ﴿Then those will be with the believers﴾.

Then He says: ﴿And Allah will soon give the believers a great reward﴾. He did not say "and He will give them," but rather said ﴿Allah will soon give the believers﴾, so that it includes them and others, and so that they themselves are among the believers. They would not deserve this promise on their own, but rather He said: ﴿Allah will soon give the believers a great reward﴾.

* In this verse: the repentance of the hypocrite is accepted, but he will not be with the believers until he is characterized by the four attributes.

Scholars have differed on this matter, may Allah have mercy on them. Some scholars said: the repentance of the hypocrite is not accepted, because nothing appeared from him except Islam; in fact, he is the one who ﴿when they meet those who believe, say, "We believe"﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:14]. So if they say that they believe and abandon hypocrisy, this is what they used to say before, while denying hypocrisy. Accordingly, their repentance is not accepted, but they are to be killed, and their affair is with Allah: if they were truthful, Allah the Exalted will reward them for their truthfulness on the Day of Resurrection, and if they were liars, they will have the Fire. But we, in this world, do not accept their repentance.

However, the correct view is that their repentance is accepted, except that it is scrutinized more carefully than that of one whose disbelief is manifest, because the one whose disbelief is manifest declares it openly: he is either a disbeliever or a believer, and does not show that he is a believer while being a disbeliever. But the affliction is the hypocrite, and for this reason we must examine carefully, testing him going and returning.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever corrupts must reform in exchange for his corruption, and mere repentance is not sufficient; he must reform what he has corrupted.

On this basis, some scholars said: the innovator has no repentance. Why? Because he has corrupted nations who followed him in his innovation, so who will reform these nations? Accordingly, he has no repentance. But the correct view is that he has repentance, and that his reform of what he corrupted is to openly announce his return from the corruption he was upon, and to call to reform.

It is said that Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, may Allah have mercy on him, when he repented from Mu'tazilism, stood on Friday on the pulpit, removed his turban, and said: "As for what follows, whoever knows me knows me, and whoever does not know me, I am so-and-so." He then openly declared his return from Mu'tazilism and began refuting the Mu'tazilites. Such a man, who had been an innovator, a Mu'tazilite, has an accepted repentance. Why? Because he reformed what he had corrupted. For this reason, the danger of innovation is great, because of the corruption it causes.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever has been holding fast to other than Allah, one of the marks of the realization of his repentance is that he turns away from holding fast to other than Allah to holding fast to Allah, because the disease is treated with its opposing remedy. Holding fast to other than Allah is shirk, and it is treated by what? By holding fast to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. For every disease there is a remedy suited to it.

* Also among the benefits of the verse: that the completion of repentance for the polytheist is sincerity, as in His saying: ﴿and devote their religion sincerely to Allah﴾, and the hypocrites have shirk, because they show off to the people and do not remember Allah except a little.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever is characterized by these attributes will be with the believers, even if he was previously a hypocrite, because these attributes rescue him from hypocrisy to faith. This companionship with the believers is without doubt a lofty rank, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast of truth, the martyrs, and the righteous﴾ [an-Nisa' 4:69].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the promise to the believers of what is the truest of promises, which is His saying: ﴿And Allah will soon give the believers a great reward﴾. "Ajran" means reward. Allah named the reward "ajr" out of His bounty, as if it were in the position of a laborer's wage which must be given to him. This is a commitment from Allah, Glorified and Exalted, which He has taken upon Himself: that He will reward the believers with a great reward. This great reward occurs in this world and in the Hereafter. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [an-Nahl 16:97].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 147:

Then He said: ﴿What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe?﴾ ﴿What would He do﴾: here "ma" (what) is interrogative, meaning: what thing would Allah do with your punishment?

﴿If you are grateful and believe﴾ means: if you thank Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for His blessings, carry out His obedience and believe, then Allah will not punish you, because you do not deserve punishment according to His promise. So what would Allah do to you if you give thanks to Him and believe in Him?

﴿And Allah is Ever Appreciative, All-Knowing﴾. He has obligated Himself to reward the believers with a great reward, and this great reward is in this world and in the Hereafter. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [An-Nahl 97].

Then He said: ﴿What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe?﴾ [An-Nisa 147]. ﴿What would He do﴾: here "ma" is interrogative, meaning: what thing would Allah do with your punishment? ﴿If you are grateful and believe﴾ means: if you thank Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for His blessings, carry out His obedience and believe, then Allah will not punish you, because you do not deserve punishment according to His promise. So what would Allah do to you if you give thanks to Him and believe in Him?

﴿And Allah is Ever Appreciative, All-Knowing﴾: Allah is Appreciative. Appreciative of whom? Of those among His servants who deserve thanks, those who stand in obedience to His command, as He said: ﴿Is the reward for good anything but good?﴾ [Ar-Rahman 60]. ﴿All-Knowing﴾ means All-Knowing of those among His servants who deserve thanks, and they are those who stood in His obedience.

* From this verse are the benefits: that Allah, the Exalted, is free of need for the punishment of creation if they are thankful and believe.

* And among its benefits: whoever does not thank Allah or does not believe in Him is exposed to retribution and punishment. Because Allah, the Exalted, negated punishment for those who are thankful and believe, this indicates that whoever is not thankful and does not believe is exposed to punishment. This is the reality. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿And beware of a trial which will not strike only those who have wronged among you specifically. And know that Allah is severe in punishment﴾ [Al-Anfal 25].

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of these two names from the names of Allah, namely: Ash-Shakir (the Appreciative) and Al-Alim (the All-Knowing).

If someone says: How does Allah thank His servants?

We say: by rewarding them for what they did more than what they did, ﴿Is the reward for good anything but good?﴾ [Ar-Rahman 60].

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged﴾. We will stop here.

* Student: May Allah reward you with good, Shaykh. Regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Messengers as bringers of good tidings and warners, so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [An-Nisa 165]. Some people said: the proof here is the proof regarding matters of obligation and legal worship. As for proof regarding matters of tawhid (monotheism), it is established by the implication of the covenant verse. So whoever opposes matters of tawhid is a disbeliever, eternal in the Fire, even if the call of the messengers never reached him. What is your view?

* The Shaykh: This is not correct. We say: who specified this? The covenant verse does not mean that a person is punished for a matter he has no knowledge or awareness of. It is what Allah has instilled in souls: "His parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian."

* The Student: They said, O Shaykh: in the verse, Allah said ﴿that you may say﴾ in Surat al-A'raf, ﴿that you may say: "There came to us no bringer of good tidings nor warner"﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 19].

* The Shaykh: No.

* The Student: I forgot it.

* The Shaykh: Help him.

* The Students: ﴿That you may say: "Only our fathers associated others with Allah before, and we were descendants after them"﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿Lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection: "Indeed, we were of this unaware." Or [lest] you should say: "Only our fathers associated others with Allah before, and we were descendants after them"﴾ [Al-A'raf 172-173]. This is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 22], and the second verse: ﴿And indeed, we are following in their footsteps as those who are guided﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 23]. And there must be knowledge, otherwise how would a person worship his Lord while he does not know?

* Student: Shaykh, we mentioned that by the sending of messengers, the proof of Allah is established against the believers.

* The Shaykh: Against the servants.

* Student: Shaykh, you said: "the believers."

* The Shaykh: No, against the servants.

* Student: Is trade with the disbelievers, and likewise when (...), and likewise matters of buying and selling (...), does this make one among the allies (awliya') of the disbelievers?

* The Shaykh: Dealing with disbelievers in trade is not wilayah (loyal alliance). Wilayah is support and reliance upon them, and fearing harm from them. As for trade, there is no harm in it. But there is no doubt that if a person is faced with the choice of trading with a disbeliever or with a believer, then trading with the believer is undoubtedly more preferable.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, in some countries where disbelievers live and work, over time you find the Muslim no longer hates them, and perhaps through habit the hatred in his heart for the disbelievers disappears, and he may befriend them. Is this included in taking them as allies?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. There is no doubt that this reflects a flaw in religion, because this is a type of loyalty. It is obligatory that I deal with them for my own benefit, not for their benefit, and that I treat them in a manner whose effect does not reach the heart. Otherwise, it is known that when a person is treated kindly by someone, he will love him. If, for example, a disbelieving doctor treats a patient whom Muslim doctors had failed to treat, and he recovers by Allah's permission, there is no doubt that love for this man will settle in his heart. But it is not a love that reaches the love of the religion; rather it is a natural love, that a person loves whoever treats him well.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, can one derive from His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire﴾ [An-Nisa 145] that the hypocrites are worse in disbelief than some original disbelievers?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, without doubt, and the hypocrite is worse, because the hypocrite combines two things: disbelief and deception. For this reason Allah said: ﴿They are the enemy, so beware of them﴾ [Al-Munafiqun 4]. He confined enmity to them because of the great corruptions that occur among them.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, a person finds it embarrassing to greet some disbelievers..

* The Shaykh: Embarrassing?

* The Student: For example, when we see a person pass by some Christians from the people of our country, workers or so on, and he only gestures to them. Is this permissible?

* The Shaykh: No, he should not gesture to them. But is he certain that these are disbelievers?

* The Student: Yes. They do not pray beside you; some of them do not pray (...). At prayer time they go out and wait?

* The Shaykh: Then do not greet them.

* The Student: Shaykh, even if it is for the sake of da'wah (calling to Islam) (...) like this..

* The Shaykh: Da'wah is something else. But this one who passes by on the road, will he stop to call them?

* The Student: No, I mean..

* The Shaykh: For the sake of ta'lif (winning their hearts), you mean?

* The Student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Even for the sake of ta'lif. As for the Prophet, he said: "Do not initiate greeting the Jews and the Christians with salam."[[Narrated by at-Tirmidhi (1602) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]]

* Student: Even a gesture, Shaykh (...)?

* The Shaykh: They count it as a greeting. Perhaps they consider a gesture greater than salam. But as happens with some people who work in a department whose head is a non-Muslim, here if he enters he must greet, because he is compelled to do so. Perhaps if he did not greet, this disbeliever's heart would be filled with rage against him and he would obstruct his progress. So such a person may say, for example: "Good morning." Good morning to whom?

* Student: To the Muslims.

* The Shaykh: No, to himself and to the Muslims. He did not mean "good morning" to you, though he may understand it as directed to him, and this is a permissible form of tawriyah (equivocation).

* Student: Pardon me, Shaykh, if I stay, how should I act with them?

* The Shaykh: With whom?

* The Student: With these people (...) every day, and he smiles in my face?

* The Shaykh: If they smile, smile back, but do not initiate with them.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "People should not say that Muhammad kills his companions"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4905) and Muslim (2584/63) from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah.]]. Shaykh, this has passed in the previous lesson. Now we do not have this. If hypocrisy appears, do we kill? (...) Why?

* The Shaykh: Because the Messenger ﷺ was a caller (da'i) calling people to the religion of Allah. If he were a caller calling people to the religion of Allah and urging them to enter it, and then he started killing his companions, people would flee from him.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No, not at all, this is not correct. Firstly, the Islamic nation, as you see now, is dispersed, each one is a commander over a country. Secondly, people would not perceive it, because the authority of these commanders is like the authority of the Messenger.

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged. And Allah is ever Hearing, Knowing (148). Whether you disclose a good deed or conceal it, or pardon an evil, indeed Allah is ever Pardoning, Powerful (149). Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and wish to make distinction between Allah and His messengers, and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and wish to adopt a way in between (150). Those are the disbelievers in truth, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment (151). And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and make no distinction between any of them—those, He will give them their rewards, and Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa' 148–152].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged﴾. It is not hidden that this sentence is a negated declarative statement: ﴿Allah does not like the public mention of evil﴾. The "public mention of evil" (al-jahr bil-su') means that one says: "So-and-so wronged me, so-and-so took my right, so-and-so denied it," and the like. Allah does not like this, except from one who has been wronged, by having his right taken or being transgressed against. The love of Allah is not negated in his case. An example of the wronged person: if a man is harmed by his neighbor, and he goes on to speak before the ruler, or before the emir, or before whoever can remove his injustice, and makes this evil publicly known. The meaning of "public" is not that he raises his voice among people; the meaning is that he explains it to others, for this is one who has been wronged, and he is entitled to say so. From this is the story of the neighbor who used to harm his neighbor: "The Prophet ﷺ commanded that his belongings be taken out of his house, so people would pass by and say, 'What is this?' and he would say, 'My neighbor harmed me.'"[[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah (25807) from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Yusuf.]] In this there is a disgracing of the neighbor, by speech or by action? By action.

And among the public mention of evil by one who has been wronged: if a person insults you in front of you and says, "You are stingy, you are a coward, you are a fool," and the like, then you may respond to him with the same defect with which he described you, saying: "You are the fool, you are the coward, you are the stingy," as he said, without adding anything more. This is based on the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you﴾ [Al-Baqarah 194], and His saying: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the same as you were punished with﴾ [An-Nahl 126], and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever retaliates after being wronged, those—there is no blame upon them. The blame is only upon those who wrong people and oppress throughout the earth without right. Those will have a painful punishment﴾ [Ash-Shura 41–42], and the saying of the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family: "The two who revile each other—what they say is upon the one who began, so long as the wronged one does not transgress."[[Narrated by Muslim (2587/68) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]

All these texts indicate that it is permissible to speak openly by one who is what? Wronged.

Among this is what a person confides to his friend and companion in complaining of his condition, such as if a person was wronged by someone and came to his friend speaking and saying: "So-and-so did such and such to me, did such and such to me, did such and such to me."

Also among this is the wife complaining of what occurs from her husband to her sisters, to her mother, and the like; because all of these are what? Wronged. And Allah, the Exalted, has excepted the one who has been wronged.

Also among this: if someone says, "May Allah curse you," you say, "May Allah curse you, you," because this is transgression in the same manner as he transgressed against you.

Based on this we say: the public mention of evil speech, when it comes from one who has been wronged, the love of Allah is not negated from him. This is from the blessing of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the removal of hardship from the Ummah. For if Allah did not like the public mention of evil speech even from the wronged, hardship would result, because the wronged person nearly has his chest split until he speaks of what is in his chest of injustice, and so the matter becomes lighter for him.

﴿And Allah is ever Hearing, Knowing﴾: ﴿Hearing﴾ of your words, ﴿Knowing﴾ of what is in your hearts. That is: beware of Him; beware of saying what He does not approve, beware of concealing in your breasts what He does not approve.

* In this noble verse: affirmation of love for Allah, meaning that Allah loves. The indication is that we derived the affirmation from the negation. How do we derive affirmation from negation? Because this negation is restricted to a specific situation, which makes it evidence that love is established in all other cases. The love—the love of Allah Mighty and Majestic for the servant—is the ultimate goal a person seeks and the most perfect rank of a human being. For this reason Allah said: ﴿Say: If you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ [Al 'Imran 31]. The answer did not come in the expected form, which would be "then follow me, you will be truthful in your claim." Rather He said: ﴿follow me, Allah will love you﴾. This is the ultimate goal, and the love of Allah Mighty and Majestic is attained by this condition, which is an easy condition for whomever Allah makes it easy for—we ask Allah to make it easy for us and for you—and it is what? Following the Messenger, peace be upon him, outwardly and inwardly, in belief, speech, and action. If you realize this, the love of Allah will be attained by you.

A people denied the love of Allah, such as the Ash'aris—we ask Allah to pardon their dead and guide their living—they denied love and said: Allah does not love. But their denial is not a denial of rejection; for if it were a denial of rejection they would have disbelieved, because it is a denial of what Allah affirmed for Himself. Rather it is a denial by interpretation; they intended thereby to declare Allah free of imperfection, but they erred. They said: love occurs only between those who are alike, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is distinct from creation: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾ [Ash-Shura 11]. So what then is the meaning of love which came in the Book and the Sunnah? They said: love is benevolence, so they interpreted it as a matter separate and detached from Allah, or as the will to benevolence, because will is established for Allah Mighty and Majestic in their view.

It is said to them: Is benevolence anything other than the fruit of love? And is the will to benevolence anything other than the fruit of love? For Allah does not show benevolence to one whom He does not love, except as a gradual leading on. For this reason, when you see Allah bestowing blessings upon a servant while he persists in his sins, know that this is istidraj (gradual enticement): ﴿And those who deny Our signs—We will lead them step by step from where they do not know﴾ [Al-A'raf 182].

So our creed is that Allah Mighty and Majestic loves, and that He is loved, exalted be He, and that His love is the highest of ranks and the best of stations.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the excellence of Islam, and that Islam calls to overlooking and not publicly mentioning evil, and not disgracing anyone with evil. For this reason backbiting is among the major sins, and it is: mentioning your brother with what he dislikes.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the justice of Islam. The indication of this is that the wronged person is permitted to speak openly, but in proportion to his injustice, without exceeding it. If he exceeds, then as the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The blame is upon the one who began, so long as the wronged one does not transgress."[[Narrated by Muslim (2587/68) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Islamic religion does not suppress souls, but widens them, expands the chest, and brings joy. For this reason a person is forbidden to expose himself to what causes grief, worry, whisperings, and illusions. Even the Prophet, peace be upon him, said about one who doubts whether wind came out of him or not: "He should not leave until he hears a sound or smells an odor."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (137) and Muslim (361/98) from the hadith of the paternal uncle of 'Abbad ibn Tamim.]] The meaning: until he is certain with a certainty like the sun. As for mere imagination that something came out of his belly, or from his behind, or from his private part, this must be cast aside. Why? So that the person does not fall into wavering and hesitation.

The Islamic religion wants you to always be in joy, always cheerful. The indication of this from this verse is that the wronged person is permitted to speak of evil, to what extent? To the extent of his injustice; because that is undoubtedly a release for himself.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of these two names of Allah Mighty and Majestic, namely: As-Sami' (the Hearing) and Al-'Alim (the Knowing). As for As-Sami', the scholars said it is divided into two types: hearing in the sense of perceiving what is heard, and hearing in the sense of responding. The hearing in the sense of perceiving what is heard also has varieties: sometimes it is meant to show the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah of everything heard, sometimes it is meant as support and victory, and sometimes it is meant as a threat, according to what the situation and context require. From the first is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah﴾ [Al-Mujadilah 1]. That woman was in the chamber of the Prophet, peace be upon him, on the earth, while the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is in the heaven above His Throne. And 'A'ishah said: "Praise be to Allah, who has encompassed all voices with His hearing. I was in the chamber, and some of her speech was hidden from me, yet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'He has heard the speech of the one who argues,' and He hears your dialogue."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (7385m) and al-Nasa'i (3460) from the hadith of 'A'ishah, and the wording is his.]] This is hearing meant to show what? The all-encompassing knowledge of Allah of everything heard.

Sometimes it is meant as support and victory, like the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted, to Musa and Harun: ﴿Do not fear; indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing﴾ [Taha 46], meaning: I will support you and grant you victory. In this verse it may also be meant as a threat, a threat to whom? A threat to Pharaoh.

As for that which is for threat, like His saying: ﴿Allah has heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich"﴾ [Al 'Imran 181]. Who are these? They are the Jews, who said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich﴾. Allah said: ﴿We will record what they said and their killing of the prophets without right, and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning"﴾ [Al 'Imran 181]. There is no doubt that this is intended as a threat.

Likewise His saying: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 80]. So it is heard and recorded, and when will it be read? On the Day of Resurrection: ﴿And every person's fate We have fastened to his neck, and We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find wide open. "Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner"﴾ [Al-Isra' 13–14]. Some of the early generation said: "By Allah, he has been just to you who made you your own reckoner."[[Narrated by Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd (1563), 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Tafsir (2953), and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (8/70) from the hadith of al-Hasan al-Basri, with the wording: "O son of Adam, he has been just to you, the one who created you; he made you the reckoner of your own self."]] Take this book, read it, and reckon your own self.

The second category of hearing is what? The hearing of responding: that Allah responds, and this occurs when it is connected to supplication or the like, such as the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾ [Ibrahim 39], meaning: the one who responds to it. It is not the intent of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, that Allah merely hears his supplication, because hearing supplication is undoubtedly a perfection, and Allah is perceiver of everything heard. Rather the purpose of the supplicant's supplication is what? The response. So the meaning of ﴿the Hearer of supplication﴾ is: the one who responds to supplication. They said: from this is the saying of the worshipper: "Allah hears whoever praises Him," meaning: He responds. This is true, and it is supported by the fact that it is construed with the preposition lam: "Allah hears whoever praises Him" (sami'a Allahu liman hamidah). Had the meaning been perceiving the praise or perceiving the words of the praiser, he would have said "sami'a Allahu man hamidah."

As for Al-'Alim, this is the broadest of all: the knowledge of Allah, exalted be He, encompasses everything, Mighty and Majestic. He encompasses the apparent and the hidden, the past and the future, the necessary, the possible, and the impossible. For this reason there is nothing more general than knowledge, as far as I can recall now; knowledge is extremely comprehensive. It relates to the past and the future. Among this is the saying of Musa, peace be upon him, when Pharaoh asked him: ﴿What is the state of the former generations?﴾ [Taha 51]. He said: ﴿Its knowledge is with my Lord in a Record; my Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ [Taha 52], glorified and exalted be He. ﴿Neither errs﴾ through ignorance, ﴿nor forgets﴾ through heedlessness; rather He, Mighty and Majestic, is knowing of everything, and does not forget the past, whereas other than Allah among the knowing are subject to forgetting.

Likewise, the knowledge of Allah Mighty and Majestic encompasses the apparent and the hidden: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him﴾ [Qaf 16]. Nothing is more hidden than this: what your soul whispers to you and speaks to you of, Allah knows it. As for the apparent, its apparentness is known to Allah. Likewise, the knowledge of Allah encompasses the necessary, the possible, and the impossible. As for the impossible, like His saying: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ [Al-Anbiya' 22]. Is this a report about knowledge or about something other than knowledge? About knowledge. And it is well known that it is impossible for there to be gods in the heavens and the earth other than Allah; it is impossible to the utmost degree. So this is a report about something impossible, issued from knowledge. As for knowledge of the necessary, it is His knowledge of Himself and of His names and attributes, for this is knowledge of the necessary, and He knows Himself better than others do.

As for His relation to the possible, it is His knowledge of what happens in the universe. Everything that happens in the universe, apart from what pertains to Allah Mighty and Majestic, is what? Possible; because the whole universe is originated after having not been. "Allah was, and nothing was before Him,"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (7418) from the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn.]] and in another wording: "and nothing was with Him,"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3191) from the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn, with the wording: "and nothing was other than Him."]] so the whole universe is originated, and the whole universe is subject to cessation, because every originated thing is subject to cessation, as evidenced by its non-existence before its existence.

The word "subject to" (qabil) does not mean that everything existent is perishing; rather it is capable of perishing. We say this so that the soul is not raised as an objection against us: the soul was created after non-existence but remains and does not perish; the youths and the houris in Paradise are created but do not perish, they remain forever and ever; Paradise too is created and remains forever and ever; Hellfire is created and remains forever and ever. For this reason we say: every existent is subject to what? To cessation, not that it is ceasing; because some created things do not cease. But its being originated after not having been is evidence that it belongs to the category of the possible, capable of non-existence and existence. The reasoning: if it were not capable of existence, it would not have come into existence; and if it were not capable of non-existence, it would not have been made non-existent at all.

The point is that the knowledge of Allah, exalted be He, encompasses everything. O my brothers, our belief in the knowledge of Allah is not merely to believe in this great, vast, and comprehensive attribute; rather what matters is that we beware lest He know in our hearts what He does not approve of us, or know of our actions what He does not approve of, or of our words what He does not approve of, or of what we leave undone what He does not approve of. This is what matters.

For this reason the student of knowledge must focus on the behavioral benefits derived from the names and attributes of Allah, not on their divisions, their categories, their generality, or their comprehensiveness. No! The most important thing is that you correct your method and your conduct. For this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them﴾ [Al-A'raf 180]; worship Him by them, that you worship Him according to the requirements of these names. And the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah has ninety-nine names; whoever enumerates them enters Paradise."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2736) and Muslim (2677/6) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] And among enumerating them is worshipping Allah according to their requirements. May Allah grant us and you success in that.

**Student:** If someone says that God's knowledge, may He be exalted, of things that will happen on earth cannot be possible, because when He knew that a thing would come to be, that thing became necessary?

**Shaykh:** No, that is a mistake, a mistake. It is necessary to occur because God has informed of it, but its origin is possible.

**Student:** If a generous man says to another man, "You are stingy," how should the second respond, if he is generous?

**Shaykh:** Yes, and is the one who says it generous?

**Student:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** Yes, in this case he says: "Sufficient for you is God, and He is the best Guardian" (﴿حَسْبُكَ اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ﴾). "God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Guardian" (﴿حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ﴾), because if he says, "You are stingy," he becomes a liar. But perhaps he will find a quality that is the opposite of stinginess.

**Student:** And should he say it with that? If he is a coward, would he say..?

**Shaykh:** Yes, indeed, this is what I wanted to say. I say: perhaps he will find another quality that is equivalent to stinginess, because a coward is stingy with his soul, and not spending is stinginess with wealth.

**Student:** Is this not retaliation in kind?

**Shaykh:** No, it is like it. The intent is a blameworthy quality that corresponds to this. But if he says, "You are an innovator (mubtadi')," he has not become like him.

**Student:** Shaykh, may God pardon you, what is the rule for the deeds for which retaliation is always permissible?

**Shaykh:** How?

**Student:** That is, sometimes he says, for example, "May God's curse be upon you," and we say, "May God's curse be upon you." But if he, for example, meets him with (...) what (...).

**Shaykh:** No, this is inherently forbidden in itself, and what we mentioned is forbidden because it is aggression against another. That is, for example, my saying, "May God curse him," or describing him as stingy, or the like. It is forbidden only because it is aggression against another. So if it is aggression against another, and then he violates my sanctity, I have the right to violate his sanctity. But what is forbidden as a right of God, you cannot match it.

**Student:** Burning with fire, Shaykh?

**Shaykh:** Whoever does this, burn him. That is, if a person kills someone by fire, we kill him by it.

**Student:** Shaykh, we cannot distinguish between the deeds that are a right of God and between..?

**Shaykh:** No, this is retaliation: ﴿فَمَنِ اعْتَدَى عَلَيْكُمْ فَاعْتَدُوا عَلَيْهِ بِمِثْلِ مَا اعْتَدَى عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Baqarah 194]. And for this reason, "The Prophet ﷺ crushed the head of the Jew between two stones."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2746) and Muslim (1672/17) from the hadith of Anas.]]

**Student:** If someone insults another by his father, may he return it even by insulting his father?

**Shaykh:** The Prophet ﷺ said, among what he counted as major sins: "May Allah curse one who curses his parents." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how does a man curse his parents?" He said: "He insults the father of a man, so he insults his father, and he insults his mother, so he insults his mother."[[Recorded by Muslim (90/149) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr, with the wording: "Among the major sins is a man's insulting his parents."]] The apparent meaning of this hadith is that there is no harm if he insults my father, and my father is free from this insult. I insult his father, because the intent is to humiliate this man, not to humiliate the father; it is to humiliate the man.

**Student:** Shaykh, may God reward you with good. An exception that comes after a prohibition conveys affirmation. For example: ﴿لَا يُحِبُّ اللَّهُ الْجَهْرَ﴾ and ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ ظُلِمَ﴾ [an-Nisa' 148]. So, whom does He love? He loves the loud speaking..

**Shaykh:** No. ﴿لَا يُحِبُّ اللَّهُ الْجَهْرَ بِالسُّوءِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ إِلَّا مَنْ ظُلِمَ﴾. As for the one who has been wronged, we do not say that the love is negated from him..

**Student:** So does He love him?

**Shaykh:** No. He may be loved and He may not be loved. For this reason we say: the one who has been wronged has the right to act, and the negation of love is negated from him. And it may be that for the one who has been wronged, it is better that he pardons and overlooks.

**Student:** For this reason came (...) ﴿وَلَئِنْ صَبَرْتُمْ لَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لِلصَّابِرِينَ﴾ [an-Nahl 126].

**Shaykh:** Yes indeed, that is it. It does not mean that when someone is wronged, God loves that he speak loudly. No. The one who has been wronged, the negation of love is negated from him. Is it clear?

**Student:** May God be good to you. A man who is an innovator and calls to innovation, may you mention him and his innovation to people?

**Shaykh:** Yes, you warn against him, as sincere counsel to God and His Messenger.

(...) The apparent meaning of the hadith is that whoever intends a good deed and whoever intends an evil deed, they know that, but by the knowledge of God, may He be mighty and majestic.

**Student:** How (...).

**Shaykh:** That is, they know by God's knowledge, meaning that God informs them of this.

**Student:** Shaykh, may God bless you, O Shaykh. Some of the scholars who are recognized for their knowledge say: a person is not counted as an innovator unless the proof has been established against him. Before the proof is established, even if he falls into innovation, we do not call him an innovator?

**Shaykh:** That is not the apparent meaning. The apparent meaning is what I mentioned to you. Does he not follow this method? That is, the innovation of the Ash'aris is not only in the attributes, but in the attributes, in the acts of the servants, in divine decree, in faith. But if a man errs in some issue, this does not count him as an innovator. One does not say, "He is an Ash'ari," for example. I gave you an example from the schools of jurisprudence.

**Student:** May God bless you. How does God, glorified and exalted, praise those who pardon people, while in another verse He addresses the believers that one may transgress against him with the like of what he transgressed against him? How (...)?

**Shaykh:** Because pardon is restricted. Not every pardon is beloved to God. God restricted pardon by His saying: ﴿فَمَنْ عَفَا وَأَصْلَحَ﴾ [ash-Shura 40]. So if pardon does not bring about reform, do not pardon.

**Student:** That is, now if someone insults me, is it better that I remain silent or..?

**Shaykh:** If you think that your silence will lead to the man's aggression and his domination over you and others, then insult him in whatever way he insulted you. And if you think that your silence will not produce this corruption, and perhaps by it the corruption of quarreling will be removed, which may lead to enmity and hatred and perhaps to fighting, then pardon.

**Student:** So the matter is a matter of benefits and harms?

**Shaykh:** Yes indeed.

**Student:** Shaykh, may God bless you all. Sometimes a person wants to advise his brother to do good, but he himself, that is, does not practice this good, so he holds back and says: "I fear that I will fall under the threat of the one whose intestines spill out in the Fire, and he goes around it as a donkey goes around a millstone"?[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (3267) from the hadith of Usama, with the wording: "The donkey goes around with its millstone."]]

**Shaykh:** Is the Messenger's saying, peace and blessings be upon him, here meant to prevent people from enjoining good and forbidding evil, or to warn them against being those who command and do not act?

**Students:** The second.

**Shaykh:** The second. So, pass by, then shame yourself. Say: "How do you command people to do this thing while you do not do it?" And likewise the reverse regarding prohibition. Do not think that the Messenger said this so that he would warn us from commanding people and not doing it. Rather, he warns us from commanding good and then persisting in abandoning it.

**Student:** Shaykh, God, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿لَا يُحِبُّ اللَّهُ الْجَهْرَ بِالسُّوءِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ﴾. Shaykh, does "speech" include the act of (...)?

**Shaykh:** No, but this is the predominant meaning (...) your ignorance of speech.

**Student:** ﴿وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَتَّخِذُوا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ سَبِيلًا (150) أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْكَافِرُونَ حَقًّا وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابًا مُهِينًا (151) وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَلَمْ يُفَرِّقُوا بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ أُولَئِكَ سَوْفَ يُؤْتِيهِمْ أُجُورَهُمْ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾ [an-Nisa' 150–152].

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿Whether you disclose a good deed or conceal it, or pardon an evil, indeed Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent.﴾ His saying, ﴿Whether you disclose﴾, is the conditional clause. As for the response to the condition, it is said that it is omitted, and it is said that it is His saying: ﴿indeed Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent﴾. Although, on the surface, there is no apparent connection between this clause and the condition, it does point to it, and we will discuss this, God willing.

He says: ﴿Whether you disclose a good deed or conceal it﴾. ﴿Tubdū﴾ means "you display" (tuzhirū). How do we know that ibdā' means izhār? From the mention of its counterpart, which is His saying: ﴿or conceal it﴾.

This is a useful principle in tafsir: the meaning of some words may be hidden from you, so look at what corresponds to them. For example, the saying of Allah, ﴿So go forth in separate groups or go forth all together﴾ [An-Nisa 71]. If someone asked you: what is the meaning of (thubāt)? You would know its meaning from the mention of its counterpart, which is His saying: ﴿or go forth all together﴾, so the meaning of (thubāt) is: separately (furādā).

So, whether you display good or conceal it, you do not lose its reward, and you will be rewarded for it, because good is sought and beneficial, whether displayed or hidden. In contrast to that: ﴿or pardon an evil﴾. ﴿Taʿfū﴾: pardon (al-ʿafw) is releasing someone from the liability (tabiʿa). So the meaning of ﴿pardon an evil﴾ is: you absolve the one who wronged you of the liability for his evil.

His saying, ﴿an evil﴾, means: from that which harms, whether by word or deed. ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent﴾ means: He is possessed of pardon while having the power to take revenge on the one who wronged. If Allah, the Exalted, pardons the one who wrongs while having power, then you are even more deserving to pardon, because you do not have the power to defend yourselves and take revenge on the criminal as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has.

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Whether you disclose a good deed or conceal it﴾.

We benefit from this several benefits:

First among the benefits: good is good, whether it is displayed or concealed. If it is said: which is better, displaying or concealing? One might say concealing is better, and his statement may be countered by the fact that Allah began with disclosure, saying ﴿Whether you disclose﴾, and one begins with what is most important first. But what appears is that this depends on the interest (maslaha). If the interest lies in displaying, then display it, such as a man who is a role model: if he displays the good that he has, people will follow his example and do as he does. This is good, whether it is done generally or specifically, such as giving charity to a specific person so that people see him giving to him and follow his example, because many people now give to no one unless they know that a certain organization has given to them, such as the Charitable Society (Jamʿiyyat al-Birr al-Khayriyya), for example. So we say: disclosure and concealment depend on the interest. If the predominant interest does not lie in disclosure, then concealment is better, because of the saying of the Prophet ﷺ regarding those whom Allah will shade in His shade: «A man who gave charity and concealed it, until his left hand does not know what his right hand spends» [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1423), and Muslim (1031/91), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra.]].

Among the benefits of this noble verse: kindness to others is either by giving good, openly or secretly, or by warding off evil, which is by pardoning it, as in His saying: ﴿or pardon an evil﴾. So pardoning evil is good, ﴿indeed Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent﴾. From this is derived the virtue of pardoning evil. But do we say that pardon is better absolutely, or does it follow the interest? The latter: it follows the interest.

For this reason Allah restricted pardon elsewhere by His saying: ﴿So whoever pardons and reconciles, his reward is upon Allah﴾ [Ash-Shura 40]. So if pardon involves reform, it is better; and if pardon involves corruption, then retaliation is better. For example, if this man is wicked, and if we pardon him he would increase in his evil and aggression against people, here retaliation is better: first, to give the self its right, since the self certainly loves to be victorious; and second, to restrain his evil from people. So here retaliation is better. But if both matters are equal, then there is no doubt that pardon is better: first, because of the kindness it shows to the wrongdoer; and second, because Allah, the Exalted, loves those who pardon people.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: an indication that if you pardon creation with pardon in its proper place, then rejoice in Allah's pardon, by His saying: ﴿indeed Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent﴾, meaning whenever you pardon, Allah pardons you. This has many witnesses in the Sharia, among them the saying of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: «Allah is in the aid of the servant as long as the servant is in the aid of his brother» [[Narrated by Muslim (2699/38), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra.]], and among them: «Whoever is in the need of his brother, Allah is in his need» [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2442), and Muslim (2580/58), from the hadith of Ibn Umar.]], and among them: the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, and the evidence for this is abundant.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the grace of Allah, glorified and exalted, in pardoning what is His right, to the extent that He, Majestic and Exalted, forgives whoever does not associate anything with Him, freely; because Allah said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [An-Nisa 48]. Even if sins are great, Allah, the Exalted, forgives them if He wills, out of His grace.

Among them: the pardon of Allah, the Exalted, is the most complete type of pardon, because it is pardon with power; as His saying: ﴿indeed Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent﴾ indicates. From the combination of pardon and power there also arises an attribute of perfection, namely that Allah, glorified and exalted, pardons while having power to take revenge, and this is true pardon. As for pardon in the state of inability to take revenge, it is not true pardon. If someone transgressed against you while he was stronger than you in body and larger in frame, and you thought: if I take my right, I fear he will increase in beating and aggression, but you say: "O so-and-so, Allah forgives you," what kind of pardon is this? It is pardon with incapacity, pardon with incapacity. If there is a possibility that he would take his right, then he has a reward commensurate with that possibility; and if there is no possibility, then he has no reward, unless it is by bringing joy to the aggressor, in that if he refrains from transgression and reflects, he feels that the one wronged had pardoned him, so his heart is reassured; here he may be rewarded.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of these two names from the names of Allah, namely: al-ʿAfuw (with the emphasized waw) and al-Qadir, which indicate the affirmation of the attributes of pardon and power, because the principle in the matter of names and attributes is that every name includes an attribute, but not vice versa.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verses 150–151:

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and intend to make distinction between Allah and His messengers, and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and intend to adopt a way between that. Those are the disbelievers in truth. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers﴾. Disbelief in Allah and His messengers is that a person disbelieves in what must be believed in, whether it is disbelief in existence, in the existence of Allah; or disbelief in His lordship, by claiming that there is another lord with Him; or disbelief in His divinity, by worshipping others along with Him; or disbelief in His names and attributes, by denying and rejecting them. The essential point is that disbelief in Allah is the rejection of what must be believed concerning Allah. ﴿And His messengers﴾ likewise: the rejection of what must be believed concerning them. This is disbelief in the messengers.

﴿And intend to make distinction between Allah and His messengers﴾. He did not say, "Those who believe in Allah disbelieve in Allah," because if they disbelieve in some, they have disbelieved in all. ﴿And intend﴾, meaning, with their resolve, ﴿to make distinction between Allah and His messengers﴾, so they believe in Allah and disbelieve in the messengers, or they believe in some of the messengers and not others, as He said: ﴿and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others."﴾ This is common. For example, the Christians claim that they believe in Allah, do they not? They claim that they believe in Jesus, Moses, and those before them, so they say. But they disbelieve in Muhammad ﷺ, who is the best of the messengers. Thus they made distinction between Allah and His messengers: they believed in Allah and disbelieved in the messengers, and they also made distinction among the messengers, believing in some of them and disbelieving in others.

﴿And intend to adopt a way between that﴾, meaning a path that leads them to Allah. They think that by this action they have taken a good path that leads them to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, but, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Their effort is lost in the life of this world, while they think that they are doing well in work. Those are the ones who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord and in the meeting with Him﴾ [al-Kahf 104, 105].

﴿And intend to adopt a way between that﴾ (ﷺ). ﴿Those are the disbelievers in truth﴾. (Ulā'ika) is a subject (mubtada'), and (hum)?

* Student: A predicate (khabar).

* Shaykh: No, (hum) cannot come as the predicate here: ﴿Those are the disbelievers in truth﴾.

* Student: A separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl).

* Shaykh: A separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl).

If someone says: Could it not be that it is a subject and (al-kāfirūn) is the predicate of that subject, and the sentence is the predicate of the first subject?

We say: This is permissible, but it is contrary to what is preferable, because the apparent meaning of the Qur'an is that what follows them is the predicate of what precedes. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Perhaps we would follow the sorcerers if they were the victorious﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 40], and He did not say "they are the victorious." This indicates that in such a construction, (hu) is a separating pronoun with no place in the grammatical structure (i'rab).

Second: If we say that it is a separating pronoun with no place in i'rab, we no longer need a sentence to be the predicate of the subject; the subject and predicate become one unit, and the basic principle for predicates is that they are a single word rather than a sentence. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Those are the disbelievers﴾.

So (hum) is a separating pronoun. The separating pronoun conveys three things:

First: emphasis (tawkīd). Second: restriction (ḥaṣr). Third: distinguishing the predicate from the qualifier (tābi'); for when the separating pronoun comes, it is determined that what follows is the predicate, and when it does not come, it may be either a predicate or a qualifier. So when you say (Zayd al-fāḍil fī al-dars), it may be that (al-fāḍil) is an adjective, is it not? The meaning would then be that Zayd, the excellent one, is present in the lesson. But when you say (Zayd huwa al-fāḍil fī al-dars), it is determined that it is a predicate, and you have restricted him to excellence, so you say: Zayd is the excellent one, and his position is in the lesson.

In any case, the separating pronoun conveys three things.

* Student: It conveys emphasis, restriction, and separation between the predicate and what follows it.

* Shaykh: May Allah bless you.

﴿Those are the disbelievers in truth﴾. (ḥaqqan) here is in the accusative. But what is its meaning, or what is its i'rab according to the most correct view? We say: its i'rab is an infinitive (maṣdar) emphasizing the content of the sentence. The content of the sentence is ﴿Those are the disbelievers﴾; Allah affirmed for them that they are the disbelievers in truth. So (ḥaqqan) comes emphasizing the content of the sentence, because the reality of these people being disbelievers is understood from His saying ﴿Those are the disbelievers﴾. When (ḥaqqan) comes, it becomes an emphasis on the content of the sentence, and its governing verb is obligatorily omitted; the governing element of this infinitive is a verb implied in meaning, obligatorily omitted. So it is not correct to say: "Those are the disbelievers, it is established as true, truly," that is not correct; because it emphasizes the content of the sentence, so it is as if the content of the sentence were the omitted verb, and the two cannot be combined. For this reason Ibn Malik and other scholars mentioned that an infinitive emphasizing the content of a preceding sentence must have its governing verb omitted.

﴿Those are the disbelievers in truth, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.﴾ (a'tadnā) means: We prepared, so it has the meaning of a'dadnā. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾ [Ali 'Imran 131]. Here He said: ﴿We have prepared for the disbelievers﴾. In this context, ﴿We have prepared for the disbelievers﴾ departs from what the context requires; for what the context requires is to say: "We have prepared for them." "Those are the disbelievers in truth and We have prepared for them," because whenever a pronoun can be used, it is not replaced by something else, since mentioning the pronoun is clearer in the sentence and more concise. But here the pronoun was set aside in favour of the explicit noun matching its description. So what is the rhetorical point in this?

The rhetorical point is that this is an explicit noun in place of a pronoun, and the explicit noun in place of a pronoun has benefits. Among them: intending generality, and applying the description to the referent of the pronoun which, had the context required a pronoun, would have been the referent. Is this Arabic or non-Arabic? No, it is Nabataean! What are the benefits of using an explicit noun in place of a pronoun?

* Student: Intending generality.

* Shaykh: Intending generality, because if he had said "We have prepared for them a humiliating punishment," this would apply only to them, but ﴿We have prepared for the disbelievers﴾ applies to every disbeliever, whether these or others.

The second benefit: applying the description to the referent of the pronoun, which, had it not been for this explicit noun, would have been what? Present. Where is the referent of the pronoun, if there were a pronoun? Those who said: "We believe in some and disbelieve in others." A similar example is His saying: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers, and Jibril and Mika'il, then indeed Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqara 98]. He did not say "an enemy to Him," which is what the context would require. The two benefits are: intending generality, and passing the judgement of this description, which is disbelief, upon these people. In this verse, ﴿an enemy to the disbelievers﴾. The third benefit is observing the endings of the verses (fawāṣil al-āyāt).

* Student: We said: observing the endings of the verses. Where is the observance of the endings of the verses?

* Shaykh: In His saying in the verse of al-Baqara.

* Student: The apodosis of the conditional clause: ﴿indeed Allah is ever Pardoning and Powerful﴾. We said there is a difficulty in it, which you will be addressed to resolve?

* Shaykh: Yes, it is said that the apodosis of the conditional is omitted: "If you show good or conceal it or pardon an evil, then indeed you will be recompensed for that." And it is said that the answer given (i.e., the phrase ﴿indeed Allah is ever Pardoning, Powerful﴾) dispenses with this, and this is the better view, because as long as the ruling is known there is no need for an estimate.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: That is, the retraction of his confession. If Allah wills, when you become a judge and this matter confuses you, there is no harm in asking the scholars about it. You may be a judge now. I say: if you are a judge and this matter arises for you and confuses you, then ask the scholars. This matter (...).

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and intend to make distinction between Allah and His messengers, and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and intend to adopt a way between that. Those are the disbelievers in truth, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment. And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not distinguish between any of them, those – We will give them their rewards, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful. The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from heaven. But they had asked Moses for greater than that and said, "Show us Allah outright," so the thunderbolt seized them for their injustice. Then they took the calf after the clear proofs had come to them, but We pardoned that, and We gave Moses clear authority. And We raised over them the mount for their covenant and said to them, "Enter the gate prostrating," and We said to them, "Do not transgress in the Sabbath," and We took from them a solid covenant. So for their breaking of their covenant and their disbelief in the signs of Allah and their killing of the prophets without right and their saying, "Our hearts are closed," – rather, Allah has sealed them for their disbelief, so they believe not, except a few﴾ [al-Nisa' 150–155].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and intend to make distinction between Allah and His messengers, and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and intend to adopt a way between that. Those are the disbelievers in truth.﴾

* From the benefits of this noble verse: that disbelief in some messengers is disbelief in all of them, by His saying: ﴿Those are the disbelievers in truth.﴾

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the dominance of desire over many people, because those who make distinction between Allah and His messengers, or believe in some messengers and not others, are moved to that only by desire. The Jews say: "We do not believe in anyone other than Moses," and the Christians say: "We do not believe in anyone other than Jesus," purely out of desire.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: that disbelief in some messengers is disbelief in all of them. This is also shown by His saying: ﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 105], although Noah was the first of the messengers, yet He made his people's denial of him a denial of all the messengers, because disbelief in a messenger is as if it were disbelief in the category, that is, in the category of messengership. Otherwise, what is the difference between Muhammad, Jesus, Moses, Idris, Noah, and so on?

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: that these distinguishers say: "We are adopting a way between that," meaning: to please both sides. This does not save them from the punishment of Allah, nor does it save them from disbelief.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the censure of that method, that is, believing in some and not others, and that this is an ugly approach.

* From this follows: the censure of the people of kalam who wanted to combine the textual (sam') and rational ('aql) evidence regarding the attributes of Allah, saying: "We have taken this and that in order to reconcile the evidences." In fact they opposed all the evidences. They wanted to combine textual and rational evidence, but in reality they opposed both the text and reason, as is well known from their debates and the refutations against them.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the warning to the disbelievers of a humiliating punishment.

* And from its benefits: that the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, because they only distinguished between the messengers out of arrogance and desire, so there was prepared for them a punishment that humiliates and disgraces them. For this reason He said: ﴿We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.﴾

* And from its benefits: that the use of an explicit noun in place of a pronoun is not considered needless prolixity without benefit. The reason for this is that the pronoun is more concise than what? Than the explicit noun. So no speaker should say that using the explicit noun in place of a pronoun is redundant and useless. We say: rather, it has a benefit. We mentioned earlier that among the benefits of the explicit noun in place of the pronoun is what? Intending generality, and applying the description to those to whom the pronoun would refer had it been present. There is a third benefit, but we said "among the benefits," and there is indeed a third benefit: explaining the causal reason for the ruling. For example, ﴿We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾: had he said "We have prepared for them," it would not have been clear why this humiliating punishment was prepared for them. But when he says ﴿for the disbelievers﴾, this description implies causation, meaning that the reason for preparing the humiliating punishment for them is disbelief.

* Shaykh: A separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl).

If someone says: Could it not be that it is a subject and (al-kāfirūn) is the predicate of that subject, and the sentence is the predicate of the first subject?

We say: This is permissible, but it is contrary to what is preferable, because the apparent meaning of the Qur'an is that what follows them is the predicate of what precedes. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Perhaps we would follow the sorcerers if they were the victorious﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 40], and He did not say "they are the victorious." This indicates that in such a construction, (hu) is a separating pronoun with no place in the grammatical structure (i'rab).

Second: If we say that it is a separating pronoun with no place in i'rab, we no longer need a sentence to be the predicate of the subject; the subject and predicate become one unit, and the basic principle for predicates is that they are a single word rather than a sentence. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Those are the disbelievers﴾.

So (hum) is a separating pronoun. The separating pronoun conveys three things:

First: emphasis (tawkīd). Second: restriction (ḥaṣr). Third: distinguishing the predicate from the qualifier (tābi'); for when the separating pronoun comes, it is determined that what follows is the predicate, and when it does not come, it may be either a predicate or a qualifier. So when you say (Zayd al-fāḍil fī al-dars), it may be that (al-fāḍil) is an adjective, is it not? The meaning would then be that Zayd, the excellent one, is present in the lesson. But when you say (Zayd huwa al-fāḍil fī al-dars), it is determined that it is a predicate, and you have restricted him to excellence, so you say: Zayd is the excellent one, and his position is in the lesson.

In any case, the separating pronoun conveys three things.

* Student: It conveys emphasis, restriction, and separation between the predicate and what follows it.

* Shaykh: May Allah bless you.

﴿Those are the disbelievers in truth﴾. (ḥaqqan) here is in the accusative. But what is its meaning, or what is its i'rab according to the most correct view? We say: its i'rab is an infinitive (maṣdar) emphasizing the content of the sentence. The content of the sentence is ﴿Those are the disbelievers﴾; Allah affirmed for them that they are the disbelievers in truth. So (ḥaqqan) comes emphasizing the content of the sentence, because the reality of these people being disbelievers is understood from His saying ﴿Those are the disbelievers﴾. When (ḥaqqan) comes, it becomes an emphasis on the content of the sentence, and its governing verb is obligatorily omitted; the governing element of this infinitive is a verb implied in meaning, obligatorily omitted. So it is not correct to say: "Those are the disbelievers, it is established as true, truly," that is not correct; because it emphasizes the content of the sentence, so it is as if the content of the sentence were the omitted verb, and the two cannot be combined. For this reason Ibn Malik and other scholars mentioned that an infinitive emphasizing the content of a preceding sentence must have its governing verb omitted.

﴿Those are the disbelievers in truth, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.﴾ (a'tadnā) means: We prepared, so it has the meaning of a'dadnā. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾ [Ali 'Imran 131]. Here He said: ﴿We have prepared for the disbelievers﴾. In this context, ﴿We have prepared for the disbelievers﴾ departs from what the context requires; for what the context requires is to say: "We have prepared for them." "Those are the disbelievers in truth and We have prepared for them," because whenever a pronoun can be used, it is not replaced by something else, since mentioning the pronoun is clearer in the sentence and more concise. But here the pronoun was set aside in favour of the explicit noun matching its description. So what is the rhetorical point in this?

The rhetorical point is that this is an explicit noun in place of a pronoun, and the explicit noun in place of a pronoun has benefits. Among them: intending generality, and applying the description to the referent of the pronoun which, had the context required a pronoun, would have been the referent. Is this Arabic or non-Arabic? No, it is Nabataean! What are the benefits of using an explicit noun in place of a pronoun?

* Student: Intending generality.

* Shaykh: Intending generality, because if he had said "We have prepared for them a humiliating punishment," this would apply only to them, but ﴿We have prepared for the disbelievers﴾ applies to every disbeliever, whether these or others.

The second benefit: applying the description to the referent of the pronoun, which, had it not been for this explicit noun, would have been what? Present. Where is the referent of the pronoun, if there were a pronoun? Those who said: "We believe in some and disbelieve in others." A similar example is His saying: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers, and Jibril and Mika'il, then indeed Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqara 98]. He did not say "an enemy to Him," which is what the context would require. The two benefits are: intending generality, and passing the judgement of this description, which is disbelief, upon these people. In this verse, ﴿an enemy to the disbelievers﴾. The third benefit is observing the endings of the verses (fawāṣil al-āyāt).

* Student: We said: observing the endings of the verses. Where is the observance of the endings of the verses?

* Shaykh: In His saying in the verse of al-Baqara.

* Student: The apodosis of the conditional clause: ﴿indeed Allah is ever Pardoning and Powerful﴾. We said there is a difficulty in it, which you will be addressed to resolve?

* Shaykh: Yes, it is said that the apodosis of the conditional is omitted: "If you show good or conceal it or pardon an evil, then indeed you will be recompensed for that." And it is said that the answer given (i.e., the phrase ﴿indeed Allah is ever Pardoning, Powerful﴾) dispenses with this, and this is the better view, because as long as the ruling is known there is no need for an estimate.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: That is, the retraction of his confession. If Allah wills, when you become a judge and this matter confuses you, there is no harm in asking the scholars about it. You may be a judge now. I say: if you are a judge and this matter arises for you and confuses you, then ask the scholars. This matter (...).

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and intend to make distinction between Allah and His messengers, and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and intend to adopt a way between that. Those are the disbelievers in truth, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
