The scholars said: if Allah had said to it, "Be coolness" only, he would have died from the cold. Allahu Akbar! But He said: ﴿coolness and safety﴾, lest the coldness destroy him. So it became coolness and safety for him. Therefore we say: causes have influence by what? By the powers Allah has placed in them, not by themselves. Then we have not associated partners with Allah. We have only said what the lordship of Allah and the wisdom of Allah require: the lordship of Allah is in the influence, and the wisdom of Allah is in linking the effect to its cause. This is the truth, and it is what Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah (the People of the Sunnah and the Community) hold.
* Student: Shaykh, if Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said to the Children of Israel: ﴿Be apes, despised﴾ [al-Baqarah 65], and then they became apes, do they remain as apes?
* Shaykh: No, no, they do not reproduce.
* Student: They do not reproduce?
* Shaykh: They do not reproduce. The apes that exist now are not descendants of the Jews who were transformed into apes.
* Student: Some of them say (...)?
* Shaykh: No, that is not correct.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, regarding the seven readings (al-qira'at al-sab'), are they attributed to men or to nations?
* Shaykh: To nations.
* Student: To peoples (...).
* Shaykh: What, the reading?
* Student: The seven readings?
* Shaykh: The origin is that the Quran was transmitted by tawatur (mass transmission, mutawatir). The early reciters, in their transmission from the Companions or from the Successors who transmitted from the Companions, had differences. This is the difference of readings.
* Student: May Allah bless you. Regarding the principle of benefits and harms: if we said that every imam should not pray with the seven readings because behind him are laypeople, then the Sunnah would also disappear. This applies to many matters; for example, the supplication after the Friday prayer at the end of Friday, which is a bid'ah (innovation), but out of accommodating the people, since they have become accustomed to it?
* Shaykh: Yes, there is no doubt that the existence of the Sunnah is good, and the readings are like the different sunnahs in the manner of worship. The person who has memorized the readings should recite for himself with this and with that. But if performing a Sunnah results in a harm, is averting harms more important? Or this benefit on which the scholars agreed that it is not obligatory; meaning the scholars agreed on the permissibility of reciting one reading, with no disagreement among them. No one said it is obligatory for a person to recite with the seven readings. So if a person recites with one reading in front of the common people, will the common people now memorize this reading and apply it in their recitation? Never. They will be confused about it. One will say, "Our imam recited such-and-such," and another will say, "No, he did not recite that, he recited such-and-such." Then what is the reference? They will not go back to the Mushaf because he recited to them in a reading other than the one in the Mushaf. So where is the reciter? They search for the reciter, and they return to him, and he says, "I recited such-and-such." And it is not the reading that either of these two said. And if we now ask you, after a short period of days, what is the reading of this word, you will be unable to answer except by consulting. How then would the common people manage?
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. Some have attributed to one of the imams the use of a legal stratagem (tahayyul) on the Sharia in this way: he tells the one who wants to break his fast in Ramadan to travel and break his fast. Is that not considered a stratagem?
* Shaykh: This is the reverse of a stratagem. It is a stratagem. For this reason the scholars, the Hanbali scholars, said: whoever travels in order to break the fast, breaking the fast and the travel are forbidden to him.
* Student: Attributed to some imams, Shaykh?
* Shaykh: Even if it is attributed, even if it is attributed to the imams. The imams make mistakes and are correct.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿And for their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander (156). And for their saying, "We killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah." And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them. Indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption; and they did not kill him for certain (157). Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise (158). And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death; and on the Day of Resurrection, he will be a witness against them﴾ [an-Nisa 156–159].
* Shaykh: Well done.
﴿So for their breaking of their covenant and their disbelief in the signs of Allah﴾, and so on [an-Nisa 155].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: breaking the covenant is a cause for the curse of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because the verse is to be understood with an omitted element, which is: "We cursed them."
* Among its benefits also: these people argued for their disobedience by the decree of Allah against His law, when they said: ﴿Our hearts are uncovered﴾. Allah refuted that. From this it follows that everyone who argues by destiny against the Sharia, his argument is baseless. Allah refuted this in His words: ﴿Those who associated partners with Allah will say: "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything." Likewise denied those before them until they tasted Our punishment﴾ [al-An'am 148]. And if their argument were valid and acceptable, Allah would not have made them taste His punishment.
If someone says: Did Allah not say in another verse: ﴿And if Allah had willed, they would not have associated﴾ [al-An'am 107]? How then does He deny their argument that their polytheism was by the will of Allah, and then affirm that their polytheism was by the will of Allah?
The answer to this is that it may be said: Allah, glorified and exalted, said that to His Prophet ﴿If Allah had willed, they would not have associated﴾ as consolation for him, not as an approval of their polytheism. Rather, to console the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, so that when it becomes clear to him that their polytheism was by the will of Allah, he would be content with the decree of Allah. Contentment with the decree of Allah here is not from the standpoint of the agent, but from an external standpoint.
As for their saying: ﴿If Allah had willed, we would not have associated﴾, their intention in arguing by destiny against the Sharia is to persist in the falsehood they were upon. There is a difference between this and that.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: disbelief in the signs of Allah is a cause for the curse, like breaking the covenant and the pact. But it may be said: breaking the covenant and pact includes what reaches the level of disbelief and what is less than that. As for disbelief in this context, it means major disbelief that takes one out of the religion.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the signs (ayat) of Allah. The signs of Allah, Exalted, are of two kinds: cosmic (kawniyyah) and legislative (shar'iyyah). The cosmic signs are all created things, which indicate their Creator, Mighty and Majestic, indicating His power, His knowledge, His wisdom, His mercy, and other matters related to these created things.
The legislative signs are what Allah sent down to His messengers as revelation: legislative signs. For if you reflect on them, you will find that no human can produce anything like them. The intended meaning is not verbal inimitability, but inimitability in meaning. As for verbal inimitability, it is said that it has been established only for the Quran, and Allah knows best.
But in any case, the legislative signs, which the messengers brought, are a sign from the signs of Allah that no one can produce something like. Allah, Exalted and Most High, has challenged those who denied the messengers with both the cosmic signs and the legislative signs. Regarding the cosmic signs He said: ﴿O mankind, an example has been presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke other than Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it﴾ [al-Hajj 73]. By which kind of sign is this challenge?
* Students: The cosmic.
* Shaykh: The cosmic. No one can do it, no one is able to create even a fly. And regarding the legislative signs He said: ﴿Say: "If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Quran, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another assistants"﴾ [al-Isra 88]. If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of this Quran, they would not produce its like. It is impossible. ﴿Even if they were to one another assistants﴾, meaning helpers and supporters. The point is that the signs of Allah, Exalted and Most High, are not disbelieved in except by the arrogant. Otherwise, it is impossible for any person to deny them, except that he acknowledges them. Even the most obstinate person we know of on earth is certain of the truth. Pharaoh and his people were certain, but they denied it out of injustice and haughtiness. And Moses, peace be upon him, addressed Pharaoh, saying: ﴿He said, "You have certainly known that these have not sent down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidence; and indeed I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed"﴾ [al-Isra 102]. He addressed him in dialogue. Did Pharaoh say, "You have said what you knew"? Never. He was silenced and did not speak, because these were clear and manifest signs.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the transgression of the Children of Israel, for they transgressed against those who brought a law by which they would guide people. They killed whom? The prophets, without right. Indeed, they killed those among people who command justice, even if they were not prophets. Everyone who commands justice among people, the Children of Israel want to kill him, and whoever they are able to kill, they kill, because they only seek corruption on earth.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the killing of prophets can never be with right. How is this derived? From the implication of the words ﴿without right﴾: that if they killed them with right, there would be no harm?
* Student: All the prophets are upon the truth.
* Shaykh: Yes. But what do we do with the phrase ﴿without right﴾? Its implication is that if they killed them with right, there would be no problem? And here it is "without right", and without right is no different.
* Student: Shaykh, this is a description of the actual situation, not a restrictive qualifier.
* Shaykh: Well done. This is a description of the actual situation, not a restrictive qualifier, and it is common in the Quran. Among examples is His words: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾ [al-Anfal 24]. The Messenger never calls to what causes death; he only calls to what contains life.
* Shaykh: Yes, we mentioned that they relied on the decree of Allah: ﴿And their saying, "Our hearts are uncovered."﴾
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, Exalted, seals the heart with disbelief. That is, when a person disbelieves and Allah does not see any good in him, Allah seals his heart, so he is never guided. This is in His words: ﴿Rather, Allah has sealed their hearts because of their disbelief﴾. This is a refutation of their argument from destiny: ﴿Rather, Allah has sealed it because of their disbelief﴾. And there is a verse that most clearly shows that whoever deviates from the truth is himself the cause, namely His words: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate, and Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾ [as-Saff 5]. No one can deviate except that he himself is the cause of his own deviation.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever Allah has sealed upon his heart will not believe except a little, meaning a little faith that does not enable him to remain steadfast. We have previously mentioned that the word ﴿little﴾ (qalilan) here has three possibilities, and that the verse encompasses all of them. For we have a principle in tafsir that should not escape our understanding: whenever a verse admits more than one meaning without contradiction between them, it is to be understood as carrying all of those meanings.

**Commentary of Ibn ʿUthaymin (Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-Karīm) on Sūrat an-Nisāʾ, verses 154–155 (part 1 of 2):**

**Student:** I seek refuge in God from Satan the accursed. ﴿So, for their breaking of their covenant, and their disbelief in the signs of God, and their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying, "Our hearts are uncircumcised." Rather, God has sealed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except a little (155). And for their disbelief and their uttering against Mary a tremendous slander (156). And for their saying, "We killed the Messiah, ʿĪsā son of Maryam, the Messenger of God," — but they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them. Indeed, those who differ concerning him are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption, and they did not kill him for certain (157). Rather, God raised him up to Himself, and God is ever Mighty, Wise (158). And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them (159)﴾ [an-Nisāʾ 155–159].

**Shaykh:** I seek refuge in God from Satan the accursed. God, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And We raised the mount above them﴾. God Most High says: ﴿And We raised the mount above them by their covenant, and We said to them, "Enter the gate prostrating"﴾.

﴿We raised above them﴾ means above their heads. ﴿The mount﴾ is the well-known mountain, which God, Mighty and Majestic, uprooted until it was above their heads, so that they would take the Book with strength, meaning that they would act by the Torah with determination.

His saying ﴿by their covenant﴾ means a raising accompanied by a covenant, because God commanded them, at the time of its raising, to take the Book with strength. A covenant (mīthāq) is a firm pledge.

﴿And We said to them, "Enter the gate prostrating"﴾ means the gate of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem).

﴿Enter the gate prostrating﴾ means prostrating to God, Mighty and Majestic, in gratitude to God Most High for the blessing, because God had commanded them to go to this town and fight its people. But they said: ﴿Indeed, in it are a people of giants﴾ [al-Māʾidah 22]. The story is set out in Sūrat al-Māʾidah. After they had been made to wander in the desert for forty years, God permitted them to enter the town, and it was said to them: ﴿Enter the gate prostrating﴾, meaning while you are prostrating, that is, prostrating to God, Mighty and Majestic.

Is the intended meaning of prostration its literal reality, or is the intended meaning of prostration humility and submission, as in His saying: ﴿And to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and their shadows in the mornings and the evenings﴾ [ar-Raʿd 15]?

The apparent meaning is the first, because they entered on their *astāhihim* (buttocks), and God says: ﴿And We said to them, "Enter the gate prostrating"﴾ [an-Nisāʾ 154], but they did not do it. What did they do? They entered on their *astāhihim*. The *ist* is the *dubur* (rear). The meaning is that they entered crawling, seeking refuge in God, out of arrogance. It was also said that they entered on their *aqfāʾihim* (the back of their necks). And it was said to them: "Say *ḥiṭṭah*" (a request for forgiveness), but they did not do it; they did not say *ḥiṭṭah*. Rather, they said *ḥinṭah* (wheat). It is as if these people wanted nothing but to eat and drink, like cattle.

﴿And We said to them, "Do not transgress in the Sabbath"﴾. In another reading it is ﴿lā taʿaddaw (not transgress)﴾ with a shadda, and *al-taʿaddī* and *al-ʿadw* have the same meaning; it is only a verbal difference. The meaning is: do not transgress in the Sabbath by hunting fish, when they had been forbidden to you. God had forbidden the Jews to hunt fish on the Sabbath as a trial and a test. The fish would come on the Sabbath *shurraʿan*, meaning openly, floating on the surface of the water, and in great numbers. The Jews, as is well known from their conduct, were people of greed and avarice, and this angered them. They said: "What is the way to take these fish that come on the Sabbath *shurraʿan*, when nothing comes on other days?" So they devised a trick for this: they placed nets on Friday, the fish came and fell into them, and then they came on Sunday and took them. The act here, outwardly, is permissible, because they did not transgress on the Sabbath itself; but its real intent was violating the sanctity of hunting on the Sabbath. For this reason it was said to them: ﴿Be apes, despised﴾ [al-Baqarah 65], and they became apes, because the ape is the most similar of creatures to a human. By this act of theirs it seemed lawful, because they had not hunted directly on the Sabbath.

When it was said to them: ﴿Do not transgress in the Sabbath﴾, did they comply? No. Rather they transgressed on the Sabbath by way of trickery, deceit and cunning. Whoever deems the forbidden lawful through a trick is more sinful than one who deems it lawful openly, because when he deems it lawful by a trick he combines two corruptions: the first is deeming the forbidden lawful, and the second is deceit and outwitting the Lord of the worlds, who knows the treachery of the eyes and what the chests conceal.

For this reason, those who devise tricks to get around *ribā* (usury) are more sinful than those who practise *ribā* openly, because those who devise tricks deceive God, so they combine the corruption of *ribā* with the corruption of deception. Also, those who devise tricks think they are right, so they hardly ever desist from it, whereas the one who does a thing openly knows that he has erred, and perhaps his soul will blame him one day until he refrains.

﴿And We said to them, "Do not transgress in the Sabbath," and We took from them a firm covenant﴾ [an-Nisāʾ 154], meaning a strong pledge to carry out what they were commanded. But they did not carry it out. They broke the covenant and did not care, and they were ungrateful for God's blessing. For this reason He said: ﴿So, for their breaking of their covenant, and their disbelief in the signs of God, and their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying, "Our hearts are uncircumcised." Rather, God has sealed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except a little (155). And for their disbelief and their uttering against Mary a tremendous slander﴾, and so on to the end.

﴿So, for their breaking of their covenant﴾: the *fā'* is conjunctive, the *bi-* is a prepositional particle, and *mā* is *zāʾidah* (superfluous) in its grammatical function (iʿrāb), but it is not superfluous in meaning, because every particle that is superfluous in iʿrāb gives emphasis, and emphasis is undoubtedly an addition to meaning. On this basis we parse *mā* as *zāʾidah*, and *naqḍ* (breaking) is a noun in the genitive after the *bi-*, because if *mā* were removed the construction would be *fa-binaqḍihim mīthāqahum*.

Where is the complement of the prepositional phrase ﴿*bi-mā naqḍihim mīthāqahum*﴾?

The speech of God explains itself in Sūrat al-Māʾidah: ﴿So, for their breaking of their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard﴾ [al-Māʾidah 13]. On this basis the prepositional phrase is attached to an omitted element that is explained by what is stated in the Noble Qur'an itself.

His saying ﴿*fa-bi-mā naqḍihim*﴾ means *fa-bi-naqḍihim mīthāqahum* (so for their breaking their covenant). And what is the breaking of a covenant?

Breaking a covenant is to oppose it: that there is a covenant between you and another and then you oppose it. This is the breaking of a covenant.

These people opposed what they had been commanded and did not carry it out, so they broke the covenant. ﴿And their disbelief in the signs of God﴾: are these the cosmic signs or the legislated signs? The apparent meaning is generality: that is, and for their disbelief in the signs of God, when they disbelieved in Mūsā and made demands of him, and said: ﴿Make for us a god as they have gods﴾ [al-Aʿrāf 138], and other things known from the history of this people, a wrathful nation. Whoever wants to know something of their history should return to the book *Ighāthat al-Lahfān* by Ibn al-Qayyim, may God have mercy on him, for he explained their faults and disgraceful acts. We seek refuge in God.

﴿And their killing of the prophets without right﴾: the word ﴿*qatlihim*﴾ has three readings: ﴿*qatluhum*﴾ (with a *ḍamma* on the *hāʾ* and the *mīm*); the second reading: a *kasra* on the *hāʾ* and a *ḍamma* on the *mīm*, ﴿*qatlihum*﴾; the third reading: a *kasra* on the *hāʾ* and the *mīm*, ﴿*qatlihim*﴾. All of these are Sabʿī (canonical seven) readings which the reciter may recite.

But this is fitting only for the student of knowledge. As for the common person, do not let him hear a reading other than the one in his own copy of the Qur'an, because if you let him hear another reading, the Qur'an would become light in his heart, or he would consider you mistaken and say that you are playing with the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic. Just as ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, objected to whom? To Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, when he recited the verse in Sūrat al-Furqān in a way different from how ʿUmar recited it, until they took their dispute to the Prophet ﷺ.

So if the common people hear a reading different from what is in their hands, without doubt they will object to you vehemently, even if you are right. Then, even if we assume they trust you, the Qur'an would become less significant in their souls, and a person must make the veneration of the Qur'an in people's hearts higher than anything else that is venerated besides God, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And their killing of the prophets without right﴾: *al-anbiyāʾ* is the plural of *nabī*. If *nabī* is with a hamza it is said *al-anbiʾāʾ*, and if it is with a *yāʾ* it is said *al-anbiyāʾ*. Both are readings: ﴿*al-anbiʾāʾ*﴾ and ﴿*al-anbiyāʾ*﴾.

His saying ﴿without right﴾ is a statement of the actual situation, not a restrictive qualifier, because it is impossible for the killing of a prophet to be rightful. Rather, it is a statement of fact that the killing of a prophet is not rightful. A qualifier that states the actual situation indicates causation, as if he had said: "And their killing of the prophets, because the killing of the prophets is without right." The right in the matter will come, God willing, in the explanation of the benefits.

﴿And their saying, "Our hearts are uncircumcised"﴾: may God grant us well-being. When they are called to the truth they say: "Our hearts are uncircumcised." *Ghulf* is the plural of *aghlaf*, and *aghlaf* is one that is wrapped, that has a covering to which nothing can reach. They speak in this way: ﴿Our hearts are uncircumcised﴾. This is like the saying of Quraysh: ﴿And they said, "Our hearts are in coverings against what you call us to, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a barrier"﴾ [Fuṣṣilat 5]. Quraysh were the greater.

﴿Our hearts are in coverings﴾ was said by Quraysh, and the Children of Israel said: ﴿Our hearts are uncircumcised﴾, ﴿and in our ears is deafness﴾, meaning we do not hear, ﴿and between us and you is a barrier﴾, meaning we do not see. Thus they blocked all the avenues, I mean Quraysh. They said: the hearts do not understand, and the ears—

**Students:** They do not hear.

**Shaykh:** And the eyes.

**Students:** They do not see.

**Shaykh:** They do not see. We seek refuge in God, even though the truth is at its clearest and most evident. But we ask God for guidance.

God Most High says: ﴿Rather, God has sealed them for their disbelief﴾. Here *bal* is for *iḍrāb ibṭālī* (a retraction that negates what preceded): meaning, rather, there is no covering in their hearts, and their hearts are not uncircumcised, but God has sealed them for their disbelief. Why? Because the origin is *fiṭrah* (the natural disposition), and the *fiṭrah* is the religion of Islam. Whatever reaches it that does not bring the truth to the heart is an incoming matter, an incoming matter, and not something original in it. So God declared them liars, saying that the hearts are not uncircumcised, but rather, what? But rather He sealed them, after they had been upon the *fiṭrah*, because of their disbelief.

His saying ﴿God has sealed them for their disbelief﴾ means He placed a seal upon them, and a sealed thing has a seal placed upon it; it is sealed, meaning in the sense of stamping.

His saying ﴿for their disbelief﴾: the *bāʾ* is causal, meaning because of their disbelief their hearts were sealed, so good does not reach them. For this reason He said: ﴿so they do not believe except a little﴾.

The scholars differed concerning His saying ﴿except a little﴾. It was said that the meaning is: they will never believe, and that such an expression is current in the Arabic language; that is, "none believes except a few" is a negation of the whole. It was also said that the meaning is: except a few of them, so the exception is from the *wāw* (the subject of the verb), meaning they do not believe except a few of them. On this basis they divide into two groups: a believer, who is the minority, and a disbeliever, who is the majority. It was also said that ﴿except a little﴾ refers to the faith, meaning they do not believe except with a little faith.

Then, does the meaning of ﴿except a little﴾ mean except a weak one, or except briefly in time, meaning that most of their time is disbelief, and faith may arise in their hearts but quickly goes out because it has no foundation?

All of this is possible, and the context does not contradict it. It is said that among them are believers and among them are disbelievers, and the disbelievers are more numerous. Then, are the believers themselves steadfast in faith and persistent in it? No. Then, is their faith strong and firmly rooted? The answer is no. On this basis the verse can accommodate all these possibilities.

Let us return to deriving the benefits. God, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And We raised the mount above them by their covenant﴾, and so on to the end.

- In this verse is a demonstration of the power of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and that when He wills something His command is only to say to it "Be," and it is. Otherwise, who could raise this great mountain? And who could place it above their heads, not upon them so that they would die, nor so far away that they would feel safe, but close above their heads? Is that not so?

**Students:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** Then there is in it evidence of the strength and power of God, Mighty and Majestic.

- Among the benefits of this noble verse: the faith of the Children of Israel was faith under compulsion, because any powerful person who says, "I will drop stones on you from the sky if you do not believe," the one threatened believes. What would his faith be?

**Students:** Compelled.

**Shaykh:** Under compulsion. Accordingly, a believer under compulsion must have a weak, unstable faith; when the compulsion is removed, he may return to disbelief.

- Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is legislated, when cities are conquered, to perform the *ṣalāt al-fatḥ* (prayer of conquest), because of His saying ﴿Enter the gate prostrating﴾. Can this be derived?

**Students:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** On the basis that the law of those before us is law for us, unless our law has come to contradict it. It has been said that our law has come in agreement with it: when the Prophet ﷺ conquered Makkah, he prayed eight *rakʿahs* of *ḍuḥā* (forenoon prayer) in the house of Umm Hāniʾ. Some scholars said: this is the forenoon prayer. Others said: it is the prayer of conquest, because it is not the habit of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, to pray the forenoon prayer as eight *rakʿahs*, so this is the prayer of conquest. Some of the caliphs acted upon it, so when they conquered a city they performed the prayer of conquest. How close this view is to the truth: that the Prophet's ﷺ forenoon prayer when he conquered Makkah was a prayer of conquest, in gratitude to God, Mighty and Majestic, for the conquest He bestowed, especially if the conquest was of a capital city. The Children of Israel conquered Bayt al-Maqdis, a capital, and Muḥammad, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, conquered what? Umm al-Qurā, the capital of all the cities.

- Among the benefits of this noble verse: God Most High may make something lawful at one time forbidden and permit it at another time, because He forbade them hunting when?

**Students:** On the Sabbath.

**Shaykh:** On the Sabbath.

- Among the benefits of this verse: the Jews are a people of cunning and deceit, since they transgressed on the Sabbath.

- Among its benefits: whoever devises a trick to get around something forbidden, even by means that appear permissible, is regarded as having actually committed it. How so? Because of His saying ﴿Do not transgress in the Sabbath﴾, and they transgressed in it through this trick. So whoever devises a trick to get around something forbidden by means that appear permissible has committed the forbidden thing, and indeed he has added to it.

- Among the benefits of this noble verse: the complete difference between this nation and the Children of Israel is made evident, and praise be to God. God forbade this nation hunting in the state of *iḥrām* (ihram): ﴿O you who believe, do not kill game while you are in the state of iḥrām﴾ [al-Māʾidah 95]. Then He tested them by sending game to them, saying: ﴿O you who believe, God will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and your lances can reach﴾ [al-Māʾidah 94]. The bird is reached by the lance, and the crawling creature is reached by the hand. What is a crawling creature like? Like rabbits and gazelles and the like, which a person reaches with his hand; he reaches out toward the rabbit and seizes what runs from him. The bird is reached by the lance, not the arrow. The lance, of course, is in a person's hand, and he hunts with it in this way. This was a trial.

God Most High says: ﴿That God may know who fears Him unseen. Whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment﴾ [al-Māʾidah 94]. What did the Companions do? What?

**Students:** They complied with their Lord's command.

**Shaykh:** They avoided it, they complied with the command, they avoided that, even though it was easy for them. But this nation is a nation that says, "We hear and we obey," and praise be to God. May God make us and you among them.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verses 154–155 (part 2 of 2):

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever employs stratagems (tahayyul, legal trickery) against the prohibitions of Allah from this Ummah resembles whom? The Jews. Any person who uses stratagems against the prohibitions of Allah has in him a resemblance to the Jews, whether in buying or selling, in what Allah has made lawful or unlawful in food, or in marriage. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) named the muhallil (the one who makes a divorced woman lawful again for her former husband); he named him, named him what? 
* Students: The borrowed billy-goat (al-tays al-musta'ar).
* Shaykh: The borrowed billy-goat.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, Exalted and Most High, does not punish His servants except after the proof has been established against them, as in His words: ﴿And We took from them a firm covenant﴾, a strong pact between Him and the creation, and then they broke their covenant. Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿And We would never punish until We sent a messenger﴾ [al-Isra 15].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of causes. Legislative causes are affirmed, and likewise the decreed (qadari) causes are affirmed all the more so, as in His words: ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant﴾, where the particle "bi" (for/because of) indicates causation. Also affirmed is that causes have real influence on their effects, which is a requirement of the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For if a thing occurred by chance in this manner, it would be foolish. But when a thing occurs bound to its cause, this indicates wisdom and perfection. O brothers, a person who does a thing arbitrarily, without a cause that necessitates it, is not considered wise. Rather, the one who does a thing through its causes and its effective factors, he is the wise one. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has tied effects to what?
* Students: To causes.
* Shaykh: To causes. But we must know that, because of our deficiency and shortcoming, we sometimes know the cause and sometimes do not. So in this there is an affirmation of causes.
People have divided regarding causes into three categories: one group was negligent, one group went to excess, and one group took the middle course. The best of matters is the middle. The first group was negligent and said: there is no influence of causes at all. Even the fire that burns paper has no influence on it; the burning of the paper did not happen by the fire but at the fire. Do you understand? They argued for this by saying that if you affirm that a cause has influence on its effect, you would have associated partners with Allah. Thus they said: any person who affirms a cause is a polytheist. In lordship or in worship?
* Students: In lordship.
* Shaykh: In lordship. The second group went to excess and exceeded the limit, saying: causes have influence by their very nature, necessarily, and causes cannot fail to produce their effects. These also erred; they went to excess.
The third category says: causes have influence, not by themselves, but by the powers Allah has placed in them. These are the people of truth, whether the cause is decreed or legislated. For this reason we find that some lawful matters have causes and also have impediments. For example, inheritance has a cause and has an impediment. Perhaps your father, who would inherit all your wealth if he were alone, inherits nothing despite the existence of the cause. Why? Because of the presence of an impediment. So the cause is not effective now. He who made fatherhood a cause for inheritance made killing, for example, an impediment to inheritance. Is this clear, O brothers?
* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: Likewise the decreed causes. This fire burns, and Allah placed in it the power of burning. When Abraham was thrown into it, Allah said to it: ﴿O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham﴾ [al-Anbiya 69]. Burning was thus negated, although it is an effective cause by the command of Allah. But why? It did not have effect when Allah said to it: ﴿O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham﴾, so it became coolness and safety for him.
The scholars said: if Allah had said to it, "Be coolness" only, he would have died from the cold. Allahu Akbar! But He said: ﴿coolness and safety﴾, lest the coldness destroy him. So it became coolness and safety for him. Therefore we say: causes have influence by what? By the powers Allah has placed in them, not by themselves. Then we have not associated partners with Allah. We have only said what the lordship of Allah and the wisdom of Allah require: the lordship of Allah is in the influence, and the wisdom of Allah is in linking the effect to its cause. This is the truth, and it is what Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah (the People of the Sunnah and the Community) hold.
* Student: Shaykh, if Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said to the Children of Israel: ﴿Be apes, despised﴾ [al-Baqarah 65], and then they became apes, do they remain as apes?
* Shaykh: No, no, they do not reproduce.
* Student: They do not reproduce?
* Shaykh: They do not reproduce. The apes that exist now are not descendants of the Jews who were transformed into apes.
* Student: Some of them say (...)?
* Shaykh: No, that is not correct.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, regarding the seven readings (al-qira'at al-sab'), are they attributed to men or to nations?
* Shaykh: To nations.
* Student: To peoples (...).
* Shaykh: What, the reading?
* Student: The seven readings?
* Shaykh: The origin is that the Quran was transmitted by tawatur (mass transmission, mutawatir). The early reciters, in their transmission from the Companions or from the Successors who transmitted from the Companions, had differences. This is the difference of readings.
* Student: May Allah bless you. Regarding the principle of benefits and harms: if we said that every imam should not pray with the seven readings because behind him are laypeople, then the Sunnah would also disappear. This applies to many matters; for example, the supplication after the Friday prayer at the end of Friday, which is a bid'ah (innovation), but out of accommodating the people, since they have become accustomed to it?
* Shaykh: Yes, there is no doubt that the existence of the Sunnah is good, and the readings are like the different sunnahs in the manner of worship. The person who has memorized the readings should recite for himself with this and with that. But if performing a Sunnah results in a harm, is averting harms more important? Or this benefit on which the scholars agreed that it is not obligatory; meaning the scholars agreed on the permissibility of reciting one reading, with no disagreement among them. No one said it is obligatory for a person to recite with the seven readings. So if a person recites with one reading in front of the common people, will the common people now memorize this reading and apply it in their recitation? Never. They will be confused about it. One will say, "Our imam recited such-and-such," and another will say, "No, he did not recite that, he recited such-and-such." Then what is the reference? They will not go back to the Mushaf because he recited to them in a reading other than the one in the Mushaf. So where is the reciter? They search for the reciter, and they return to him, and he says, "I recited such-and-such." And it is not the reading that either of these two said. And if we now ask you, after a short period of days, what is the reading of this word, you will be unable to answer except by consulting. How then would the common people manage?
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. Some have attributed to one of the imams the use of a legal stratagem (tahayyul) on the Sharia in this way: he tells the one who wants to break his fast in Ramadan to travel and break his fast. Is that not considered a stratagem?
* Shaykh: This is the reverse of a stratagem. It is a stratagem. For this reason the scholars, the Hanbali scholars, said: whoever travels in order to break the fast, breaking the fast and the travel are forbidden to him.
* Student: Attributed to some imams, Shaykh?
* Shaykh: Even if it is attributed, even if it is attributed to the imams. The imams make mistakes and are correct.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿And for their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander (156). And for their saying, "We killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah." And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them. Indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption; and they did not kill him for certain (157). Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise (158). And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death; and on the Day of Resurrection, he will be a witness against them﴾ [an-Nisa 156–159].
* Shaykh: Well done.
﴿So for their breaking of their covenant and their disbelief in the signs of Allah﴾, and so on [an-Nisa 155].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: breaking the covenant is a cause for the curse of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because the verse is to be understood with an omitted element, which is: "We cursed them."
* Among its benefits also: these people argued for their disobedience by the decree of Allah against His law, when they said: ﴿Our hearts are uncovered﴾. Allah refuted that. From this it follows that everyone who argues by destiny against the Sharia, his argument is baseless. Allah refuted this in His words: ﴿Those who associated partners with Allah will say: "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything." Likewise denied those before them until they tasted Our punishment﴾ [al-An'am 148]. And if their argument were valid and acceptable, Allah would not have made them taste His punishment.
If someone says: Did Allah not say in another verse: ﴿And if Allah had willed, they would not have associated﴾ [al-An'am 107]? How then does He deny their argument that their polytheism was by the will of Allah, and then affirm that their polytheism was by the will of Allah?
The answer to this is that it may be said: Allah, glorified and exalted, said that to His Prophet ﴿If Allah had willed, they would not have associated﴾ as consolation for him, not as an approval of their polytheism. Rather, to console the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, so that when it becomes clear to him that their polytheism was by the will of Allah, he would be content with the decree of Allah. Contentment with the decree of Allah here is not from the standpoint of the agent, but from an external standpoint.
As for their saying: ﴿If Allah had willed, we would not have associated﴾, their intention in arguing by destiny against the Sharia is to persist in the falsehood they were upon. There is a difference between this and that.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: disbelief in the signs of Allah is a cause for the curse, like breaking the covenant and the pact. But it may be said: breaking the covenant and pact includes what reaches the level of disbelief and what is less than that. As for disbelief in this context, it means major disbelief that takes one out of the religion.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the signs (ayat) of Allah. The signs of Allah, Exalted, are of two kinds: cosmic (kawniyyah) and legislative (shar'iyyah). The cosmic signs are all created things, which indicate their Creator, Mighty and Majestic, indicating His power, His knowledge, His wisdom, His mercy, and other matters related to these created things.
The legislative signs are what Allah sent down to His messengers as revelation: legislative signs. For if you reflect on them, you will find that no human can produce anything like them. The intended meaning is not verbal inimitability, but inimitability in meaning. As for verbal inimitability, it is said that it has been established only for the Quran, and Allah knows best.
But in any case, the legislative signs, which the messengers brought, are a sign from the signs of Allah that no one can produce something like. Allah, Exalted and Most High, has challenged those who denied the messengers with both the cosmic signs and the legislative signs. Regarding the cosmic signs He said: ﴿O mankind, an example has been presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke other than Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it﴾ [al-Hajj 73]. By which kind of sign is this challenge?
* Students: The cosmic.
* Shaykh: The cosmic. No one can do it, no one is able to create even a fly. And regarding the legislative signs He said: ﴿Say: "If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Quran, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another assistants"﴾ [al-Isra 88]. If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of this Quran, they would not produce its like. It is impossible. ﴿Even if they were to one another assistants﴾, meaning helpers and supporters. The point is that the signs of Allah, Exalted and Most High, are not disbelieved in except by the arrogant. Otherwise, it is impossible for any person to deny them, except that he acknowledges them. Even the most obstinate person we know of on earth is certain of the truth. Pharaoh and his people were certain, but they denied it out of injustice and haughtiness. And Moses, peace be upon him, addressed Pharaoh, saying: ﴿He said, "You have certainly known that these have not sent down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidence; and indeed I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed"﴾ [al-Isra 102]. He addressed him in dialogue. Did Pharaoh say, "You have said what you knew"? Never. He was silenced and did not speak, because these were clear and manifest signs.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the transgression of the Children of Israel, for they transgressed against those who brought a law by which they would guide people. They killed whom? The prophets, without right. Indeed, they killed those among people who command justice, even if they were not prophets. Everyone who commands justice among people, the Children of Israel want to kill him, and whoever they are able to kill, they kill, because they only seek corruption on earth.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the killing of prophets can never be with right. How is this derived? From the implication of the words ﴿without right﴾: that if they killed them with right, there would be no harm?
* Student: All the prophets are upon the truth.
* Shaykh: Yes. But what do we do with the phrase ﴿without right﴾? Its implication is that if they killed them with right, there would be no problem? And here it is "without right", and without right is no different.
* Student: Shaykh, this is a description of the actual situation, not a restrictive qualifier.
* Shaykh: Well done. This is a description of the actual situation, not a restrictive qualifier, and it is common in the Quran. Among examples is His words: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾ [al-Anfal 24]. The Messenger never calls to what causes death; he only calls to what contains life.
* Shaykh: Yes, we mentioned that they relied on the decree of Allah: ﴿And their saying, "Our hearts are uncovered."﴾
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, Exalted, seals the heart with disbelief. That is, when a person disbelieves and Allah does not see any good in him, Allah seals his heart, so he is never guided. This is in His words: ﴿Rather, Allah has sealed their hearts because of their disbelief﴾. This is a refutation of their argument from destiny: ﴿Rather, Allah has sealed it because of their disbelief﴾. And there is a verse that most clearly shows that whoever deviates from the truth is himself the cause, namely His words: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate, and Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾ [as-Saff 5]. No one can deviate except that he himself is the cause of his own deviation.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever Allah has sealed upon his heart will not believe except a little, meaning a little faith that does not enable him to remain steadfast. We have previously mentioned that the word ﴿little﴾ (qalilan) here has three possibilities, and that the verse encompasses all of them. For we have a principle in tafsir that should not escape our understanding: whenever a verse admits more than one meaning without contradiction between them, it is to be understood as carrying all of those meanings.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 156–158 (part 1 of 3):

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And for their disbelief﴾, conjoined to His saying: ﴿for their breaking their covenant﴾. This is the preferred reading, although there is a difference among the grammarians (i'rab scholars), but this is the most preferred view. The meaning is: ﴿And for their disbelief﴾ We cursed them.
﴿And for their disbelief﴾: this is an emphasis that they disbelieved with a great disbelief, which is stressed by this repetition.
﴿and for their saying against Mary a tremendous slander﴾: their saying against Mary, who was the daughter of 'Imran and the sister of Harun. Here there is a difficulty: how could she be the sister of Harun when there were many long years between Harun and her?
This was raised to the Messenger (ﷺ), and he said: They used to name themselves after their prophets, and the Harun who was the brother of Mary is not the Harun who was the brother of Musa. Rather, they used to be named after the names of their prophets, until it reached Harun, the brother of Mary, daughter of 'Imran. Allah has described her as one who guarded her chastity and as being far from unchastity, even though the Children of Israel said to her: ﴿O sister of Harun, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother an unchaste woman﴾ [Maryam 28]. This is a negation. Are they praising them by that?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: They are not praising her father and mother by that. Her father was not a man of evil and her mother was not unchaste. What is meant by it? What is meant is accusing her of fornication, as if they were saying: From where did this come to you? The mother is pure and the father is far from evil, so from where did this come to you? For this reason some of the jurist scholars held that slander by allusion (tawriya) requires the hadd punishment. Slander by allusion requires the hadd punishment. So if two people dispute, and one of them says to the other: I, praise be to Allah, am chaste and modest, I have not committed fornication, he is speaking about himself.
The meaning is: you are the opposite. For this reason some scholars said that he must be punished with hadd, because this insinuation is more severe. ﴿and for their saying against Mary﴾, the daughter of 'Imran, ﴿a tremendous slander﴾, in that they said: she was an unchaste woman. It follows from this that 'Isa, one of the prophets of firm resolve, would be the child of fornication, and Allah forbid, and this is a tremendous slander.
A parallel to this is what the hypocrites did regarding 'A'isha in the incident of the slander. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think good of their own kind and say, "This is an obvious lie"?﴾ [al-Nur 12] clear. ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it? When they did not bring the witnesses, then they, with Allah, are the liars﴾ [al-Nur 13] ﴿When you received it with your tongues and said with your mouths what you had no knowledge of, and you considered it trivial, while it was, with Allah, tremendous﴾ [al-Nur 15].
﴿and for their saying: Indeed, we killed the Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam, the Messenger of Allah﴾. This too is something the Jews, the Children of Israel, claimed. They say: ﴿Indeed, we killed the Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam﴾. Look, they mentioned him by his title, his name and his patronymic. "Messiah" is a title, "'Isa" is the name, "son of Maryam" is the patronymic. There is no doubt this was said by the Jews. They said: We killed the Messiah 'Isa son of Maryam, so that no confusion would arise about him. That is, they mentioned him by name, title and patronymic so that confusion would not occur. This is from the category of emphasizing the individual and the person, that he is the one meant.
As for ﴿the Messenger of Allah﴾, the exegetes differed about it: is this part of their saying or part of Allah's saying? Some scholars said: it is part of Allah's saying. That is, when these people said "the Messiah 'Isa son of Maryam", they do not acknowledge that he was a messenger, for had he been a messenger they would not have killed him. But Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿the Messenger of Allah﴾, as if He, glorified is He, says: he does not deserve to be killed because he is a messenger.
Some exegetes said: this is part of their speech, and that they said it in mockery; that is, the one who claims he is the Messenger of Allah. This is like the saying of the Quraysh to the Messenger: ﴿They said: O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, indeed you are mad﴾ [al-Hijr 6]. How was the Reminder sent down to him while you say he is mad?!
But this is from the category of mockery. In any case, the Qur'an, which is great, came in this form so that a person would turn his thought in every direction and consider which of them is more deserving.
It may be said: Allah said it in honor and exaltation of 'Isa, peace be upon him, and these people said it in mockery and derision.
Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him﴾. The killing exists; they said: we killed the Messiah. But where is the crucifixion? They say: this is omission of what is known from context; here they said: we killed and we crucified. But He left out its mention, being content with what will be mentioned.
﴿And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him﴾: they claimed that they killed him and crucified him. Crucifixion is placing a piece of wood along the length of the body of the crucified person, with a crossbar laid over it at the level of the two upper arms; he is then made to stand and tied to this wood, and his hands are bound to the two crossbars. This is crucifixion. For this reason the Christians, out of their foolishness, misguidance and lack of intellect, took the cross on which their prophet was crucified as a what? A god, or at least as something sacred. Yet if they had been intelligent, when they saw the cross they would have broken it and set fire with it. But they are foolish and astray, not distinguishing between truth and falsehood.
He said: ﴿But it was made to appear so to them﴾. ﴿Made to appear﴾ means: his likeness was cast upon another person, so they killed that person. See the misguidance and the trial: Allah cast his likeness upon a man, so they killed that man and crucified him, and they said: we killed the Messiah. All those who were present with him agreed that he was raised, as Allah, mighty and majestic, said, and we have no need of the testimony of anyone after the testimony of Allah, mighty and majestic.
Who was made to appear so?
It is said: the one made to appear was himself the one who pointed the Jews to 'Isa, because the Jews were searching for 'Isa, and 'Isa, as you know, was wandering through the land with his mother out of fear for himself from the Jews. It was said to them: he is in such-and-such a house. They sent a group to kill him, and their guide was one of them. When they reached the house in which he was with his companions, about thirteen or twelve men, the guide entered to make sure. When he entered, Allah cast upon him the likeness of 'Isa. Glory be to Allah! He was treated contrary to his intention. The Jews entered and seized him, and he said: 'Isa, 'Isa! He said: I am your companion. They said: You are 'Isa. So they killed him and crucified him.
As for 'Isa, peace be upon him, it is said that Allah opened a window in the wall for him and he went out through other than the door, and Allah raised him to Himself, glorified and exalted is He.
It is also said: the one made to appear was a man from his people, from the people of 'Isa. He said to his thirteen companions: whoever is patient in being killed, Allah will cast my likeness upon him, and he will be my companion in Paradise. A young man among them stood up and said: I. They considered him too young, so he repeated it a second or third time, and he said: I. He said: You are that one. Allah cast his likeness upon him, and 'Isa was saved, and this young man is the one the Jews entered upon, and they killed him and crucified him.
Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿But it was made to appear so to them﴾. As for 'Isa, peace be upon him, Allah mentions that He raised him.
He said: ﴿Indeed, those who differ concerning it are in doubt about it﴾. Those who differed about it: some said it was 'Isa, and some said it was not 'Isa; as if the likeness was not complete, for it had features of 'Isa and features of others, and for this reason they differed.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness (159). For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We prohibited to them good things which had been lawful for them and for their avoidance of the way of Allah many times over (160), and their taking of interest, although they had been forbidden from it, and their consuming of the wealth of people unjustly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment (161). But those firm in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and those who establish prayer and those who give zakah and those who believe in Allah and the Last Day. Those We will give a great reward﴾ [al-Nisa' 159–162].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, those who differ concerning it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption﴾. We have already mentioned that Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him﴾, meaning they did not kill 'Isa and did not crucify him, and the Jews claimed that they killed him and crucified him. ﴿But it was made to appear so to them﴾, meaning his likeness was cast upon a person.
It has also been mentioned that the exegetes differed about this: some said his likeness was cast upon one of those who were with him, and some said it was cast upon the Jew who pointed to him.
They also differed: some said, we killed 'Isa; others said, we did not kill him, because the likeness does not necessitate identity. Perhaps, due to the intensity of their agitation, they did not take care, so the likeness was cast upon one of them or upon someone in the house, and they killed him. Then after killing him they disputed whether in reality they had killed 'Isa or not, and they differed about it. Those who differed did not differ from knowledge, but from doubt: some said, we killed him, and some said, we did not kill him, and they differed, and this ultimately became a religious disagreement. Among the Jews some acknowledged that they had killed him, and some denied it and said: the one we killed was the likeness, the body was not his body. The Jews differed about him, some saying one thing and some another, and the Christians likewise followed them, and in their disagreement too; even the Christians differed about him. He, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿they are in doubt about it, they have no knowledge﴾, so Allah negated that they had knowledge.
The reason for this: knowledge is perceiving a thing as it is in reality, with certainty. This is knowledge. Knowledge is perceiving a thing as it is in reality with a firm certainty. These people did not reach this level; rather we know they did not have this knowledge because they did not kill him or crucify him.
﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾: the ﴿mā﴾ here is negating. Is it Hijazi, Tamimi, or Hijazi that did not complete its conditions?
* Student: Hijazi that did not complete its conditions.
* Shaykh: Hijazi that did not complete its conditions. Which of the conditions was lacking?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Lack of the ordering between its subject and predicate. Ibn Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, says in the Alfiyya:
.................................. ∗∗∗ with the persistence of the negation and the ordering being observed
That is, it is known. Here the ordering is different. If you say: ma Zaydun qa'iman, you are Hijazi; if you say: ma Zaydun qa'imun, you are Tamimi. A poet describing his beloved said:
And one of slender flanks, I said to him: declare your lineage, and he answered: the killing of the lover is not forbidden.
So it is Tamimi. Had it been Hijazi, he would have said: ma qatlu al-muhibbi harāman. But the Hijazis make it work like laysa only with the ordering and the persistence of negation, and here there is no ordering. Therefore we parse ﴿mā﴾ as a negation, ﴿lahum﴾ as a prepositional phrase functioning as a fronted predicate, and ﴿'ilm﴾ as a postponed subject. But the extra preposition has entered on it, extra in parsing but extra in meaning; the grammatically superfluous particles serve to strengthen the speech.
﴿except the following of assumption﴾: ﴿illā﴾ here is a particle of exception, but the exception is disjunctive (munqati'), and the sign of a disjunctive exception is that the excepted item is not of the same kind as the item it is excepted from. We all know that following assumption is not knowledge, so the exception here is not... complete.
* Students: Connected.
* Shaykh: It is not connected; rather it is disjunctive, because following assumption is not knowledge, so the excepted item is now not of the same kind as what it is excepted from, and it is disjunctive. In a disjunctive exception, ﴿illā﴾ is read as ﴿lākin﴾: that is, they have no knowledge of it, but [they follow] assumption.
﴿except the following of assumption﴾. Assumption (zann) is the preponderant of one of two possibilities or several possibilities: if a matter admits two or more things and one of them is preponderant, the preponderant is called zann, and the weaker is called wahm (a supposition). If both are equal, it is shakk (doubt). This is the usage of the usulis (scholars of legal theory).
As for the jurists, shakk is what is opposite to certainty, so it includes wahm, zann and shakk. For this reason they said: if one is certain of purity and doubts a nullifier, he remains in his purity, and the meaning of "doubts a nullifier" includes zann, wahm and shakk. But the usulis, may Allah have mercy on them, divided what is not knowledge into these categories: zann, shakk and wahm. ﴿except the following of assumption﴾, and at that point they have no knowledge.
Can we bring an example from the Qur'an, other than this one, where the exception is disjunctive? Yes, there are many, such as His saying: ﴿You are not over them a controller. Except one who turns away and disbelieves. Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment﴾ [al-Ghashiya 22–24]. Here ﴿illā﴾ is disjunctive, because the absence of control over these people includes those who disbelieved and those who were not disbelievers; for this reason the ﴿fa﴾ appears in the answer. The estimated meaning: you are not over them a controller, but whoever turns away and disbelieves, Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment.
He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him with certainty﴾. ﴿mā﴾ is negating, ﴿qatalūhu﴾ is a verb, subject and object, ﴿yaqīnan﴾. It is said that it is a verbal noun in the accusative of state from the waw in ﴿qatalūhu﴾, meaning: they did not kill him while certain, but they were in doubt about him. This fits His saying: ﴿they have no knowledge of it﴾ and His saying: ﴿those who differ concerning it are in doubt about it﴾. Accordingly, ﴿yaqīnan﴾ is a verbal noun in the position of a state. Where is its governing element?
* Student: The waw.
* Shaykh: No, where is its governing element?
* Student: "Killed."
* Shaykh: "Killed." And where is its owner of the state?
* Students: The waw.
* Shaykh: The waw. That is: they did not kill him while certain. It is also said that ﴿yaqīnan﴾ is an emphasis of the negation, meaning: they did not kill him, I say this with certainty. It is not correct for it to be an emphasis of the negated item, meaning: they did not kill him with a certain killing but with a speculative killing; this is not correct.
So it is either a verbal noun in the position of a state from the subject of "killed", meaning: they did not kill him while certain, but they were in doubt; or it is an emphasis of the negation, meaning: I negate that they killed him with certainty, or: I say that with certainty. Based on the principle we have covered in exegesis: if the speech admits two or more meanings with no contradiction between them and no preference for one, what is the rule?
* Students: It is carried to both meanings.
* Shaykh: It is carried to both meanings together. Accordingly we say that the word ﴿yaqīnan﴾ has two meanings: the first meaning: they did not kill him while certain; the second meaning: I negate that they killed him, with certainty.
﴿Rather, Allah raised him to Himself﴾. This ﴿bal﴾ is a particle of retraction. Is this retraction a nullifying retraction or a transitional one?
* Students: Nullifying.
* Shaykh: Nullifying. The sign of the nullifying retraction is that it nullifies what preceded it, while the sign of the transitional one is that it does not nullify what preceded it but moves from one state to another, such as His saying: ﴿Rather, their knowledge has failed concerning the Hereafter; rather, they are in doubt about it; rather, they are blind to it﴾ [al-Naml 66]. That one is transitional, but the retraction here is nullifying; ﴿bal﴾ means: they were not truthful in their claim.
﴿Allah raised him to Himself﴾: was He raising him alive or dead?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 156–158 (part 2 of 3):

* The students: "Alive."
* The Shaykh: Alive. God, exalted is He, raised him to Himself alive; whether it was through an opening in the house or through the door, God knows best. All of that is possible, and all of it is by the power of God, mighty and majestic.
﴿رَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ﴾ And where was he? He was in the second heaven. The evidence for that is: "When the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey (ʿurija bihi), he found Adam in the first heaven, he found ʿIsa and Yahya in the second, he found Yusuf in the third, he found Idris in the fourth, he found Harun in the fifth, he found Musa in the sixth, and he found Ibrahim in the seventh."[[Narrated by Muslim (162 / 259) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]] Ibrahim, peace be upon him, because he is the highest of these in rank with God, mighty and majestic; and for this reason he was in the seventh heaven. Adam was in the lowest heaven so as to be near his descendants, for his descendants were on the earth, and the closest of the heavens to the earth is the lowest heaven. The closest of the heavens to the earth is the lowest heaven. And the bounty of God is vast; He gives it to whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty.
So then, ﴿رَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ﴾ to what place? To the second heaven, along with his maternal cousin Yahya. But Yahya was not raised during his lifetime; rather, he was raised after he died.
﴿بَلْ رَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا﴾ ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا﴾ means: possessor of might (ʿizzah). The scholars said that ʿizzah has three divisions: ʿizzat al-qahr (the might of subjugation), and ʿizzah...?
* A student: Al-qadr (the might of rank).
* The Shaykh: And ʿizzat al-imtinaʿ (the might of inaccessibility).
ʿIzzat al-qahr: God, glorified and exalted, is the Overpowerer who is not overpowered. On this the pre-Islamic poet says:
Where is the escape, and the Seeker is God... and the one with the cut ear is the overcome, not the Victor.
Among the examples of this—that is, examples of the manifestation of dominance in might—is the saying of God, blessed and exalted, in response to the words of the hypocrites: ﴿لَئِنْ رَجَعْنَا إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ لَيُخْرِجَنَّ الْأَعَزُّ مِنْهَا الْأَذَلَّ﴾ [al-Munafiqun 8]. God said: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ الْعِزَّةُ وَلِرَسُولِهِ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾. The most apparent meaning of ʿizzah here is what? Dominance; because it is in response to the words of those hypocrites. The might of dominance is clear: that He is dominant over everything, so He is Victorious and not overcome, exalted is He.
ʿIzzat al-qadr: that He has a great rank for which there is no equal.
ʿIzzat al-imtinaʿ: that deficiency is impossible for Him. They derived this from the saying of the Arabs: "arḍ ʿazzāz" (ʿazzāz), meaning a hard, strong land.
And ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ means: possessor of wisdom (ḥikmah). So what is wisdom?
Ḥikmah is the perfecting of a thing, its mastery, and placing it in its proper place, such that no sensible person says, "I wish it were not here." That is wisdom.
We may expand on the meaning and say: al-Hakim is derived from ḥikmah and ḥukm. God, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ﴾ [al-An'am 57] and He said: ﴿مَا اخْتَلَفْتُمْ فِيهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَحُكْمُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Shura 10]. So He is al-Hakim, meaning the Judge over His servants and among His servants. He is the Judge over His servants, legislating what He wills for them by His command and prohibition, and He is the Judge among them by His law in this world and by His recompense in the Hereafter. This is ḥukm.
It also comes from ḥikmah, which is the perfecting of a thing and placing it in its proper place. There is no doubt that God, glorified and exalted, possesses consummate wisdom in His legislation and in His decree; therefore we say: wisdom is legislative and decreed.
﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا﴾ The appropriateness, meaning the appropriateness of ending the verse with these two noble names: because these Jews came contending, wanting to kill one of the messengers of God, mighty and majestic. So it was fitting to end the verse with might and wisdom, and here ḥukm is more apparent than ḥikmah; that is, He is the Judge, mighty and majestic, and for this reason He prevented these people from their corruption and from killing the Prophet.
* We take the benefits:
God, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿وَبِكُفْرِهِمْ وَقَوْلِهِمْ عَلَى مَرْيَمَ بُهْتَانًا عَظِيمًا﴾.
* From this verse is derived: the establishment of cause, due to His saying: ﴿وَبِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾.
* Among its benefits: disbelief is a cause of evil, corruption, curse, and distance from the mercy of God, mighty and majestic; because it is connected to an omitted element, as we said regarding His saying: ﴿فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثَاقَهُمْ لَعَنَّاهُمْ﴾ [al-Ma'idah 13].
* Among its benefits: the Jews accused Maryam with a great slander when they said she was an adulteress and that ʿIsa was the son of fornication—we ask God for well-being—and this is a great slander.
But do we say that they disbelieved by their accusing her?
We say: As for whoever accuses her of that after God has cleared her of it, he is a disbeliever; not for the accusation itself, but for his denial of God's exoneration of her, may He be exalted. So his disbelief in this case is of the type of disbelief by denial (kufr al-juḥud), because he denied what God, mighty and majestic, affirmed. God, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿وَمَرْيَمَ ابْنَتَ عِمْرَانَ الَّتِي أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا﴾ [al-Tahrim 12]. So God bore witness to her chastity of womb. Accordingly, whoever accuses her with what the Jews accused her of is a disbeliever, denying God, mighty and majestic. This is not on account of the slander itself; we declare him a disbeliever now because his slander is a denial of God, mighty and majestic.
We move on—though there is no complete connection—if someone slanders one of the wives of the Prophet, peace be upon him, ʿAʾishah, with what God cleared her of, would he be a disbeliever?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Yes, he would be a disbeliever for two reasons:
The first reason: denying the report of God, mighty and majestic. The first thing God mentioned of the story was the slander: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ جَاءُوا بِالْإِفْكِ عُصْبَةٌ مِنْكُمْ﴾ [al-Nur 11], which indicates that this matter, in its root and its details, is a lie. Whoever accuses the Mother of the Believers ʿAʾishah with what God cleared her of is a disbeliever, denying God, mighty and majestic.
Also, from another aspect: he has defiled the bed of the Prophet, peace be upon him. If the Mother of the Believers ʿAʾishah—and far be it from her that she did what she was accused of—were an adulteress, God forbid, then she would be corrupt, and ﴿الْخَبِيثَاتُ لِلْخَبِيثِينَ﴾ [al-Nur 26]. So it follows from this that he has impugned the Messenger, peace be upon him.
Add to that: he has impugned the wisdom of God, that He would make this adulterous woman a bed for the best of mankind in His sight—we seek refuge in God. Is it from wisdom that He would make His friend, His chosen one, and His intimate, Muhammad ﷺ, lie with an adulterous woman? It is not from wisdom. Those who accuse her of what God cleared her of are without doubt disbelievers; we testify before God that they are disbelievers and have nothing to do with Islam, because they denied God and His Messenger, because they defiled the bed of the Prophet, peace be upon him, and because they impugned the wisdom of God. There is no difficulty in this.
If someone slanders a wife of the Messenger, peace be upon him, other than the Mother of the Believers ʿAʾishah, who died while still married to him or who died leaving them, is it the same?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: The same. The correct view is that he is a disbeliever. Why? We do not say it is because it is a denial of God, since God did not clear any one of them. Rather, it is because he has defiled the bed of the Prophet ﷺ and impugned the wisdom of God, mighty and majestic. Therefore the preponderant view is that whoever slanders one of the Mothers of the Believers is a disbeliever whose blood and property are lawful unless he repents. If he repents, the ruler considers whether to lift the death penalty from him because he repented, or not to lift it because it is a fixed penalty (ḥadd); this is a matter for the ruler's judgment.
* A student: The second category of those who slandered Maryam, may God be pleased with her, before God cleared her.
* The Shaykh: No. If someone slanders her with something other than what God cleared her of, then he is like anyone else who was slandered, because she is not the wife of a prophet, so that we would say he has impugned the Prophet.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: slandering chaste women is a great slander, and for this reason God prescribed for it a fixed penalty. How much is its measure?
* The students: Eighty lashes.
* The Shaykh: Its measure is eighty lashes. Even if someone testifies that so-and-so, a man or a woman, committed fornication, and that he saw this man's member in her private part, and he gave this testimony, we say: now you receive eighty lashes, even if he was one of the most truthful people, even if he was one of the most pure people; we say: you receive eighty lashes. He says: I have another witness, bring him; the second testifies, and we lash him too, eighty lashes along with the first. They say: we have a third witness; we say: bring him, and we lash him also eighty lashes. All of this is protection of honour and of lineage. That is, the lashing of the slanderer is not a protection only for the honour of the one slandered, but also for lineages; because if his adultery were proven, the lineage of the adulterer would mix with the lineage of the husband, and one would not know whether this child belongs to this one or that one, and lineages would be lost. For this reason it is obligatory to impose the prescribed penalty on the slanderer.
Moreover, it is not enough to impose the penalty on him; his testimony is never accepted, not even if he testifies to something worth a single fils, because He said: ﴿وَلَا تَقْبَلُوا لَهُمْ شَهَادَةً أَبَدًا﴾ [al-Nur 4], He emphasized the negation with perpetuity. So if he testifies, even if he is one of the most just of people, we say: it is not accepted. Why? This is God's command: ﴿وَلَا تَقْبَلُوا لَهُمْ شَهَادَةً أَبَدًا﴾.
The third penalty: the loss of his uprightness (ʿadalah); ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ﴾ [al-Nur 4]. Accordingly, every religious or worldly work that requires uprightness, he is never entrusted with it. But God made an exception: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ وَأَصْلَحُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [al-Nur 5]. This exception, by agreement, refers to the last clause, which is the lifting of the status of corruption (fisq) from him if he repents. By agreement it does not refer to the first clause, which is His saying: ﴿فَاجْلِدُوهُمْ ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً﴾ [al-Nur 4]. The scholars differed as to whether it refers to the second clause, which is ﴿وَلَا تَقْبَلُوا لَهُمْ شَهَادَةً أَبَدًا﴾, or not, on two views; and the matter should be referred to the judgment (ijtihad) of the ruling judge.
He said: ﴿وَقَوْلِهِمْ إِنَّا قَتَلْنَا الْمَسِيحَ عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ﴾ and so on to the end.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the Jews bore the sin of killing the Messiah, being held to account by their own confession; for God made confession a testimony, when He said: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾. So we say: the Jews killed the Messiah and they did not kill him. What, they killed him and did not kill him? They killed him legally (ḥukman) and did not kill him in actual reality (waqʿan); they killed him legally because they confessed that they killed him, but in reality they did not actually kill him.
* So among the benefits of the noble verse: the ruling of the killing of the Messiah is established against the Jews by their confession.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that they—I mean the Jews—either confessed that he was a messenger and said ﴿رَسُولَ اللَّهِ﴾ to declare upon themselves that they did that out of obstinacy, or that ﴿رَسُولَ اللَّهِ﴾ is a statement of God, as the two views concerning it were mentioned earlier among the exegetes.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: attributing a person who has no father to his mother. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ﴾.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse, a grammatical benefit: when a person is well known by his epithet, there is no harm in placing it before the proper name, because He placed ﴿الْمَسِيحَ﴾ first. Otherwise, the rule is that the name comes first, then the epithet, then the kunyah; but when he is famous by it, the epithet is placed first, as when you say: "al-Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal," or "Ahmad ibn Hanbal al-Imam"? The first, because he is known by it.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that ʿIsa, peace be upon him, is a messenger of God, from His saying: ﴿رَسُولَ اللَّهِ﴾, and he is the last prophet before Muhammad ﷺ was sent; for this reason God, exalted is He, said: ﴿يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولُنَا يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ﴾, what? ﴿عَلَى فَتْرَةٍ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ﴾ [al-Ma'idah 19]. "It is established from the Prophet ﷺ that there was no messenger between him and ʿIsa"[[Narrated by Muslim (2365 / 144) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]; and by this we know the falsity of the reports which claim that Khalid ibn Sinan—who was an Arab—was a messenger. It is said: there was no messenger between ʿIsa and Muhammad.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the nobility of ʿIsa, peace be upon him. How?
