Calling is for one who is far, and intimate discourse is for one who is near. It is known that the distant one needs a louder voice, while the near one is satisfied with a quiet voice.

Then He said: ﴿Messengers as bringers of good news and as warners﴾. ﴿Messengers﴾ is the plural of rasul (messenger), in the sense of one who is sent (mursil). The apparent reading is that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial clause) relating to His words: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him﴾, meaning: while they were messengers, bringers of good news and warners. It is a ḥāl because it carries the sense of a derived noun (mushtaq), since rusulan means mursalīn (sent ones). ﴿Bringers of good news and warners﴾: bishārah (good news) is informing of what gladdens, and indhār (warning) is frightening with what is feared. This is because the sharā'i' (laws) that the messengers brought are commands and prohibitions. What fits commands? Good news: one gives glad tidings of reward to the one who acts upon them. What fits warning is prohibitions: a person is warned against falling into them. Hence the types of taklīf (legal obligation) are two: command, and second, prohibition. What befits command is good news, and what befits prohibition is warning. This is what the messengers brought: good news and warning. Even Muhammad (ﷺ), of whom God said: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and as a bringer of good news and a warner﴾ [al-Aḥzāb 45].

﴿So that there will not be for the people against God any argument after the messengers﴾. The lām here in His words ﴿so that (li'allā)﴾ is the lām of causation (ta'līl), meaning: for the sake of there not being for the people against God any argument after the messengers. The ḥujjah (argument) is what one party puts forward against another to ward off blame from himself and to lift punishment from himself. This is the ḥujjah, meaning proof, evidence, or the like.

His words ﴿after the messengers﴾ mean after the sending of the messengers, because the messengers, upon them be blessings and peace, make things clear to the people with a complete clarity that needs no further explanation, as God said: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people﴾ — for what? ﴿So that he might make clear to them﴾ — and after clarification ﴿God leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾ [Ibrāhīm 4]. So there must be clarification with every messenger. ﴿So that there will not be for the people against God any argument after the messengers. And God is ever Almighty, All-Wise﴾. So by His might He sent the messengers and gave them victory in this world and the Hereafter, and by His wisdom He legislated the laws and made them firm and perfect.

* In this noble verse: a statement of the condition of the messengers, upon them be blessings and peace, that it is not free of what? Good news and warning, according to commands and prohibitions.

* Among its benefits: it is fitting for the person calling to God to deal with people as the messengers dealt with their peoples, so at times he gives good news and at times he warns. For if he always follows the path of good news, he draws people into irjā' (complacency about sin), and if he always follows the path of warning, he draws people into despair and hopelessness. Therefore a person must be wise, considering people's conditions. For example, if he sees people engrossed in a forbidden matter, is it better here to follow the path of good news, which causes people to feel secure from God's plotting, or warning? Warning, and he should be firm. If religious admonition does not benefit them, then the authority's deterrence (al-radʿ al-sulṭānī) is applied.

It was from the policy of ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, that he used authoritative deterrence when people could not be reformed without it. Hence when the command to kill the wine-drinker on the fourth offence, if he does not desist, was reported, Shaykh al-Islam said: this ruling stands if people do not desist without it.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of causation (ta'līl) in God's actions, just as it is in His legal rulings; that is, the affirmation of causation for God's decreed (qadarī) rulings as it is established for the legal rulings. From where is it derived? From the lām of causation. This is established by many proofs, some of which have been counted by some scholars at a thousand proofs, that God's actions and rulings have reasons. Even if there were nothing but the name al-Ḥakīm (All-Wise), that would suffice. So everything He does is for a wisdom, and everything He legislates is for a wisdom.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: God, exalted is He, loves that people be given an excuse, because He sent the messengers so that people would have no argument against God.

* Among its benefits, the great and supreme benefit: the excuse of ignorance, even in the fundamentals of religion, because the messengers come with fundamentals and branches. So if a person is ignorant and no messenger has reached him, he has an argument against God. An argument cannot be established against him by God unless what? Unless he is excused, because if he is not excused, he has no argument. This principle is what the Book and the Sunnah indicate. However, a person may be negligent, so he is not excused for his ignorance, as when it is conveyed to him that there is a divine Islamic religion, but he does not seek this religion, turns away, and is arrogant. Here we say he is not excused, and why? Because of his negligence and failure to search. And if a person wanted to go to some village and took a road, then he was told: this will not bring you to that village, he would refrain and ask: where is the road to that village?

Therefore we say: the excuse of ignorance is not absolute in every respect, but on condition of what? That he is not negligent in learning. If he is negligent, he has no excuse. What is negligence? That it is mentioned to him that religion is other than what he is upon, yet he says: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a community﴾ [al-Zukhruf 22], and I will not investigate, as some of the foolish or the common people say?

* Students: The common people (al-ʿawāmm).

* The Shaykh: "al-ʿawāmm" are the "hawāmm" (vermin/heedless ones), as some of the hawāmm say: ﴿Do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you﴾ [al-Māʾidah 101]. Do what you want and do not ask; if you ask, they say: it is forbidden, a problem; and if you ask, they say: this is obligatory, a problem. This is a grave error.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of God's mercy to His servants, in that He sent to them messengers who teach them, guide them, and lead them to the religion of God. Had it not been for mercy, He would not have sent them; He would have left them to the earlier covenant He took from them in their loins and punished them accordingly.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of two of God's names, al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty) and al-Ḥakīm (the All-Wise). Their explanation and what follows from them has already passed, so there is no need to repeat it, so that we may proceed, God willing, Mighty and Majestic.

Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you﴾. The word "lākin" (but) is a particle of *istidrāk* (qualification or contrast). So why does this particle come in this position? Because the Prophet ﷺ had people who denied him and said: "You were not sent as the messengers were sent." So He said: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you﴾. Contrary to whom? Contrary to the one who denied him and said that nothing had been sent down to him. ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge﴾. ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you﴾, which is the Qur'an. His witness, glorified and exalted is He, to His Prophet is of two kinds: verbal witness, as in this verse, and practical witness, which is His enabling him on earth, His granting him victory over his enemy, and His manifesting, through his hand ﷺ, signs that defeat human beings. So this is witness of what kind?

* Student: Verbal.

* The Shaykh: Verbal? That Allah supports him, establishes him on earth, causes him to inherit the land, and gives him these signs is practical witness. Therefore, Allah's witness to His Prophet with the truth divides into two parts: verbal witness, as in this verse, and practical witness, which is what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has given him of signs and of establishment on earth.

﴿with what He has sent down to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge﴾ means that it was sent down with knowledge from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, or that He sent it down with what He knows, that is, with what He, glorified and exalted is He, knows to be beneficial for creation and servants. Both meanings are correct and do not contradict each other. Therefore the verse must be understood according to both meanings, based on the earlier principle that if the evidence allows two meanings equally, with no contradiction between them, it must be taken to both together.

﴿And the angels bear witness﴾. The angels also bear witness that Allah sent down to Muhammad ﷺ a Qur'an by which he was a messenger. Regarding "the angels": is the intended meaning one angel, Jibril, since he brought down the Qur'an, or is it general? It is general. We must know that when a term comes in general form, it must be taken in its generality unless there is a strong indication that it is meant specifically, whether that indication is legal (*sharʿī*) or rational (*ʿaqlī*).

It is known to all of us that when the Prophet ﷺ ascended, Jibril asked for entry, and it was said: "Who is with you?" He said: "Muhammad." It was said: "Has he been sent for?" He said: "Yes."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (349) and Muslim (163/263), from the hadith of Abu Dhar al-Ghifari.]] Thus the angels knew by this that he had been given revelation, peace and blessings be upon him.

The angels are an unseen world that Allah created from light, and He assigned them acts of worship as His wisdom required, and some of them He made superior to others. The discussion of them has been given much earlier, so there is no need to repeat it.

﴿And sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾. "Shahīdan" (as witness) is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial accusative), meaning: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is sufficient as a witness. They have said that the *bāʾ* here is extra, to beautify the wording, and the original is "kafā Allāhu shahīdan" (Allah suffices as witness). "Ni'ma wa-llāhi kafā Allāhu shāhidan" [such emphatic usage]. However, when another witness and a third come, the matter gains more strength, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 18]. So the witness to His oneness came from three parties: the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic; second, the angels; and third, those of knowledge. As for the witness to prophethood, only two parties were mentioned: Allah and the angels. Why? Because those of knowledge do not become people of knowledge until prophethood is established, so they are in fact followers.

﴿And sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾.

* Student: Is "shahīdan" a *ḥāl* or a *tawkīd* (emphasis)?

* The Shaykh: No, it is a *ḥāl*; "shahīdan" means "as a witness."

* In this noble verse there are benefits. Among them: the affirmation of witnessing for Allah, from His saying ﴿But Allah bears witness﴾, and from His saying ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾. He, glorified and exalted is He, is a witness over all the deeds of His creation, over everything that happens in the heavens and the earth, and even over what does not happen, were it to happen, how it would be. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him﴾ [Qāf 16], even though he has not spoken it, yet Allah knows it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the Prophet's ﷺ prophethood, from His saying ﴿with what He has sent down to you﴾.

* Among its benefits: that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah. From where is this taken?

* Student: From His saying, exalted is He: ﴿with what He has sent down to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge﴾. The sending down of the Qur'an with the knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is a meaning that does not subsist by itself, and this indicates that it is one of the attributes of Allah.

* The Shaykh: That it is the speech of Allah. By this, the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jamāʿah) have argued that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah.

If someone says: Allah, exalted is He, mentions "sending down" regarding things that are not His speech, such as His saying: ﴿And We sent down iron, in which is great might﴾ [al-Ḥadīd 25], and likewise ﴿And He sent down for you eight pairs of the cattle﴾ [al-Zumar 6].

The answer: what is mentioned there are entities that subsist by themselves, whereas speech is a meaning that subsists only in something else. On this basis it becomes clear that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The scholars have also used this verse and its like to show that Allah, exalted is He, is above; from His saying ﴿with what He has sent down to you﴾. And this is so, for He, exalted is He, is above everything. The evidences for this are abundant, praise be to Allah, and their explanation has been given at length before. But it is strange that when we mix with people in this season, it becomes clear to us that many Muslims, regrettably, do not believe in the elevation of Allah, and they say: Allah is in His essence in every place. This is because their scholars establish this for them. We have discussed it at length in our gatherings in the Sacred Mosque, to the point that, praise be to Allah, they were convinced and said: "Glory be to Allah, how can our scholars say such and such?!" We even met a young student from China who speaks Arabic well. When we finished speaking about this and the lesson ended, he came to me and said: "Glory be to Allah, what you said is true, but my head is still spinning, why? Because the false statement has become firmly fixed in him, that our scholars say this, and that whoever says Allah is high in His essence is a disbeliever, and that Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn al-Qayyim and Ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb were all innovators." Glory be to Allah! Why? He said: "Because they departed from the four madhhabs." I said: "Who told you this? Tell your people who taught you this: Ibn Taymiyyah was a Ḥanbalī, his whole jurisprudence was according to the Ḥanbalī school, and likewise Ibn al-Qayyim, and likewise Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, and there is nothing to return to but this." But praise be to Allah, glory be to Allah, he was at ease, meaning the sign of joy and acceptance appeared on his face, and this is beneficial. So I say: Glory be to Allah. The indication of elevation, the elevation of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is a clear indication, by revelation, by reason, and by natural disposition, yet they say this reprehensible statement. We ask Allah for well-being.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah's sending down of the Qur'an was with His knowledge, so no defect can reach it, because Allah knows when it was sent down, with what, how, and upon whom it was sent down. There can be no disagreement, no claim of deficiency, and no claim of addition, none at all, because Allah sent it down with what? With His knowledge. That is, its sending down is joined with the knowledge of Allah. Whoever claims that it contains an addition or a deficiency has attributed ignorance to Allah, because Allah sent it down with His knowledge. Likewise the Qur'an was sent down with what Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knows to be beneficial for creation.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the angels. From where do we take it?

* Student: ﴿But Allah bears witness﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿But Allah bears witness﴾ is the witness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Student: The angels.

* The Shaykh: And where? Where are the angels?

* Student: The sending down was through the angels.

* The Shaykh: The sending down was through the angels. All the angels, or some of them?

* Student: Jibril.

* The Shaykh: We say: the angels. The affirmation of angels in general.

* Student: ﴿And the angels bear witness﴾.

* The Shaykh: Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of the angels, and that the angels have minds, contrary to the one who said they have no minds, as some people said, for whom we ask Allah for well-being and pardon. The angels have minds; they know, they understand, they hear, and they speak.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the care of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, for His Messenger and for what He revealed to him, in that He mentioned that Allah bears witness to it, and so do the angels. The multiplicity of evidences for a thing, or the multiplicity of evidences brought for a thing, indicates what? It indicates care for it, and so it is.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah's witness is in reality sufficient in place of every other witness, from His saying ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 167:

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, those who have disbelieved and averted [others] from the way of Allah have certainly gone far astray.﴾ [An-Nisa' 167]

* Student: Allah has spoken truly. Which is better to say: "al-mala'ika dhu 'uqul" or "dhat 'uqul"?

* Shaykh: "Dhat."

He says: ﴿Indeed, those who have disbelieved and averted [others] from the way of Allah have certainly gone far astray.﴾

As you see, this sentence is emphasized by two emphatics: the first is (inna), and the second is "qad dallu" (have certainly gone astray).

﴿Disbelieved﴾ means in Allah. Kufr (disbelief) in its original sense is covering, and from it comes al-kafra (the sheath of the date-palm spathe), which is the covering of the date-palm blossom, because it covers what is inside it.

As for His words ﴿averted [others] from the way of Allah﴾, it has two meanings. The first meaning: they turned away from the way of Allah. On this view, it is intransitive, i.e., "sadda" is an intransitive verb. The second meaning: they averted others, i.e., they caused them to turn away. On this view, it is transitive, and its object is omitted, meaning: and they averted others from the way of Allah. So the verse admits of both meanings, and neither contradicts the other, so it is taken to mean both together. Undoubtedly the disbelievers both turn away themselves and turn others away. If they are callers to disbelief, their averting [others] is clear. And if they are not callers to disbelief, people still follow them, and so they turn away from the way of Allah as these did, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever establishes an evil practice, upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it."[[Reported by Muslim (1017/69) from the hadith of Jarir ibn 'Abdullah.]] So the disbelievers averting others occurs by speech and occurs by action. When does it occur by speech?

* Student: When they are callers.

* Shaykh: When they are callers to disbelief. Whenever they see a person seeking guidance, they go to him to turn him away. It occurs by action when they act [as examples], but they do not call people, except that people, when they see them, follow them, especially if they are from the nobles and notables of the people, for people generally follow the group.

As for His words ﴿from the way of Allah﴾: al-sabil means the path, and Allah attributed it to Himself because He, blessed and exalted, is the One who legislated it for His servants, so it is attributed to Him.

Know that al-sabil, al-tariq (the road), and al-sirat (the path) are sometimes attributed to Allah and sometimes to other than Allah. They are attributed to Allah in terms of Allah being the One who legislated for the servants, and attributed to other than Him in terms of those who travel them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers – We will leave him in what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination.﴾ [An-Nisa' 115]. So He attributed the way (sabil) to the believers. Here He attributed it to Allah, because He is the One who legislated it, and because it leads to Allah; whoever travels it arrives at Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, just as you say, "The road to Makkah is from here," because if you travel it, it brings you to it.

﴿They have certainly gone astray﴾: ﴿dallu﴾ (they went astray). Dalal means bewilderment, i.e., they wandered away from the truth. ﴿A far-reaching straying﴾: this is because of their disbelief and their averting [others] from the way of Allah. It is described as "far" because this straying, may Allah protect us, is straying from something clear, for the truth is a beacon and a knowledge by which every one who has gone astray can be guided. So when people stray from it, their straying is far, because the evidence is strong.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, what about the strength of Shaykh al-Islam's (may Allah have mercy on him) rejection of the one who said: "Religion consists of usul (fundamentals) and furu' (branches)." Shaykh al-Islam, for example, sees (...). So is it not the case that affirming Allah's elevation (above His creation) is not like abandoning, for example, the siwak during wudu', so that some of this is false?

* Shaykh: No. The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, says: his division into usul and furu' in the sense that this is fundamentals and this is branches is an error. He says: all practical rulings are branches and doctrinal rulings are fundamentals. This is not correct, because among the practical rulings there are some that are of the foundation of the foundations.

* Student: How do we get out of this?

* Shaykh: Like the five pillars of Islam, for example. We get out of it by saying: the religion of Islam is some of it higher than some, more emphatic than some, and greater than some. So abandoning a sunnah of prayer is not like abandoning an obligation within it, and abandoning a regular sunnah prayer is not like abandoning the prayer. This is what we say.

* Student: If the listener understands this?

* Shaykh: What does he understand?

* Student: That he understands that the one who did not divide religion into, for example, beliefs and actions says: usul al-din and furu' ...?

* Shaykh: No. We say: it is beliefs and actions. And we also say: beliefs and actions have degrees. Some matters of belief, if you reject them, are extremely serious, and other matters are below this.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Indeed, those who have disbelieved and averted [others] from the way of Allah have certainly gone far astray (167). Indeed, those who have disbelieved and wronged – Allah would never forgive them, nor would He guide them to a path (168), except the path of Hell, wherein they will abide forever. And that is ever easy for Allah (169). O mankind, the Messenger has certainly come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you. But if you disbelieve – indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and ever is Allah Knowing and Wise (170). O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion or say about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, 'Isa, the son of Maryam, was but a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Maryam and a spirit from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers, and do not say, "Three"; desist – it is better for you. Indeed, Allah is but one God. Glory be to Him that He should have a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾ [An-Nisa' 167–170].

* Shaykh: In this noble verse, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic – and His report is the true report – informs, with an emphatic report by (inna), that those who combined these two attributes, namely disbelief and averting [others] from the way of Allah, have gone far astray.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the emphasis of a statement, even an initial (ibtida'i) statement, when the need calls for it. The scholars of rhetoric (balagha) have said: the basic principle regarding a statement is that it is delivered without emphasis, as when you say: "Muhammad is diligent" (mujtahid). Emphasis is good when the addressee is hesitant, and it is obligatory when the addressee denies it. For example, if we say "Muhammad is standing" to a simple person who knows nothing about him, this does not need emphasis, because the addressee will accept the statement. If we are addressing a hesitant person, then it is good to emphasize it so that his hesitation is removed. If we are addressing a denier, or one who is in the position of a denier, we emphasize it obligatorily, and the emphatic particles multiply according to the strength of the denial. Here Allah emphasized the statement, although a statement is addressed to one with an empty mind, because of the importance of the subject; for when a subject is important, it is good to emphasize it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that whoever believes and remains upright upon the way of Allah and calls people to it is upon guidance. How do we know this from anything?

* Student: From the opposite.

* Shaykh: From the opposite and its contrary, for when a ruling is established for something, its opposite is established for its contrary.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that straying is divided into near straying and far straying, and likewise sins are divided into major and minor sins, as is well known.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verses 168–169:

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and wrong [themselves] — Allah would never forgive them or guide them to a path.﴾ This verse is like the first verse. It contains the emphasis on this ruling, but it explicitly mentions wrongdoing. So with what did they wrong [themselves]? They wronged [themselves] by persisting in disbelief, because when a person persists in disbelief, he has wronged himself, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾ [Hud 101]. Wrongdoing (zulm) originally means deficiency, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Each of the two gardens produced its fruit and did not fail therein in anything﴾ [al-Kahf 33].

"And [whoever] remains upon the way of Allah and calls people to it, he is upon guidance." How do we know this from anything?

* Student: From the opposite.

* Shaykh: From the opposite and the contrary, for when a ruling is established for something, its opposite is established for its contrary.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: misguidance is divided into near misguidance and far misguidance. Likewise, sins are divided into major sins and minor sins, as is well known.

* * *

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and wrong [themselves] — Allah would never forgive them or guide them to a path﴾ [an-Nisa' 168]. This verse is like the first verse; it contains the emphasis on this ruling, but it explicitly mentions wrongdoing. So with what did they wrong [themselves]? They wronged [themselves] by persisting in disbelief, because when a person persists in disbelief, he has wronged himself, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾ [Hud 101]. Wrongdoing (zulm) originally means deficiency, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Each of the two gardens produced its fruit and did not fail therein in anything﴾ [al-Kahf 33], meaning: did not fall short.

The transgressor is called a wrongdoer (zalim) because he has diminished the right of the one he transgresses against. Here, whom did they wrong? Did they wrong others or did they wrong themselves?

* The students: Both.

* Shaykh: Both. That is, wrongdoing occurred from them against themselves and against others, since they directed others to the paths of disbelief.

﴿Allah would never forgive them﴾. The lam in His saying ﴿la-yaghfira﴾ is called by the grammarians "lam al-juhud" (the lam of denial) or "lam al-nafy" (the lam of negation). Its sign is that it occurs after (ma kana) or (lam yakun). Whenever the lam occurs after (lam yakun) or after (ma kana), it is the lam of denial or the lam of negation. So in His saying: ﴿And Allah would never punish them﴾ [al-Anfal 33], what is the lam?

* Students: The lam of denial.

* Shaykh: The lam of denial, because it occurs after (ma kana). ﴿Allah would never forgive them﴾ is also called the lam of denial, because it occurs after ﴿lam yakun﴾.

﴿Allah would never forgive them﴾: the meaning is that He does not grant them success in repentance until He forgives them. The meaning is not: "Allah would not forgive them if they repented," for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, accepts the repentance of whoever repents, whatever his deeds. Rather, the intended meaning is that He does not grant them success in repentance until He forgives them. Forgiveness (maghfirah) is covering a sin together with overlooking it. We explained it with these two meanings because it is derived from al-maghfar, which is the helmet placed on the head in battle to protect the head from arrows, and it contains both meanings: covering and protection. This is supported by the authentic hadith: "Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will privately confront His believing servant on the Day of Resurrection and make him acknowledge his sins, and He will say: 'I concealed them for you in the world, and today I forgive them for you.'"[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2441), and Muslim (2768/52), from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]

﴿Nor to guide them to a path﴾: that is, He does not grant them success. The guidance here is the guidance of success (hidayat al-tawfiq). ﴿A path﴾ means a way they walk upon, except one path, which is the path of Hell: ﴿except the path of Hell﴾ [an-Nisa' 169], and it is one of the names of the Fire.

﴿Wherein they will abide forever﴾: ﴿abiding﴾ means remaining therein, and ﴿forever﴾ means continually. Abad (eternity) is continuity in the future, while amad (a period) is continuity up to a specific limit that is not everlasting.

﴿Wherein they will abide forever. And that is ever for Allah easy﴾: that is, their abiding in the Fire in perpetuity is easy for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, although it entails that the Fire remain with its blaze, its punishment, and its various kinds of torment. Despite this, it is easy for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If a person wanted to light an oven, he would need labor, would he not? He would need labor, fuel, fatigue, and effort. But the Fire, which is the greatest thing in heat, if it remains in perpetuity, this is an easy matter for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and not difficult for Him.

* From this noble verse, indeed from the two verses, it is derived that whoever has these two characteristics, disbelief and wrongdoing, the door of success is closed to him, because of His saying: ﴿Allah would never forgive them﴾.

* And from it: the affirmation of Allah's voluntary acts, meaning that He does what He wills by His will whenever He wills, because of His saying: ﴿Allah would never forgive them﴾. Forgiveness is a voluntary act. This is what the pious predecessors (al-salaf al-salih) and the People of the Sunnah hold: affirming voluntary acts for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Those who deny the attributes (ahl al-ta'til), such as the Ash'arites (al-Ash'ariyyah) and the Mu'tazilites (al-Mu'tazilah), deny this. They say: It is impossible for a voluntary act that renews and occurs to subsist in Allah, the Exalted. They justified this with weak reasons. They said: A originated thing subsists only in an originated thing, and if we affirm for Allah acts that He brings into being whenever He wills, it would follow that Allah is originated.

There is no doubt that this is a false analogy, because it contradicts the text. The numerous verses, which cannot be counted, all indicate that Allah does what He wills whenever He wills: ﴿And your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses﴾ [al-Qasas 68]; ﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Accomplisher of what He intends﴾ [Hud 107]; ﴿And Allah does what He wills﴾ [Ibrahim 27]; ﴿Indeed, Allah decrees what He intends﴾ [al-Ma'idah 1]; and other numerous verses that can scarcely be counted, indicating that Allah, the Exalted, does what He wills whenever He wills.

So this analogy is false, because it contradicts the text. It is also erroneous, because we ourselves are originated beings, and there subsist in us renewing acts that were not necessary for us since we were created, is that not so? It does not follow from the occurrence of these acts that we did not come into existence except at their occurrence. Rather, our coming into existence precedes them. Likewise, the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, His existence is eternal and everlasting, and there is nothing to prevent Him from bringing into being whatever He wills of His acts, His rulings, and His words.

* And from this noble verse: the disbeliever is not granted success in guidance, because of His saying: ﴿nor to guide them to a path﴾.

If someone says: Are there not people among the stubborn, rebellious disbelievers, who oppose the call of God, whom Allah has guided?

The answer: Yes. But there is no objection to specifying the general. This generality is specified for those whom Allah wills to guide. Whoever Allah wills to guide may be guided, even if he had disbelieved and wronged. It is known that among the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, there were those who were disbelievers and wrongdoers, yet they embraced Islam and became leaders in Islam, and they have a sure standing.

* And from this noble verse: that the Fire has a path and Paradise has a path. What is the path of the Fire? The path of the Fire is summarized in opposing the command of Allah and His Messenger: abandoning what is commanded and committing what is forbidden. This is the path. Opposition to the command of Allah and His Messenger is the path of Hell, and conformity to the command of Allah and His Messenger is the path of Paradise.

* And from this noble verse: the affirmation of eternal abiding, because of His saying: ﴿Wherein they will abide forever﴾. Eternal abiding entails the everlastingness of the place in which the abiding occurs. On this basis, the verse contains clear evidence for the everlastingness of the Fire. The mention of eternity has also come in this verse, and in another verse in which surah? al-Ahzab, and in a third verse in surah al-Jinn, and this is well known.

On this basis, no one's saying is valid after the saying of Allah and His Messenger, whatever his knowledge may be. As long as there are explicit verses, we do not rely on the saying of anyone, whoever he may be, because the report of Allah is true, issuing from what? From knowledge intended for complete clarification, so its implication can never be contradicted. Even if it is said: "So-and-so says such-and-such, and so-and-so says such-and-such," we say: There is no saying after the saying of Allah and His Messenger.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: that everything, however difficult, is easy for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because of the completeness of His power, capability, and dominion: ﴿And that is ever for Allah easy﴾.
