Those who deny the attributes (ahl al-ta'til), such as the Ash'arites (al-Ash'ariyyah) and the Mu'tazilites (al-Mu'tazilah), deny this. They say: It is impossible for a voluntary act that renews and occurs to subsist in Allah, the Exalted. They justified this with weak reasons. They said: A originated thing subsists only in an originated thing, and if we affirm for Allah acts that He brings into being whenever He wills, it would follow that Allah is originated.

There is no doubt that this is a false analogy, because it contradicts the text. The numerous verses, which cannot be counted, all indicate that Allah does what He wills whenever He wills: ﴿And your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses﴾ [al-Qasas 68]; ﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Accomplisher of what He intends﴾ [Hud 107]; ﴿And Allah does what He wills﴾ [Ibrahim 27]; ﴿Indeed, Allah decrees what He intends﴾ [al-Ma'idah 1]; and other numerous verses that can scarcely be counted, indicating that Allah, the Exalted, does what He wills whenever He wills.

So this analogy is false, because it contradicts the text. It is also erroneous, because we ourselves are originated beings, and there subsist in us renewing acts that were not necessary for us since we were created, is that not so? It does not follow from the occurrence of these acts that we did not come into existence except at their occurrence. Rather, our coming into existence precedes them. Likewise, the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, His existence is eternal and everlasting, and there is nothing to prevent Him from bringing into being whatever He wills of His acts, His rulings, and His words.

* And from this noble verse: the disbeliever is not granted success in guidance, because of His saying: ﴿nor to guide them to a path﴾.

If someone says: Are there not people among the stubborn, rebellious disbelievers, who oppose the call of God, whom Allah has guided?

The answer: Yes. But there is no objection to specifying the general. This generality is specified for those whom Allah wills to guide. Whoever Allah wills to guide may be guided, even if he had disbelieved and wronged. It is known that among the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, there were those who were disbelievers and wrongdoers, yet they embraced Islam and became leaders in Islam, and they have a sure standing.

* And from this noble verse: that the Fire has a path and Paradise has a path. What is the path of the Fire? The path of the Fire is summarized in opposing the command of Allah and His Messenger: abandoning what is commanded and committing what is forbidden. This is the path. Opposition to the command of Allah and His Messenger is the path of Hell, and conformity to the command of Allah and His Messenger is the path of Paradise.

* And from this noble verse: the affirmation of eternal abiding, because of His saying: ﴿Wherein they will abide forever﴾. Eternal abiding entails the everlastingness of the place in which the abiding occurs. On this basis, the verse contains clear evidence for the everlastingness of the Fire. The mention of eternity has also come in this verse, and in another verse in which surah? al-Ahzab, and in a third verse in surah al-Jinn, and this is well known.

On this basis, no one's saying is valid after the saying of Allah and His Messenger, whatever his knowledge may be. As long as there are explicit verses, we do not rely on the saying of anyone, whoever he may be, because the report of Allah is true, issuing from what? From knowledge intended for complete clarification, so its implication can never be contradicted. Even if it is said: "So-and-so says such-and-such, and so-and-so says such-and-such," we say: There is no saying after the saying of Allah and His Messenger.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: that everything, however difficult, is easy for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because of the completeness of His power, capability, and dominion: ﴿And that is ever for Allah easy﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 170 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿O mankind, the Messenger has certainly come to you with the truth from your Lord﴾ [An-Nisa' 170].

﴿O mankind﴾: Here the address is to all people, even though the surah is Madani. In Madani surahs the address is generally to the believers, because the Quran was revealed among a community of believers. But the address may come in general terms when accompanied by indicators, and here the address will shift from this general audience to the People of the Book, who are not believers. For this reason He said: ﴿O mankind, the Messenger has certainly come to you﴾. The Messenger is Muhammad ﷺ, because (al) here is for a known reference (al-'ahd). Which known reference? A mental one (al-'ahd al-dhihni), since there is no other messenger with Muhammad ﷺ. A parallel is when you say: "The amir has come," and there is only one amir in the town, so every mind turns to what? To this amir, the amir of the town. So (al) is for the mental reference. Likewise, ﴿the Messenger has certainly come to you﴾ means Muhammad ﷺ.

The scholars have mentioned that references are of three kinds: the presential reference (al-'ahd al-huduri), the mentioned reference (al-'ahd al-dhikri), and the mental reference (al-'ahd al-dhihni). What is specified by the mind has (al) for the mental reference, and what is specified by prior mention has (al) for the mentioned reference. An example is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent to you a messenger as a witness over you, as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger. But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger﴾ [Al-Muzzammil 15-16]. Who? The messenger previously mentioned.

Another example is His saying: ﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease. Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾ [Ash-Sharh 5-6]. Which two hardships? The second hardship is the first. For this reason Ibn 'Abbas said: "Hardship will never overcome two eases"[[See: Bahr al-'Ulum by al-Samarqandi (3/594), and al-Wasit by al-Wahidi (4/517).]].

It may also be for the presential reference, as in His saying: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 3], and His saying: ﴿Whose is the dominion today?﴾ [Ghafir 16]. Its rule is this: the (al) of the presential reference is the one that comes after a demonstrative noun, because it is for the presential reference. This is because the demonstrative indicates proximity. When you say "this man" (hadha al-rajul), the (al) here is for the presential reference, since the one pointed to is near.

He said: ﴿the Messenger has certainly come to you with the truth﴾. The (ba') here may indicate accompaniment and transitivity, meaning: accompanied by the truth, so whatever he brings is true. Or ﴿with the truth﴾ means that he is truly a messenger from Allah. The verse allows both meanings. Is there any contradiction between them? There is no contradiction. Accordingly, we say that both meanings are intended together: he came with the truth and not with falsehood, and he is a messenger of truth, not a liar against Allah, upon him be blessings and peace. Truth (al-haqq) is the opposite of falsehood (al-batil), and its root is firmness, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified﴾ [Yunus 96], meaning: established and binding. The basic meaning of this root is establishment. Truth is firm and falsehood is vanishing, as He said: ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it destroys it, and behold, it departs﴾ [Al-Anbiya' 18].

﴿the Messenger has certainly come to you with the truth from your Lord﴾: (min) here indicates the starting point, meaning the truth came from Allah. Reflect on His saying ﴿from your Lord﴾, for in it is an indication that you must accept this Messenger, because he came from your Lord, who is your owner and the manager of your affairs. Therefore you must accept what this Messenger brought, because it is from your Lord.

﴿So believe; it is better for you﴾: The (fa') here is for consequence (al-tafri'), meaning that the obligation of belief follows from this. Believe in whom? In the Messenger and in what he brought.

His saying ﴿better for you﴾ (khayran lakum) is in the accusative, as the predicate of the deleted (yakun), and the sense is: "So believe; it would be better for you." Better than what? Better than disbelief. There is no doubt that belief is better than disbelief, because belief in him brings happiness in this world and the next, while disbelief in him brings loss in this world and the next. This is because of Allah's saying about disbelief: ﴿Say: Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Az-Zumar 15], and about belief: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [An-Nahl 97].

﴿But if you disbelieve﴾: meaning, in the Messenger ﷺ and what he brought. ﴿then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾: meaning He is free of need of you, because He owns whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Among what He owns are these disbelievers. Among what these disbelievers own, too. So it is as if He said: "If you disbelieve, then Allah is free of need of you, because to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth."

His saying ﴿whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ here: the grammarians discuss it and ask: why is the expression (ma), which is used for non-rational beings, used instead of (man), which is used for rational beings?

The answer: they said that non-rational beings are more numerous than rational ones. Someone may object that this is questionable, because among the rational beings are the angels, who are undoubtedly rational, and they are a number that none can count except Allah. The answer to this is: the angels each occupy a place, and the places in the heavens and the earth are more numerous than the angels. Accordingly, non-rational things in the heavens and the earth are more numerous. It is not far-fetched to say that non-rational beings were given precedence because——?

* A student: It was given precedence because non-rational beings are the majority.
* The Shaykh: Because they are the majority.

﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾: He ended the verse with knowledge and wisdom, as an indication that the disbelief of those who disbelieved in the Messenger ﷺ was with knowledge from Allah and with wisdom from Allah. As for it being with knowledge, that is because it occurs in His dominion, and nothing in His dominion can be unknown to Him. As for it being with wisdom, that is because the affairs of the servants and their religion cannot be established except through this division, that some of them are believers and some are disbelievers. Were it not for this division, the banner of jihad would not stand, the believer would not be distinguished from the disbeliever, the believer would not have a distinction by which he is set apart from the disbeliever, and the Fire would not be filled, and Allah has guaranteed that for it. So it is from the wisdom of Allah that among people there should be a believer and what? And a disbeliever.

* From this noble verse: a clarification that Muhammad ﷺ is truly a messenger from Allah, based on His saying: ﴿O mankind, the Messenger has certainly come to you with the truth from your Lord﴾.
* Among its benefits: the universality of the Prophet's ﷺ message to all people, based on His saying: ﴿O mankind﴾.

If someone says: could "mankind" not be meant specifically, as in His saying: ﴿Those to whom people said: Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them﴾ [Ali 'Imran 173]?

The answer: the default in generality is that it is meant generally.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation to accept what the Messenger brought, by reason as well as by law. What is the proof of this? His saying: ﴿from your Lord﴾. If it is from our Lord, who is our owner, our creator, and the one who disposes of us as He wills, then acceptance is obligatory upon us.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that what the Messenger, upon him be blessings and peace, brought is true.

Could we say instead of "what the Messenger brought is true" that everything attributed to the Messenger is true?

* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: Why?
* The students: Because things are attributed to him other than his words...
* The Shaykh: Because there are weak hadiths and fabricated hadiths. But everything the Messenger brought is true.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of general lordship (rububiyyah 'ammah), based on His saying: ﴿O mankind﴾, together with His saying: ﴿from your Lord﴾. Allah's lordship is both general and specific. The general is like His saying: ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾ [Al-Fatihah 2]. The specific is like His saying: ﴿Lord of Musa and Harun﴾ [Al-A'raf 122], and His saying: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all, about what they used to do﴾ [Al-Hijr 92-93], and ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves﴾ [An-Nisa' 65]. Examples of this are many.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: sending messengers is a requirement of lordship, because it is a disposition over creation and an act of Allah. Whatever is of this kind falls under the content of what? Lordship.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation to believe in the truth from the one who brings it, based on His saying: ﴿So believe﴾, after His saying: ﴿the Messenger has certainly come to you with the truth﴾.

Is this a rule for everyone who brings the truth, that we must believe what he brings? The answer: yes. The truth is accepted from any person, from whomever brings it. If the one who brings it is known for falsehood, is the truth accepted from him?

* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Yes. There is an example of this in His saying: ﴿And when they commit an immorality, they say: We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to it. Say: Indeed, Allah does not command immorality﴾ [Al-A'raf 28]. He remained silent about their saying: ﴿We found our fathers doing it﴾, and silence about one of two parts while denying the other indicates acceptance of the second part, which was not denied.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: all belief is good. It is good in this world and good in the next. Even in livelihood, though it be straitened, it is, for the believer, what? Good. This is because the believer, as the Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, described him: "If adversity befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him; and if ease befalls him, he is grateful, and that is good for him"[[Reported by Muslim (2999), from the hadith of Suhayb al-Rumi.]].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: Allah's command to His servants to believe in Him and His rewarding them for it does not arise from any need of theirs. Rather, He is free of need of them, based on His saying: ﴿But if you disbelieve, then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ [An-Nisa' 170].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the universality of Allah's dominion, based on His saying: ﴿whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾. Everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

If someone says: do we not have properties that each of us owns exclusively?

The answer: Yes, but our ownership of what we possess is not absolute. Therefore it is not lawful for us to do with our wealth whatever we wish; we do not do with it except what Allah has permitted us. If a person wished to burn his wealth, would that be permitted? No. So the ownership is limited. Absolute and comprehensive ownership belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and what is attributed to us as ownership is limited ownership, bound by what Allah has permitted.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the plural "heavens." How many are they?
* A student: Seven heavens.
* The Shaykh: Seven heavens, which is stated explicitly in the Quran. As for the earth, it always appears in the singular in the Quran, but in the Sunnah it appears in the plural. The Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, said: "Whoever unjustly takes a handspan of land, Allah will collar him with it on the Day of Resurrection, from seven earths"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3198) and Muslim (1610/137), the wording is Muslim's, from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Zayd.]].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, namely: al-'Alim (the All-Knowing) and al-Hakim (the All-Wise), based on His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾. It has come up many times that Allah's knowledge is vast and encompasses everything in the heavens or on the earth. Our belief in this obliges us to beware of disobeying Him. Why? Because if we disobey Him, He knows about us, and His knowledge is more comprehensive than hearing and sight. The All-Hearing, if we believe in what that requires, makes us beware of what is said; the All-Seeing, if we believe in what that requires, makes us beware of what?

* The students: Of what is seen.
* The Shaykh: Of what is seen. But al-'Alim, if we believe in Him, makes us beware of what is said, or seen, or done, or left undone, because Allah, the Exalted, knows about it. As for al-Hakim, it is derived from judgment (hukm) and wisdom (hikmah). To Allah belongs judgment, and to Him belongs perfect wisdom.

Judgment is of two kinds: cosmic (kawni) and legislative (shar'i). What the servants are charged with is legislative judgment, and what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, alone determines is cosmic judgment. Each of them proceeds only from wisdom. So wisdom is both cosmic and what? And legislative. Then wisdom is of two kinds: wisdom in a specific form and wisdom in the intended end. For this reason we say that wisdom is teleological (ghā'iyyah) and what? And formal (suwariyyah). That is, wisdom resides in the specific form. The imposition of an obligation is wise, and the reward for it is wise. The first is formal and the second is teleological. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾.

* A student: May Allah reward you, O Shaykh. (...) by our saying "between the Meccan and the Madani"...
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: (...) ﴿O mankind﴾.
* The Shaykh: No, this is a general indicator (dabit), not a rule (qa'idah).
* The student: Perhaps it may be exception?
* The Shaykh: It may be an exception, yes, it may be an exception in this and that.

* A student: May Allah be good to you, O Shaykh. Regarding the earths: if someone says, since the Quran and the Sunnah both say there are seven earths, is the punishment only through the matter of punishment, as if Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, punishes, multiplying the punishment seven times?
* The Shaykh: Yes. First we say: the Quran has pointed to this, when He said: ﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them﴾ [At-Talaq 12]. Likeness in type, extent, and greatness is not possible, because it is well known that the heaven is far greater than the earth. Only number remains. This is from the Quran's perspective. From the Sunnah's perspective: if there were not seven earths, it would not be possible for a person to be punished for something that does not exist. Were it not for the existence of seven earths, a person would not be punished for that. But his being punished from seven earths indicates that the floor (qarar) belongs to the owner of the upper earth, just as the air, and this came up in the discussion of settlement (sulh), belongs to him. You mentioned yesterday that the air up to the lowest heaven belongs entirely to the owner of the earth. Likewise to the bottom of the earth, to the seventh earth, it belongs to him. For this reason, if a person wished to dig a trench beneath another person's house or beneath his land, would he own this?
* A student: No.
* The Shaykh: He does not own it.

* A student: Some grammarians say that in His saying: ﴿But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger﴾, the (al) here is for the mentioned reference (al-'ahd al-dhikri), because at the beginning of the verse He said: ﴿We have sent to you a messenger﴾ and ﴿as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger﴾. And it is known that only Musa was sent to Pharaoh. So the messenger at the end of the verse is for the mentioned reference?
* The Shaykh: The mentioned (dhikri)?
* The student: The mental (dhihni).
* Another student: Perhaps he means the mental.
* The Shaykh: We say it this way.
* The student: The mental?
* The Shaykh: No, the mentioned (dhikri).

* A student: May Allah bless you, Shaykh, the rule for the fa' of tafrigh (fa' al-tafrigh)?
* The Shaykh: Tafri' (consequence) means that what follows it is a branch (far') of what preceded it, i.e., derived from it. When the fa' comes after the mention of a general statement and then the detail follows, it is for tafrigh (dividing out), or for taqsim (division), it is for tafri'. This is known from the context. Moreover, a single word may have two meanings, meaning the fa' may be causal and consequential upon what came before it.

* A student: Shaykh, the complement of ﴿with the truth﴾: is it one, or does it apply under both interpretations?
* The Shaykh: If its meaning is that he is truly a messenger, it may be a circumstantial clause (hal) from the Messenger.

* A student: Shaykh, explain the hadith "he will be collared with seven earths." For example, what is the shape of these earths, if we know that the heavens are one above another? And what is the meaning of "collared with seven earths"?

Sheikh: We do not know. As for the "earths" in His saying "seven earths" (﴿مِنْ سَبْعِ أَرَضِينَ﴾), Ibn Kathir mentioned in al-Bidaya wal-Nihaya that the scholars differed about them: are they contiguous, meaning adjoining, with the separation between them being something unknown; or is there a gap between them, like the gap between one heaven and another? This last estimate is not correct, because the distance of the earth now, if an aircraft were to fly over it, would not be reckoned even up to the lowest heaven. Rather, it is said: these are seven earths, and Allah knows best how they are; whether they are adjoining or have a separation between them, we do not know. We must believe in it, and it is something beyond our capacity.

Student: What is the meaning of His saying "طُوِّقَ" (will be encircled)?

Sheikh: It means it will be a collar around his neck which he carries on the Day of Resurrection.

Student: May Allah be gracious to you, O Sheikh. If someone said regarding His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿فَإِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾, that (مَا) here is also used for the rational being, as in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَلَا أَنْتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَا أَعْبُدُ﴾ [al-Kafirun 3], so there is no difficulty in this; would it be correct?

Sheikh: No. The use of (مَا) for a specific rational being, or if you wish to say: a knowing one, is not correct, because the word (rational, ʿāqil) cannot be applied to Allah. This is when the intention is to give precedence to the attribute, as in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿فَانْكِحُوا مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ﴾ [al-Nisa' 3], and He did not say "man ṭāba" (who is good), because the intention is not to specify a woman; the intention is the attributes of women.

Student: May Allah be gracious to you, O our Sheikh. There is a report narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that in every earth there are people (...), meaning there are people (...). Can it be said that it has the ruling of being traced to the Prophet (raised, marfūʿ), or is it said that it is among what was transmitted from the Children of Israel?

Sheikh: As for the view of those who hold that Ibn ʿAbbas was among those who took from the Children of Israel, then it does not establish for him the ruling of being raised (marfūʿ). As for the view that Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him, denied taking from the Children of Israel, as we have passed in Sahih al-Bukhari, then this has the ruling of being raised if it is authentically transmitted from him. We now need an intermediary between us and Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him.

Student: (...) does it include both the essences and the attributes?

Sheikh: This is possible; it includes both essences and attributes, but if the intended meaning is the essences, the attributes are included within them.

Student: Sheikh, may Allah be gracious to you. In this verse, ﴿لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾, and in some other places, ﴿لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾: is there a difference between them?

Sheikh: Apparently this is from the category of variation in expression and style, like ﴿سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ [al-Hadid 1] and ﴿سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ [al-Hashr 1]. The surah (qad sami'a), the surah of Fussilat, separates between two glorifications. In al-Hadid He says: ﴿سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾, and in al-Hashr: ﴿سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾.

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion or say about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, was but a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary and a soul [created] from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And do not say, "Three"; desist – it is better for you. Indeed, Allah is but one God. Exalted is He above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs. The Messiah will never be too proud to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels who are near [to Him]. And whoever is too proud to worship Him and is arrogant – He will gather them to Himself all together. As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them in full their rewards and give them extra from His bounty. But as for those who were disdainful and arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves other than Allah any ally or any helper.﴾ [An-Nisa 171–173].

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion or say about Allah except the truth﴾. His words here: ﴿O People of the Scripture﴾ are a general address intended for a specific group, and what is meant by them are the Christians, because Allah, glorified and exalted, mentioned the state of the Jews earlier in His words: ﴿and their saying, "We killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the messenger of Allah"﴾ and so on [An-Nisa: 157], and what precedes it as well.

Then He addressed the People of the Scripture who are the Christians, saying: ﴿O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion﴾. Ghuluw (excess) means exceeding, and exceeding in something is called ghuluw, and it is also called ifrat (going to extremes), and its opposite is tafrit (negligence) and taqsir (shortcoming).

His words: ﴿do not commit excess in your religion﴾ mean: in what you worship Allah with. That is because they believed that the Messiah is God, or the third of three, or they said: the Messiah and his mother are two gods, and they said: the Messiah is the son of God. All these statements they consider to be what? They consider them religion, so Allah said to them: ﴿do not commit excess in your religion﴾, meaning: in what you worship Allah with.

﴿and do not say about Allah except the truth﴾, meaning: do not say about Allah, in what you describe Him with, except the truth, that is, the established thing accepted by reason, natural disposition and transmitted text. Its opposite is falsehood. So whoever says, "The Messiah is the son of God," has said about Allah other than the truth, and whoever says, "God is the third of three," has said about Allah other than the truth, and whoever says, "The Messiah and his mother are two gods," has said about Allah other than the truth. ﴿and do not say about Allah except the truth﴾.

﴿The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary﴾: this sentence is a refutation of their saying that the Messiah is the son of God, that the Messiah and his mother are two gods, that God is the third of three, and what is similar to that.

He said: ﴿The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the messenger of Allah﴾. We have here four words: al-Masih, Isa, ibn Maryam, and rasul Allah, so their i'rab (grammatical analysis) must be explained.

As for His words ﴿al-Masih﴾, it is a mubtada' (subject).
As for ﴿Isa﴾, it is 'atf bayan (an explanatory apposition).
As for ﴿ibn Maryam﴾, it is a sifah (attribute).
As for ﴿rasul Allah﴾, it is the khabar (predicate).

This sentence ﴿The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, is but the messenger of Allah﴾ is a sentence that indicates restriction (hasr), so the structure is: "The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, is not but what?" Not but the messenger of Allah, meaning: he is not a part of God, nor a god.

﴿The Messiah﴾: al-Masih is a title (laqab) for Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, and he was named thus because he would wipe (yamsah) any person with a defect and that person would be healed; he would heal the blind and the leper by Allah's permission, mighty and majestic is He. This is unlike the Masih ad-Dajjal; he was named al-Masih because his eye is wiped (mamsuh al-'ayn), that is, one-eyed.

His words ﴿Isa﴾ are the proper name.

If someone says: how is the title placed before the proper name, when a title is a description and a proper name is an essence? We say: when the one titled becomes well known by his title, it takes the place of a proper name, indeed it is more clear in identifying the one titled than a proper name. That is why you say: "Imam Ahmad," for example, you put the title first. "The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary": you put the title first, because by his title he is more manifest and clearer.

His words ﴿ibn Maryam﴾: she is Mary daughter of Imran, and he is attributed to her because he has no father. Otherwise, it is well known that one who has a legal father must be attributed to him, not to his mother. Our phrase "legal father" is to exclude one who has a natural (qadari) father but not a legal one, which is what results from fornication – may Allah protect us – for such a person has a natural father, who is the fornicator, but the fornicator is not a legal father.

﴿Isa son of Mary, the messenger of Allah﴾: that is, sent by Allah, mighty and majestic, and not a lord nor a part of a lord, but rather he is truly the messenger of Allah.

﴿the messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary﴾: the waw is a conjunction particle.
﴿His word﴾ is conjoined to ﴿the messenger of Allah﴾.
﴿His word﴾ means: the word of Allah, that is, the one who came into being by a word, and he is not the Word itself, because "word" is an attribute of the speaker, not something separate from him. Accordingly, the meaning of ﴿His word﴾ is: the one who came into being by His word, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus with Allah is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him, "Be," and he was﴾ [Al 'Imran: 59].

﴿His word which He directed to Mary﴾: He conveyed it to Mary by saying to her: "Conceive," for example, or a word like it. We seek refuge in Allah from saying about Allah what He did not say. But this is the meaning of a word reaching Mary: through whom? Through Gabriel, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Mary, daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit﴾ [At-Tahrim: 12]. ﴿We breathed into her﴾: Allah attributed the breathing to Himself because it was the act of His messenger, whom He sent to breathe into her, into her private part. Attributing the breathing to Allah, although it came from Gabriel, is like attributing the recitation to Allah although it came from Gabriel, in His words: ﴿So when We have recited it, follow its recitation﴾ [Al-Qiyamah: 18]. Who recites it? Gabriel recites it, and the Prophet ﷺ follows it.

﴿His word which He directed to Mary and a soul from Him﴾: ﴿He directed to Mary﴾, daughter of 'Imran, and Musa son of 'Imran: are they two brothers?
* Students: No.
* Shaykh: Subhan Allah! Mary daughter of 'Imran and Musa son of 'Imran.
* Students: Similarity of names...
* Shaykh: Is that not so? Is she not a sister of Musa? How? Do they not have one father?

Answer: This objection was raised to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "Indeed they used to name themselves after the names of their prophets" [Narrated by Muslim (2135/9) from the hadith of al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah]. That is, Musa son of 'Imran, and also Mary daughter of 'Imran. 'Imran, who is the father of Musa, we do not know that he was a prophet, but he was the father of a prophet, so this name was common among the Children of Israel, and so the father of Mary was named 'Imran.

﴿and a soul from Him﴾: what is the meaning of ﴿a soul from Him﴾? Does it mean that it is a breath from Him, which occurred by the breathing of Gabriel? Or that it is a soul from Him, meaning that His soul is created by Allah, mighty and majestic? Or both? Both, because they are not contradictory. Gabriel breathed into her private part, and breath is wind, and likewise Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, was a body into which a soul was breathed, so he became a human being. That is why Allah, exalted is He, called him a "spirit," which led the spiritual and monastic paths in his religion, and what is similar to that.

His words ﴿a soul from Him﴾: from Allah, and "from" (min) here is certainly not for partitioning, and the Christian has used it to argue that Jesus is a part of God, taking "from" to mean partitive, because he is deviant, and the deviators are those who follow the ambiguous parts of the texts seeking discord and seeking its interpretation.

It has been mentioned that a Christian used it to argue that Jesus is a part of God, and said: "Your Qur'an indicates what we say, that Jesus is a part of God." One of the scholars was with him, and he recited this verse: ﴿And He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 13]. He said to the Christian: "So the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them are a part of God?" The Christian was bewildered, recognized that he was in error, and then embraced Islam, because the truth became clear to him. So "from" here is not partitive, but for origin (ibtida'), meaning that it is from Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿and a soul from Him﴾.

He says: (Know that what is attributed to Allah, mighty and majestic...) we will discuss it, Allah willing, in the benefits.

﴿So believe in Allah and His messengers﴾ (believe): the pronoun waw refers to whom?
* Student: The Christians.
* Shaykh: To the People of the Scripture, who are meant as the Christians.

﴿Believe in Allah and His messengers﴾: Jesus, Musa, and Muhammad, all the messengers. Do not say: "We believe only in Jesus," because Muhammad is not the one foretold by him; rather, believe in Allah and all His messengers from the first of them to the last.

Iman (faith) in the language is well known to mean tasdiq (affirmation/belief), but the correct view is that it is not merely tasdiq, but iqrar (acknowledgment), and for this reason it is construed with the preposition ba' (bi), one says: "amana bi kadha," meaning he acknowledged it with the acknowledgment of a believer who affirms it. Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned this in his book al-Iman, that whoever explains it as tasdiq is not correct. However, it may be given the sense of tasdiq and then construed with the preposition lam, like His words: ﴿So Lut believed in him﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 26], and faith here means submission, that is, Lut submitted to him, ﴿and said: "Indeed I am emigrating to my Lord"﴾.

﴿So believe in Allah and His messengers and do not say, "Three"﴾: the phrase ﴿do not say﴾ is a present-tense verb, or we may say it is a clause composed of a present verb and a subject. Qawl (saying) is uttering with the tongue, and here the word ﴿three﴾: does the verb fall upon it?
* Students: No.
* Shaykh: No, because qawl only governs a clause or a clause-like phrase; it does not govern a single noun in the object position except according to the dialect of some Arabs who treat qawl like zann (to think), governing a single noun with it. Accordingly, we say that ﴿three﴾ is not an object of ﴿say﴾, but is the predicate of an omitted subject. The estimate is: "Do not say: God is three," and they used to say trinity, as Allah mentioned about them in His words: ﴿They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three"﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 73].

﴿Desist﴾: desist from what? From the saying "three." So He first prohibited, then commanded a second time: ﴿desist﴾.

﴿it is better for you﴾: ﴿better﴾ here is the predicate of the omitted verb "yakun" (let it be). The estimate: "Desist, it will be better for you."

﴿Indeed, He is but one God﴾: this is a rebuttal of His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the third of three﴾. "Innama" is a particle of restriction, so the sentence restricts divinity to Allah, mighty and majestic.

﴿Indeed, Allah is but one God, exalted is He above having a son﴾: (subhan) means tanzih (transcendence), and it is an ism al-masdar (verbal noun), its verb being sabbaha, its masdar being tasbih, and subhan is the ism al-masdar. It is always necessarily in the accusative as an absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq), whenever subhan comes it is in the accusative as an absolute object, and its governing verb is omitted obligatorily; it is not combined with its governing verb.

His words ﴿exalted is He above that He should have﴾: "an" here is masdariyyah, and the preposition has been removed from it because it is understood, that is, transcending Him above having a son. He is transcendent above having a son, mighty and majestic, for several reasons:

First: because He is the owner of everything, and the owner must be distinct from what he owns in all circumstances.

Second: He has no wife. A son is generally born from one who has a wife, as Allah mentioned in Surat al-An'am: ﴿How can He have a son when He has no companion?﴾ [Al-An'am: 101].

Also among them: a son is only for one who needs to continue, that is, the continuation of the species through the continuation of offspring, and the Lord, mighty and majestic, has no need of that. Why? Because He is the Living who does not die.

Also among them: a son is needed by his father to help and assist him in his affairs, and Allah, glorified and exalted, is self-sufficient, and Allah pointed to this in His words: ﴿Exalted is He; He is the Free of need﴾ [Yunus: 68]. In any case, He is transcendent above having a son, and whoever says He has a son has not measured Allah with His due measure.

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾: this is like evidence that He is exalted above having a son: that to Him belongs what is in the heavens and the earth as dominion, and a son must be like his father in having a share of dominion, since he will inherit from his father if he dies, for example, while Allah, glorified, has dominion over the heavens and earth.

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾: "ma" here is general, that is, everything in the heavens, of beings, states and affairs, belongs to Allah, mighty and majestic, and likewise what is on the earth.

﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾: the grammarians say that the "ba'" here is superfluous, and the estimate is "sufficient is Allah as a Disposer," that is, a guardian over everything, so He does not need a son to help Him or assist Him in guarding the dominion.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the prohibition of ghuluw in religion, from His words: ﴿O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion﴾. When Allah forbids a nation from something and relates it to us, it is a lesson for us, meaning that we are forbidden from it. This is confirmed by the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "Do not praise me excessively as the Christians praised Jesus son of Mary" [Narrated by al-Bukhari (3445) from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab], that is, do not exceed the limits regarding me.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that ghuluw in religion is like deficiency in it; just as a person is forbidden from deficiency in his religion, he is also forbidden from excess.

* Among the benefits of this verse: it is not permissible for us to exceed in our religion, whether concerning our Messenger ﷺ or our deeds. So whoever loves the Prophet ﷺ more than the love of Allah is, what? An extremist regarding him, peace be upon him. Whoever elevates him to the rank of the Lord and claims that he disposes of the universe is an extremist regarding him. Whoever claims that another, lower than him, disposes of the universe is an extremist regarding him. So ghuluw is exceeding the limit in everything.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the prohibition of saying about Allah except the truth, from His words: ﴿and do not say about Allah except the truth﴾, which is the established thing.

* Branching from this benefit: the prohibition of distorting the verses and hadiths about the Divine attributes, because whoever distorts them has not said about Allah the truth, but has said falsehood about Him. Is that clear?
* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: Yes. Verses about the attributes, for example: ﴿Rather, His hands are both outstretched﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 64]. If someone says: "The intended meaning of the two hands is not the real hand, but rather blessing and power, and what is similar," we say: this one has said about Allah other than the truth, because he has said what Allah does not intend.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the clarification that the Messiah, peace be upon him, possesses no share of lordship. From where is this derived? From His words: ﴿the messenger of Allah﴾.

* Among its benefits: the permissibility of attributing a person to his mother if he has no father; from His words: ﴿Isa son of Mary﴾, and Jesus son of Mary had no father, as is known to all. If the child is the child of fornication, we say he has no legal father, so to whom is he attributed?
* Student: To his mother.

**Shaykh:** …to his mother. A problem remains. He is ascribed to his mother, in fact and in ruling, and there is no doubt about that. But when we call him, and we give him a name by which he becomes known among people and is addressed, do we ascribe him to his mother, which would expose her shame and break his heart? Or do we give him a name ascribing him to the one who is in fact his father, so we say, for example, "'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Karim"? The second is better. If we say "He is 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Karim," have we erred? The fornicator is a slave of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Even if he is a fornicator, he is still a slave of Allah. So we name him with this name, because if we named him after his mother, everyone who heard it would ask, "Why?" The shame would then fall on this man and his descendants, and it would remain a stain on their history for as long as Allah wills.

We say: All praise is due to Allah. As for the legal rulings, there is no doubt that we do not confer the rights of fatherhood on him. For this reason, if the son of fornication dies, who inherits from him? His mother. She inherits as a fixed-share heir (*fard*) and as an agnatic heir (*ta'sib*). Yes. So we say: he is given a name that ascribes him to his father, and this does not contradict the reality.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the affirmation of the messengership of 'Isa ibn Maryam, from His saying ﴿the Messenger of Allah﴾. For this reason, we must believe that 'Isa is a messenger who has no share in divinity under any circumstances.

* **Student:** May Allah bless you. If a child is born of fornication, but after the woman became pregnant, the fornicator married her in a valid marriage, and then she gave birth, to whom is this child ascribed?

* **Shaykh:** First, we say: the repentance of the male and female fornicators is necessary. Their repentance must be verified. Second, if he marries her, most scholars say it is not permitted for him to marry her, because she is now in an *'iddah* (waiting period) and her child cannot be attributed to him. He must wait until the *'iddah* ends, which is by giving birth in the known manner. Some scholars permit it if repentance is verified, and that if the fornicator acknowledges the child, the child is attributed to him. But this matter must absolutely not be opened to the public, because even if this view is theoretically correct, it must not be issued as a fatwa publicly. Why?

* **Students:** Because they are lax.

* **Shaykh:** They are lax in this matter. Every man who fornicates with a woman, when she becomes pregnant, goes and marries her, and her family will be forced to marry her to him, and a door of evil will be opened to people.

* **Student:** Shaykh, what about when someone says: the saying of Allah, ﴿He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it, from Him﴾ [al-Jathiyah 13], differs from His saying ﴿and a spirit from Him﴾. There, "subjected from Him."

* **Shaykh:** No, "all of it from Him."

* **Student:** The point is that subjection initially comes from Him, meaning the subjugation is from Him, meaning He directly does it…

* **Shaykh:** Is the spirit the one who created itself? It must be created. How has the Christian become more knowledgeable than you?! The Christian became Muslim; he left his religion because of this.

* **Student:** I said, if it is a doubtful point, for example.

* **Shaykh:** It is not a doubtful point.

* **Student:** In the example that we passed, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Karim, (ibn), Shaykh, and mention his name, Shaykh…

* **Shaykh:** Yes. This, may Allah bless you, there is no doubt that he is his son by destiny (*qadaran*). He is his son by destiny, created from his water, and no one doubts this. But since it was not in a legally valid manner, he is not legally attached to him. As for destiny, he is his son, and there is no problem with that.

* **Student:** Yes, Shaykh, but (ibn)?

* **Shaykh:** Ibn what?

* **Student:** Ibn 'Abd al-Karim, (ibn). The word (ibn) regarding himself, Shaykh.

* **Shaykh:** This is a son, but not a legal son; a son by destiny, because this one is a fornicator.

* **Student:** The one ascribed to Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

* **Shaykh:** No.

* **Student:** So the ascription is 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Karim.

* **Shaykh:** Yes. If we had a man named 'Abd Allah whose father is 'Abd al-Karim, would we not say 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Karim?

* **Student:** Yes, the word (ibn) is what causes the problem.

* **Shaykh:** There is no problem.

* **Student:** May Allah bless you, Shaykh. Some Christians, after they were debated with some people, said: "We acknowledge that Allah is one, and that 'Isa is a messenger." They do not mention it with their tongues. Is this an equivocation (*tawriyah*), Shaykh? That is, do they want to get out of a dilemma? Or is it their belief? Some of them say it this way.

* **Shaykh:** Perhaps. Some of them may say that, because they are sects like others. The Christians split into seventy-two sects. This may be the case. But if they do not believe in Muhammad, they are disbelievers, even regarding 'Isa.

* **Student:** May Allah be good to you. They call the Messiah the Dajjal "al-Masikh," with a kha.

* **Shaykh:** No, that is a mistake. What is established in the two Sahihs and others is: «And from the trial of the Messiah, the Dajjal» [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (832) and Muslim (589/129), from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]].

* **Student:** May Allah be good to you. To whom do we ascribe him, Shaykh, the tribe? The son of fornication?

* **Shaykh:** It is sufficient to say 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Karim only. The family that he will have, if Allah wills him to have a family, will be Al 'Abd al-Karim.

* **Student:** If we find a young child and we do not know of either a father or a mother, to whom is he ascribed?

* **Shaykh:** The foundling (*laqit*). He is ascribed as we said. A name is given to him, such as 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Karim, or 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, or "so-and-so, son of his father," the one from whose water he was created, but he is not a legal father. It may be that he is a legal father, because some people may throw their children in the streets and in mosques, being unable to support them. This foundling, in reality, we do not know whether he is the son of fornication or the son of lawful marriage. But his father abandoned him because he was unable to care for him.

* **Student:** How is he treated legally, Shaykh, regarding his inheritance, or regarding the rulings that apply to the son of fornication? This foundling…

* **Shaykh:** According to the well-known view among the scholars, his inheritance goes to the public treasury (*bayt al-mal*), and his blood money, if he is killed, goes to the public treasury. Unless, for example, he marries and has children, then his children inherit. However, the preponderant view is that his property belongs to the one who picked him up. His property belongs to the one who picked him up, because he took care of him, nursed him, and exerted effort on him, so it is his. This is more deserving than the public treasury, which belongs to people in general.

* **Student:** Did we forget to mention the types of additions (*idafat*) to Allah?

* **Shaykh:** What?

* **Student:** We had mentioned "a spirit from Him." You said, Shaykh, that you would mention the types of additions.

* **Shaykh:** Yes. We have not reached them yet. Insha'Allah, they are in the benefits.

* **Student:** May Allah be good to you, Shaykh. Regarding what became well known in the time of the Companions, concerning ascription to the mother, such as Ibn Umm Maktum and Ibn Buhaynah, how is this possible when they have fathers?

* **Shaykh:** Yes. This is because they were content with it, and this became well known. There is absolutely no doubt that they are truly the sons of their fathers. Otherwise, there was Ibn Maktum, and there was 'Abd Allah ibn Malik Ibn Buhaynah.

* **Student:** And the hadith with the threat: «Whoever claims to be son of other than his father, knowing it» [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3508) and Muslim (61/112), from the hadith of Abu Dharr.]].

* **Shaykh:** No, he did not claim it. Everyone knows that his father is so-and-so.

* **Student:** May Allah be good to you, Shaykh: one of the brothers… (...)

* **Student:** ﴿So He will gather them all to Himself. As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty. But as for those who disdained and were arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper. O mankind, there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light. As for those who believed in Allah and held fast to Him, He will admit them into mercy from Him and bounty and guide them to Himself on a straight path﴾ [an-Nisa' 172–175].

* **Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Among the benefits of this noble verse: in His saying ﴿and His word which He directed to Maryam﴾ is the mention of the cause to refer to its effect, from His saying ﴿and His word which He directed to Maryam﴾. 'Isa is not the Word itself, but he was created by the Word, so the cause is mentioned and the effect is intended.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that 'Isa, peace be upon him, is among the most noble of Allah's servants and the most honored by Him, because He attributed him to Himself, saying ﴿His word﴾, and the attribution is for specification and honor.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that 'Isa, peace be upon him, is a spirit from Allah, meaning that he is among the spirits that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created, but he was attributed to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as a matter of honor and distinction.

Know that what is attributed to Allah, exalted is He, is of two types. The first type is a meaning that does not exist except by another, and this is among His attributes, such as the knowledge of Allah, the power of Allah, the hearing of Allah, the speech of Allah, and what is similar to that. These are meanings, and when they are attributed to Allah they are among His attributes and are not created.

The second type is what is attributed to Allah but is separate from Him and distinct from Him, and this is created, but it is attributed to Allah as a matter of honor and distinction. Among this is His saying here: ﴿and a spirit from Him﴾, and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So the Messenger of Allah said to them: "The she-camel of Allah, and her drink"﴾ [ash-Shams 13]. He attributed the she-camel to Himself. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned in them?﴾ [al-Baqarah 114], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And purify My House for those who circumambulate﴾ [al-Hajj 26], "My House." All of these are entities that exist in themselves, so their attribution to Allah is an attribution of what? Honor and distinction.

Mention what we have mentioned of the division. Is that which is attributed to Allah divided?

* **Student:** The first type: the entities…

* **Shaykh:** The entities, yes.

* **Student:** The second type…

* **Shaykh:** No, that which is attributed to Allah is of two types. The first?

* **Student:** Entities.

* **Shaykh:** What is it? Wrong.

* **Student:** (...).

* **Shaykh:** The first is what is not self-subsistent. This is an attribute, such as?

* **Student:** (...).

* **Shaykh:** Yes. And the second.

* **Student:** (...).

* **Shaykh:** That which is a self-subsistent entity. This one?

* **Student:** (...).

* **Shaykh:** Its attribution to Allah?

* **Student:** (...).

* **Shaykh:** Good. Its example?

* **Student:** (...).

* **Shaykh:** If a thing is not a meaning but is attributed to Allah, and in relation to us it is parts and portions, such as the hand of Allah, this also falls under the attributes, because it is not separate or detached from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so it is among His attributes.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation to believe in Allah and all His messengers, from Nuh to Muhammad, peace be upon them; from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So believe in Allah and His messengers﴾. What belief in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, entails has been mentioned to us many times before, so there is no need to repeat it, and likewise what belief in the messengers entails.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the prohibition of Trinitarianism, from His saying ﴿and do not say "Three"﴾, meaning it is forbidden for a person to say that Allah is the third of three. This is shirk, and the prohibition of it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him﴾ [an-Nisa' 36]. No one should say: why was it limited to the prohibition only? We say: yes, it was limited to the prohibition, even though it is shirk, because shirk is prohibited.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that whoever repents from Trinitarianism and refrains from it, Allah accepts his repentance, from His saying…?

* **Student:** (...).

* **Shaykh:** From which of the two words?

* **Student:** (...).

* **Shaykh:** Yes, from His saying: ﴿Cease; it is better for you﴾. This indicates that whoever repents, it is better for him, and this necessarily entails the acceptance of repentance.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the exclusive divinity of Allah, exalted is He. From where is it derived from the verse?

* **Student:** (...).

* **Shaykh:** What is the indication that Allah is exclusively the deity?

* **Student:** ﴿One God﴾.

* **Shaykh:** From His saying ﴿One God﴾: "One," the word "one." Is there another proof as well?

* **Student:** ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾.

* **Shaykh:** No.

* **Student:** Separation, the separation…

* **Shaykh:** Wrong, there is no separation.

* **Student:** Restriction.

* **Shaykh:** Restriction?

* **Student:** Qasr.

* **Shaykh:** Qasr? In our language we say *hasr* (restriction), and it is called *qasr*, but we are accustomed to *hasr*. The restriction is in His saying ﴿Allah is only one God﴾. So His saying ﴿Allah is only one God﴾ indicates restriction, that Allah, exalted is He, is the deity alone. But His saying ﴿One﴾ is an additional emphasis.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the exaltation of Allah above having a son. That is, He is exalted above having a son. From where is it derived?

* **Student:** His saying ﴿Glory be to Him that He should have a son﴾.

* **Shaykh:** His saying ﴿Glory be to Him that He should have a son﴾ is a declaration of His transcendence. What is the reason that taking a son is a defect and deficiency with respect to Allah, exalted is He?

* **Student:** Because he would be needy (...).

* **Shaykh:** A deficiency…

* **Student:** (...).

* **Shaykh:** Because it entails?

* **Student:** That He would be in need of it.

* **Shaykh:** That He would be in need of it, and that He would remain if the father perished. Who are the ones who said that Allah has taken a son?

* **Student:** The Christians.

* **Shaykh:** Others?

* **Student:** The Jews.

* **Shaykh:** Others?

* **Student:** (...).

* **Shaykh:** The polytheists. Three. The three categories we know of who claimed that Allah has a son.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the exclusive sovereignty of Allah, exalted is He. From where is it derived?

* **Student:** (...).

* **Shaykh:** What is the reasoning for that?

* **Student:** The reasoning is (...).

* **Shaykh:** We have no object here, my son.

* **Student:** (...).

* **Shaykh:** What was placed first?

* **Student:** What should be delayed.

* **Shaykh:** What should be delayed. Well done. Placing what should be delayed first conveys restriction.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation that the heavens are a number but unspecified. The question about the plural ﴿the heavens﴾: has it been specified?

* **Student:** Yes.

* **Shaykh:** In which verse?

* **Student:** In His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾ [at-Talaq 12].

* **Shaykh:** Well done. The earth?

* **Student:** The earth has a verse with an indication, and the Sunnah has clarified that the earth is seven earths.

* **Shaykh:** Yes, the Sunnah came with that explicitly, such as in the saying of what?

* **Student:** His saying (ﷺ): «Whoever usurps a span of land unjustly, Allah will encircle him with it from seven earths» [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3198) and Muslim (1610/137), with his wording, from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Zayd.]].

* **Shaykh:** «Allah will encircle him with it on the Day of Resurrection from seven earths.» Well done. Can Allah be an agent (*wakil*) for another?

* **Student:** No, Shaykh.

* **Shaykh:** No?!

* **Student:** Allah is a guardian (*wakil*) over (...).

* **Shaykh:** What does that mean? Is Allah a guardian over creation?

* **Student:** Yes, a guardian.

* **Shaykh:** In what sense?

* **Student:** Lord of them.

* **Shaykh:** Lord of them, and protector of them, not in the sense that He is an agent for another regarding them. Are you certain?

* **Student:** Yes.

* **Shaykh:** Well done. Where is the evidence for that?

* **Student:** The evidence is that to Allah belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth.

* **Shaykh:** Where is the evidence that He is a guardian over His creation?

* **Student:** ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Guardian﴾.

* **Shaykh:** ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Guardian﴾. Good. But is Allah an appointer (*muwakkil*)? He is a guardian now, but is He an appointer?

* **Student:** He is not an appointer.

* **Shaykh:** He is not an appointer.

* **Student:** He appoints the angels.

* **Shaykh:** Where is the evidence?

* **Student:** Do you not know that Allah (...).

* **Shaykh:** There is no agency here.

* **Student:** That Allah, glorified and exalted, commanded the Prophet (ﷺ) (...).

* **Shaykh:** No, brother. We want to establish that Allah appoints. ﴿If these disbelieve in it, We have already entrusted it to a people who are not disbelievers in it﴾ [al-An'am 89].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 171 (part 3 of 3):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah is sufficient as Disposer of affairs﴾. This obligates a person to have true reliance upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to depend upon Allah alone, due to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah is sufficient as Disposer of affairs﴾. Do not rely except upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; make your reliance upon Allah, for He is sufficient for you. And if we were truthful in this, Allah would be sufficient for us, and whoever has Allah as his sufficiency, his affair is accomplished. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾ [At-Talaq 3]. Complete it; ﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾.

So you, my brother, rely upon Allah. If you are truthful in relying upon Allah, then Allah is your sufficiency and your protector; He will make your affair easy for you. This is a promise from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, not from Zayd or 'Amr.

And it has come from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: "If you were to rely upon Allah with the reliance due to Him, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out in the morning hungry and return in the evening full."[[Narrated by at-Tirmidhi (2344), an-Nasa'i in al-Mujtaba (11805), and Ibn Majah (4164) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]] The birds leave their nests in the morning hungry, the night having passed over them and what is in their bellies having been exhausted, yet they are reliant upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; they know their Lord and depend upon Him. And they do not return except that they are what? Full, with bellies filled.

So if we relied upon Allah with the reliance due to Him, it would suffice us; but we fall far short of that. The existence of material means is such that you find most people depending upon them and forgetting the Causer, the Mighty and Majestic.

Commentary of Ibn ʿUthaymin (*Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Karim*) on Surah 4 (al-Nisa'), verse 172:

﴿Never will the Messiah disdain to be a servant of Allah﴾. ﴿The Messiah﴾ is the son of Maryam, whom these people took as a god. He makes clear that the Messiah himself cannot disdain the worship of Allah. Rather, peace be upon him, he seeks the means of drawing near to his Lord: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek the means of access to their Lord, as to which of them is nearest﴾ [al-Isra' 17:57]. This means they seek the means that brings them near to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, while those they call upon are themselves humble servants.

So He says: ﴿Never will the Messiah disdain to be a servant of Allah﴾: he will not refuse. ﴿Yastankif﴾ means: he refuses out of arrogance and haughtiness.

And His saying: ﴿to be a servant of Allah﴾, does this mean a legislated (sharʿi) servitude or a cosmic (kawni) servitude?

* Students: Legislated.

* The Shaykh: Legislated. For the cosmic kind, no one disdains it, since even the most wicked of Allah's servants cannot disdain being a servant of Allah in the sense of divine decree: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam 19:93].

* A student: Pharaoh?

* The Shaykh: Pharaoh was arrogant, but in terms of decree he could not be arrogant. Our discussion concerns decree. As for arrogance toward the legislated command, that is common.

And His saying: ﴿to be a servant of Allah﴾ means legislated servitude. ﴿Nor the angels who are brought near﴾: meaning, the angels brought near will not disdain either. The angels are an unseen world that Allah created from light, and He made their sustenance glorification (tasbih). For this reason they are ṣumud, neither eating nor drinking.

His saying: ﴿who are brought near﴾ means brought near to Allah. If the angels who are brought near do not disdain His worship, then others are more deserving of that.

And His saying: ﴿who are brought near﴾: is it a descriptive (kashifa) attribute or a restrictive (qayd) attribute? It may be a descriptive attribute, since the angels are all brought near to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. It may also be a restrictive attribute, and on this possibility, among the angels there are those who are brought near and those who are not. And Allah knows best.

If someone asks: what is the connection in mentioning the angels when mentioning ʿIsa? We say: the connection is that some people made the angels daughters of Allah, just as some made the Messiah a son of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. That is the connection. That is, even the angels whom you took as children of Allah will not disdain to be servants of Allah.

Then He said: ﴿And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant, He will gather them to Himself all together﴾. ﴿Whoever disdains﴾: the sentence here is conditional, with ﴿man﴾ as the conditional particle, ﴿yastankif﴾ as the conditional verb, and the response of the condition is ﴿fa-sa-yaḥshuruhum ilayhi jamiʿan﴾. It is joined with fa because it begins with sa (the future particle), and when the response begins with sa or sawfa, it must be linked with fa.

And His saying: ﴿whoever disdains His worship﴾: the worship of whom? The worship of Allah in the legislated sense, correct? Whoever disdains His legislated worship.

﴿wa-yastakbir﴾: he exalts himself, elevates himself, and refuses to submit to the commands and prohibitions.

﴿fa-sa-yaḥshuruhum ilayhi jamiʿan﴾: both the arrogant one who disdains and the worshipful one who is humble will all be gathered to Him. Accordingly, the pronoun in His saying ﴿fa-sa-yaḥshuruhum﴾ refers to all of them.

Here there are points of discussion. First: in ﴿man yastankif﴾, the verb of the condition took account of the form of the conditional word: ﴿yastankif﴾ is singular, its subject is singular. In ﴿fa-sa-yaḥshuruhum﴾, the response took account of the meaning. Moreover, it took account of meaning in its broader sense, since His saying ﴿fa-sa-yaḥshuruhum﴾ includes both the one who disdains and the one who does not. Therefore there is a wider generality here.

If someone asks: is it permissible in the Arabic language for the referent of a pronoun to vary, sometimes returning in the singular and sometimes in the plural?

We say: yes, this exists in Arabic, on condition that the word, that is the referent of the pronoun, is apt for both singular and plural. If it is apt for both, the pronoun may return to it in the singular, or in the plural, or it may vary. Allah the Most High said at the end of Surah al-Talaq: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness – He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah has certainly perfected for him a provision﴾ [al-Talaq 65:11]. You find in this verse that the pronoun first returned according to the form of the word, then according to its meaning, then according to its form again.

I say: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness – He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah has certainly perfected for him a provision﴾ [al-Talaq 65:11]. You see the context: once the pronoun returns to the form, once to the meaning, once to the form again, say it. La ilaha illa Allah! Subhan Allah!

In this noble verse, the pronoun returned to the form, then the meaning, then the form.

* A student: His saying, the Most High: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness – He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever﴾: in ﴿khalidin﴾ he took account of the meaning.

* The Shaykh: And what came before it?

* The student: What came before it took account of the form.

* The Shaykh: In ﴿khalidin﴾ he took account of the meaning, and what came before took account of the form.

* The student: (...) took account of the form in it.

* The Shaykh: He took account of the form in it. The wisdom behind this is to alert us that words like ﴿man﴾, whether conditional or relative, are general. From the fact that what refers back to them is sometimes singular and sometimes plural, we benefit from this.

And His saying: ﴿fa-sa-yaḥshuruhum﴾ means: He will gather them. That will be on the Day of Resurrection, for Allah, glory be to Him and Exalted, gathers the first and the last in one place, with no buildings, no mountains, no trees, no hills, no sand, in one place where the caller makes them hear and the sight reaches all of them, because they are on a flat earth stretched out like a hide, as Allah the Most High said: ﴿When the sky splits open, and it hearkens to its Lord and is right to do so, and when the earth is stretched out﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 84:1–3]. It is not stretched now. Now it is spread out but not stretched, now it is folded: ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾ [al-Zumar 39:5]. But when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be stretched: ﴿and when the earth is stretched out﴾, as in the hadith: "It will be stretched like a hide"[[Narrated by Ibn Majah (4081) from the hadith of Ibn Masʿud with the wording: "The earth will be stretched like a hide."]], that is, stretched like a skin. For this reason the caller makes them hear: when he calls, the last of them hears the first. There is no curvature to block the sound, no mountains or trees. Also, the sight reaches them: He sees them all, with no curvature so that some are hidden from sight, but all are seen together. All creatures will be gathered on that Day in this plain, as Allah said in response to those who said: ﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected? And our forefathers, the earlier ones?﴾ [al-Waqiʿa 56:47–48]. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: Indeed, the former and the latter will surely be gathered to the appointed time of a known Day﴾ [al-Waqiʿa 56:49–50]. The former and the latter are all gathered in this place. Furthermore, the wild beasts and all animals are gathered with the people. What a magnificent scene!

This scene we must always remember, standing and sitting. If a person remembers it, he may one day say: "Would that I were a tree that is cut down,"[[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (35524) from the hadith of Ibn Masʿud.]] as the Commander of the Faithful ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) said. A person sometimes passes a sparrow or a cat and says: "Would that I were like it," fearing sin. For it is known that when Allah decrees happiness for a human being, it is far better than that: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾ [al-Duha 93:4]. But who guarantees this for himself? Who guarantees for himself that he is safe from this great standing, from this Day that turns children grey, when the sky is torn apart by it?!

If a person were assured of this, he would say: "Praise be to Allah who created me," though Allah is praised in every state. But a person fears sins, so he says: all creation will be gathered to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and each person will be recompensed for what he did, and there is no need to say "bring evidence, bring witnesses." If a person denies, what will testify against him? The very body, its limbs, its skin. All the skin testifies to whatever evil deed it touched, and to whatever sweat it released from vain desire, and other things. If you wish, deny it: ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾ [al-Nur 24:24]. O Allah, save us from that Day.

﴿Then He will gather them all to Himself﴾: then He mentioned the outcome of these and those.

* * *

* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Never will the Messiah disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels brought near. And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant – He will gather them to Himself all together. As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty. But as for those who disdained and were arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or any helper﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:172–173].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. We have taken the verse he recited, and I think we have not yet taken the benefits.

* Among its benefits: it is impossible for the Messiah, ʿIsa son of Maryam, whom these people made a god, to disdain the worship of Allah.

* A consequence of this benefit: a servant is not fit to be a lord or an object of worship, because he himself is a worshipper and one who is nurtured.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: digression (istitrad), by mentioning what is associated with a thing even if it was not mentioned. This is found in His saying: ﴿nor the angels brought near﴾, because we mentioned in the tafsir that they were mentioned alongside the Messiah, since some people worship the angels and claim they are daughters of Allah.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: if we say the attribute is descriptive (kashifa), then the angels are all brought near; if we say that the angels are divided into two kinds, those brought near and those not brought near, then it is restrictive (qayd).

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a warning to whoever disdains the worship of Allah and is arrogant, by His saying: ﴿He will gather them to Himself all together﴾, and then He elaborated.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: disdain (istinkaf) is not the same as arrogance (istikbar). Disdain is in the heart, when a person has inner aversion and pride toward the worship of Allah. Arrogance is when he abandons worship, puts himself above it, and despises worship and the Messenger, as in their saying: ﴿Is this the one whom Allah sent as a messenger?﴾ [al-Furqan 25:41].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of resurrection, by His saying: ﴿He will gather them to Himself all together﴾.

* Among its benefits also: it is general for everyone. Every living being must be resurrected, whether a descendant of Adam or not; even beasts and wild animals will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection.

Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾ ﴿and as for those who disdained and were arrogant﴾. In this verse and the one after it there is detailed explanation (tafsil), and detailing after a general statement (ijmal) is one of the methods of eloquence, and it is known that the Qur'an is at the highest kind of eloquence: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty﴾. The particle (amma) here is conditional, and with the condition it conveys detailing. Its being conditional is because it has an apodosis (jawab), which is His saying: ﴿He will give them in full﴾. And its being detailing is because the believers and those who disdained and were arrogant are distinguished in it.

As for His saying: ﴿believed and did righteous deeds﴾, these have been repeated before us many times, so there is no need to explain them again. ﴿He will give them their rewards in full﴾, meaning He will give them their rewards complete and whole. The Qur'an and the Sunnah have explained how these rewards are: that a good deed is rewarded tenfold up to seven hundred times, up to many multiples. Therefore He said: ﴿and increase them from His bounty﴾, meaning in addition to their rewards. So when a person deserves a good deed, it is multiplied tenfold, then to seven hundred times, then to many multiples.

﴿And as for those who disdained and were arrogant﴾: they disdained with their hearts and were arrogant with their limbs, refusing to worship Allah. ﴿He will punish them with a painful punishment﴾, meaning a punishment of retribution and pain. The word ﴿painful﴾ means (mu'lim, causing pain), and the word ﴿punishment (adhaban)﴾, which the grammarians call, in terms of its i'rab, what?

* Student: It is a substitute for the absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq), a verbal noun (masdar).

* The Shaykh: A masdar; because the absolute object is that which is not like the verb or like the governing word; this is the absolute object. But if it comes from the governing verb, it is called a masdar. The masdar has several purposes, among them emphasis, as here: ﴿punishment, painful﴾. It is emphasis in that it returns with the word of the governing verb (yu'adhdhibu, He punishes), and it is also a preparation for what follows, since it is described as painful.

﴿And they will not find for themselves, besides Allah, any protector or helper﴾. The protector (wali) means one who takes charge of them if Allah punishes them. ﴿Nor any helper﴾ who prevents Allah's punishment from them. So there is no repeller and no remover of the punishment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Who is the repeller?

* Student: The protector.

* Another student: Allah.

* The Shaykh: The protector. And the remover?

* Students: The helper.

* The Shaykh: The helper. In this noble verse there is evidence for recompense, and that a person is repaid according to his deeds, but in the manner that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has promised.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of faith and righteous deeds, due to His saying: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾.

Among its benefits: that it may indicate that righteous deeds will not be accepted except with faith, because faith was mentioned first, and what is mentioned first is the earlier. This is a matter indicated by the Sunnah, and indeed by the Qur'an, as in the Exalted's saying: ﴿And nothing prevented their contributions from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Tawbah 54]. So faith must precede righteous deeds. Can this be used as evidence that righteous deeds are not part of faith, since the default in conjunction (ataf) is difference?

Those who argue that faith is not righteous deeds may use it as evidence, but we say: the Book and the Sunnah have shown that deeds are part of faith. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And Allah would not let your faith go to waste﴾ [al-Baqarah 143]. The people of tafsir said: that is, your prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis, and prayer is a deed. And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Faith has seventy-some branches, the highest of which is the saying 'There is no god but Allah,' and the lowest of which is removing harm from the road, and modesty is a branch of faith."
