[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (9) and Muslim (35/58), the wording being his, from Abu Hurayrah.] It may also be said: when faith and righteous deeds are mentioned together, faith means the deed and speech of the heart, and righteous deeds mean the deeds and speech of the limbs and tongue, so this falls under what differs when combined and coincides when separated.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a refutation of the Jabriyyah. It is taken from His saying: ﴿did righteous deeds﴾, where He attributed the deeds to them. The Jabriyyah say that a person does not act, and the deed is attributed to him only figuratively, and that his deed is not by his choice or intention.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of Allah's favor, the Mighty and Majestic, in calling the reward a wage (ajr), as if He had hired workers who work and He pays them wages. Although the benefit of the deed is for whom?

* Students: For the doer himself.

* The Shaykh: For the doer himself, whereas in wages outside of dealing with Allah, the work is for the one who pays the wage. But here the work is for the person himself, and yet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, rewards him.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the reward for righteous deeds exceeds what Allah, Exalted, has decreed; due to His saying: ﴿and increase them from His bounty﴾.

* Among its benefits: that the arrogant who disdain have as their recompense punishment: ﴿He will punish them with a painful punishment﴾. Does this include people of sin? If you say yes, it follows that punishment befalls them in every case; if you say no, that is closer, because believers deserve punishment but are not punished if Allah wills, either by Allah's forgiveness, or by intercession, or by the prayers of believers for them, or the like; the sinners.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that whomever Allah intends harm for, there is no turning it back and no protection from it; due to His saying, Exalted: ﴿And they will not find for themselves, besides Allah, any protector or helper﴾.

It follows from this that the polytheists will never benefit from their gods, whatever they may be. Rather, Allah said: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], all of them, the worshipper and the worshipped, will be cast into it.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light. As for those who believed in Allah and held fast to Him﴾ [An-Nisa 4:174–175], and so on to the end of the verses.

﴿O mankind﴾: The address here with ﴿O mankind﴾ is to indicate that the message of the Prophet (ﷺ) is universal and not restricted to one people over another. All of mankind is addressed by the Prophet's law (ﷺ), including the Jews and Christians.

His saying ﴿there has certainly come to you﴾: The sentence is emphasized with one emphasis, which is (qad). His saying ﴿a proof from your Lord﴾: The burhan (proof) is the evidence, and what is meant by it is the signs that the messengers, peace be upon them, brought. The greatest sign brought by the Messenger is the sign of the Prophet (ﷺ), which is the Noble Qur'an, the sign that remains for the Messenger until Allah, Most High, permits the ruin of the world.

His saying ﴿from your Lord﴾: The lordship here is lordship in the more specific sense, because His, Mighty and Majestic, bestowing upon us clear and decisive signs is undoubtedly among the requirements of a special lordship. He, glory be to Him, is the Lord of all, but there is a special lordship by which Allah bestows favor upon whomever He wills of His servants.

﴿And We have sent down to you a clear light﴾: ﴿We have sent down to you a light﴾ means the Qur'an. Light is the opposite of darkness. Is it a light in meaning or a sensory light? It is undoubtedly a light in meaning, because by it the heart, the face, the grave and the resurrection are illuminated. So the whole Qur'an is light, but it requires reflection and contemplation on its meanings and acting upon it.

﴿A clear light﴾: The word (mubin), as we mentioned earlier, may mean what? Clear, and it may mean making manifest. This is because it is derived from (abana), and abana may be transitive and intransitive. You say: abana li al-tariq (he made the road clear to me), and then it is what? Abana li al-tariq is transitive. You also say: abana al-fajr, meaning (tala'a) (dawned), and this is intransitive. Accordingly, the word ﴿mubinan﴾ may be interpreted as making clear to others, and as being clear in itself. Do the two meanings conflict?

The answer: No. We have already gone over the important and established principle: whenever the texts of the Qur'an and the Sunnah are capable of two meanings, with no preference for one over the other and no contradiction between them, the text must be understood as bearing both meanings together.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Noble Qur'an was sent down for all creation, as shown by His saying ﴿there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord﴾, and from this follows the universality of the message of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is obligatory upon one who does not know the Arabic language to learn it in order to be able to benefit from the Qur'an, as shown by His saying ﴿a proof from your Lord﴾. It is well known that if you recited it to a non-Arab, as Allah, Most High, said: ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs, and he recited it to them, they would not have been believers in it﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara 26:198–199], because they do not understand it and do not taste its flavor.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of lordship, and that the sending of messengers and the sending down of books are among the requirements of what? His lordship, as shown by His saying ﴿there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord﴾.

Among its benefits: the Noble Qur'an is light, but, my brothers, that is not tasted, or not witnessed, except by one who combines two matters. The first: reflection (tadabbur). The second: remembrance (tadhakkur). The evidence for this is the saying of Allah, Most High: ﴿A Book We have sent down to you, blessed, [so that they may reflect upon its verses]﴾ for what purpose?

Student: ﴿that they may reflect upon its verses﴾.

Shaykh: ﴿that they may reflect upon its verses﴾ is one, and ﴿and that those of understanding may remember﴾ [Sad 38:29]. So whoever reflects upon the verses, and is safe from desire, and is safe from distorting the evidences, and takes admonition from what is in them, he will find a great light in his heart, and there will be unveiled to him of knowledge what is not unveiled to others.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Noble Qur'an contains the explanation of everything, because light is something by which things must be made apparent, like the daytime when it dawns and things become clear by it, and like a lamp when you light it, for it must make clear what was hidden. So the Qur'an is an explanation of everything, but the explanation may be obscured, either due to weakness of faith, or due to lack of knowledge, or due to deficiency of understanding, or due to bad intention. Otherwise the Qur'an is clear and a light for everyone. But a person may have weak faith, meaning that he does not trust that the Qur'an contains the explanation of everything, or he may be deficient in knowledge, lacking the tool by which he can derive rulings from the evidences, and for this reason we have become in need of learning the principles of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh) (the foundations of Islamic jurisprudence). Or it may be due to deficiency of understanding: a person may have knowledge and reflection, yet he does not comprehend, and people differ greatly in this. You find some people who can derive from a verse or a hadith many benefits that others can derive from it only in small measure in comparison to them, and that is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whomever He wills.

For this reason, when 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked: Did the Prophet (ﷺ) single you out with anything? (meaning, and entrust you with it?) He said: "No, by Him who split the grain and created the soul, except an understanding that Allah grants a person concerning His Book." Note: "except an understanding that Allah grants a person concerning His Book." And what is in this document? They said: What is in it? He said: "The intellect, the ransoming of captives, and that a Muslim is not to be killed for a disbeliever." [Narrated by al-Bukhari (6903) from the hadith of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.]

So the point of this report is his saying: "an understanding that Allah grants to whomever He wills." If you reflect upon the words of the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, you will find a great difference among them in understanding. For example, you find one scholar explaining a hadith and then deriving twenty benefits from it, while another explains it and derives only five or four benefits. Likewise with the verses.

Fourth: bad intention. A person may have knowledge, awareness and understanding, but his intention is corrupt. He studies the Book and studies the Sunnah in order to support his own opinion, even though he knows it to be false. We ask Allah for well-being. This is one of bad intention, and it prevents him from reaching the goal.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿As for those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him, He will admit them into mercy from Him and bounty, and guide them to Himself on a straight path.﴾

﴿As for those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him﴾: this combines faith and reliance (tawakkul). They believed in Him and held fast to Him, seeking refuge in no one other than Him. They made Him their protection, the Exalted, and their safeguard. They do not hold fast to anyone besides Allah, nor do they depend or rely on anyone except Allah.

﴿So He will admit them into mercy from Him and bounty and guide them to Himself on a straight path.﴾ The sin (س) in His words ﴿will admit them﴾ conveys two things. The first is certainty (tahqiq), and the second is nearness (qurb). The certainty is evident. As for nearness, how near the Hereafter is to this world! Between a person and the Hereafter there is nothing but the soul leaving his body, and then he is in the world of the Hereafter. For this reason Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, said in al-'Aqidah al-Wasitiyyah: Included in belief in the Last Day is belief in everything the Prophet ﷺ reported that will occur after death.

And His words ﴿in mercy from Him﴾: the word ﴿mercy﴾ may be an attribute of Allah, and it may be a created thing of Allah. Which is intended here?

* Student: The created one.

* The Shaykh: The created mercy, yes, because the attribute of mercy is not something people can enter, but created mercy is that which people can enter. For this reason He said ﴿in mercy from Him﴾. And "min" (من) here is not for partition, but for origin, meaning: mercy originating from Him.

﴿And bounty﴾: that is, in addition to the mercy, or, more correctly, in addition to what they deserve of reward and recompense.

﴿And guide them to Himself on a straight path﴾: Allah the Exalted mentioned for those who believed in Allah and held fast to Him two great fruits. The first fruit: that Allah admits them into mercy and bounty. The second: that He guides them to Himself on a straight path, that is, He points them the way. This indicates that faith and holding fast to Allah are a cause of increased knowledge, which is clear, and other texts also indicate it, such as His saying: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad 17], and ﴿That those who believe may increase in faith﴾ [al-Muddaththir 31].

And His words ﴿straight (mustaqiman)﴾ have two readings: one with the sin (س), and the other with the sad (ص), because sin and sad alternate due to the closeness of their points of articulation. And His words ﴿a path (sirat)﴾: sirat is the road that is wide and easy. Its origin is from their saying: "zaraṭa al-luqmah" when one swallows the morsel quickly; "sarraṭahā" and "ṣarraṭahā," all of which have the same meaning.

And His words ﴿straight (mustaqim)﴾ are the opposite of crooked. Crookedness may be an up-and-down crookedness, and it may be a right-and-left crookedness. The path of Allah the Exalted is straight, with no right or left turns, and no ascent or descent, because it is easy.

* Student: What is the difference between yastankif and yastakbir? Could it be that when they are combined, istinkaf is in the heart and istikbar is in action, and that originally they have one meaning?

* The Shaykh: No, but they are mutually implicative. Every person who is arrogant in refusing (istinkaf) will be proud (istikbar), and every proud person is one who refuses. But when they are combined, istinkaf is in the heart and istikbar is in the limbs.

* Student: (...)

* The Shaykh: From this verse, that the Qur'an is superior to other [scriptures]. What is the basis for that?

* Student: The basis is that it described the heavenly books (...), and described the Qur'an as "clear" (mubin) (...).

* The Shaykh: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord﴾. It may be said: by "mankind" after the sharia of Muhammad, what is meant is the community of Muhammad to whom the call was addressed.

* Student: They said: mention must precede the pronoun, ﴿so He will gather them﴾. We say: that means all people, and it was not preceded, [since] the Messiah and the angels were not preceded.

* The Shaykh: What is it? We say: generality is derived from the detail that follows?

In any case, we have mentioned this: first, those other than the Messiah and the angels were not mentioned, neither the disbelievers nor the believers, but we mentioned that the detail that follows indicates that.

* Student: May Allah bless you. Regarding the interpretation of His words ﴿And as for those who were disdainful and arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment﴾, we said: a believer is not included in this, since Allah the Exalted may forgive them.

* The Shaykh: Yes, the disobedient one.

* Student: Yes, the believing disobedient one. And when we were explaining Riyad al-Salihin after the Asr prayer, we said that His words ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾ [an-Nisa 48] may include practical shirk.

* The Shaykh: No, the minor shirk.

* Student: The minor shirk, (...) the plural?

* The Shaykh: We say: it may include it, but it is not as clear.

* Student: Shaykh, what is the reason some of the Salaf denounced the saying of one who says: "in the abode of Your mercy," although mercy includes created mercy, and complete mercy upon the servant is not except by his entering Paradise?

* The Shaykh: There is no basis for this, unless their time had an innovation that requires a person to avoid this expression.

* Student: This was reported from some of the Successors.

* The Shaykh: I say: there is no basis for it, since Paradise is an abode (mustaqarr).

* Student: So there is no harm in saying it?

* The Shaykh: There is no harm in saying it. ﴿The companions of Paradise on that day are better in abode and finer in resting place﴾ [al-Furqan 24].

* Student: His words ﴿As for those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him﴾: we said that "as for" (أما) is for detailing. What is the second division?

* The Shaykh: It is omitted here, its mention folded away, and mention may be folded away in the context of division because it is understood from the opposite.

* Student: May Allah be good to you, Shaykh. His words ﴿As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will pay them in full﴾: ﴿So He will pay them in full﴾, the fa' (ف), in terms of grammar?

* The Shaykh: It is the linking response, located in the answer to (أما).

* Student: But Shaykh, we said before that the fa' is required only in specific places?

* The Shaykh: That is with the conditional (إن) which governs, this does not govern.

* Student: (...)

* The Shaykh: This does not govern, but its response must have the fa', ﴿So as for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. But as for he who withholds and considers himself free of need, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾ [al-Layl 5–10].

* Student: So, Shaykh, the linking particles mentioned are only for (إن)?

* The Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, what is the validity of the saying of one who says: the position of the People of the Sunnah regarding the believing disobedient ones on the Day of Resurrection is that some of them enter Paradise immediately without punishment, and some enter the Fire with certainty, so there must be a group that enters the Fire, and some have their punishment delayed, for example, but he made a category that enters the Fire with certainty.

* The Shaykh: No one among the people of sins enters the Fire with certainty, ever, because Allah says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [an-Nisa 48].

* Student: He says (...) no, it is by way of perpetuity, rather it is in (...).

* The Shaykh: From where? From where did we take this, when there is the explicit verse?

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿They ask you for a legal ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning al-kalalah. If a man dies leaving no child and has a sister, she will have half of what he left, and he inherits from her if she has no child. If there are two sisters, they will have two-thirds of what he left. And if there are brothers and sisters, men and women, the male has the share of two females. Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray, and Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ [an-Nisa 176].
* The Shaykh: Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light﴾. What is meant by the clear light?

* Student: The Qur'an.

* The Shaykh: The Qur'an. And what is the meaning of (mubin)?

* Student: It has two meanings. The first meaning: clear in itself, if we take it as an active participle. The second meaning: that it makes clear, meaning it indicates the way, if we take it as a passive participle.

* The Shaykh: How?

* Student: We said: mubin comes in the sense of (fa'il) and in the sense of (maf'ul).

* The Shaykh: Wrong.

* Student: We said: it has two meanings: bayyin and mubin, bayyin in itself, with bayyin derived from abana, and this verb...

* The Shaykh: From (bana).

* Student: From (bana), which comes intransitive and comes transitive.

* The Shaykh: So bayyin is from bana, and mubin is from abana? But it has two meanings; what is the first meaning?

* Student: That it is clear in itself, and that it is clear (...).

* Student: Both are from abana, Shaykh.

* The Shaykh: Both are from abana, but bayyin is from bana. As for the verse we have, mubin is from abana, and from bana, no, from abana, both intransitive and transitive.

What is the reconciliation between His words ﴿We have sent down to you﴾ and His words ﴿A Book We have sent down to you﴾, with the address being to the Messenger ﷺ?

* Student: The address to the Messenger ﷺ is in the singular, because it was sent down from Allah the Exalted to the Prophet ﷺ, and ﴿to you﴾ (plural) means it was sent down as a general law for all believers.

* The Shaykh: That is, insofar as it was sent down upon the Messenger ﷺ as revelation, it was sent down to him, and insofar as it came down to us as guidance and direction, it is sent down to us.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿As for those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him﴾, and so on to the end.

* In this verse there are benefits. Among them: the virtue of faith in Allah and reliance upon Him. The indication of this is that He promised them that He would admit them into mercy from Him.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that whoever believes and holds fast to Allah will attain mercy both immediate and deferred, from His saying ﴿So He will admit them﴾, and the sin indicates nearness, and we explained its basis in the commentary, and that the people most at ease in mind and most expansive in breast are the believers who hold fast to Allah.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that mercy is used both for an attribute of Allah and for what results from it. Is this verse an instance of the attribute's usage or of the usage of its effects?

* Student: Of the effects of the attribute.

* The Shaykh: Of the usage of the effects of the attribute. Why?

* Student: The reason is that it is not an attribute of Allah.

* The Shaykh: What do you say? "Mercy" here: is it the mercy of Allah or the mercy that is among its effects, among the effects of His mercy?

* Student: The mercy of Allah.

* The Shaykh: The mercy of Allah itself? Wrong.

* Student: Of the effects of His mercy.

* The Shaykh: Why was it not the mercy which is His attribute?

* Student: Because He said ﴿So He will admit them into mercy from Him﴾. If it were the mercy of Allah the Exalted which is His attribute, He could not admit them into it.

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. Do you agree with this reasoning?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Good. Is there evidence that mercy is used for what results from mercy?

* Student: Yes, what is established in the hadith of Allah's saying to Paradise: "You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will of My servants."

* The Shaykh: What is established in the Sahih as Allah's saying to Paradise: "You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will."

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the explanation of Allah the Exalted's favor upon those who believed in Allah and held fast to Him, from His saying ﴿and bounty﴾.

* Among its benefits: that whoever believes in Allah and holds fast to Him, his faith and holding fast are a cause of guidance, from His saying ﴿and guide them to Himself on a straight path﴾.

* Among its benefits: that the path leading to Allah the Exalted is straight, with no crookedness in it?

* Student: ﴿and guide them to Himself on a straight path﴾.

* The Shaykh: Straight, with no crookedness in it. And is the straightness here the straightness of this world only, or of this world and the Hereafter? The answer: the generality; the religion of Allah the Exalted is straight in this world and the next.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 4, verse 176 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah﴾, to the end of the verse. Al-istifta' (seeking a ruling) is the request for al-ifta' (issuing a ruling), and al-ifta' is the giving of information about a legal ruling, or a non-legal one as well, since a person may be asked for a ruling in worldly matters. The subject of ﴿they ask﴾ is the Companions, and the kaf in ﴿they ask you﴾ refers to the Messenger, may Allah's prayers and peace be upon him.

﴿Say﴾, answering them: ﴿Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah﴾.

The phrase ﴿concerning the kalalah﴾: according to what we have preferred, to what is it connected? To ﴿they ask you﴾ and ﴿gives you a ruling﴾, because we have said there is no objection to two governing elements acting on one governed element, as is the view of the Kufans. On this basis we say: ﴿They ask you. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah﴾. As for the view of the Basrans, they say that ﴿concerning the kalalah﴾ is connected to ﴿gives you a ruling﴾, and the verb ﴿they ask you﴾ has been omitted from it, and it did not contain a pronoun because it is not a principal element.

In any case, ﴿Say: Allah gives you a ruling﴾. What is the kalalah about which they asked? Allah, the Exalted, clarified what the kalalah is by mentioning the matter it involves. The root of kalalah is taken from al-iklil (the crown), which is what surrounds a thing. For this reason, in explaining it, we say: they are the collateral relatives (al-hawashi), because a person's relatives are of three branches: a branch from him, a branch that is his origin, and a branch from his fathers and grandfathers. The branch that is from him is called?
* Students: The descendants (al-furu').
* The Shaykh: The descendants. And the branch he is from?
* Students: The ascendants (al-usul).
* The Shaykh: The ascendants. And the branch from his fathers and grandfathers?
* Students: The collaterals (al-hawashi).
* The Shaykh: The collaterals. On this basis we say: what is meant by kalalah is the collaterals: the brother and his sons, and the paternal uncle and his sons, whether he is your uncle, your father's uncle, or your grandfather's uncle; these are the kalalah. For this reason, al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, explained it, according to what has been reported from him, as "one who has neither child nor parent"[[Recorded by al-Darimi (3015) and 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf (19191), the wording being his, from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.]].

﴿Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah: if a man dies leaving no child, and has a sister, she receives half of what he left﴾, ﴿If a man dies﴾.

﴿If﴾ is a conditional particle, and conditional particles only enter upon verbs. Here it has entered upon a noun: ﴿If a man dies﴾. Does this violate the rule established by the grammarians, that (in) the conditional, and indeed all conditionals, enter only upon verbs, or is this a point of disagreement?

This is a point of disagreement. According to the view that the condition enters only upon verbs, ﴿a man﴾ is the subject of an omitted verb, and the estimate is: if a man died.

But there is another view: that conditional particles may enter upon nouns, because this occurs frequently in the Arabic language: ﴿When the sky is split asunder﴾ [al-Infitar 1], ﴿When the sky is rent apart﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 1], ﴿When the stars are scattered﴾ [al-Infitar 2], and many examples. So this view says there is no objection to a conditional particle entering upon nouns.

A third view says that what follows the conditional (in) is the object of the verb after it: if it is a subject, it is a fronted subject; if it is a deputy subject, it is a fronted deputy subject; and if it is accusative, it is a fronted object, and there is no objection. In any case, what we see is that when the grammarians differ on a matter, we follow the easier view.

﴿If a man dies﴾: i.e., dies. ﴿Leaving no child﴾: neither male nor female, because "child" (walad) is indefinite in a negative context and therefore general. ﴿And has a sister, she receives half of what he left﴾: is the sister a full sister, a paternal sister, or a maternal sister?
* A student: A full sister (...).
* The Shaykh: A full sister or a paternal sister. The evidence that the maternal sister is not meant is that Allah mentioned her at the beginning of the surah, saying: ﴿And if a man or a woman leaves neither ascendants nor descendants as heirs, but has a brother or a sister, then each of them shall have a sixth. But if they are more than that, they shall share in a third﴾ [al-Nisa' 12]. So what is meant here by ﴿and has a sister﴾?
* A student: The full sister and the paternal sister.
* The Shaykh: The full sister and the paternal sister. Why do we not say it is general: a full sister, a paternal sister, or a maternal sister?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, but what is the evidence?
* The student: The evidence is that (...).
* The Shaykh: The evidence is that Allah mentioned the inheritance of the maternal sister at the beginning of the surah, saying: ﴿and has a brother or a sister﴾, meaning from the mother, ﴿each of them shall have a sixth﴾. So this verse concerns a full sister or a paternal sister. Pay attention now: the child is absent, meaning there is no inheriting descendant.

﴿She receives half of what he left﴾: it is necessary that there be no male ascendants with her, for what reason? Because if there were male ascendants with her, she would not receive the half, since a condition for the full or paternal sister to receive a half is that there be no inheriting male ascendant. So here there is no child... what? Nor a father among the males, correct? ("No child") from where is it taken? ﴿Leaving no child﴾. ("Nor a father") from the fact that the sister's share here is a half, since if there were a male father she would not receive a half.

﴿She receives half of what he left, and he inherits from her if she has no child﴾. Who is it that inherits from her?
* Students: Her brother.
* The Shaykh: Yes, her brother.
* A student: The full sister.
* The Shaykh: No, ﴿if she has no child﴾, meaning she has no child, neither male nor female, such as a woman who dies leaving only her full brother, or only her paternal brother, and she has no child.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿and he inherits from her if she has no child﴾. Here is the difficulty of the matter: how does Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, say ﴿and he inherits from her if she has no child﴾, when, if she had a husband, he would inherit only what remains after the husband's share? Yet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says ﴿he inherits from her if she has no child﴾?

We say: this statement concerns kalalah, those who inherit by kinship apart from (...) by marriage. The question now is about what? About kalalah, and kalalah relates only to kin. So His saying ﴿and he inherits from her if she has no child﴾ means: if she has a husband, he inherits what remains after the husband; and if she has no husband, he inherits all of it. If someone says: perhaps she has a mother, so does her brother inherit from her?
* A student: She has no child.
* The Shaykh: Why?
* The student: Because of kalalah.
* The Shaykh: As we said, kalalah means he has no father, that is, no male ascendant. We restricted it a little while ago. A male father inherits after the mother's share. Why? It may be answered that Allah, glorified and exalted, here mentioned the one who inherits by agnatic relationship (ta'sib), and therefore did not specify a fixed share for him, but said: ﴿and he inherits from her if she has no child﴾.

﴿If there are two sisters﴾: ("if there are two") the pronoun refers to the two sisters.
﴿Two﴾: meaning there is no male with them.
﴿Then they shall have two-thirds of what he left﴾: of what did he leave? Of whom?
* A student: The brother.
* The Shaykh: The brother. ﴿And if they are brothers and sisters, men and women, the male has the equivalent of the share of two females﴾. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, did not fix a share because, when there are brothers along with sisters, they inherit by agnatic relationship. So Allah mentioned here the pure female siblings: a single one, multiple pure females, and females with males. This is because the division cannot go outside these three categories: either one female, or multiple females, or a mixed group of males and females. So the single one has a half, the two or more have two-thirds, and if they are men and women, then by agnatic relationship, the male has the equivalent of the share of two females.
* A student: The pure males?
* The Shaykh: Yes, how?
* The student: The pure males?
* The Shaykh: What he mentioned here.
* The student: ﴿And he inherits from her﴾.
* The Shaykh: Yes, ﴿and he inherits from her if she has no child﴾. This is the case of sole inheritance. Correct. So the categories are four: pure males; pure females, multiple; single females; and the fourth, the combination of males and females.

On this basis (...), for the inheritance of the sister to be a half, the sister receives a half under conditions:
That there is no inheriting descendant, taken from His saying: ﴿he has no child﴾.
The second condition: that there is no inheriting male ascendant, also taken from His saying: ﴿and he inherits from her﴾, ﴿if she has no child﴾, since if there were a father she would not have inherited.
The third condition: that she be alone.
The fourth condition: the absence of an agnatic male.
These are the conditions for the full sister's inheritance of a half. The paternal sister adds one condition only: that there be no full brother or full sister.

What are the conditions for the full sister's inheritance of a half?
* A student: Four conditions are required.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: First: that the deceased has no inheriting descendant; second, that there is no inheriting male ascendant; and third, that there is no male with her.
* The Shaykh: That is: an agnatic male?
* The student: Yes, and that she be alone.
* The Shaykh: Yes, and that she be alone. So: being alone, the absence of an agnatic male, the absence of an inheriting descendant, and the absence of an inheriting male ascendant: these are the conditions of the full sister.
The paternal sister adds only one condition: that there be no full brother or full sister.
If a man dies leaving a full sister and a husband, how much is her share generally?
* Students: A half.
* The Shaykh: A half, given the conditions are complete. Two full sisters and a husband?
* Students: Two-thirds.
* The Shaykh: Two-thirds. A full sister and a full brother?
* Students: Agnatic inheritance.
* The Shaykh: Agnatic inheritance, because of His saying: ﴿And if they are brothers and sisters, men and women, the male has the equivalent of the share of two females﴾.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾. ﴿Makes clear﴾: i.e., shows the truth plainly.
﴿To you, lest you go astray﴾: the scholars said its meaning is "lest you go astray." It was also said: the estimate is "out of dislike that you go astray," because Allah, the Exalted, wants to guide us.
﴿That you go astray, and Allah is All-Knowing of everything﴾. His knowledge, glorified and exalted, is comprehensive of everything, past, present, or future, whether concerning His own actions or the actions of the servants. He is All-Knowing of everything; nothing is hidden from Him on earth or in heaven. And from His knowledge, the Mighty and Majestic, is that He has given us a ruling on what is difficult for us.
* This verse contains many benefits. Among them: the eagerness of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, to know the truth, as shown by His saying ﴿they ask you﴾. How often they asked, and how often they inquired to reach the truth!
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, may find some matter difficult, and Allah gives the ruling on it, as in His saying ﴿Say: Allah gives you a ruling﴾, and He did not say "so give them a ruling."
* Among its benefits: applying the word ifta' (giving a ruling) to Allah, as in His saying ﴿Say: Allah gives you a ruling﴾. This is a verb; though it is speech, may we derive from it a divine name and say "the Mufti"? No, but we may derive from it an attribute, because an attribute is broader and more general.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the arrangement of the verses is tawqifi (divinely prescribed). The reason is that this verse is connected to the verses of inheritance at the beginning of the surah, and if the arrangement were a matter of personal reasoning, the consequence of reasoning would be that it should be linked with its sister verses and mentioned there. But since the arrangement of the Qur'an is tawqifi, that is, in its verses, its place is here. A parallel to this is His saying, blessed and exalted: ﴿Guard over the prayers, and the middle prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion. And if you fear, then on foot or riding; but when you are safe, remember Allah as He taught you what you did not know. And those of you who die and leave wives﴾ [al-Baqarah 238–240]. These two verses were mentioned in the context of the verses of 'iddah, because the arrangement of the verses is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, or from the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, and personal opinion has no room in it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: if a man dies leaving no child, and has a sister, and no father, she has a half, by His saying ﴿she receives half of what he left﴾. If he has a descendant, that is, a child, we consider: if the child is male, the sister is excluded; if the child is female, she takes her fixed share, and the remainder goes to the sister. The first example: if a man dies leaving a full sister and a son, the estate goes to the son and nothing to the sister.
If he dies leaving a full sister and a son's son, likewise the estate goes to the son's son, and the full sister receives nothing, because the sons of sons, however far down, are in the position of sons.
If a man dies leaving a sister and a father?
* A student: The sister is excluded.
* The Shaykh: Yes, she is excluded, because of the presence of a male ascendant.
If a man dies leaving a sister and a grandfather?
* A student: There is a difference.
* The Shaykh: Wrong.
* The student: She is not excluded.
* The Shaykh: Wrong. We must ask about the grandfather: is he from the mother's side or not? If he is from the mother's side, she receives a half, because a maternal grandfather is among the dhawu al-arham (uterine kin). If he is from the father's side, such as the father's father, this is a point of disagreement among the scholars, and the firmly established view is that she is excluded in the presence of the grandfather, and that she has no inheritance with the grandfather.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: if a woman dies leaving only a full brother or a paternal brother, the estate is his, by His saying ﴿and he inherits from her if she has no child﴾. So if a woman dies leaving only a full brother, the whole estate is his.
If she leaves a full nephew (son of a full brother), the estate is his. If she leaves a full niece (daughter of a full brother)?
* Students: She has nothing.
* The Shaykh: She has nothing, because she is among the dhawu al-arham. If she leaves a full nephew and a full niece?
* A student: To the full nephew.
* The Shaykh: The estate goes to the full nephew, and his sister has nothing, because he is an agnate and she is among the dhawu al-arham.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: two or more sisters have two-thirds, by the words of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿If there are two, then they shall have two-thirds of what he left﴾.
If a woman dies leaving two full sisters and a husband: the husband's share is a half, and theirs is two-thirds. This is a problem, because a half and two-thirds cannot both be given in full. The scholars say the case is subject to 'awl (proportional reduction), and the method is: the case here is from six; the husband has a half, three; the two full sisters have two-thirds, four; so it rises to seven. The husband, instead of having three and a half out of seven, has only three out of seven. Is it clear?
The doctrine of 'awl was adopted by 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, on the counsel of the Companions, and only a few people disagreed with it.
Among the benefits of this noble verse: inheritance enters the ownership of the heir, whether he wishes or not. From where is this taken? ﴿She receives half of what he left﴾ and ﴿for them two-thirds﴾, and the lam is for ownership (tamlik).
Among the benefits of this noble verse: a slave does not inherit. The enslaved servant does not inherit. From where is this taken? From the lam that denotes ownership, since the servant does not own; the servant's property belongs to his master, by the saying of the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family: "Whoever sells a slave who has property, his property belongs to the one who sold him, unless the buyer stipulates otherwise"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2379) and Muslim (1543/80), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar.]]. And because if we made a brother inherit from his sister when he is a slave, the reality would be that we inherited from whom?
* Students: His master.
* The Shaykh: His master, who is a stranger to her.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the preference of the male over the female in agnatic inheritance, by His saying ﴿the male has the equivalent of the share of two females﴾.
If someone asks: what is the wisdom?
We say: the wisdom is the superiority of maleness over femaleness, and because the male has obligations in life, such as marriage and providing for others, and other things.
If someone says: this objection applies to uterine brothers, since they are equal, we say: because they do not inherit by agnatic relationship, but by fixed share.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the fixed share may increase with an increase in the number of beneficiaries. What is the evidence? What is the question?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Good. The evidence? It is in the verse.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No.
* A student: Shaykh, His saying: ﴿If she is one, she has the half﴾ [al-Nisa' 11], and when they become two, they have two-thirds.

* **Shaykh:** The evidence that a single daughter receives half and two or more receive two-thirds. However, there is a category of share (*fard*, a fixed share) that does not increase with the number of its recipients. This category has four types. The first?
* **Student:** The first is the one-third (...).
* **Shaykh:** Wrong.
* **Student:** The wife's one-eighth.
* **Shaykh:** Yes, the share of the wife. Whether there is one wife or several, her share does not increase with their number. The second?
* **Student:** The maternal siblings, O Shaykh.
* **Shaykh:** Well done! A single one receives a sixth, and two or more receive a third.
* **Student:** (...), O Shaykh.
* **Shaykh:** No.
* **Student:** The grandmothers.
* **Shaykh:** The grandmothers.
* **Student:** For a single one, a sixth, and...
* **Shaykh:** For a single one, a sixth, and for multiple ones, a sixth.
* **Student:** The paternal sisters, when they inherit a sixth.
* **Shaykh:** A sixth, correct. The paternal sisters, when they inherit a sixth.
* **Student:** The daughters of a son, when they inherit a sixth.
* **Shaykh:** The daughters of a son, when they inherit a sixth. These are four categories whose share does not increase with their number.

* One of the benefits of this noble verse is that Allah, glorified and exalted, has made clear to us everything we need so that we do not go astray, based on His saying, ﴿Allah makes clear to you﴾, where the object is omitted to indicate generality.

* Another benefit of this noble verse is the refutation of the Delegationists (*ahl al-tafwid*) regarding the attributes of Allah, glorified and exalted, who say: "We do not know the meanings of His attributes." For if we did not know them, it would follow that there is no clarification in the Qur'an, while Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾. Moreover, going astray in the matter of the attributes is graver than going astray in the matter of rulings, because going astray in the attributes concerns the Creator, glorified and exalted, the One who is worshipped, whereas going astray in rulings concerns only acts of worship. And there is a difference between the two.

* Another benefit of this noble verse is the exhortation to seek knowledge by returning to the Book of Allah, glorified and exalted, for we do not know Allah's clarification except through the Book and the Sunnah. Every person flees from going astray and seeks clarity and guidance, so we say: the way to that is to be keen to follow the Book and the Sunnah.

* Another benefit of this noble verse is the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah, glorified and exalted, of everything, based on His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of everything﴾.

* **Student:** Shaykh, is the natural creation (*khilqah*) among the causes of the difference in inheritance between males and females?
* **Shaykh:** The creation?
* **Student:** Yes, because we said that among the causes is: the first cause, that males and females differ?
* **Shaykh:** Yes indeed, a difference in responsibility.
* **Student:** No, we said... we made this a cause, and we made obligations a second cause.
* **Shaykh:** In responsibility, and in bearing matters. As for the creation itself, that is not possible.

* **Student:** May Allah be good to you, O Shaykh. What is the ruling on the obligatory bequest (*wasiyyah wajibah*), which is enforced and applied in some laws, that the children of a son take their father's share alongside the presence of paternal uncles, up to no more than one-third?
* **Shaykh:** It is obligatory for everyone who has wealth to bequeath to relatives who do not inherit, because Allah made this obligatory when He said: ﴿It is prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, that he make a bequest to parents and relatives in kindness; this is a duty upon the righteous﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:180].
* **Student:** These are given to them by regulation, even if he did not make a bequest.
* **Shaykh:** And if he did not make a bequest?
* **Student:** Even if he did not make a bequest.
* **Shaykh:** No, this opinion is not permissible.
* **Student:** Like a fixed share, I mean.
* **Shaykh:** This is not permissible.

* **Student:** Shaykh, if a man dies leaving a full sister and a paternal brother, the half goes to the full sister and the remainder to her relatives (*ahluha*). But if a man dies leaving a paternal sister and a full brother, the entire estate goes to the full brother. What is the reason for this difference? For if we say the residuaries ('*asabah*, residuary heirs) take all, then the entire estate goes to the brothers and sisters and they receive nothing. And if we say, based on "Give the shares to their rightful owners" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6732) and Muslim (1615/2), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas.]], then will the sisters inherit absolutely?
* **Shaykh:** If we say the residuaries take all, in the case of a full sister and a paternal brother there is no residuary taking, because the full sister is stronger than the paternal brother, since she has a relationship to the deceased through two ties: motherhood and fatherhood. So she became stronger than him, and she inherits by fixed share. Conversely, if she is a paternal sister and he is a full brother, we say: he is also stronger than her, because he is connected through two ties while she is connected through one. His inheritance is by residuary taking, and the residuary takes the entire estate.
* **Student:** Why did the residuary not operate here?
* **Shaykh:** Where?
* **Student:** In the first case?
* **Shaykh:** Because she is stronger than him.
* **Student:** Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿If they are siblings, men and women, then to the male is the equivalent of the portion of two females﴾.
* **Shaykh:** Yes, they must be equal in the description; that is, they must be siblings and equal in the description, meaning either full siblings or paternal siblings. If they differ, then there is a detailed ruling.

* **Student:** If a man dies leaving two sisters, they receive two-thirds. Then where is the remaining third, the rest?
* **Shaykh:** Yes. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Give the shares to their rightful owners; then whatever remains goes to the nearest male." [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6732) and Muslim (1615/2), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas.]] One looks to the residuary heir: either an uncle, or a paternal cousin, or a nephew, or whatever is similar. If there is no residuary heir, the scholars have differed, may Allah have mercy on them, as to whether the remainder is returned to the holders of fixed shares or is placed in the public treasury (*bayt al-mal*). Some of them said it is returned, and some said it is placed in the public treasury. The correct view is that it is returned.
* **Student:** To the two sisters?
* **Shaykh:** To the two sisters. So they receive two-thirds as a fixed share, and the remainder by return (*radd*).

* **Student:** Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, what is the criterion for distant kindred (*dhawu al-arham*)? Are they only those on the mother's side, or all relatives who do not inherit?
* **Shaykh:** All relatives who inherit neither by fixed share nor by residuary taking.
* **Student:** What is the evidence for the non-inheritance of the male heir in the estate?
* **Shaykh:** What evidence?
* **Student:** The evidence for the non-inheritance of the male heir in the estate of a full sibling?
* **Shaykh:** Regarding what?
* **Student:** That the male ascendant (*asl*) heir is absent in the estate of a full sibling?
* **Shaykh:** Based on His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And he has a sister, so for her is half of what he left﴾. For it is impossible that a sister inherits half of what her brother left if there is a male ascendant present. For if the father is present, the sister is excluded by consensus. And if it is the grandfather or one above him, there is a difference of opinion, and the correct view is that she is excluded.
* **Student:** May Allah pardon you. His saying "a man who leaves kalalah" (a person with no ascendants or descendants)... is this not evidence?
* **Shaykh:** Actually, the whole matter is basically about the *kalalah* itself. Its basic structure is connected to the *kalalah*, and the division Allah has prescribed indicates this.

* **Student:** Shaykh, may Allah bless you, we know that there is no bequest to an heir. So if he bequeaths to his paternal uncle while the father is alive, is the bequest enforced?
* **Shaykh:** It is enforced up to a third, from a third or less.
* **Student:** Is this one an heir, is the uncle among the heirs?
* **Shaykh:** The uncle does not inherit alongside the father.
* **Student:** What is meant, O Shaykh, by "There is no bequest to an heir" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2870) and al-Tirmidhi (2120), from the hadith of Abu Umamah al-Bahili.]]?
* **Shaykh:** Truly, to an heir, that is what it means.
* **Student:** If the father bequeaths to the children of one of his sons?
* **Shaykh:** If he bequeaths to the children of one of the sons, one looks: if they are heirs, then the bequest is not valid. For example, if he has a daughter and a son's son, then the bequest to the son's son is not valid, because he is an heir, and a bequest to an heir is forbidden, because it is a transgression of the limits of Allah. Allah, the Exalted, has given the heir a specific portion, and then you come and bequeath to him?! That means you have transgressed the limits of Allah, glorified and exalted.
* **Student:** Shaykh, may Allah bless you. Is debt or bequest given precedence over inheritance?
* **Shaykh:** Yes indeed, debt takes precedence over inheritance. If a man dies and has ten thousand riyals, and he owes ten thousand riyals, then the heirs have no right in it. This is based on His saying: ﴿After any bequest he has made or debt﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:12].
But someone may say: How can the bequest be given precedence over the heirs when they must inherit alongside it?
We say: Does the bequest take precedence over inheritance while the heirs must still have a share? Yes. This becomes clear in an example: if a woman bequeaths one-third of her estate, and she leaves a husband and a full sister. If there were no bequest, the husband would have... what?
* **Group:** Half.
* **Shaykh:** Half in full. And the full sister?
* **Group:** Half.
* **Shaykh:** Half in full. Now, since the bequest has taken effect, we say: the case is from three. One for the bequest, the husband has half of the remainder, one; and the full sister, one. So in reality, the husband only has a third, and the full sister only has a third. Has the bequest decreased or not? The bequest?
* **Group:** It did not decrease.
* **Shaykh:** It did not decrease. Are you sure?
* **Group:** Yes.
* **Shaykh:** Why? Because she bequeathed one-third and the beneficiary received one-third. But the husband ended up with only a third, whereas if there were no bequest he would have inherited...?
* **Group:** Half.
* **Shaykh:** Half. This is the reason for giving precedence to the bequest over inheritance. For the meaning of our saying that the bequest takes precedence over inheritance is not that the heirs do not inherit alongside the bequest. No. The meaning is that if there is a shortfall, the shortfall falls on the heirs and not on the bequest.
* **Student:** The excluded heir (*al-warith al-mahjub*), can a bequest be made to him?
* **Shaykh:** Yes indeed, because he is not an heir, like the son of a son alongside his uncle.
